children.title: Minimal Face of a Point
children.top_down_role: Facial localization of an individual cone element.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Face of the Origin
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of the origin is the cone's lineality space and is the zero face exactly for pointed cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The minimal face of the origin is the lineality space:
\[\operatorname{face}_K(0)=K\cap(-K)=\operatorname{lin}K.\]
In particular, \(\operatorname{face}_K(0)=\{0\}\) exactly when \(K\) is pointed.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(0)=\operatorname{lin}K\), and this equals \(\{0\}\) if and only if \(K\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes nonpointed cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Order Representation of the Minimal Face
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone element y lies in the minimal face of x exactly when some positive multiple of x dominates y in the cone order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in K\),
\[\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\{y\in K:\exists\alpha>0\text{ such that }\alpha x-y\in K\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\{y\in K:\exists\alpha>0,\ \alpha x-y\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic membership representation valid without pointedness or closedness.

notation.meaning: Minimal face of K containing x.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Face of a Point
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of a cone element is the intersection of all faces containing it and is the unique smallest such face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex cone \(K\subseteq V\) and a point \(x\in K\), the minimal face of \(K\) containing \(x\) is defined by
\[\operatorname{face}_K(x):=\bigcap\{F:F\unlhd K,\ x\in F\}.\]
It is the unique smallest face of \(K\) containing \(x\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\bigcap\{F:F\unlhd K,\ x\in F\}\) is the unique smallest face of \(K\) containing \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional facial localization inside a convex cone.

notation.meaning: F is a face of K.
Minimal face of K containing x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone-Order Representation of the Minimal Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise algebraic membership test for a minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in K\),
\[\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\{y\in K:\exists\,\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }x-\varepsilon y\in K\}.\]
Consequently,
\[\operatorname{face}_K(0)=K\cap(-K),\qquad \operatorname{face}_K(tx)=\operatorname{face}_K(x)\quad(t>0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of a point consists of the cone elements dominated by that point in the cone order; at zero it is the lineality space and it is constant along positive rays.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\{y\in K:\exists\varepsilon>0,\ x-\varepsilon y\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Order Representation of the Minimal Face

children.title: Minimal Face of a Set or Section
children.top_down_role: Facial localization of subsets and conic sections.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Representative of a Section
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any relative-interior point of a nonempty convex subset has the same minimal face as the whole subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(S\subseteq K\) is nonempty and convex, then
\[x\in\operatorname{ri}S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{face}_K(x)=\operatorname{face}_K(S).\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(S)=\operatorname{face}_K(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to nonempty convex subsets, including affine or conic sections.

notation.meaning: Relative interior of S in its affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Join of Pointwise Minimal Faces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of a nonempty subset is the face-lattice join of the minimal faces of its points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty subset \(S\subseteq K\),
\[\operatorname{face}_K(S)=\bigvee_{x\in S}\operatorname{face}_K(x),\]
where the join is taken in the face lattice of \(K\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
The join is taken in the face lattice of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(S)=\bigvee_{x\in S}\operatorname{face}_K(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary nonempty subsets; avoids convention-dependent empty joins.

notation.meaning: Least face containing the indexed faces.
Minimal face of K containing S.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Face of a Set or Section
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of a subset is the intersection of all faces of the cone that contain the subset and is the unique smallest such face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a subset \(S\subseteq K\), the minimal face of \(K\) containing \(S\) is defined by
\[\operatorname{face}_K(S):=\bigcap\{F:F\unlhd K,\ S\subseteq F\}.\]
It is the unique smallest face of \(K\) containing \(S\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_K(S)=\bigcap\{F:F\unlhd K,\ S\subseteq F\}\) is the unique smallest face of \(K\) containing \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to arbitrary subsets, including affine or conic sections of the cone; for the empty subset the displayed intersection determines the minimal face under the adopted face convention.

Minimal face of K containing S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Interior Reduction for Sets and Sections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A relative-interior point determines the minimal face of a nonempty convex subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq K\) be nonempty and convex. For every \(x\in\operatorname{ri}S\),
\[\operatorname{face}_K(S)=\operatorname{face}_K(x).\]
In particular, when an affine section \(S=K\cap A\) is nonempty, every point of \(\operatorname{ri}S\) determines the minimal face containing the section.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face of a nonempty convex subset, including an affine conic section, is the minimal face of any relative-interior point of that subset.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Incidence Test by Relative-Interior Membership
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is contained in another face exactly when its relative interior meets that face; relative interiors of two faces meet exactly when the faces coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F,G\unlhd K\) be nonempty faces. Then \[\operatorname{ri}F\cap G\ne\varnothing\iff F\subseteq G.\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{ri}F\cap\operatorname{ri}G\ne\varnothing\iff F=G.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ri}F\cap G\ne\varnothing\iff F\subseteq G\), and \(\operatorname{ri}F\cap\operatorname{ri}G\ne\varnothing\iff F=G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order characterization for nonempty faces of a finite-dimensional convex cone.

notation.meaning: F is a face of K.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Characterization of Faces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point lies in the relative interior of exactly its minimal face; relative interiors of nonempty faces therefore partition the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty face \(F\unlhd K\) and every \(x\in K\),
\[x\in\operatorname{ri}F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{face}_K(x)=F.\]
Hence each \(x\in K\) belongs to the relative interior of exactly one face, namely \(\operatorname{face}_K(x)\), and
\[K=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{\substack{F\unlhd K\\F\ne\varnothing}}\operatorname{ri}F.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\iff \operatorname{face}_K(x)=F\); consequently, the relative interiors of the nonempty faces partition \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional relative-interior stratification by nonempty faces.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.
Minimal face of x in K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face containment detected by a relative-interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty faces \(F,G\unlhd K\),
\[F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{ri}F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{ri}F\cap G\ne\varnothing.\]
Consequently, distinct faces have disjoint relative interiors, and
\[F\subsetneq G\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\dim F<\dim G.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is contained in another exactly when some, equivalently every, relative-interior point of the first belongs to the second.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq G\iff\operatorname{ri}F\cap G\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex set, and relative interiors are taken in the affine hulls of the corresponding faces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex sets, including nonclosed sets when their faces and relative interiors are understood in the usual affine sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[C=\bigsqcup_{\substack{F\in\mathcal F(C)\\F\neq\varnothing}}\operatorname{ri}F,\qquad x\in\operatorname{ri}F\iff F=\operatorname{face}_C(x).\] Thus each point belongs to the relative interior of exactly one nonempty face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative-interior characterization organizes a convex set into disjoint facial strata. Every point lies in the relative interior of one and only one nonempty face, and that face is precisely the minimal face containing the point. Hence two points occupy the same facial stratum exactly when their minimal faces coincide. The relative interiors of faces are the maximal relatively open convex subsets of the ambient convex set. This supplies an intrinsic localization rule: relative-interior membership identifies the face without reference to active inequalities or a particular representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in C\ \exists!F\in\mathcal F(C)\setminus\{\varnothing\}:\quad x\in\operatorname{ri}F.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\) iff every face of \(C\) containing \(x\) also contains \(F\), with equality for the minimal one.
\(\operatorname{face}_C(x)=\operatorname{face}_C(y)\) iff \(x\) and \(y\) belong to the same relative-interior facial stratum.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial duality associates with a primal face all dual-cone vectors orthogonal to that face, and symmetrically associates with a dual face all primal vectors orthogonal to it. Thus facial duality naturally forms an order-reversing correspondence between primal and dual facial structures, with exact involution on the faces fixed by double conjugation.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed-Face Duality Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugation gives an inclusion-reversing bijection between exposed faces of a closed cone and its dual; double conjugation exposes the smallest exposed superface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F\in\mathcal E(K)\), set \(F^\triangle=K^*\cap F^\perp\); for \(G\in\mathcal E(K^*)\), set \(G^\triangle=K\cap G^\perp\). Then
\[F^{\triangle\triangle}=F,\qquad G^{\triangle\triangle}=G.\]
Thus conjugation is an inclusion-reversing bijection between \(\mathcal E(K)\) and \(\mathcal E(K^*)\). For an arbitrary face \(F\unlhd K\), \(F^{\triangle\triangle}\) is the smallest exposed face of \(K\) containing \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(\mathcal E(K)\) denotes the exposed faces of \(K\), including \(K\) and \(\{0\}\) when applicable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\mapsto F^\triangle\) is an inclusion-reversing bijection from \(\mathcal E(K)\) to \(\mathcal E(K^*)\), with inverse \(G\mapsto G^\triangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anti-isomorphism of exposed-face lattices for closed finite-dimensional cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exposed-face duality is the regime in which conjugation is restricted to exposed faces of a closed cone and its dual. Within these lattices, orthogonal complementation reverses inclusion and double conjugation returns the starting face. The restriction is essential: arbitrary nonexposed faces need not be fixed by double conjugation. The regime therefore separates the universally involutive exposed correspondence from stronger cone classes in which every face participates. Improper faces may be included, with the top and bottom elements exchanged according to the cone's lineality and dual lineality.

equivalent_formulations_latex: Conjugation gives a bijection between exposed primal faces and exposed dual faces and reverses every inclusion.
The fixed points of double conjugation are the exposed faces.
special_cases_latex: For a polyhedral cone, every face is exposed, so the regime covers the full face lattice.
For a facially exposed nonpolyhedral cone, the primal face lattice lies entirely in the fixed-point set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Covering relations are reversed under the exposed-face correspondence.
Minimal exposed primal faces correspond to maximal proper exposed dual faces, subject to lineality conventions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone; for a face \(F\), \(F^*:=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in F\}\) is taken in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex cones; two standard dual-facial regularity classes are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[K\text{ is facially exposed}\iff \forall F\in\mathcal F(K)\ \exists y\in K^*:\ F=K\cap y^\perp.\] \[K\text{ is nice}\iff \forall F\in\mathcal F(K):\ K^*+F^\perp\text{ is closed},\] equivalently \(F^*=K^*+F^\perp\) for every face \(F\) under the finite-dimensional ambient-dual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A facially exposed cone is a closed cone all of whose faces are exposed by dual vectors. A nice cone, also called facially dual complete in some sources, satisfies a stronger closure compatibility between each face and the ambient dual cone: adding the orthogonal complement of the face to the dual cone yields a closed set, equivalently the full ambient dual of the face. These definitions classify cones according to how completely their facial structure is represented by dual certificates. They must not be conflated without an additional theorem specifying when one property implies the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{fexp}}:=\{K:\mathcal F(K)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{exp}}(K)\},\qquad \mathcal C_{\mathrm{nice}}:=\{K:K^*+F^\perp\text{ closed for every }F\unlhd K\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Facial exposedness is equivalent to \(F^{\triangle\triangle}=F\) for every face \(F\).
Niceness is equivalent to \(F^*=K^*+F^\perp\) for every face when the ambient-space dual is used.
special_cases_latex: Polyhedral cones belong to both classes.
Self-duality alone does not define either regularity class.
immediate_consequences_latex: For a facially exposed cone, conjugation is involutive on every primal face.
For a nice cone, dual certificates for a face admit the stated sum representation without an additional closure operation.
boundary_notes: The equivalence defining niceness depends on finite dimensionality and on the ambient dual convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Nice Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex cone is nice when adding the orthogonal complement of any face to the dual cone always produces a closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone \(K\) is called nice if, for every face \(F\unlhd K\), the Minkowski sum
\[K^*+F^\perp:=\{y+z:y\in K^*,\ z\in F^\perp\}\]
is closed in the ambient space. Equivalently, the image of \(K^*\) under orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{span}F\) is closed for every face \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is nice exactly when \(K^*+F^\perp\) is closed for every face \(F\unlhd K\).

Facially Dual-Complete Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial dual completeness means every functional nonnegative on a face extends from a dual-cone functional, equivalently the projected dual cone equals the face dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone \(K\) is facially dual-complete if, for every face \(F\unlhd K\), every functional nonnegative on \(F\) is the restriction of a functional nonnegative on \(K\). Under inner-product identification, this means
\[F^*=\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*).\]
Without facial dual completeness one always retains only
\[F^*=\operatorname{cl}\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*).\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is facially dual-complete exactly when \(F^*=\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*)\) for every face \(F\unlhd K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Facial Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed finite-dimensional cones, closed dual-plus-orthogonal sums, closed projected duals, and exact face-dual extension are equivalent conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each face \(F\unlhd K\), the following conditions are equivalent:
\[K^*+F^\perp\ \text{is closed},\]
\[\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*)\ \text{is closed},\]
\[\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*)=F^*.\]
Consequently, \(K\) is nice if and only if \(K\) is facially dual-complete.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The niceness condition and facial dual completeness are equivalent face by face and hence equivalent for \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalence between the sum-closedness and projection-surjectivity formulations.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projection onto the span of F.
Dual of F within its span.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is consistent with the finite-dimensional quotient/projection formulation of niceness, and theorem is the correct content kind. Because no citation is supplied for this specialized equivalence, source uncertainty prevents acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Facial Divergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonniceness appears at a face whose projected dual cone is nonclosed and strictly smaller than the face dual, despite being dense in it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(K\) is not nice, then there exists a face \(F\unlhd K\) for which \(K^*+F^\perp\) is not closed. Equivalently,
\[\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*)\subsetneq F^*=\operatorname{cl}\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*).\]
Thus some functional nonnegative on \(F\) is a limit of restrictions of elements of \(K^*\) but is not itself the restriction of any element of \(K^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some face \(F\unlhd K\) satisfies \(\Pi_{\operatorname{span}F}(K^*)\subsetneq F^*\), although its closure equals \(F^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure mechanism for nonnice finite-dimensional cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Translation-invariant order induced by a cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(V\) is a real vector space and \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone containing \(0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic ordered vector spaces; topological closure, pointedness, and solidity are additional regularity properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[x\leq_K y\iff y-x\in K.\] The pair \((V,K)\) is a preordered vector space with positive cone \(K=\{x:0\leq_Kx\}\). The relation is a partial order exactly when \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone induces a generalized inequality by declaring one vector no larger than another when their difference lies in the cone. Convex-cone closure under addition and nonnegative scaling makes the relation reflexive, transitive, translation invariant, and compatible with multiplication by nonnegative scalars. Thus every convex cone produces a vector preorder. Antisymmetry is present exactly when the cone is pointed. Conversely, the positive elements of any translation-invariant, positively homogeneous vector preorder form a convex cone, so the cone and the preorder determine one another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\leq_K y\Longleftrightarrow 0\leq_K(y-x),\qquad K=\{x\in V:0\leq_Kx\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\geq_Ky\) iff \(x-y\in K\).
A cone-induced preorder is characterized by translation invariance and compatibility with nonnegative scalar multiplication.
special_cases_latex: \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\) gives componentwise order.
\(K=\mathbb S_+^n\) gives the Loewner order on symmetric matrices.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(x\leq_Ky\) implies \(x+z\leq_Ky+z\).
If \(x_i\leq_Ky_i\), then \(\alpha_1x_1+\alpha_2x_2\leq_K\alpha_1y_1+\alpha_2y_2\) for \(\alpha_i\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a proper cone: convex, closed, pointed, and solid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional generalized inequalities induced by proper cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[x\preccurlyeq_Ky\iff y-x\in K,\qquad x\prec_Ky\iff y-x\in\operatorname{int}K.\] The first relation is the nonstrict generalized inequality and the second is its strong or strict generalized inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper cone defines two standard comparison relations. The nonstrict generalized inequality uses membership of the displacement in the cone. The strict generalized inequality uses membership in the cone's interior. Properness supplies the usual regularity: pointedness makes the nonstrict relation antisymmetric, convexity gives transitivity and compatibility with vector operations, closure makes its graph closed, and solidity ensures that the strict relation is nonempty. These comparisons need not be total; two vectors can be incomparable when neither displacement belongs to the ordering cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\preccurlyeq_K\text{ is a partial order on }\mathbb R^n,\qquad \prec_K\text{ is its interior-based strict comparison}.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered-Vector-Space Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-induced preorders are translation invariant and preserved by nonnegative linear combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(x_i\preceq_K y_i\) and \(\alpha_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i x_i\preceq_K\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i y_i.
\]
In particular, \(x\preceq_K y\) implies \(x+z\preceq_K y+z\) and \(\lambda x\preceq_K\lambda y\) for every \(z\in V\) and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i\alpha_i x_i\preceq_K\sum_i\alpha_i y_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic compatibility of every cone-induced preorder.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Induced Preorders
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone defines a reflexive and transitive generalized inequality, and its lineality space consists exactly of the differences between mutually related elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y\in V\), define the cone-induced relation by
\[x\preceq_K y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y-x\in K.\]
This relation is a preorder. Its symmetric part is characterized by
\[x\preceq_K y\ \text{and}\ y\preceq_K x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y-x\in\operatorname{lin}K,\]
where \(\operatorname{lin}K:=K\cap(-K)\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone containing \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relation \(x\preceq_K y\iff y-x\in K\) is reflexive and transitive, and \(x\preceq_K y\preceq_K x\iff y-x\in K\cap(-K)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No pointedness assumption; lineality produces equivalent directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak, nonzero, strong, and generalized-interior conic comparisons
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(V\) is a real topological vector space, \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone, and \(I(K)\subseteq K\) denotes a chosen interior-type set such as \(\operatorname{int}K\), \(\operatorname{ri}K\), \(\operatorname{sri}K\), or \(\operatorname{qri}K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-strength taxonomy; transitivity of a selected strict variant requires the indicated direction set to be stable under addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[x\leq_Ky\iff y-x\in K,\qquad x<_Ky\iff y-x\in K\setminus\{0\},\] \[x\ll_Ky\iff y-x\in\operatorname{int}K,\qquad x\ll_{K,I}y\iff y-x\in I(K).\] These are respectively weak, nonzero, topologically strong, and generalized-interior comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic order strength is classified by the portion of the ordering cone in which the displacement lies. Weak comparison allows the boundary and zero. Nonzero comparison excludes equality but may still use boundary directions. Strong comparison requires an interior direction and is the standard strict generalized inequality for a solid cone. In lower-dimensional or infinite-dimensional settings, relative, strong-relative, or quasirelative interiors can replace the ordinary interior, producing explicitly named generalized-interior regimes. The relations are not interchangeable: an interior-based comparison is generally stronger than a nonzero comparison, and ordinary interior may be empty even when generalized interiors are useful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\ll_Ky\Longrightarrow x<_Ky\Longrightarrow x\leq_Ky\quad\text{when }\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\text{ and }K\text{ is pointed}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\ll_Ky\) iff \(y\in x+\operatorname{int}K\).
Relative-strong comparison uses \(y-x\in\operatorname{ri}K\) when order is considered in \(\operatorname{span}K\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), \(x\ll_Ky\) means strict inequality in every coordinate.
For a lower-dimensional cone, \(\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\) in \(V\) while \(\operatorname{ri}K\) can be nonempty.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(K\) is pointed, the nonzero relation is irreflexive.
If \(I(K)+K\subseteq I(K)\), then \(x\ll_{K,I}y\leq_Kz\) implies \(x\ll_{K,I}z\).
boundary_notes: For nonpointed cones, \(K\setminus\{0\}\) need not define a transitive strict order because opposite lineality directions may cancel.
The chosen generalized interior must always be named; there is no universal default in infinite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonzero-difference comparison is transitive exactly for pointed cones; any nonzero lineality direction exhibits failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Conic Orders
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pointed cone, strict conic inequality means a nonzero cone difference. It defines an irreflexive, transitive strict partial order preserved by translations and positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y\in V\), define
\[x\prec_K y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y-x\in K\setminus\{0\}.\]
For pointed \(K\), this is equivalently the relation \(x\preceq_K y\) with \(x\ne y\). It is an irreflexive, transitive strict partial order and satisfies
\[x\prec_K y\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x+z\prec_K y+z\]
for every \(z\in V\), as well as
\[x\prec_K y\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha x\prec_K\alpha y\]
for every \(\alpha>0\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a pointed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\prec_K y\iff y-x\in K\setminus\{0\}\) defines an irreflexive, transitive strict partial order compatible with translation and positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict means nonzero cone difference, distinct from the interior-based strong order.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong comparison is irreflexive unless the cone is the whole space, which is the sharp failure case.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Transitivity of Strong Comparison
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a weakly positive direction to an interior direction preserves interiority, giving mixed transitivity and open strong-order sections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is a convex cone with nonempty interior, then \(\operatorname{int}K+K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K\). knowledge_statements.title: Strong Conic Orders
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is strongly below another when their displacement lies in the ordinary interior of the ordering cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in X\), define the strong conic comparison by \[x\ll_K y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y-x\in\operatorname{int}K.\] Thus the displacement from \(x\) to \(y\) must lie in the ordinary interior of \(K\). \(K\subseteq X\) is a convex cone with \(\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\ll_K y\iff y-x\in\operatorname{int}K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generating, normal, and topologically closed ordered spaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \((V,\|\cdot\|)\) is a normed real vector space, \(K\subseteq V\) is a convex cone, and \(x\leq_Ky\iff y-x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normed ordered vector spaces; generating, normal, and closed-order properties are recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[K\text{ is generating}\iff K-K=V.\] \[K\text{ is normal}\iff \exists c>0\ \forall x,y\in V:\quad 0\leq_Ky\leq_Kx\Longrightarrow\|y\|\leq c\|x\|.\] The order is closed when \(K\) is closed, equivalently its graph \(\{(x,y):x\leq_Ky\}\) is closed in \(V\times V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered normed space is controlled by several independent cone properties. A generating cone permits every vector to be written as a difference of positive vectors, giving order decomposability. A normal cone makes order intervals norm bounded in a uniform way: vectors between zero and a positive upper bound cannot have arbitrarily larger norm than that bound. A closed cone gives a topologically closed order relation, so inequalities persist under limits. Pointedness may additionally be imposed to obtain a partial order, but it is distinct from generating and normal behavior outside specialized finite-dimensional settings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(V,K)\text{ is a closed generating normal ordered normed space}\iff K-K=V,\ K\text{ is closed, and }\exists c>0:\ 0\leq_Ky\leq_Kx\Rightarrow\|y\|\leq c\|x\|.\]

children.title: Generating Cones
children.top_down_role: Positive cones supporting signed decompositions of ambient vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Dual Pointedness Characterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional cone generates the ambient space exactly when its dual cone has no nonzero lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a finite-dimensional inner-product space, \(\operatorname{lin}(K^*)=(\operatorname{span}K)^\perp\). Consequently, \(K\) is generating if and only if its positive-sign dual cone \(K^*\) is pointed.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-dual characterization restricted to finite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Generating Cones and Directed Orders
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone generates the space exactly when its cone-induced preorder is upward directed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex cone \(K\) is generating if and only if its induced preorder is upward directed: for every \(x,y\in X\), there exists \(z\in X\) with \(x\le_Kz\) and \(y\le_Kz\). Equivalently, every finite subset of \(X\) has a common upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K-K=X\iff \forall x,y\in X\;\exists z\in X:\ x\le_Kz\ \land\ y\le_Kz.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic equivalent of signed positive decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Interior Characterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, a cone is generating exactly when it is full-dimensional, equivalently when it has nonempty ambient interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty convex cone \(K\) in a finite-dimensional vector space, generatingness, full dimensionality, and nonempty ambient interior are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K-K=X\iff\operatorname{span}K=X\iff\operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional geometric characterization of algebraic generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Generating Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone is generating when every ambient vector is the difference of two vectors in the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(K\) is generating in \(X\) if \[K-K=X.\] Equivalently, every \(x\in X\) admits a signed positive decomposition \(x=u-v\) with \(u,v\in K\). For the preorder \(x\le_K y\) defined by \(y-x\in K\), this says that every vector is the difference of two \(K\)-positive vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is generating exactly when \(K-K=X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic generating property of an ordering cone.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equivalences among generation, full dimensionality, solidity, and pointed duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K^*=\{y\in X^*: \langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}.\] If \(X\) is finite dimensional, then \[K-K=X\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{span}K=X\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow K^*\cap(-K^*)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, a cone is generating exactly when it is full-dimensional, has nonempty ambient interior, and has a pointed dual cone.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ generating}\iff\operatorname{span}K=X\iff\operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\iff K^*\text{ is pointed}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Generating-Cone Equivalences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the finite-dimensional solidity characterization in infinite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the Banach space \(\ell^1\), the positive cone \[\ell^1_+=\{x=(x_n):x_n\ge0\ \forall n\}\] is closed and generating because every \(x\in\ell^1\) satisfies \(x=x^+-x^-\), but \(\operatorname{int}\ell^1_+=\varnothing\). Thus generation does not imply nonempty ambient interior outside finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive cone of ℓ¹ is closed and generating but has empty interior, so the finite-dimensional solidity equivalence does not extend to infinite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K-K=X\) and \(\operatorname{int}K=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise positive and negative parts of \(x\)

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Dimensional Interior Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic equivalent of signed positive decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the preorder induced by a convex cone \(K\subseteq X\), the following are equivalent: \[K-K=X;\] every pair \(x,y\in X\) has a common upper bound; and every finite subset of \(X\) has a common upper bound. Thus \(K\) is generating exactly when \((X,\preceq_K)\) is directed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone is generating exactly when its induced preorder is directed, equivalently when every finite collection has a common upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K-K=X\iff (X,\preceq_K)\text{ is upward directed}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Generating Cones and Directed Preorders

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly bounded signed positive decomposition for closed generating cones in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(X\) is a Banach space and \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed generating convex cone, then there exists \(C>0\) such that every \(x\in X\) admits \(u,v\in K\) satisfying \[x=u-v,
\qquad \|u\|+\|v\|\le C\|x\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed generating cone in a Banach space admits positive and negative parts whose total norm is uniformly controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C>0\ \forall x\in X\ \exists u,v\in K:\ x=u-v\text{ and }\|u\|+\|v\|\le C\|x\|.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Andô Decomposition Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dual test for generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a finite-dimensional inner-product space, the lineality space of \(K^*\) is \((\operatorname{span}K)^\perp\). Hence \(K\) is generating if and only if its dual cone \(K^*\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional cone generates the space exactly when its dual cone has no nonzero lineality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Pointedness Characterization

children.title: Normal Cones in Ordered Spaces
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of cone-induced order with norms and topologies.

knowledge_statements.title: A Pointed Nonclosed Cone Need Not Be Normal
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The open upper-half-plane cone is pointed but has an unbounded order interval, so it is not normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(K=\{(a,b):b>0\}\cup\{0\}\). This convex cone is pointed and nonclosed. For \(y=(0,1)\) and \(x_n=(n,1/2)\), one has \(0\le_Kx_n\le_Ky\), while \(\|x_n\|/\|y\|\to\infty\). Hence \(K\) is not normal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is pointed but not normal}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that pointedness alone does not imply normality, even in finite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Normality-Generation Duality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed Banach-space cone is normal exactly when its dual has uniformly bounded signed positive decompositions, with the converse primal-dual statement obtained by exchanging normality and bounded generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed convex cone \(K\) in a Banach space is normal if and only if there exists \(G_*<\infty\) such that every \(f\in X^*\) can be written \[f=f_+-f_-,\qquad f_+,f_-\in K^*,\qquad \|f_+\|+\|f_-\|\le G_*\|f\|.\] Dually, \(K^*\) is normal if and only if there exists \(G<\infty\) such that every \(x\in X\) can be written \[x=x_+-x_-,\qquad x_+,x_-\in K,\qquad \|x_+\|+\|x_-\|\le G\|x\|.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
\(K^*=\{f\in X^*:f(x)\ge0\ \forall x\in K\}\) is taken in the continuous norm dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ normal}\iff K^*\text{ has uniformly bounded positive decompositions},\qquad K\text{ has uniformly bounded positive decompositions}\iff K^*\text{ normal}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed ordering cones in Banach spaces; bounded decompositions are the quantitative form of generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Normality Forces Pointedness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every normal ordering cone is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is normal in a normed space, then \(K\) is pointed.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a normal convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic algebraic consequence of norm-order compatibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Monotone Renorming
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordering cone is normal exactly when the ambient topology admits an equivalent order-monotone norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(K\) is normal with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\) if and only if there is a norm \(p\) on \(X\), equivalent to \(\|\cdot\|\), such that \[0\le_Kx\le_Ky\quad\Longrightarrow\quad p(x)\le p(y).\] Thus normality is equivalent to the existence, within the same norm topology, of a norm for which the normality constant is \(1\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a convex cone inducing \(\le_K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is normal for }\|\cdot\|\iff\exists\text{ an equivalent norm }p\text{ with }0\le_Kx\le_Ky\Rightarrow p(x)\le p(y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent-renorming characterization of compatibility between the norm topology and the cone order.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Closed-Pointed Normality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed pointed cones are automatically normal in finite dimensions, and normality is invariant under equivalent renorming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every closed pointed convex cone in a finite-dimensional normed space is normal. Normality is unchanged under replacement by an equivalent norm, although the normality constant may change.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed pointed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists M>0\ \forall x,y:\ 0\le_Kx\le_Ky\Rightarrow\|x\|\le M\|y\|.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional sufficient condition; closedness is not claimed necessary for every cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Cones in Ordered Spaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone is normal when order domination controls norm size up to one uniform constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The ordering cone \(K\) is normal with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\) if there exists \(M>0\) such that, for all \(x,y\in X\), \[0\le_K x\le_K y\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|x\|\le M\|y\|.\] Equivalently, for every \(y\in K\), the order interval \([0,y]_K\) is contained in the norm ball \(\{x\in X:\|x\|\le M\|y\|\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a convex cone inducing \(x\le_K y\iff y-x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is normal when there exists \(M>0\) such that \(0\le_K x\le_K y\Rightarrow\|x\|\le M\|y\|\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm compatibility, distinct from variational normal cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Pointed Cones Need Not Be Normal in Infinite Dimensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-dimensional closed-pointed sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(X=C^1([0,2\pi])\) with \(\|f\|=\|f\|_\infty+\|f'\|_\infty\), let \(K=\{f:f(t)\ge0\ \forall t\}\). Then \(K\) is closed, convex, and pointed but is not normal. Indeed, for \(g\equiv1\) and \(f_n(t)=(1+\sin nt)/2\), \(0\le_Kf_n\le_Kg\), while \(\|f_n\|\ge n/2\) and \(\|g\|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise positive cone in C1 is closed and pointed, but order bounds do not control the derivative-sensitive norm.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the cone of pointwise nonnegative functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is closed and pointed but not normal}.

notation.meaning: order-bounded sequence with unbounded C1 norm

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Pointed Cones Need Not Be Normal in Infinite Dimensions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary structural consequences of norm normality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is normal with constant \(M\), then \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\). Its norm closure \(\overline K\) is also normal with constant \(M\), and hence is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal cones are pointed, and norm closure preserves normality with the same constant.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a convex cone normal with constant \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\cap(-K)=\{0\},\qquad \overline K\text{ is normal with constant }M.

notation.meaning: norm closure of the ordering cone

knowledge_statements.title: Pointedness and Stability under Closure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Closed Pointed Cones Are Normal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficiency and its sharp topological assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every closed pointed convex cone \(K\) in a finite-dimensional normed space is normal. Consequently, it is normal with respect to every norm on that space, although the normality constant may depend on the norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, closedness and pointedness guarantee normality for any norm.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real normed space.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a closed pointed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists M>0\ \forall x,y\in X:\quad 0\le_Kx\le_Ky\Rightarrow\|x\|\le M\|y\|.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Closed Pointed Cones Are Normal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-dimensional sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every closed pointed convex cone in a finite-dimensional normed space is normal. Since all norms are equivalent in finite dimensions, normality is independent of the chosen norm, although its constant may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed pointed cones are automatically normal in finite dimensions, for every choice of norm.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed pointed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists M>0\ \forall x,y:\ 0\le_Kx\le_Ky\Rightarrow\|x\|\le M\|y\|
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Normality Theorem

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
\(K^*=\{f\in X^*:f(x)\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}\) is formed in the continuous norm dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ normal}\iff K^*\text{ admits uniformly bounded signed positive decompositions},\qquad K\text{ generating}\iff K^*\text{ normal}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed ordering cones in Banach spaces; the bounded decompositions provide the quantitative form of generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex cone \(K\) in a Banach space, \(K\) is normal if and only if there exists \(G_*<\infty\) such that every \(f\in X^*\) has a decomposition \[f=f_+-f_-,\qquad f_+,f_-\in K^*,\qquad \|f_+\|+\|f_-\|\le G_*\|f\|.\] Conversely, \(K\) is generating if and only if it has a bounded decomposition modulus \(G<\infty\), meaning that every \(x\in X\) can be written \(x=x_+-x_-\) with \(x_\pm\in K\) and \(\|x_+\|+\|x_-\|\le G\|x\|\); this is equivalent to normality of \(K^*\). Under these conventions, a dual decomposition bound \(G_*\) is itself a valid normality constant for \(K\), and a primal decomposition bound \(G\) is a valid normality constant for \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed Banach-space cone is normal exactly when its dual cone generates the dual with uniformly bounded positive decompositions; bounded primal generation is dually equivalent to normality of the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Normality–Generation Duality

children.title: Order-Unit Base Gauge System
children.top_down_role: Distinguished positive directions and normalized positive sections in ordered spaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(V\) is a real vector space ordered by a pointed generating cone \(K\); \(e\in K\), and \(\varphi\in V^*\) is positive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic ordered spaces with finite-valued gauges; norm terminology additionally requires Archimedean or definiteness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[e\text{ is an order unit}\iff \forall x\in V\ \exists\lambda>0:\ -\lambda e\leq_Kx\leq_K\lambda e,\qquad \|x\|_e:=\inf\{\lambda>0:-\lambda e\leq_Kx\leq_K\lambda e\}.\] If \(\varphi(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\), then \(B_\varphi:=\{x\in K:\varphi(x)=1\}\) is a base, and its base gauge is \[\|x\|_{B_\varphi}:=\inf\{\varphi(u)+\varphi(v):u,v\in K,\ x=u-v\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order unit is a distinguished positive direction whose symmetric order intervals absorb the whole vector space. The Minkowski gauge of the interval from minus the order unit to the order unit is the order-unit gauge. Dually, a strictly positive functional normalizes every nonzero positive ray to a base of the cone. When the cone is generating, every vector is a difference of positive vectors, and minimizing the total functional mass of such decompositions defines the base gauge. Under the customary pointedness and Archimedean hypotheses these gauges are norms; without those hypotheses they may be seminorms or merely finite sublinear gauges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[[-e,e]_K:=\{x:-e\leq_Kx\leq_Ke\}\text{ has gauge }\|\cdot\|_e,\qquad B_\varphi=K\cap\{x:\varphi(x)=1\}\text{ normalizes positive rays}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\|x\|_e\) is the Minkowski functional of the symmetric order interval \([-e,e]_K\).
\(\|x\|_{B_\varphi}=\inf\{\alpha+\beta:x=\alpha b_+-\beta b_-,\ \alpha,\beta\geq0,\ b_\pm\in B_\varphi\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(V=\mathbb R^n\), \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), and \(e=\mathbf1\), the order-unit gauge is \(\|x\|_\infty\).
With \(\varphi(x)=\sum_i x_i\), the associated base is the probability simplex and the base gauge is \(\|x\|_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The order-unit gauge is monotone on symmetric order intervals.
Every nonzero \(x\in K\) has the unique normalization \(x=\varphi(x)b\) with \(b\in B_\varphi\).
boundary_notes: Strict positivity of \(\varphi\) is needed for the normalized section to meet each nonzero ray exactly once.

knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Order-Unit Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity excludes vectors that remain infinitesimally outside the cone despite every positive order-unit perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An order unit \(e\) is Archimedean when \(x+\varepsilon e\in K\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) implies \(x\in K\). Equivalently, \(x\le_K\varepsilon e\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) implies \(x\le_K0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}(K-\varepsilon e)=K.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional condition not implied by the bare order-unit property.

knowledge_statements.title: Order Units Need Not Be Archimedean
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lexicographic cone has an order unit that is not Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,b):b\ge0\}\) and \(e=(1,0)\). Then \(e\) is an order unit. For \(x=(0,-1)\), one has \(x+\varepsilon e\in K\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), while \(x\notin K\). Hence \(e\) is not Archimedean.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb R^2\) is ordered by the lexicographic cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\text{ is an order unit but is not Archimedean}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic ordered-space boundary example.

knowledge_statements.title: An Order Unit Makes the Cone Generating
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The existence of an order unit implies that every vector is a difference of two positive vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e\) is an order unit for \((X,K)\), then \(K\) is generating: \(K-K=X\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is ordered by the convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed-positive decomposition consequence of order-unit absorption.

knowledge_statements.title: Order Units as Algebraic Interior Points
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order units are exactly the algebraic interior points of the positive cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex cone \(K\), a vector \(e\in K\) is an order unit if and only if \(e\) lies in the algebraic interior of \(K\): for every \(x\in X\), there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(e+tx\in K\) whenever \(|t|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\text{ is an order unit}\iff e\in\operatorname{core}K.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic geometric equivalent of the absorbing-order-interval definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Order Unit Need Not Be Archimedean
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic-order failure of the Archimedean implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R^2\), let \[K=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,b):b\ge0\}\] be the lexicographic positive cone and let \(e=(1,0)\). Then \(e\) is an order unit and \(K\) is pointed. However, \(x=(0,-1)\notin K\) while \(x+\varepsilon e=(\varepsilon,-1)\in K\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). Thus \(e\) is not Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lexicographic cone has a pointed order unit but also positive infinitesimals, so the order unit is not Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e\text{ is an order unit but is not Archimedean}.
knowledge_statements.title: An Order Unit Need Not Be Archimedean

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space ordered by a convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\) is an order unit exactly when \(\forall x\in X\;\exists\lambda>0:\ -\lambda e\le_Kx\le_K\lambda e\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(e\in K\) is an order unit for \((X,K)\) if, for every \(x\in X\), there exists \(\lambda>0\) satisfying \[-\lambda e\le_K x\le_K\lambda e.\] Equivalently, the symmetric order intervals \([ -\lambda e,\lambda e ]_K\), as \(\lambda>0\) varies, absorb \(X\). This definition does not by itself impose the Archimedean condition or pointedness of \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positivity Is Necessary and Sufficient for Functional Normalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional section normalizes every nonzero cone ray exactly when its functional is strictly positive on every nonzero cone vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi\) be linear and nonnegative on \(K\), and set \(B=\{x\in K:\varphi(x)=1\}\). The section \(B\) meets every nonzero ray of \(K\) exactly when \(\varphi(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\). If \(0\ne u\in K\) satisfies \(\varphi(u)=0\), then \(\mathbb R_+u\) does not meet \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ meets every nonzero ray}\iff \varphi>0\text{ on }K\setminus\{0\}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact obstruction to a functional section meeting every nonzero ray.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex set \(B\subseteq K\) is a normalized base of \(K\) if every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\) has a unique representation \[x=t b,\qquad t>0,\quad b\in B.\] When a linear functional \(\varphi:X\to\mathbb R\) is strictly positive on \(K\setminus\{0\}\), the normalized section \(B=\{x\in K:\varphi(x)=1\}\) is such a base, and the unique scalar is \(t=\varphi(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Positivity Is Necessary for Functional Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact obstruction to meeting every nonzero ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero linear functional \(\varphi\ge0\) on \(K\), the section \(B=\{x\in K:\varphi(x)=1\}\) meets every nonzero ray of \(K\) exactly when \(\varphi(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\). If \(0\ne u\in K\) satisfies \(\varphi(u)=0\), then the ray \(\mathbb R_+u\) never meets \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional section normalizes every ray precisely when the functional is strictly positive on every nonzero cone vector.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is linear and nonnegative on K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ meets every nonzero ray}\iff \varphi>0\text{ on }K\setminus\{0\}
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positivity Is Necessary for Functional Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial correspondence induced by radial normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x\in K:\varphi(x)=1\}\) be a normalized convex base. For \(b\in B\), the ray \(\mathbb R_+b\) is an extreme ray of \(K\) if and only if \(b\) is an extreme point of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme points of a normalized base correspond exactly to extreme rays of its cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\in\operatorname{ext}B\iff\mathbb R_+b\text{ is an extreme ray of }K
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Points and Extreme Rays

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone Reconstruction from a Normalized Base
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique radial reconstruction owned by the normalized-base leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(B\) is a normalized base of \(K\), then \[K=\{tb:t\ge0,\ b\in B\},\] with the convention that \(t=0\) gives the origin. Every nonzero element has a unique positive scale and base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized base reconstructs the cone by nonnegative scaling, uniquely away from the origin.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a normalized base of the convex cone K.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Reconstruction from a Normalized Base
Non-Archimedean Degeneracy of an Order-Unit Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic order yields a pointed order-unit space whose gauge vanishes on a nonzero infinitesimal direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^2\) have the lexicographic cone \(K=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,b):b\geq0\}\) and let \(e=(1,0)\). Then \(K\) is pointed and \(e\) is an order unit, but \(-\lambda e\le_K(0,1)\le_K\lambda e\) for every \(\lambda>0\). Consequently \[p_e(0,1)=0\quad\text{although}\quad(0,1)\ne0.\]
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^2\) is ordered by the lexicographic cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_e(0,1)=0\quad\text{although}\quad(0,1)\ne0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of definiteness without Archimedeanness.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Representation of the Order-Unit Norm
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Archimedean order-unit norm is the supremum of absolute evaluations over normalized positive states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[S_e=\{\varphi\in X^*: \varphi(K)\subseteq\mathbb R_+,\ \varphi(e)=1\}.\] In an Archimedean order-unit space, \[p_e(x)=\sup_{\varphi\in S_e}|\varphi(x)|.\] Equivalently, \(-\lambda e\le_Kx\le_K\lambda e\) exactly when \(|\varphi(x)|\le\lambda\) for every \(\varphi\in S_e\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real Archimedean order-unit space with cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_e(x)=\sup_{\varphi\in S_e}|\varphi(x)|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean order-unit spaces, using positive normalized continuous functionals for the order-unit norm.
Concrete failure of definiteness and exact interval recovery without Archimedeanity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the lexicographic cone \[K=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,b):b\ge0\}\subset\mathbb R^2\] and order unit \(e=(1,0)\), the order-unit gauge is \[p_e(a,b)=|a|.\] Hence \(K\) is pointed but \(\ker p_e=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\). Moreover, \(\{p_e\le1\}\) is the full strip \(|a|\le1\), whereas \([-e,e]_K\) omits part of its boundary, demonstrating both failures caused by non-Archimedeanity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lexicographic order-unit gauge ignores the infinitesimal coordinate and has a unit ball larger than the generating order interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_e(a,b)=|a|,\qquad\ker p_e=\{0\}\times\mathbb R,\qquad[-e,e]_K\subsetneq\{p_e\le1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Order-Unit Gauge Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic status and degeneracy boundary of the order-unit gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e\) is an order unit, then its order-unit gauge \(p_e\) is a finite seminorm and \[\ker p_e=\{x\in X:-\varepsilon e\le_Kx\le_K\varepsilon e\ \text{for every }\varepsilon>0\}.\] Thus \(p_e\) is a norm exactly when the only order infinitesimal is zero. In particular, pointedness together with the Archimedean order-unit condition implies definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-unit gauge is a finite seminorm whose kernel consists exactly of elements dominated by every positive multiple of the unit.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is ordered by a convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker p_e=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}[-\varepsilon e,\varepsilon e]_K;\quad p_e\text{ is a norm}\iff\ker p_e=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Seminorm Structure and Infinitesimal Kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unit-ball identification under the condition that closes the interval boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e\) is an Archimedean order unit, then \[p_e(x)\le1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad-e\le_Kx\le_Ke.\] Thus the closed unit ball is exactly \([-e,e]_K\). Without Archimedeanity, the implication from \(p_e(x)\le1\) to interval membership can fail at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an Archimedean order unit, its symmetric order interval is exactly the closed gauge unit ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Unit Ball

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is ordered by a pointed convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_e(x)=\inf\{\lambda>0:-\lambda e\le_Kx\le_K\lambda e\}\).

It is a seminorm under the stated algebraic assumptions; if the order is Archimedean and \(K\) is pointed, then \(p_e(x)=0\) implies \(x=0\), so \(p_e\) is a norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Base-Gauge Formula
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual base gauge is the largest absolute value of the functional on the normalized base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup(-B))\), the polar gauge on every linear functional \(f\) bounded on \(B\) is \(\|f\|_{B,*}=\sup_{b\in B}|f(b)|\). Thus its dual unit ball consists of the functionals satisfying \(|f(b)|\le1\) for all \(b\in B\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a linear functional bounded on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar formula for linear functionals bounded on the base.

knowledge_statements.title: Base Gauge on the Positive Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the positive cone, the base gauge equals the normalizing mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a base gauge normalized by a linear functional \(\varphi\), every \(x\in K\) satisfies \(\|x\|_B=\varphi(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is linear and strictly positive on \(K\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in K:\ \|x\|_B=\varphi(x).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-mass formula.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolutely Convex Hull Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The base gauge is the gauge of the symmetric convex hull of the base and is a norm exactly when that gauge is definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a normalized convex base of a generating cone and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup(-B))\). The base gauge is the Minkowski functional \(\gamma_C\). It is finite, symmetric, subadditive, and positively homogeneous, and it is a norm exactly when \(\bigcap_{t>0}tC=\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a normalized convex base of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_B=\gamma_C(x),\qquad \|\cdot\|_B\text{ is definite}\iff\bigcap_{t>0}tC=\{0\}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation with the exact algebraic definiteness boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Pointed Base Gauge Need Not Be Definite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of definiteness for an unbounded normalized base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^2\), \[K=\{(s,t):t>0\}\cup\{0\},\qquad\varphi(s,t)=t,\qquad B=\{(s,1):s\in\mathbb R\}.\] Then \(K\) is pointed, convex, and generating, and \(B\) is its normalized base, but \[p_B(s,t)=|t|.\] Hence every nonzero \((s,0)\) lies in \(\ker p_B\), so pointedness and generatingness alone do not make the base gauge a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The open upper-half-plane cone has an unbounded normalized base whose base gauge ignores the horizontal coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_B(s,t)=|t|\quad\text{and}\quad\ker p_B=\mathbb R\times\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: A Pointed Base Gauge Need Not Be Definite

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Representation of the Base Gauge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic polar formula and continuous-dual specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the base gauge \(p_B\), \[p_B(x)=\sup\{|\ell(x)|:\ell\in X^\#,\ \sup_{b\in B}|\ell(b)|\le1\},\] where \(X^\#\) is the algebraic dual. When \(p_B\) is a norm and continuous functionals are used, its dual norm is \[p_B^*(\ell)=\sup_{b\in B}|\ell(b)|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The base gauge is represented by the polar of its symmetric base hull, and its dual norm is the largest absolute value on the base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_B(x)=\sup_{\ell:\,\sup_{b\in B}|\ell(b)|\le1}|\ell(x)|.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact restriction of the base gauge to the positive cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every \(x\in K\) satisfies \[p_B(x)=\varphi(x).\] Consequently \(p_B(b)=1\) for every \(b\in B\), and \[B=\{x\in K:p_B(x)=1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On positive elements the base gauge equals the normalizing functional, so the base is the positive unit sphere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base Gauge as a Symmetric Minkowski Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation of the decomposition gauge without assuming definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be generating, let \(B=\{u\in K:\varphi(u)=1\}\) be a normalized convex base, and set \(U=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup(-B))\). Then \[p_B(x)=\inf\{\varphi(u)+\varphi(v):u,v\in K,\ x=u-v\}=\inf\{t>0:x\in tU\}.\] Thus \(p_B\) is a finite seminorm and is a norm exactly when its kernel is trivial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The base gauge is the Minkowski functional of the symmetric convex hull of the base and its negative.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a generating convex cone in a real vector space \(X\).
\(B=\{u\in K:\varphi(u)=1\}\) is a normalized convex base for a strictly positive linear functional \(\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_B=\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}(B\cup-B)}\text{ is a finite seminorm}.

Generatingness makes the infimum finite, and pointedness makes this gauge definite under the standard base-norm hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and let \(K\subseteq V\) be a convex cone, so \(0\in K\), \(K+K\subseteq K\), and \(\lambda K\subseteq K\) for every \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic cone-induced orders on real vector spaces; topology is needed only for the closed-order and strict-interior variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone-induced relation on \(V\) is defined by \[x\preceq_K y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y-x\in K.\] Its positive cone is \(K=\{x\in V:0\preceq_Kx\}\). For \(a,b\in V\), the order interval is \[[a,b]_K:=\{x\in V:a\preceq_Kx\preceq_Kb\}=(a+K)\cap(b-K).\] The relation is a partial order precisely when \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\); without pointedness it is a preorder. If \(V\) is topological and \(K\) has nonempty interior, define \(x\prec_Ky\) by \(y-x\in\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone K defines x below y when the difference y−x belongs to K. The positive elements are exactly K. The order interval from a to b is the intersection of a+K and b−K. This relation is reflexive, transitive, translation invariant, and compatible with nonnegative scaling; it is antisymmetric exactly when K contains no nonzero line. In a topological vector space with nonempty cone interior, strict comparison means that the difference lies in the interior.
assumptions_latex: For the strict relation, \(V\) is topological and \(\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\preceq_Ky\iff y-x\in K\), with \([a,b]_K=(a+K)\cap(b-K)\) and antisymmetry equivalent to \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\preceq_Ky\iff x+K\supseteq y+K\iff y-K\supseteq x-K\).
\(K=\{x:0\preceq_Kx\}\), so the cone and the translation-invariant homogeneous preorder determine one another.
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), \(x\preceq_Ky\) is componentwise inequality.
For \(K=\mathbb{S}_+^n\), \(X\preceq_KY\) means \(Y-X\) is positive semidefinite.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(x\preceq_Ky\), then \(x+z\preceq_Ky+z\) for every \(z\in V\).
If \(x\preceq_Ky\) and \(\lambda\geq0\), then \(\lambda x\preceq_K\lambda y\).
If \(K\) is closed and \(x_j\to x\), \(y_j\to y\), and \(x_j\preceq_Ky_j\), then \(x\preceq_Ky\).
boundary_notes: A nonpointed cone induces only a preorder because elements differing by \(K\cap(-K)\) are mutually comparable.
The strict relation based on \(\operatorname{int}K\) is unavailable when the cone has empty interior in the chosen topology; relative-interior variants are separate conventions.
Cone-induced orders need not be total.

knowledge_statements.title: Topological and Boundedness Properties of Order Intervals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed finite-dimensional ordering cone, order intervals are closed and are compact when the cone is pointed; nonzero lineality makes the zero interval unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(a\le_K b\). Then \([a,b]_K\) is closed. If \(K\) is pointed, the interval is bounded and hence compact. Conversely, if every nonempty order interval is bounded, then \(K\) is pointed; in particular,
\[
[0,0]_K=K\cap(-K),
\]
so nonzero lineality makes this interval unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ pointed}\Rightarrow[a,b]_K\text{ compact},\qquad[0,0]_K=K\cap(-K).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compactness and its sharp pointedness boundary.

notation.meaning: inclusive interval for the cone-induced preorder

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Covariance of Order Intervals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order intervals translate with their endpoints and scale equivariantly by positive scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(c\in X\) and \(\lambda>0\),
\[
[a+c,b+c]_K=c+[a,b]_K,
\qquad
[\lambda a,\lambda b]_K=\lambda[a,b]_K.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space ordered by a convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [a+c,b+c]_K=c+[a,b]_K,\qquad[\lambda a,\lambda b]_K=\lambda[a,b]_K.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic covariance requiring neither topology nor pointedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Order Intervals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order interval consists of the vectors above its lower endpoint and below its upper endpoint in the cone-induced order, equivalently the intersection of the corresponding translated cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a,b\in X\) with \(a\le_K b\), the order interval with endpoints \(a\) and \(b\) is \[[a,b]_K=\{x\in X:a\le_K x\le_K b\}=(a+K)\cap(b-K).\] If \(K\) is convex, then \([a,b]_K\) is convex.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space ordered by a convex cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusive interval for the cone-induced order; no topological closedness is asserted.

notation.meaning: inclusive order interval between the endpoints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Translation and Degeneracy of Order Intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic structure valid for cone-induced preorders, including nonpointed cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex cone \(K\) and \(a\le_K b\),
\[
[a,b]_K=a+[0,b-a]_K=b-[0,b-a]_K.
\]
Moreover,
\[
[a,a]_K=a+\operatorname{lin}(K).
\]
Thus every equal-endpoint interval is a singleton exactly when \(K\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every order interval is a translated interval from zero, while equal endpoints yield the affine lineality class and need not give a singleton.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([a,b]_K=a+[0,b-a]_K=b-[0,b-a]_K,\qquad [a,a]_K=a+\operatorname{lin}(K).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Translation and Degeneracy of Order Intervals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological interval theorem for closed pointed cones in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed pointed convex cone in a finite-dimensional normed space. For every \(a\le_K b\), the order interval \([a,b]_K\) is compact. Closedness alone gives closed intervals; pointedness is essential for boundedness because nonzero lineality makes \([a,a]_K=a+\operatorname{lin}(K)\) unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order intervals of a closed pointed finite-dimensional cone are compact; nonzero lineality destroys boundedness even for equal endpoints.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed pointed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([a,b]_K\text{ is compact}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Linear Map Between Cone-Ordered Spaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((V,K)\) and \((W,L)\) be real vector spaces ordered by convex cones \(K\subseteq V\) and \(L\subseteq W\), and let \(T:V\to W\) be linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic positivity and order preservation for linear maps; no continuity, strict positivity, or cone isomorphism is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear map \(T:(V,K)\to(W,L)\) is positive, or \((K,L)\)-order preserving, when \[T(K)\subseteq L.\] Equivalently, \[\forall x,y\in V,\qquad x\preceq_Ky\Longrightarrow T x\preceq_LT y.\] The cone of positive linear maps is \[\mathcal{L}_+(V,W;K,L):=\{T\in\mathcal{L}(V,W):T(K)\subseteq L\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear map between two cone-ordered vector spaces is positive when it maps every positive source vector into the target positive cone. This is equivalent to preserving every comparison induced by the source cone. Positive maps form a convex cone under addition and multiplication by nonnegative scalars. The definition does not require the map to be injective, surjective, continuous, strictly positive, or invertible.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) and \(L\subseteq W\) are convex cones.
The orders satisfy \(x\preceq_Ky\iff y-x\in K\) and \(u\preceq_Lv\iff v-u\in L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is positive exactly when \(T(K)\subseteq L\), equivalently when \(x\preceq_Ky\Rightarrow Tx\preceq_LTy\) for all \(x,y\in V\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(T(K)\subseteq L\iff T^{-1}(L)\supseteq K\).
\(T\in\mathcal{L}_+(V,W;K,L)\iff T(y-x)\in L\) whenever \(y-x\in K\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\) and \(L=\mathbb{R}_+^m\), a matrix represents a positive map exactly when all of its entries are nonnegative.
A functional \(\varphi:V\to\mathbb{R}\) is positive exactly when \(\varphi(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in K\), i.e. \(\varphi\in K^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(S:(W,L)\to(U,M)\) and \(T:(V,K)\to(W,L)\) are positive, then \(S\circ T\) is positive.
If \(T_1,T_2\) are positive and \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\), then \(\alpha T_1+\beta T_2\) is positive.
boundary_notes: Mapping \(K\setminus\{0\}\) into \(L\setminus\{0\}\) is a stronger condition than positivity.
An order isomorphism requires bijectivity and positivity of both \(T\) and \(T^{-1}\).
Preservation of strict orders generally needs additional interior-mapping hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Cone of positive linear maps from the K-ordered space to the L-ordered space.
Cone of linear functionals nonnegative on K.
