children.title: Sum-of-Squares Cones
children.top_down_role: Algebraically generated inner cones of polynomial positivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Membership Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS membership is exactly a finite semidefinite feasibility problem obtained by coefficient matching against a PSD Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\). SOS membership is tested by introducing \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\), imposing \(Q\succeq0\), and matching every coefficient in \[p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x).\] This semidefinite system is feasible exactly when \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\), and every feasible Q is a Gram certificate.
assumptions_latex: Coefficient matching uses the monomial basis \(v_d(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: SOS membership is exactly feasibility of an SDP with a Gram matrix of order \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-degree SOS test, not an exact test for unrestricted polynomial nonnegativity.

notation.meaning: Size of the monomial vector and Gram matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Motzkin Nonnegative Non-SOS Polynomial
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Motzkin polynomial is a globally nonnegative bivariate sextic that is not a sum of squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Motzkin polynomial \[M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1\] is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) but does not belong to \(\Sigma_{2,6}\). Hence \(\Sigma_{2,6}\subsetneq P_{2,6}(\mathbb R^2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Motzkin polynomial is globally nonnegative but is not in \(\Sigma_{2,6}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical explicit witness for strict containment in the bivariate sextic regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Cones and Gram Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS polynomials form a convex inner cone of global nonnegativity and are exactly the polynomials admitting positive-semidefinite Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Sigma_{n,2d}:=\left\{p\in\mathbb R[x]_{\leq2d}:p=\sum_{j=1}^r q_j^2,\ q_j\in\mathbb R[x]_{\leq d}\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\) exactly when \[p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x)\] for some symmetric \(Q\succeq0\). The cone is convex and satisfies \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\subseteq P_{2d}(\mathbb R^n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\) is a convex cone contained in \(P_{2d}(\mathbb R^n)\), and membership is equivalent to a PSD Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globally nonnegative, degree-truncated SOS cone.

notation.meaning: Degree-2d sum-of-squares cone in n variables.
Full monomial vector through degree d.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SOS Cone as a Moment-Matrix Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual SOS cone consists exactly of coefficient functionals whose truncated moment matrices are positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(M_d(y)_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}\) for \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq d\). Under the coefficient pairing, \[\Sigma_{n,2d}^*=\{y:M_d(y)\succeq0\}.\] Thus a functional is nonnegative on every degree-2d SOS polynomial exactly when its moment matrix is positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(L_y\) is a linear functional on \(\mathbb R[x]_{\leq2d}\) represented by \(y=(y_\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}^*=\{y:M_d(y)\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-pairing dual of the fixed-degree SOS cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness and Interior of the SOS Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded-degree SOS cone is closed and full-dimensional, and its interior consists exactly of polynomials with a positive-definite Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]_{\leq2d}\) is closed, convex, and full-dimensional. Moreover, \[p\in\operatorname{int}\Sigma_{n,2d}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x)\ \text{for some }Q\succ0.\]
assumptions_latex: \(v_d\) is the full monomial vector through degree d.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\) is closed and full-dimensional, and its interior consists exactly of polynomials with a positive-definite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary topology and interior in the full finite-dimensional coefficient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert Equality Regimes for Nonnegativity and SOS
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegativity and SOS coincide only for univariate polynomials, quadratics, and bivariate quartics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For globally nonnegative polynomials of degree at most \(2d\), \[P_{n,2d}=\Sigma_{n,2d}\] if and only if \(n=1\), \(d=1\), or \((n,d)=(2,2)\). For every other pair \((n,d)\), the inclusion \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\subseteq P_{n,2d}\) is strict.
assumptions_latex: \(P_{n,2d}\) is the cone of globally nonnegative polynomials in n variables of degree at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-polynomial version of Hilbert's exceptional equality regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual SOS Cone and Moment Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-pairing dual of the truncated SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the coefficient functional \(L_y\) associated with \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\), \[y\in\Sigma_{n,2d}^*\iff L_y(q^2)\ge0\ \forall q\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\iff M_d(y)\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SOS dual consists exactly of truncated coefficient functionals with positive-semidefinite moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}^*=\{y:M_d(y)\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual SOS Cone and Moment Matrices

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness of the Truncated SOS Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coefficient topology for fixed variable count and degree bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(n,d\), the cone \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\) of sums of squares of polynomials of degree at most \(d\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed variables and degree, sums of squares form a closed convex cone of coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness of the Truncated SOS Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert Boundary for Nonnegative Forms versus Sums of Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous-form version of Hilbert's classification; it does not concern arbitrary domain-restricted positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^{\mathrm{hom}}_{n,2d}\) be the globally nonnegative real homogeneous forms of degree \(2d\), and \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{hom}}_{n,2d}\) their SOS subcone. Apart from the trivial one-variable case, \[P^{\mathrm{hom}}_{n,2d}=\Sigma^{\mathrm{hom}}_{n,2d}\] exactly when \(n=2\), \(d=1\), or \((n,2d)=(3,4)\). Outside these regimes the inclusion is strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative forms are all sums of squares only for binary forms, quadratic forms, ternary quartics, and the trivial one-variable case.
assumptions_latex: Forms are real, homogeneous, and of even degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality holds precisely in Hilbert's exceptional regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert Boundary for Nonnegative Forms versus Sums of Squares

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\) is a convex cone contained in \(P_{2d}(\mathbb{R}^n)\).

notation.meaning: The cone of sums of squares of degree at most 2d.
The vector of monomials of degree at most d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the globally nonnegative, degree-truncated sum-of-squares cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sum-of-squares cone is
\[
\Sigma_{n,2d}:=\left\{p\in\mathbb{R}[x]_{\le2d}:p=\sum_{j=1}^r q_j^2\ \text{for some }r\in\mathbb{N},\ q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x]_{\le d}\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\) exactly when there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\succeq0\) such that \(p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x)\). Consequently, \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\subseteq P_{2d}(\mathbb{R}^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sum-of-squares polynomials form a tractable inner cone of globally nonnegative polynomials and admit positive-semidefinite Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Cones

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\). To test whether \(p\in\Sigma_{n,2d}\), introduce \(Q\in\mathbb S^N\), impose \(Q\succeq0\), and equate the coefficient of every monomial in

p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x).
\]

children.title: Moment Cones
children.top_down_role: Cones generated by evaluation and moment data.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Generated Moment Cone and Its Dual
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed cone generated by bounded-degree evaluation vectors is dual to the cone of bounded-degree polynomials nonnegative on the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_{2d}(a)=(a^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\) and define \[M_{2d}(K):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{v_{2d}(a):a\in K\}.\] Under the coefficient pairing with \(p(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq2d}p_\alpha x^\alpha\), \[M_{2d}(K)^*=P_{2d}(K):=\{p:p(a)\geq0\ \text{for every }a\in K\}.\]
assumptions_latex: Polynomials and moment vectors use the monomial coefficient pairing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the closed conic hull; on noncompact K this may be larger than the unclosed cone of finite atomic moment vectors.

notation.meaning: Closed truncated moment cone generated on K.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matrix Test and Its Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representable moment sequences have positive-semidefinite moment matrices, but that condition alone can fail to yield a representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y\in M_{2d}(K)\) has a positive representing measure, then \[M_d(y):=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq d}\succeq0.\] Positive semidefiniteness is not sufficient in general: for \(n=2\) and \(d=3\), there are truncated sequences y with \(M_3(y)\succeq0\) but \(y\notin M_6(\mathbb R^2)\).
assumptions_latex: \(y\) has a positive representing measure on \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), but this condition is not sufficient for moment-cone membership in general.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary PSD test and its multivariate insufficiency boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Moment Cones and Atomic Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain the evaluation cone is closed, and every truncated moment vector has a finite atomic representation with at most one atom per coordinate dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is compact, then \[M_{2d}(K)=\operatorname{cone}\{v_{2d}(a):a\in K\}\] is closed. Every \(y\in M_{2d}(K)\) can be written as \[y=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i v_{2d}(a_i),\qquad a_i\in K,\quad w_i\geq0,\quad r\leq N.\] Equivalently, y has a positive representing measure on K supported on at most N points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{2d}(K)=\operatorname{cone}v_{2d}(K)\), and every member has an atomic representation with at most N atoms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-domain truncated moment cone; the constant coordinate is included in v_{2d}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Can Add Nonrepresentable Limit Moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the closed evaluation-cone convention from the raw conic hull and from moments of measures supported on a nonclosed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=(0,\infty)\) and \(v_1(x)=(1,x)\), \[\operatorname{cone}\{v_1(x):x\in K\}=\{(a,b):a>0,\ b>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.\] This cone is not closed: \((1,1/k)\to(1,0)\). Thus \((1,0)\) belongs to its closure, although no positive measure supported on \(K\) with total mass one has first moment zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing an evaluation cone can add limit vectors that have no representing measure on the original nonclosed domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The raw evaluation cone is nonclosed, and its closure contains the nonrepresentable vector \((1,0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated moment cone supported on a set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[K\subseteq\mathbb R^n,\qquad \mathbb N_d^n:=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:|\alpha|\le d\},\qquad [x]_d:=(x^\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n}.\] A measure is understood to be a finite nonnegative Borel measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional truncated real moment sequences of degree at most \(d\), with a prescribed support set \(K\); no compactness of \(K\) is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal R_d(K):=\left\{y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n}:\exists\mu\ge0,\ \operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq K,\ y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\ \forall\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(\mathcal R_d(K)=\operatorname{cone}\{[u]_d:u\in K\}\), where the zero sequence is represented by the zero measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degree-\(d\) moment cone over \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) consists of all truncated arrays \(y=(y_\alpha)\) that are the moments of some finite nonnegative Borel measure supported on \(K\). Thus \(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha d\mu\) for every \(|\alpha|\le d\). It is also the conic hull of the evaluation vectors \([u]_d\), \(u\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal R_d(K)=\left\{\int_K[x]_d\,d\mu:\mu\text{ is a finite nonnegative Borel measure supported on }K\right\}=\operatorname{cone}([K]_d).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[y\in\mathcal R_d(K)\iff \operatorname{meas}(y,K)\ne\varnothing.\]
\[y\in\mathcal R_d(K)\iff y=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i[u_i]_d\quad\text{for some }r<\infty,\ \lambda_i>0,\ u_i\in K.\]
special_cases_latex: \[K=\varnothing\implies\mathcal R_d(K)=\{0\}.\]
If \(K\) is compact, then \(\mathcal R_d(K)\) is closed.
For \(d=0\) and nonempty \(K\), \(\mathcal R_0(K)=\mathbb R_+\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The cone is convex and contains \(0\).
Its dual is \(\mathcal R_d(K)^*=\{p\in\mathbb R[x]_d:p(u)\ge0\ \forall u\in K\}\) under the coefficient-moment pairing whenever the dual is taken in the stated finite-dimensional spaces.
boundary_notes: For noncompact \(K\), \(\mathcal R_d(K)\) need not be closed; its closure, rather than the cone itself, generally equals the dual of the cone of polynomials nonnegative on \(K\).
Positive semidefiniteness of a truncated moment matrix alone is generally not sufficient for membership in a multivariate moment cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_{2d}(x)\) list all monomials of degree at most \(2d\), and define
\[
M_{2d}(K):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\left\{v_{2d}(a):a\in K\right\}.
\]
If \(p(x)=c^{\mathsf T}v_{2d}(x)\), then \(c\) belongs to the dual cone precisely when \(c^{\mathsf T}v_{2d}(a)=p(a)\ge0\) for every \(a\in K\). Hence
\[
M_{2d}(K)^*=P_{2d}(K).
\]

\[
M_d(y):=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq d}

satisfies \(M_d(y)\succeq0\). Equivalently, the associated functional is nonnegative on every square of degree at most \(2d\). This condition is not sufficient in general: for \(n=2\) and \(d=3\), there exist truncated sequences \(y\) with \(M_3(y)\succeq0\) but \(y\notin M_6(\mathbb R^2)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hyperbolicity cone of a homogeneous polynomial
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[V\text{ is a finite-dimensional real vector space},\quad p:V\to\mathbb R\text{ is homogeneous of degree }m,\quad e\in V,\quad p(e)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real homogeneous polynomials, using the closed-cone convention; the associated open cone is its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) if, for every \(x\in V\), the polynomial \(t\mapsto p(te-x)\) has only real roots. Writing \[p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m(t-\lambda_i(x)),\] the closed hyperbolicity cone is \[\Lambda_+(p,e):=\{x\in V:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Equivalently, it is the closure of the connected component of \(\{x:p(x)>0\}\) containing \(e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous polynomial \(p\) is hyperbolic in direction \(e\) when every univariate restriction \(t\mapsto p(te-x)\) has only real zeros. The hyperbolicity cone \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\) consists of the points whose resulting hyperbolic eigenvalues \(\lambda_i(x)\) are all nonnegative. With the closed-cone convention, it is the closure of the positivity component containing \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_{\min}(x):=\min_i\lambda_i(x)\ge0\}=\overline{\operatorname{comp}_e\{x:p(x)>0\}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(s\mapsto p(x-se)=p(e)\prod_i(\lambda_i(x)-s)\), membership is equivalent to every root of this polynomial being nonnegative.
The open hyperbolicity cone is \(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_i(x)>0\ \forall i\}\), the positivity component containing \(e\).
special_cases_latex: For \(p(x)=x_1\cdots x_n\) and \(e=\mathbf1\), \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^n\).
For \(p(X)=\det X\) on real symmetric matrices and \(e=I\), \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb S_+^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive rescaling of \(p\) does not change \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\).
The cone contains \(e\) in its interior and is a convex cone.
boundary_notes: The definition requires homogeneity; real-zero polynomials give an affine, nonhomogeneous analogue.
Changing the hyperbolicity direction within the same open hyperbolicity cone does not change the associated closed cone.
The cited source states hyperbolicity and the positivity-component construction, but uses the adjacent real-zero and rigid-convexity terminology rather than the displayed eigenvalue notation.

notation.meaning: Roots, counted with multiplicity, of \(t\mapsto p(te-x)/p(e)\).

children.title: Basic Hyperbolicity-Cone Geometry
children.top_down_role: Convex cone structure arising from hyperbolic polynomial regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolicity Cones Need Not Be Pointed
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A power of one coordinate has a halfspace hyperbolicity cone, so hyperbolicity alone does not imply pointedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p(x)=x_1^m\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) and \(e=(1,0,\ldots,0)\), \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), but \[\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:x_1\geq0\}\] has lineality space \(\{x:x_1=0\}\). Thus a hyperbolicity cone can be a nonpointed halfspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:x_1=0\}\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pointedness when the polynomial ignores ambient directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolicity and Hyperbolic Eigenvalues
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolicity means that every line parallel to the selected direction gives a real-rooted polynomial; those roots are the hyperbolic eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous polynomial \(p:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) of degree \(m\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) if \(p(e)>0\) and, for every \(x\), the polynomial \(t\mapsto p(te-x)\) has only real zeros. Its hyperbolic eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, satisfy \[p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m(t-\lambda_i(x)).\]
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a nonzero homogeneous real polynomial of degree \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hyperbolicity with respect to \(e\) is characterized by \(p(e)>0\) and real-rootedness of every \(t\mapsto p(te-x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definition for basic hyperbolicity-cone geometry.

notation.meaning: Hyperbolic eigenvalue of x relative to e

knowledge_statements.title: Translation and Scaling of Hyperbolic Eigenvalues
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolic eigenvalues translate along the hyperbolicity direction and scale positively with the vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a common ordering of the roots, \[\lambda_i(x+se)=\lambda_i(x)+s\quad(s\in\mathbb R),\qquad \lambda_i(\alpha x)=\alpha\lambda_i(x)\quad(\alpha\geq0),\] and \(\lambda_i(e)=1\).
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i(x+se)=\lambda_i(x)+s\), \(\lambda_i(\alpha x)=\alpha\lambda_i(x)\), and \(\lambda_i(e)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic spectral identities for the selected hyperbolicity direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Characterization of Lineality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineality space consists exactly of vectors whose hyperbolic eigenvalues all vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\Lambda_+(p,e)\), \[\operatorname{lin}K=K\cap(-K)=\{x:\lambda_i(x)=0\text{ for every }i\}.\] Equivalently, \(x\in\operatorname{lin}K\) exactly when \(p(te-x)=p(e)t^m\).
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_1(x)=\cdots=\lambda_m(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lineality test in terms of hyperbolic eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: Largest linear subspace contained in K

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Boundary of a Hyperbolicity Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a hyperbolicity cone, its boundary is exactly the zero set of the defining polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), with \(p(e)>0\), and let \(K=\Lambda_+(p,e)\). Then \[\partial K=K\cap\{x:p(x)=0\}.\] Equivalently, a point of \(K\) is interior exactly when all its hyperbolic eigenvalues are positive, and it is on the boundary exactly when at least one is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\Lambda_+(p,e)=\Lambda_+(p,e)\cap p^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary characterization within the selected Gårding cone.

notation.meaning: Hyperbolicity cone of p containing e

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolic Multiplicity and Boundary Strata
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional vanishing order equals the number of zero hyperbolic eigenvalues and stratifies the cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\). For \(x\in\Lambda_+(p,e)\), \[\operatorname{ord}_{t=0}p(x+te)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(x)=0\},\] counting eigenvalues with multiplicity. Thus \(x\) is interior exactly when this order is zero, and every boundary point has positive order.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ord}_{t=0}p(x+te)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity stratification by vanishing hyperbolic eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Products Give Intersections of Hyperbolicity Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying polynomials hyperbolic in a common direction intersects their hyperbolicity cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,p_2\) be homogeneous polynomials hyperbolic with respect to the same \(e\), with \(p_1(e),p_2(e)>0\). Then \(p_1p_2\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), its hyperbolic eigenvalue multiset is the union of those of the factors, and \[\Lambda_+(p_1p_2,e)=\Lambda_+(p_1,e)\cap\Lambda_+(p_2,e).\]
assumptions_latex: \(p_1\) and \(p_2\) are homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to the same \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+(p_1p_2,e)=\Lambda_+(p_1,e)\cap\Lambda_+(p_2,e)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic construction rule for hyperbolic polynomials sharing a direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Orthant and Semidefinite Hyperbolicity Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative orthant and positive-semidefinite cone are hyperbolicity cones of the coordinate product and determinant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\) and \(e=\mathbf1\), \(p\) is hyperbolic and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^n\); its hyperbolic eigenvalues are the coordinates of \(x\). For \(p(X)=\det X\) on \(\mathbb S^n\) and \(e=I\), \(p\) is hyperbolic and \(\Lambda_+(p,I)=\mathbb S_+^n\); its hyperbolic eigenvalues are the ordinary eigenvalues of \(X\).
assumptions_latex: The standard direction \(\mathbf1\) is used for the coordinate product and \(I\) for the determinant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+(\prod_i x_i,\mathbf1)=\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(\Lambda_+(\det,I)=\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two fundamental realizations of hyperbolicity-cone geometry.

notation.meaning: Cone of positive-semidefinite real symmetric matrices

knowledge_statements.title: Definite Determinantal Hyperbolicity Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A definite symmetric determinantal polynomial has the associated spectrahedral cone as its hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i\) be a real symmetric matrix pencil and suppose \(A(e)\succ0\). Then \(p(x)=\det A(x)\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:A(x)\succeq0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det A(x)\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) and \(\Lambda_+(\det A,e)=\{x:A(x)\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear symmetric-matrix pencils give a basic spectrahedral subclass of hyperbolicity cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Concavity of the Minimum Hyperbolic Eigenvalue
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least hyperbolic eigenvalue is concave, the greatest is convex, and the hyperbolicity cone is a superlevel set of the least eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and put \(\lambda_{\min}(x)=\min_i\lambda_i(x)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(x)=\max_i\lambda_i(x)\). Then \(\lambda_{\min}\) is concave, \(\lambda_{\max}\) is convex, and \[\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_{\min}(x)\geq0\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a homogeneous real polynomial hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}\) is concave, \(\lambda_{\max}\) is convex, and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{\lambda_{\min}\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental spectral convexity underlying basic hyperbolicity-cone geometry.

notation.meaning: Smallest hyperbolic eigenvalue relative to e
Largest hyperbolic eigenvalue relative to e

knowledge_statements.title: Gårding Concavity of the Hyperbolic Root
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degree-normalized hyperbolic polynomial is concave and superadditive on its hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p\) has degree \(m\), is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\), then \(p^{1/m}\) is concave on \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\). By positive homogeneity, for \(x,y\in\Lambda_+(p,e)\), \[p(x+y)^{1/m}\geq p(x)^{1/m}+p(y)^{1/m}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\), hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^{1/m}\) is concave on \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\) and \(p(x+y)^{1/m}\geq p(x)^{1/m}+p(y)^{1/m}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-normalized concavity on the basic hyperbolicity cone.
Exact conceptual membership and strict-membership test from the defining polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x\), form
\[
q_x(t)=p(te-x)/p(e).
\]
Then
\[
x\in\Lambda_+(p,e)
\iff \text{every zero of }q_x\text{ is nonnegative},
\]
and
\[
x\in\operatorname{int}\Lambda_+(p,e)
\iff \text{every zero of }q_x\text{ is positive}.
\]
Thus exact real-root isolation and sign testing decide membership whenever the coefficients of \(q_x\) are exactly available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolicity-cone membership is decided by checking whether all roots of the associated univariate polynomial are nonnegative; strict positivity certifies the interior.
assumptions_latex: The coefficients of \(q_x\) can be evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\Lambda_+(p,e)\iff\operatorname{roots}(q_x)\subseteq[0,\infty)\).

notation.meaning: The univariate polynomial encoding the hyperbolic eigenvalues of x.

knowledge_statements.title: Membership by Univariate Root Signs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hyperbolicity Cones Need Not Be Pointed or Self-Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitations of the basic convex-cone conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb R^3\), let \(p(x)=x_1x_2\) and \(e=(1,1,0)\). Then \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), but
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R.
\]
This cone contains the line \(\{(0,0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}\), so it is not pointed. Its Euclidean dual is \(\mathbb R_+^2\times\{0\}\), so it is not self-dual in \(\mathbb R^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hyperbolicity cone can have lineality and fail self-duality; a product polynomial independent of one coordinate gives an explicit example.
assumptions_latex: Duality uses the Euclidean inner product on \(\mathbb R^3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+(x_1x_2,(1,1,0))=\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R\) is neither pointed nor self-dual.
knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolicity Cones Need Not Be Pointed or Self-Dual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hyperbolicity with Respect to a Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Underlying polynomial condition for the Gårding-cone construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonzero homogeneous polynomial \(p:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) of degree \(m\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) if \(p(e)>0\) and, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the univariate polynomial
\[
t\longmapsto p(x+te)
\]
has only real zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous polynomial is hyperbolic in a direction when it is positive there and every line parallel to that direction meets its zero set only at real parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a nonzero real homogeneous polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\text{ is hyperbolic with respect to }e\iff p(x+te)\text{ is real-rooted in }t\text{ for every }x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolicity with Respect to a Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary identities governing the eigenvalue description of a hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With eigenvalues normalized by
\[
p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m(t-\lambda_i(x)),
\]
their unordered multiset satisfies
\[
\{\lambda_i(x+se)
\}_i=\{\lambda_i(x)+s\}_i,
\qquad
\{\lambda_i(\alpha x)\}_i=\{\alpha\lambda_i(x)\}_i\quad(\alpha\geq0).
\]
Consequently, \(\lambda_{\min}(x):=\min_i\lambda_i(x)\) is positively homogeneous and
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_{\min}(x)\geq0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolic eigenvalues translate along the hyperbolicity direction and scale nonnegatively, so the cone is the nonnegative superlevel set of the smallest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(x+se)=\lambda_{\min}(x)+s\) and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_{\min}(x)\geq0\}\).

notation.meaning: The smallest hyperbolic eigenvalue of x relative to e.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolic Eigenvalue Translation and Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concavity of the Smallest Hyperbolic Eigenvalue
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral convexity principle underlying basic hyperbolicity-cone geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), then
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)
\geq
\theta\lambda_{\min}(x)+(1-\theta)\lambda_{\min}(y)
\]
for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(0\leq\theta\leq1\). Thus \(\lambda_{\min}\) is concave, and every superlevel set \(\{x:\lambda_{\min}(x)\geq c\}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest hyperbolic eigenvalue is concave, giving a spectral explanation for convexity of the hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}\) is concave on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Concavity of the Smallest Hyperbolic Eigenvalue

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree \(m\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\) is a closed convex cone, and its interior is the connected component of \(\{x:p(x)>0\}\) containing \(e\).

notation.meaning: The ordered hyperbolic eigenvalues relative to e.
The hyperbolicity cone of p containing e.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the finite-dimensional Gårding-cone geometry in eigenvalue form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the real numbers \(\lambda_i(x)\) by
\[
p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m\bigl(t-\lambda_i(x)\bigr),
\]
and set
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e):=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\ \text{for all }i\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\) is a closed convex cone. Its interior is \(\{x:\lambda_i(x)>0\ \text{for all }i\}\), equivalently the connected component of \(\{x:p(x)>0\}\) containing \(e\). Moreover, \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to every point in that interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hyperbolic polynomial determines a closed convex cone whose interior is the positive component containing the hyperbolicity direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Basic Hyperbolicity-Cone Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role and local geometry are appropriate, but the convexity, connected-component characterization, and change-of-hyperbolicity-direction conclusion require an authoritative hyperbolicity reference with a theorem or page locator.

children.title: Derivative-Cone Relaxation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Nested algebraic cone families derived from directional differentiation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[p:V\to\mathbb R\text{ is homogeneous of degree }m\ge1\text{ and hyperbolic with respect to }e,\qquad D_e^kp(x):=\left.\frac{d^k}{dt^k}p(x+te)\right|_{t=0}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact derivative relaxations generated by repeated differentiation in the fixed hyperbolicity direction \(e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=0,1,\ldots,m-1\), define \(p_e^{(k)}:=D_e^kp\) and the \(k\)-th derivative cone by \[\Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e):=\Lambda_+(p_e^{(k)},e).\] The derivative-cone relaxation hierarchy is the nested family \[\Lambda_+(p,e)=\Lambda_+^{(0)}(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(1)}(p,e)\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(m-1)}(p,e).\] Each member is the hyperbolicity cone of a degree-\(m-k\) directional derivative and is therefore a conic relaxation of the original cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with a degree-\(m\) polynomial \(p\) hyperbolic in direction \(e\), differentiate \(p\) repeatedly in that same direction. The hyperbolicity cone of the \(k\)-th derivative \(D_e^kp\) is the \(k\)-th derivative cone. These cones form nested outer relaxations, beginning with the original hyperbolicity cone and ending, before the constant derivative, with a halfspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e):=\Lambda_+(D_e^kp,e),\qquad \Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(k+1)}(p,e)\quad(0\le k<m-1).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m(t-\lambda_i(x))\), then \(x\in\Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e)\) precisely when all roots associated with \(D_e^kp\) are nonnegative.
Multiplying \(D_e^kp\) by a positive scalar leaves \(\Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e)\) unchanged.
special_cases_latex: For \(p(X)=\det X\) and \(e=I\), the derivatives are scalar multiples of the elementary symmetric polynomials of the eigenvalues of \(X\).
The last nonconstant derivative \(D_e^{m-1}p\) is linear, so \(\Lambda_+^{(m-1)}(p,e)\) is a closed halfspace containing \(e\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any conic program over \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\) obtains a sequence of outer conic relaxations by replacing its cone with \(\Lambda_+^{(k)}(p,e)\).
The index \(k=0\) reproduces the original cone; the hierarchy normally stops at \(m-1\), since \(D_e^mp\) is constant.
boundary_notes: Differentiation must use a hyperbolicity direction; arbitrary directional derivatives need not define this hierarchy.
The available inspected source supports the underlying hyperbolic-polynomial definition but not the nested derivative-cone result with an exact locator.

notation.meaning: The \(k\)-fold directional derivative of \(p\) in direction \(e\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hierarchy is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for preservation of hyperbolicity under directional differentiation or for the nested cone inclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Inequality Membership Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in the kth derivative cone is equivalent to nonnegativity of all derivatives from order k through m−1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^{(k)}=D_e^kp\), and suppose it is nonzero and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\). Then \[x\in\Lambda_+(p^{(k)},e)\iff D_e^jp(x)\geq0\quad\text{for }j=k,k+1,\ldots,m-1.\] The last derivative \(D_e^mp=m!p(e)>0\) is automatic.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
\(D_e^kp\) is nonzero and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\Lambda_+(D_e^kp,e)\iff D_e^jp(x)\geq0\) for \(j=k,\ldots,m-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite algebraic membership certificate for a fixed derivative cone.

notation.meaning: kth derivative of p along e

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Derivative-Inequality Interior Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is interior to the kth derivative cone exactly when every nonconstant derivative from level k onward is strictly positive there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) have degree \(m\), let \(p^{(k)}=D_e^kp\) be nonzero and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and set \(K_k=\Lambda_+(p^{(k)},e)\). Then \[x\in\operatorname{int}K_k\iff D_e^jp(x)>0\quad\text{for }j=k,k+1,\ldots,m-1.\]
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
\(D_e^kp\) is nonzero and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{int}\Lambda_+(D_e^kp,e)\iff D_e^jp(x)>0\) for \(j=k,\ldots,m-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite strict-inequality certificate for the interior of a fixed derivative cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Values as Elementary Symmetric Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated derivatives along the hyperbolicity direction are elementary symmetric polynomials of the hyperbolic eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p(te-x)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^m(t-\lambda_i(x))\), then for \(0\leq k\leq m\), \[D_e^kp(x)=k!\,p(e)\,e_{m-k}(\lambda_1(x),\ldots,\lambda_m(x)),\] where \(e_j\) is the jth elementary symmetric polynomial and \(e_0=1\).
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_e^kp(x)=k!p(e)e_{m-k}(\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral representation of repeated derivatives in the hyperbolicity direction.

notation.meaning: Vector of hyperbolic eigenvalues of x

knowledge_statements.title: Interlacing of Directional-Derivative Roots
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive derivatives along the hyperbolicity direction have interlacing real roots on every parallel line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), set \(f_x(t)=p(te-x)\). For every \(0\le k<m-1\), the zeros of \(f_x^{(k+1)}\) interlace those of \(f_x^{(k)}\), counting multiplicities. Since \(f_x^{(k)}(t)=D_e^kp(te-x)\), every member of this fixed-direction derivative sequence is real-rooted on each line parallel to \(e\).
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The zeros of \(t\mapsto D_e^{k+1}p(te-x)\) interlace those of \(t\mapsto D_e^kp(te-x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root interlacing along the fixed hyperbolicity direction; hierarchy-wide nesting belongs to the sibling hierarchy leaf.

notation.meaning: Univariate restriction of p to the line through -x parallel to e

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_e^k p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+(D_e^k p,e)\).

notation.meaning: The k-th directional derivative in direction e.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses repeated differentiation in the fixed hyperbolicity direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0\le k\le m-1\), let \(p^{(k)}:=D_e^k p\) and define the derivative cone
\[
\Lambda_+^{(k)}:=\Lambda_+\bigl(p^{(k)},e\bigr).
\]
The polynomial \(p^{(k)}\) is homogeneous of degree \(m-k\), is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and satisfies
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(k)}.
\]
Thus each derivative cone is a convex conic relaxation of the original hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated differentiation along the hyperbolicity direction produces lower-degree hyperbolic polynomials whose cones relax the original cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolic Derivative Cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The derivative-cone construction fits the leaf, but preservation of hyperbolicity and cone containment are substantive results lacking a cited theorem or section locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Exterior Directions Need Not Preserve Hyperbolicity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the orthant polynomial, differentiation along an exterior direction produces a polynomial vanishing at the original hyperbolicity direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\), \(e=(1,1)\), and \(v=(1,-1)\). Then \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), but \[D_vp(x)=x_2-x_1,\qquad D_vp(e)=0.\] Hence \(D_vp\) is not hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) under the convention requiring a positive value at \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_vp(e)=0\), so \(D_vp\) is not hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure when the differentiation direction is not in the hyperbolicity-cone interior.

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of p along v

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Rescaling Invariance of Derivative Directions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling of a derivative direction rescales the polynomial but leaves its hyperbolicity cone unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), \[D_{\alpha v}^kp=\alpha^kD_v^kp.\] Hence, whenever these derivative polynomials are hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), \[\Lambda_+(D_{\alpha v}^kp,e)=\Lambda_+(D_v^kp,e).\] The derivative-cone variant depends on the ray \(\mathbb R_{++}v\), not the normalization of \(v\).
assumptions_latex: \(D_v^kp\) is nonzero and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+(D_{\alpha v}^kp,e)=\Lambda_+(D_v^kp,e)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of derivative directions defining the same cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Commutation of Mixed Directional Derivatives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed directional derivatives commute, so their polynomial is independent of differentiation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial \(p\), directions \(u,v\), and nonnegative integers \(r,s\), \[D_u^rD_v^sp=D_v^sD_u^rp.\] Thus the mixed derivative polynomial depends on the selected directions and multiplicities, not their order.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a real polynomial and \(u,v\) are fixed directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_u^rD_v^sp=D_v^sD_u^rp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic consistency of variants using several derivative directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Covariance of Directional Derivative Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible changes of coordinates transport directional derivative cones together with their polynomials and directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:V\to W\) be invertible, set \(\widetilde p=p\circ L^{-1}\), \(\widetilde e=Le\), and \(\widetilde v=Lv\). Then \[D_{\widetilde v}^k\widetilde p=(D_v^kp)\circ L^{-1}.\] Whenever the indicated derivative polynomials are hyperbolic, \[\Lambda_+(D_{\widetilde v}^k\widetilde p,\widetilde e)=L\Lambda_+(D_v^kp,e).\]
assumptions_latex: \(L:V\to W\) is an invertible linear map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{Lv}^k(p\circ L^{-1})=(D_v^kp)\circ L^{-1}\), with the corresponding hyperbolicity cones related by \(L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate covariance of directional variants under invertible linear transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Interior-Direction Derivative Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed differentiation in interior cone directions preserves hyperbolicity and gives an outer relaxation independently of differentiation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and let \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\operatorname{int}\Lambda_+(p,e)\), where \(1\le k<m\). Then \[q=D_{v_k}\cdots D_{v_1}p\] is nonzero, homogeneous of degree \(m-k\), hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \[\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+(q,e).\] The polynomial \(q\) is independent of the order of the listed directions.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{v_k}\cdots D_{v_1}p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), has degree \(m-k\), and its cone contains \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive differentiation in possibly distinct directions from the original cone interior.

notation.meaning: Mixed directional derivative with the listed directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure for an Unrestricted Differentiation Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that derivative hyperbolicity with respect to the distinguished direction is not guaranteed outside the hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\), \(e=(1,1)\), and \(v=(1,-1)\). Then \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^2\), but \[D_vp(x)=x_2-x_1,\qquad D_vp(e)=0.\] Hence \(D_vp\) is not hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction outside the original hyperbolicity cone can produce a derivative polynomial that is not hyperbolic with respect to the distinguished direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\notin\Lambda_+(p,e)\quad\text{and}\quad D_vp(e)=0,\text{ so }D_vp\text{ is not hyperbolic with respect to }e.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure for an Unrestricted Differentiation Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the normalization freedom in the selected differentiation direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\alpha>0\), \(D_{\alpha v}^k p=\alpha^kD_v^k p\). Whenever \(D_v^k p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), \[\Lambda_+(D_{\alpha v}^k p,e)=\Lambda_+(D_v^k p,e).\] Thus the derivative cone depends on the positive ray generated by \(v\), not its normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling of the differentiation direction scales the derivative polynomial but leaves its hyperbolicity cone unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(D_v^k p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_{\alpha v}^k p=\alpha^kD_v^k p\quad\text{and}\quad\Lambda_+(D_{\alpha v}^k p,e)=\Lambda_+(D_v^k p,e).

notation.meaning: The kth repeated directional derivative of p along v.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Ray Invariance of Derivative Directions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the interior-direction result to directions on the closed hyperbolicity cone while recording the possible zero-polynomial degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), with \(p(e)>0\), and let \(v\in\Lambda_+(p,e)\). For \(1\leq k\leq\deg p-1\), \(D_v^k p\) is either identically zero or is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) and satisfies \[\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+(D_v^k p,e).\] Interior directions exclude the zero-polynomial alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions on the cone boundary still yield a containing derivative cone whenever the derivative is nonzero, but boundary directions can make a derivative vanish identically.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_v^k p\equiv0\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl(D_v^k p\text{ is hyperbolic with respect to }e\text{ and }\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+(D_v^k p,e)\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Direction Extension and Degeneracy

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\), hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_v^k p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+(D_v^k p,e)\).

notation.meaning: The k-th directional derivative in direction v.
The derivative cone generated by direction v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricts derivative directions to the interior of the original hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(v\in\operatorname{int}\Lambda_+(p,e)\), define
\[
q_{k,v}:=D_v^k p,
\qquad
\Lambda_+^{(k,v)}:=\Lambda_+(q_{k,v},e).
\]
For \(1\le k\le m-1\), the polynomial \(q_{k,v}\) is homogeneous of degree \(m-k\) and hyperbolic with respect to \(e\). Its hyperbolicity cone contains the original cone:
\[
\Lambda_+(p,e)\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(k,v)}.
\]
Taking \(v=e\) recovers the standard derivative-cone construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiating along any interior cone direction yields directional derivative cones that contain the original hyperbolicity cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Derivative Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the directional-variant leaf, but hyperbolicity with respect to e and containment for every interior direction v are source-sensitive claims with no cited authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Nesting of Dual Derivative Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualization reverses the derivative-cone hierarchy: larger primal relaxation cones have smaller dual cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \[K_0\subseteq K_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_{m-1}\] are derivative cones and \(K_k^*=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in K_k\}\), then \[K_0^*\supseteq K_1^*\supseteq\cdots\supseteq K_{m-1}^*.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_{m-1}\) are convex cones in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_0^*\supseteq\cdots\supseteq K_{m-1}^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual order induced by an established primal derivative-cone hierarchy.

notation.meaning: Positive dual of the kth derivative cone

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Bounds from Nested Derivative Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested derivative cones give nested feasible regions and nonincreasing minimization values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_0\subseteq K_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_{m-1}\), and define \[F_k:=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\in K_k\},\qquad v_k:=\inf_{x\in F_k}\langle c,x\rangle.\] Then \(F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_{m-1}\) and \[v_0\geq v_1\geq\cdots\geq v_{m-1}.\]
assumptions_latex: All levels use the same affine equations and linear objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k\subseteq F_{k+1}\) and \(v_k\geq v_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization consequence conditional on the nested outer-relaxation order.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Bounds Along the Derivative-Cone Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the optimization-bound consequence of the nested derivative cones without asserting exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_k=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\in\Lambda_+^{(k)}\}\) and \(v_k=\inf_{x\in F_k}\langle c,x\rangle\), allowing extended-real values. Then \[F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_{m-1},\qquad v_0\geq v_1\geq\cdots\geq v_{m-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively larger derivative cones produce nested feasible sets and successively weaker lower bounds for minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_k\subseteq F_{k+1}\quad\text{and}\quad v_k\geq v_{k+1}\quad(0\leq k<m-1).

notation.meaning: The affine feasible set intersected with the kth derivative cone.
The extended-real minimization value at hierarchy level k.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Bounds Along the Derivative-Cone Hierarchy

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is homogeneous of degree \(m\), hyperbolic with respect to \(e\), and \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_+^{(0)}\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(1)}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(m-1)}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: The k-th directional derivative along e.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the nesting of fixed-direction derivative relaxations through degree one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(p^{(k)}:=D_e^k p\) and \(\Lambda_+^{(k)}:=\Lambda_+(p^{(k)},e)\) for \(0\le k\le m-1\). Interlacing of the real roots under differentiation gives the nested sequence
\[
\Lambda_+^{(0)}\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(1)}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Lambda_+^{(m-1)}.
\]
Here \(\Lambda_+^{(0)}=\Lambda_+(p,e)\), while \(p^{(m-1)}\) is linear, so the last nontrivial derivative cone is a halfspace. If \(D_e^m p\) is included, it is the positive constant \(m!p(e)\) and its cone is \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive directional derivatives form nested outer relaxations, ending with a halfspace and, after the final derivative, the whole space.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Relaxation Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nesting property and terminal halfspace description fit the leaf, but the hierarchy and final-derivative conventions lack a cited theorem or section locator. The appeal to interlacing is proof-like.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictness Already Occurs for the Orthant Polynomial
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the two-variable orthant polynomial, the first derivative cone is a halfspace strictly larger than the orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\) and \(e=(1,1)\). Then \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^2\), while \[D_ep(x)=x_1+x_2,\qquad \Lambda_+(D_ep,e)=\{x:x_1+x_2\geq0\}.\] Hence \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\subsetneq\Lambda_+(D_ep,e)\); for example, \((-1,2)\) lies only in the derivative cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R_+^2\subsetneq\{x:x_1+x_2\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing strict derivative-cone enlargement.

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of p along e

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Exact Derivative Relaxation with No Optimizer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A determinant-product hyperbolicity cone and its first derivative cone have an affine slice on which both problems share a finite unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(V=\mathbb R\times\mathbb S^2\), let \(p(z,X)=z\det X\) and \(e=(1,I)\). Then \(K_0=\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb S_+^2\). For \(q=D_ep=\det X+z\operatorname{tr}X\), set \(K_1=\Lambda_+(q,e)\). Its slice at \(z=0\) is \[K_1\cap(\{0\}\times\mathbb S^2)=\{0\}\times\mathbb S_+^2.\] Impose \(z=0\) and \(X_{12}=1\), and minimize \(X_{11}\). The original and derivative-relaxed feasible sets coincide; both infima equal \(0\), and neither infimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: Both problems impose \(z=0\) and \(X_{12}=1\) and minimize \(X_{11}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf(P_0)=\inf(P_1)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}(P_0)=\operatorname*{argmin}(P_1)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Genuine derivative-cone instance showing that equal finite infima need not yield optimizer recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Exactness Without Attainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value exactness means equality of infima and remains meaningful when neither problem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested feasible sets \(F_0\subseteq F_k\) and extended-real infima \[v_j:=\inf_{x\in F_j}\langle c,x\rangle,\] the level-\(k\) relaxation is value-exact when \(v_k=v_0\). This definition makes no assertion that either infimum is attained and is weaker than optimizer-recovery exactness.
assumptions_latex: Both values use the same extended-real minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{value-exact at level }k\iff v_k=v_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-only exactness convention valid whether or not either problem has a minimizer.

notation.meaning: Infimum over the level-j feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Solution-Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong solution-set exactness requires the original and relaxed problems to have exactly the same minimizers; with minimizers present, it is stronger than equality of optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested feasible sets \(F_0\subseteq F_k\) with a common linear objective, write \(S_j=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F_j}\langle c,x\rangle\), allowing \(S_j=\varnothing\). The relaxation is strongly solution-set exact when \[S_k=S_0.\] If this common set is nonempty, strong solution-set exactness implies value exactness and recovery of every relaxed optimizer. Equality of values alone need not imply equality or nonemptiness of the solution sets.
assumptions_latex: \(F_0\subseteq F_k\) use the same linear objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{strong solution-set exactness}\iff S_k=S_0\); if \(S_0=S_k\ne\varnothing\), then \(v_k=v_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong exactness convention distinct from value equality and existence of one recoverable optimizer.

notation.meaning: Minimizer set at hierarchy level j

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative relaxation is feasible-set exact when its affine slice adds no feasible points, which guarantees exactness for every common objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an original feasible set \(F_0\) and derivative-relaxed feasible set \(F_k\) with \(F_0\subseteq F_k\), level \(k\) is feasible-set exact when \[F_k=F_0.\] This implies equality of optimal values and minimizer sets for every common objective for which those objects are defined, whereas one objective may be value-exact even when \(F_0\subsetneq F_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(F_0\subseteq F_k\) are the original and level-k feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{feasible-set exactness}\iff F_k=F_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-independent exactness convention stronger than value equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Equality versus Instance Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone equality guarantees exactness for all problems, but one problem may remain exact even when the derivative cone is strictly larger.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K_0\subseteq K_k\), equality \(K_0=K_k\) leaves every affine conic optimization problem unchanged. The converse fails for a fixed instance: even if \(K_0\subsetneq K_k\), its affine slice can satisfy \[\{x:Ax=b\}\cap K_0=\{x:Ax=b\}\cap K_k,\] or a selected objective can have the same value and an original-feasible minimizer on both sets. Thus cone equality is sufficient for universal instance exactness but is stronger than exactness of one instance.
assumptions_latex: \(K_0\subseteq K_k\) are cones in the same finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_0=K_k\) implies universal exactness, while fixed-instance exactness need not imply \(K_0=K_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes structural cone equality from exactness of one optimization instance.
Clarifies the relation between value preservation and optimizer recovery under the attainment assumptions of the immutable seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F_0\subseteq F_k\) and the original minimization problem attains its value. Then \[v_k=v_0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F_k}\langle c,x\rangle\cap F_0\neq\varnothing.\] Consequently, under the seed's assumption that both problems attain, value equality already guarantees an original-feasible relaxed optimizer.

Then \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\mathbb R_+^2\), whereas \(D_ep(x)=x_1+x_2\) and \[\Lambda_+(D_ep,e)=\{x:x_1+x_2\geq0\}\supsetneq\mathbb R_+^2.\] For \(\min x_1\) subject to \(x_2=1\), the original problem has value \(0\) at \((0,1)\), while the derivative-cone relaxation has value \(-1\) at \((-1,1)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Automorphism, homogeneity, symmetry, and spectral cone hierarchy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[E\text{ is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space},\qquad K\subseteq E\text{ is a closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An organizational hierarchy for proper finite-dimensional cones; the term names a package of nested structural classes rather than a single universally standardized cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\operatorname{Aut}(K):=\{g\in\operatorname{GL}(E):gK=K\}\). The automorphism-spectral hierarchy assigns to \(K\) the successive properties \[K\text{ homogeneous}\iff \operatorname{Aut}(K)\text{ acts transitively on }\operatorname{int}K,\] \[K\text{ symmetric}\iff K\text{ is homogeneous and }K=K^*,\] and, for a symmetric cone, a Euclidean Jordan algebra structure \((E,\circ,e)\) for which \[K=\{x\circ x:x\in E\},\qquad x=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i c_i\] in a Jordan frame. Thus the hierarchy progresses from linear cone symmetries, through homogeneous and self-dual cones, to Jordan-algebraic spectral data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper cone \(K\), its invertible linear stabilizer is \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\). The cone is homogeneous when this group acts transitively on its interior. It is symmetric when it is also self-dual for the chosen inner product. Symmetric cones admit a Euclidean Jordan algebra realization as cones of squares, in which elements possess eigenvalues and Jordan-frame decompositions. These linked levels form the automorphism-spectral hierarchy used here.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{\text{symmetric cones}\}\subseteq\{\text{homogeneous cones}\}\subseteq\{\text{proper cones with their automorphism actions}\},\qquad K\text{ symmetric}\Longleftrightarrow K=\mathcal K(\mathfrak J)\text{ for some Euclidean Jordan algebra }\mathfrak J.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Homogeneity means that for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{int}K\), some \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) satisfies \(gx=y\).
At the spectral level, \(x\in K\) exactly when every Jordan eigenvalue \(\lambda_i(x)\) is nonnegative.
special_cases_latex: The orthant \(\mathbb R_+^n\), Lorentz cones, and positive-semidefinite matrix cones are symmetric.
A homogeneous cone that admits no compatible self-duality remains in the homogeneous level but not the symmetric level.
immediate_consequences_latex: Automorphisms preserve \(\operatorname{int}K\), \(\partial K\), faces, and all orbit-defined strata.
Direct products correspond to direct sums of Euclidean Jordan algebras; irreducible factors give the atomic spectral classes.
boundary_notes: Not every proper cone is homogeneous, and not every homogeneous cone is symmetric.
Jordan eigenvalues in this hierarchy belong to the symmetric-cone level; a general homogeneous nonsymmetric cone need not carry such a spectral calculus.
The hierarchy title is organizational terminology, not a separately standardized object in the cited source.

notation.meaning: Group of invertible linear maps preserving \(K\).
Dual cone with respect to the fixed inner product.
Cone of squares of a Euclidean Jordan algebra.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear automorphism of a convex cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[E\text{ is a finite-dimensional real vector space},\qquad K\subseteq E\text{ is a convex cone}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible linear, rather than affine or nonlinear, cone symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone automorphism of \(K\) is an invertible linear map \(g:E\to E\) satisfying \[g(K)=K.\] Equivalently, \(g(K)\subseteq K\) and \(g^{-1}(K)\subseteq K\). If \(K\) is closed and full-dimensional, every such \(g\) also satisfies \[g(\operatorname{int}K)=\operatorname{int}K,\qquad g(\partial K)=\partial K,\] and maps every face \(F\unlhd K\) to the face \(gF\unlhd K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone automorphism is an invertible linear transformation \(g\) whose image of the cone \(K\) is exactly \(K\). Requiring equality is equivalent to requiring both \(g\) and its inverse to preserve the cone. For closed full-dimensional cones, automorphisms preserve the interior, boundary, facial relation, and dimensions of faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\iff g\in\operatorname{GL}(E)\text{ and }gK=K.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\iff gK\subseteq K\text{ and }g^{-1}K\subseteq K.\]
For a proper cone, \(g\) is an order isomorphism for \(x\preceq_Ky\iff y-x\in K\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), positive diagonal scalings and coordinate permutations are automorphisms.
For \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\), every congruence \(X\mapsto PXP^T\) with \(P\) nonsingular is a cone automorphism.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F\) is an extreme ray or an exposed face of \(K\), then \(gF\) has the same respective property.
Automorphisms preserve the dimensions of faces and the inclusion order of the face lattice.
boundary_notes: A linear map satisfying only \(gK\subseteq K\) is cone-preserving but need not be an automorphism.
Translations are excluded even if they preserve some affine slice of a cone.
For cones not spanning \(E\), the definition may instead be applied on \(\operatorname{span}K\).

notation.meaning: Group of invertible linear maps on \(E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Contragredient Automorphisms of the Dual Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse adjoints identify the automorphism groups of a closed cone and its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space. Then every \(T\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) satisfies \(T^{-\top}K^*=K^*\), and \[\Phi:\operatorname{Aut}(K)\to\operatorname{Aut}(K^*),\qquad \Phi(T)=T^{-\top},\] is a group isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\cong\operatorname{Aut}(K^*)\) via \(T\mapsto T^{-\top}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural isomorphism between automorphism groups of a closed cone and its nonnegative dual.

knowledge_statements.title: Automorphisms Preserve Cone Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone automorphisms preserve relative interior, relative boundary, the facial lattice, face dimensions, extreme rays, and facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\), then \[T(\operatorname{ri}K)=\operatorname{ri}K,\qquad T(\operatorname{rbd}K)=\operatorname{rbd}K.\] For every face \(F\unlhd K\), \(T(F)\unlhd K\), and \(F\mapsto T(F)\) is an inclusion- and dimension-preserving automorphism of the facial lattice. Consequently, extreme rays and facets are preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\mapsto T(F)\) is a dimension-preserving automorphism of the facial lattice of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic topology and facial geometry preserved by an invertible linear cone automorphism.

notation.meaning: F is a face of K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central dilation subgroup present for every cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\lambda>0\), \(\lambda I\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\). These dilations form a central subgroup isomorphic to \((\mathbb R_{++},\cdot)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cone automorphism group contains the central subgroup of positive scalar dilations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\lambda I:\lambda>0\}\subseteq Z(\operatorname{Aut}(K))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Scalar Automorphisms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness is relative to the ambient general linear group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is closed, then \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) is a closed subgroup of \(\operatorname{GL}(V)\). By the closed-subgroup theorem, it is a finite-dimensional Lie group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The automorphism group of a closed finite-dimensional cone is a closed matrix subgroup and hence a Lie group.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq V\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\leq\operatorname{GL}(V)\) is closed and is a Lie group.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Automorphism group of a convex cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[E\text{ is a finite-dimensional real vector space and }K\subseteq E\text{ is a convex cone}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The full linear stabilizer of a cone, equipped with composition; orthogonal automorphism subgroups are nearby but distinct objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The automorphism group of \(K\) is \[\operatorname{Aut}(K):=\{g\in\operatorname{GL}(E):g(K)=K\}.\] Its multiplication is composition, its identity is \(I_E\), and the inverse of each \(g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) again belongs to \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\). It acts on \(K\) by \((g,x)\mapsto gx\), and the stabilizer of \(x\in K\) is \[\operatorname{Aut}(K)_x:=\{g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K):gx=x\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) is the subgroup of the general linear group consisting of all invertible linear transformations that map \(K\) onto itself. Composition supplies the group operation. The group acts naturally on the cone; each point has an orbit and a stabilizer subgroup.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{Aut}(K)\le\operatorname{GL}(E),\qquad \operatorname{Aut}(K)\cdot x=\{gx:g\in\operatorname{Aut}(K)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) is the setwise stabilizer of \(K\) under the natural action of \(\operatorname{GL}(E)\) on subsets of \(E\).
If \(K\) is proper, \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) is the group of linear order automorphisms of the order induced by \(K\).
special_cases_latex: \[\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb S_+^n)=\{X\mapsto PXP^T:P\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\},\] with distinct matrices \(P\) possibly inducing the same transformation.
The orthogonal automorphism group is \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\cap O(E)\), generally a proper subgroup.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every orbit is contained wholly in \(\operatorname{int}K\), \(\partial K\), or \(\{0\}\), according to the location of its representative.
The cone is homogeneous exactly when the action of \(\operatorname{Aut}(K)\) on \(\operatorname{int}K\) is transitive.
boundary_notes: The group depends on the ambient linear representation of \(K\); linearly isomorphic cones have conjugate automorphism groups.
The orthogonal subgroup depends additionally on a chosen inner product.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition of a cone into automorphism orbits
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[K\subseteq E\text{ is a convex cone},\qquad G:=\operatorname{Aut}(K).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic orbit stratification under the full linear automorphism group; no claim is made that each orbit equals a face or a rank stratum for arbitrary cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define an equivalence relation on \(K\) by \[x\sim_Gy\iff \exists g\in G\text{ such that }y=gx.\] The automorphism-orbit stratification is the disjoint partition \[K=\bigsqcup_{[x]\in K/G}G\cdot x,\qquad G\cdot x:=\{gx:g\in G\}.\] The isotropy subgroup is \(G_x:=\{g\in G:gx=x\}\), and the orbit is canonically represented as the homogeneous space \(G/G_x\) at the level of group actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two points of \(K\) belong to the same automorphism stratum when an automorphism of \(K\) carries one to the other. The resulting equivalence classes are the orbits \(G\cdot x\), and their disjoint union is the cone. Each orbit has a stabilizer \(G_x\); orbit invariants include interior or boundary location and all facial properties preserved by automorphisms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K/G:=\{G\cdot x:x\in K\},\qquad K=\bigsqcup_{\mathcal O\in K/G}\mathcal O.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\sim_Gy\) if and only if \(x\) and \(y\) have the same image in the quotient set \(K/G\).
For a fixed representative \(x\), the orbit map \(g\mapsto gx\) has fibers equal to right cosets of \(G_x\).
special_cases_latex: If \(K\) is homogeneous, \(\operatorname{int}K\) is one orbit.
For \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\), congruence orbits are indexed by matrix rank, so \(K=\bigsqcup_{r=0}^n\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{rank}X=r\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The origin is always a singleton orbit.
No orbit can meet both \(\operatorname{int}K\) and \(\partial K\).
Automorphism-invariant quantities are constant on each orbit.
boundary_notes: For a general cone, orbit classes need not coincide with relative interiors of faces.
The word “stratification” is used for the orbit partition; additional regularity or frontier axioms require separate hypotheses.
The inspected source establishes automorphism groups and transitivity but does not present this quotient construction under the exact node title.
