children.title: Perspective Conjugacy Interface
children.top_down_role: Dual and support representations associated with homogenized epigraph geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and define its Fenchel conjugate by \(f^*(u)=\sup_x(\langle x,u\rangle-f(x))\). Let \(P_f\) be the positive-scale perspective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition uses the product-space pairing between primal scale-state coordinates and dual intercept-slope coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[C_f:=\{(\mu,u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathcal H:\mu+f^*(u)\le0\}.\] The perspective conjugacy interface is the identity \[P_f^*=\iota_{C_f},\] where \(\iota_{C_f}\) is zero on \(C_f\) and \(+\infty\) outside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual object associated with a perspective is the closed convex set of intercept-slope pairs whose intercept plus the source conjugate is nonpositive. The conjugate of the perspective is precisely the indicator of this set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C_f=\{(\mu,u):\mu+f^*(u)\le0\},\qquad P_f^*(\mu,u)=\iota_{C_f}(\mu,u).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[(\mu,u)\in C_f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mu+\langle z,u\rangle\le f(z)\ \text{for every }z\in\mathcal H.\]
\[C_f=\operatorname{epi}f^*\ \text{after the coordinate reflection }(\mu,u)\mapsto(u,-\mu).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(f=\iota_D\) for a nonempty set \(D\), then \(C_f=\{(\mu,u):\mu+\sigma_D(u)\le0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever the closed perspective equals its biconjugate, it is the support function of \(C_f\).
The dual feasibility boundary is the graph \(\mu=-f^*(u)\); strict inequality gives noncontacting dual points.
boundary_notes: The formula concerns Fenchel conjugacy with the pairing \(\xi\mu+\langle x,u\rangle\).
No differentiability or strict convexity of \(f\) is required.

notation.meaning: Closed convex dual set associated with the perspective.
Extended-real indicator of the dual set.

children.title: Epigraph-Cone Dual Representations
children.top_down_role: Dual objects associated with perspective epigraph cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Epigraph-Coefficient Face of the Dual Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the epigraph-height coefficient vanishes, dual membership reduces to a support bound over the source domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the seed's positive-dual convention, a triple \((y,\alpha,0)\) belongs to \(K_f^*\) exactly when
\[
\alpha+\langle y,u\rangle\geq0
\quad\text{for every }u\in\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\alpha\geq\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(-y).
\]
Thus a finite \(\alpha\) exists for a given \(y\) exactly when \(-y\) belongs to the barrier cone of \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,\alpha,0)\in K_f^*\iff\alpha\geq\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(-y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary regime complementary to the seed's positive-coefficient conjugate formula.

notation.meaning: support function of the effective domain of f

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph-Cone Dual Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of the closed perspective epigraph cone consists of triples whose associated affine-conjugate inequality is nonnegative on the entire source epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K_f:=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(u,1,r):u\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ r\geq f(u)\}.
\]
Using \(K_f^*:=\{z:\langle z,w\rangle\geq0\ \text{for all}\ w\in K_f\}\),
\[
K_f^*=\{(y,\alpha,\beta):\beta\geq0,\ \alpha+\langle y,u\rangle+\beta f(u)\geq0\ \text{for every}\ u\in\operatorname{dom}f\}.
\]
For \(\beta>0\), the latter condition is equivalently
\[
\alpha\geq \beta f^*(-y/\beta).
\]
Thus conjugate inequalities give the dual halfspaces supporting the perspective epigraph cone.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_f^*=\{(y,\alpha,\beta):\beta\geq0,\ \alpha+\langle y,u\rangle+\beta f(u)\geq0\ \forall u\in\operatorname{dom}f\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-dual description of the closed perspective epigraph cone.

notation.meaning: Closed conic hull of the lifted epigraph.
Positive dual cone under the nonnegative-pairing convention.
Fenchel conjugate of the source function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar representation of a homogenized epigraph cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), let \(\widetilde f\) be its closed perspective, and set \(K_f:=\operatorname{epi}\widetilde f\subset\mathbb R\times\mathcal H\times\mathbb R\). The negative polar is \(K_f^\circ:=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\le0\ \forall k\in K_f\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The sign convention is the negative polar convention. A positive-dual-cone convention reverses all displayed polar signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The epigraph-cone dual representation is \[K_f=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}\{(1,x,r):r\ge f(x)\}\] together with \[K_f^\circ=\left\{(\mu,u,\eta):\begin{array}{l}\eta<0,\ \mu+(-\eta)f^*(u/(-\eta))\le0,\quad\text{or}\\\eta=0,\ u=0,\ \mu\le0\end{array}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogenized epigraph is the closed conic hull of the unit-scale epigraph. Its negative polar consists of triples whose last coordinate is negative and whose remaining coordinates satisfy a scaled conjugate inequality, together with the limiting vertical-polar ray at last coordinate zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_f=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}(\{1\}\times\operatorname{epi}f),\qquad K_f^\circ=\{(\mu,u,\eta):\eta<0,\ \mu+(-\eta)f^*(u/(-\eta))\le0\}\cup\{(\mu,0,0):\mu\le0\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\eta=-1\), the slice of the polar is \[K_f^\circ\cap\{\eta=-1\}=\{(\mu,u,-1):\mu+f^*(u)\le0\}.\]
\[(\mu,u,\eta)\in K_f^\circ\Longleftrightarrow \mu\xi+\langle u,x\rangle+\eta r\le0\quad\forall(\xi,x,r)\in K_f.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|^2\), the slice \(\eta=-1\) is the hypograph \(\mu\le-\tfrac12\|u\|^2\).
If \(f\) is sublinear, the scale-zero slice of \(K_f\) is \(\{0\}\times\operatorname{epi}f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The conjugacy set \(C_f\) is a normalized affine slice of \(K_f^\circ\).
Every valid homogeneous linear inequality for \(K_f\) corresponds to an element of its polar cone.
boundary_notes: The case \(\eta>0\) is impossible because epigraph coordinates \(r\) are unbounded above.
The closure in the definition of \(K_f\) is essential when the raw conic hull omits recession points.

notation.meaning: Negative polar cone of the homogenized epigraph.

children.title: Perspective Support Representations
children.top_down_role: Support-function views of homogenized convex functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Support Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the full homogenized space, the closed perspective is the support function of the hypograph of the negative conjugate. The hypograph supplies the infinite negative-scale branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_f:=\{(y,s):s\le -f^*(y)\}=\operatorname{hypo}(-f^*)\). Then, for every \((x,t)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}\),
\[
\bar p_f(x,t)=\sigma_{C_f}(x,t).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\bar p_f(x,t)=\begin{cases}t f(x/t),&t>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&t=0,\\ +\infty,&t<0.\end{cases}
\]
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p_f=\sigma_{\operatorname{hypo}(-f^*)}\) on \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support representation of the closed perspective on positive, zero, and negative scales.

notation.meaning: Hypograph of the negative Fenchel conjugate.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Support Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective is the support function of the conjugate graph with negated height. At zero scale, this reduces to the support function of the conjugate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,+\infty)\),
\[
\bar p_f(x,t)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\{\langle y,x\rangle-t f^*(y)\}.
\]
Equivalently, with
\[
S_f:=\{(y,-f^*(y)):y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\},
\]
one has \(\bar p_f(x,t)=\sigma_{S_f}(x,t)\) for \(t\geq0\). At \(t>0\), this is the Fenchel representation of \(t f(x/t)\); at \(t=0\), it becomes
\[
f^\infty(x)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(x).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(t\geq0\), \(\bar p_f(x,t)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}(\langle y,x\rangle-t f^*(y))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support representation on nonnegative scales, including the recession boundary.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective extension of the source function.
Fenchel conjugate of the source function.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), define \(C_f:=\{(\mu,u):\mu+f^*(u)\le0\}\), and let \(\sigma_{C_f}(\xi,x):=\sup_{(\mu,u)\in C_f}(\xi\mu+\langle x,u\rangle)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The representation is for the closed perspective, so it includes the recession boundary at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perspective support representation is \[\widetilde f(\xi,x)=\sigma_{C_f}(\xi,x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal H}\bigl(\langle x,u\rangle-\xi f^*(u)\bigr)\quad(\xi\ge0),\] with \(\widetilde f(\xi,x)=+\infty\) for \(\xi<0\). At \(\xi=0\), this becomes \((\operatorname{rec}f)(x)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective is the support function of the dual set defined by the conjugate inequality. At positive scale this is the supremum of the linear pairing minus the scaled source conjugate; at zero scale it reduces to the support function of the conjugate domain, which is the recession function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widetilde f=\sigma_{C_f},\qquad \widetilde f(\xi,x)=\sup_u\{\langle x,u\rangle-\xi f^*(u)\}\ \text{for }\xi\ge0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\widetilde f^*=\iota_{C_f}.\]
\[(\operatorname{rec}f)(x)=\widetilde f(0,x)=\sup_{u\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\langle x,u\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|^2\), then \(\widetilde f(\xi,x)=\sup_u(\langle x,u\rangle-\tfrac\xi2\|u\|^2)\).
If \(f=\sigma_D\) for a nonempty closed convex set \(D\), then \(f^*=\iota_D\) and \(\widetilde f(\xi,x)=\sigma_D(x)\) for every \(\xi\ge0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The closed perspective is lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous as a support function.
Dual maximizers, when they exist, expose supporting hyperplanes of the homogenized epigraph.
boundary_notes: The supremum need not be attained without additional compactness or coercivity assumptions.
For \(\xi<0\), the downward-unbounded intercept coordinate in \(C_f\) makes the support value \(+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Space Support Representation of the Closed Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function formula on all scales, including the negative-scale branch omitted by the graph representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let C_f:=\{(y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:s\leq-f^*(y)\}. Then, for every (x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R,
\[\bar p_f(x,t)=\sigma_{C_f}(x,t)=\sup_{(y,s)\in C_f}\bigl(\langle y,x\rangle+ts\bigr).\]
Consequently, \(\bar p_f(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) for \(t>0\), \(\bar p_f(x,0)=f^\infty(x)\), and \(\bar p_f(x,t)=+\infty\) for \(t<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective on the entire homogenized space is the support function of the hypograph of the negative conjugate. The hypograph, rather than only its graph, produces infinity at negative scales.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p_f=\sigma_{C_f}\) on \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\), where \(C_f=\operatorname{hypo}(-f^*)\).

notation.meaning: Hypograph of the negative Fenchel conjugate.

children.top_down_role: Primal-dual contact and equality geometry in homogenized coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Scale Fenchel Contact
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero scale, lifted Fenchel contact occurs exactly when the dual point exposes the conjugate domain in the recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\),
\[
\bar p_f(d,0)=f^\infty(d)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f^*}(d)\geq\langle d,y\rangle.
\]
Equality holds exactly when
\[
y\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\langle d,v\rangle.
\]
When equality holds, the homogeneous affine minorant
\[
(z,s)\mapsto\langle y,z\rangle-s f^*(y)
\]
contacts the closed perspective at \((d,0)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^\infty(d)\geq\langle d,y\rangle\), with equality exactly when \(y\) maximizes \(\langle d,\cdot\rangle\) over \(\operatorname{dom}f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting equality geometry on the recession face of the closed perspective.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Fenchel Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel's inequality lifts directly to perspective coordinates. Equality, equivalent to a subgradient relation, certifies that a conjugate-generated homogeneous hyperplane supports the perspective at the given point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The lifted Fenchel inequality is
\[
p_f(x,t)+t f^*(y)=t\bigl(f(x/t)+f^*(y)\bigr)\geq\langle x,y\rangle.
\]
Equality holds if and only if
\[
y\in\partial f(x/t),
\]
or equivalently \(x/t\in\partial f^*(y)\). When equality holds, the affine homogeneous function
\[
(z,s)\mapsto\langle y,z\rangle-s f^*(y)
\]
supports \(p_f\) at \((x,t)\). Thus the pair \((y,f^*(y))\), together with the displayed equality, certifies primal-dual contact in homogenized coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_f(x,t)+t f^*(y)\geq\langle x,y\rangle\), with equality exactly when \(y\in\partial f(x/t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scale Fenchel equality as a verifiable primal-dual contact certificate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), let \(\xi>0\), set \(z=x/\xi\), and let \((\mu,u)\in C_f:=\{(\mu,u):\mu+f^*(u)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition describes positive-scale primal-dual contact. Scale-zero contact requires recession and normal-cone formulations and is not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lifted primal point \((\xi,x,\xi f(x/\xi))\) and a dual point \((\mu,u)\in C_f\) are in Fenchel contact when \[\xi f(x/\xi)=\xi\mu+\langle x,u\rangle.\] Equivalently, \[\mu=-f^*(u),\qquad f(x/\xi)+f^*(u)=\langle x/\xi,u\rangle,\] or \(u\in\partial f(x/\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted Fenchel contact occurs when a feasible dual affine functional attains the perspective support value at a positive-scale primal point. The contact condition is exactly ordinary Fenchel equality at the normalized point, together with equality in the dual intercept constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\xi,x;\mu,u)\in\mathcal C_f\Longleftrightarrow \xi>0,\ \mu=-f^*(u),\ u\in\partial f(x/\xi),\] where \(\mathcal C_f\) denotes the lifted Fenchel contact set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[f(x/\xi)+f^*(u)=\langle x/\xi,u\rangle.\]
\[\widetilde f(\xi,x)=\sigma_{C_f}(\xi,x)=\xi\mu+\langle x,u\rangle.\]
\[u\in\partial f(x/\xi)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x/\xi\in\partial f^*(u).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable at \(x/\xi\), contact requires \(u=\nabla f(x/\xi)\).
For \(f(z)=\tfrac12\|z\|^2\), contact gives \(u=x/\xi\) and \(\mu=-\tfrac12\|x/\xi\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A contacting dual point defines a supporting hyperplane to \(\operatorname{epi}\widetilde f\) at the lifted primal boundary point.
Failure of Fenchel equality means the dual affine functional lies strictly below the perspective value.
boundary_notes: Subgradients may be empty at boundary points of \(\operatorname{dom}f\), so a support value need not have a contacting dual maximizer.
The definition fixes \(\xi>0\); the slice \(\xi=0\) is governed by exposed recession directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of closed perspective modeling functions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) range over real Hilbert spaces and let \(\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) denote the proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This defines the common structural family rather than a particular quadratic, entropic, or on-off atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perspective modeling family is \[\mathfrak P:=\left\{\widetilde f:\mathbb R\times\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\ \middle|\ f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H),\ \widetilde f(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi f(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\(\operatorname{rec}f)(x),&\xi=0,\\+\infty,&\xi<0\end{cases}\right\}.\] Each member is a closed convex positively homogeneous lift whose unit-scale slice recovers its generator: \(\widetilde f(1,x)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective modeling family consists of all closed perspective lifts of proper lower-semicontinuous convex generators. Every member is defined on a scale-state product space, is convex and positively homogeneous, contains a recession boundary at zero scale, and recovers its generator on the unit-scale slice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak P=\{\widetilde f:f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\},\qquad \widetilde f(1,\cdot)=f,\quad \widetilde f(0,\cdot)=\operatorname{rec}f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\widetilde f\in\mathfrak P\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{epi}\widetilde f=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}(\{1\}\times\operatorname{epi}f)\ \text{for some }f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H).\]
Every member satisfies \[\widetilde f(\lambda\xi,\lambda x)=\lambda\widetilde f(\xi,x)\quad(\lambda>0).\]
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(f(x)=\|x\|^2\) yields the quadratic-over-linear atom.
Choosing \(f(s)=s\log s-s\) on \(s\ge0\) yields an entropic perspective.
Choosing an indicator \(f=\iota_C\) yields the homogeneous feasibility lift \(\widetilde f(\xi,x)=\iota_{\overline{\operatorname{cone}}(\{1\}\times C)}(\xi,x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine precomposition in the state variable and nonnegative sums of compatible members produce convex lifted models.
The epigraph of every family member is a closed convex cone.
boundary_notes: The family definition does not assert that every positively homogeneous convex function arises from a unique generator unless a unit-scale slice and scale orientation are fixed.
Raw perspectives without recession completion are excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of the Closed Quadratic-over-Linear Atom
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of the closed quadratic-over-linear atom is the indicator of a reverse quadratic epigraph, with a range restriction in the singular case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fenchel conjugate of \(q_Q\) is \[q_Q^*(y,\eta)=\delta_{D_Q}(y,\eta),\qquad D_Q=\left\{(y,\eta):y\in\operatorname{ran}Q,\ \eta+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger y\leq0\right\},\] where \(Q^\dagger\) is the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.
assumptions_latex: \(q_Q\) is the closed perspective of \(x\mapsto\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_Q^*=\delta_{D_Q}\) with \(D_Q=\{(y,\eta):y\in\operatorname{ran}Q,\ \eta+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger y\leq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit atom-specific Fenchel representation, including singular positive-semidefinite matrices.

notation.meaning: Dual feasible set of the atom

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-over-Linear Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic becomes quadratic-over-linear under perspective. Its closed epigraph is a rotated second-order cone, including kernel directions on the zero-scale face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(u)=\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}Qu\), its closed perspective is
\[
q_Q(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{x^{\mathsf T}Qx}{2t},&t>0,\\
0,&t=0\ \text{and}\ Qx=0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(t>0\), its epigraph admits the rotated second-order-cone representation
\[
q_Q(x,t)\leq r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r\geq0,\ t>0,\ 2rt\geq\lVert Lx\rVert_2^2.
\]
The closed conic representation replaces \(t>0\) by \(t\geq0\), retaining the same quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(t>0\), \(q_Q(x,t)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx/(2t)\), and \(q_Q(x,t)\leq r\) iff \(2rt\geq\lVert Lx\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective and rotated second-order-cone epigraph of a positive-semidefinite quadratic.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the quadratic function.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\ne\{0\}\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(\alpha>0\). The generator is \(q_\alpha(x)=\alpha\|x\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the closed extended-real quadratic-over-linear family with scalar denominator. The zero-scale value is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[Q_\alpha(\xi,x):=\begin{cases}\alpha\|x\|^2/\xi,&\xi>0,\\0,&(\xi,x)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] This is the closed perspective of \(q_\alpha\). Its effective domain is \((0,+\infty)\times\mathcal H\) together with \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed quadratic-over-linear function divides a nonnegative squared norm by a strictly positive scale. It assigns zero at the joint origin and positive infinity at every other point with nonpositive scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q_\alpha(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\alpha\|x\|^2/\xi,&\xi>0,\\0,&\xi=0,\ x=0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[Q_\alpha(\xi,x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal H}\left(\langle x,u\rangle-\frac{\xi}{4\alpha}\|u\|^2\right)\quad(\xi\ge0).\]
Its epigraph is \[\{(\xi,x,r):\xi\ge0,\ r\ge0,\ \|x\|^2\le \xi r/\alpha\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\alpha=1\), the positive-scale expression is \(\|x\|^2/\xi\).
In \(\mathbb R^n\), replacing \(\|x\|^2\) by \(\|Ax\|^2\) gives the positive-semidefinite quadratic-over-linear atom, whose zero-scale domain contains \(\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(Q_\alpha\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous.
Every sublevel inequality \(Q_\alpha(\xi,x)\le r\) admits a rotated second-order-cone representation.
boundary_notes: Assigning \(+\infty\) at \((0,0)\) produces the raw, nonclosed perspective.
For a semidefinite quadratic with a nontrivial nullspace, the correct zero-scale boundary is zero on that nullspace, not only at the origin.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(s)=s\log s-s\) for \(s\ge0\), with \(0\log0:=0\), and \(\phi(s)=+\infty\) for \(s<0\). Then \(\phi\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers the scalar entropy perspective and finite separable sums. It uses natural logarithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scalar closed entropic perspective is \[E(t,x):=\begin{cases}x\log(x/t)-x,&t>0,\ x\ge0,\\0,&t=0,\ x=0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] For vectors \(t,x\in\mathbb R^m\), the separable family is \(E_m(t,x)=\sum_{i=1}^m E(t_i,x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropic perspective scales the Boltzmann–Shannon entropy. At positive scale it is the relative-entropy term minus its mass coordinate; the closed extension is finite at zero scale only at zero mass. Finite sums give the standard separable vector family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[E(t,x)=\begin{cases}x\log(x/t)-x,&t>0,\ x\ge0,\\0,&(t,x)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad E_m(t,x)=\sum_iE(t_i,x_i).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\phi^*(u)=e^u\), \[E(t,x)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb R}\{xu-te^u\}\quad(t\ge0).\]
special_cases_latex: Adding the affine term \(x\) gives the relative-entropy atom \(x\log(x/t)\).
On the probability simplex with equal scale coordinates, summing \(x_i\log x_i\) gives negative Shannon entropy.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(E\) and \(E_m\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous.
Their epigraphs are representable using exponential-cone constraints.
boundary_notes: The convention \(0\log(0/t)=0\) applies for \(t>0\).
If \(t=0\) and \(x>0\), the value is \(+\infty\); negative mass or negative scale is also excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of separable negative entropy is the sum of scaled logarithmic terms. Its closed zero-scale boundary is finite only at the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
h(u):=\sum_{i=1}^m u_i\log u_i
\quad\text{for}\quad u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,
\]
and set \(h(u)=+\infty\) outside \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Its closed perspective is
\[
H(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m x_i\log(x_i/t),&x\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,\ t>0,\\
0,&x=0,\ t=0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The function \(H\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous. The zero-scale value is finite only at \(x=0\), because \(h^\infty(x)=+\infty\) for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perspective of \(h(u)=\sum_i u_i\log u_i\) is \(H(x,t)=\sum_i x_i\log(x_i/t)\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable negative-entropy perspective with its closed zero-scale behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Entropy as Coordinatewise Entropy Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended relative entropy is the sum of closed scalar entropy perspectives and is jointly convex in both nonnegative vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
d(a,b):=\begin{cases}a\log(a/b),&a>0,\ b>0,\\0,&a=0,\ b\ge0,\\+\infty,&a>0,\ b=0,\end{cases}
\]
and set \(d(a,b)=+\infty\) outside \(\mathbb R_+^2\). For \(x,y\in\mathbb R_+^n\), define
\[
D(x\|y):=\sum_{i=1}^n d(x_i,y_i).
\]
Each \(d\) is the closed perspective of \(u\mapsto u\log u\); hence \(D\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, jointly convex, and positively homogeneous in \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x\|y)=\sum_i d(x_i,y_i)\) is lower semicontinuous and jointly convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended finite-dimensional relative entropy represented as a separable sum of closed scalar perspectives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x\|y)\) is jointly convex in \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional extended-value relative entropy and its scalar perspective construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi(u)=u\log u\) for \(u>0\), with \(\phi(0)=0\). Its closed perspective is \(p(a,b)=b\phi(a/b)=a\log(a/b)\) when \(a\geq 0\) and \(b>0\), extended by \(p(0,0)=0\) and \(p(a,0)=+\infty\) for \(a>0\). The extended relative entropy is
\[
D(x\|y)=\sum_{i=1}^n p(x_i,y_i).
\]
Because a closed perspective of a convex function is convex and finite sums preserve convexity, \(D\) is jointly convex on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\times\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative entropy is the sum of scalar entropy perspectives, using the standard boundary conventions, and is jointly convex in both nonnegative arguments.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Relative-Entropy Exponential-Cone Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar relative-entropy epigraph is exactly one closed exponential-cone constraint after a fixed sign change and coordinate placement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
K_{\exp}:=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R^3:v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\le w\}.
\]
For \(x,y\ge0\), with
\[
d(x,y):=\begin{cases}x\log(x/y),&x>0,\ y>0,\\0,&x=0,\ y\ge0,\\+\infty,&x>0,\ y=0,\end{cases}
\]
one has
\[
r\ge d(x,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(-r,x,y)\in K_{\exp}.
\]
assumptions_latex: The displayed closed exponential-cone coordinate convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\ge d(x,y)\iff(-r,x,y)\in K_{\exp}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed exponential-cone encoding with fixed coordinate order and all nonnegative boundary cases.

notation.meaning: Closed exponential cone in the displayed coordinate order.

assumptions_latex: The exponential cone uses the closed-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\geq x\log(x/y)\iff(-r,x,y)\in K_{\exp}\) for \(x,y\geq0\), with extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-dimensional closed exponential-cone encoding of scalar relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the closed exponential cone by
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb{R}^3:v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}.
\]
For \(x>0\) and \(y>0\), the inequality \(r\geq x\log(x/y)\) is equivalent to \(x\exp(-r/x)\leq y\), and hence to \((-r,x,y)\in K_{\exp}\). Taking closures extends this equivalence to \(x,y\geq0\) under the conventions \(0\log(0/y)=0\) and \(x\log(x/0)=+\infty\) for \(x>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perspective lift for an on-off epigraph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n)\) satisfy \(f(0)=0\), let \(z\in\{0,1\}\) be an activation variable, and let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) be a state constrained to vanish when \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the ideal convex perspective interface for a single on-off convex epigraph. Additional side constraints can change its convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the disjunctive on-off epigraph \[S_f:=\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}\cup\{(1,x,r):r\ge f(x)\}.\] Its perspective relaxation is \[\widehat S_f:=\{(z,x,r):0\le z\le1,\ r\ge\widetilde f(z,x)\},\] where \(\widetilde f\) is the closed perspective of \(f\). The on-off interface is the replacement of \(r\ge f(x)\) under activation by \(r\ge zf(x/z)\) for \(z>0\), with the recession boundary at \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An on-off epigraph has an inactive state at zero activation and the original convex epigraph at unit activation. Its perspective lift uses a continuous activation variable between zero and one and imposes the closed perspective epigraph inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S_f=\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}\cup\{(1,x,r):r\ge f(x)\},\qquad \widehat S_f=\{(z,x,r):0\le z\le1,\ r\ge\widetilde f(z,x)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(0<z\le1\), the lifted inequality is \[r\ge zf(x/z).\]
When \(\operatorname{rec}f=\iota_{\{0\}}\), the zero-scale constraint \(r\ge\widetilde f(0,x)\) forces \(x=0\) and \(r\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\|x\|^2\), the strengthened inequality is \(r\ge\|x\|^2/z\) for \(z>0\).
For separable \(f(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\), separate activations may be modeled with the corresponding component perspectives.
immediate_consequences_latex: The lifted epigraph is convex in \((z,x,r)\).
At binary \(z\), the perspective constraint reproduces the inactive and active epigraph branches under the stated recession condition.
boundary_notes: No inspected source in the supplied discovery set was found that states the exact convex-hull equality for this on-off formulation.
The equality \(\widehat S_f=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S_f\) requires explicit hypotheses and is therefore not asserted here.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source is needed for the on-off modeling formulation and any desired convex-hull characterization.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective lift for an on-off epigraph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is plausible and avoids asserting an unsupported convex-hull equality, but it has no independently inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-State Failure without Supercoercivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perspective regularizer forces the variable to zero when inactive exactly when every nonzero recession direction has infinite cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f^\infty(d)<+\infty\) for some \(d\neq0\), then the closed perspective satisfies \(\widetilde f(d,0)=f^\infty(d)<+\infty\). Thus the zero-activity branch does not force the regularized variable to vanish. It enforces \(x=0\) at \(z=0\) exactly when \(f^\infty(d)=+\infty\) for every \(d\neq0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:\widetilde f(x,0)<+\infty\}=\{0\}\) if and only if \(f^\infty(d)=+\infty\) for all \(d\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact failure boundary for zero-activity enforcement by a closed perspective regularizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Regularizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective regularizer for an indicator-controlled convex penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, with \(f(0)=0\). Its closed perspective regularizer is
\[
R_f(x,z)=\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0,\end{cases}
\]
where \(f^\infty\) is the recession function of \(f\). The function \(R_f\) is closed, convex, and positively homogeneous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\). For binary \(z\), the values \(R_f(x,1)=f(x)\) and \(R_f(0,0)=0\) encode the active and inactive penalty states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective scales a convex penalty by an activity variable, using its recession function at zero to obtain a closed convex homogeneous regularizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_f\text{ is closed, convex, and positively homogeneous}\)

notation.meaning: closed perspective regularizer generated by f

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Hull of an Isolated On–Off Epigraph
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph is the exact closed convex hull of the isolated inactive and active epigraph disjunction. Its zero-indicator slice records recession directions unless the function is supercoercive in every nonzero direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S:=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):f(x)\le t\},
\]
and let \(\widetilde f\) be the closed perspective of \(f\). Then
\[
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S
=
\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ \widetilde f(x,z)\le t\}.
\]
At \(z=1\) this recovers \(\operatorname{epi}f\), while at \(z=0\) it gives \(f^\infty(x)\le t\). In particular, the zero slice reduces to \(x=0,\ t\ge0\) when \(f^\infty(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\ne0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ \widetilde f(x,z)\le t\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact closed-perspective formulation, including the recession slice when the indicator is zero.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(f(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\leq z\leq1,\ \widetilde f(x,z)\leq t\}\).

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the epigraph function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex hull of an unbounded binary on-off epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\{(0,0,t):t\geq0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):f(x)\leq t\},
\]
and let \(\widetilde f\) be the closed perspective of \(f\). Then
\[
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S
=
\{(x,z,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}:0\leq z\leq1,\ \widetilde f(x,z)\leq t\}.
\]
Thus the perspective epigraph is an ideal continuous formulation of the isolated on-off epigraph: its slices at \(z=0\) and \(z=1\) recover the two disjuncts, while intermediate slices give their closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph over a relaxed indicator is exactly the closed convex hull of the corresponding inactive and active epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.title: On–Off Epigraph Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is a precise closed-convex-hull formulation for the isolated binary on-off epigraph and its content kind fits the leaf. An authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is required before review can determine source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Equality Boundary for Perspective Dominance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective dominance is an equality exactly along source rays on which the regularizer is affine; strict curvature makes the strengthening strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u=x/z\). For \(0<z<1\), equality \(f(x)=zf(x/z)\) holds if and only if \(f\) is affine on \([0,u]\), equivalently \(f(\theta u)=\theta f(u)\) for every \(0\leq\theta\leq1\). Consequently, strict convexity on this segment and \(x\neq0\) imply \(f(x)<zf(x/z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=zf(x/z)\) if and only if \(f\) is affine on \([0,x/z]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise equality characterization for the perspective-dominance inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Boundary for Dominance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual dominance comparison requires suitable normalization at the inactive point; a positive origin value can reverse it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every admissible \(x\) and \(0<z\leq1\), convexity gives \(f(x)\leq zf(x/z)+(1-z)f(0)\). Hence \(f(x)\leq zf(x/z)\) follows when \(f(0)\leq0\). If \(f(0)>0\), unshifted dominance can fail; for \(f\equiv c>0\), one has \(c>zc\) whenever \(z<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\leq zf(x/z)+(1-z)f(0)\), while unshifted dominance can fail when \(f(0)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of the inactive reference value on perspective dominance.

notation.meaning: Regularizer value at the inactive reference point

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\leq zf(x/z)\), with equality along every ray precisely at the positive-homogeneity boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between strict perspective strengthening and equality with the unscaled convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Convexity and \(f(0)=0\) imply
\[
f(x)=f\bigl(z(x/z)+(1-z)0\bigr)\leq zf(x/z).
\]
Hence the perspective inequality \(t\geq zf(x/z)\) dominates the unscaled inequality \(t\geq f(x)\) on \(0<z\leq1\). If \(f\) is strictly convex, \(x\neq0\), and \(0<z<1\), the inequality is strict whenever both points are in its effective domain. Conversely, equality \(f(x)=zf(x/z)\) for all admissible \(x,z\) holds when \(f\) is positively homogeneous of degree one; in that regime perspective scaling supplies no strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective scaling dominates the naive relaxation; strengthening is strict for strictly convex penalties but disappears for degree-one positively homogeneous functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance inequality and the strict-convexity and positive-homogeneity boundaries are plausible and locally appropriate, but the record has no citation. The displayed Jensen derivation is proof text, and the conclusion's “precisely” characterization requires an explicitly sourced statement with matching quantifiers and domain qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Epigraph Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed conic hull of an epigraph embedded at height one is exactly the epigraph of the function's closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Embed the epigraph of \(f\) at homogenizing coordinate one and define
\[
K_f=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1,t):(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.
\]
If \(\widetilde f\) denotes the closed perspective,
\[
\widetilde f(x,z)=
\begin{cases}
z f(x/z),&z>0,\\
f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\
+\infty,&z<0,
\end{cases}
\]
then
\[
K_f=\{(x,z,t):\widetilde f(x,z)\leq t\}=\operatorname{epi}\widetilde f.
\]
Consequently, homogenizing a closed convex epigraph produces a closed convex cone whose section at \(z=1\) is the original epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph of the closed perspective is the closed conic hull of the unit-height embedding of \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic homogenization of a closed convex epigraph.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Convex Cones p. 111; 9.2 Proper Lower Semicontinuous Convex Functions p. 160

knowledge_statements.title: Supercoercive Zero-Face Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-height face is only its vertical ray exactly when the source function is supercoercive; finite recession cost creates a nonzero boundary direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following are equivalent: \[\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty}\frac{f(x)}{\|x\|}=+\infty,\qquad f^\infty=\delta_{\{0\}},\qquad K_f\cap\{z=0\}=\{(0,0,\tau):\tau\geq0\}.\] Thus a nonzero horizontal zero-height direction exists exactly when \(f^\infty(d)<+\infty\) for some \(d\neq0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is supercoercive if and only if \(K_f\cap\{z=0\}=\{(0,0,\tau):\tau\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp criterion for absence of nonvertical directions in the zero-height face.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Geometry of Homogeneous Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-height slice of a homogenized epigraph cone is the epigraph of the recession function, hence records all epigraph recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The recession function of \(f\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rec}(\operatorname{epi}f)=\operatorname{epi}f^\infty
=
\{(d,\tau):f^\infty(d)\leq\tau\}.
\]
For the homogenized epigraph cone
\[
K_f=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1,t):(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\},
\]
its zero-height slice is therefore
\[
K_f\cap\{(d,0,\tau):d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \tau\in\mathbb{R}\}
=
\{(d,0,\tau):f^\infty(d)\leq\tau\}.
\]
Thus points added at homogenizing height zero encode exactly the recession directions of the original epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_f\cap\{z=0\}=\{(d,0,\tau):f^\infty(d)\leq\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-height slice of a homogenized epigraph and its recession interpretation.

notation.meaning: Recession function of the original function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Catalog of canonical finite-dimensional convex families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with extended-real-valued functions. Let \(\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n)\) denote proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a taxonomy-level definition of a reusable catalog, not a claim that the listed subclasses exhaust all convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the canonical catalog \[\mathfrak C:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{aq}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{ph}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{met}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{poly}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{ent}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{spec}},\] where the components respectively contain affine-quadratic functions with positive-semidefinite curvature, proper closed sublinear functions, convex metric-residual losses, polyhedral convex functions, closed entropic functions, and convex spectral functions. Membership requires the defining domain and convexity conditions of the selected component family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical convex-function catalog is the union of six explicitly typed reusable families: affine-quadratic, positive-homogeneous, metric-residual, finite-piece polyhedral, entropic, and spectral. The catalog is organizational and does not purport to include every proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak C=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{aq}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{ph}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{met}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{poly}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{ent}}\cup\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{spec}}\subset\bigcup_{n\ge1}\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n).\]
special_cases_latex: Norms belong to \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{ph}}\) and also generate metric residuals.
A maximum of finitely many affine functions belongs to \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{poly}}\).
A positive-semidefinite quadratic belongs to \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{aq}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A function can belong to several catalog components; the union is not disjoint.
Perspective transforms of catalog members form associated homogeneous modeling atoms when their closed extensions are used.
boundary_notes: No single inspected source was found that canonically defines this exact six-part catalog.
Spectral functions require a separate matrix-space definition and are mentioned here only as one catalog component.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex; let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\); and let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The family groups the elementary Euclidean convex atoms used to build affine-quadratic, homogeneous, and residual models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\mathfrak M_n:=\left\{x\mapsto\tfrac12\langle x,Qx\rangle+\langle a,x\rangle+\alpha\right\}\cup\{\text{proper closed sublinear }h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\}\cup\{x\mapsto d_C(x)\},\] where \(d_C(x):=\inf_{y\in C}\|x-y\|\). Every member is convex; the displayed quadratic members are finite and continuous, and each distance member is finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The foundational metric family consists of positive-semidefinite affine quadratics, proper closed sublinear functions such as norms and support functions, and Euclidean distance functions to nonempty closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak M_n=\mathfrak M_n^{\mathrm{aq}}\cup\mathfrak M_n^{\mathrm{ph}}\cup\mathfrak M_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\subset\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A quadratic member is convex exactly when \(Q\succeq0\).
A proper lower-semicontinuous sublinear member has the representation \(h=\sigma_D\) for a unique nonempty closed convex set \(D\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(Q=0\) gives affine functions.
Taking \(C=\{b\}\) gives \(d_C(x)=\|x-b\|\).
Every norm is a finite sublinear member.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine precomposition yields residual functions such as \(x\mapsto d_C(Ax-b)\).
Nonnegative sums of compatible members remain convex.
boundary_notes: The union notation defines a modeling family, not a closure under every convexity-preserving operation.
Distance to a nonconvex set is generally not convex, so convexity of \(C\) is essential.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the finite-valued Euclidean affine-quadratic family. Extended-valued quadratic functions on restricted affine domains are not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-quadratic curvature family is \[\mathfrak Q_n:=\left\{q_{Q,a,\alpha}:x\mapsto\tfrac12x^\top Qx+a^\top x+\alpha\ \middle|\ Q\succeq0\right\}.\] The affine term controls tilt and offset, while \(Q\) controls curvature. The member is affine exactly when \(Q=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex affine-quadratic function is a quadratic polynomial whose symmetric curvature matrix is positive semidefinite. Its linear and constant terms do not affect convexity, and zero curvature yields the affine subfamily.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q_{Q,a,\alpha}(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+a^\top x+\alpha\text{ is convex on }\mathbb R^n\Longleftrightarrow Q\succeq0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[z^\top Qz\ge0\quad\forall z\in\mathbb R^n.\]
If \(Q=B^\top B\), then \[q_{Q,a,\alpha}(x)=\tfrac12\|Bx\|^2+a^\top x+\alpha.\]
special_cases_latex: \(Q=0\) gives an affine function.
\(Q\succ0\) gives a strictly convex quadratic with unique unconstrained minimizer \(-Q^{-1}a\).
\(Q=\lambda I\), \(a=0\), gives the scaled squared Euclidean norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The gradient is \(\nabla q(x)=Qx+a\) and the Hessian is the constant matrix \(Q\).
The perspective of the homogeneous quadratic part produces a quadratic-over-linear function.
boundary_notes: An indefinite \(Q\) yields a nonconvex quadratic on \(\mathbb R^n\).
Positive semidefiniteness does not imply strict convexity when \(Q\) has a nontrivial nullspace.

notation.meaning: Convex affine-quadratic family on Euclidean space.
The symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Minimization of an Affine Function
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine function has a global minimizer exactly when its linear part vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a(x)=\ell(x)+\beta\) on a real vector space \(X\). If \(\ell=0\), then \(a\equiv\beta\), every point minimizes \(a\), and \(\inf_Xa=\beta\). If \(\ell\ne0\), then \(a\) is unbounded above and below, so \(\operatorname*{argmin}_Xa=\varnothing\) and \(\inf_Xa=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_Xa=X\) if \(\ell=0\); otherwise it is empty and \(\inf_Xa=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic minimization over the entire vector space.

notation.meaning: linear part of the affine function

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine function is a linear functional plus a constant, equivalently a function preserving every affine combination; it is both convex and concave.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(a:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is affine if there exist a linear functional \(\ell:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and a scalar \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
a(x)=\ell(x)+\beta\qquad(x\in X).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(x,y\in X\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
a(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)=\lambda a(x)+(1-\lambda)a(y).
\]
Every affine function is both convex and concave because the defining equality implies both corresponding Jensen inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The domain is a real vector space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)=\ell(x)+\beta\) is affine and satisfies the affine-combination identity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valued affine functions on an arbitrary real vector space.

source_witnesses.locator: 8 Convex Functions p. 139

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Quadratic Minimizer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic completes the square around its unique stationary minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q\succ0\) and \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\), then with \(x_\star=-Q^{-1}b\), \[q(x)=q(x_\star)+\tfrac12(x-x_\star)^{\mathsf T}Q(x-x_\star),\qquad \min q=c-\tfrac12b^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}b.\] Thus \(x_\star\) is the unique minimizer and the unique solution of \(Qx+b=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}q=\{-Q^{-1}b\}\) and \(\min q=c-\tfrac12b^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate quadratics; singular Hessians belong to the sibling boundary leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Curvature Constants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extreme Hessian eigenvalues give the sharp smoothness and strong-convexity constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(Q\succeq0\), \(\nabla q(x)=Qx+b\). The sharp global Euclidean gradient-Lipschitz constant is \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). If \(\mu=\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\), then \(q\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and \(\mu\) is sharp.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\) and, when positive, \(\mu=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) are the sharp global curvature constants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global Euclidean curvature constants for a convex quadratic.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic function with symmetric Hessian is convex exactly when its quadratic coefficient matrix is positive semidefinite, and strictly convex when it is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+b^\top x+c,
\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The function \(q\) is convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) if and only if \(Q\) is positive semidefinite, meaning
\[
d^\top Qd\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Equivalently, its constant Hessian satisfies \(\nabla^2q(x)=Q\succeq0\). It is strictly convex if \(Q\succ0\); positive semidefiniteness alone permits flat directions and therefore need not imply strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+b^\top x+c\) is convex if and only if \(Q\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of a Singular Convex Quadratic
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate is pseudoinverse-quadratic on the affine Hessian range and infinite outside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with symmetric singular \(Q\succeq0\), \[q^*(y)=\begin{cases}\tfrac12(y-b)^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger(y-b)-c,&y-b\in\operatorname{range}Q,\\+\infty,&y-b\notin\operatorname{range}Q.\end{cases}\] Thus \(\operatorname{dom}q^*=b+\operatorname{range}Q\).
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, positive semidefinite, and singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}q^*=b+\operatorname{range}Q\), with the displayed pseudoinverse formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular curvature expressed by an affine effective-domain restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Quadratic Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular convex quadratic has minimizers precisely when its linear term lies in the Hessian range; otherwise a null direction makes it unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(b\in\operatorname{range}Q\), then the stationary equation \(Qx+b=0\) is solvable and
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}q(x)=-Q^\dagger b+\ker Q,
\qquad
\min q=c-\tfrac12b^\top Q^\dagger b.
\]
The minimizer is nonunique because every null direction of \(Q\) is flat. If \(b\notin\operatorname{range}Q\), then there exists \(d\in\ker Q\) with \(b^\top d\neq0\); choosing the sign of \(d\) gives \(q(x+td)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, positive semidefinite, and singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum is attained exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}Q\); otherwise \(\inf q=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability boundary for an unconstrained convex quadratic with singular Hessian.

children.top_down_role: Positive-homogeneous convex function families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be extended-real-valued with \(0\in\operatorname{dom}h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The family consists of convex degree-one positive-homogeneous functions, equivalently proper closed sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\mathfrak H_n:=\{h:h(\lambda x)=\lambda h(x)\ \forall x,\lambda>0,\quad h(x+y)\le h(x)+h(y)\ \forall x,y,\quad h\text{ proper and lsc}\}.\] Equivalently, \(h\in\mathfrak H_n\) exactly when \(h=\sigma_D\) for a unique nonempty closed convex set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-homogeneous convex family consists of proper lower-semicontinuous sublinear functions. Such a function scales linearly under positive dilation, is subadditive, and is exactly the support function of a unique nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h\in\mathfrak H_n\Longleftrightarrow h\text{ is proper, lsc, positively homogeneous, and subadditive}\Longleftrightarrow h=\sigma_D\text{ for a unique nonempty closed convex }D.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{epi}h\text{ is a closed convex cone}.\]
\[D=\{v:\langle v,x\rangle\le h(x)\ \forall x\},\qquad h(x)=\sup_{v\in D}\langle v,x\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: Every norm and seminorm is sublinear; a norm is finite and symmetric.
Every linear function is sublinear, with a singleton representing set \(D\).
Indicators of closed convex cones are extended-valued sublinear functions.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\), \(\partial h(x)=\operatorname{argmax}_{v\in D}\langle v,x\rangle\).
The conjugate of \(h=\sigma_D\) is \(h^*=\iota_D\).
boundary_notes: Positive homogeneity alone does not imply convexity; subadditivity supplies the missing condition.
The value at \(\lambda=0\) is governed by properness and lower semicontinuity rather than by the displayed scaling rule.

notation.meaning: Family of proper closed sublinear functions.

knowledge_statements.title: The Finite-Dimensional ℓp Norm Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate ℓp formula defines a norm for p at least one; below one it violates the triangle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^n\), \[\|x\|_p=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|^p\right)^{1/p}\quad(1\le p<\infty),\qquad \|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|\] are norms. If \(n\ge2\) and \(0<p<1\), the power formula is not a norm because \(\|e_1+e_2\|_p=2^{1/p}>2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\cdot\|_p\text{ is a norm for }1\le p\le\infty,\text{ while the power formula is not a norm for }0<p<1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical coordinate-norm family and its sharp exponent boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Triangle Inequality and Continuity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every norm satisfies the reverse triangle inequality and is 1-Lipschitz in its own metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every norm and all \(x,y\), \[\bigl|\|x\|-\|y\|\bigr|\le\|x-y\|.\] Consequently the norm function is 1-Lipschitz in its induced metric and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl|\|x\|-\|y\|\bigr|\le\|x-y\|\quad\forall x,y\in X.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic metric regularity shared by every norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm is positive definite, absolutely homogeneous, and subadditive; equivalently, it is a symmetric positive-definite finite sublinear function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(\|\cdot\|:X\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is a norm when, for all \(x,y\in X\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
\|x\|=0\iff x=0,
\qquad
\|\alpha x\|=|\alpha|\,\|x\|,
\qquad
\|x+y\|\leq\|x\|+\|y\|.
\]
These conditions make every norm finite-valued, convex, and positively homogeneous. Conversely, a finite-valued sublinear function that is positive definite and symmetric, meaning \(p(x)=p(-x)\), satisfies absolute homogeneity and is a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A norm is exactly a finite-valued, positive-definite, symmetric sublinear function on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norms characterized as symmetric positive-definite sublinear functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm can be represented as the Minkowski functional of its balanced convex unit ball.

knowledge_statements.title: Definiteness and Coercivity of Finite-Dimensional Gauges
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed finite-dimensional gauge is positive definite and coercive exactly when its unit set is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, convex, absorbing, and contain \(0\). Then \[\gamma_C(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname{rec}C.\] Hence \(\gamma_C\) is positive definite iff \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{0\}\), equivalently iff \(C\) is bounded. In this case there are \(0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty\) with \[\alpha\|x\|_2\le\gamma_C(x)\le\beta\|x\|_2,\] so \(\gamma_C\) is coercive.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness of \(\gamma_C\), boundedness of \(C\), and \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{0\}\) are equivalent and imply two-sided norm bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex absorbing sets in finite-dimensional Euclidean space; symmetry is not assumed.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Minkowski gauge of a convex absorbing set containing the origin is a finite sublinear function. Its open unit sublevel set lies in the original set, the original set lies in its closed unit sublevel set, and a closed original set equals that closed unit sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, convex, absorbing, and contain \(0\). The Minkowski gauge of \(C\) is
\[
\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\lambda>0:x\in\lambda C\},
\qquad x\in X.
\]
The function \(\gamma_C:X\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is finite and sublinear; explicitly,
\[
\gamma_C(x+y)\leq\gamma_C(x)+\gamma_C(y)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\gamma_C(\alpha x)=\alpha\gamma_C(x)
\]
for all \(x,y\in X\) and all \(\alpha\geq0\). Moreover,
\[
\{x\in X:\gamma_C(x)<1\}\subseteq C
\subseteq\{x\in X:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}.
\]
If \(C\) is closed in the Hilbert-space topology, then
\[
C=\{x\in X:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty, convex, contains \(0\), and is absorbing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\lambda>0:x\in\lambda C\}\) is a finite sublinear gauge, with \(\{x:\gamma_C(x)<1\}\subseteq C\subseteq\{x:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}\); if \(C\) is closed, then \(C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski gauge of a convex absorbing subset of a real Hilbert space containing the origin.

notation.meaning: Nonempty convex absorbing subset of the Hilbert space containing the origin

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Symmetry Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of a compact convex set containing the origin in its interior is a norm exactly when the set is centrally symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gauge \(\gamma_C\) is finite, nonnegative, convex, positively homogeneous, and positive definite. Moreover,
\[
\gamma_C(-x)=\gamma_C(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in V
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C=-C.
\]
Thus \(\gamma_C\) is a norm if and only if \(C\) is centrally symmetric.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(C\subset V\) is nonempty, compact, convex, contains \(0\) in its interior, and has gauge \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tC\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a norm if and only if \(C=-C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the symmetry condition separating gauges of convex bodies from norms.

notation.meaning: Minkowski gauge of the set C

children.title: Metric Residual Loss Family
children.top_down_role: Metric and residual-based convex functions used across modeling domains.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex; let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear; let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\); and let \(\rho:[0,+\infty)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional family covers distances, norm residuals, and convex monotone penalties of such residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[L_{A,b,C,\rho}(x):=\rho\bigl(d_C(Ax-b)\bigr),\qquad d_C(y):=\inf_{c\in C}\|y-c\|.\] The metric residual loss family is the collection of all such \(L_{A,b,C,\rho}\). Every member is convex; it is finite whenever \(\rho\) is finite on \([0,+\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric residual loss applies a convex nondecreasing scalar penalty to the Euclidean distance between an affine residual and a nonempty closed convex target set. This includes plain distance, norm residuals, and powers or robust convex penalties of distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak R:=\{x\mapsto\rho(d_C(Ax-b)):C\ne\varnothing\text{ closed convex},\ \rho\text{ proper lsc convex nondecreasing}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\rho(t)=t\), \[L_{A,b,C,\rho}(x)=d_C(Ax-b).\]
special_cases_latex: \(\rho(t)=t^2\) gives squared-distance residual loss.
\(A=I\), \(b=0\), and \(C\) a closed convex feasibility set gives the distance-to-feasibility loss.
A singleton target \(C=\{c\}\) gives \(\rho(\|Ax-b-c\|)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The zero set of the unpenalized distance residual is \(\{x:Ax-b\in C\}\).
If \(C\) is nonempty closed convex, the projection defining the nearest point is single-valued.
boundary_notes: Distance to a nonconvex set need not be convex and may have multiple nearest points.
If \(\rho\) is convex but decreasing on part of its domain, the composition need not be convex.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance to the target set.

knowledge_statements.title: Variational Characterization of the Metric Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is the projection of x exactly when its residual is normal to the set there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\). For \(x\in H\) and \(p\in C\),
\[
p=P_Cx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle x-p,c-p\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }c\in C.
\]
Equivalently, \(x-p\in N_C(p)\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=P_Cx\) if and only if \(\langle x-p,c-p\rangle\leq0\) for every \(c\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearest-point certificate for a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: metric projection of x onto C
convex normal cone to C at p

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Sets Need Not Have Convex Distance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the two-point set {-1,1} violates midpoint convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\), \[d_C(x)=\min\{|x-1|,|x+1|\}.\] Here \(d_C(-1)=d_C(1)=0\) but \(d_C(0)=1\), so \(d_C\) is not convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_C\) is not convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of distance convexity without convexity of the generating set.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential of Convex-Set Distance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the set, distance has the normalized projection residual as its gradient; on the set its subgradients are unit normal vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\). Then \[\partial d_C(x)=\begin{cases}\left\{\dfrac{x-P_Cx}{\|x-P_Cx\|}\right\},&x\notin C,\\N_C(x)\cap\{u:\|u\|\le1\},&x\in C.\end{cases}\] In particular, \(d_C\) is Fréchet differentiable on \(H\setminus C\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inside/outside formula holds for \(\partial d_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance to a nonempty closed convex set in a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: metric projection of x onto C
convex normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Infimal-Convolution Representation of Distance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a set is the infimal convolution of its indicator with the norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) be a nonempty subset of a normed space \(X\), let \(\delta_A\) be its indicator, and let \(q(x)=\|x\|\). Then
\[
d_A(x)=(\delta_A\mathbin{\square}q)(x)=\inf_{z\in X}\{\delta_A(z)+\|x-z\|\}=\inf_{a\in A}\|x-a\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_A=\delta_A\mathbin{\square}\|\cdot\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance to an arbitrary nonempty subset of a normed space.

knowledge_statements.title: Offset-Set Representation of Distance Sublevels
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative sublevel set of distance to a closed convex set is its closed metric offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(B=\{u\in H:\|u\|\leq1\}\). For every \(r\geq0\),
\[
\{x\in H:d_C(x)\leq r\}=C+rB.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:d_C(x)\leq r\}=C+rB\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublevel geometry for distance to a nonempty closed convex set in a real Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-to-Set Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean distance to a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), its distance function is \[d_C(x)=\inf_{z\in C}\|x-z\|_2=\|x-P_C(x)\|_2,\] where \(P_C(x)\) is the unique Euclidean projection of \(x\) onto \(C\). The function \(d_C:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is convex and satisfies \(|d_C(x)-d_C(y)|\leq\|x-y\|_2\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Its zero set is exactly \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a nonempty closed convex set is convex, 1-Lipschitz, attained at the unique projection, and vanishes exactly on the set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_C\text{ is convex and }1\text{-Lipschitz, with }d_C^{-1}(0)=C

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Loss Subgradient Chain Rule
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified residual-loss subgradients are pullbacks of penalty subgradients, yielding exact stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x)=\phi(Ax-b)\), where \(\phi\) is proper convex and continuous at \(Ax-b\). Then \[\partial L(x)=A^{\mathsf T}\partial\phi(Ax-b).\] Consequently, \(x\) minimizes \(L\) iff some \(u\in\partial\phi(Ax-b)\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}u=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(\phi\) is proper convex and continuous at \(Ax-b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\phi\circ(A\cdot-b))(x)=A^{\mathsf T}\partial\phi(Ax-b)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine-composition rule under a continuity qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Residual Loss
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least squares has gradient, Hessian, normal equations, and strict-convexity boundary determined by A.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2\), \[\nabla L(x)=A^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b),\qquad \nabla^2L(x)=A^{\mathsf T}A.\] Its minimizers solve \(A^{\mathsf T}Ax=A^{\mathsf T}b\), and it is strictly convex exactly when \(A\) is injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}L=\{x:A^{\mathsf T}Ax=A^{\mathsf T}b\}\), and strict convexity holds iff \(\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical smooth quadratic member of the residual-loss family.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Loss Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying a convex penalty to an affine residual produces a convex loss, including sums of scalar convex residual penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A residual loss generated by \(\phi\) is the extended-real-valued function
\[
L(x)=\phi(r(x))=\phi(Ax-b).
\]
It is convex and satisfies
\[
L(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\leq \lambda L(x)+(1-\lambda)L(y)
\]
for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). If \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and each \(\phi_i:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is convex, then \(x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)\) is a separable residual loss.
assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual loss \(L(x)=\phi(Ax-b)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex penalties composed with affine residual maps.

notation.meaning: convex penalty applied to the residual

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Losses Cannot Redescend Nontrivially
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconstant differentiable convex loss cannot have a score returning to zero in both tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex and \[\lim_{t\to-\infty}\rho'(t)=\lim_{t\to+\infty}\rho'(t)=0,\] then \(\rho\) is constant. Thus a nonconstant differentiable convex loss cannot have influence that redescends to zero in both tails.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two-sided redescending derivative implies that \(\rho\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between convex bounded-influence and nonconvex redescending losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Influence and Lipschitz Convex Losses
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite scalar convex loss has uniformly bounded subgradients exactly when it is globally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite convex \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) and \(M\ge0\), the following are equivalent: \[|\rho(s)-\rho(t)|\le M|s-t|\quad(s,t\in\mathbb R),\] and \[\partial\rho(t)\subseteq[-M,M]\quad(t\in\mathbb R).\]
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\) is \(M\)-Lipschitz iff every subgradient has magnitude at most \(M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scalar convex losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Huber Loss as a Moreau Envelope
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Huber loss is the Moreau envelope of scaled absolute value, with soft thresholding as auxiliary minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\), \[h_\delta(t)=\min_{u\in\mathbb R}\left\{\delta|u|+\tfrac12(t-u)^2\right\}.\] The unique minimizer is \(u_\star=\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-\delta)_+\), and \(h_\delta'(t)=t-u_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_\delta(t)=\min_u\{\delta|u|+\tfrac12(t-u)^2\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational representation of the seeded Huber loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Convex Losses
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Huber loss joins a quadratic center to linear tails and is convex, continuously differentiable, and bounded in slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Huber loss is defined for \(t\in\mathbb R\) by
\[
h_\delta(t)=
\begin{cases}
\tfrac12t^2,&|t|\leq\delta,\\
\delta|t|-\tfrac12\delta^2,&|t|>\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
It is convex and continuously differentiable, with
\[
h_\delta'(t)=
\begin{cases}
t,&|t|\leq\delta,\\
\delta\operatorname{sign}(t),&|t|>\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
The loss is quadratic near zero, linear in the tails, and has slope bounded in magnitude by \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Huber loss is convex, continuously differentiable, quadratic near zero, and linear in the tails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the Huber family as the canonical robust convex residual loss.
