knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Monotone Vector Composition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradients of a cone-monotone vector composition are exactly subgradients of scalarizations generated by outer subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(a\preceq_K b\) by \(b-a\in K\), and suppose \(F\) is \(K\)-convex. Since \(h\) is \(K\)-nondecreasing, every \(y^*\in\partial h(F(\bar x))\) belongs to \(K^*\), so \(x\mapsto\langle y^*,F(x)\rangle\) is convex. Under the stated continuity assumptions,
\[
\partial(h\circ F)(\bar x)=\bigcup_{y^*\in\partial h(F(\bar x))}\partial\langle y^*,F\rangle(\bar x).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a closed convex cone, and \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is \(K\)-convex and continuous near \(\bar x\).
\(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper convex, \(K\)-nondecreasing, and continuous at \(F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(h\circ F)(\bar x)=\bigcup_{y^*\in\partial h(F(\bar x))}\partial\langle y^*,F\rangle(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional cone-ordered chain rule with continuity qualification.

notation.meaning: Order defined by the cone K
Scalarization mapping x to the dual pairing of y-star and F(x)

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the cone-monotone vector-composition container and is plausible, but no source is supplied for the exact union formula or the sufficiency of the stated cone-convexity and continuity hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), let \(F=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have finite convex components, and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex and \(K\)-nondecreasing: \(y-z\in K\Rightarrow g(y)\ge g(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, finite-valued vector composition ordered by the positive orthant. This is the sourced cone-monotone specialization; arbitrary ordering cones require a corresponding dual-cone formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone-monotone vector composition is
\[h(x)=g(F(x))=g(f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x)).\]
Its outer subgradients satisfy \(\partial g(F(x))\subseteq K^*=\mathbb R_+^m\), and its exact subdifferential is
\[\partial h(x)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^mho_i s_i:ho\in\partial g(F(x)),\ s_i\in\partial f_i(x)ight\}.\]
Equivalently,
\[\partial h(x)= igcup_{ho\in\partial g(F(x))}\sum_{i=1}^mho_i\partial f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-orthant cone-monotone vector composition applies a componentwise nondecreasing finite convex outer function to a vector of finite convex component functions. Outer subgradients lie in the dual ordering cone, so their coordinates are nonnegative. The composite subdifferential is the union, over all outer subgradients, of the corresponding nonnegative weighted Minkowski sums of the component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(g\circ F)(x)=\bigcup_{\rho\in\partial g(F(x))}\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i\partial f_i(x),\qquad\partial g(F(x))\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A vector \(u\) is in \(\partial(g\circ F)(x)\) exactly when there are \(\rho\in\partial g(F(x))\) and \(s_i\in\partial f_i(x)\) with \(u=\sum_i\rho_i s_i\).
The order condition is \(g(z+k)\ge g(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(k\in K\).
special_cases_latex: For \(g(y)=\max_i y_i\), the weights form a simplex supported on the active coordinates.
For \(g(y)=\sum_i y_i\), the only outer subgradient is \((1,\ldots,1)\), yielding the finite sum rule.
For \(m=1\), the rule is monotone scalar composition.
immediate_consequences_latex: If all functions are differentiable, \(\nabla(g\circ F)(x)=\sum_i\partial_i g(F(x))\nabla f_i(x)\).
Nondifferentiability of the outer function is represented by the choice of a weight vector in \(\partial g(F(x))\).
boundary_notes: The stated order cone is \(\mathbb R_+^m\); no unsupported arbitrary-cone chain rule is asserted.
Finite-valuedness ensures the compact subdifferentials used in the exact formula.
Without cone monotonicity, negative outer weights can invalidate convexity of the composition.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the ordering cone; here K*=R⁺ᵐ.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active and nearby-active calculus for convex suprema
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\) be an index set, let \(f_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and assume \(f(x)=\sup_{j\in J}f_j(x)<+\infty\) for every \(x\). Define \(J(x)=\{j:f_j(x)=f(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional finite-valued suprema. The calculus distinguishes the unconditional active inclusion, compact-index exactness, and qualification-free recovery by nearby points and almost-active indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extremum subdifferential calculus is organized by
\[\overline{\operatorname{co}}\! igcup_{j\in J(x)}\partial f_j(x)\subseteq\partial f(x).\]
If \(J\) is compact and \(j\mapsto f_j(y)\) is upper semicontinuous for every \(y\), then
\[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\! igcup_{j\in J(x)}\partial f_j(x).\]
Without these assumptions, define \(J_\delta(x_0)=\{j:f_j(x_0)\ge f(x_0)-\delta\}\) and
\[S_\delta= igcup_{\substack{j\in J_\delta(x_0)\\|x-x_0\|\le\delta}}\partial f_j(x).\]
Then the general recovery formula is
\[\partial f(x_0)= igcap_{\delta>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}S_\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extremum subdifferential calculus uses active indices for exact compactly indexed suprema and nearby almost-active indices for general suprema. Active component subgradients always generate a subset of the supremum subdifferential. Compactness and upper semicontinuity make the active convex hull exact. Without them, exact recovery requires closed convex hulls of subgradients evaluated both at almost-active indices and at nearby points, followed by intersection as the tolerance tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(x_0)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}\bigcup_{\substack{j\in J_\delta(x_0)\\\|x-x_0\|\le\delta}}\partial f_j(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under compact-index upper-semicontinuity, nearby almost-active recovery collapses to the convex hull of subdifferentials at exactly active indices.
The unconditional inclusion means every active component subgradient is a subgradient of the supremum.
special_cases_latex: For finite \(J\), compactness and upper semicontinuity are automatic, giving the finite-maximum rule.
If all active \(f_j\) are differentiable, the exact compact-index formula is the convex hull of their active gradients.
immediate_consequences_latex: Almost-active indices repair the possibility that \(J(x_0)\) is empty.
Nearby evaluation repairs examples where all subdifferentials at \(x_0\) are too small to generate \(\partial f(x_0)\).
boundary_notes: Almost-active indices alone are insufficient in the fully general formula; nearby points are also required.
Closure cannot generally be removed from the qualification-free recovery formula.
The supremum is assumed finite-valued on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) in the cited general result.

notation.meaning: Union of component subdifferentials at nearby points for delta-active indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Maximum Rules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a finite maximum is the convex hull of the subdifferentials of the active functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\) and \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\). Then only active functions contribute, and the exact maximum rule is
\[
\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x)\right).
\]
Equivalently, every subgradient is a convex combination of subgradients selected from active pieces.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is finite and continuous at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional rule for a finite maximum.

notation.meaning: Indices attaining the maximum at x

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The active-piece convex-hull formula is standard and appropriately classified as a representation, but the record supplies no inspectable source with a section, theorem, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-piece convex-hull rule for a finite maximum
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions and define \(f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\). The active index set is \(I(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=f(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional finite maxima of finite-valued convex functions. The active set is nonempty and finite, so no closure or approximate-activity construction is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The finite maximum rule is
\[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left( igcup_{i\in I(x)}\partial f_i(x)ight).\]
Equivalently, \(u\in\partial f(x)\) exactly when there exist coefficients \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and vectors \(u_i\in\partial f_i(x)\), indexed by \(i\in I(x)\), such that
\[\sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i=1,\qquad u=\sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i u_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the pointwise maximum of finitely many finite convex functions, the subdifferential at a point is the convex hull of the subdifferentials of precisely the active functions. Thus every subgradient of the maximum is a convex combination of subgradients chosen from active pieces, and every such convex combination is a subgradient of the maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial\!\left(\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\right)(x)=\operatorname{co}\bigcup_{i:f_i(x)=f(x)}\partial f_i(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\partial f(x)=\left\{\sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i u_i:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i=1,\ u_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\]
The rule is the monotone-vector composition formula for \(g(y)=\max_i y_i\), whose subdifferential is the simplex supported on active coordinates.
special_cases_latex: If \(I(x)=\{k\}\), then \(\partial f(x)=\partial f_k(x)\).
If every active function is differentiable at \(x\), then \(\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_i(x):i\in I(x)\}\).
For affine pieces \(f_i(x)=\langle a_i,x\rangle+b_i\), \(\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\{a_i:i\in I(x)\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition \(0\in\partial f(x)\) is equivalent to the existence of active subgradients whose convex combination is zero.
If exactly one piece is active and differentiable, the maximum is differentiable at that point with the same gradient.
boundary_notes: Inactive functions contribute no subgradients to the formula.
The finite-valued hypothesis avoids additional domain-normal terms.
For infinite index sets, compactness, upper semicontinuity, closure, or nearby almost-active constructions may be necessary.

notation.meaning: Set of indices attaining the finite maximum at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Index Supremum Rules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a jointly continuous compact family, the supremum subdifferential is the convex hull of active component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sup_{t\in T}f_t(x)\). Compactness and joint continuity ensure that the supremum is attained locally and that \(T(\bar x)=\{t\in T:f_t(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\) is nonempty and compact. The subdifferential is
\[
\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{t\in T(\bar x)}\partial f_t(\bar x)\right).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is compact and each \(f_t:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex.
The mapping \((x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)\) is jointly continuous on \(U\times T\) for a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{t\in T(\bar x)}\partial f_t(\bar x)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-index exact supremum rule under joint continuity.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The claimed active-index representation matches the terminal container, but an authoritative source is needed to confirm that compactness and the stated joint continuity alone yield the exact formula without an additional closure or qualification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\) be a compact metric space and let \(f_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(j\in J\), be finite convex functions such that \(j\mapsto f_j(y)\) is upper semicontinuous for every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, finite-valued convex analysis with a compact index set and pointwise upper semicontinuity in the index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the supremum function and its active-index set by \[f(y):=\sup_{j\in J}f_j(y),\qquad J(x):=\{j\in J:f_j(x)=f(x)\}.\] The compact-index supremum rule is the identity \[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{j\in J(x)}\partial f_j(x)\right).\] Compactness and upper semicontinuity ensure that \(J(x)\) is nonempty and compact. If every \(f_j\) is differentiable, the generating set reduces to the active gradients: \[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_j(x):j\in J(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pointwise supremum of finite convex functions indexed by a compact metric space, with upper-semicontinuous dependence on the index, the active indices at \(x\) are those attaining the supremum. The compact-index rule identifies the subdifferential of the supremum with the convex hull of the subdifferentials of the active functions. In the differentiable case it is the convex hull of the active gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{j\in J(x)}\partial f_j(x)\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable members, \(\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla f_j(x):j\in J(x)\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(J(x)=\{j_x\}\) and \(f_{j_x}\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\) and \(\nabla f(x)=\nabla f_{j_x}(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The active set is nonempty because an upper-semicontinuous real function on compact \(J\) attains its maximum.
boundary_notes: Without compactness or upper semicontinuity, the active set may be empty and active subgradients alone need not recover the full subdifferential.
The stated rule is finite-dimensional and does not assert an infinite-dimensional weak-star analogue.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate-active closure calculus for arbitrary suprema
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\) be arbitrary, let \(f_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and suppose \(f:=\sup_{j\in J}f_j\) is finite on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Fix \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, finite-valued convex supremum calculus without compactness or attainment of the index supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\), define the approximately active indices and nearby subgradients by \[J_\delta(x_0):=\{j\in J:f_j(x_0)\ge f(x_0)-\delta\},\] \[S_\delta(x_0):=\bigcup\{\partial f_j(x):j\in J_\delta(x_0),\ \|x-x_0\|\le\delta\}.\] The general supremum closure object at \(x_0\) is \[\mathcal G(x_0):=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}S_\delta(x_0).\] General supremum closure calculus identifies this object with the convex subdifferential: \[\partial f(x_0)=\mathcal G(x_0).\] Thus approximate activity, nearby base points, convexification, closure, and intersection over all tolerances replace an exact active-index formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a general index family, exact maximizers may not exist. At each tolerance \(\delta\), retain indices whose value at \(x_0\) is within \(\delta\) of the supremum and collect their subgradients at points within distance \(\delta\) of \(x_0\). The closed convex hulls of these sets form a decreasing family, and their intersection is the subdifferential of the supremum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f(x_0)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}S_\delta(x_0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: It suffices to intersect along any sequence \(\delta_k\downarrow0\): \(\partial f(x_0)=\bigcap_k\overline{\operatorname{co}}S_{\delta_k}(x_0)\).
special_cases_latex: When the compact-index hypotheses make exact active indices stable, the construction collapses to the convex hull of active subdifferentials.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every exact active subgradient belongs to each sufficiently enlarged approximate-active construction.
boundary_notes: Dropping the nearby-point component can lose limiting subgradients.
The formula assumes the supremum is finite-valued; extended-valued variants require additional domain qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Active Indices
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An index is epsilon-active when its value lies within epsilon of the supremum at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a family \((f_t)_{t\in T}\) with \(f(x)=\sup_{t\in T}f_t(x)<+\infty\), the set of \(\varepsilon\)-active indices at \(x\) is
\[
T_\varepsilon(x):=\{t\in T:f_t(x)\ge f(x)-\varepsilon\}.
\]
Thus \(T_0(x)\) is the exact active set, while \(T_\varepsilon(x)\) may be nonempty even when the supremum is not attained.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sup_{t\in T}f_t(x)\) is finite at the point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\varepsilon(x)=\{t\in T:f_t(x)\ge f(x)-\varepsilon\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate activity for arbitrary supremum families.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, internally consistent, and correctly placed, but the record contains neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale satisfying the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex-Hull Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general supremum subdifferential is recovered by intersecting closed convex hulls of epsilon-subgradients from epsilon-active functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(T_\varepsilon(\bar x)=\{t:f_t(\bar x)\ge f(\bar x)-\varepsilon\}\), the general supremum formula is
\[
\partial f(\bar x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\!\left(\bigcup_{t\in T_\varepsilon(\bar x)}\partial_\varepsilon f_t(\bar x)\right).
\]
The intersection removes the approximation error, while closure and convexification retain limiting mixtures of subgradients whose indices need not be exactly active.
assumptions_latex: \(f=\sup_{t\in T}f_t\) is proper convex and finite and continuous at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial f(\bar x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\bigl(\bigcup_{t\in T_\varepsilon(\bar x)}\partial_\varepsilon f_t(\bar x)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional recovery using approximate activity and closed convexification.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation belongs in the closed convex-hull recovery container, but the exact use of the same epsilon for activity and approximate subdifferentials, together with the stated hypotheses, requires authoritative source validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Index Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noncompact affine family can have no active index even though its supremum has a nonempty subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
f(x)=\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\left(x-\frac1n\right)=x,
\]
but no finite index attains the supremum. Hence \(T(x)=\varnothing\), whereas \(\partial f(x)=\{1\}\). Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{n\in T(x)}\partial f_n(x)\right)=\varnothing\ne\partial f(x).
\]
Approximate active indices are therefore indispensable in this noncompact regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(x)=\varnothing\) but \(\partial f(x)=\{1\}\), so the exact active-index formula fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of exact activity without compactness or attainment.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex marginal function and minimizing-fiber calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(Y=\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and jointly convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex partial minimization; lower semicontinuity and attainment are recorded separately rather than inferred from convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The marginal function, minimizing fiber, and approximate minimizing fiber are \[p(x):=\inf_{y\in Y}g(x,y),\qquad M(x):=\{y:g(x,y)=p(x)\},\] \[M_\varepsilon(x):=\{y:g(x,y)\le p(x)+\varepsilon\}\quad(\varepsilon>0).\] Equivalently, with the projection \(A:X\times Y\to X\), \(A(x,y)=x\), the marginal is the infimal image \[(Ag)(x):=\inf\{g(z):Az=x\}=p(x).\] Whenever \(p(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\), joint convexity makes \(p\) convex. The associated exact attained-fiber subgradient object is \[\{u\in X:(u,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\},\qquad y\in M(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal-marginal calculus begins with a jointly convex extended-real function and eliminates the second variable by taking an infimum. It records the value function \(p\), the exact minimizer set \(M\), and the approximate minimizer sets \(M_\varepsilon\). The same operation is the infimal image of \(g\) under the coordinate projection. At an attained fiber, marginal subgradients are represented by joint subgradients whose eliminated-coordinate component is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}g(x,y)=(Ag)(x),\qquad M(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}g(x,y).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The strict epigraph of \(p\) is the projection of the strict epigraph of \(g\) onto \(X\times\mathbb{R}\).
special_cases_latex: Infimal convolution is obtained from \(g(x,y)=f_1(y)+f_2(x-y)\).
Linear elimination is obtained by replacing the coordinate projection with a general surjective linear map.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g\) is jointly convex and the marginal never equals \(-\infty\), then \(p\) is convex.
boundary_notes: Joint convexity does not by itself guarantee that \(p\) is lower semicontinuous or that \(M(x)\) is nonempty.
The exact subgradient representation requires an attained minimizing fiber.

children.title: Danskin Value-Function Family
children.top_down_role: Value-function subgradients organized through optimizer sets and active parameter selections.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Y\) be a compact metric space and \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy: \(x\mapsto\phi(x,y)\) is finite convex for every \(y\), and \(y\mapsto\phi(x,y)\) is upper semicontinuous for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex maximization value functions with compact parameter sets; the differentiable specialization uses gradients with respect to the decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the value function and optimizer set by \[V(x):=\max_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y),\qquad Y(x):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y).\] The Danskin subgradient family at \(x\) is \[\mathcal D(x):=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{y\in Y(x)}\partial_x\phi(x,y)\right).\] Under the stated compactness and semicontinuity hypotheses, \(Y(x)\neq\varnothing\), and the associated value-function rule is \[\partial V(x)=\mathcal D(x).\] If every \(x\mapsto\phi(x,y)\) is differentiable, then \(\mathcal D(x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla_x\phi(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Danskin family consists of a maximum value function, its set of maximizing parameters, and the convex hull of the decision-variable subgradients selected at those maximizers. Compactness and upper semicontinuity give an attained optimizer set, and the family equals the convex subdifferential of the value function. For smooth parameterized functions, only the gradients at maximizing parameters are needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial V(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{y\in Y(x)}\partial_x\phi(x,y)\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the differentiable case, \(\partial V(x)=\operatorname{co}\{\nabla_x\phi(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Y(x)=\{y(x)\}\) and \(\phi(\cdot,y(x))\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(\nabla V(x)=\nabla_x\phi(x,y(x))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiple maximizers generate a convex set of possible value-function subgradients.
boundary_notes: This record uses a maximizing value function; minimizing value functions require joint-convex marginal calculus rather than a sign change without further hypotheses.
Uniqueness of an optimizer is sufficient for the displayed smooth specialization but is not part of the general definition.

children.title: Attained Value-Function Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Attained Value-Function Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any attained minimizer, value-function subgradients are exactly joint subgradients whose optimizer-coordinate component is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar y\in Y(\bar x)\). Attainment gives \(F(\bar x,\bar y)=p(\bar x)\), and the exact marginal relation is
\[
u\in\partial p(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (u,0)\in\partial F(\bar x,\bar y).
\]
This equivalence holds for every \(\bar y\in Y(\bar x)\); thus the projected subgradient description is independent of which minimizing selection is chosen.
assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\inf_y F(x,y)\) is finite at \(\bar x\), and \(Y(\bar x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_yF(\bar x,y)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in\partial p(\bar x)\iff (u,0)\in\partial F(\bar x,\bar y)\) for every \(\bar y\in Y(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex marginal rule when the infimum is attained.

notation.meaning: Zero vector in the y-dual component

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The attained marginal equivalence is mathematically plausible and correctly classified as a representation, but no inspectable source is supplied for the exact every-minimizer formulation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y)\), where each \(\phi(\cdot,y)\) is finite convex, and fix \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise attained convex maximum-value functions; compactness is one sufficient mechanism for attainment but is not built into the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The value function is in an attained regime at \(x\) when \[Y(x):=\{y\in Y:\phi(x,y)=V(x)\}\neq\varnothing.\] Its active selection graph and selected-subgradient set are \[\operatorname{gph}Y:=\{(x,y):y\in Y(x)\},\qquad G(x):=\bigcup_{y\in Y(x)}\partial_x\phi(x,y).\] An attained exact-selection regime is one for which the value-function subdifferential is generated without limiting approximate optimizers: \[\partial V(x)=\operatorname{co}G(x).\] For a minimizing marginal \(p(x)=\inf_y g(x,y)\), the analogous attained condition is \(M(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)\neq\varnothing\), with selected joint subgradients satisfying \((u,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained value-function regime is a point where the supremum or infimum defining the value is realized by at least one parameter. The optimizer mapping, its graph, and the subgradients selected from exact optimizers are explicit objects. In an exact-selection regime these selected subgradients, after convexification for a maximum value function, generate the full value-function subdifferential without closure over approximate optimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Y(x)\neq\varnothing,\qquad \partial V(x)=\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{y\in Y(x)}\partial_x\phi(x,y)\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Attainment means that the optimal value belongs to \(\{\phi(x,y):y\in Y\}\), rather than merely to its closure.
special_cases_latex: A compact parameter set with upper-semicontinuous parameter dependence yields attainment.
A singleton optimizer set gives a single selected subdifferential.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact optimizer selections can be used directly in the active subgradient formula.
boundary_notes: Attainment alone does not guarantee the exact subdifferential identity; the appropriate compactness, semicontinuity, or marginal hypotheses remain necessary.
Nonattained values require approximate-selection closure objects.

notation.meaning: union of subdifferentials selected by exact optimizers

children.title: Approximate-Selection Recovery Boundary
children.top_down_role: Closure and approximate-selection structures when exact optimizers are unavailable.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y)\) be finite and convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with no assumption that the supremum is attained. Fix \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex maximum-value functions at the boundary between exact optimizer selection and recovery from approximate selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), define the approximate optimizer set \[Y_\varepsilon(x_0):=\{y\in Y:\phi(x_0,y)\ge V(x_0)-\varepsilon\}.\] Define the nearby approximate-selection subgradient set \[G_\varepsilon(x_0):=\bigcup\{\partial_x\phi(x,y):y\in Y_\varepsilon(x_0),\ \|x-x_0\|\le\varepsilon\}.\] The approximate-selection recovery object is \[\mathcal R(x_0):=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}G_\varepsilon(x_0).\] The recovery boundary separates exact selection, where an optimizer set generates \(\partial V(x_0)\) directly, from nonattainment, where the closure-intersection object is required. In the supported finite-valued convex regime, \(\partial V(x_0)=\mathcal R(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When exact optimizers are unavailable, one selects parameters whose values are arbitrarily close to optimal, permits their subgradients to be evaluated at nearby points, then takes closed convex hulls and intersects over vanishing tolerances. This limiting object is the approximate-selection recovery object and recovers the value-function subdifferential in the finite-dimensional finite-valued convex setting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal R(x_0)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\operatorname{co}}G_\varepsilon(x_0)=\partial V(x_0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Recovery may be computed along any sequence \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: If stable exact optimizers exist, the limiting construction reduces to the active-optimizer formula.
immediate_consequences_latex: The construction remains meaningful when \(Y(x_0)=\varnothing\).
boundary_notes: Approximate optimality at \(x_0\) alone may be insufficient; nearby evaluation points are part of the recovery construction.
The record does not claim compactness of approximate optimizer sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattained Infima
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex marginal can have subgradients although its infimum is never attained, making exact-selection formulas empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(F(x,y)=x+e^y\) is finite and convex. For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
p(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}}(x+e^y)=x,
\]
yet the infimum is not attained because \(e^y>0\) for every finite \(y\). Therefore \(\partial p(x)=\{1\}\), while the union of projected joint subgradients over exact minimizers is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(x)=x\) and \(\partial p(x)=\{1\}\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_yF(x,y)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment invalidates formulas requiring an exact minimizing selection.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Optimizer Selections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-optimizer selection chooses a feasible point whose objective value is within epsilon of the marginal infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)>-\infty\), define the \(\varepsilon\)-optimizer set by
\[
Y_\varepsilon(x):=\{y\in Y:F(x,y)\le p(x)+\varepsilon\}.
\]
A mapping \(y_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(y_\varepsilon(x)\in Y_\varepsilon(x)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-optimizer selection. Exact optimizers correspond to \(\varepsilon=0\), whereas positive tolerances permit recovery when the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_\varepsilon(x)=\{y\in Y:F(x,y)\le p(x)+\varepsilon\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate minimizing selections for possibly unattained marginals.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The epsilon-optimizer definition is precise and fits the terminal container, but no citation or explicit standard-field rationale is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing and intersecting horizontal approximate joint subgradients over increasingly accurate minimizers recovers the marginal subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(Y_\varepsilon(\bar x)=\{y:F(\bar x,y)\le p(\bar x)+\varepsilon\}\). Then
\[
\partial p(\bar x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\{u:\exists y\in Y_\varepsilon(\bar x),\ (u,0)\in\partial_{2\varepsilon}F(\bar x,y)\}}.
\]
Thus exact marginal subgradients are recovered as closed limits of horizontal approximate joint subgradients evaluated at increasingly accurate optimizer selections.
assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial p(\bar x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\{u:\exists y\in Y_\varepsilon(\bar x),\ (u,0)\in\partial_{2\varepsilon}F(\bar x,y)\}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional marginal recovery from approximate minimizers and approximate subgradients.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and recovery theme fit the container, but the exact factor 2 epsilon, the requirement that the optimizer-coordinate subgradient be exactly zero, and the sufficiency of the stated lower-semicontinuity assumptions cannot be accepted without an authoritative theorem-level source.

children.title: Infimal-Convolution Rule Family
children.top_down_role: Subgradient compatibility organized by exact and nonattained decompositions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions with a common affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex infimal convolution, distinguishing exact from nonattained decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal convolution is \[(f_1\square f_2)(x):=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f_1(y)+f_2(x-y)\}=\inf_{x_1+x_2=x}\{f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\}.\] Its exact decomposition set and \(\varepsilon\)-decomposition set are \[D(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)=(f_1\square f_2)(x)\},\] \[D_\varepsilon(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\le(f_1\square f_2)(x)+\varepsilon\}.\] For \((x_1,x_2)\in D(x)\), the compatible-subgradient set is \[C(x_1,x_2):=\partial f_1(x_1)\cap\partial f_2(x_2),\] and the exact infimal-convolution rule is \(\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=C(x_1,x_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal convolution minimizes the sum of two functions over all decompositions of \(x\). The rule family records exact and approximate decomposition sets. At an exact decomposition, a subgradient is compatible when it belongs simultaneously to the subdifferential of the first term at the first component and that of the second term at the second component; this common set is the subdifferential of the infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=\partial f_1(x_1)\cap\partial f_2(x_2)\quad\text{for }(x_1,x_2)\in D(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The operation is the infimal image of \((x_1,x_2)\mapsto f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\) under \((x_1,x_2)\mapsto x_1+x_2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f_2(z)=\|z\|^2/2\), the operation is a Moreau-type regularization.
immediate_consequences_latex: At any two exact decompositions, the displayed intersection represents the same set \(\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)\).
boundary_notes: Even for closed convex inputs, an infimal convolution need not be closed.
The exact intersection formula requires \(D(x)\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Exact Infimal Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Subgradient structure supported by attained infimal decompositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Infimal Decompositions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attained infimal decomposition, the infimal-convolution subdifferential is the intersection of the component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
(f\square g)(\bar x)=f(\bar z)+g(\bar x-\bar z).
\]
Then the subdifferential of the infimal convolution is exactly
\[
\partial(f\square g)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar z)\cap\partial g(\bar x-\bar z).
\]
Hence a vector is a subgradient of the marginal value precisely when it is simultaneously a subgradient of both terms at the two components of the attained decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \((f\square g)(\bar x)=\inf_z\{f(z)+g(\bar x-z)\}\) is finite and attained at \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f\square g)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar z)\cap\partial g(\bar x-\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact infimal-convolution rule at an attained decomposition.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The attained infimal-convolution intersection formula matches the terminal container and is correctly classified as a representation, but the record provides no inspectable source locator supporting the exact statement.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact infimal decomposition and common subgradient
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions whose infimal convolution is proper, and fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(f_1\square f_2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise attained infimal convolution in finite-dimensional convex analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\) is an exact infimal decomposition of \(x\) when \[\bar x_1+\bar x_2=x,\qquad (f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(\bar x_1)+f_2(\bar x_2).\] The infimal convolution is exact at \(x\) if at least one such pair exists. Its common-subgradient certificate set is \[K(x;\bar x_1,\bar x_2):=\partial f_1(\bar x_1)\cap\partial f_2(\bar x_2).\] Under the standard common-affine-minorant regime, exactness yields \[\partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=K(x;\bar x_1,\bar x_2).\] Exactness does not require the decomposition to be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact infimal decomposition is a feasible splitting of \(x\) that attains the infimum defining the infimal convolution. Associated with any exact splitting is the intersection of the two component subdifferentials. In the supported convex regime, this intersection equals the subdifferential of the infimal convolution and therefore does not depend on which exact decomposition is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f_1\square f_2)(x)=f_1(\bar x_1)+f_2(\bar x_2),\qquad \partial(f_1\square f_2)(x)=\partial f_1(\bar x_1)\cap\partial f_2(\bar x_2).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exactness is equivalent to \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_1+x_2=x}[f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)]\).
special_cases_latex: If one component is differentiable at its exact component, every common subgradient must equal that component gradient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different exact decompositions produce the same common-subgradient set whenever the exact rule applies.
boundary_notes: Exactness is a pointwise property and need not hold at every point of the domain.
Exactness does not imply that the infimal convolution is globally lower semicontinuous.

children.title: Infimal-Convolution Attainment Boundary
children.top_down_role: Infimal-convolution behavior requiring closure or approximate decompositions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h=f_1\square f_2\) be a proper convex infimal convolution on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise nonattainment and closure phenomena for finite-dimensional convex infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), define \[D_\varepsilon(x):=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=x,\ f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)\le h(x)+\varepsilon\}.\] The point \(x\) lies on the infimal-convolution attainment boundary when \[D_\varepsilon(x)\neq\varnothing\ \text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad D_0(x)=\varnothing.\] A sequence \((x_{1,k},x_{2,k})\) is an approximate decomposition if \(x_{1,k}+x_{2,k}=x\) and \[f_1(x_{1,k})+f_2(x_{2,k})\downarrow h(x).\] The closed infimal convolution is the lower-semicontinuous hull \[\overline h:=\operatorname{cl}h,\qquad \operatorname{epi}\overline h=\overline{\operatorname{epi}h}.\] These objects distinguish failure of minimizer attainment from failure of epigraphical closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attainment-boundary point, arbitrarily accurate decompositions exist but no exact minimizing decomposition exists. Approximate decomposition sequences approach the infimal value while their components may escape or fail to converge. Separately, the infimal convolution may fail to be lower semicontinuous, in which case its epigraphical closure is recorded by the lower-semicontinuous hull. Nonattainment and nonclosedness are distinct boundary phenomena.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D_0(x)=\varnothing,\qquad D_\varepsilon(x)\neq\varnothing\ \ (\forall\varepsilon>0),\qquad \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}h)=\overline{\operatorname{epi}h}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Nonattainment means that the infimum defining \(h(x)\) is finite but is not a minimum.
special_cases_latex: If an approximate decomposition sequence has a convergent subsequence and both functions are lower semicontinuous at its limit components, the boundary point becomes attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: The exact common-subgradient formula cannot be invoked through a pair in \(D_0(x)\) when that set is empty.
boundary_notes: Nonattainment does not by itself imply \(h(x)\ne(\operatorname{cl}h)(x)\).
The record defines the boundary objects but does not assert a general approximate-subgradient equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Corrected Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a sum is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimal convolution of the conjugates; attainment or qualification can make the closure unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x^*\in X^*\), define \((f^*\square g^*)(x^*)=\inf\{f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*):u^*+v^*=x^*\}\). The conjugate of the sum satisfies \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)(x^*).\] Thus closure is required unless an additional qualification guarantees that the infimal convolution is lower semicontinuous. When the infimum is attained and no closure gap occurs, the right-hand side equals the minimum over exact dual decompositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conjugate representation when the dual infimum need not be attained.

source_witnesses.locator: 12 Infimal Convolution p. 203

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattained Decompositions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two closed convex functions can have a finite infimal convolution whose defining decomposition infimum is never attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The functions \(p(u)=e^u\) and \(q(v)=0\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(y\in\mathbb R\), \[(p\square q)(y)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R}\bigl(e^u+q(y-u)\bigr)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R}e^u=0.\] No finite \(u\) realizes this value. Hence the infimal convolution is finite and closed, while every exact decomposition \(y=u+(y-u)\) has objective value strictly greater than its infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p\square q)(y)=0\) for every \(y\), but no minimizing decomposition exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional example showing that closed convex summands do not ensure decomposition attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Decomposition Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate minimizers and approximate subgradients combine additively into an approximate subgradient certificate for the infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=u+v\) be an \(\eta\)-optimal decomposition, meaning \(f(u)+g(v)\le h(x)+\eta\). If a common vector satisfies \(x^*\in\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f(u)\cap\partial_{\varepsilon_2}g(v)\), then it provides the checkable certificate \[x^*\in\partial_{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2+\eta}h(x).\] The three errors respectively measure the two inexact subgradient inequalities and the failure of the chosen primal decomposition to attain the infimal convolution.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper convex functions and \(h=f\square g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\partial_{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2+\eta}h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A verifiable approximate substitute for an unattained exact infimal-convolution decomposition.

notation.meaning: The epsilon-subdifferential of a convex function.

children.title: Linear-Elimination Calculus
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential behavior under elimination through linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal image under a linear mapping
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a surjective linear map and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex and bounded below on every fiber \(A^{-1}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex elimination through a surjective linear mapping, with an attained fiber at the point of subdifferentiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal image of \(g\) under \(A\) and its minimizing fiber are \[(Ag)(x):=\inf\{g(y):Ay=x\},\qquad Y(x):=\{y:Ay=x,\ g(y)=(Ag)(x)\}.\] If \(Y(x)\neq\varnothing\), the linear-elimination subgradient set is \[E(x;y):=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^*s\in\partial g(y)\},\qquad y\in Y(x).\] The calculus rule is \[\partial(Ag)(x)=E(x;y).\] Hence the set is independent of the chosen minimizing fiber point. For the coordinate projection \(A(x,y)=x\), this becomes \[\partial p(x)=\{s:(s,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-elimination calculus defines a value function by minimizing a convex function over each affine fiber of a surjective linear map. At an attained fiber, a vector is a subgradient of the value function exactly when its adjoint lift is a subgradient of the original function at a minimizing point. Coordinate projection gives ordinary partial minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial(Ag)(x)=\{s:A^*s\in\partial g(y)\}\quad\text{for every }y\in Y(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For coordinate elimination, \(A^*s=(s,0)\), so \(\partial p(x)=\{s:(s,0)\in\partial g(x,y)\}\).
special_cases_latex: The addition map \(A(y_1,y_2)=y_1+y_2\) produces infimal convolution.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g\) is differentiable at a minimizing fiber point, injectivity of \(A^*\) gives at most one marginal subgradient.
boundary_notes: If the fiber minimum is not attained, the displayed formula has no minimizing point at which to evaluate \(\partial g\).
Nonsurjective maps require restriction to the range and corresponding relative-space conventions.

notation.meaning: infimal image of g under A

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Marginals
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a linear-image marginal equals the original conjugate composed with the adjoint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linear-image marginal by \[g(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=y\},\] using \(+\infty\) when the fiber is empty. Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\), its Fenchel conjugate is \[g^*(y^*)=f^*(A^*y^*).\] This identity does not require fiberwise attainment. Lower-semicontinuity of \(g\), however, is a separate issue and can fail when projected epigraphs or relevant ranges are not closed.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate representation for a convex function projected through a linear map.

notation.meaning: Marginal value over the fiber of the linear image.

knowledge_statements.title: Infimal Postcomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal postcomposition assigns to each image point the infimum of the function over its linear fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal postcomposition of \(f\) by \(A\) is the function \(A\triangleright f:Y\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) defined by \[(A\triangleright f)(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=y\}.\] The infimum over an empty fiber is \(+\infty\). Thus the operation eliminates the variable \(x\) subject to its linear image being fixed; it may take the value \(-\infty\) unless additional assumptions exclude unbounded descent along a fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A\triangleright f)(y)=\inf_{Ax=y}f(x)\), with value \(+\infty\) on empty fibers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extended-real definition of elimination along fibers of a linear map.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition of the function by the linear map.

knowledge_statements.title: Fiberwise Attainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a minimizing point of a fiber, marginal subgradients correspond exactly to original subgradients lying in the adjoint image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that \(\bar x\) attains the fiberwise infimum defining \(g(\bar y)\), so \(A\bar x=\bar y\) and \(f(\bar x)=g(\bar y)\). Then every \(y^*\in Y^*\) satisfies the equivalence \[y^*\in\partial g(\bar y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A^*y^*\in\partial f(\bar x).\] Consequently, attainment converts the subgradient inequality for the marginal into an exact subgradient condition at a minimizing preimage.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper convex and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^*\in\partial g(\bar y)\iff A^*y^*\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subgradient transfer at a fiberwise minimizer.

notation.meaning: A point attaining the marginal infimum on the fiber over \(\bar y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Closure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclosed operator range makes the marginal of even the zero function non-lower-semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in Y\), the marginal of the zero function is \[(A\triangleright f)(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\in\operatorname{ran}A,\\+\infty,&y\notin\operatorname{ran}A.\end{cases}\] Hence \(A\triangleright f=\iota_{\operatorname{ran}A}\). If \(\operatorname{ran}A\) is not closed, this convex marginal is not lower-semicontinuous, although \(f\) itself is continuous and every nonempty fiber attains its infimum. Closedness of the projected range is therefore a genuine boundary for closure-free image calculus.
assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is bounded linear with nonclosed range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A\triangleright f)=\iota_{\operatorname{ran}A}\) is not lower-semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonclosed operator ranges obstruct lower-semicontinuity of linear-image marginals.

notation.meaning: Indicator function of a set, zero on the set and positive infinity outside.

children.title: Set-Induced Subdifferential Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone and exposed-face rules obtained through indicator and support representations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indicator, normal cone, support function, and exposed face
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-set calculus induced by indicator and support-function representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the indicator and support functions by \[\delta_C(x):=\begin{cases}0,&x\in C,\\+\infty,&x\notin C,\end{cases}\qquad \sigma_C(u):=\sup_{z\in C}\langle u,z\rangle.\] For \(x\in C\), the normal cone is \[N_C(x):=\{u:\langle u,z-x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }z\in C\}=\partial\delta_C(x).\] For \(u\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_C\), the exposed face is \[F_C(u):=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_C(u)\}.\] Whenever the supremum is attained, \[F_C(u)=\partial\sigma_C(u),\qquad u\in N_C(x)\Longleftrightarrow x\in F_C(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set-induced subdifferential calculus represents a closed convex set through its indicator and support functions. The indicator subdifferential is the normal cone. A direction exposes the points maximizing its linear functional; this exposed face is the support-function subdifferential when the maximum is attained. Normality and exposed-face membership are reciprocal descriptions of the same pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_C(x)=\partial\delta_C(x),\qquad F_C(u)=\partial\sigma_C(u),\qquad u\in N_C(x)\Longleftrightarrow x\in F_C(u).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(u\in N_C(x)\) is equivalent to \(\sigma_C(u)=\langle u,x\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is compact, \(F_C(u)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(u\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Support functions depend only on \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}C\).
boundary_notes: For unbounded \(C\), \(\sigma_C(u)\) may equal \(+\infty\), and an exposed face may be empty.
The normal cone is empty outside \(C\) under the convex-subdifferential convention.

notation.meaning: face of C exposed by u

children.title: Normal-Cone Intersection Rules
children.top_down_role: Qualification-dependent normal geometry for intersections.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Intersection Rules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of nonempty closed convex sets having a common relative-interior point, the normal cone to their intersection equals the sum of their individual normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be a positive integer. If the relative interiors have a common point, then at every \(\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\) the normal cone to the intersection is exactly the Minkowski sum of the individual normal cones: \[N_{\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i}(\bar x)=\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(\bar x).\] Without an appropriate qualification, the sum is always contained in the intersection normal cone, but equality and closedness of the sum need not hold.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are nonempty closed convex subsets of a finite-dimensional space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i}(\bar x)=\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional normal-cone intersection rule under relative-interior qualification.

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to a convex set.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Tangent and Normal Cones p. 125

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets, let \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\), and fix \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections of closed convex sets in finite dimensions under a relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconditional normal-cone inclusion is \[\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(x)\subseteq N_C(x).\] The family is qualified when \[\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}C_i\neq\varnothing.\] Under this qualification, the normal-cone intersection rule is exact: \[N_{\cap_{i=1}^m C_i}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m N_{C_i}(x)\] \[=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m u_i:u_i\in N_{C_i}(x)\right\}.\] Equivalently, since \(\delta_C=\sum_i\delta_{C_i}\), this is the qualified convex subdifferential sum rule for indicator functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite intersection of closed convex sets, sums of normals to the individual sets are always normal to the intersection. If the relative interiors of all sets have a common point, every normal to the intersection decomposes as a sum of individual normals. This is exactly the indicator-function subdifferential sum rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}C_i\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad N_{\cap_i C_i}(x)=\sum_iN_{C_i}(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\partial(\sum_i\delta_{C_i})(x)=\sum_i\partial\delta_{C_i}(x)\) under the same qualification.
special_cases_latex: For affine subspaces with nonempty intersection, the rule gives the sum of their orthogonal normal subspaces.
immediate_consequences_latex: A normal to a qualified intersection admits multiplier-like component normals.
boundary_notes: Without qualification, only the displayed inclusion is guaranteed; equality may fail.
The formula concerns finite intersections, not arbitrary infinite intersections.

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of the component normal cones

children.title: Normal-Cone Set-Mapping Calculus
children.top_down_role: Normal-cone constructions for products, inverse images, and affine constraints.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product and affine inverse-image normal calculus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C_i\subset\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be nonempty closed convex sets. Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty closed convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex products and affine inverse images under a relative-interior range qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_i\in C_i\), product normal calculus is \[N_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_k}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=N_{C_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_k}(x_k).\] Define the affine inverse image \[S:=\{x:Ax+b\in D\}.\] If the range qualification \[(b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap\operatorname{ri}D\neq\varnothing\] holds, then for every \(x\in S\), \[N_S(x)=A^*N_D(Ax+b)=\{A^*v:v\in N_D(Ax+b)\}.\] For the affine equality set \(S=\{x:Ax=b_0\}\), this specializes to \(N_S(x)=\operatorname{range}A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal cones factor componentwise over Cartesian products. For an affine inverse image of a convex set, a relative-interior range qualification permits every normal to be obtained by lifting a normal to the target set through the adjoint map. Affine equality constraints reduce this construction to the range of the adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\prod_iC_i}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=\prod_iN_{C_i}(x_i),\qquad N_{A^{-1}(D-b)}(x)=A^*N_D(Ax+b).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inverse-image formula is the indicator composition rule \(\partial(\delta_D\circ(A\cdot+b))(x)=A^*\partial\delta_D(Ax+b)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(D=\{b_0\}\), then \(N_{\{x:Ax+b=b_0\}}(x)=\operatorname{range}A^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Normals to separable product constraints can be chosen independently by block.
boundary_notes: Without the inverse-image qualification, the adjoint image is always a natural candidate but equality can fail.
The affine equality set must be nonempty for its normal cone to be evaluated.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear mapping A

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Set Normal Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of nonempty closed convex sets in Hilbert spaces, the normal cone to their Cartesian product is the Cartesian product of the factor normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be a positive integer. For the product set \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and any \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in C\), the normal cone separates componentwise: \[N_C(x)=N_{C_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}(x_m).\] Equivalently, \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) is normal to \(C\) at \(x\) if and only if \(u_i\in N_{C_i}(x_i)\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). No intersection qualification is required for this product identity.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\subseteq X_i\) is a nonempty closed convex set for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_m}(x)=N_{C_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times N_{C_m}(x_m)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact factorization of convex normal cones over finite Cartesian products.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Tangent and Normal Cones p. 125

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Preimage Rules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the linear range meets the set's relative interior, every preimage normal is the adjoint image of a normal to the target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the range of \(A\) meets \(\operatorname{ri}C\), then for each feasible \(x\in A^{-1}C\), \[N_{A^{-1}C}(x)=A^*N_C(Ax)=\{A^*y^*:y^*\in N_C(Ax)\}.\] Thus every normal to the preimage admits an adjoint multiplier representation. Without the range-relative-interior qualification, the right-hand side remains contained in the preimage normal cone, but the reverse inclusion may fail.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(C\subseteq Y\) is nonempty closed convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{A^{-1}C}(x)=A^*N_C(Ax)\) for every \(x\in A^{-1}C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional normal-cone preimage rule under relative-interior qualification.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Tangent and Normal Cones p. 125

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Constraint Preimages
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a qualified affine preimage, normals are target-set normals evaluated at the affine image and pulled back by the adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)=Ax+b\) and \(D=T^{-1}C\). If the affine range \(b+\operatorname{ran}A\) meets \(\operatorname{ri}C\), then every \(x\in D\) satisfies \[N_D(x)=A^*N_C(Ax+b).\] Translation affects the point at which the target normal cone is evaluated but not the adjoint multiplier map. In particular, normals to qualified affine constraints are represented by target-set normals pulled back through the linear part.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, and \(b\in Y\).
\(C\subseteq Y\) is nonempty closed convex and \(D=\{x:Ax+b\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_D(x)=A^*N_C(Ax+b)\) for every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine version of the qualified convex normal-cone preimage rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Preimage Qualification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangential contact between a linear range and a convex set can make the adjoint-normal formula strictly underestimate the preimage normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Here \(A^{-1}C=\{0\}\), so \(N_{A^{-1}C}(0)=\mathbb R\). At the tangency point, \[N_C(0,0)=\{(0,-\lambda):\lambda\ge0\},\qquad A^*(a,b)=a,\] and therefore \(A^*N_C(0,0)=\{0\}\). Hence the usual inclusion is strict. The qualification fails because \(\operatorname{ran}A\cap\operatorname{ri}C=\varnothing\): the range touches \(C\) only tangentially at its boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^*N_C(A0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=N_{A^{-1}C}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential contact gives strict failure of the unqualified normal-cone preimage equality.

children.top_down_role: Exposed-face structures induced by support-function operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Operation Rules
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support functions convert Minkowski sums and strictly positive scaling into addition and scaling; when support points exist, the associated exposed faces obey the same operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), support functions satisfy \(\sigma_{C+D}(u)=\sigma_C(u)+\sigma_D(u)\) and, for every \(\lambda>0\), \(\sigma_{\lambda C}(u)=\lambda\sigma_C(u)\). If the relevant support maxima are attained, then \(F_{C+D}(u)=F_C(u)+F_D(u)\) and \(F_{\lambda C}(u)=\lambda F_C(u)\) for \(\lambda>0\).
assumptions_latex: The support maxima defining any displayed exposed faces in direction \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{C+D}(u)=F_C(u)+F_D(u)\) and \(F_{\lambda C}(u)=\lambda F_C(u)\) for \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Minkowski addition and strictly positive scaling, restricted to directions having support points when exposed faces are used.

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1 Support Points p. 133; 7.2 Support Functions p. 135

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C,D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets, let \(t>0\), and let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional support-function calculus; exposed-face identities are asserted when the relevant support suprema are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support function is \(\sigma_C(u)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle\), and its exposed face is \(F_C(u)=\{x\in C:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_C(u)\}\). The canonical operation rules are \[\sigma_{tC}=t\sigma_C,\qquad \sigma_{C+D}=\sigma_C+\sigma_D,\qquad \sigma_{A(C)}(v)=\sigma_C(A^*v),\] \[\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)}=\max\{\sigma_C,\sigma_D\}.\] When the corresponding maxima are attained, \[F_{C+D}(u)=F_C(u)+F_D(u),\qquad F_{A(C)}(v)=A(F_C(A^*v)),\] and the exposed face of \(\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)\) is the convex hull of the faces belonging to sets attaining the larger support value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support functions transform scaling into scaling, Minkowski addition into function addition, linear images into adjoint composition, and closed convex hulls of unions into pointwise maxima. When support values are attained, the corresponding subdifferentials describe exposed faces and inherit parallel operation rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma_{C+D}=\sigma_C+\sigma_D,\quad \sigma_{A(C)}=\sigma_C\circ A^*,\quad \sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}(C\cup D)}=\max(\sigma_C,\sigma_D).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The support-function correspondence converts geometric set operations into convex functional operations.
special_cases_latex: For compact \(C\) and \(D\), all exposed faces in the displayed formulas are nonempty for every direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\sigma_C=\sigma_{\overline{\operatorname{co}}C}\), so the support function determines a closed convex set uniquely.
boundary_notes: For unbounded sets, support functions may be extended-valued.
Linear images or Minkowski sums may require closure when interpreted as closed convex sets, although their support functions are unchanged by closure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)\) be a measure space and let \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be measurable in \(\omega\) and proper lower-semicontinuous convex in \(x\) for almost every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional integral convex functionals; this candidate records the interchange object but lacks an inspected authoritative locator for the exact qualification regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the integral functional by \[I(x):=\int_\Omega f(\omega,x)\,d\mu(\omega),\] whenever the extended integral is well defined. For fixed \(x\), define the integrable subgradient-selection set \[\mathcal S(x):=\{s:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^n:s\text{ is measurable and integrable, }s(\omega)\in\partial_x f(\omega,x)\text{ a.e.}\}.\] The interchange set is the Aumann integral \[\int_\Omega\partial_x f(\omega,x)\,d\mu:=\left\{\int_\Omega s(\omega)\,d\mu:s\in\mathcal S(x)\right\}.\] An exact subdifferential-integral interchange regime is one in which \[\partial I(x)=\int_\Omega\partial_x f(\omega,x)\,d\mu.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calculus object consists of an integral convex functional, measurable integrable selections from the pointwise subdifferentials, and the set of their integrals. Exact interchange means that this selection integral equals the subdifferential of the integral functional. Measurability, integrability, normal-integrand, and qualification conditions are essential to any theorem asserting the equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial I(x)=\left\{\int_\Omega s(\omega)\,d\mu:s(\omega)\in\partial_xf(\omega,x)\ \text{a.e.}\right\}\] defines an exact interchange regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a probability measure, \(I(x)=\mathbb E[f(\omega,x)]\) and the selection integral is an expectation of measurable pointwise subgradients.
special_cases_latex: A finite atomic probability space reduces the construction to a weighted finite subdifferential sum.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every integrable pointwise subgradient selection supplies a candidate aggregate subgradient whenever the interchange equality holds.
boundary_notes: Pointwise convexity alone does not guarantee measurability, integrability, or exact interchange.
No infinite-dimensional Bochner-space or decomposability variant is asserted.
review_flags: No supplied authoritative-source hint was found to support the exact measurable-selection and subdifferential-interchange scope.
A precise normal-integrand theorem and its qualification hypotheses must be sourced before promotion.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(i=1,\ldots,N\), be proper convex functions, and let \(p_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^Np_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic scenario aggregation and sample-average functions in finite-dimensional convex analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The discrete scenario aggregate and its scenario-subgradient aggregation set are \[F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^Np_i f_i(x),\qquad \mathcal A(x):=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^Np_i s_i:s_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\] If the weighted summands satisfy a finite-sum qualification, for example \[\bigcap_{i:p_i>0}\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing,\] then the exact aggregation rule is \[\partial F(x)=\mathcal A(x)=\sum_{i=1}^Np_i\partial f_i(x).\] The sample-average specialization uses \(p_i=1/N\): \[F_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i(x),\qquad \partial F_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\partial f_i(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete scenario aggregate is a convex combination of scenario functions. Its aggregation set consists of the same convex combination of one subgradient selected from each scenario. Under the standard relative-interior qualification, this set is exactly the subdifferential of the aggregate. Equal weights give the sample-average rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^Np_if_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^Np_i\partial f_i(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s\in\partial F(x)\) exactly when \(s=\sum_ip_is_i\) for suitable \(s_i\in\partial f_i(x)\), under the stated qualification.
special_cases_latex: If every \(f_i\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(\nabla F(x)=\sum_ip_i\nabla f_i(x)\).
Equal weights yield the sample-average function.
immediate_consequences_latex: A scenario with \(p_i=0\) has no effect on the aggregate or its subdifferential.
boundary_notes: For extended-valued functions, the finite-sum qualification cannot generally be omitted.
This finite atomic rule does not by itself establish interchange for a nonatomic expectation.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a common relative-interior qualification, the subdifferential of a finite convex sum equals the Minkowski sum of the individual subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\). Under the stated common relative-interior qualification, the convex subdifferential of the finite sum is the Minkowski sum of the individual subdifferentials:
\[\partial F(x)=\partial f_1(x)+\cdots+\partial f_m(x)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m v_i:v_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\]
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional convex sum rule under a relative-interior qualification.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional Moreau–Rockafellar formula and its content kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Weighted Aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a qualified finite scenario expectation is the probability-weighted Minkowski sum of the scenario subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the scenario-weighted aggregate \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i(x)\), the relative-interior qualification yields
\[\partial F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\partial f_i(x)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m p_i v_i:v_i\in\partial f_i(x)\right\}.\]
A zero-weight scenario, if admitted, contributes \(\{0\}\) and need not participate in the domain qualification.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\partial f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete probability distribution with strictly positive scenario weights.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive scaling combined with the finite convex sum rule

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The weighted finite-sum specialization is mathematically plausible and locally appropriate, but it has no cited authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Average Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified sample-average objective has a subdifferential equal to the arithmetic average, in the Minkowski sense, of its sample-loss subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed sample \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), define \(F_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\ell(x,\xi_i)\). Under the common relative-interior qualification,
\[\partial F_N(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\partial_x\ell(x,\xi_i)=\left\{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N v_i:v_i\in\partial_x\ell(x,\xi_i)\right\}.\]
assumptions_latex: Each sample loss \(\ell(\cdot,\xi_i):\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial F_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\partial_x\ell(x,\xi_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic subdifferential structure of a fixed finite sample-average approximation.
