knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elementary Scalar, Translation, and Tilt Conjugate Rules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, let \(a\in\mathbb R\), \(\alpha>0\), \(x_0,s_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be invertible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional elementary transformations that require no constraint qualification beyond properness and the displayed positivity or invertibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The elementary transformation calculus of \(f\) is the family of transformed functions \(g\) and conjugate identities
\[g=f+a\Rightarrow g^*=f^*-a,\qquad g=\alpha f\Rightarrow g^*(s)=\alpha f^*(s/\alpha),\]
\[g=f\circ A\Rightarrow g^*=f^*\circ(A^{-1})^*,\qquad g(x)=f(x-x_0)\Rightarrow g^*(s)=f^*(s)+\langle s,x_0\rangle,\]
\[g(x)=f(x)+\langle s_0,x\rangle\Rightarrow g^*(s)=f^*(s-s_0).\]
For a product decomposition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) with product pairing and \(g(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m f_j(x_j)\), the elementary separability rule is \(g^*(s_1,\ldots,s_m)=\sum_{j=1}^m f_j^*(s_j)\). These identities collectively define the elementary calculus family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elementary conjugate calculus consists of the exact rules for vertical shifts, positive value scaling, invertible changes of variables, translations of the argument, addition of a linear functional, and separable product sums. Vertical shifts reverse sign in the conjugate; positive value scaling also rescales the dual argument; translation adds the corresponding dual linear form; a primal linear tilt translates the dual argument; and an invertible coordinate change acts through the adjoint of the inverse. Under a product pairing, conjugation preserves a separable sum component by component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f+a)^*=f^*-a,\quad (\alpha f)^*(s)=\alpha f^*(s/\alpha),\quad (f\circ A)^*=f^*\circ(A^{-1})^*,\quad (f(\cdot-x_0))^*=f^*+\langle\cdot,x_0\rangle.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tilt rule can be written \((f+\langle s_0,\cdot\rangle)^*=f^*(\cdot-s_0)\).
The translation and tilt operations are dual translations in graph coordinates.
special_cases_latex: If \(A=\beta I\) with \(\beta\ne0\), then \((f(\beta\cdot))^*(s)=f^*(s/\beta)\).
If \(a=0\), \(x_0=0\), or \(s_0=0\), the corresponding rule reduces to the identity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The order reversal property \(f_1\le f_2\Rightarrow f_1^*\ge f_2^*\) is compatible with all displayed transformations.
Known scalar or coordinatewise conjugates can be assembled without solving a new supremum.
boundary_notes: The invertible-map formula does not cover rank-deficient precomposition; that case is an infimal image formula and may require closure.
Negative value scaling is excluded because it does not preserve convexity and has no analogous Fenchel rule.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the inverse linear map.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(Y=\mathbb R^m\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear with adjoint \(A^*:Y\to X\), and let \(g:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear-map transformations; this child-level calculus isolates the dual pair formed by precomposition and infimal postcomposition, rather than scalar shifts and tilts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the infimal image of \(g\) under \(A^*\) by
\[(A^*\triangleright g^*)(s):=\inf\{g^*(p):p\in Y,\ A^*p=s\},\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the fiber is empty. Define linear precomposition by \(P_Ag=g\circ A\). The linear-map elementary calculus is the correspondence
\[(P_Ag)^*=\operatorname{cl}(A^*\triangleright g^*).\]
Dually, for a proper \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define its infimal image under \(A\) by \((A\triangleright h)(y)=\inf\{h(x):Ax=y\}\); whenever it has an affine minorant, its conjugate satisfies \((A\triangleright h)^*=h^*\circ A^*\). Thus precomposition and infimal linear image form the elementary linear transformation pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the linear-map level, elementary transformation calculus has two paired operations. Precomposition sends \(g\) to \(g\circ A\), while infimal image sends \(h\) to the function whose value at \(y\) is the infimum of \(h(x)\) over the fiber \(Ax=y\). The conjugate of precomposition is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimal image of \(g^*\) under \(A^*\). Conversely, the conjugate of a well-defined infimal image is \(h^*\circ A^*\). Exactness requires the relevant relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(g\circ A)^*=\operatorname{cl}(A^*\triangleright g^*),\qquad (A\triangleright h)^*=h^*\circ A^*.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Pointwise, \((g\circ A)^*(s)=\operatorname{cl}_s\inf_{A^*p=s}g^*(p)\).
The operation \(A\triangleright h\) is the marginal of \(h(x)+\iota_{\{y=Ax\}}(x,y)\) over \(x\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is invertible, \(A^*\triangleright g^*=g^*\circ(A^{-1})^*\), so no closure is needed.
If \(A\) is a coordinate projection, the infimal image is an ordinary marginal value function.
immediate_consequences_latex: A rank-deficient linear map generally converts a direct substitution rule into a constrained dual minimization.
Relative-interior regularity can simultaneously remove closure and guarantee attainment on each finite dual fiber.
boundary_notes: The infimal image may take \(-\infty\) unless a compatible affine minorant exists.
The notation \(A\triangleright h\) denotes infimal postcomposition, not ordinary function composition.

notation.meaning: Infimal image or infimal postcomposition of \(h\) by \(A\).
Lower-semicontinuous closure of a convex function.

knowledge_statements.title: Translation Calculus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translating the argument adds a linear term to the conjugate, while adding a linear term shifts the conjugate's dual argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g(x)=f(x-a)+c\). Then, for every \(u\in X^*\),
\[
g^*(u)=f^*(u)+\langle u,a\rangle-c.
\]
More generally, if \(h(x)=f(x-a)+\langle b,x\rangle+c\), then
\[
h^*(u)=f^*(u-b)+\langle u-b,a\rangle-c.
\]
These identities hold as extended-real equalities directly from the definition of the Fenchel conjugate; no convexity or lower-semicontinuity assumption on \(f\) is required.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Translations and affine perturbations become explicit affine changes of the conjugate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Argument translations, vertical shifts, and linear perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Calculus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying function values by a positive scalar rescales conjugate values and arguments; invertible scalar precomposition inversely rescales the dual argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(g(x)=\alpha f(x)\), then for every \(u\in X^*\),
\[
g^*(u)=\alpha f^*(u/\alpha).
\]
If \(h(x)=f(sx)\), then
\[
h^*(u)=f^*(u/s).
\]
Combining both transformations, \(k(x)=\alpha f(sx)\) satisfies
\[
k^*(u)=\alpha f^*\!\left(\frac{u}{\alpha s}\right).
\]
All formulas are extended-real identities and require only \(\alpha>0\) and \(s\ne0\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive value scaling and nonzero scalar argument scaling have explicit conjugate formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive value scaling and invertible scalar argument scaling.

source_witnesses.locator: 2 Calculus Rules on the Conjugacy Operation p. 54

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 2 Calculus Rules on the Conjugacy Operation p. 54

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate regimes excluded by the seed's positive-value and nonzero-argument hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(0)\in\mathbb R\). For zero argument scaling, \(h(x)=f(0)\) and
\[
h^*(u)=\delta_{\{0\}}(u)-f(0).
\]
Hence the seed's nonzero argument-scaling formula cannot be extended by substituting \(s=0\). For an extended-real function, value scaling by zero has no convention-independent meaning because \(0(+\infty)\) is undefined; under the convention \(0f\equiv0\), its conjugate is \(\delta_{\{0\}}\). Negative value scaling has no corresponding formula in terms of \(f^*\): for \(f(x)=x^2/2\) and \(\alpha=-1\),
\[
(\alpha f)^*(u)=+\infty\quad\text{for every }u,
\]
whereas \(\alpha f^*(u/\alpha)=-u^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero argument scaling produces a constant-function conjugate, zero value scaling is convention-dependent for extended-real functions, and negative value scaling invalidates the positive-scaling formula.
assumptions_latex: For the zero argument-scale identity, \(f(0)\) is finite.
The negative-value-scale counterexample is on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At zero argument scale, \((x\mapsto f(0))^*=\delta_{\{0\}}-f(0)\); zero or negative value scaling does not satisfy the seed's positive-scaling rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero and Negative Scaling Boundaries
Reflection Calculus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflecting a function through the primal origin reflects its Fenchel conjugate through the dual origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(g(x)=f(-x)\). Then, for every \(u\in X^*\),
\[
g^*(u)=f^*(-u).
\]
Thus reflection commutes with Fenchel conjugacy after applying the corresponding reflection in the dual space. The identity is valid for arbitrary extended-real \(f\); convexity and lower semicontinuity are unnecessary.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reflection of the primal argument reflects the dual argument of the conjugate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reflection through the origin in primal and dual variables.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3 Calculus Rules with Conjugacy p. 43

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Elementary Transformations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single formula describes how conjugacy transforms any composition of translations, linear perturbations, positive scaling, dilation, and reflection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
g(x)=\alpha f\bigl(s(x-a)\bigr)+\langle b,x\rangle+c.
\]
Then, for every \(u\in X^*\),
\[
g^*(u)=\alpha f^*\!\left(\frac{u-b}{\alpha s}\right)+\langle u-b,a\rangle-c.
\]
This extended-real identity simultaneously covers argument translation, vertical translation, linear perturbation, positive value scaling, and either scalar dilation or reflection according to the sign of \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate of the composite elementary transformation is given by one affine-rescaling formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed formula combining translation, scaling, reflection, and affine perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Precomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, affine precomposition conjugates to minimizing the shifted conjugate over dual vectors mapped to the requested argument by the transpose.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
g^*(u)=\min\left\{f^*(y)-\langle y,a\rangle:y\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=u\right\},
\]
with the convention that the minimum is \(+\infty\) when the constraint set is empty. The relative-interior qualification ensures exactness and attainment whenever the value is finite. Without such a qualification, the right-hand infimum can require lower-semicontinuous closure and need not be attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate of \(x\mapsto f(Ax+a)\) is an attained constrained infimum of \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact formula under a relative-interior qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unqualified Closure Formula for Affine Precomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine-precomposition formula without an exactness or attainment qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and let \(a\in\mathbb R^m\). Suppose \(g(x)=f(Ax+a)\) is proper, and define
\[
h(u)=\inf\{f^*(y)-\langle y,a\rangle:A^{\mathsf T}y=u\}.
\]
Then
\[
g^*=h^{**}=\operatorname{cl}h.
\]
Thus the unclosed fiber infimum is exact at every point where it agrees with its lower-semicontinuous hull. The relative-interior qualification in the seed ensures global exactness and attainment at finite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a range qualification, the conjugate of an affine precomposition is the lower-semicontinuous convex closure of the corresponding adjoint-fiber infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \(\mathbb R^m\).
\(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(f\circ(A\cdot+a)\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f\circ(A\cdot+a))^*=\operatorname{cl}\bigl[u\mapsto\inf_{A^{\mathsf T}y=u}(f^*(y)-\langle y,a\rangle)\bigr]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unqualified Closure Formula for Affine Precomposition

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_0:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(y_0\in\mathbb R^m\), set \(A(x)=A_0x+y_0\), and let \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^m)\) with \(A(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed proper convex functions in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; both the always-valid closure formula and its relative-interior exact form are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine precomposition of \(g\) by \(A\) is \(P_Ag:=g\circ A\). Its affine-precomposition conjugate transform is the function
\[Q_Ag^*(s):=\inf\{g^*(p)-\langle y_0,p\rangle:p\in\mathbb R^m,\ A_0^*p=s\}.\]
The canonical correspondence is
\[(g\circ A)^*=\operatorname{cl}Q_Ag^*.\]
If \(A(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\), then \(Q_Ag^*\) is already closed on its effective domain, and for every \(s\in\operatorname{dom}(g\circ A)^*\) the defining infimum is attained and equals \((g\circ A)^*(s)\). The translation \(y_0\) therefore contributes the dual affine term \(-\langle y_0,p\rangle\), while the linear part contributes the fiber constraint \(A_0^*p=s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine precomposition forms the function \(g(A_0x+y_0)\). Its conjugate is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the function obtained by minimizing \(g^*(p)-\langle y_0,p\rangle\) over all dual vectors satisfying \(A_0^*p=s\). When the affine range meets the relative interior of \(\operatorname{dom}g\), the closure is unnecessary and the constrained minimum is attained for every dual argument where the conjugate is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(g\circ A)^*(s)=\operatorname{cl}_s\inf_{A_0^*p=s}\bigl(g^*(p)-\langle y_0,p\rangle\bigr),\] with an attained minimum under \(A(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(y_0=0\), \((g\circ A_0)^*=\operatorname{cl}(A_0^*\triangleright g^*)\).
The qualification is equivalently \(0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g-A(\mathbb R^n))\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A_0\) is invertible, \((g\circ A)^*(s)=g^*((A_0^{-1})^*s)-\langle y_0,(A_0^{-1})^*s\rangle\).
If \(y_0=0\), the dual correction term vanishes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine translation changes dual values but not the fiber equation.
The relative-interior condition supplies both equality without closure and dual attainment.
boundary_notes: Mere feasibility \(A(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing\) does not in general ensure attainment.
In infinite dimensions, algebraic relative interior is generally insufficient for this formulation.

notation.meaning: Fiberwise dual infimal image associated with affine precomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal Linear Image and Its Conjugate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper. The empty-fiber infimum is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional infimal postcomposition; a compatible affine minorant excludes the value \(-\infty\) and makes the displayed conjugate a proper extended-real function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear-image infimal postcomposition of \(g\) by \(A\) is
\[(A\triangleright g)(x):=\inf\{g(y):y\in\mathbb R^m,\ Ay=x\},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n.\]
Assume \(\operatorname{Im}A^*\cap\operatorname{dom}g^*\ne\varnothing\); equivalently, \(g\) has an affine minorant whose slope belongs to \(\operatorname{Im}A^*\). Then \(A\triangleright g\) is proper in the sense of never taking \(-\infty\), and its conjugate is exactly
\[(A\triangleright g)^*(s)=g^*(A^*s),\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n.\]
This identity defines the linear-image infimal-postcomposition correspondence: the primal fiberwise infimum becomes ordinary precomposition of the conjugate by the adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infimal postcomposition of \(g\) by a linear map \(A\) assigns to \(x\) the infimum of \(g\) over the fiber \(Ay=x\). If \(g^*\) is finite at some point in the range of \(A^*\), the image function has a compatible affine lower bound and does not take the value \(-\infty\). Its Fenchel conjugate is then exactly \(g^*\circ A^*\). Thus a fiberwise primal minimization is transformed into a simple adjoint precomposition in dual space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(A\triangleright g)^*=g^*\circ A^*.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The domain condition is \(\exists s_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(g^*(A^*s_0)<+\infty\).
The epigraph of \(A\triangleright g\) is the vertical closure-sensitive image of \(\operatorname{epi}g\) under \(A\times\operatorname{Id}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is invertible, \((A\triangleright g)(x)=g(A^{-1}x)\).
If \(A(x,z)=x\) is a product-space projection, \(A\triangleright g\) is the marginal \(x\mapsto\inf_z g(x,z)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No closure appears in the conjugate identity, even though the primal image function itself need not be lower semicontinuous.
The effective domain satisfies \(\operatorname{dom}(A\triangleright g)=A(\operatorname{dom}g)\).
boundary_notes: Without a compatible affine minorant, a fiber infimum can equal \(-\infty\).
Attainment of the primal fiber infimum is not part of this definition.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition or infimal image of \(g\) under \(A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Scope of Linear-Image Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward linear-image conjugacy is an algebraic identity and does not require finite dimensionality, convexity, closedness, or fiber attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be real vector spaces in separating duality with \(X^*,Y^*\), let \(A:X\to Y\) admit an adjoint \(A^*:Y^*\to X^*\), and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Defining \((A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)(y)=\inf_{Ax=y}f(x)\) with extended infimum conventions, one has \[(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)^*(y^*)=f^*(A^*y^*)\qquad(y^*\in Y^*).\] Finite dimensionality, convexity, lower semicontinuity, properness of the infimal image, and attainment of fiber infima are not needed for this forward algebraic identity.
assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is linear and admits the adjoint \(A^*:Y^*\to X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)^*=f^*\circ A^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp assumption variant of the forward conjugacy identity on a dual pair.

notation.meaning: linear infimal image of f under A
adjoint of A relative to the stated pairings

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of the infimal image of a function under a linear map equals its conjugate postcomposed with the adjoint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linear infimal image by \((A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)(y)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=y\}\), with the infimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\). Then, for every \(y^*\in Y^*\), \[(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)^*(y^*)=f^*(A^*y^*).\] Thus conjugation converts a linear image into postcomposition of the conjugate by the adjoint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)^*=f^*\circ A^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conjugacy of a linear infimal image.

notation.meaning: Infimal image of f under A

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-linear locally convex variant of the finite-dimensional seed identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be real locally convex spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be continuous linear, and define \(h(y)=\inf_{Ax=y}f(x)\). Then, with extended-real Fenchel conjugates, \[h^*(y^*)=f^*(A^*y^*)\qquad(y^*\in Y^*).\] Convexity, lower semicontinuity, and attainment of the fiber infima are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The adjoint-composition identity extends algebraically to continuous linear maps between locally convex spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Pair Linear-Image Conjugacy
Identity and Associativity of Infimal Postcomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal postcomposition by the identity changes nothing, and successive linear infimal postcompositions equal postcomposition by the composite map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) be linear, and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). With extended infima over empty fibers, \[\operatorname{Id}_X\mathbin{\triangleright}f=f,\qquad B\mathbin{\triangleright}(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)=(B\circ A)\mathbin{\triangleright}f.\] These equalities remain valid when a fiber infimum is not attained or equals \(-\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) are linear maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Id}_X\triangleright f=f\) and \(B\triangleright(A\triangleright f)=(B\circ A)\triangleright f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functorial algebra of successive linear infimal images, without convexity, closedness, or attainment assumptions.

notation.meaning: infimal postcomposition of f by A

knowledge_statements.title: Infimal Postcomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal postcomposition assigns to each image point the infimum of the original function over its linear-map fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal postcomposition of \(f\) by \(A\) is the function \(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f:Y\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) defined by \[(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x):Ax=y\}.\] If the fiber \(\{x\in X:Ax=y\}\) is empty, its value is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)(y)=\inf_{Ax=y}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition using extended-real conventions.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition, or infimal image, of f by A

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of properness under infimal postcomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A(u,v)=u\) and \(f(u,v)=v\), the function \(f\) is proper closed convex, but \[(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)(u)=\inf_{v\in\mathbb R}v=-\infty\] for every \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function can have an infimal image that is identically negative infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f\equiv-\infty\), so properness is not preserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Properness Can Fail

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebra of successive infimal postcompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) are linear, then \[B\mathbin{\triangleright}(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)=(B\circ A)\mathbin{\triangleright}f.\] Moreover, \(I_X\mathbin{\triangleright}f=f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive infimal postcompositions compose their linear maps, and the identity map acts neutrally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\mathbin{\triangleright}(A\mathbin{\triangleright}f)=(B\circ A)\mathbin{\triangleright}f\) and \(I_X\mathbin{\triangleright}f=f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Composition Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural properties of fiberwise infimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h=A\mathbin{\triangleright}f\). Then \[\operatorname{dom}h=A(\operatorname{dom}f).\] If \(f\) is convex, then \(h\) is convex, although it may take the value \(-\infty\), fail to be lower semicontinuous, or fail to be proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain of an infimal postcomposition is the linear image of the source domain, and convexity is preserved, but properness and closedness need not be.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}h=A(\operatorname{dom}f)\), and convexity of \(f\) implies convexity of \(h\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Effective Domain
Image–Postcomposition Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provided the adjoint composition is proper, conjugating it produces the lower-semicontinuous convex closure of the corresponding infimal image; no closure is needed when that image is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(q=A\mathbin{\triangleright}g^*:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \[q(y)=\inf\{g^*(x):x\in X,\ Ax=y\}.\] Then postcomposition by the adjoint and infimal imaging by the original map satisfy \[(g\circ A^*)^*=q^{**}=\operatorname{cl}q.\] In particular, if \(q\) is lower semicontinuous, then \[(g\circ A^*)^*=A\mathbin{\triangleright}g^*.\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(g:X^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g\circ A^*)^*=\operatorname{cl}(A\mathbin{\triangleright}g^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper finite-dimensional biconjugate correspondence, including the necessary functional closure.

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex closure of a function

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions. Define \((f_1\square\cdots\square f_m)(x)=\inf_{x_1+\cdots+x_m=x}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proper convex functions; the family distinguishes the unconditional conjugate of infimal convolution from the closure-sensitive conjugate of a sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The additive-infimal conjugate calculus is the dual operation pair
\[(f_1\square\cdots\square f_m)^*=f_1^*+\cdots+f_m^*,\]
\[(\operatorname{cl}f_1+\cdots+\operatorname{cl}f_m)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f_1^*\square\cdots\square f_m^*).\]
When \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\ne\varnothing\), the second rule becomes exact:
\[(f_1+\cdots+f_m)^*(s)=\min_{s_1+\cdots+s_m=s}\sum_i f_i^*(s_i).\]
The minimum notation records attainment. This collection of the primal addition operation, the primal infimal-convolution operation, their dual identities, and the exactness qualification is the additive-infimal calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Addition and infimal convolution form a dual pair under Fenchel conjugation. The conjugate of an infimal convolution is always the sum of the conjugates. In the reverse direction, the conjugate of a sum is generally the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimal convolution of the conjugates. If the relative interiors of the primal domains have a common point, closure is unnecessary and the dual decomposition infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\square_i f_i)^*=\sum_i f_i^*,\qquad (\sum_i f_i)^*=\operatorname{cl}(\square_i f_i^*),\] with exact attained infimal convolution under the common-relative-interior condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact sum rule is \((\sum_i f_i)^*(s)=\min\{\sum_i f_i^*(s_i):\sum_i s_i=s\}\).
Epigraphically, infimal convolution corresponds to addition of epigraphs when the defining infimum is exact.
special_cases_latex: For indicator functions, infimal convolution encodes Minkowski addition of the underlying sets.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal regularization by infimal convolution becomes additive penalization in dual space.
Failure of exactness is represented by a closure correction, not by changing the algebraic dual operation.
boundary_notes: Infimal convolution of proper functions can take \(-\infty\) without a common affine minorant.
A finite value of the infimum does not by itself imply that a minimizing decomposition exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum–Infimal-Convolution Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a sum is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimal convolution of the individual conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^*\in X^*\), define \[(f^*\square g^*)(x^*)=\inf_{u^*+v^*=x^*}\bigl(f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*)\bigr).\] Then \[(f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*).\] Equivalently, conjugation changes pointwise addition into infimal convolution, with lower-semicontinuous closure included unless an exact sum-rule qualification applies.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sum rule with closure correction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional relative-interior qualification removing closure and guaranteeing an attaining dual decomposition at finite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \[\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing,\] then for every \(x^*\in X^*\), \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=(f^*\square g^*)(x^*).\] Whenever this value is finite, \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=\min_{u^*+v^*=x^*}\bigl(f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the relative-interior qualification, the conjugate of a sum equals the unclosed infimal convolution of the conjugates, and every finite value admits an attaining dual split.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+g)^*=f^*\square g^*\), and the defining infimum is attained wherever its value is finite.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions, and define \((f\square g)(x)=\inf_{u+v=x}\{f(u)+g(v)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary finite-dimensional correspondence, with the exact qualification stated separately from the universal closure formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sum–infimal-convolution correspondence is the pair of identities
\[(f\square g)^*=f^*+g^*,\qquad (f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*).\]
Here
\[(f^*\square g^*)(s)=\inf_{p+q=s}\{f^*(p)+g^*(q)\}.\]
If \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\), then the second correspondence is exact and decomposable:
\[(f+g)^*(s)=\min_{p+q=s}\{f^*(p)+g^*(q)\}\quad\text{for every }s,\]
where the minimum is attained whenever the value is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two proper convex functions, the infimal convolution is the fiberwise infimum over decompositions \(x=u+v\). Its conjugate is the ordinary sum \(f^*+g^*\). Conversely, the conjugate of the pointwise sum \(f+g\) is the lower-semicontinuous closure of \(f^*\square g^*\). A common relative-interior point of the primal domains removes the closure and guarantees an attaining dual split \(s=p+q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f\square g)^*=f^*+g^*,\qquad (f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first identity is equivalent after biconjugation to \(\operatorname{cl}(f\square g)=(f^*+g^*)^*\).
Under qualification, the dual variable \(s\) admits an optimal decomposition \(s=p+q\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g=\iota_{\{0\}}\), then \(f\square g=f\).
If \(f=\iota_C\) and \(g=\iota_D\), then \(f\square g=\iota_{C+D}\) when the infimum is exact.
immediate_consequences_latex: The effective domain of \(f\square g\) is \(\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}g\).
Infimal convolution is commutative and, under compatible minorants, associative.
boundary_notes: Even for \(f,g\in\Gamma_0\), \(f\square g\) need not be lower semicontinuous or exact.
The common-relative-interior condition is sufficient, not necessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugation of a Separable Product-Space Sum
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be a finite product of Euclidean spaces with product pairing \(\langle s,x\rangle=\sum_i\langle s_i,x_i\rangle\), and let \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite products with a pairing compatible with the product decomposition; no convexity or closure qualification is needed for the basic identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is separable across the stated product when
\[F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i).\]
Its product-space conjugate calculus is the componentwise identity
\[F^*(s_1,\ldots,s_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(s_i).\]
Thus the conjugate of a separable sum on independent blocks is itself separable on the dual product. The definition includes compatibility of the pairing: each \(s_i\) pairs only with \(x_i\). Without that compatibility, the displayed componentwise formula is not the conjugate associated with the chosen bilinear form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product-space function is separable when it is the sum of functions acting on independent coordinate blocks. With the product inner product, its Fenchel conjugate equals the sum of the individual conjugates evaluated at the corresponding dual blocks. The requirement on the pairing is part of the definition because cross-block terms would destroy the componentwise factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\right)^*(s_1,\ldots,s_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(s_i).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The epigraphical supremum defining \(F^*\) separates into \(m\) independent one-block suprema.
For identical one-dimensional blocks, separability means \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) and \(F^*(s)=\sum_i f_i^*(s_i)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f_i=\iota_{C_i}\), then \(F=\iota_{C_1\times\cdots\times C_m}\) and \(F^*=\sum_i\sigma_{C_i}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The effective dual domain factors as \(\operatorname{dom}F^*=\prod_i\operatorname{dom}f_i^*\).
Coordinatewise conjugate tables extend directly to block-separable models.
boundary_notes: This rule differs from the conjugate of a sum of functions sharing the same primal variable, which produces infimal convolution.
Infinite products require additional summability and dual-pair specifications.

notation.meaning: Separable direct sum of functions on independent product blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Conjugate Calculus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a finite separable sum on a product space is the sum of the component conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the canonical pairing on \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\) and \(X^*=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i^*\), the conjugate of the separable sum is separable: \[F^*(x_1^*,\ldots,x_m^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x_i^*).\] This equality holds as an extended-real identity because the supremum defining \(F^*\) separates across the finitely many coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces for \(1\le i\le m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-product separability identity.

notation.meaning: Finite Cartesian product of the primal spaces

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Conjugate Calculus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable convex function on a finite product, conjugation, biconjugation, and subdifferentiation all decompose componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_i)_{i=1}^m\in X\), product-space conjugate calculus is componentwise: \[F^*(x^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x_i^*),\qquad F^{**}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^{**}(x_i).\] Moreover, \[\partial F(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x_i).\] Hence closedness, biconjugacy, and subgradient membership can be checked coordinate by coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\) is a finite product of finite-dimensional spaces.
Each \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\circ\pi_i\), where \(\pi_i\) is the coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial F(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x_i)\) and \(F^{**}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^{**}(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise calculus on finite product spaces.

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the ith factor

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate maximization of a finite separable function splits into independent component problems, and, when all component optima are attained, its maximizers form their Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conjugate maximization decomposes componentwise: \[F^*(x^*)=\sup_{(x_i)\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(\langle x_i^*,x_i\rangle-f_i(x_i)\bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x_i^*).\] If every component supremum is attained, then \[\operatorname{Argmax}_{x\in X}\bigl(\langle x^*,x\rangle-F(x)\bigr)=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Argmax}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(\langle x_i^*,x_i\rangle-f_i(x_i)\bigr).\]
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 1\) is an integer and \(X_i\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space for each \(1\le i\le m\).
\(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper for each \(1\le i\le m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*(x^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x_i^*)\), with a Cartesian-product decomposition of the maximizers when every component supremum is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and optimizer decomposition of a finite separable conjugate problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure and Exactness Corrections for Dual Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\) be proper convex functions on \(\mathbb R^n\), and set \(H=f_1^*\square\cdots\square f_m^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sum conjugacy; the record formalizes the two distinct defects that may occur: lack of lower semicontinuity and lack of attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closure-exactness correction system attached to the sum \(F=\sum_i f_i\) consists of:
(1) the closure-corrected identity \(F^*=\operatorname{cl}H\);
(2) pointwise exactness at \(s\), meaning that there exist \(s_1,
\ldots,s_m\) with \(\sum_i s_i=s\) and \(H(s)=\sum_i f_i^*(s_i)\);
(3) global exactness, meaning pointwise exactness for every \(s\in\operatorname{dom}H\); and
(4) closure exactness, meaning \(H=\operatorname{cl}H\).
Under \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\ne\varnothing\), both corrections vanish: \(H\) is closed and every finite defining infimum is attained, hence \(F^*=H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a sum, the raw dual candidate is the infimal convolution \(H\) of the conjugates. The closure correction replaces \(H\) by its lower-semicontinuous closure. Exactness is a separate property: it says that the infimum defining \(H(s)\) is achieved by a decomposition of \(s\). The correction system records these defects independently. A common relative-interior point of the primal domains guarantees both closedness of \(H\) and attainment of its finite values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F^*=\operatorname{cl}H,\qquad \bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow F^*=H\text{ and }H\text{ is exact}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Closure exactness is equivalent to lower semicontinuity of \(H\).
Pointwise exactness at \(s\) is equivalent to existence of an optimal dual decomposition \(s=\sum_i s_i\).
special_cases_latex: For two functions, exactness means \((f^*\square g^*)(s)=f^*(p)+g^*(s-p)\) for some \(p\).
If one conjugate is supercoercive and the other is bounded below, standard coercivity conditions can also yield exact closed infimal convolution.
immediate_consequences_latex: Equality \(F^*=H\) alone identifies the value function; explicit exactness additionally supplies an optimizer.
Closure and nonattainment must not be conflated, since either defect can be considered separately.
boundary_notes: The relative-interior condition is sufficient but not necessary.
Exactness at one dual argument does not imply global exactness or closedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Corrections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When infimal convolution is not closed, its lower-semicontinuous convex closure gives the conjugate of the primal sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The raw infimal convolution \(f^*\square g^*\) is convex but need not be lower semicontinuous. The universally valid repaired formula is \[(f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)=(f^*\square g^*)^{**}.\] Thus biconjugation removes precisely the lower-semicontinuity defect in the unqualified sum–infimal-convolution rule.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+g)^*=\operatorname{cl}(f^*\square g^*)=(f^*\square g^*)^{**}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure repair for nonclosed infimal convolution.

source_witnesses.locator: 12 Infimal Convolution p. 203

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Exactness Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one summand is polyhedral, intersection of its domain with the relative interior of the other domain suffices for the exact attained conjugate-sum formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) is polyhedral and \[\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing.\] Then for every \(x^*\) for which the common value is finite, \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=\min_{u^*+v^*=x^*}\bigl(f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*)\bigr).\] This condition may hold even when \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)=\varnothing\). The symmetric assertion holds when \(g\) is the polyhedral summand.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and polyhedral}.
g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (f+g)^*(x^*)=\min_{u^*+v^*=x^*}\bigl(f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*)\bigr)\quad\text{whenever the value is finite}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed polyhedral relaxation of the ordinary relative-interior qualification for exact conjugate addition.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Corrections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior intersection condition removes the closure and ensures attainment in the conjugate sum formula whenever the value is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relative-interior qualification \[\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\] removes the closure correction. For every \(x^*\in X^*\), \[(f+g)^*(x^*)=\min_{u^*+v^*=x^*}\bigl(f^*(u^*)+g^*(v^*)\bigr)\] whenever the common value is finite. Hence the infimal convolution is lower semicontinuous and exact at such points.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+g)^*=f^*\square g^*\), and the defining infimum is attained whenever finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior qualification for exact conjugate addition.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure–Exactness Gap
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonclosed sums of orthogonal complements in Hilbert space show that raw infimal convolution can differ from the conjugate of a sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(f+g=\delta_{U\cap V}\), one has \[(f+g)^*=\delta_{(U\cap V)^\perp}=\delta_{\overline{U^\perp+V^\perp}}.\] However, \[f^*\square g^*=\delta_{U^\perp}\square\delta_{V^\perp}=\delta_{U^\perp+V^\perp}.\] If \(U^\perp+V^\perp\) is not closed, the raw infimal convolution differs from the conjugate sum, and closure is indispensable.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is an infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(U,V\subset H\) are closed subspaces with \(U^\perp+V^\perp\) nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\square g^*=\delta_{U^\perp+V^\perp}\ne\delta_{\overline{U^\perp+V^\perp}}=(f+g)^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional nonclosed-subspace-sum failure mechanism.

source_witnesses.locator: 12 Infimal Convolution p. 203

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates pointwise attainment failure from a lower-semicontinuity closure defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(p(u)=e^u\) and \(q(v)=0\). Both functions are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, and for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), \[(p\square q)(x)=\inf_{u+v=x}e^u=0.\] Hence \(p\square q\equiv0\) is lower-semicontinuous and equals its closure, but the infimum is never attained because \(e^u>0\) for every finite \(u\). Equivalently, taking \(f=p^*\) and \(g=q^*\) produces closed proper convex conjugate operands whose raw infimal convolution is closed but nowhere exact at a finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infimal convolution can already be closed while none of its finite values has an attaining decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\square q\equiv0=\operatorname{cl}(p\square q),\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{u+v=x}(p(u)+q(v))=\varnothing\ \forall x\in\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Value without Attained Decomposition

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(g,h:C\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions. Extend \(f=g-h\) by \(+\infty\) outside \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional difference-of-convex functions. The Fenchel conjugate is defined even though \(f\) need not be convex; no convex biconjugacy claim is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A DC decomposition of \(f\) on \(C\) is an ordered pair \((g,h)\) of finite convex functions satisfying \(f(x)=g(x)-h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\). Its difference-conjugacy interface is the extended-real transform
\[\mathcal D_{g,h}(s):=f^*(s)=\sup_{x\in C}\{\langle s,x\rangle-g(x)+h(x)\}.\]
When \(g\) and \(h\) are proper closed convex extensions and the extended-real expressions are well defined, the associated lifted dual representation is
\[\mathcal D_{g,h}(s)=\sup_{p\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{g^*(s+p)-h^*(p)\}.\]
The interface depends on the represented function through \(f^*\), while the lifted representation depends on the selected DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC function is represented on a convex domain as a difference \(f=g-h\) of two finite convex functions. Its difference-conjugacy interface is the Fenchel transform of this generally nonconvex function, namely the supremum of \(\langle s,x\rangle-g(x)+h(x)\). For suitable closed convex extensions, this may be expressed as a supremum over a lifted dual variable of \(g^*(s+p)-h^*(p)\). Different DC decompositions can produce different lifted formulas even though they represent the same conjugate \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f^*(s)=\sup_{x\in C}\bigl(\langle s,x\rangle-g(x)+h(x)\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A pair \((g,h)\) is a DC decomposition exactly when \(f+h=g\) is convex on \(C\).
Adding the same convex function \(q\) to both components gives the equivalent decomposition \((g+q,h+q)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h=0\), the interface reduces to ordinary convex conjugacy of \(g\).
An affine \(h\) reduces the interface to a translation of the dual argument plus a constant.
immediate_consequences_latex: The conjugate \(f^*\) is always convex and lower semicontinuous even when \(f\) is nonconvex.
The DC decomposition is nonunique, so algorithms using \((g,h)\) may depend on the chosen representation.
boundary_notes: The lifted formula requires extended-real compatibility not established by the inspected DC-definition source.
The biconjugate \(f^{**}\) is the closed convex envelope of \(f\), not generally \(f\) itself.

notation.meaning: Difference-conjugacy interface induced by the DC decomposition \((g,h)\).
Effective domain of the conjugate of \(h\).

review_flags: The inspected local source supports the definition of a DC function as a difference of convex functions, but no inspected locator supports the full lifted conjugate identity with its precise extended-real hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition and Fenchel-Conjugacy Interface
Conjugates of Differences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a convex difference is the supremum of shifted conjugate differences over the effective domain of the subtractand's conjugate, rather than an infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(g-h\) need not be convex, for every \(x^*\in X^*\) its Fenchel conjugate satisfies \[(g-h)^*(x^*)=\sup_{y^*\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\bigl(g^*(x^*+y^*)-h^*(y^*)\bigr).\] Thus subtraction leads to a supremal shifted-conjugate representation rather than an infimal convolution.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(h:X\to\mathbb R\) is finite-valued, continuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g-h)^*(x^*)=\sup_{y^*\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\bigl(g^*(x^*+y^*)-h^*(y^*)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued subtractand and restriction to the effective domain avoid undefined extended-real differences.

notation.meaning: Effective domain of the conjugate of h

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary ensuring that the convex difference and its conjugate formula are unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper convex functions \(g,h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the formal difference \(g-h\) is undefined under standard extended-real arithmetic at any point where \(g(x)=h(x)=+\infty\). Therefore the shifted-conjugate formula for \((g-h)^*\) requires either domain hypotheses excluding this case or an explicit nonstandard convention. Requiring the subtractand \(h\) to be finite-valued on \(X\) removes this ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two extended-valued convex terms, the difference can contain infinity minus infinity; a finite-valued subtractand makes the conjugate-of-a-difference formula unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:g(x)=h(x)=+\infty\}\ne\varnothing\implies g-h\text{ is undefined there under standard extended-real arithmetic}.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Value Subtraction Boundary
Conjugate-Subgradient DCA Update
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DCA selects a subgradient of the subtracted component and minimizes the leading component minus that linear form, equivalently applying the subdifferential of the leading component's conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical DC algorithm uses \[y_k\in\partial h(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl(g(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle\bigr).\] Equivalently, \[y_k\in\partial g(x_{k+1})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y_k).\]
assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the indicated subgradient and convex-subproblem solution exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choose \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}\in\partial g^*(y_k)\), equivalently \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{argmin}_x\{g(x)-\langle y_k,x\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical difference-of-convex algorithm written through the local conjugate-subgradient interface; existence of each selection is assumed.

notation.meaning: Selected subgradient of the subtracted component

knowledge_statements.title: General DC Necessary Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimum of a finite-valued DC function, every subgradient of the subtracted convex component is also a subgradient of the leading component, with an equivalent conjugate-subgradient formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar x\) locally minimizes the finite-valued DC function \(g-h\), then \[\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x).\] For each \(y\in\partial h(\bar x)\), the equivalent conjugate relation is \[\bar x\in\partial g^*(y).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\); equivalently, every \(y\in\partial h(\bar x)\) satisfies \(\bar x\in\partial g^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite-dimensional first-order necessary condition; the differentiable immutable seed is its singleton-subdifferential specialization.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the leading convex component

knowledge_statements.title: DCA Descent and Step Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive aggregate strong convexity of the DC components gives sufficient descent, square-summable steps, vanishing displacement, and an O(1/N) best squared-step bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every DCA step obeys \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge \frac{\rho_g+\rho_h}{2}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2.\] Consequently, \(f(x_k)\) is nonincreasing, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le \frac{2(f(x_0)-\inf f)}{\rho_g+\rho_h},\qquad \|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0,\] and, for every \(N\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le \frac{2(f(x_0)-\inf f)}{(\rho_g+\rho_h)N}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and \(f=g-h\).
\(g\) and \(h\) are respectively \(\rho_g\)- and \(\rho_h\)-strongly convex, where \(\rho_g,\rho_h\ge0\) and \(\rho_g+\rho_h>0\).
The DCA iterates satisfy \(y_k\in\partial h(x_k)\cap\partial g(x_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\rho_g+\rho_h}{2}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\), and \(\min_{0\le k<N}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le\frac{2(f(x_0)-\inf f)}{(\rho_g+\rho_h)N}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent and best-iterate step complexity for a well-defined DCA sequence under positive aggregate component curvature.

notation.meaning: Strong-convexity moduli of the two DC components

knowledge_statements.title: Nonoptimal DC Critical Point
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function x^4-x^2 has a DC-critical DCA fixed point at zero that is a strict local maximum, so componentwise criticality is not sufficient for optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=g(x)-h(x)=x^4-x^2\), \[\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\}.\] DCA initialized at zero remains at zero, while \(f(x)<f(0)\) for every sufficiently small nonzero \(x\); thus zero is a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)\) and DCA remains at \(0\), but \(0\) is a strict local maximizer of \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional boundary showing that DC criticality and DCA fixed-point status are not sufficient for local minimality.

knowledge_statements.title: DCA Cluster-Point Criticality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounded DCA iterates with differentiable subtractand and sufficient component curvature, every cluster point satisfies the DC criticality relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) of the stated DCA sequence satisfies \[\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x),\qquad \bar x\in\partial g^*(\nabla h(\bar x)).\] This is a criticality conclusion and does not assert local optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and continuously differentiable.
The DCA iteration satisfies \(\nabla h(x_k)\in\partial g(x_{k+1})\).
The iterates are bounded, \(g\) and \(h\) have positive aggregate strong-convexity modulus, and \(g-h\) is bounded below along the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x)\), equivalently \(\bar x\in\partial g^*(\nabla h(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequential criticality for bounded DCA iterates under differentiability and positive aggregate component curvature.

notation.meaning: A cluster point of the DCA primal sequence

knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimum of a finite-dimensional DC objective with differentiable subtractand, the subtractand's gradient is a subgradient of the leading convex component, equivalently giving a conjugate-subgradient relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local minimizer \( ar x\) of \(g-h\) necessarily satisfies \[
abla h( ar x)\in\partial g( ar x).\] Equivalently, by Fenchel subgradient inversion, \[ ar x\in\partial g^*(
abla h( ar x)).\] The vector \(
abla h( ar x)\) is therefore a primal-dual interface between the two convex components.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(h:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x)\), equivalently \(\bar x\in\partial g^*(\nabla h(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional first-order interface for a differentiable DC component.

notation.meaning: Gradient of the differentiable convex component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth extension of the seeded differentiable interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(g-h\), then \[\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x).\] Hence every \(y^*\in\partial h(\bar x)\) satisfies \[\bar x\in\partial h^*(y^*)\cap\partial g^*(y^*)\] and \[g(\bar x)+g^*(y^*)=h(\bar x)+h^*(y^*)=\langle y^*,\bar x\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimum of a finite-dimensional DC function, every subgradient of the subtracted convex component is also a subgradient of the leading component, yielding paired conjugate-subgradient interfaces.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(g-h\) is well-defined on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\), with the stated conjugate relations for every \(y^*\in\partial h(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth DC Necessary Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp logical boundary for the common-subgradient interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(g(x)=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), \[\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\},\] but \((g-h)(x)=-x^2<0=(g-h)(0)\) for every \(x\ne0\). Thus common-subgradient criticality does not imply local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common subgradient is only a DC criticality test, not a sufficient local-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)=\{0\}\), although \(0\) is not a local minimizer of \(g-h\).
knowledge_statements.title: DC Criticality Is Not Sufficient for Minimality
Explicit Decomposition-Dependence Counterexample
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decompositions zero minus zero and absolute value minus absolute value represent the same function but have different component subdifferentials and conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\equiv0\) has the decompositions \[f=0-0=|\cdot|-|\cdot|.\] At the origin, \[\partial g_1(0)=\{0\},\qquad \partial g_2(0)=[-1,1],\] while \[g_1^*=\delta_{\{0\}},\qquad g_2^*=\delta_{[-1,1]}.\] Thus the represented function is unchanged although its componentwise subgradient and conjugate interfaces differ.
assumptions_latex: The zero function has the DC decompositions \(f=g_1-h_1=0-0\) and \(f=g_2-h_2=|\cdot|-|\cdot|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented function is identical, but \(\partial g_1(0)=\{0\}\ne[-1,1]=\partial g_2(0)\) and \(g_1^*=\delta_{\{0\}}\ne\delta_{[-1,1]}=g_2^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness that componentwise subdifferential and conjugate interfaces are not invariants of the represented DC function.

notation.meaning: Convex indicator function of a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional witness that common-subgradient criticality is not invariant under common convex augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\), \(g(x)=x\), and \(h(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(f=g-h\) and \(\partial g(0)=\{1\}\), \(\partial h(0)=\{0\}\), so the component subdifferentials do not intersect. For \(q(x)=|x|\), the same function satisfies \[f=(g+q)-(h+q),\] while \[\partial(g+q)(0)=[0,2],\qquad \partial(h+q)(0)=[-1,1],\] whose intersection is \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding absolute value to both components preserves the represented linear function but changes common-subgradient criticality at zero from false to true.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The truth of \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)\ne\varnothing\) changes after replacing \((g,h)\) by \((g+q,h+q)\), although the represented function is unchanged.

notation.meaning: Common convex augmentation of both DC components

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Dependent DC Criticality
Decomposition Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete example showing that DC criticality is not intrinsic to the represented function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb{R}\), let \(h(x)=x\). The decomposition \(h=f_1-g_1\), with \(f_1(x)=x\) and \(g_1(x)=0\), has no DC-critical point because \(\partial f_1(x)=\{1\}\) and \(\partial g_1(x)=\{0\}\). The same function also has the decomposition \(h=f_2-g_2\), where
\[
f_2(x)=x+|x|,
\qquad g_2(x)=|x|.
\]
At \(x=0\),
\[
\partial f_2(0)=[0,2],
\qquad \partial g_2(0)=[-1,1],
\]
so their intersection is nonempty. Hence the common-subgradient critical set depends on the selected DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same linear function has one DC decomposition with no critical points and another for which zero is critical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{crit}(f_1,g_1)=\varnothing\) while \(0\in\operatorname{crit}(f_2,g_2)\).

notation.meaning: set of points x with nonempty intersection of the subdifferentials of f and g

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\), let \(J\) be an index set, let \(g_j:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper closed convex functions, and let \(G:X\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional pointwise extrema and product-space marginalization; closure corrections for suprema are retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The extremal-marginal conjugate calculus is the family generated by
\[g(x)=\sup_{j\in J}g_j(x),\qquad m(x)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^p}G(x,z),\]
and the corresponding rules
\[g^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_{j\in J}g_j^*\right),\qquad m^*(s)=G^*(s,0),\]
provided the supremum is proper and the marginal has a compatible affine minorant. The first formula uses the lower-semicontinuous convex hull of the pointwise infimum of conjugates. The second uses the product pairing and evaluates the full conjugate at zero in the eliminated dual coordinate. The family also includes finite maxima as the finite-index specialization and linear-image marginals as projection specializations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extremal-marginal calculus treats pointwise suprema and value functions obtained by minimizing out variables. The conjugate of a proper supremum is the lower-semicontinuous convex hull of the pointwise infimum of the individual conjugates. For a product-space marginal \(m(x)=\inf_zG(x,z)\), the conjugate is the slice \(G^*(s,0)\), assuming a compatible affine lower bound. Finite maxima and ordinary partial minimization are the canonical special cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\sup_j g_j\right)^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_j g_j^*\right),\qquad \left(\inf_zG(\cdot,z)\right)^*(s)=G^*(s,0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A marginal is the infimal image of \(G\) under the projection \((x,z)\mapsto x\).
A finite maximum is a supremum indexed by \(J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(G(x,z)=f(x-z)+h(z)\), the marginal is an infimal convolution.
For \(g=\max\{g_1,g_2\}\), \(g^*\) is the closed convex hull of \(\min\{g_1^*,g_2^*\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Eliminating a primal variable forces its corresponding dual coordinate to zero.
Pointwise maximization generally creates a convexification operation in dual space.
boundary_notes: The supremum formula does not generally reduce to the pointwise infimum of conjugates without convexification and closure.
The marginal infimum need not be attained.

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex hull of an extended-real function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate Calculus for Suprema and Finite Maxima
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{f_j\}_{j\in J}\subset\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n)\), and suppose \(f=\sup_{j\in J}f_j\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional supremum calculus; a stronger attained representation is stated only for finitely many real-valued convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The supremum conjugate-calculus family assigns to \(f=\sup_jf_j\) the function
\[f^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_{j\in J}f_j^*\right).\]
For a finite family of real-valued convex functions \(f_1,\ldots,f_p\), let \(f=\max_jf_j\) and \(r=\min\{p,n+1\}\). Then for every \(s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\), there exist indices, weights \(\alpha_k\ge0\) with \(\sum_{k=1}^r\alpha_k=1\), and \(s_k\in\operatorname{dom}f_{j_k}^*\) such that
\[s=\sum_{k=1}^r\alpha_ks_k,\qquad f^*(s)=\sum_{k=1}^r\alpha_k f_{j_k}^*(s_k).\]
This finite convex-mixture representation is the maximum specialization of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a pointwise supremum is the lower-semicontinuous convex hull of the pointwise infimum of the component conjugates. For a finite maximum of real-valued convex functions on \(\mathbb R^n\), each finite conjugate value admits an attaining convex-mixture representation using at most \(\min\{p,n+1\}\) component dual points. Thus maximum conjugacy combines selection among component conjugates with convexification in the dual variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\sup_j f_j\right)^*=\overline{\operatorname{co}}\left(\inf_j f_j^*\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite maxima, \(\operatorname{dom}f^*=\operatorname{co}\bigcup_j\operatorname{dom}f_j^*\).
The finite representation is an attained convexification of the disjoint family of epigraphs of \(f_j^*\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f=\max\{0,g\}\) and \(s\ne0\), \(f^*(s)=\min_{0<\alpha\le1}\alpha g^*(s/\alpha)\).
For a singleton index set, the rule reduces to \(f^*=f_1^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Dual convexification can mix conjugates from different active primal functions.
The dimension bound \(n+1\) limits the number of mixture terms in the real-valued finite case.
boundary_notes: Extended-valued component functions can destroy the attained finite-mixture representation.
For an infinite family, closure and convexification generally cannot be omitted.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Suprema
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of an arbitrary proper supremum is the closed convex envelope of the pointwise infimum of the individual conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g:X^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(g(x^*)=\inf_{i\in I}f_i^*(x^*)\). Then \[f^*=g^{**}=\operatorname{clconv}g.\] Equivalently, with closure taken in the product of the weak-star topology on \(X^*\) and the usual topology on \(\mathbb R\), \[\operatorname{epi}f^*=\operatorname{clconv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{epi}f_i^*\right).\] Thus an arbitrary pointwise supremum becomes a closed convexification operation after conjugation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real locally convex space with dual \(X^*\).
Each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and \(f=\sup_{i\in I}f_i\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate of the supremum is the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of the pointwise infimum of the conjugates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-conjugate formula for an arbitrary proper supremum.

source_witnesses.locator: X. Conjugacy in Convex Analysis p. 35

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for replacing the closed convex envelope by the raw infimum of conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(f_a(x)=ax\) for \(a\in(0,1)\). Then \[f(x)=\sup_{a\in(0,1)}f_a(x)=\max\{0,x\},\qquad f_a^*=\delta_{\{a\}}.\] Hence \[\inf_{a\in(0,1)}f_a^*=\delta_{(0,1)},\qquad f^*=\delta_{[0,1]}.\] Thus the raw infimum of the component conjugates need be neither convex nor lower semicontinuous, and both convexification and closure in the arbitrary-supremum formula are essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An open family of affine slopes yields the ReLU function and shows that the infimum of component conjugates requires both convexification and closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure and Convexification Are Indispensable
Finite Pointwise Maxima
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugating a finite maximum produces the closed convex hull of the union of the component-conjugate epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the finite maximum \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\), one has \[f^*=\left(\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i^*\right)^{**}.\] Equivalently, \[\operatorname{epi}f^*=\operatorname{clconv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m\operatorname{epi}f_i^*\right).\] Hence every point \((x^*,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f^*\) is a limit of convex combinations of points drawn from the epigraphs of the component conjugates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(f_1,\ldots,f_m:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions and \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph of \(f^*\) is the closed convex hull of the union of the component-conjugate epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family specialization of supremum conjugacy.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the ith component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-family boundary for the raw minimum of component conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1(x)=0\) and \(f_2(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \[f(x)=\max\{f_1(x),f_2(x)\}=\max\{0,x\},\quad f_1^*=\delta_{\{0\}},\quad f_2^*=\delta_{\{1\}}.\] Consequently \[\min\{f_1^*,f_2^*\}=\delta_{\{0,1\}},\qquad f^*=\delta_{[0,1]}.\] Thus even for two affine components the raw minimum of conjugates is generally nonconvex and must be convexified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of two affine functions shows that the minimum of their conjugates must generally be convexified.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Cannot Be Omitted

\(f_1,\ldots,f_m:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions and \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph of \(f^*\) is the closed convex hull of the union of the component-conjugate epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Directional Derivative
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a finite convex maximum is the largest directional derivative among the components active at the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every direction \(d\), with directional derivatives understood in the extended one-sided sense, \[f'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}f_i'(x;d).\] A component having a strict value gap at \(x\) does not affect the first-order directional derivative there.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper convex functions, \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\), and \(f(x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}f_i'(x;d).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order directional geometry of a finite convex maximum.

notation.meaning: Indices attaining the maximum at the base point

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Index Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a continuity-qualified point, subgradients of a finite maximum are convex combinations of subgradients from the active component functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\) and define the active set \(I(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=f(x)\}\). Then \[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}\partial f_i(x)\right).\] Equivalently, \(x^*\in\partial f(x)\) precisely when there exist coefficients \(\alpha_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i\in I(x)}\alpha_i=1\) and subgradients \(x_i^*\in\partial f_i(x)\) such that \(x^*=\sum_{i\in I(x)}\alpha_i x_i^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
Each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper convex, and every \(f_i\) is continuous at a fixed point \(x\) where \(f(x)=\max_i f_i(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subdifferential of the maximum is the convex hull of the subdifferentials belonging to active indices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional active-set geometry for a finite convex maximum.

notation.meaning: Indices attaining the pointwise maximum at x

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If every convex component \(f_i\) is differentiable at \(x\) and finite on a neighborhood of \(x\), then \[f=\max_i f_i	ext{ is differentiable at }x\iff 
abla f_i(x)=
abla f_j(x)\quad(i,j\in I(x)).\] In that case the common active gradient equals \(
abla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite maximum of differentiable convex functions is differentiable exactly when all active gradients coincide.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) is convex, differentiable at \(x\), and finite near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f\text{ is differentiable at }x\iff\{\nabla f_i(x):i\in I(x)\}\text{ is a singleton}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i\), where every convex \(f_i\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(x\). For \(I(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=f(x)\}\), \[f'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}f_i'(x;d)\qquad(d\in X).\] Components with a strict value gap at \(x\) make no first-order contribution there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative of a finite convex maximum is the maximum of the directional derivatives of its active components.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is convex and finite on a neighborhood of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}f_i'(x;d).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Index Directional-Derivative Rule

assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) are proper convex and the qualified active-index subdifferential rule holds at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\partial f(x)\Longleftrightarrow\exists\,\alpha_i,x_i^*:\ \alpha\in\Delta_m,\ \alpha_i>0\Rightarrow i\in I(x),\ x_i^*\in\partial f_i(x),\ x^*=\sum_i\alpha_i x_i^*.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise Fenchel-equality certificate for active maximum subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(x^*\) lies in \(\partial f(x)\) exactly when there are \(\alpha\in\Delta_m\) and \(x_i^*\in\partial f_i(x)\) for the positively weighted indices such that \[\alpha_i>0\Rightarrow f_i(x)=f(x),\qquad x^*=\sum_i\alpha_i x_i^*.\] Equivalently, every positively weighted component satisfies the Fenchel equality \(f_i(x)+f_i^*(x_i^*)=\langle x_i^*,x\rangle\), and no inactive component receives positive weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum subgradient is certified by weights supported on active components and component subgradients satisfying their individual Fenchel equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Fenchel Certificate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, and equip the product space with \(\langle(s,t),(x,z)\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle+\langle t,z\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional marginalization with a product-compatible pairing; the affine-minorant condition prevents the marginal from taking \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The infimal-marginal value function generated by \(G\) is
\[m(x):=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^p}G(x,z).\]
Assume that there exists \(s_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \((s_0,0)\in\operatorname{dom}G^*\). Then \(m\) has a finite affine minorant and its conjugate is the zero slice of the product-space conjugate:
\[m^*(s)=G^*(s,0),\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n.\]
Equivalently, if \(P(x,z)=x\) is the canonical projection, then \(m=P\triangleright G\) and \(P^*s=(s,0)\), so \(m^*=G^*\circ P^*\). This identity defines the infimal-marginal conjugate calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infimal marginal is the value function obtained by minimizing a joint function \(G(x,z)\) over the auxiliary variable \(z\). If \(G^*\) is finite at some dual point whose \(z\)-coordinate is zero, the marginal has a compatible affine lower bound. Its conjugate is then obtained by evaluating \(G^*\) at \((s,0)\). In projection notation, marginalization is an infimal linear image and conjugation inserts a zero dual coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[m(x)=\inf_zG(x,z),\qquad m^*(s)=G^*(s,0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(P(x,z)=x\), \(m=P\triangleright G\) and \(m^*=G^*\circ P^*\).
The condition \((s_0,0)\in\operatorname{dom}G^*\) means that \(G(x,z)\) admits a lower affine bound independent of \(z\).
special_cases_latex: If \(G(x,z)=f(z)+g(x-z)\), then \(m=f\square g\).
If \(G=\iota_C\), then \(m\) is the indicator of the projection of \(C\), subject to properness.
immediate_consequences_latex: The eliminated primal coordinate corresponds to a zero dual coordinate.
The formula does not require attainment of the minimizing \(z\).
boundary_notes: Without the affine-minorant condition, \(m\) may take \(-\infty\).
A non-product pairing changes the adjoint of the projection and invalidates the literal zero-slice formula.

notation.meaning: Infimal image of \(G\) under the projection \(P\).
