knowledge_statements.title: Infimal Constructions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel conjugate of a proper infimal convolution equals the pointwise sum of the two conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal convolution is defined by \[(f\square g)(x)=\inf_{u+v=x}\bigl(f(u)+g(v)\bigr).\] Its Fenchel conjugate satisfies the exact identity \[(f\square g)^*(x^*)=f^*(x^*)+g^*(x^*)\qquad(x^*\in X^*).\] No attainment of the defining infimum is required. Lower-semicontinuous closure may be needed for the reverse operation of recovering \(f\square g\) from \(f^*+g^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real locally convex space with dual \(X^*\).
\(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper functions, and their infimal convolution never takes \(-\infty\) and is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conjugation converts infimal convolution into pointwise addition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic Fenchel duality rule for an infimal construction.

notation.meaning: Infimal convolution of f and g

source_witnesses.locator: X. Conjugacy in Convex Analysis p. 35

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - X. Conjugacy in Convex Analysis p. 35

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexed-family identity complementing the seed's infimal-convolution identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((f_i)_{i\in I}\) be extended-real functions on a dual-paired space and let \(h(x)=\inf_{i\in I}f_i(x)\). If \(h\) is proper, then \[h^*(x^*)=\sup_{i\in I}f_i^*(x^*).\] Convexity, closedness, and attainment of the pointwise infimum are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugating a proper pointwise infimum gives the pointwise supremum of the individual conjugates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\inf_{i\in I}f_i)^*=\sup_{i\in I}f_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of an Indexed Infimum
Marginal Subgradient Lift
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attained marginal value, a vector is a marginal subgradient exactly when adjoining a zero eliminated-coordinate component makes it a joint subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(x,\bar y)=p(x)\), then for every \(x^*\in X^*\), \[x^*\in\partial p(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x^*,0)\in\partial F(x,\bar y).\] Thus a marginal subgradient is certified by a joint subgradient whose eliminated-coordinate component is zero. Without an attained minimizer, this finite-point certificate need not be available.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real locally convex spaces with continuous duals.
\(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) is finite, and \(F(x,\bar y)=p(x)\) for some \(\bar y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^*\in\partial p(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x^*,0)\in\partial F(x,\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact joint-subgradient certificate for an attained marginal value.

notation.meaning: Marginal after eliminating the second coordinate

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Convex Reconstruction of a Marginal
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-coordinate slice of the joint conjugate reconstructs the marginal's biconjugate and reconstructs the marginal itself exactly in the closed convex case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The seed identity \(p^*(x^*)=F^*(x^*,0)\) gives \[p^{**}(x)=\sup_{x^*\in X^*}\bigl\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-F^*(x^*,0)\bigr\}.\] This recovers \(p\) exactly when \(p\) is lower semicontinuous and convex in the chosen dual pairing; otherwise it gives its Fenchel biconjugate rather than the original marginal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real locally convex spaces with continuous duals.
\(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, and \(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biconjugate reconstruction from the zero-coordinate slice of the joint conjugate.

notation.meaning: Marginal after eliminating the second coordinate
Fenchel biconjugate in the chosen locally convex dual pairing

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a primal variable by infimization corresponds to setting that variable's dual coordinate to zero in the joint conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the marginal function \(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\), its Fenchel conjugate is \[p^*(x^*)=F^*(x^*,0)\qquad(x^*\in X^*).\] Indeed, the eliminated primal variable corresponds to setting its dual coordinate to zero. This identity is algebraic and does not require attainment of the infimum defining \(p\); properness excludes indeterminate conjugacy conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real locally convex spaces with continuous duals \(X^*\) and \(Y^*\).
\(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, and \(p(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate of the marginal is the restriction of \(F^*\) to dual vectors whose eliminated coordinate is zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conjugacy identity for elimination by partial infimization.

notation.meaning: Marginal of F after eliminating y

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Image and Marginal Functions p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of several auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:X\times Y\times Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \[\inf_{y\in Y}\inf_{z\in Z}F(x,y,z)=\inf_{(y,z)\in Y\times Z}F(x,y,z)=\inf_{z\in Z}\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y,z).\] Thus successive marginalization is independent of the order of eliminated coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several variables may be marginalized jointly or successively in either order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_y\inf_zF=\inf_{(y,z)}F=\inf_z\inf_yF\).
knowledge_statements.title: Order Independence of Successive Marginalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-projection representation of marginalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_X:X\times Y\to X\) be \(P_X(x,y)=x\). For \(p(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\), \[p=P_X\mathbin{\triangleright}F,\qquad P_X^*x^*=(x^*,0),\qquad p^*(x^*)=F^*(x^*,0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginal is infimal postcomposition by a coordinate projection, whose adjoint inserts zero in the eliminated dual coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(P_X(x,y)=x\), and the marginal is proper when invoking the seed's conjugacy convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=P_X\mathbin{\triangleright}F\), \(P_X^*x^*=(x^*,0)\), and \(p^*(x^*)=F^*(x^*,0)\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the retained primal coordinate

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal as Coordinate Infimal Postcomposition
Value Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbation value function is a marginal, and its conjugate is the zero-decision-coordinate slice of the joint conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Regard \(u\) as a perturbation parameter and define the optimal-value function by \[v(u)=\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x,u).\] Then its conjugate satisfies \[v^*(u^*)=\Phi^*(0,u^*)\qquad(u^*\in U^*).\] Thus the dual description of the value function is the zero-decision-coordinate slice of the joint conjugate. If \(v\) is proper convex and lower semicontinuous, it is recovered from this slice by \(v=v^{**}\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are real locally convex spaces.
\(\Phi:X\times U\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a proper perturbation function, and \(v(u)=\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x,u)\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate value function is obtained by restricting the joint conjugate to a zero decision-variable dual coordinate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation value functions viewed through marginal conjugacy.

notation.meaning: Joint Fenchel conjugate of the perturbation function

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Image and Marginal Functions p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity certificate for an attained perturbation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(w)=\inf_z\Phi(z,w)\), and suppose \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\Phi(z,u)\). Then \[u^*\in\partial v(u)\iff(0,u^*)\in\partial\Phi(x,u)\iff v(u)+\Phi^*(0,u^*)=\langle u^*,u\rangle.\] Thus \(u^*\) also gives \(v(w)\ge v(u)+\langle u^*,w-u\rangle\) for every \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attained value, a value-function subgradient is exactly a joint subgradient with zero decision coordinate, equivalently a Fenchel-equality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[u^*\in\partial v(u)\iff(0,u^*)\in\partial\Phi(x,u)\iff v(u)+\Phi^*(0,u^*)=\langle u^*,u\rangle.\]

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of the value function
Joint dual vector with zero decision-variable coordinate

knowledge_statements.title: Value Subgradients as Primal–Dual Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Perturbations Can Have Nonclosed Value Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of lower semicontinuity under elimination of the decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[C=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ u\ge 1/x\},\qquad \Phi=\delta_C.\] Although \(C\) is closed and convex, \[v(u)=\inf_x\Phi(x,u)=\delta_{(0,\infty)}(u),\qquad v^{**}=\delta_{[0,\infty)}.\] Thus partial minimization can destroy closedness, and at \(u=0\) the biconjugate dual value is strictly below the primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex perturbation can have a nonclosed value function; the reciprocal-epigraph example produces the indicator of an open ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v=\delta_{(0,\infty)},\qquad v^{**}=\delta_{[0,\infty)}\ne v.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Perturbations Can Have Nonclosed Value Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Closedness and Exact Perturbation Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conjugate-dual representation at a fixed perturbation parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper convex value function \(v(u)=\inf_x\Phi(x,u)\), \[v^{**}(u)=\sup_{u^*\in U^*}\{\langle u^*,u\rangle-\Phi^*(0,u^*)\}\le v(u).\] Equality holds exactly when \(v(u)=v^{**}(u)\); hence failure of pointwise biconjugate closedness is exactly a perturbation-duality gap at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate dual value is the biconjugate value and equals the primal value exactly at parameters where the value function agrees with its closed convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) form separated real locally convex dual pairs.
\(\Phi\) is proper and convex, and \(v(u)=\inf_x\Phi(x,u)\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{u^*}\{\langle u^*,u\rangle-\Phi^*(0,u^*)\}=v^{**}(u)\le v(u),\qquad v^{**}(u)=v(u)\iff\text{exact duality at }u.\]

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex hull represented by the biconjugate

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Closedness and Exact Perturbation Duality

assumptions_latex: \(v(u)=\inf_x\Phi(x,u)\) is finite at \(u\), and \(\bar x\) attains the infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[u^*\in\partial v(u)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(0,u^*)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,u).\]

notation.meaning: An attained optimizer at parameter u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-function sensitivity certificate at an attained optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Phi(\bar x,u)=v(u)\), then \[u^*\in\partial v(u)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(0,u^*)\in\partial\Phi(\bar x,u).\] Hence a value-function subgradient, interpreted as a perturbation sensitivity, is exactly the parameter component of a joint subgradient whose decision component vanishes. Attainment is required for this certificate at a finite pair \((\bar x,u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an attained optimizer, perturbation sensitivities are exactly the parameter components of joint subgradients having zero decision component.
knowledge_statements.title: Attained Value-Function Sensitivity
Marginal–Value Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization is both marginalization and value-function formation; attainment determines whether its epigraph equals the projected joint epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \[m(u)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x,u)\] is simultaneously the marginal of \(F\) under elimination of \(x\) and the optimal-value function of the parameterized problem indexed by \(u\). It obeys \[m^*(u^*)=F^*(0,u^*).\] Moreover, \[\operatorname{epi}m\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_{U\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F),\] and equality holds when every finite infimum defining \(m(u)\) is attained; without attainment, the projection may omit boundary points of \(\operatorname{epi}m\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are real locally convex spaces.
\(F:X\times U\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and its partial infimum is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Marginal functions and optimization value functions are the same construction, with identical conjugacy and epigraphical descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Qualification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasing convex outer function can destroy convexity, and without a regularity qualification the scalar dual infimum may fail to be attained or may require closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The monotonicity and continuity hypotheses in the qualified postcomposition theorem cannot simply be discarded. If the convex outer function is decreasing, the composition with a convex inner function need not be convex: for \(f(x)=x^2\) and \(\varphi(t)=-t\), \((\varphi\circ f)(x)=-x^2\). Even when the composition is convex, without an appropriate continuity or relative-interior qualification the infimum over \(\lambda\ge0\) need not be attained and an unclosed minimum formula cannot in general be asserted; the corresponding marginal may require lower-semicontinuous closure.
assumptions_latex: The monotonicity or continuity qualification of the seed theorem is omitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither convexity of \(\varphi\circ f\) nor the seed's attained, closure-free multiplier formula is guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convexity or of the attained multiplier formula when the postcomposition hypotheses are removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Increasing Convex Postcomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of an increasing convex postcomposition is a qualified minimum over a nonnegative scalar multiplier and the perspective of the inner conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated qualification, \(\varphi\circ f\) is proper closed convex and \[(\varphi\circ f)^*(x^*)=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\varphi^*(\lambda)+(\lambda f)^*(x^*)\right\}.\] For \(\lambda>0\), \((\lambda f)^*(x^*)=\lambda f^*(x^*/\lambda)\); the term at \(\lambda=0\) is interpreted by the closed perspective of \(f^*\). Monotonicity of \(\varphi\) restricts the scalar dual variable to the nonnegative half-line.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex.
\(\varphi:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex and nondecreasing on a neighborhood of \(f(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
\(\varphi\) is finite and continuous at some value \(f(x_0)\) with \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjugate of the postcomposition is obtained by minimizing over a nonnegative scalar multiplier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional qualified formula with a nonnegative scalar dual variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate of an Increasing Convex Postcomposition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb R)\) be nondecreasing on its effective domain, set \(g(+\infty)=+\infty\), and suppose \(f(\mathbb R^n)\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scalar postcomposition by a closed convex nondecreasing outer function, with the interior qualification ensuring an attained dual scalar minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The increasing convex postcomposition is \(h=g\circ f\). For \(s\in\operatorname{dom}h^*\), define
\[\psi_s(\alpha)=\begin{cases}\alpha f^*(s/\alpha)+g^*(\alpha),&\alpha>0,\\ \sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(s)+g^*(0),&\alpha=0,\\ +\infty,&\alpha<0.\end{cases}\]
The postcomposition conjugate calculus is
\[h^*(s)=\min_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\psi_s(\alpha).\]
The minimum is attained at some \(\alpha\ge0\). The value at \(\alpha=0\) is the closed perspective extension of \(\alpha f^*(s/\alpha)\), expressed through the support function of \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex function \(f\) and a closed convex nondecreasing scalar function \(g\), postcomposition gives \(h=g\circ f\). Under an interior-domain qualification, \(h^*(s)\) is the attained minimum over a nonnegative scalar \(\alpha\) of \(\alpha f^*(s/\alpha)+g^*(\alpha)\). At \(\alpha=0\), the perspective term is defined by the support function of \(\operatorname{dom}f\). Negative multipliers are excluded by assigning value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(g\circ f)^*(s)=\min_{\alpha\ge0}\left[g^*(\alpha)+(\operatorname{persp}f^*)(s,\alpha)\right].\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), \((\operatorname{persp}f^*)(s,\alpha)=\alpha f^*(s/\alpha)\), while at \(\alpha=0\) it equals \(\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(s)\).
Monotonicity implies \(\operatorname{dom}g^*\subseteq\mathbb R_+\).
special_cases_latex: For \(g(r)=r\), the minimum forces \(\alpha=1\) and returns \(f^*\).
For \(g(r)=\max\{0,r\}\), the multiplier is restricted to \([0,1]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}f}(s)=+\infty\) or \(g^*(0)=+\infty\), every minimizing multiplier satisfies \(\alpha>0\).
The rule converts nonlinear scalar postcomposition into a one-dimensional dual minimization.
boundary_notes: Without the interior qualification, the minimum formula can fail.
This scalar rule does not directly cover vector-valued inner maps or outer functions that are not coordinatewise nondecreasing.

notation.meaning: Scalar dual objective defining the conjugate at \(s\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be either a finite product of Euclidean spaces or a finite-dimensional matrix space with Frobenius pairing. Let \(T:E\to Z\) be a canonical structure map such as block coordinates, the eigenvalue map \(\lambda\), or the singular-value map \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable and orthogonally invariant structures for which Fenchel conjugation reduces to conjugation of lower-dimensional associated functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(F:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) belongs to the structured-function conjugacy class generated by \(T\) when there is a proper associated function \(\phi:Z\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), invariant under the symmetry group of \(T\), such that \(F=\phi\circ T\) and
\[F^*=\phi^*\circ T.\]
For product structure, this means \(T(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), \(\phi(z)=\sum_i\phi_i(z_i)\), and \(F^*=
\sum_i\phi_i^*\). For symmetric matrices, \(T=
\lambda\) and \(\phi\) is permutation invariant; for rectangular matrices, \(T=\sigma\) and \(\phi\) is absolutely permutation invariant. Structure-preserving conjugacy means that the same structure map appears before and after conjugation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain:
A structured function is represented as \(F=
\phi\circ T\), where \(T\) extracts independent blocks, eigenvalues, or singular values and \(\phi\) respects the corresponding symmetry. It has structure-preserving conjugacy when \(F^*=
\phi^*\circ T\). In the separable case, the conjugate remains a blockwise sum. In spectral cases, it remains an eigenvalue- or singular-value function. The associated lower-dimensional function is conjugated while the structural map is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F=\phi\circ T\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F^*=\phi^*\circ T\] for the specified product or spectral structure and symmetry hypotheses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The conjugacy diagram commutes: applying \(T\) and then conjugating the associated function gives the same value as conjugating \(F\).
For product separability, structure preservation is \((\oplus_i f_i)^*=\oplus_i f_i^*\).
special_cases_latex: Permutation-invariant \(\phi\) yields eigenvalue spectral functions on \(\mathbb S^n\).
Absolutely permutation-invariant \(\phi\) yields unitarily invariant singular-value functions on \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Conjugate evaluation reduces from the ambient structured space to the lower-dimensional invariant coordinates.
Proper closed convexity of many spectral functions can be checked on their associated functions.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary nonlinear feature map \(T\) does not satisfy structure-preserving conjugacy.
The integral-functional case requires separate measurability and interchange hypotheses and is not included here.

notation.meaning: Canonical structure map extracting blocks, eigenvalues, or singular values.
Associated symmetry-invariant function on the structure-coordinate space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Conjugacy for Orthogonally Invariant Matrix Functions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Equip \(\mathbb S^n\) and \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with the Frobenius pairing. Let \(\lambda(X)\in\mathbb R^n\) list eigenvalues in nonincreasing order and let \(\sigma(X)\in\mathbb R^r\), \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), list singular values in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real symmetric and rectangular matrix spaces; “unitary invariance” is represented over the real field by orthogonal invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper permutation-invariant function \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), the symmetric spectral function is \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on \(\mathbb S^n\), and its conjugate is
\[F^*(Y)=\phi^*(\lambda(Y)).\]
For a proper absolutely permutation-invariant function \(\psi:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), the orthogonally invariant singular-value function is \(G(X)=\psi(\sigma(X))\) on \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and
\[G^*(Y)=\psi^*(\sigma(Y)).\]
Permutation invariance means invariance under coordinate permutations; absolute permutation invariance additionally permits independent sign changes. These identities define spectral unitary-invariance conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric-matrix spectral function applies a permutation-invariant scalar function to the eigenvalue vector. Its Fenchel conjugate applies the scalar conjugate to the eigenvalue vector of the dual matrix. A rectangular orthogonally invariant function applies an absolutely permutation-invariant function to singular values, and its conjugate has the same singular-value structure with the associated function conjugated. Thus orthogonal invariance and spectral form are preserved by Fenchel conjugation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\phi\circ\lambda)^*=\phi^*\circ\lambda,\qquad (\psi\circ\sigma)^*=\psi^*\circ\sigma.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F(QXQ^T)=F(X)\) for every orthogonal \(Q\), while \(G(UXV^T)=G(X)\) for all compatible orthogonal \(U,V\).
The conjugate can be computed entirely in eigenvalue or singular-value coordinates.
special_cases_latex: The conjugate of \(\alpha\|X\|_*\) is the indicator of the spectral-norm ball of radius \(\alpha\).
The conjugate of \(\lambda_{\max}(X)\) is the indicator of \(\{Y\succeq0:\operatorname{Tr}Y=1\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\phi\) is proper closed convex, then \(\phi\circ\lambda\) is proper closed convex, and conversely.
Dual norms of Schatten norms follow from the corresponding vector \(\ell_p\)-norm conjugacy.
boundary_notes: For nonsymmetric square matrices, eigenvalues do not furnish the stated convex spectral calculus; singular values are used instead.
Complex Hermitian and unitary variants require the complex trace pairing but have analogous formulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Eigenvalue Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral conjugacy supremum reduces to ordered eigenvalues, and an ordered vector optimizer lifts through a shared eigenbasis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\), the matrix conjugacy supremum equals the supremum over nonincreasing eigenvalue vectors and hence \(\phi^*(\lambda(Y))\). If the ordered vector problem is attained at \(x^\downarrow\), and \(Y=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(Y))Q^{\mathsf T}\), then \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(x^\downarrow)Q^{\mathsf T}\) attains the matrix supremum. An unordered attaining vector must first be permuted into compatible nonincreasing order.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and invariant under coordinate permutations.
\(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on \(\mathbb S^n\), with eigenvalues ordered nonincreasingly.
\(\mathbb S^n\) carries the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\{\operatorname{tr}(XY)-F(X)\}=\sup_{x_1\geq\cdots\geq x_n}\{\langle\lambda(Y),x\rangle-\phi(x)\}=\phi^*(\lambda(Y)).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Eigenvalue-Orbit Trace Extrema
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace pairing over a symmetric matrix's orthogonal orbit is extremized by aligned or reverse-aligned ordered eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real symmetric \(A,Y\), the trace pairing over the orthogonal orbit of \(A\) is maximized by aligning their ordered eigenvalues and minimized by reverse alignment. Equality representatives may be chosen to commute with \(Y\).
assumptions_latex: \(A,Y\in\mathbb S^n\), and both eigenvalue vectors are arranged in nonincreasing order.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of the Unrestricted Nonsymmetric Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp counterexample showing why ordered-chamber restriction cannot be omitted for a nonsymmetric generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=2\), take \(\psi(x)=x_1\). Then \(F(X)=\psi(\lambda(X))=\lambda_{\max}(X)\) and \[F^*(Y)=\delta_{\{Y\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}Y=1\}}(Y).\] In contrast, \(\psi^*(\lambda(Y))\) is finite only when \(\lambda(Y)=(1,0)\). Thus \(F^*=\psi^*\circ\lambda\) fails without permutation invariance, whereas the ordered-chamber formula remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum-eigenvalue function disproves the unrestricted vector-conjugate formula for a nonsymmetric generator.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) carries the trace pairing and eigenvalues are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*\ne\psi^*\circ\lambda\) for this nonsymmetric generator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordered Eigenvalue Reduction and Aligned Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ordered-eigenvalue optimization and attainment correspondence for symmetric-matrix conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_1\ge\cdots\ge x_n\}\), let \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dom}\psi\cap\mathcal D\ne\varnothing\), and define \(F(X)=\psi(\lambda(X))\) on \(\mathbb S^n\). Then, for every \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\), \[F^*(Y)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal D}\{\langle\lambda(Y),x\rangle-\psi(x)\}=(\psi+\delta_{\mathcal D})^*(\lambda(Y)).\] The matrix supremum is attained if and only if this ordered vector supremum is attained. If \(x\in\mathcal D\) attains it and \(Y=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(Y))Q^{\mathsf T}\), then \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(x)Q^{\mathsf T}\) is a matrix maximizer. If \(\psi\) is permutation invariant, the value simplifies to \(F^*(Y)=\psi^*(\lambda(Y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix conjugacy reduces exactly to optimization over ordered eigenvalues. Attaining ordered eigenvalues can be placed in an ordered eigenbasis of the dual matrix, and permutation invariance permits the unrestricted vector-conjugate formula.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^n\) carries the trace pairing and \(\lambda(X)\) is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*=(\psi+\delta_{\mathcal D})^*\circ\lambda\), with equivalent matrix and ordered-vector attainment and an aligned matrix optimizer.

\(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and invariant under coordinate permutations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix conjugacy supremum reduces to a vector supremum over eigenvalues, with an optimizer commuting with the dual matrix when attained.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of the spectral conjugacy optimization to ordered eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\), the conjugacy problem reduces as \[\sup_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\bigl\{\operatorname{tr}(XY)-\phi(\lambda(X))\bigr\}=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl\{\langle\lambda(Y),x\rangle-\phi(x)\bigr\}.\] The reduction follows from optimizing the relative eigenvector orientation: for fixed \(\lambda(X)=x\), the largest trace pairing is obtained by aligning ordered eigenvectors. If the vector supremum is attained at \(x\), then a matrix optimizer can be chosen as \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(x)Q^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Y=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(Y))Q^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral matrix conjugacy problem reduces to a vector conjugacy problem, and optimizers may be chosen to share eigenvectors with the dual matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue-reduction formula is plausible but uncited. In addition, the optimizer statement must require the attaining vector to be ordered compatibly with the ordered eigenvalues, or replace it by an appropriately permuted ordered optimizer; as written, an arbitrary attaining vector need not yield the displayed aligned matrix optimizer. The sentence explaining how the reduction follows is proof text and should be removed from a sourced replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Vector Orbit Reduction and Optimizer Lifting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aligning singular-vector frames gives the trace maximum, and an ordered nonnegative vector optimizer lifts to a matrix optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The real Frobenius pairing over the two-sided orthogonal or unitary orbit of \(A\) is maximized by compatible singular-vector frames. If \(s\) attains the vector conjugacy supremum for an absolutely symmetric \(\phi\), then an ordered nonnegative representative \(s^\downarrow\) with the same objective value may be chosen; combining \(s^\downarrow\) with singular-vector frames of \(Y\) yields a matrix optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(A,Y\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}\), where \(\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\) and \(r=\min\{m,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\max_{U,V}\langle UAV^*,Y\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^r\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular orbit maximization and optimizer lifting for singular-value reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of an absolutely symmetric convex function of a matrix's singular values is the conjugate scalar-vector function evaluated at the dual matrix's singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{K}^{m\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be given by \(F(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\). Then the Fenchel conjugate of \(F\), computed with the pairing \(\langle X,Y\rangle=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(X^*Y)\), reduces to the vector conjugate of \(\phi\): \[F^*(Y)=\sup_X\{\langle X,Y\rangle-F(X)\}=\phi^*(\sigma(Y)).\] Thus conjugation preserves the singular-value representation and reduces the matrix optimization to \(\mathbb{R}^r\).
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^r\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric, where \(r=\min\{m,n\}\).
Matrices are in \(\mathbb{K}^{m\times n}\), with \(\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\), under the real Frobenius pairing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional rectangular-matrix form for convex functions generated by singular values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of Singular-Value Reduction, let \(Y=U\operatorname{Diag}(\sigma(Y))V^*\) be a compact singular-value decomposition. The matrix supremum defining \(F^*(Y)\) is attained if and only if the vector supremum defining \(\phi^*(\sigma(Y))\) is attained. When attained, a vector maximizer can be chosen with \(s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r\ge0\), and \[X=U\operatorname{Diag}(s)V^*\] is a matrix maximizer. Conversely, the singular-value vector of every matrix maximizer is a vector maximizer after an absolute-symmetry-preserving signed permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix and vector attainment are equivalent, and an ordered nonnegative vector maximizer placed in the dual matrix's singular-vector bases gives a matrix optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R^r\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric.
\(F(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\) on real or complex rectangular matrices with the real Frobenius pairing.

Integral-Functional Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard normal-integrand hypotheses, the conjugate of an integral functional is the integral of the pointwise conjugates on the dual function space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(I_f(x)=\int_\Omega f(\omega,x(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega)\), with the extended integral convention. Relative to the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) pairing, conjugation is pointwise under the normal-integrand interchange theorem: \[I_f^*(y)=\sup_{x\in L^p}\left\{\int_\Omega\langle x(\omega),y(\omega)\rangle\,d\mu(\omega)-I_f(x)\right\}=\int_\Omega f^*(\omega,y(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega).\] The right side may equal \(+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal{A},\mu)\) is a complete sigma-finite measure space, \(1\le p<\infty\), and \(q\) is conjugate to \(p\).
\(f:\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a proper convex normal integrand.
The integral functional \(I_f\) is proper on \(L^p(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_f^*(y)=\int_\Omega f^*(\omega,y(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega),\qquad y\in L^q.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise conjugacy formula on the standard \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) dual pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-everywhere optimality certificate under the Lp–Lq integral-conjugacy regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the hypotheses of Integral Conjugacy on an Lp–Lq Dual Pair, for \(x\in\operatorname{dom}I_f\) and \(y\in L^q\), \[y\in\partial I_f(x)\iff y(\omega)\in\partial f(\omega,x(\omega))\quad\text{for almost every }\omega.\] Equivalently, the pointwise Fenchel gaps vanish almost everywhere: \[f(\omega,x(\omega))+f^*(\omega,y(\omega))=\langle x(\omega),y(\omega)\rangle\quad\text{a.e.}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An Lq function is a subgradient of the integral functional exactly when it is a pointwise subgradient almost everywhere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Conjugacy on an Lp–Lq Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise conjugacy for a convex normal integrand on the standard decomposable Lebesgue-space dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1\le p<\infty\), let \(q\) be conjugate to \(p\), and define \[I_f(x)=\int_\Omega f(\omega,x(\omega))\,d\mu.\] If \(f\) is a proper convex normal integrand and there exists \(x_0\in L^p\) with \(f(\cdot,x_0(\cdot))\in L^1\), then, relative to the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) pairing, \[I_f^*(y)=\int_\Omega f^*(\omega,y(\omega))\,d\mu\qquad(y\in L^q).\] The right side is a well-defined extended integral and may equal \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the standard Lp–Lq dual pair, the conjugate of a proper integral functional generated by a convex normal integrand is the integral of the pointwise conjugates.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a complete sigma-finite measure space.
\(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a proper convex normal integrand.
There exists \(x_0\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\) such that \(f(\cdot,x_0(\cdot))\in L^1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_f^*(y)=I_{f^*}(y)=\int_\Omega f^*(\omega,y(\omega))\,d\mu\qquad(y\in L^q).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral functional and its pointwise conjugate candidate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) be a measure space, let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(X^*\), and let \(\varphi:\Omega\times X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be an integrand. Let \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal X^\times\) be decomposable spaces of measurable \(X\)- and \(X^*\)-valued functions paired by \(\langle u,x\rangle=\int_\Omega\langle u(\omega),x(\omega)\rangle\,d\mu\) whenever this integral is defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This record defines the integral functional and the pointwise-conjugate integral that participate in integral-functional conjugacy. It does not assert equality of the functional conjugate with the latter integral without normal-integrand and interchange hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[I_\varphi(x):=\int_\Omega \varphi(\omega,x(\omega))\,d\mu,\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\] with the extended integral convention, and \[\varphi^*(\omega,u):=\sup_{z\in X}\{\langle u,z\rangle-\varphi(\omega,z)\},\qquad I_{\varphi^*}(u):=\int_\Omega\varphi^*(\omega,u(\omega))\,d\mu.\] The conjugate of \(I_\varphi\) relative to the displayed pairing is \[I_\varphi^*(u):=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\int_\Omega\langle u(\omega),x(\omega)\rangle\,d\mu-I_\varphi(x)\right\}.\] Integral-functional conjugacy is the identification \(I_\varphi^*=I_{\varphi^*}\) on \(\mathcal X^\times\) when hypotheses permitting interchange of supremum and integration are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integral functional generated by an integrand is obtained by integrating the integrand along a measurable function. The pointwise conjugate integrand is formed separately at almost every point, and its integral defines the natural candidate dual functional. The conjugate of the original integral functional is taken with respect to the integral pairing. “Integral-functional conjugacy” refers to equality between that functional conjugate and the integral of the pointwise conjugates, but the equality is not part of the bare definition and requires additional measurability, decomposability, properness, and interchange conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_\varphi^*(u)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\langle u,x\rangle-I_\varphi(x)\},\qquad I_{\varphi^*}(u)=\int_\Omega\sup_{z\in X}\{\langle u(\omega),z\rangle-\varphi(\omega,z)\}\,d\mu.\]
special_cases_latex: For a finite atomic measure space, \(I_\varphi\) is a finite weighted sum of coordinate functions, so the construction reduces to separable finite-dimensional conjugacy.
immediate_consequences_latex: Pointwise Fenchel inequalities give \(\langle u(\omega),x(\omega)\rangle\leq\varphi(\omega,x(\omega))+\varphi^*(\omega,u(\omega))\) almost everywhere whenever the terms are meaningful.
boundary_notes: The supplied local sources do not contain an inspectable statement of the exact normal-integrand interchange theorem needed for \(I_\varphi^*=I_{\varphi^*}\).
The dual of a Banach function space may contain singular functionals; in that setting the full conjugate can have an additional singular component.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed-Face Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of a closed sublinear function is exactly a dominated dual functional that attains the support value at the primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}p\), \[\partial p(x)=\bigl\{x^*\in C:\langle x^*,x\rangle=p(x)\bigr\}.\] Thus the subgradients are exactly the dual-feasible elements attaining the support value in direction \(x\); geometrically, \(\partial p(x)\) is the face of \(C\) exposed by \(x\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real locally convex space with continuous dual \(X^*\).
\(p:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous.
\(C=\{x^*\in X^*:\langle x^*,z\rangle\le p(z)\ \forall z\in X\}\), and \(p(x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial p(x)=\{x^*\in C:\langle x^*,x\rangle=p(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradients of a closed sublinear function as an exposed face of its dominated dual set.

notation.meaning: Dual set dominated by the sublinear function

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Sublinear Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclosed sublinear function still has an indicator conjugate, but conjugating back gives the support function of its dominated continuous-dual set and may fail to recover the original function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Proper sublinearity gives \[p^*=\delta_C\] even without lower semicontinuity. Consequently \[p^{**}=\delta_C^*=\sigma_C.\] Exact recovery \(p=p^{**}\) holds precisely when \(p\) is lower semicontinuous in the chosen dual pairing. If there are insufficient continuous affine minorants, \(C\) may be empty and the biconjugate may be improper, so it should not be described unconditionally as a proper closed sublinear function.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real locally convex space with continuous dual \(X^*\).
\(p:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, convex, and positively homogeneous, but need not be lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p^*=\delta_C,\qquad p^{**}=\sigma_C.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp role of lower semicontinuity in positively homogeneous conjugacy.

notation.meaning: Support function of the dominated dual set, with the standard extended-value convention

knowledge_statements.title: Positively Homogeneous Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed sublinear function is the support function of its dominated dual set, and its Fenchel conjugate is that set's indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive homogeneity and convexity make \(p\) sublinear. Define \(C=\{x^*\in X^*: \langle x^*,x\rangle\le p(x)\text{ for every }x\in X\}\). Then \[p^*(x^*)=\sup_{x\in X}\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-p(x)\}=\delta_C(x^*).\] Equivalently, the biconjugate representation is \(p(x)=\sup_{x^*\in C}\langle x^*,x\rangle\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real locally convex space with continuous dual \(X^*\).
\(p:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and positively homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p^*=\delta_C,\qquad C=\{x^*\in X^*: \langle x^*,x\rangle\le p(x)\ \text{for every }x\in X\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugacy of closed sublinear functions on a locally convex dual pair.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonclosed Sublinear Functions Recover Only Their Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-semicontinuity boundary for exact sublinear biconjugate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p\) is proper, convex, and positively homogeneous but not necessarily lower semicontinuous, then for \[C=\{x^*:\langle x^*,x\rangle\le p(x)\ \forall x\}\] one still has \[p^*=\delta_C,\qquad p^{**}=\sigma_C=\operatorname{cl}p,\] and \(p^{**}\) may differ from \(p\). For example, if \(M\) is a proper dense linear subspace of an infinite-dimensional normed space and \(p=\delta_M\), then \(M^\perp=\{0\}\), so \(p^*=\delta_{\{0\}}\) and \(p^{**}=0\) on the whole space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lower semicontinuity, conjugation still yields an indicator, but biconjugation recovers only the closed sublinear hull; a dense nonclosed subspace gives strict failure.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is proper, convex, and positively homogeneous.
For the example, \(M\) is a proper dense linear subspace of an infinite-dimensional normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p^*=\delta_C,\qquad p^{**}=\sigma_C=\operatorname{cl}p,\] with possible strict inequality from \(p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support–indicator conjugacy for closed sublinear functions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space. For \(C\subset\mathcal H\), write \(\sigma_C(x)=\sup_{u\in C}\langle x,u\rangle\) and \(\iota_C(u)=0\) for \(u\in C\), \(+\infty\) otherwise. Let \(\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) denote the proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space, proper closed convex regime. Positive homogeneity means degree one for nonnegative scalars; the conjugacy statement concerns closed sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is positively homogeneous when \[f(\lambda x)=\lambda f(x)\qquad(\lambda>0,\ x\in\mathcal H).\] For a positively homogeneous \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), define its representing set by \[C_f:=\{u\in\mathcal H:\ \langle x,u\rangle\leq f(x)\ \text{for every }x\in\mathcal H\}.\] Positively homogeneous conjugacy is the support–indicator pair \[f=\sigma_{C_f},\qquad f^*=\iota_{C_f}.\] Conversely, every nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathcal H\) generates the positively homogeneous closed convex function \(\sigma_C\), whose conjugate is \(\iota_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function is in the positively homogeneous conjugacy class when scaling its argument by a positive scalar scales its value by the same scalar. Its representing set consists of all continuous linear slopes dominated by the function. The function is exactly the support function of this nonempty closed convex set, while its Fenchel conjugate is the set’s indicator. Conversely, the support function of every nonempty closed convex set belongs to this class and is conjugate to that set’s indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C_f=\{u:(\forall x)\ \langle x,u\rangle\leq f(x)\},\qquad f=\sigma_{C_f},\qquad f^*=\iota_{C_f}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\ \text{is positively homogeneous}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\exists C\neq\varnothing\ \text{closed convex})\ f=\sigma_C.\]
For convex \(f\) with \(f(0)=0\), positive homogeneity together with subadditivity is equivalently sublinearity.
special_cases_latex: If \(C=\{u_0\}\), then \(\sigma_C(x)=\langle x,u_0\rangle\) and \(\sigma_C^*=\iota_{\{u_0\}}\).
If \(C\) is the closed unit ball, then \(\sigma_C\) is the norm and its conjugate is the indicator of that ball.
immediate_consequences_latex: The effective domain of \(f^*\) is exactly \(C_f\), and \(f^*\) takes only the values \(0\) and \(+\infty\).
boundary_notes: Degree-zero homogeneity and homogeneity for negative scalars are different notions and are not included.
If lower semicontinuity is dropped, the representing support function recovers the closed convex envelope rather than necessarily the original function.

notation.meaning: Closed convex set of slopes dominated by the positively homogeneous function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal regularization by an additive kernel
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f,k:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,r):f(x)\leq r\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real Hilbert-space calculus. The definition permits the value \(-\infty\); properness, exactness, convexity, and lower semicontinuity are separate regime properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal regularization of \(f\) by the kernel \(k\) is the marginal function \[R_kf:=f\square k,\qquad (R_kf)(x):=\inf_{y\in\mathcal H}\{f(y)+k(x-y)\}.\] Its domain and decomposition map are \[\operatorname{dom}(R_kf)=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}k,\qquad D_{f,k}(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathcal H}\{f(y)+k(x-y)\}.\] It is exact at \(x\) precisely when \(D_{f,k}(x)\neq\varnothing\) and the attained value is greater than \(-\infty\). The associated epigraph operation satisfies \[\operatorname{epi}f+\operatorname{epi}k\subseteq\operatorname{epi}(R_kf),\] with equality when the infimal convolution is exact on its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal-regularization calculus replaces a function by the minimum-cost decomposition of each argument into a point evaluated by the function and a residual evaluated by a kernel. The resulting object is an infimal convolution. Its effective domain is the Minkowski sum of the two effective domains. The set of minimizing decompositions records exactness. Epigraph addition always lies inside the epigraph of the regularization, and exactness upgrades this inclusion to equality. Convexity and lower semicontinuity are not built into the operation and must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(R_kf)(x)=\inf_{y}\{f(y)+k(x-y)\},\qquad \operatorname{dom}(R_kf)=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(L(u,v)=u+v\), \[R_kf=L\mathbin{\triangleright}(f\oplus k),\] where \(\triangleright\) denotes infimal postcomposition.
special_cases_latex: For \(k(z)=\|z\|^2/(2\gamma)\), \(R_kf\) is the Moreau envelope of parameter \(\gamma>0\).
For \(k(z)=\beta\|z\|\), \(R_kf\) is the Pasch–Hausdorff envelope.
immediate_consequences_latex: Choosing \(y=x\) gives \((R_kf)(x)\leq f(x)+k(0)\) whenever that sum is defined.
If \(f\) and \(k\) are convex, then \(R_kf\) is convex, although it need not be proper, exact, or lower semicontinuous.
boundary_notes: The infimum may equal \(-\infty\) even when both inputs are real-valued.
Exactness is an attainment property and is not synonymous with lower semicontinuity.

notation.meaning: Infimal regularization of the function by the kernel.
Set of minimizing decompositions at the point.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(L:X\to Y\) be a map. Empty-fiber infima are assigned the value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The family includes ordinary infimal convolution, multiway decomposition, and elimination of latent variables as instances of one fiberwise infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infimal operation induced by \((L,F)\) is the function \[L\mathbin{\triangleright}F:Y\to[-\infty,+\infty],\qquad (L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)(y):=\inf\{F(x):x\in X,\ Lx=y\}.\] Its domain is \[\operatorname{dom}(L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)=L(\operatorname{dom}F).\] It is exact at \(y\) if there exists \(x\in X\) with \(Lx=y\) and \((L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)(y)=F(x)>-\infty\). For product variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), a separable cost \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\), and \(Lx=\sum_i A_ix_i\), this gives the family \[y\mapsto\inf_{\sum_iA_ix_i=y}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infimal operation is a fiberwise projection of an extended-real cost through a constraint map. At each output, it takes the infimum of the cost over the corresponding fiber. The effective domain is exactly the image of the cost’s effective domain. Exactness means that a finite minimizing point exists in the fiber. Separable costs on product spaces produce infimal convolutions, weighted decompositions, and latent-variable elimination by choosing the map and the component functions appropriately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)(y)=\inf_{x:Lx=y}F(x),\qquad \operatorname{dom}(L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)=L(\operatorname{dom}F).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(F(x,y)\) is a bifunction and \(L(x,y)=x\), then \((L\mathbin{\triangleright}F)(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\).
For \(L(u,v)=u+v\) and \(F=f\oplus g\), \[L\mathbin{\triangleright}F=f\square g.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(L=\operatorname{Id}\), then \(L\mathbin{\triangleright}F=F\).
If a fiber is empty, its value is \(+\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F\) is convex and \(L\) is affine, then the infimal projection is convex.
The construction separates the algebraic constraint \(Lx=y\) from attainment and closedness questions.
boundary_notes: A linear image of a closed convex epigraph need not be closed, so lower semicontinuity is not automatic.
A nonempty fiber does not guarantee a finite or attained infimum.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition or infimal projection of a function through a map.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space and let \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where \(m\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-arity extended-real definition. Common affine minorants are sufficient to exclude \(-\infty\) and make repeated binary association unambiguous in the cited Hilbert-space treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(m\)-ary infimal convolution is \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x):=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=x\right\}.\] Its effective domain is \[\operatorname{dom}\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i.\] For \(m=2\) this is the ordinary infimal convolution. Whenever the extended-real expressions are well defined—particularly when all \(f_i\) possess affine minorants with a common slope—the operation is commutative and associative, so every parenthesized iteration of binary infimal convolutions represents the same \(m\)-ary function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite-arity infimal convolution assigns to each point the infimum of the total component cost over all additive decompositions of that point. Its domain is the Minkowski sum of the component domains. Binary infimal convolution is the case of two functions. Under conditions excluding undefined extended-real behavior, the operation is invariant under permutations and parenthesization, which makes repeated binary convolution a canonical representation of the same finite-arity object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\inf_{x_1+\cdots+x_m=x}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Let \(S:X^m\to X\) be \(S(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_i x_i\) and \(F=\bigoplus_i f_i\). Then \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=S\mathbin{\triangleright}F.\]
For three admissible functions, \[f_1\square(f_2\square f_3)=(f_1\square f_2)\square f_3.\]
special_cases_latex: For indicator functions, \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m\iota_{C_i}=\iota_{C_1+\cdots+C_m}\] whenever the infimal convolution is interpreted exactly.
For \(m=1\), the natural extension is \(\square_{i=1}^1f_i=f_1\), though the defined family begins at \(m=2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any feasible decomposition gives the upper bound \((\square_i f_i)(x)\leq\sum_i f_i(x_i)\).
boundary_notes: Infinite-arity convolutions require an additional topology and summability convention and are excluded.
Without a condition preventing \(-\infty\), associative expressions can encounter undefined extended-real sums.

knowledge_statements.title: Neutral Element for Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of the origin is the neutral element of binary infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta_{\{0\}}\) be zero at \(0\) and \(+\infty\) elsewhere. For every extended-real function \(f\), \[f\square\delta_{\{0\}}=\delta_{\{0\}}\square f=f.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\square\delta_{\{0\}}=\delta_{\{0\}}\square f=f
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity law for the binary operation.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain, Convexity, and Commutativity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary infimal convolution is commutative, has the Minkowski sum of the operand domains as its domain, and preserves convexity and properness once minus-infinite values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h=f\square g\) avoid \(-\infty\). Then \[\operatorname{dom}h=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}g,\qquad f\square g=g\square f.\] If \(f\) and \(g\) are convex, then \(h\) is convex. Consequently, if both operands are proper and \(h\) avoids \(-\infty\), then \(h\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}(f\square g)=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}g,\quad f\square g=g\square f,\quad f,g\text{ convex}\Rightarrow f\square g\text{ convex}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural laws specific to the binary operation.

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of the effective domains

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary infimal convolution minimizes the sum of two functions over additive decompositions of the argument; its conjugate is the sum of their conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The binary infimal convolution of \(f\) and \(g\) is the extended-real function \[(f\mathbin{\square}g)(x)=\inf\{f(u)+g(v):u+v=x\}=\inf_{u\in X}\{f(u)+g(x-u)\}.\] With the convention that the resulting function does not take \(-\infty\), its Fenchel conjugate satisfies the exact identity \[(f\mathbin{\square}g)^*(x^*)=f^*(x^*)+g^*(x^*)\] for every \(x^*\in X^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\).
\(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are extended-real functions and their infimal convolution never takes \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f\mathbin{\square}g)(x)=\inf_{u+v=x}\{f(u)+g(v)\},\qquad (f\mathbin{\square}g)^*=f^*+g^*.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary operation and its unconditional algebraic conjugacy identity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common-Subgradient Certificate at an Exact Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization at an attained binary decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper convex, let \(h=f\square g\) be proper, and suppose \(u+v=x\) with \(h(x)=f(u)+g(v)\). Then \[x^*\in\partial h(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^*\in\partial f(u)\cap\partial g(v).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a minimizing decomposition, a vector is a convolution subgradient exactly when it is a common subgradient of both operands at their decomposition points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial h(x)=\partial f(u)\cap\partial g(v)

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of f at u

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subgradient Certificate at an Exact Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic binary-operation laws; associativity remains with the arity-decomposition sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For extended-real functions whose displayed infimal convolutions avoid \(-\infty\), \[f\square g=g\square f,\qquad f\square\delta_{\{0\}}=f,\qquad \operatorname{dom}(f\square g)=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}g.\] If \(f\) and \(g\) are convex, then \(f\square g\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary infimal convolution is commutative, has the singleton indicator as identity, adds effective domains, and preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\square g=g\square f,\quad f\square\delta_{\{0\}}=f,\quad \operatorname{dom}(f\square g)=\operatorname{dom}f+\operatorname{dom}g,\quad f,g\text{ convex}\Rightarrow f\square g\text{ convex}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic specialization of binary infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary sets \(C,D\subseteq X\), \[\delta_C\square\delta_D=\delta_{C+D},\qquad C+D=\{c+d:c\in C,\ d\in D\}.\] Thus binary infimal convolution extends Minkowski addition from sets to extended-real functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infimal convolution of two set indicators is the indicator of their Minkowski sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_C\square\delta_D=\delta_{C+D}

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of C and D

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski-Sum Indicator Representation
Domain, Convexity, and Properness of Multiway Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain of a finite multiway convolution is the Minkowski sum of the operand domains; convexity and properness are preserved once minus-infinite values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h=\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\) avoid \(-\infty\). Then \[\operatorname{dom}h=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i.\] If every \(f_i\) is convex, then \(h\) is convex. If every \(f_i\) is proper, then, under the no-\(-\infty\) assumption, \(h\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{dom}f_i,\qquad (\forall i\ f_i\text{ convex})\Rightarrow\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\text{ convex}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural preservation for the finite-arity operation.

notation.meaning: finite Minkowski sum of the effective domains

knowledge_statements.title: Multiway Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiway infimal convolution minimizes a sum over all additive decompositions into the prescribed number of components, and conjugation turns it into an ordinary sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge2\), the multiway infimal convolution is \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=x\right\}.\] Its conjugate separates across all components: \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)^*(x^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x^*)\] for every \(x^*\in X^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\), and \(m\ge2\).
Each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and the displayed infimum never equals \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i\right)^*(x^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(x^*).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-arity infimal convolution on a common vector space.

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Invariance of Finite Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite infimal convolution is invariant under reordering of its operands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge2\), let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and suppose the relevant infima avoid \(-\infty\). For every permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_{\pi(i)}.\] Thus a finite infimal convolution depends on the multiset of operands, not their enumeration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_{\pi(i)}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order independence of the finite decomposition problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Arity-Dependent Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any finite infimal convolution can be decomposed into binary convolutions, and the result is independent of grouping or parenthesization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=x\) can be introduced one component at a time. Consequently, finite infimal convolution is associative: \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=((f_1\mathbin{\square}f_2)\mathbin{\square}\cdots)\mathbin{\square}f_m,\] and every other parenthesization gives the same function. More generally, if \(\{1,\ldots,m\}=I\mathbin{\dot\cup}J\) is a nontrivial partition, then \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=\left(\mathop{\square}_{i\in I}f_i\right)\mathbin{\square}\left(\mathop{\square}_{j\in J}f_j\right).\]
assumptions_latex: All intermediate and multiway infimal convolutions under consideration avoid the value \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m f_i=((f_1\mathbin{\square}f_2)\mathbin{\square}\cdots)\mathbin{\square}f_m,\] independently of parenthesization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Associative decomposition of finite-arity infimal convolution into binary operations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted infimal convolution under linear synthesis
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_i\) and \(Y\) be real vector spaces, let \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) be linear maps, let \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(\lambda_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite, strictly positive weights and linear synthesis maps. Zero or negative weights require separate recession or sign conventions and are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scaled-weighted infimal convolution associated with \((\lambda_i,A_i,f_i)_{i=1}^m\) is \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m{}^{A_i}_{\lambda_i}f_i\right)(y):=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=y\right\}.\] Its effective domain is \[\sum_{i=1}^m A_i(\operatorname{dom}f_i).\] Equivalently, with \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_i\lambda_i f_i(x_i)\) and \(L(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_iA_ix_i\), the family is \(L\mathbin{\triangleright}F\). When every \(X_i=Y\), every \(A_i=\operatorname{Id}\), and every \(\lambda_i=1\), it reduces to ordinary finite-arity infimal convolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled-weighted infimal convolution minimizes a positively weighted sum of component costs over decompositions synthesized by specified linear maps. Its domain is the Minkowski sum of the mapped component domains. It is equivalently the infimal postcomposition of the separable weighted cost by the synthesis map. Ordinary finite-arity convolution is recovered when all maps are identities and all weights equal one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m{}^{A_i}_{\lambda_i}f_i\right)(y)=\inf_{\sum_iA_ix_i=y}\sum_i\lambda_if_i(x_i).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m{}^{A_i}_{\lambda_i}f_i=L\mathbin{\triangleright}\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\lambda_if_i\right).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(m=2\), \(A_1=A_2=\operatorname{Id}\), the value is \(\inf_x\{\lambda_1f_1(x)+\lambda_2f_2(y-x)\}\).
If one \(A_i\) is the zero map, its component contributes the constant \(\inf \lambda_i f_i\), when meaningful.
immediate_consequences_latex: If every \(f_i\) is convex, then the weighted separable cost and its infimal projection are convex.
Exactness at \(y\) means that the displayed constrained infimum has a finite minimizer.
boundary_notes: The inspected sources support infimal postcomposition and separable infimal convolution but do not name this full weighted-linear family as a standalone definition.
Weights equal to zero are excluded because \(0\cdot(+\infty)\) needs an explicit convention.

notation.meaning: Component function with positive objective weight and synthesis map.

knowledge_statements.title: Semigroup Law for Positive Perspective Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive perspective scalings compose multiplicatively and have unit scale one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda,\mu>0\) and every extended-real function \(g\), \[\lambda\odot(\mu\odot g)=(\lambda\mu)\odot g.\] In particular, \(1\odot g=g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\odot(\mu\odot g)=(\lambda\mu)\odot g,\qquad 1\odot g=g
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition law for the scaling convention used by this leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain and Convexity of Scaled Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive perspective scaling multiplies the second effective domain by the scale; scaled infimal convolution preserves convexity and properness once minus-infinite values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda>0\), \((\lambda\odot g)(v)=\lambda g(v/\lambda)\), and \(h=f\square(\lambda\odot g)\). If \(h\) avoids \(-\infty\), then \[\operatorname{dom}h=\operatorname{dom}f+\lambda\operatorname{dom}g.\] If \(f\) and \(g\) are convex, then \(h\) is convex; if they are proper, then under the no-\(-\infty\) assumption \(h\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}h=\operatorname{dom}f+\lambda\operatorname{dom}g,\qquad f,g\text{ convex}\Rightarrow h\text{ convex}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural effect of a strictly positive perspective scale.

notation.meaning: scalar dilation of the effective domain of g

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled infimal convolution uses perspective scaling on one operand; Fenchel conjugation converts that scaling and convolution into a correspondingly scaled sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), define the perspective scaling \((\lambda\odot g)(v)=\lambda g(v/\lambda)\). The scaled infimal convolution of \(f\) with \(g\) is \[(f\mathbin{\square}(\lambda\odot g))(x)=\inf_{u+v=x}\{f(u)+\lambda g(v/\lambda)\}.\] Since \((\lambda\odot g)^*(x^*)=\lambda g^*(x^*)\), its conjugate is \[(f\mathbin{\square}(\lambda\odot g))^*(x^*)=f^*(x^*)+\lambda g^*(x^*).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(f\mathbin{\square}(\lambda\odot g))^*=f^*+\lambda g^*.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective-scaled second operand with strictly positive scale.

source_witnesses.locator: 12 Infimal Convolution p. 203

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subgradient Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained weighted decomposition is characterized by a common subgradient of all operands at their barycentric components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i=\alpha_i y_i\) and \(\sum_i x_i=x\). A vector \(u\in X^*\) satisfying \(u\in\partial f_i(y_i)\) for every \(i\) certifies \[W(x)=\sum_i\alpha_i f_i(y_i),\qquad u\in\partial W(x),\qquad W(x)+W^*(u)=\langle u,x\rangle.\] Conversely, if this decomposition attains \(W(x)\) and \(u\in\partial W(x)\), then \(u\in\partial f_i(y_i)\) for every \(i\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, \(\alpha_i>0\), and \(W\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in\bigcap_i\partial f_i(y_i)\) is the primal-dual optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for an attained weighted decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Barycentric Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted infimal convolution is a barycentric minimization; normalized averaging of identical convex operands leaves the operand unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha_i>0\), substituting \(x_i=\alpha_i y_i\) gives \[W(x)=\inf_{\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=x}\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(y_i).\] If \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\) and every operand equals the same convex function \(f\), then \(W=f\).
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper and convex and each \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(x)=\inf_{\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=x}\sum_i\alpha_i f_i(y_i)\), and normalized identical operands satisfy \(W=f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent primal formulation for positive weights.

notation.meaning: Weighted infimal convolution under the seed convention

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted infimal convolution combines perspective-scaled operands over additive decompositions; its conjugate is the same weighted sum of the individual conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive weights \(\alpha_i\), define \((\alpha_i\odot f_i)(x_i)=\alpha_i f_i(x_i/\alpha_i)\). Their weighted infimal convolution is \[W(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(x_i/\alpha_i):\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=x\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(W=\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f_i)\), and therefore \[W^*(x^*)=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i^*(x^*).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space paired with \(X^*\), and \(m\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f_i)\right)^*=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i^*.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multiway convolution with positive perspective weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collapse rule for positive perspective copies of one convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex, let \(\alpha_i>0\), and set \(A=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i\). Then
\[
\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f)=A\odot f.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=x}\sum_i\alpha_i f(y_i)=A f(x/A),
\]
and whenever this value is finite it is attained by \(y_i=x/A\) for every \(i\). In particular, normalized weights reproduce \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive perspective copies of one convex function combine into a single perspective copy with the total weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\square_i(\alpha_i\odot f)=A\odot f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation of Identical Convex Operands

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barycentric Form of Weighted Infimal Convolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent positive-weight formulation obtained by rescaling decomposition variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha_i>0\), substituting \(x_i=\alpha_i y_i\) gives
\[
\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f_i)\right)(x)
=
\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(y_i):\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i y_i=x\right\}.
\]
When \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), the constraint represents \(x\) as the weighted barycenter of the component arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted infimal convolution equivalently minimizes a weighted sum over weighted decompositions of the target.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infimum does not equal \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\square_i(\alpha_i\odot f_i)(x)=\inf_{\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=x}\sum_i\alpha_i f_i(y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Barycentric Form of Weighted Infimal Convolution
Negative-Weight Convexity Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative perspective weight can turn a convex operand into a concave function, so the weighted convex-conjugacy rules fail outside the nonnegative regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The positive perspective formula does not extend as convex calculus to negative weights. For \(f(t)=t^2\) and \(\alpha<0\), \[(\alpha\odot f)(x)=\alpha f(x/\alpha)=\frac{x^2}{\alpha},\] which is strictly concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto x^2/\alpha\) is concave and is not a convex perspective-scaled operand.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary beyond the nonnegative closed-perspective regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Weight Collapse
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all weights vanish and the resulting convolution is proper, its conjugate is the indicator of the intersection of the closed conjugate domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_0=\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m\operatorname{rec}f_i\). If \(W_0\) is proper, then \[W_0^*=\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_{\overline{\operatorname{dom}f_i^*}}=\delta_{\bigcap_{i=1}^m\overline{\operatorname{dom}f_i^*}}.\] Thus complete weight collapse retains precisely the common dual-domain constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and each \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_0^*=\delta_{\cap_i\overline{\operatorname{dom}f_i^*}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-zero boundary of closed perspective-weighted infimal convolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Weight Degeneracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero weight, closed perspective scaling becomes the recession function. Its conjugate is the indicator of the closed domain of the original conjugate, so zero-weight operands impose dual-domain constraints rather than contributing an everywhere-zero term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), let \((\alpha\odot f)(x)=\alpha f(x/\alpha)\). Its closed convex extension to zero weight is \[(0\odot f)(x)=\operatorname{rec}f(x).\] In finite dimensions, the conjugate of this zero-weight term is \[(0\odot f)^*=\delta_{\overline{\operatorname{dom}f^*}},\] rather than the zero function on the entire dual space. Consequently, if \(P=\{i:\alpha_i>0\}\) and \(Z=\{i:\alpha_i=0\}\), then \[\left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f_i)\right)^*=\sum_{i\in P}\alpha_i f_i^*+\sum_{i\in Z}\delta_{\overline{\operatorname{dom}f_i^*}}.\] Thus a zero-weight operand imposes a dual-domain constraint and does not generally disappear.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(m\ge 2\), and each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The weights satisfy \(\alpha_i\ge 0\), with at least one positive weight, and the resulting infimal convolution does not take the value \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(0\odot f_i)=\operatorname{rec}f_i,\qquad \left(\mathop{\square}_{i=1}^m(\alpha_i\odot f_i)\right)^*=\sum_{i:\alpha_i>0}\alpha_i f_i^*+\sum_{i:\alpha_i=0}\delta_{\overline{\operatorname{dom}f_i^*}}.\]

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces and let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General extended-real marginal functions. Convexity passes to the marginal under joint convexity, while closedness and attainment require additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fiberwise infimal elimination of the variable \(y\) from \(F\) is the marginal function \[M_F:X\to[-\infty,+\infty],\qquad M_F(x):=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y).\] Its domain and minimizing fiber are \[\operatorname{dom}M_F=\{x\in X:(\exists y\in Y)\ F(x,y)<+\infty\},\qquad S_F(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}F(x,y).\] The elimination is exact at \(x\) when \(S_F(x)\neq\varnothing\) and \(M_F(x)>-\infty\). Equivalently, if \(P:X\times Y\to X\) is the projection \(P(x,y)=x\), then \[M_F=P\mathbin{\triangleright}F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fiberwise infimal elimination removes a latent variable by taking the infimum of a joint extended-real function over each fiber above the retained variable. The marginal domain is the projection of the joint domain. The minimizing fiber records whether elimination is exact. This is precisely infimal postcomposition through the coordinate projection. Joint convexity implies convexity of the marginal, but neither attainment nor lower semicontinuity follows from the definition alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M_F(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)=\left(P\mathbin{\triangleright}F\right)(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using an indicator of the fiber, \[M_F(x)=\inf_{(u,y)\in X\times Y}\{F(u,y)+\iota_{\{x\}}(u)\}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(F(x,y)=f(y)+g(x-y)\), then \(M_F=f\square g\).
If \(Y\) is a singleton, then \(M_F\) is the corresponding section of \(F\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F\) is jointly convex, then \(M_F\) is convex.
If \(F(x,\cdot)\) has a minimizer, then \(S_F(x)\neq\varnothing\) and the fiberwise infimum is attained at that point.
boundary_notes: Partial minimization of a closed convex function need not be closed in infinite-dimensional spaces or under a nonclosed projection.
A value of \(-\infty\) is an improper marginal, not an attained finite elimination.
