knowledge_statements.scope_note: General closedness obstruction caused solely by excluding scale zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and set \(E_+=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\ge t f(x/t)\}\). Then \(E_+\) is convex but not closed, and \((0,0,0)\in\operatorname{cl}E_+\setminus E_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-scale perspective epigraph of every proper convex function is convex but nonclosed because it excludes the limiting origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_+\text{ is convex and }(0,0,0)\in\operatorname{cl}E_+\setminus E_+.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Universal Positive-Scale Nonclosedness

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\). Set \(C=\{1\}\times\operatorname{epi}\varphi\subset\mathbb R\times\mathcal H\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The model is the raw positive-scale homogenization. Nonclosedness is an epigraph property in the ambient product topology; the entry does not claim that every subsequent projection is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonclosed perspective model generated by \(\varphi\) is \[F(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\+\infty,&\xi\leq0.
\end{cases}\] Its epigraph is \(\operatorname{epi}F=\operatorname{cone}C\). It is called nonclosed when \[\operatorname{epi}F\neq\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}F),\] equivalently when \(F\) is not lower semicontinuous. Its closed completion is obtained by assigning \((\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\) at \(\xi=0\) and \(+\infty\) at \(\xi<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw perspective model uses the ordinary perspective formula only for positive scale and assigns positive infinity for nonpositive scale. Its epigraph is the conic hull of the unit-scale epigraph. The model is nonclosed when that conic hull is not closed, or equivalently when the extended-real function is not lower semicontinuous. Closing the model adds the recession-function slice at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{epi}F=\operatorname{cone}(\{1\}\times\operatorname{epi}\varphi),\qquad F\text{ is nonclosed}\iff \operatorname{epi}F\neq\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}F).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Nonclosedness means that there are \((\xi_k,x_k,r_k)\in\operatorname{epi}F\) converging to a point outside \(\operatorname{epi}F\).

The closed completion is \[\overline F(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x),&\xi=0,\\+\infty,&\xi<0.
\end{cases}\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\varphi(x)=\|x\|^p\), \(p>1\), the missing finite zero-scale point is the origin, with all epigraph heights above zero.
For sublinear \(\varphi\), the closed completion has the full slice \(\overline F(0,x)=\varphi(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A minimization model using \(F\) may have the same infimum as its completion while failing to attain a limiting zero-scale solution.
Replacing \(F\) by its closed completion preserves every positive-scale value.
boundary_notes: Convexity alone does not imply closedness.
The restriction of \(F\) to \(\xi>0\) can be continuous even though the ambient extended-real function is nonclosed.
This definition concerns the perspective before any additional affine image or elimination.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Scale Perspective Epigraphs Are Not Closed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic closure failure caused solely by excluding the zero-scale slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and define \[E_+(f):=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\ge t f(x/t)\}.\] Then \(E_+(f)\) is not closed. Indeed, for any \(u\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(a\ge f(u)\), \((tu,t,ta)\in E_+(f)\) for every \(t>0\), while \((tu,t,ta)\to(0,0,0)\notin E_+(f)\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every proper function, excluding zero scale makes the positive-scale perspective epigraph nonclosed because scaled epigraph points converge to the omitted origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_+(f)\text{ is not closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Scale Perspective Epigraphs Are Not Closed
Missing Homogenized Domain Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing the indicator of an interval requires all inequalities defining its scaled domain; omitting one admits invalid zero-scale points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed perspective epigraph of \(f\) is \[E=\bigl\{(x,t,r)\in\mathbb R^3:0\le x\le t,\ t\ge0,\ r\ge0\bigr\}.\] Retaining only \(x\le t\) and \(r\ge0\) admits, for example, \((-1,0,0)\), which does not belong to \(E\). Thus homogenization must preserve every domain inequality, including the scale constraint and the homogenized lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping homogenized domain inequalities strictly enlarges the perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator example exposing indispensable homogenized domain constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-by-constraint audit of the homogenized domain for the interval indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f=\delta_{[0,1]}\), the homogenized domain is \(K=\{(x,t):0\le x\le t\}\). Omitting \(x\ge0\) admits \((-1,1)\), and omitting \(x\le t\) admits \((2,1)\). The separate inequality \(t\ge0\) is redundant once both inequalities are retained, since \(0\le x\le t\) implies \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both scaled interval bounds are indispensable, while a separate nonnegative-scale inequality is redundant for this particular representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(x\ge0\) and \(x\le t\) are individually necessary, whereas \(t\ge0\) is implied by them.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex on a finite-dimensional space. Let \(G\) be its closed perspective and \(E=\operatorname{epi}G\subset\mathbb R\times X\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition diagnoses set-theoretic omission of scale-domain or recession-slice constraints. It does not prescribe a particular algebraic modeling language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed homogenized feasible set \(M\subset\mathbb R\times X\times\mathbb R\) has missing homogenized domain constraints when it agrees with the perspective epigraph at positive scale but is not equal to the closed epigraph: \[M\cap\{t>0\}=E\cap\{t>0\},\qquad M\neq E.\] It is an outer domain omission when \(E\subsetneq M\), and an inner domain omission when \(M\subsetneq E\). The canonical domain conditions encoded by \(E\) are \(t\geq0\), \(r\geq t\varphi(x/t)\) for \(t>0\), and \(r\geq(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\) for \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogenized model is domain-incomplete when it is correct at every positive scale but differs from the closed perspective epigraph somewhere else. If it contains extra points it is an outer omission; if it loses required points it is an inner omission. The complete model requires nonnegative scale, the perspective inequality at positive scale, and the recession inequality at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M\cap\{t>0\}=E\cap\{t>0\},\ M\neq E,\qquad E=\{(t,x,r):t>0,\ r\geq t\varphi(x/t)\}\cup\{(0,x,r):r\geq\operatorname{rec}\varphi(x)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The defect set is \(\Delta(M,E)=(M\setminus E)\cup(E\setminus M)\), and domain completeness is equivalent to \(\Delta(M,E)=\varnothing\).
An outer omission admits at least one spurious point in \(M\setminus E\); an inner omission excludes at least one valid point in \(E\setminus M\).
special_cases_latex: Omitting \(t\geq0\) can admit negative-scale points if the remaining algebraic constraints do not exclude them.
Using only \((t,x)=(0,0)\) at zero scale is an inner omission whenever \(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)\neq\{0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Agreement on \(t=1\) or even on all \(t>0\) does not establish equality of closed homogenized models.
An outer omission may weaken an optimization problem; an inner omission may destroy closedness or attainment.
boundary_notes: A redundant omitted inequality is not a missing domain constraint because it does not change \(M\).

Errors unrelated to scale or recession geometry lie outside this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted Representation of a Set or Function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be an extended-space feasible set, and let \(\pi_x(x,u)=x\). For a function \(f\), apply the same construction to \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the abstract finite-dimensional projection interface. The internal set may be polyhedral, conic, semidefinite, or another closed convex representable set; cone catalogs and solver consequences are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lifted representation interface for \(X\) is a pair \((Q,\pi_x)\) satisfying \[X=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^m\text{ with }(x,u)\in Q\}.\] It is exact when equality holds and outer-relaxed when only \(X\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\) holds. A lifted representation of an extended-real function \(f\) is a set \(Q_f\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m\) such that \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists u\ (x,t,u)\in Q_f\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted representation introduces auxiliary variables and a feasible set in the enlarged variable space. The target set consists exactly of the original-variable components that possess at least one feasible auxiliary completion. For a function, the represented object is its epigraph. Equality gives an exact lift; one-sided containment gives an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in X\iff\exists u\in\mathbb R^m:(x,u)\in Q,\qquad (x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\iff\exists u:(x,t,u)\in Q_f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The indicator satisfies \(\iota_X(x)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\iota_Q(x,u)\).

If \(Q=\{(x,u):A x+B u-b\in K\}\), the interface is a conic lift.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a convex cone, \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(B:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition captures the common structural architecture of lifted convex representations: an affine inverse image of a cone followed by coordinate projection. It does not classify particular cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone-based lift architecture is the tuple \(\mathfrak L=(K,A,B,b,\pi_x)\) with lifted feasible set \[Q_{\mathfrak L}=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m:A x+B u-b\in K\}\] and represented set \[X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(Q_{\mathfrak L})=\{x:\exists u,\ A x+B u-b\in K\}.\] Two architectures are representation-equivalent when their represented sets coincide, even if their auxiliary dimensions, cones, or affine maps differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift architecture consists of a cone, affine data linking original and auxiliary variables, and projection back to the original variables. Its lifted feasible set is the affine inverse image of the cone, and its represented set is the coordinate projection of that feasible set. Architectures with different internal data are representation-equivalent when they project to the same target set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak L=(K,A,B,b,\pi_x),\quad Q_{\mathfrak L}=\{(x,u):Ax+Bu-b\in K\},\quad X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(Q_{\mathfrak L}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Membership has the quantified form \(x\in X_{\mathfrak L}\iff\exists u\; Ax+Bu-b\in K\).
Writing \(L(x,u)=Ax+Bu-b\), one has \(Q_{\mathfrak L}=L^{-1}(K)\) and \(X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(L^{-1}(K))\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^q\), the architecture is a polyhedral extended formulation.
For \(K\) a product of second-order cones, it is a conic-quadratic architecture.
For \(K\) a positive-semidefinite cone and an affine symmetric-matrix map, it is a semidefinite architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(K\) is convex, then both \(Q_{\mathfrak L}\) and \(X_{\mathfrak L}\) are convex.
An invertible affine change of auxiliary coordinates preserves the represented set after the corresponding change to \(B\) and \(b\).
boundary_notes: Closedness of \(K\) and \(Q_{\mathfrak L}\) does not by itself ensure closedness of \(X_{\mathfrak L}\).
Representation equivalence does not assert equal lift size or equal computational behavior.
Nonconic extended formulations require a broader architecture than the tuple defined here.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), define \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(f(x)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^m}F(x,z)\), and let \(P(x,z,r)=(x,r)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional definition allows unattained infima. It separates the projected epigraph from its closure and therefore records the exactness boundary of the lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The epigraph-partial-minimization lift generated by \(F\) is \[Q_F:=\operatorname{epi}F=\{(x,z,r):F(x,z)\leq r\},\qquad f(x):=\inf_zF(x,z).\] Its projected epigraph satisfies \[P(Q_F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}f\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P(Q_F).\] The lift is epigraph-exact when \(P(Q_F)=\operatorname{epi}f\); equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), the infimum defining \(f(x)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a function of original and auxiliary variables, partially minimize over the auxiliary variable. The epigraph of the original function is the lifted set. Its projection is always contained in the epigraph of the marginal function, while the marginal epigraph is contained in the closure of that projection. Equality with the projection is the exact regime and corresponds to attainment of every finite partial infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}f\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P(\operatorname{epi}F),\qquad f(x)=\inf_zF(x,z).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A point \((x,r)\) belongs to \(P(\operatorname{epi}F)\) exactly when some \(z\) satisfies \(F(x,z)\leq r\).
At a finite marginal value, \((x,f(x))\in P(\operatorname{epi}F)\) exactly when \(\operatorname{argmin}_zF(x,z)\neq\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: If \(F\) is convex, then \(f\) is convex.
If \(F\) is closed proper convex and an auxiliary-variable level set is nonempty and compact under the cited criterion, then \(f\) is closed proper convex and all finite partial minima are attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failure of attainment can remove lower-boundary points from the projected epigraph without changing its closure.
Closedness of \(\operatorname{epi}F\) alone is insufficient to guarantee epigraph exactness after projection.
boundary_notes: The marginal function may take \(-\infty\) unless additional properness assumptions are imposed.
The equality criterion concerns all finite marginal values, not merely equality of optimal values in one optimization problem.
Infinite-dimensional analogues require additional topological qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph lift places retained and auxiliary variables in a jointly convex epigraph. Its projection lies in the marginal epigraph and equals it exactly when every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An epigraph lift of the marginal \(g\) is the convex set \[L=\operatorname{epi}F=\bigl\{(x,y,r)\in X\times Y\times\mathbb R:F(x,y)\le r\bigr\},\] in which \(y\) is auxiliary and \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\). Its projection is \[\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(L)=\bigl\{(x,r)\in X\times\mathbb R:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ with }F(x,y)\le r\bigr\}\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g.\] Equality holds if and only if, for every \(x\in X\) with \(g(x)\in\mathbb R\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \(F(x,y)=g(x)\).
assumptions_latex: The marginal \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) satisfies \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of \(\operatorname{epi}F\) is contained in \(\operatorname{epi}g\), with equality exactly when every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph lift with auxiliary variables in finite dimensions and an explicit marginal interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Minimization Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization of a jointly convex function is convex, and under attainment its epigraph equals the projection of the lifted epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the partial-minimization lift by \[g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y).\] Then \(g\) is convex, possibly extended-valued, and attainment yields the exact identity \[\operatorname{epi}g=\bigl\{(x,r)\in X\times\mathbb R:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ such that }F(x,y)\le r\bigr\}=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] Without attainment, the displayed projection can omit boundary points at height \(g(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F(x,\cdot)\) has a minimizer whenever its infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The marginal \(g\) is convex and its epigraph is the projection of \(\operatorname{epi}F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact marginal representation under pointwise attainment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain projection and the unbounded-below fiber obstruction to a proper marginal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex and define \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\). If \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\), then
\[
\operatorname{dom}g=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F),
\]
and \(g\) is proper and convex. Joint properness alone is insufficient: if \(F(x,y)=y\) on \(X\times\mathbb R\), then \(F\) is proper, closed, and affine, but \(g(x)=-\infty\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absent fibers unbounded below, the marginal is proper and its domain is the projection of the joint domain; joint properness alone does not prevent a marginal equal to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(g(x)>-\infty\) for all \(x\), then \(\operatorname{dom}g=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F)\) and \(g\) is proper; an unbounded-below fiber can destroy properness.

notation.meaning: partial minimum of \(F\) over the auxiliary variable

knowledge_statements.title: Properness Boundary for Partial Minimization
Exact Strict-Epigraph Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected lifted epigraph always contains the strict epigraph of the marginal; only unattained boundary points can be absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\), and suppose \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\). Then \[\{(x,r):g(x)<r\}\subseteq\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g.\] Hence the projection can omit only a boundary point \((x,g(x))\), and that point belongs to the projection exactly when the infimum defining \(g(x)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}_{<}g\subseteq\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g\), with boundary membership equivalent to attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment-free part of the epigraphical projection interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraphical Projection Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected lifted epigraph may miss unattained boundary points; attainment gives exact projection, while lower semicontinuity identifies the marginal epigraph with its closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] Then \[P\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P.\] The first inclusion follows from the definition of the infimum, while the second records approximation by auxiliary points with values arbitrarily close to \(g(x)\). Moreover, \(P=\operatorname{epi}g\) exactly when every finite marginal value is attained. If \(g\) is lower semicontinuous, then \(\operatorname{epi}g=\operatorname{cl}P\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex on finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection lies between the marginal epigraph and its closure, with exactness under attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and closure-level interfaces between epigraph projection and marginalization.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Image and Marginal Functions p. 118

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Closure Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected epigraph is closed precisely when the marginal is lower semicontinuous and all finite marginal values are attained; without attainment, closure recovers the marginal epigraph when the marginal is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] The following conditions are equivalent: \(P\) is closed; \(g\) is lower semicontinuous and, for every \(x\in X\) with \(g(x)\in\mathbb R\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \(F(x,y)=g(x)\); and \[P=\operatorname{epi}g\quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{epi}g\text{ closed}.\] If attainment fails while \(g\) remains lower semicontinuous, then \[\operatorname{cl}P=\operatorname{epi}g.\]
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The marginal \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) satisfies \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected epigraph is closed exactly when elimination yields the closed marginal epigraph; equivalently, \(g\) is lower semicontinuous and every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent closedness conditions for eliminating auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be convex, let \(L:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, let \(c\in\mathbb R^q\), and let \(\pi_x(x,u)=x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional correspondence identifies existential affine constraints with projection of an affine inverse image. It includes conic and semidefinite slices but makes no cone-specific duality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-slice lift determined by \((C,L,c)\) is \[Q:=\{(x,u):L(x,u)-c\in C\}=L_c^{-1}(C),\qquad L_c(x,u)=L(x,u)-c.\] Its projection is \[X:=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^m,\ L(x,u)-c\in C\}.\] The affine-slice projection-lift correspondence is the equivalence \[x\in X\iff\exists u\;(x,u)\in Q\iff\exists u\;L(x,u)-c\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take an affine inverse image of a convex set in a space containing original and auxiliary variables, then project away the auxiliary variables. Membership in the projected set is equivalent to the existence of an auxiliary completion satisfying the affine-slice constraint. This is the affine-slice projection-lift correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X=\pi_x(L_c^{-1}(C))=\{x:\exists u,\ L(x,u)-c\in C\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(L(x,u)=Ax+Bu\), then \(X=\{x:\exists u,\ Ax+Bu-c\in C\}\).
The indicator identity is \(\iota_X(x)=\inf_u\iota_C(L(x,u)-c)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(C=\{0\}\), the lift consists of affine equality constraints.
For \(C=K\) a convex cone, this is a conic lift.
For \(C=\mathbb S_+^k\) and symmetric-matrix-valued \(L_c\), the construction is a semidefinite representation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convexity of \(C\) implies convexity of both \(Q\) and \(X\).
Multiple auxiliary witnesses may correspond to the same projected point.
boundary_notes: A linear image of a closed convex set need not be closed when the set is unbounded.
The word slice includes affine inverse images, not only intersections with coordinate hyperplanes.
The correspondence asserts set equality and does not assert preservation of facial structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Slice Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-slice lift intersects a lifted convex set with affine equations and projects away auxiliary variables to represent a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b\in Z\), an affine-slice lift represents \(C\subseteq X\) by \[C=\bigl\{x\in X:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ such that }(x,y)\in K\text{ and }Ax+By=b\bigr\}.\] Equivalently, \[C=\pi_X\bigl(K\cap\{(x,y):Ax+By=b\}\bigr).\] The sliced lift is convex, so its projection \(C\) is convex, although it need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented set is the projection of a convex set cut out by an affine slice.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine-slice extended formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection lift represents a set as the coordinate image of a higher-dimensional convex set; convexity survives projection, but closedness may not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projection lift of \(C\subseteq X\) is a convex set \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) satisfying \[C=\pi_X(L)=\bigl\{x\in X:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ with }(x,y)\in L\bigr\}.\] Because linear images of convex sets are convex, \(C\) is convex. Even when \(L\) is closed, \(C\) may fail to be closed, so closed representability requires an additional image-closedness condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\pi_X(L)\) is convex, but closedness need not pass from \(L\) to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-projection formulation of convex lifts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Identity and Visible Separation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function and strict nonmembership interface for a convex projection lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) be nonempty and convex and let \(C=\pi_X(L)\). For every \(u\in X^*\), \[\sigma_C(u)=\sigma_L(u,0).\] Moreover, for \(\bar x\in X\), \[\bar x\notin\operatorname{cl}C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists u\in X^*:\ \langle u,\bar x\rangle>\sigma_L(u,0).\] Thus a strict visible-space separator is precisely a lifted separator with zero auxiliary dual component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a projection is the lifted support function at zero auxiliary dual coordinate, yielding exact strict certificates outside the projected closure.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_C(u)=\sigma_L(u,0)\), and \(\bar x\notin\operatorname{cl}C\) exactly when some \(u\) satisfies \(\langle u,\bar x\rangle>\sigma_L(u,0)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitivity of existential auxiliary-variable representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\times Z\), set \(L=\pi_{X\times Y}(Q)\), and set \(C=\pi_X(L)\). Then \[C=\pi_X(Q)=\{x:\exists y\in Y,\exists z\in Z\text{ such that }(x,y,z)\in Q\}.\] Hence projection lifts compose, and convexity of \(Q\) implies convexity of both \(L\) and \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested projection lifts flatten into one projection by retaining all auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(\pi_{X\times Y}(Q))=\pi_X(Q)\); if \(Q\) is convex, its intermediate and final projections are convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Projection Lifts
Slice–Projection Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine-slice lifts are projection lifts of constrained convex sets, while ordinary projection lifts arise by using a vacuous affine slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-slice representation \[C=\pi_X\bigl(K\cap M^{-1}(b)\bigr)\] is a projection lift with lifted set \(L=K\cap M^{-1}(b)\). Conversely, any projection lift \(C=\pi_X(L)\) is an affine-slice lift by taking \(K=L\), the zero map \(M=0\), and \(b=0\). Thus the two architectures differ only in whether affine constraints are displayed separately from the lifted convex set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\times Y\) is convex in finite dimensions.
\(M:X\times Y\to Z\) is linear and \(b\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every affine-slice lift is a projection lift, and every projection lift is the trivial-slice case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of slicing-plus-projection and projection of a constrained lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Image Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex epigraph can have a nonclosed coordinate projection, so closed lifted sets do not automatically yield closed represented sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \[L=\bigl\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge1/x\bigr\}\] is the epigraph of the convex function \(x\mapsto1/x\) on \((0,+\infty)\), extended by \(+\infty\) elsewhere; hence \(L\) is closed and convex. Nevertheless, \[\pi_x(L)=(0,+\infty),\] which is not closed. Indeed, \(1/n\in\pi_x(L)\) converges to \(0\notin\pi_x(L)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is closed and convex, but \(\pi_x(L)=(0,+\infty)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional example of a nonclosed projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-Witness Escape at a Missing Image Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary finite-dimensional mechanism for closure loss under coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) be closed, with \(X,Y\) finite-dimensional, and suppose \(x_n\in\pi_X(L)\) converges to \(\bar x\notin\pi_X(L)\). For every choice of witnesses \(y_n\) satisfying \((x_n,y_n)\in L\), the sequence \((y_n)\) is unbounded. Equivalently, a bounded witness sequence would have a convergent subsequence whose limit, by closedness of \(L\), witnesses \(\bar x\in\pi_X(L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a missing limit point of the projection of a closed finite-dimensional set, every corresponding sequence of auxiliary witnesses must escape every bounded set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall (y_n)\,[(x_n,y_n)\in L\ \forall n\Rightarrow (y_n)\text{ is unbounded}]\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be an extended formulation in variables \((x,u)\), and let \(\iota_Q\) be its extended-real indicator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination is defined semantically through existential quantification and partial minimization, not through a particular symbolic elimination algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The elimination interface of \(Q\) is the projected set and marginal indicator \[X_Q:=\{x:\exists u\ (x,u)\in Q\},\qquad h_Q(x):=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\iota_Q(x,u).\] Then \[h_Q=\iota_{X_Q},\qquad X_Q=\operatorname{dom}h_Q=\pi_x(Q).\] For a lifted epigraph \(Q_f\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m\), elimination yields \[E_f:=\{(x,t):\exists u\ (x,t,u)\in Q_f\};\] the formulation represents \(f\) exactly when \(E_f=\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating auxiliary variables means existentially quantifying them. The resulting set is the projection of the extended feasible set. Equivalently, partially minimizing the extended-set indicator over the auxiliary variables gives exactly the indicator of the projected set. For a lifted epigraph, exact elimination requires the resulting projection to equal the target epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X_Q=\pi_x(Q),\qquad \iota_{X_Q}(x)=\inf_u\iota_Q(x,u),\qquad E_f=\pi_{x,t}(Q_f).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\notin X_Q\) exactly when every auxiliary completion violates membership in \(Q\).
For each \(x\), \(h_Q(x)=0\) if a feasible witness exists and \(+\infty\) otherwise.
special_cases_latex: Eliminating slack variables from affine conic constraints produces their projected conic-representable set.
Eliminating the auxiliary variable from \(\operatorname{epi}F\) gives the partial-minimization epigraph interface.
immediate_consequences_latex: The projected description can be exact even when no finite inequality description in the original variables is supplied.
Closure may be required after elimination if the projected epigraph omits limiting points.
boundary_notes: This definition does not claim that quantifier elimination is computationally tractable.
If a marginal objective rather than an indicator is eliminated, an infimum may be unattained.
Replacing \(\pi_x(Q)\) by its closure changes the represented set unless the projection is already closed.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Preservation by an Exact Extended Formulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact extended formulation preserves the value and original-variable minimizers of every objective depending only on the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\pi_X(Q)\) and let \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Then \[\inf_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\varphi(x)\] and \[\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}\varphi(x)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}\varphi(x).\] Thus every lifted minimizer projects to an original minimizer, and every original minimizer has a lifted minimizing witness.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) depends only on the original variable \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_S\varphi=\inf_Q\varphi\), and the projected lifted argmin set equals the original argmin set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of exact set projection for objectives depending only on original variables.

notation.meaning: set of attained minimizers, possibly empty

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation describes a set as the projection of a feasible set involving original and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended formulation of \(S\) is a set \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\) satisfying \[S=\pi_X(Q)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}.\] The variables in \(Y\) are auxiliary. If \(S\) and \(Q\) are convex, this is a convex extended formulation; if \(Q\) is described by affine and conic constraints, it is a conic extended formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional set lifts; convexity or conic structure may be imposed on the lifted feasible set.

notation.meaning: feasible set in the lifted space

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Pullback through an Extended Formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization equivalence induced by an exact set lift for objectives depending only on visible variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\pi_X(Q)\), and let \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\varphi(x)
\]
and
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}\varphi(x)\right).
\]
Thus pulling a visible-variable objective back to an exact extended formulation preserves its optimal value and visible minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing an objective that depends only on the visible variables over an exact extended formulation preserves the infimum and the visible minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The lifted objective is \((x,y)\mapsto\varphi(x)\) and is independent of the auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\varphi(x)\) and the visible argmin sets agree after projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Pullback through an Extended Formulation
Exact Domain and Strict-Sublevel Elimination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination exactly projects the effective domain and strict sublevels without requiring minimizers; only closed-sublevel boundaries can be lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) and suppose \(f(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\). Then \[\operatorname{dom}f=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F)\] and, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \[\{x:f(x)<\alpha\}=\pi_X\bigl(\{(x,y):F(x,y)<\alpha\}\bigr).\] No attainment assumption is required. Replacing strict inequalities by \(\leq\) can fail at an unattained marginal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F)\) and \(\{f<\alpha\}=\pi_X\{F<\alpha\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment-free set identities for eliminating an auxiliary block by infimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Elimination Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization eliminates auxiliary variables. Projecting the lifted epigraph gives the marginal epigraph exactly when finite marginal infima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminating \(y\) from \(F\) produces the marginal function \[f(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y).\] Its lifted epigraph satisfies \[\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)=\{(x,t):\exists y\in Y,\ F(x,y)\leq t\}\subseteq\operatorname{epi}f.\] Equality holds if, for every \(x\) with \(f(x)\in\mathbb R\), the infimum defining \(f(x)\) is attained. Without attainment, only boundary points at height \(f(x)\) can be missing from the projection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}f\), with equality under attainment at every \(x\) where \(f(x)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraphical interface between partial minimization and projection.

notation.meaning: function before eliminating the auxiliary variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal values, projected minimizers, and auxiliary lifting witnesses for partial minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}F(x,y).
\]
Every joint minimizer \((\bar x,\bar y)\) projects to a minimizer \(\bar x\) of \(f\). Conversely, a marginal minimizer \(\bar x\) lifts to a joint minimizer exactly when its fiber infimum is attained, namely when some \(\bar y\) satisfies \(F(\bar x,\bar y)=f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination preserves the global infimum; joint minimizers project to marginal minimizers, and marginal minimizers lift exactly under fiberwise attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x f=\inf_{x,y}F\), and lifting a marginal minimizer is equivalent to attainment of its fiber infimum.

notation.meaning: candidate joint minimizer and its visible projection

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Interface under Elimination
Equivalence-Relation Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Formulation equivalence is an equivalence relation whose classes consist of all lifts representing the same original-variable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On lifted feasible sets with a fixed designated original-variable space \(X\), \[Q_1\sim_XQ_2\iff\pi_X(Q_1)=\pi_X(Q_2)\] is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Its equivalence classes are indexed by the represented subsets of \(X\).
assumptions_latex: Every formulation under comparison has the same designated original-variable space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sim_X\) is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic structure of extensional equivalence among compatible lifted formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Invariance under Formulation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulations give identical values and projected solution sets for every original-variable objective, although their lifted solutions may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q_1\sim_XQ_2\), with \(\pi_X(Q_1)=\pi_X(Q_2)=S\). For every \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \[\inf_{(x,y_1)\in Q_1}\varphi(x)=\inf_{x\in S}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y_2)\in Q_2}\varphi(x),\] and \[\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q_1}\varphi(x)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{S}\varphi=\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q_2}\varphi(x)\right).\] Auxiliary minimizers and lifted geometry need not coincide.
assumptions_latex: The objective depends only on \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent formulations have equal infimal values and equal projected argmin sets for every original-variable objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization consequences of equality of original-variable projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two lifted formulations are equivalent when eliminating their auxiliary variables produces the same feasible set in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lifted formulations \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are formulation-equivalent over \(X\), written \(Q_1\sim_X Q_2\), exactly when \[\pi_X(Q_1)=\pi_X(Q_2).\] Thus they admit precisely the same original-variable feasible points, although their auxiliary spaces, lifted feasible points, constraint systems, and attainment behavior may differ. If both projections equal a prescribed set \(S\subseteq X\), both are exact extended formulations of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_1\sim_X Q_2\iff\pi_X(Q_1)=\pi_X(Q_2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence is extensional in the original variables, not equality of lifted feasible sets.

notation.meaning: equivalence with respect to original variables

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Dualization of Linear Programs p. 165

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent characterization of formulation equivalence by all objectives on the visible-variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q_i\subseteq X\times Y_i\),
\[
Q_1\sim_XQ_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\inf_{(x,y_1)\in Q_1}\varphi(x)=\inf_{(x,y_2)\in Q_2}\varphi(x)
\quad\text{for every }\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty].
\]
When these conditions hold, the projected argmin sets also agree for every such visible-variable objective:
\[
\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y_1)\in Q_1}\varphi(x)\right)
=
\pi_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y_2)\in Q_2}\varphi(x)\right).
\]
No equality of auxiliary fibers, lifted geometry, or constraint descriptions follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations have the same visible projection exactly when every objective on the visible variables has the same infimum over both; equivalent formulations also have the same visible minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_1\sim_XQ_2\) if and only if all visible-variable objective infima agree; under equivalence, projected argmin sets agree as well.

notation.meaning: arbitrary extended-real objective on the visible-variable space

knowledge_statements.title: Visible Optimization Characterization
Elimination-Induced Closure Loss
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed convex epigraph of the reciprocal function projects onto the nonclosed positive half-line, demonstrating closure loss under elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\geq 1/x\}.\] This set is closed and convex in \(\mathbb R^2\), while elimination of \(y\) gives \[\pi_x(C)=(0,\infty),\] which is convex but not closed. Hence projecting a closed convex extended formulation can remove a boundary point and destroy closedness, even in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex, but \(\pi_x(C)=(0,\infty)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional closed convex lift whose elimination loses closedness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness, Attainment, and Closedness Boundaries of a Lift
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be a lifted set with projection \(Y=\pi_x(Q)\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the intended target. For an epigraph lift, replace \(x\) by \((x,t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The taxonomy separates three logically different properties: target equality, witness existence, and topological closedness. It is finite-dimensional and set-theoretic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lift \((Q,\pi_x)\) is classified by: \[(E)\quad Y=X\quad\text{(representation exactness)},\] \[(C)\quad Y=\operatorname{cl}Y\quad\text{(projection closedness)},\] and, for a partial-minimization epigraph lift \(Q=\operatorname{epi}F\), \[(A)\quad\forall x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \operatorname{argmin}_uF(x,u)\neq\varnothing\quad\text{(boundary attainment)}.\] Failure of \((E)\) is outer when \(X\subsetneq Y\) and inner when \(Y\subsetneq X\); failure of \((C)\) is the projection-closure boundary \(\operatorname{cl}Y\setminus Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift has three distinct boundaries. Representation exactness asks whether its projection equals the target. Projection closedness asks whether the projected set contains all its limits. For epigraph lifts created by partial minimization, boundary attainment asks whether every finite marginal value has an auxiliary minimizer. Exactness can fail by adding points or losing points, while closedness fails through missing limiting points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(E):\pi_x(Q)=X,\qquad(C):\pi_x(Q)=\operatorname{cl}\pi_x(Q),\qquad(A):\operatorname{argmin}_uF(x,u)\neq\varnothing\ \forall x\in\operatorname{dom}f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a partial-minimization lift, \((A)\) is equivalent to \(P(\operatorname{epi}F)=\operatorname{epi}f\).
Projection closedness fails exactly when \(\operatorname{cl}Y\setminus Y\neq\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: An exact lift may have a nonclosed projection when the intended target itself is nonclosed.
A closed projected relaxation may fail exactness by strictly containing \(X\).
Under the compact auxiliary-level-set criterion for closed proper convex \(F\), both closedness and attainment hold for the marginal epigraph.
immediate_consequences_latex: Equality of optimal infima does not imply representation exactness.
Closedness of the lifted set is distinct from closedness of its projection.
Attainment identifies whether lower epigraph boundary points possess auxiliary witnesses.
boundary_notes: Property \((A)\) is defined only for lifts equipped with a partial-minimization function.
The taxonomy does not grade approximation quality when neither set contains the other.
The labels are local organizational notation; the cited source supplies the underlying distinctions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a target set and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be a lifted feasible set. Write \(Y=\pi_x(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This entry defines exactness and outer relaxation purely by projected-set relations. Approximation metrics and hierarchy convergence are not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lift \(Q\) is in the exact representability regime for \(X\) when \[X=Y=\{x:\exists u\ (x,u)\in Q\}.\] It is in the outer-relaxed representability regime when \[X\subseteq Y,\] and it is strictly relaxed when \(X\subsetneq Y\). For minimization of an objective \(c:X\to\mathbb R\) extended to \(Y\), the associated exact and relaxed values are \[v_X=\inf_{x\in X}c(x),\qquad v_Q=\inf_{(x,u)\in Q}c(x)=\inf_{x\in Y}c(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation is exact when projecting its feasible set gives precisely the target. It is an outer relaxation when every target point remains representable but additional projected points may appear. The relaxation is strict when at least one spurious projected point exists. For minimization, the lifted value is the infimum over the projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q\text{ exact}\iff\pi_x(Q)=X,\qquad Q\text{ outer-relaxed}\iff X\subseteq\pi_x(Q),\qquad Q\text{ strict}\iff X\subsetneq\pi_x(Q).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exactness is \(x\in X\iff\exists u\ (x,u)\in Q\).
Outer relaxation is \(x\in X\Rightarrow\exists u\ (x,u)\in Q\), without the reverse implication.
special_cases_latex: When \(Q=X\times\{0\}\), the lift is exact and trivial.
If \(X\subsetneq Y\) but every added point has objective value no smaller than \(v_X\), the relaxation can have the correct value without being exact.
immediate_consequences_latex: For minimization, \(X\subseteq Y\) implies \(v_Q\leq v_X\).
Equality \(v_Q=v_X\) for one objective does not imply \(X=Y\).
Exactness preserves feasibility after projection, independently of uniqueness of auxiliary witnesses.
boundary_notes: An inner approximation \(Y\subsetneq X\) is not an outer-relaxed regime.
If neither \(X\subseteq Y\) nor \(Y\subseteq X\), the pair is unclassified by this two-regime definition.
No inspected source supplied this exact named regime definition at the requested scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact and Outer-Relaxed Lift Regimes
Exact Representability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift represents a target set exactly when its projection contains every target point and no point outside the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The target set \(S\) is exactly representable by the lifted feasible set \(Q\) when \[S=\pi_X(Q)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}.\] Equivalently, every point of \(S\) has a feasible lift and no point outside \(S\) has one. Exact representability is always relative to the permitted structural class for \(Q\), such as polyhedral, conic, or closed convex lifts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(S\subseteq X\), and \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\) belongs to the permitted class of lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) represents \(S\) exactly if and only if \(S=\pi_X(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set representability relative to a specified admissible class of lifts.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Dualization of Linear Programs p. 165

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Representability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed lift projects to an outer approximation of the target; projected points outside the target constitute the relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lift \(Q\) is an outer relaxed representation of \(S\) if its projection \[R=\pi_X(Q)\] satisfies \[S\subseteq R.\] Points in \(R\setminus S\) are relaxation-feasible but not target-feasible. The representation is exact precisely when \(R\setminus S=\varnothing\). For minimization of any objective over these sets, enlarging \(S\) to \(R\) can only decrease the optimal value, under the usual extended-real convention.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(Q\subseteq X\times Y\) is an admissible lifted feasible set, and \(R=\pi_X(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is an outer relaxed representation when \(S\subseteq R\), with exactness precisely when \(S=R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer set relaxation induced by an admissible lift.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Dualization of Linear Programs p. 165

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate that an outer relaxation solves the original minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq R\) and let \(f:R\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). If \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)\) and \(\bar x\in S\), then \[\inf_{x\in R}f(x)=f(\bar x)=\inf_{x\in S}f(x),\] and \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x)\). Thus target feasibility of a relaxed optimizer certifies zero objective relaxation gap even when \(R\neq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed minimizer that is feasible for the target set is also target-optimal and certifies equality of the two optimal values.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) attains the minimum of \(f\) over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x)\quad\text{and}\quad\inf_R f=\inf_S f=f(\bar x).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Optimizer Exactness Certificate
Relaxation Gap Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact convex outer relaxations, directional support-function differences are nonnegative and their maximum over unit directions equals the Hausdorff gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), define the directional relaxation gap by \[g(u)=\sigma_R(u)-\sigma_S(u)\geq0.\] Because \(S\) and \(R\) are nonempty compact convex sets and \(S\subseteq R\), their Hausdorff distance satisfies \[d_H(S,R)=\sup_{\|u\|_2=1}g(u).\] Thus the support-function gaps record the geometry of the outer relaxation direction by direction, and their largest unit-direction value is its Hausdorff size.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_H(S,R)=\sup_{\|u\|_2=1}\bigl(\sigma_R(u)-\sigma_S(u)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function geometry for compact convex outer relaxations.

notation.meaning: support function of a compact convex set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spatial and Inflation Representations of the Outer Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent metric descriptions of the discrepancy between nested compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets and let \(B_2\) be the closed Euclidean unit ball. Then \[d_H(S,R)=\max_{r\in R}\operatorname{dist}(r,S)=\inf\{\varepsilon\geq0:R\subseteq S+\varepsilon B_2\}.\] Equivalently, \(d_H(S,R)\leq\varepsilon\) exactly when \(R\subseteq S+\varepsilon B_2\), or exactly when \(\sigma_R(u)-\sigma_S(u)\leq\varepsilon\) for every unit vector \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nested compact convex sets, the Hausdorff relaxation gap is the largest distance of a relaxed point from the target and the least Euclidean inflation covering the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
Distance and Hausdorff distance use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_H(S,R)=\max_{r\in R}\operatorname{dist}(r,S)=\inf\{\varepsilon\geq0:R\subseteq S+\varepsilon B_2\}.\)

notation.meaning: distance from a relaxed point to the target

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(Q)\ne S\) iff some target fiber is empty or some outside fiber is nonempty.

notation.meaning: fiber of the lifted feasible set over \(x\)

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex outer lift is inexact exactly when some direction has a strictly larger support value than the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty compact convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\sigma_C(u)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle u,x\rangle\). The lifted outer representation fails to be exact exactly when \[R\setminus S\neq\varnothing.\] Under compact convexity, this is equivalent to the existence of a separating direction: \[R\neq S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists u\in\mathbb R^n\ \text{such that}\ \sigma_R(u)>\sigma_S(u).\] Consequently, exactness holds if and only if \(\sigma_R(u)=\sigma_S(u)\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), and \(Y\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
\(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Y\) is a lifted feasible set, and \(R=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\neq S\iff\exists u\in\mathbb R^n:\sigma_R(u)>\sigma_S(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp support-function test for failure of exact compact convex representation.

notation.meaning: support function of a compact convex set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness obstruction specific to finite polyhedral extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) is a polyhedron, then its coordinate projection \(\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(Q)\) is a polyhedron. Hence a nonpolyhedral target cannot have an exact finite polyhedral lift. In particular, the Euclidean unit ball in dimension \(n\geq2\) has no exact finite polyhedral lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves polyhedrality, so a nonpolyhedral target such as a Euclidean ball cannot have a finite polyhedral exact lift.
assumptions_latex: Exactness is required within the class of finite polyhedral lifts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(Q)\text{ is polyhedral};\quad S\text{ nonpolyhedral}\Longrightarrow S\neq\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(Q).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Lift Obstruction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative impossibility boundary for exact representation by a convex lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be real vector spaces and let \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\) be convex. Then \(\pi_X(Q)\) is convex. Consequently, a nonconvex target \(S\subseteq X\) admits no exact representation \(S=\pi_X(Q)\) by a convex lift. For example, \(S=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\) has no convex exact lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves convexity, so a nonconvex target cannot be represented exactly by a convex lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(Q)\text{ is convex};\quad S\text{ nonconvex}\Longrightarrow S\neq\pi_X(Q).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Lift Obstruction

\(S\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
\(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Y\) is a lifted feasible set, and \(R=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(Q)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Defect of a Projected Lift
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) be a nonempty set and let \(P:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear, typically a coordinate projection. Set \(Y=P(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is finite-dimensional. Its principal convex-analytic use is when \(Q\) is closed and convex but unbounded, because such a set can have a nonclosed linear image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The projection-closedness failure boundary of \((Q,P)\) is \[\partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P):=\operatorname{cl}(P(Q))\setminus P(Q).\] Projection closedness holds exactly when this set is empty. A point \(y\) lies in \(\partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P)\) exactly when there is a sequence \(q_k\in Q\) with \(Pq_k\to y\), but no \(q\in Q\) satisfies \(Pq=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection-closedness failure boundary is the set of limit points of the projected lift that are absent from the projection itself. It is empty precisely when the projection is closed. Equivalently, each failure point can be approached by projections of feasible lifted points but has no feasible lifted preimage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P)=\operatorname{cl}(P(Q))\setminus P(Q),\qquad \partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P)=\varnothing\iff P(Q)\text{ is closed}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in\partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P)\) iff \(y\notin P(Q)\) and \(\inf_{q\in Q}\|Pq-y\|=0\).
For an epigraph projection, failure points are limiting epigraph points lacking an auxiliary witness.
special_cases_latex: If \(Q\) is compact, then \(P(Q)\) is compact and the failure boundary is empty.
A closed convex unbounded \(Q\) can have a nonempty failure boundary.
For partial minimization, missing points \((x,f(x))\) arise when the auxiliary infimum is not attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: Closing the projection adds exactly \(\partial_{\mathrm{pc}}(Q,P)\).
Closedness of \(Q\) alone does not imply an empty failure boundary.
Nonempty failure boundary can obstruct attainment in projected epigraph formulations.
boundary_notes: This is not the ordinary topological boundary \(\operatorname{bd}P(Q)\); points already in \(P(Q)\) are excluded.
The definition does not assert that every failure point corresponds to a finite optimizer.
In infinite-dimensional spaces, closure depends on the chosen topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Projected Limits Force Auxiliary Escape
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed finite-dimensional lifted set, a missing limit of its projection can occur only when every associated sequence of auxiliary witnesses escapes to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be closed and let \(x_k\to\bar x\) with \((x_k,y_k)\in C\). If \((y_k)\) has a bounded subsequence, then \(\bar x\in\pi_x(C)\). Hence, if \(\bar x\in\overline{\pi_x(C)}\setminus\pi_x(C)\), then for every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) and every choice of lifts \(y_k\) satisfying \((x_k,y_k)\in C\), one has \(\|y_k\|\to+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: The retained and auxiliary spaces are finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\bar x\in\overline{\pi_x(C)}\setminus\pi_x(C)\), then every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) with lifts \((x_k,y_k)\in C\) satisfies \(\|y_k\|\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization of how closed-set projections lose closedness in finite dimensions.

notation.meaning: coordinate projection onto the retained variable

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Failures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex reciprocal epigraph projects to the open positive half-line because auxiliary variables diverge as projected points approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\geq1/x\}\] is a closed convex subset of \(\mathbb R^2\). Its coordinate projection is \[\pi_x(C)=(0,\infty).\] Therefore a finite-dimensional coordinate projection preserves convexity but need not preserve closedness. The missing point \(0\) is approached by projected feasible points whose corresponding auxiliary coordinates diverge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex whereas \(\pi_x(C)=(0,\infty)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a closed convex set need not be closed.

notation.meaning: coordinate projection onto the original variable

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-Escape Characterization of Missing Projected Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization of coordinate-projection failure for closed sets in finite-dimensional product spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\times Y\) be closed, where \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional, and let \(\bar x\in\overline{\pi_X(C)}\). Then \[\bar x\in\pi_X(C)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there exists }(x_k,y_k)\in C\text{ with }x_k\to\bar x\text{ and }(y_k)\text{ bounded}.\] Consequently, if \(\bar x\in\overline{\pi_X(C)}\setminus\pi_X(C)\), every feasible sequence with visible coordinates converging to \(\bar x\) has unbounded auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional closed lifted set, a limit point is missing from its projection exactly when all feasible approaches to it escape to infinity in the auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\pi_X(C)\iff\exists (x_k,y_k)\in C:\ x_k\to\bar x\text{ and }(y_k)\text{ is bounded}.\)

notation.meaning: Coordinate projection onto the visible space X.
Auxiliary coordinates of a feasible approximating sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Escape Characterization of Missing Projected Points
Closedness Failures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization of a closed convex indicator can produce a nonclosed convex indicator when minimizing auxiliary variables escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\delta_C\), where \[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\geq1/x\}.\] Then \(F\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function. Eliminating \(y\) yields \[f(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}F(x,y)=\delta_{(0,\infty)}(x).\] Hence \(f\) is convex but not lower semicontinuous at \(0\). This shows that partial minimization need not preserve closedness when auxiliary sublevel sets can escape to infinity; an appropriate level-boundedness or compactness hypothesis can exclude this behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\delta_C\), where \(\delta_C\) is the extended-real indicator of \(C\), and \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}F(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex, but \(f=\delta_{(0,\infty)}\) is convex and not lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-semicontinuity failure under partial minimization.

notation.meaning: extended-real indicator function of a set
marginal function obtained by eliminating the second variable

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificates Detect Only the Closure of a Cone Image
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual cone inequalities characterize the closure of a linear cone image, so a missing boundary point of a nonclosed image cannot be strictly separated from the image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone and \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. Then \[\overline{A(K)}=\bigl\{y\in\mathbb R^m:\langle z,y\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }z\in\mathbb R^m\text{ such that }A^*z\in K^*\bigr\}.\] Consequently, \(y\notin\overline{A(K)}\) has a strict certificate \(z\) satisfying \(A^*z\in K^*\) and \(\langle z,y\rangle<0\). If \(y\in\overline{A(K)}\setminus A(K)\), all such dual inequalities hold even though \(Ax=y\), \(x\in K\), is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{A(K)}=\{y:\langle z,y\rangle\geq0\ \forall z\text{ with }A^*z\in K^*\}\); strict dual separation detects exclusion from the closure, not exclusion from \(A(K)\) itself.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual characterization of the closure gap responsible for a nonclosed linear cone image.

notation.meaning: dual cone of K under the nonnegative-pairing convention
adjoint of the linear map A

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Linear Images
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous linear coordinate map sends the closed two-by-two positive-semidefinite cone to a convex set that is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linear map \[A\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}\right)=(a,b).\] For the closed convex cone \(\mathbb S_+^2\), its image is \[A(\mathbb S_+^2)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},\] which is convex but not closed.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^2\) is the cone of positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices of order two.
\(A:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) is the linear map defined by \(A\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}\right)=(a,b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(\mathbb S_+^2)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\), which is not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit nonclosed linear image of a closed convex cone.

notation.meaning: linear coordinate map retaining the first diagonal and off-diagonal entries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Description Recovers the Closure of a Cone Image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual characterization explaining why homogeneous separation detects the closure rather than missing boundary points of a nonclosed cone image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone and \(A:E\to F\) linear, where the spaces are finite-dimensional and \(K^*=\{u:\langle u,x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in K\}\). Then \[(AK)^*=\{y\in F:A^*y\in K^*\},\qquad \overline{AK}=(AK)^{**}=\{z\in F:\langle y,z\rangle\ge0\ \forall y\text{ with }A^*y\in K^*\}.\] Thus every point of \(\overline{AK}\setminus AK\) satisfies all homogeneous dual inequalities valid for \(AK\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint dual inequalities characterize the closure of a cone image, so missing boundary points of a nonclosed image pass every such inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Description Recovers the Closure of a Cone Image
Recession-Kernel Closed-Image Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set has a closed linear image when it has no nonzero recession direction annihilated by the image map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear. If \[\operatorname{rec}C\cap\ker A=\{0\},\] then \(A(C)\) is closed. The condition rules out a nonzero recession direction that is invisible to the image map.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(C)\text{ is closed}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficient condition preventing unbounded hidden motion along fibers of a linear image.

notation.meaning: directions annihilated by the linear image map

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Projection Closedness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear images of convex polyhedra are closed polyhedra, so polyhedral lifts avoid the nonclosed-projection pathology of general closed convex lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex polyhedron and let \(A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear. Then \(A(P)\) is a convex polyhedron and hence is closed. In particular, every coordinate projection of a polyhedral lifted feasible set is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(P)\text{ is a closed convex polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral regime restoring closedness of projected lifted representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Restoration Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform local level-boundedness prevents auxiliary minimizers from escaping, restoring attainment, epigraph projection equality, and lower semicontinuity of the marginal function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and is locally level-bounded in \(y\) uniformly over \(x\): for every compact \(K\subseteq X\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \[\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:x\in K,\ F(x,y)\leq\alpha\}\] is compact. If \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) is proper, then \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and convex, every finite infimum is attained, and \[\operatorname{epi}f=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
For every compact \(K\subseteq X\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the set \(\{(x,y):x\in K,\ F(x,y)\leq\alpha\}\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex, its finite infima are attained, and \(\operatorname{epi}f=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local level-boundedness regime for closed marginalization.

notation.meaning: epigraph projection retaining the original variable and height

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex, fix a norm with closed unit ball \(B\), and fix a class \(\mathcal L\) of admissible lifts equipped with an integer size map \(s:\mathcal L\to\mathbb N\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is an abstract size-versus-outer-accuracy profile. A concrete theory must specify the lift class and size measure, such as cone dimension, number of inequalities, or matrix order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the lift-size complexity profile of \(X\) relative to \((\mathcal L,s)\) is \[\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;\varepsilon):=\inf\{s(Q):Q\in\mathcal L,\ X\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\subseteq X+\varepsilon B\}.\] The exact lift size is \(\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;0)\). The lift-size complexity tradeoff is the nonincreasing relation \(\varepsilon\mapsto\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;\varepsilon)\) between permitted outer error and the least admissible representation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix a class of allowed lifted formulations and a numerical notion of their size. For each nonnegative tolerance, consider lifts whose projections contain the target but remain within the target enlarged by that tolerance. The lift-size profile is the smallest size among such lifts. At zero tolerance it is the exact lift size; as the allowed error increases, the minimum required size cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;\varepsilon)=\inf\{s(Q):X\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\subseteq X+\varepsilon B\},\qquad \varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2\Rightarrow\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;\varepsilon_2)\leq\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;\varepsilon_1).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accuracy constraint is the one-sided Hausdorff condition \(\sup_{y\in\pi_x(Q)}\operatorname{dist}(y,X)\leq\varepsilon\) together with \(X\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\).
Exact representability by a finite lift in \(\mathcal L\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{ls}_{\mathcal L}(X;0)<+\infty\).
special_cases_latex: For polyhedral lifts, size may count inequalities or facets of the extension.
For semidefinite lifts, size may be the matrix order, number of blocks, or a declared aggregate measure; these choices produce different profiles.
immediate_consequences_latex: The profile is nonincreasing in \(\varepsilon\).
Changing the norm changes the approximation scale but not the exact value at \(\varepsilon=0\).
boundary_notes: The size map must be fixed before profiles can be compared.
The definition does not itself provide upper or lower complexity bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Lift-Size Profile
Language-Relative Lift Size
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift size is a declared, representation-language-specific measure; inequality count, matrix order, cone data, auxiliary dimension, and encoding length are distinct conventions unless an aggregation rule is explicitly fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lift-size measure is part of the specification of a representation language \(\mathfrak R\): it is a declared map \[s:\mathfrak R\to[0,+\infty].\] Its definition must state which description features it counts and which presentations are identified. Typical language-specific choices include the number of inequalities in a polyhedral extension, the matrix order or block data in a semidefinite lift, and cone-order, auxiliary-dimension, or encoding-length measures in other conic languages. Distinct choices need not induce the same ordering of lifts and therefore must not be combined by an unstated componentwise or scalar aggregation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak R\) is a fixed language of lifted representations.
The counted description features and equivalence conventions are explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s:\mathfrak R\to[0,+\infty]\text{ is the size map used for comparisons within }\mathfrak R.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines lift size without imposing a noncanonical aggregation of inequivalent structural parameters.

notation.meaning: declared scalar size of representation R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scalar size measure for exact polyhedral extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its polyhedral extension complexity is \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\left\{m:\ P=\{x:\exists y,\ Ax+By\leq b\}\text{ for a system with }m\text{ scalar inequalities}\right\}.\] Affine equations may be included without being counted, or eliminated, under this convention. Auxiliary-variable dimension is not the measured quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral extension complexity is the minimum number of scalar inequalities in an exact polyhedral lift, with equations not counted.
assumptions_latex: Size counts scalar inequalities in an exact polyhedral extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{m:P\text{ has an exact polyhedral extension with }m\text{ inequalities}\}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Extension Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical matrix-order size measure for exact single-cone semidefinite lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its semidefinite extension complexity under the single-cone matrix-order convention is \[\operatorname{sxc}(C)=\min\left\{r:C=\pi\bigl(\mathbb S_+^r\cap L\bigr)\text{ for an affine subspace }L\subseteq\mathbb S^r\text{ and a linear map }\pi\right\}.\] The value is \(+\infty\) if no such lift exists. The measured size is the matrix order \(r\), not the ambient scalar dimension \(r(r+1)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semidefinite extension complexity is the smallest matrix order of a positive-semidefinite cone whose affine slice projects exactly to the target.
assumptions_latex: Size is measured by the order of one positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sxc}(C)=\min\{r:C=\pi(\mathbb S_+^r\cap L)\},\) with value \(+\infty\) when the admissible set is empty.

notation.meaning: cone of real positive-semidefinite matrices of order r
affine slice in the lifted matrix space
semidefinite extension complexity under the stated convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural behavior shared by inequality-count and cone-order lift-size measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For either polyhedral extension complexity or single-cone semidefinite extension complexity, taking an affine image cannot increase lift size: if \(D=T(C)\) for an affine map \(T\), then \[\operatorname{xc}(D)\leq\operatorname{xc}(C)\quad\text{or}\quad\operatorname{sxc}(D)\leq\operatorname{sxc}(C),\] respectively. Consequently these measures are invariant under affine isomorphism. Passing to a nonempty exposed face also does not increase the corresponding size when affine equations are free under the adopted convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact LP and SDP lift sizes do not increase under affine images or exposed faces and are invariant under affine isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: The same lift language and size convention are used on both sides.
Affine equations are not charged to the size measure.
The face under consideration is nonempty and exposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=T(C)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{size}(D)\leq\operatorname{size}(C),\qquad C\cong D\Longrightarrow\operatorname{size}(C)=\operatorname{size}(D).\)

notation.meaning: affine map applied after the lifted projection
either xc or sxc under its stated convention
