If \(C=\{x:Ax=b\}\), the dual feasibility condition can be represented through the adjoint map.

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Sublevel Intersection Formulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge minimization finds the infimal positive scale at which the scaled gauge unit set meets the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_\kappa=\{x:\kappa(x)\le1\}\). For every \(t>0\), positive homogeneity gives \(\{x:\kappa(x)\le t\}=tB_\kappa\). Hence
\[
p^*=\inf_{x\in C}\kappa(x)=\inf\{t>0:C\cap tB_\kappa\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
This remains valid when \(p^*=0\), with the right side understood as an infimum over positive scales; it does not assert intersection or attainment at scale zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) is a gauge on a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\inf\{t>0:C\cap tB_\kappa\ne\varnothing\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear-residual gauge primal problem is \[({\rm P}_{\rm res})\qquad\min_{x\in X}\ \kappa(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma.\] Its represented gauge dual is \[({\rm D}_{\rm res})\qquad\min_{y\in Y}\ \kappa^\circ(A^*y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1.\] Here \(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\) are the polar gauges. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear-residual pair minimizes a model gauge subject to a gauge-bounded data residual. Its gauge dual minimizes the polar model gauge applied to the adjoint variable, subject to a reverse-separation inequality involving the data and the polar residual gauge. Under surjectivity, this is exactly the abstract antipolar gauge dual.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous-conic embedding of a gauge program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(A:X\to Y\) linear, \(b\in Y\), \(\sigma\geq0\), and let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) and \(\rho:Y\to[0,+\infty]\) be closed gauges. Write \(K_\kappa=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\subset X\times\mathbb R\) and \(K_\rho=\operatorname{epi}\rho\subset Y\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-gauge formulation. The embedding concerns the primal residual-constrained gauge problem and its homogeneous epigraph-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous-conic gauge embedding of \(\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}\) is the conic program \[\inf_{x,t}\{t:(x,t)\in K_\kappa,\ (b-Ax,\sigma)\in K_\rho\}.\] The correspondence preserves feasible points and objective values: \(x\) is gauge-feasible exactly when some \(t\) makes \((x,t)\) conically feasible, and the least such \(t\) is \(\kappa(x)\). Both epigraphs are convex cones because their defining gauges are convex and positively homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite-dimensional spaces and closed gauges κ and ρ, the residual-constrained problem minimizing κ(x) subject to ρ(b−Ax)≤σ is embedded by introducing a scalar t and imposing membership of (x,t) in the epigraph cone of κ and membership of (b−Ax,σ) in the epigraph cone of ρ. Feasibility is preserved, and minimizing t recovers κ(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\kappa,\ (b-Ax,\sigma)\in\operatorname{epi}\rho\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using slack \(r=b-Ax\), the same embedding is \[\inf_{x,r,t}\{t:Ax+r=b,\ (x,t)\in K_\kappa,\ (r,\sigma)\in K_\rho\}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are norms, \(K_\kappa\) and \(K_\rho\) are norm epigraph cones.
If \(\rho=\delta_{\{0\}}\) and \(\sigma=0\), the residual condition reduces to \(Ax=b\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Gauge feasibility and conic feasibility have the same projection onto the \(x\)-space.
Any conic optimal pair \((x,t)\) satisfies \(t=\kappa(x)\) whenever the optimal value is finite.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert conic strong duality, closedness of linear images, or attainment.
Nonclosed gauges require an explicit closure convention and are excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-conic embedding of a gauge program
Polar of the Gauge Epigraph Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the negative-polar convention, polarizing a gauge epigraph cone produces the reflected epigraph of the polar gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_\kappa=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\) and use the negative-polar convention
\[
K_\kappa^-=\{(y,s):\langle y,x\rangle+st\le0\ \text{for all }(x,t)\in K_\kappa\}.
\]
Then
\[
K_\kappa^-=\{(y,-\alpha):\alpha\ge\kappa^\circ(y)\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\kappa^\circ(y)=\inf\{\alpha\ge0:(y,-\alpha)\in K_\kappa^-\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_\kappa^-=\{(y,-\alpha):\alpha\ge\kappa^\circ(y)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-polar representation of the polar gauge induced by the homogeneous epigraph embedding.

notation.meaning: Negative polar cone of the gauge epigraph.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Gauge Embeddings
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed gauge is represented exactly by its closed convex epigraph cone and recovered by minimizing the cone’s scalar coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
K_\kappa=\operatorname{epi}\kappa=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge\kappa(x)\}.
\]
Positive homogeneity and convexity of \(\kappa\) make \(K_\kappa\) a convex cone, and closedness of \(\kappa\) makes it closed. Conversely, the gauge is recovered from its homogeneous embedding by
\[
\kappa(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:(x,t)\in K_\kappa\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa\) is a closed convex cone and \(\kappa(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\kappa\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph-cone representation of a closed gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Gauge Embeddings
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing an epigraph coordinate represents gauge minimization as a conic program with the same infimal value; whenever an optimizer exists, its original variable solves the gauge problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_\kappa=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:\kappa(x)\le t\}\). Then gauge minimization has the conic epigraph representation
\[
\inf_{x\in F}\kappa(x)=\inf_{x,t}\{t:(x,t)\in K_\kappa,\ x\in F\}.
\]
Because \(K_\kappa\) is a closed convex cone and \(F\) has an affine conic representation, the problem on the right is a conic program. Whenever a minimizing pair \((x^*,t^*)\) exists, it satisfies \(t^*=\kappa(x^*)\), and \(x^*\) minimizes \(\kappa\) over \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(F\subseteq X\) is nonempty and is representable by affine constraints over closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F}\kappa(x)=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in K_\kappa,\ x\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic epigraph formulation of gauge minimization without an unsupported attainment assumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenization–Conic Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set is exactly the unit-height slice of its closed homogenization cone, while the zero-height slice records its recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq X\), define
\[
H_C=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})}.
\]
Its unit-height slice recovers the set exactly:
\[
H_C\cap(X\times\{1\})=C\times\{1\}.
\]
Its zero-height slice records the recession directions:
\[
H_C\cap(X\times\{0\})=\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_C\cap(X\times\{1\})=C\times\{1\}\), where \(H_C=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-height and zero-height slices of the closed homogenization cone.

notation.meaning: Closed homogenization cone of the convex set.
Recession cone of the closed convex set.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Cone with a Nonclosed Epigraph Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rotated-second-order-cone lift projects to a nonclosed epigraph-like set whose closure preserves value zero but introduces unattained boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the closed convex cone
\[
L=\{(u,t,z)\in\mathbb R^3:t\ge0,\ z\ge0,\ tz\ge u^2\}.
\]
Its projection onto \((u,t)\) is
\[
E=\{(u,t):t>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},
\]
which is not closed, while
\[
\overline E=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+=\operatorname{epi}0.
\]
For every \(u\ne0\), minimizing \(t\) subject to \((u,t)\in E\) has infimum zero but no minimizer, even though \((u,0)\) belongs to the closed projected epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\ne\overline E,\quad \inf\{t:(u,t)\in E\}=0\ \text{is unattained for every }u\ne0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete lifted-cone example showing loss of boundary witnesses and attainment after projection.

notation.meaning: Its projection onto the proposed epigraph variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Projection Boundary for Lifted Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a nonclosed conic projection can preserve an infimum while creating boundary epigraph points that have no lifted witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\times Z\) be a closed convex conic lift and set
\[
E=\{(x,t):\exists z\in Z,\ (x,t,z)\in L\}.
\]
A linear projection of a closed convex cone need not be closed. If \(E\) is nonclosed, an identity \(\overline E=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\) is only closure-exact: points in \(\overline E\setminus E\) have no lifted witnesses. Infimal values can therefore agree after closure while boundary feasibility, attainment, and recovery of lifted optimizers fail. Exact lifted representation requires \(E=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\) before closure.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(L\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\times Z\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline E=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\ \text{does not imply}\ E=\operatorname{epi}\kappa\ \text{or attainment of lifted boundary points}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for conic lifts whose projected epigraph is not closed.

notation.meaning: Projection of the conic lift onto the epigraph variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw homogenization when the gauge unit set is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=(-1,1)\subset\mathbb{R}\). Its gauge is \(\gamma_C(x)=|x|\), because the defining value is an infimum, but the raw homogenization is
\[
H=\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})=\{(x,t):t>0,\ |x|<t\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.
\]
Hence \(\gamma_C(1)\leq1\) holds while \((1,1)\notin H\). Therefore raw conic membership is not an exact representation at unattained boundary scales. Closure is essential: \(\operatorname{cl}H=\operatorname{epi}|\cdot|\). More generally, replacing a gauge epigraph by an unclosed homogenization can preserve infimal values while losing feasible boundary points and attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without closure, homogenization may omit boundary points: the open interval gauge equals absolute value, yet its raw cone excludes points where equality holds.
assumptions_latex: The gauge uses an infimum over positive dilations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1,1)\notin\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})\) although \(\gamma_C(1)=1\), while \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})=\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y,A,b,\sigma,\kappa,\rho\) be as in the residual-constrained gauge model. Let \(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\) be the polar gauges. Define \[v_P=\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}\] and \[v_D=\inf\{\kappa^\circ(A^*y):\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex gauges, using the minimization-form gauge dual. Values are extended nonnegative reals unless a stated regime restricts them to \((0,+\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gauge duality theorem family is the collection of logically distinct assertions attached to \((v_P,v_D)\): weak duality requires \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1\) for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\); value reciprocity is \(v_Pv_D=1\) when both values are finite and positive; strong gauge duality adds equality without a multiplicative gap under an explicit regularity condition; and primal or dual attainment requires membership of the corresponding argmin set. Each assertion is defined separately because reciprocity does not itself imply attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the residual-constrained gauge primal and its minimization-form gauge dual, the duality family consists of weak multiplicative comparison, reciprocal optimal values, regularity-based strong duality, and separate primal and dual attainment statements. Reciprocity is interpreted only for finite positive values and does not automatically include existence of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal D(\kappa,\rho,A,b,\sigma)=\{\text{weak comparison},\ v_Pv_D=1,\ \operatorname{Argmin}P\neq\varnothing,\ \operatorname{Argmin}D\neq\varnothing\},\] with each member asserted only under its own stated hypotheses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(0<v_P,v_D<+\infty\), reciprocity is equivalently \(v_D=1/v_P\) or \(v_P=1/v_D\).
special_cases_latex: When \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are norms, polar gauges are the corresponding dual norms.
For exact equations, the term \(\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\) vanishes when \(\sigma=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The family separates value equality from solution existence.
Weak duality gives \(v_Pv_D\geq1\) whenever both feasible sets are nonempty.
boundary_notes: Products involving \(0\) and \(+\infty\) are not assigned a reciprocity meaning.
This definition does not select a particular constraint qualification.

children.title: Weak Gauge Duality
children.top_down_role: Universal comparison for gauge primal–dual feasible pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Real Boundary for the Value-Product Form
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise weak gauge duality is unconditional for finite feasible objectives, but the product-of-values form requires positive finite values or an explicitly declared convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible points with finite objectives, \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(y)\ge 1\). Consequently, when \(0<p^*,d^*<+\infty\), one has \(p^*d^*\ge1\). If one infimal value is zero, feasible points with arbitrarily small finite objective force every feasible point on the opposite side to have infinite objective. The resulting formal expression \(0\cdot(+\infty)\) is undefined in ordinary extended-real arithmetic and is not an unconditional value-product statement.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(y)\ge1\) for every feasible pair with finite objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<p^*,d^*<+\infty\implies p^*d^*\ge1; no ordinary extended-real product assertion is made for a \(0\)-and-\(+\infty\) value pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes unconditional feasible-pair weak duality from multiplication of extended-real infimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Gauge Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative weak duality for the residual-constrained gauge primal and its gauge dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) be closed gauges, and define
\[
(P)\quad \min_x\{\kappa(x):\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\},
\qquad
(D)\quad \min_y\{\kappa^\circ(A^*y):\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}.
\]
For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\), polar-gauge inequalities give
\[
1\leq\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)
\leq\langle Ax,y\rangle
\leq\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y).
\]
Consequently, whenever both optimal values are defined in \((0,+\infty]\), they satisfy \(p^*d^*\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible primal–dual pair has objective product at least one; therefore the optimal primal and gauge-dual values obey the same multiplicative lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed gauges on finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1\) for feasible \(x,y\), hence \(p^*d^*\geq1\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) be closed gauges on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, and define primal and dual feasible sets \[F_P=\{x:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\},\qquad F_D=\{y:\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal feasible-pair comparison for the minimization-form residual gauge primal-dual pair. No constraint qualification or attainment is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak gauge duality is the property \[\forall x\in F_P\ \forall y\in F_D:\quad \kappa(x)\,\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1.\] Consequently, whenever both feasible sets are nonempty, their extended optimal values satisfy \(v_Pv_D\geq1\) whenever the product is well-defined. The pointwise statement is primary; the value statement alone is weaker when either infimum is unattained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak gauge duality means that every primal-feasible point x and every gauge-dual-feasible vector y have objective product at least one. It is a pointwise, qualification-free comparison. When both optimal values are meaningful, it implies that the product of the primal and dual infima is at least one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in F_P,\ y\in F_D\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any feasible \(y\) with \(0<\kappa^\circ(A^*y)<+\infty\), weak duality is \(\kappa(x)\geq1/\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\) for all \(x\in F_P\).
special_cases_latex: For norm gauges, the comparison becomes \(\|x\|\,\|A^*y\|_*\geq1\).
If \(\sigma=0\), dual feasibility reduces to \(\langle b,y\rangle\geq1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every dual-feasible vector supplies a positive lower bound on the primal objective when its dual objective is finite.
A feasible pair with product one is simultaneously value-tight if both members attain their respective infima.
boundary_notes: Weak duality alone asserts neither reciprocal values nor attainment.
If either feasible set is empty, the universal pointwise statement is vacuous and must not be read as a finite-value result.

children.title: Primal–Dual Value Reciprocity
children.top_down_role: The characteristic multiplicative value relationship of gauge duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Value Reciprocity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong gauge duality, the positive primal and dual values are reciprocals, and attained optimal objective values multiply to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Strong gauge duality replaces the weak inequality by the reciprocal identity
\[
p^*d^*=1.
\]
Equivalently, \(d^*=1/p^*\) and \(p^*=1/d^*\). If optimal solutions \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) exist, they therefore satisfy
\[
\kappa(x^*)\kappa^\circ(y^*)=1.
\]
This multiplicative reciprocity is the gauge-duality analogue of equality of primal and dual values in additive Lagrange duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*d^*=1\), equivalently \(d^*=1/p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive-value reciprocity under strong gauge duality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:defining value relation of strong gauge duality

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The reciprocity statement matches the leaf, and the positivity, finiteness, and strong-duality assumptions make the formulas coherent. It still requires an inspectable gauge-duality source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the residual gauge primal-dual pair, let \(v_P\) and \(v_D\) denote the two infimal objective values. Assume in this definition that \(0<v_P<+\infty\) and \(0<v_D<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive-value regime. The definition concerns equality of optimal values and is independent of whether either infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal-dual value reciprocity holds when \[v_Pv_D=1.\] Equivalently, the dual value is the multiplicative inverse of the primal value. The associated multiplicative duality gap is \(G_\times=v_Pv_D-1\); reciprocity is exactly \(G_\times=0\). This differs from additive Fenchel or Lagrangian equality, where primal and dual values are ordinarily compared by subtraction rather than multiplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal and gauge-dual values are finite and strictly positive, value reciprocity means that their product equals one. Equivalently, either value is the reciprocal of the other. The multiplicative gap is the product minus one, so reciprocity is zero multiplicative gap and does not require minimizers to exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v_Pv_D=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v_D=v_P^{-1}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v_P=v_D^{-1}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With logarithmic values, reciprocity is \(\log v_P+\log v_D=0\).
Under weak gauge duality, reciprocity is equivalent to the sharpness of the lower bound \(v_Pv_D\geq1\).
special_cases_latex: If \(v_P=1\), reciprocity requires \(v_D=1\).
For positively rescaled primal objectives, the reciprocal dual normalization must be rescaled inversely.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reciprocity determines either finite positive value from the other.
If both optima are attained, their optimal objective product equals one.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes zero, infinite, and indeterminate extended-real products.
Reciprocity is a value relation, not an attainment or uniqueness statement.
review_flags: No inspected source states this exact value-reciprocity definition for the specified gauge-dual normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Gauge Duality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior qualification, closedness, and a finite positive primal value yield dual attainment and reciprocal primal-dual values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated closedness, positivity, and relative-interior qualification, the antipolar gauge dual
\[
d^*=\inf_{y\in C'}\kappa^\circ(y)
\]
has an optimal solution \(y^*\), and its value is reciprocal to the primal value:
\[
p^*d^*=1.
\]
Thus weak gauge duality is exact and \(d^*=1/p^*\). This record states the finite-dimensional relative-interior version; alternative closure qualifications require separate formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) is a closed gauge and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, with \(0\notin C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gauge dual is attained and \(p^*d^*=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional relative-interior strong-duality regime.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is appropriately placed, but the precise relative-interior qualification and the asserted dual attainment are source-sensitive. No citation is supplied to establish that these hypotheses are sufficient for both reciprocity and attainment.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(v_P\) and \(v_D\) be the values of the residual-constrained gauge primal and its minimization-form gauge dual. Let \(F_P\) and \(F_D\) be their feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex setting. Strong gauge duality is defined as a no-gap value property; attainment is recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A data instance \((\kappa,\rho,A,b,\sigma)\) is in a strong gauge-duality regime when \(F_P\neq\varnothing\), \(F_D\neq\varnothing\), \(0<v_P,v_D<+\infty\), and \[v_Pv_D=1.\] A regularity-qualified strong-duality statement additionally specifies a sufficient condition, typically formulated through relative-interior feasibility or closedness of the relevant perturbation epigraph or linear image. Primal attainment, dual attainment, and simultaneous attainment are not incorporated into the term unless stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong gauge duality is the finite, positive, feasible regime in which the primal and gauge-dual optimal values are exact reciprocals. A theorem asserting this property must state its relative-interior, closure, or perturbation regularity assumption. Existence of primal or dual minimizers remains a separate issue.

After the monotone transformation \(s\mapsto\log s\), it is the additive equality \(\log v_P=-\log v_D\).

Polyhedral gauges often permit closure conditions to be checked through finite-dimensional polyhedral images.

The value of either problem determines the other by inversion.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) and \(D\) denote a gauge primal-dual pair with feasible sets \(F_P,F_D\), objective functions \(p(x)=\kappa(x)\) and \(d(y)=\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\), and values \(v_P,v_D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence classification for finite-dimensional gauge programs. Value finiteness and strong duality are tracked independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Primal attainment means \(S_P:=\{x\in F_P:p(x)=v_P\}
eq\varnothing\), and dual attainment means \(S_D:=\{y\in F_D:d(y)=v_D\}
eq\varnothing\). The four attainment regimes are: simultaneous attainment \((S_P
eq\varnothing,S_D
eq\varnothing)\); primal-only attainment \((S_P
eq\varnothing,S_D=\varnothing)\); dual-only attainment \((S_P=\varnothing,S_D
eq\varnothing)\); and nonattainment \((S_P=S_D=\varnothing)\). These labels presuppose that the corresponding infimal values are defined, but they do not presuppose reciprocal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal attainment means that a feasible primal point achieves the primal infimum, and dual attainment means that a feasible dual vector achieves the dual infimum. Their two truth values produce simultaneous, primal-only, dual-only, and neither-side attainment regimes. This classification is separate from feasibility, finite values, and strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S_P=\operatorname{Argmin}_{x\in F_P}\kappa(x),\qquad S_D=\operatorname{Argmin}_{y\in F_D}\kappa^\circ(A^*y),\] and the attainment regime is determined by the emptiness pattern of \((S_P,S_D)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Primal attainment is equivalent to the existence of \(x^*\in F_P\) satisfying \(\kappa(x^*)=v_P\); analogously for the dual.
special_cases_latex: Compact nonempty feasible level sets with lower-semicontinuous objectives yield the corresponding side's attainment.
Strong duality with only one attained side remains a one-sided attainment regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Simultaneous attainment and value reciprocity produce a feasible pair with objective product one.
Nonempty feasible sets may still belong to a nonattainment regime.
boundary_notes: Attainment does not imply uniqueness.
An infeasible problem is classified as infeasible rather than as merely unattained.
review_flags: General existence sources were inspected, but no single source states this exact gauge-specific four-regime classification.

Exact Primal-Attainment Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal gauge problem is attained exactly when a feasible point realizes its finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P:=\inf_{x\in X_P}\kappa(x)\) have finite value \(v_P\). Primal attainment holds exactly when \[\operatorname{argmin}P:=\{x\in X_P:\kappa(x)=v_P\}\neq\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is attained}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{argmin}P\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued primal gauge minimization; no assertion of dual attainment or strong duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-sublevel sufficient condition for attainment of the gauge primal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}\), where \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed gauges. Suppose \(F_P\neq\varnothing\), the primal value \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F_P}\kappa(x)\) is finite, and for some \(\alpha>p^*\) the set
\[
L_\alpha=F_P\cap\{x:\kappa(x)\leq\alpha\}
\]
is nonempty and compact. Then there exists \(x^*\in F_P\) such that \(\kappa(x^*)=p^*\). In particular, the compactness condition holds when \(F_P\) is closed and \(\kappa\) is level-bounded on \(F_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite gauge-primal infimum is attained whenever one feasible objective sublevel above the optimum is nonempty and compact.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed gauges on finite-dimensional spaces.
\(F_P\cap\{x:\kappa(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is nonempty and compact for some \(\alpha>p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Dual-Attainment Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge dual is attained exactly when a dual-feasible point realizes its finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:=\inf_{y\in Y_D}\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\) have finite value \(v_D\). Dual attainment holds exactly when \[\operatorname{argmin}D:=\{y\in Y_D:\kappa^\circ(A^*y)=v_D\}\neq\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is attained}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{argmin}D\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued gauge-dual minimization; no assertion of primal attainment or strong duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-sublevel sufficient condition for attainment of the gauge dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
F_D=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^m:\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}
\]
and let \(d^*=\inf_{y\in F_D}\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\). Suppose \(F_D\neq\varnothing\), \(d^*<+\infty\), and for some \(\beta>d^*\) the set
\[
M_\beta=F_D\cap\{y:\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\leq\beta\}
\]
is nonempty and compact. Since the polar-gauge objective is lower semicontinuous, there exists \(y^*\in F_D\) such that \(\kappa^\circ(A^*y^*)=d^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite gauge-dual infimum is attained whenever a nonempty feasible objective sublevel above the optimum is compact.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed gauges on finite-dimensional spaces.
\(F_D\cap\{y:\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\leq\beta\}\) is nonempty and compact for some \(\beta>d^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y^*\in F_D\) such that \(\kappa^\circ(A^*y^*)=d^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Joint-Attainment Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint attainment means both finite infima are realized; reciprocal values additionally require strong gauge duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible finite-valued problems \(P\) and \(D\), joint attainment holds exactly when \[\operatorname{argmin}P\neq\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{argmin}D\neq\varnothing.\] Joint attainment alone does not imply \(v_Pv_D=1\).
assumptions_latex: The primal and gauge-dual feasible sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{joint attainment}\Longleftrightarrow(\operatorname{argmin}P\neq\varnothing\land\operatorname{argmin}D\neq\varnothing).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous realization of two finite infima; reciprocal values require an additional strong-duality hypothesis.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous attainment and reciprocal objectives under strong duality and compact sublevels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the finite-dimensional gauge primal–dual pair \((P),(D)\). Assume strong gauge duality gives \(0<p^*,d^*<+\infty\) and \(p^*d^*=1\). If there exist \(\alpha>p^*\) and \(\beta>d^*\) such that
\[
\{x:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma,\ \kappa(x)\leq\alpha\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\{y:\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1,\ \kappa^\circ(A^*y)\leq\beta\}
\]
are nonempty and compact, then both problems attain their infima. Thus there are feasible \(x^*,y^*\) satisfying
\[
\kappa(x^*)\kappa^\circ(A^*y^*)=p^*d^*=1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong reciprocity plus compact primal and dual sublevels yields optimizers on both sides whose objective values multiply to one.
assumptions_latex: A nonempty compact primal sublevel exists above \(p^*\).
A nonempty compact dual sublevel exists above \(d^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^*,y^*\) optimal with \(\kappa(x^*)\kappa^\circ(A^*y^*)=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact One-Sided-Attainment Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided attainment means that exactly one of the two finite infima is attained; zero gap is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible finite-valued problems \(P\) and \(D\), one-sided attainment holds exactly when \[\bigl(\operatorname{argmin}P\neq\varnothing\bigr)\mathbin{\mathsf{xor}}\bigl(\operatorname{argmin}D\neq\varnothing\bigr).\] Equivalently, precisely one of the two infima is realized. This regime is independent of whether \(v_Pv_D=1\); strong gauge duality may be imposed as an additional specialization.
assumptions_latex: The primal and gauge-dual feasible sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{one-sided attainment}\Longleftrightarrow(\operatorname{argmin}P\neq\varnothing)\mathbin{\mathsf{xor}}(\operatorname{argmin}D\neq\varnothing).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly one side of a feasible finite-valued gauge-dual pair has a minimizer; no zero-gap assumption is part of the definition.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-sided attainment for a finite-dimensional primal–gauge-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_P=\{x:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}\), \(F_D=\{y:\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}\), \(p^\star=\inf_{x\in F_P}\kappa(x)\), and \(d^\star=\inf_{y\in F_D}\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\). The pair is in a one-sided attainment regime when \(0<p^\star,d^\star<+\infty\), \(p^\star d^\star=1\), and exactly one of the sets \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F_P}\kappa(x)\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in F_D}\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\) is nonempty. Thus equality of optimal values does not imply attainment on both sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong gauge duality holds, but exactly one of the primal and dual finite optimal values is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional paired spaces, and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed proper gauges, with polar gauges \(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star d^\star=1\) and exactly one primal or dual argmin set is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a gauge primal-dual pair, let \(F_P,F_D\) be feasible sets, \(v_P,v_D\) extended optimal values, and \(S_P,S_D\) solution sets. When both values are finite and positive, let \(G_\times=v_Pv_D-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional classification of failures of feasibility, reciprocal value equality, and attainment. It does not claim that the listed causes are mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gauge-duality failure regime is any instance satisfying at least one of: primal infeasibility \(F_P=\varnothing\); dual infeasibility \(F_D=\varnothing\); finite positive multiplicative gap \(G_\times>0\); primal nonattainment \(F_P\neq\varnothing\) and \(S_P=\varnothing\); or dual nonattainment \(F_D\neq\varnothing\) and \(S_D=\varnothing\). A regularity failure is the absence of the relative-interior, closure, or lower-semicontinuity condition required by a selected strong-duality theorem; it is a missing guarantee, not by itself evidence that a positive gap occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge-duality failure regimes distinguish primal or dual infeasibility, a positive multiplicative value gap, and nonattainment on either side. Failure of a sufficient regularity condition is recorded separately: it removes a theorem's guarantee but does not logically force an actual duality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak F=\{F_P=\varnothing,\ F_D=\varnothing,\ G_\times>0,\ S_P=\varnothing,\ S_D=\varnothing\},\] interpreted with the feasibility and finite-value qualifications stated above.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the finite positive regime, value failure is \(v_D>1/v_P\), equivalently \(v_P>1/v_D\).
special_cases_latex: A problem may have reciprocal values but fail through nonattainment.
A problem may violate a standard constraint qualification yet still have reciprocal attained values.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure diagnosis must separate actual value or existence behavior from absence of a sufficient hypothesis.
Several failure labels may apply simultaneously.
boundary_notes: Indeterminate products involving \(0\) or \(+\infty\) are not called positive multiplicative gaps.
Unboundedness and infeasibility must be recorded using the adopted extended-value conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-duality failure classification
Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge weak duality makes the product of positive primal and dual values at least one; excess above one is the multiplicative duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\), gauge weak duality gives \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1\), hence \(v_Pv_D\geq1\). The multiplicative duality gap is \(G_{\mathrm{val}}=v_Pv_D-1\). Strong gauge duality is the boundary case \(G_{\mathrm{val}}=0\), equivalently \(v_P=1/v_D\). A strict duality gap occurs when \(G_{\mathrm{val}}>0\). This value gap is distinct from nonattainment: either infimum may fail to be attained even when \(G_{\mathrm{val}}=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(E,F,A,b,\kappa,\rho,\sigma\) define the finite-dimensional primal and gauge-dual pair displayed below.
Both feasible sets are nonempty and \(0<v_P,v_D<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[G_{\mathrm{val}}:=v_Pv_D-1\geq0,\qquad G_{\mathrm{val}}>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ v_P>1/v_D.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive finite values; the gap is multiplicative rather than additive.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal is infeasible precisely when the datum cannot be decomposed into the image of a finite-gauge point plus a residual whose gauge is at most the prescribed radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal gauge problem \(P\) is infeasible exactly when \(\{x\in\operatorname{dom}\kappa:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}=\varnothing\). By the definition of \(B_\rho(\sigma)\), feasibility is equivalent to \(b\in A(\operatorname{dom}\kappa)+B_\rho(\sigma)\). Thus primal infeasibility is equivalent to \(b\notin A(\operatorname{dom}\kappa)+B_\rho(\sigma)\), and under the extended-value convention the primal value is \(+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \(E,F\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, \(A:E\to F\) is linear, and \(b\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P\text{ is infeasible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b\notin A(\operatorname{dom}\kappa)+B_\rho(\sigma).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric feasibility criterion for an extended-valued gauge objective, including the case \(\sigma=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Test for Gauge-Dual Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge dual is feasible exactly when some finite polar-gauge direction has positive residual surplus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Y_0=\{y:\kappa^\circ(A^*y)<\infty,\ \rho^\circ(y)<\infty\},
\qquad \phi(y)=\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y).
\]
Because \(Y_0\) is a cone and \(\phi\) is positively homogeneous,
\[
Y_D\ne\varnothing\iff \exists y\in Y_0:\phi(y)>0,
\]
and hence
\[
Y_D=\varnothing\iff \phi(y)\le0\quad\forall y\in Y_0.
\]
A positive-surplus direction becomes normalized-feasible after scaling by \(1/\phi(y)\).
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional gauge-dual notation is that of the accepted seed.
\(\sigma\ge0\), and the polar gauges are positively homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_D=\varnothing\iff \langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\le0\) for every \(y\in Y_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent infeasibility test for the normalized gauge dual.
review_flags: Positive homogeneity rules out a genuinely unattained positive normalized threshold: any positive surplus can be scaled to equality. This sharpens a misleading boundary sentence in the immutable seed.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge dual is infeasible when no finite polar-gauge direction satisfies its normalized affine residual inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gauge dual is infeasible when there is no direction \(y\in F\) for which the polar objective and residual polar gauge are finite and the normalized dual constraint holds. Explicitly, infeasibility is \(Y_D=\varnothing\), where \(Y_D=\{y\in Y_0:\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}\). Under the extended-value convention, \(\inf_{y\in\varnothing}\kappa^\circ(A^*y)=+\infty\). This condition does not require the supremum of the left-hand constraint expression to be strictly below \(1\); equality may be approached without being attained.
assumptions_latex: \(E,F\) are finite-dimensional, \(A:E\to F\) is linear, and \(b\in F\).
\(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\) are the polar gauges, and \(\sigma\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D\text{ is infeasible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Y_D=\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility includes finiteness of both polar-gauge quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonattainment occurs on either side when that gauge problem is feasible and has a finite infimum, but no feasible point realizes the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal nonattainment means \(X_P\neq\varnothing\), \(v_P<+\infty\), and no \(x\in X_P\) satisfies \(\kappa(x)=v_P\); equivalently, \(\operatorname{argmin}P=\varnothing\) under these feasibility and finiteness conditions. Dual nonattainment means \(Y_D\neq\varnothing\), \(v_D<+\infty\), and no \(y\in Y_D\) satisfies \(\kappa^\circ(A^*y)=v_D\); equivalently, \(\operatorname{argmin}D=\varnothing\) under the corresponding conditions. Nonattainment is an attainment failure rather than infeasibility and is logically distinct from a value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(E,F\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(A:E\to F\) is linear, and \(b\in F\).
\(\kappa:E\to[0,+\infty]\) and \(\rho:F\to[0,+\infty]\) are gauges with polar gauges \(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\), and \(\sigma\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigl(X_P\neq\varnothing,\ v_P<+\infty,\ \operatorname{argmin}P=\varnothing\bigr)\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl(Y_D\neq\varnothing,\ v_D<+\infty,\ \operatorname{argmin}D=\varnothing\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-value nonattainment on either side of a finite-dimensional gauge-dual pair, separated from infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Open-Interval Bipolar Closure Example
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The open interval and its closed convex hull containing zero have the same polar, so double polarity cannot recover the omitted points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C=(0,1)\subset\mathbb R\) and \(C^\circ=\{y:xy\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\),
\[
C^\circ=(-\infty,1],\qquad C^{\circ\circ}=[0,1].
\]
Thus bipolar reconstruction adds the origin and the missing endpoint.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is \(\mathbb R\) with its usual pairing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional witness that polar reconstruction restores omitted boundary points and the origin.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Driven Failures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking a polar twice reconstructs the closed convex hull containing zero, so nonclosed or nonconvex geometry is irreversibly relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Polarity cannot distinguish \(C\) from its closed convex hull containing the origin: the bipolar identity is \(C^{\circ\circ}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(C\cup\{0\})\). Consequently, if \(C\neq\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(C\cup\{0\})\), reconstruction from polar data returns a strict relaxation rather than \(C\). Gauge or dual recovery based only on \(C^\circ\) can therefore lose excluded boundary points, nonconvex structure, or nonclosed structure. The failure disappears when \(C\) is closed, convex, and contains \(0\), because then \(C^{\circ\circ}=C\).
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(C\subset E\) is nonempty.
The polar uses the convention \(C^\circ:=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\leq1\ \forall x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C^{\circ\circ}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(C\cup\{0\}),\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closure loss under polar reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional certificate for the residual-constrained primal and minimization-form gauge dual. The certificate includes feasibility and both equality cases underlying weak duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact primal-dual gauge certificate is a pair \((x,y)\) satisfying \[\rho(r)\leq\sigma,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1,\] together with objective alignment \[\langle x,A^*y\rangle=\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\] and constraint alignment \[\langle r,y\rangle=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)=\sigma\rho^\circ(y).\] Its certificate value is the product \(C(x,y)=\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\); a unit certificate additionally requires \(C(x,y)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact gauge certificate consists of a primal-feasible point and a dual-feasible vector for which the polar-gauge inequality is tight in the objective geometry and in the residual geometry. A unit certificate also has primal-dual objective product one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x,y)\text{ is an exact unit certificate}\iff\text{feasibility, both alignment equalities, and }\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)=1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When all denominators are positive, alignment means the normalized vectors attain equality in the two polar-gauge inequalities.
Objective alignment may be written \(A^*y/\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\in\partial\kappa(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For norm gauges, the equalities are norm-dual Hölder equalities.
If \(\sigma=0\), constraint alignment requires \(r=0\) whenever \(\rho\) is definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: A unit certificate identifies a tight feasible primal-dual pair.
The two alignment conditions expose the primal objective face and the active residual face.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee that certificates exist.
Degenerate zero gauge values require the equality formulation rather than normalized vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Division-Free Objective-Alignment Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is a gauge subgradient exactly when it is polar-feasible and saturates the gauge pairing; normalization yields the usual alignment certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed gauge \(\kappa\), \[z\in\partial\kappa(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \kappa^\circ(z)\leq1\ \text{ and }\ \langle x,z\rangle=\kappa(x).\] Consequently, if \(0<\kappa^\circ(w)<+\infty\), then \[\langle x,w\rangle=\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(w)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{w}{\kappa^\circ(w)}\in\partial\kappa(x),\] including when \(\kappa(x)=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa:E\to[0,+\infty]\) is a proper closed gauge on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[z\in\partial\kappa(x)\iff \bigl(\kappa^\circ(z)\leq1\ \text{and}\ \langle x,z\rangle=\kappa(x)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient form of objective alignment, including zero finite gauge values and avoiding division by the candidate polar direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Alignment Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective alignment is certified when a finite-gauge primal point and a finite nonzero polar direction attain equality in the polar-gauge inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,z\in E\), the polar-gauge inequality is \(\langle x,z\rangle\leq\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(z)\). Under the stated positive finiteness assumptions, equality is an objective-alignment certificate and is equivalent to \(z/\kappa^\circ(z)\in\partial\kappa(x)\). In a gauge primal-dual pair, taking \(z=A^*y\) certifies saturation of the objective-polar inequality. This certificate alone does not establish primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or constraint alignment.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa:E\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed gauge on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space \(E\), and \(\kappa^\circ\) is its polar gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\langle x,z\rangle=\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{z}{\kappa^\circ(z)}\in\partial\kappa(x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact saturation certificate for the polar-gauge inequality at a finite positive gauge value.

knowledge_statements.title: Reciprocal Subgradient Form of Constraint Alignment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact residual alignment is equivalently a subgradient contact condition for either the residual gauge or its polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0<\rho(r)<+\infty\) and \(0<\rho^\circ(y)<+\infty\), then \[\langle r,y\rangle=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{y}{\rho^\circ(y)}\in\partial\rho(r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{r}{\rho(r)}\in\partial\rho^\circ(y).\]
assumptions_latex: \(\rho\) is a proper closed gauge on a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(r\) and \(y\) have finite, strictly positive primal and polar gauge values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polar-gauge equality is equivalent to both reciprocal normalized subgradient conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric subgradient characterization of positive finite residual alignment.

notation.meaning: Subdifferential of the polar residual gauge

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Alignment Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint alignment is certified when a finite-gauge residual and a finite nonzero polar direction attain equality in their polar-gauge inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r,y\in F\), the polar-gauge inequality is \(\langle r,y\rangle\leq\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)\). Under the stated positive finiteness assumptions, equality is a constraint-alignment certificate and is equivalent to \(y/\rho^\circ(y)\in\partial\rho(r)\). In a gauge primal-dual application with a defined residual \(r=b-Ax\), an active constraint \(\rho(r)=\sigma\) turns the certificate into \(\langle b-Ax,y\rangle=\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\). The certificate alone does not establish primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or objective alignment.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:F\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed gauge on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space \(F\), and \(\rho^\circ\) is its polar gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\langle r,y\rangle=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{y}{\rho^\circ(y)}\in\partial\rho(r).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual-direction saturation at finite positive primal and polar gauge values.

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of the residual gauge

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\rho:Y\to[0,+\infty]\) be a closed gauge, let \(r=b-Ax\in Y\), let \(y\in Y\), and let \(\sigma\geq0\). Assume \(\rho(r)\leq\sigma\) and finite \(\rho^\circ(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual-side equality case for an active gauge constraint. Objective alignment is not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The triple \((r,y,\sigma)\) is constraint-aligned when \[\langle r,y\rangle=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)=\sigma\rho^\circ(y).\] If \(\rho^\circ(y)>0\), the second equality forces activity \(\rho(r)=\sigma\). In the nondegenerate case \(\rho(r)>0\) and \(\rho^\circ(y)>0\), alignment is equivalently \[y/\rho^\circ(y)\in\partial\rho(r),\qquad r/\rho(r)\in\partial\rho^\circ(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual r and dual direction y are constraint-aligned at radius σ when the polar-gauge inequality for ρ is tight and the residual constraint is active in the dual direction. For a nonzero polar value, this requires ρ(r)=σ. In the nondegenerate case, normalized residual and dual vectors are reciprocal subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(r,y,\sigma)\text{ constraint-aligned}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle r,y\rangle=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)=\sigma\rho^\circ(y).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(u=r/\rho(r)\) and \(w=y/\rho^\circ(y)\), nondegenerate alignment is \(\rho(u)=\rho^\circ(w)=\langle u,w\rangle=1\).
The normalized residual belongs to the face of the \(\rho\)-unit set exposed by \(w\).
special_cases_latex: For a norm residual, alignment is equality in Hölder's inequality plus \(\|r\|=\sigma\).
When \(\sigma=0\) and \(\rho\) is definite, primal feasibility gives \(r=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Constraint alignment makes the residual term in the weak-duality comparison exact.
A positive dual polar value certifies activity of the primal residual constraint.
boundary_notes: If \(\rho^\circ(y)=0\), the displayed equality need not force constraint activity.
Constraint alignment alone does not imply objective alignment or optimality.

children.title: Normal-Support Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Geometric optimality certificates expressed through supporting and normal directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C_\kappa=\{u\in X:\kappa(u)\leq1\}\) and \(C_\rho=\{v\in Y:\rho(v)\leq1\}\). For a closed convex set \(C\) and \(q\in C\), use \(N_C(q)=\{z:\langle z,w-q\rangle\leq0\ \forall w\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric, nondegenerate formulation of objective and residual alignment through normal cones and supporting hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\kappa(x)>0\), \(\rho(r)>0\), and nonzero directions \(A^*y\) and \(y\), a normal-support certificate is the system \[A^*y\in N_{C_\kappa}\!\left(x/\kappa(x)\right),\qquad y\in N_{C_\rho}\!\left(r/\rho(r)\right),\] together with primal and dual feasibility and the required normalization. Equivalently, the hyperplanes with normals \(A^*y\) and \(y\) support the two unit gauge sets at the normalized primal point and residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-support certificate represents gauge alignment geometrically. The adjoint dual direction is normal to the objective unit-gauge set at the normalized primal point, and the dual direction is normal to the residual unit-gauge set at the normalized residual. The associated hyperplanes therefore support the two unit sets at the certificate points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A^*y\in N_{C_\kappa}(x/\kappa(x)),\qquad y\in N_{C_\rho}(r/\rho(r)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first inclusion is equivalent to \(x/\kappa(x)\in\operatorname{argmax}_{u\in C_\kappa}\langle A^*y,u\rangle\); the second has the analogous residual form.
Each normal inclusion is equivalent to a supporting-hyperplane contact condition.
special_cases_latex: If a unit set is strictly convex, a nonzero normal exposes at most one contact point.
For polyhedral gauges, each contact point lies in an exposed face determined by active linear inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate identifies exposed faces containing all compatible normalized primal and residual points.
Normal directions provide a geometric interface for primal recovery from a dual solution.
boundary_notes: The normalized statement excludes zero gauge values; an unnormalized subgradient formulation is needed there.
Normality alone does not impose the scalar gauge-dual feasibility normalization.

notation.meaning: Unit sublevel sets of the two gauges.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal vector certifies that the point maximizes its associated linear functional over the convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(y\) is a normal-cone certificate for \(x\in C\) when \(y\in N_C(x)\), meaning \(\langle y,z-x\rangle\leq0\) for every \(z\in C\). The inequalities are equivalent to \(\langle y,x\rangle=\sigma_C(y)\), so they certify that \(x\) maximizes the linear functional \(z\mapsto\langle y,z\rangle\) over \(C\). If \(y\neq0\), the certificate also identifies a supporting hyperplane. If \(y=0\), membership is automatic and conveys no exposed-boundary information.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y\in N_C(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle y,z-x\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }z\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-normal convention for closed convex sets.

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Tangent and Normal Cones p. 125

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting-Hyperplane Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting-hyperplane certificate gives a nonzero normal whose halfspace contains the set and whose boundary touches it at the stated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((y,\alpha)\) is a supporting-hyperplane certificate for \(C\) at \(x\) when \(y\neq0\), every \(z\in C\) satisfies \(\langle y,z\rangle\leq\alpha\), and \(\langle y,x\rangle=\alpha\). These conditions verify that \(H=\{z:\langle y,z\rangle=\alpha\}\) meets \(C\) at \(x\) while \(C\) lies in the associated closed halfspace. The contact set \(F_C(y)=\{z\in C:\langle y,z\rangle=\alpha\}\) is the exposed face certified by the hyperplane.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C\subseteq\{z:\langle y,z\rangle\leq\alpha\},\quad \langle y,x\rangle=\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonzero normal and a touching equality form the certificate.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C\subseteq\{z:\langle y,z\rangle\leq\alpha\},\quad \langle y,x\rangle=\alpha.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Support Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point supports a direction exactly when that direction belongs to the point's normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normal and support descriptions coincide pointwise. Specifically, \(y\in N_C(x)\) holds exactly when \(\langle y,z-x\rangle\leq0\) for all \(z\in C\), which is exactly the assertion that \(x\) attains the support value in direction \(y\): \(\langle y,x\rangle=\sigma_C(y)\). Hence \(F_C(y)=\{x\in C:y\in N_C(x)\}\). For \(y\neq0\), this set is the exposed face cut out by the supporting hyperplane with level \(\sigma_C(y)\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y\in N_C(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle y,z\rangle\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle y,x\rangle=\sigma_C(y).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise equivalence between normal membership and support attainment.

notation.meaning: Normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Support Need Not Be Attained on a Closed Convex Set
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of 1/u on the positive half-line is closed and convex, but its downward support value zero is approached only at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\geq u^{-1}\}
\]
and \(y=(0,-1)\). Then \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and unbounded, and
\[
\sigma_C(y)=0,
\qquad
F_C(y)=\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_C(y)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle y,z\rangle=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semialgebraic closed unbounded convex example with finite unattained support.

notation.meaning: support value of C in direction y

knowledge_statements.title: Compactness and Strict Convexity Remove Support Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness guarantees support attainment, and strict convexity makes every nonzero support direction select a unique point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty compact subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space. Then \(F_C(y):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle\) is nonempty for every \(y\). If \(C\) is also convex and strictly convex, then \(F_C(y)\) is a singleton for every \(y\neq0\), whereas \(F_C(0)=C\).
assumptions_latex: For uniqueness, \(C\) is convex and strictly convex.
The ambient inner-product space is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(y)\neq\varnothing\) for all \(y\), and under strict convexity \(|F_C(y)|=1\) for \(y\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundaries for support maximizers.

notation.meaning: support maximizer set selected by y

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Attainment Degeneracy Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support degeneracy consists of zero direction, infinite or unattained support, or multiple maximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(C\subset E\), define \(\sigma_C(y)=\sup_{z\in C}\langle y,z\rangle\) and \(F_C(y)=\{x\in C:\langle y,x\rangle=\sigma_C(y)\}\). Then \(F_C(0)=C\). If \(\sigma_C(y)=+\infty\), then \(F_C(y)=\varnothing\). For finite \(\sigma_C(y)\), the supremum is either unattained, uniquely attained, or multiply attained. If \(C\) is convex, every nonempty \(F_C(y)\) is an exposed face of \(C\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support maximizer set is all of \(C\), empty, a singleton, or a nontrivial exposed face according to the stated regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of empty, unique, nonunique, and zero-direction support regimes.

notation.meaning: support maximizer set selected by y

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Support Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes caused by zero normals, infinite support, or unattained finite support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal–support certificate is informative only when \(y\ne0\), \(\sigma_C(y)<+\infty\), and the support supremum is attained. The zero vector exposes no proper face. If \(\sigma_C(y)=+\infty\), no supporting hyperplane with normal \(y\) exists. Finite support also need not be attained for an unbounded closed convex set: for
\[C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge e^u\},\qquad y=(0,-1),\]
one has \(\sigma_C(y)=0\), but \(\langle y,x\rangle<0\) for every \(x\in C\); hence \(y\notin N_C(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support certificates become degenerate for a zero normal, infinite support, or a finite support value that no point attains.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pointwise normal certificate requires a nonzero support direction whose finite support value is attained.

notation.meaning: normal cone of C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Recovery from Gauge-Dual Solutions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible point exposed and aligned by an optimal gauge-dual vector is primal optimal when the normalized dual constraint is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^\star\) solve \(\inf\{\kappa^\circ(A^*y):\langle b,y\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y)\geq1\}\). A primal-feasible point \(x\) is recovered from the face exposed by \(A^*y^\star\) if, with \(r=b-Ax\), \[\langle x,A^*y^\star\rangle=\kappa(x)d^\star,\qquad \langle r,y^\star\rangle=\sigma\rho^\circ(y^\star),\qquad \langle b,y^\star\rangle-\sigma\rho^\circ(y^\star)=1.\] These identities imply \(1=\kappa(x)d^\star\); gauge weak duality then certifies that \(x\) is primal optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, and \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are closed gauges.
The primal problem is \(p^\star=\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\}\), and the gauge dual has an attained solution \(y^\star\) with \(d^\star=\kappa^\circ(A^*y^\star)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is primal optimal and \(\kappa(x)d^\star=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional recovery through exposed faces and exact primal–dual alignment.

notation.meaning: Polar gauge of the objective gauge

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(y^*\) be a gauge-dual solution with \(0<\kappa^\circ(A^*y^*)<+\infty\). Let \(v_P>0\) be the primal value and define \(C_\kappa=\{u:\kappa(u)\leq1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued recovery interface based on an attained dual solution and an exposed objective face. A known or independently recovered primal scale is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The objective face exposed by \(y^*\) is \[E(y^*)=\operatorname{argmax}_{u\in C_\kappa}\langle A^*y^*,u\rangle.\] The associated primal recovery set at scale \(v_P\) is \[R_P(y^*)=\{x=v_Pu:u\in E(y^*),\ \rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma,\ \langle b-Ax,y^*\rangle=\sigma\rho^\circ(y^*)\}.\] Recovery succeeds when \(R_P(y^*)\neq\varnothing\); every member is compatible with both objective and residual alignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge-dual solution exposes a face of the primal objective's unit-gauge set through the direction A*y*. After scaling that face by the primal value, primal recovery consists of selecting points that are primal feasible and satisfy residual alignment with the dual solution. Recovery is successful when this set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_P(y^*)=v_PE(y^*)\cap\{x:\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma,\ \langle b-Ax,y^*\rangle=\sigma\rho^\circ(y^*)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Membership \(u\in E(y^*)\) is equivalent to \(A^*y^*\in N_{C_\kappa}(u)\).
When \(v_Pv_D=1\), the recovery scale is \(v_P=1/v_D\).
special_cases_latex: If \(E(y^*)\) is a singleton and its scaled point is residual-feasible and aligned, recovery is unique.
For polyhedral gauges, recovery reduces to feasibility over an exposed polyhedral face.
immediate_consequences_latex: The dual solution can reduce primal search to a lower-dimensional exposed face.
Multiple recovered points are possible when the exposed face is not a singleton.
boundary_notes: Dual optimality alone need not make the recovery set nonempty.
The definition excludes recovery methods based on smoothing or additional regularizers.

notation.meaning: Objective unit face exposed by the dual solution.

children.title: Inexact Gauge Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Residual-based certificate families for approximate optimality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x\in X\), \(y\in Y\), \(r=b-Ax\), and let \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_P,\varepsilon_D,\varepsilon_O,\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_G)\in\mathbb R_+^5\). Assume all displayed gauge values are finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-error certificate for approximate feasibility, objective alignment, constraint alignment, and multiplicative complementarity. Relative-error variants are not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-inexact gauge certificate is a pair \((x,y)\) satisfying \[[\rho(r)-\sigma]_+\leq\varepsilon_P,\qquad[1-\langle b,y\rangle+\sigma\rho^\circ(y)]_+\leq\varepsilon_D,\] \[0\leq\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)-\langle x,A^*y\rangle\leq\varepsilon_O,\] \[0\leq\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)-\langle r,y\rangle\leq\varepsilon_C,\qquad |\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)-1|\leq\varepsilon_G.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact gauge certificate bounds five independently interpretable residuals: primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, failure of objective polar alignment, failure of residual polar alignment, and deviation of the primal-dual objective product from one. All tolerances are nonnegative absolute errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x,y)\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\iff(R_P,R_D,R_O,R_C,R_G)\leq(\varepsilon_P,\varepsilon_D,\varepsilon_O,\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_G)\] componentwise, with the residuals defined in the statement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact certificate system is recovered by setting \(\varepsilon=0\).
A single tolerance \(\eta\) may be imposed by requiring the maximum of the five residuals to be at most \(\eta\).
special_cases_latex: For norm gauges, \(R_O\) and \(R_C\) are Hölder-equality defects.
If an iterate is exactly feasible, the corresponding feasibility residual vanishes.
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual vector identifies which component prevents exact certification.
Sequences with all five residuals converging to zero are asymptotically certificate-consistent, subject to boundedness and closedness needed for limit passage.
boundary_notes: Absolute residuals are scale-dependent.
Vanishing residuals along an unbounded sequence do not by themselves imply convergence to an attained optimum.

notation.meaning: Set of pairs satisfying the five tolerance bounds.

review_flags: The five-residual absolute-error system is a precise candidate formulation, but no matching authoritative source was located.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-based inexact gauge certificate
Dual Relative-Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small multiplicative gauge-duality gap gives the same relative-error guarantee for the feasible gauge-dual objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d(y)=\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\). If \(x\) and \(y\) are primal and gauge-dual feasible, the positive optimal values satisfy \(p^\star d^\star=1\), and \(\kappa(x)d(y)\leq1+\varepsilon\), then \[d^\star\leq d(y)\leq(1+\varepsilon)d^\star.\]
assumptions_latex: The primal and gauge-dual optimal values are positive and satisfy \(p^\star d^\star=1\).
\(x\) and \(y\) are respectively primal and gauge-dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(y)/d^\star-1\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge-dual objective guarantee supplied by the same multiplicative gap used for primal certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible pair whose multiplicative gauge-duality gap is at most epsilon certifies relative primal suboptimality at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Gauge weak duality gives \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\geq1\). Hence \(G(x,y)\geq0\) is directly computable. If \(G(x,y)\leq\varepsilon\), then \[\frac{1}{\kappa^\circ(A^*y)}\leq p^\star\leq\kappa(x)\leq\frac{1+\varepsilon}{\kappa^\circ(A^*y)}\leq(1+\varepsilon)p^\star.\] Thus the feasible pair certifies relative primal suboptimality at most \(\varepsilon\), without knowing \(p^\star\).
assumptions_latex: The primal and gauge-dual problems attain positive values and satisfy \(p^\star d^\star=1\).
\(x\) is primal feasible and \(y\) is gauge-dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)\leq1+\varepsilon\), then \(\kappa(x)\leq(1+\varepsilon)p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative objective certification under positive strong gauge duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Residual-Gauge Feasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive constraint radius, normalized gauge violation exactly certifies relative feasibility error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\sigma>0\), define \[\eta_f(x)=\left[\frac{\rho(b-Ax)}{\sigma}-1\right]_+=\frac{\delta_f(x)}{\sigma}.\] Then \(\eta_f(x)\leq\varepsilon\) if and only if \(\rho(b-Ax)\leq(1+\varepsilon)\sigma\), and \(\eta_f(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) is exactly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_f(x)\leq\varepsilon\Longleftrightarrow\rho(b-Ax)\leq(1+\varepsilon)\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-free normalization of the absolute feasibility excess for a positive constraint radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive part of the residual-gauge violation exactly measures and certifies absolute inexact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any candidate \(x\), define \[\delta_f(x)=\max\{\rho(b-Ax)-\sigma,0\}.\] Then \(\delta_f(x)\geq0\) and \(\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma+\delta_f(x)\). Consequently, the verifiable inequality \(\delta_f(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\) is an inexact feasibility certificate with absolute residual-gauge tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\); the special value \(\delta_f(x)=0\) certifies exact primal feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho\) is a gauge on a finite-dimensional residual space.
The required primal constraint is \(\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma\), where \(\sigma\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar \(\delta_f(x)\) certifies \(\rho(b-Ax)\leq\sigma+\delta_f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute feasibility error measured in the residual gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Alignment Defects as Epsilon-Subgradient Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After positive finite polar normalization, each alignment defect is exactly an epsilon-subgradient contact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w=A^*y\). If \(\kappa(x)<+\infty\) and \(0<\kappa^\circ(w)<+\infty\), then \[\frac{w}{\kappa^\circ(w)}\in\partial_{\Delta_\kappa(x,y)/\kappa^\circ(w)}\kappa(x).\] If \(r=b-Ax\), \(\rho(r)<+\infty\), and \(0<\rho^\circ(y)<+\infty\), then \[\frac{y}{\rho^\circ(y)}\in\partial_{\Delta_\rho(x,y)/\rho^\circ(y)}\rho(r).\] Each defect is the corresponding normalized Fenchel–Young residual multiplied by its polar normalization.
assumptions_latex: The relevant primal-gauge values are finite, and the relevant polar-gauge denominators are finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized dual directions are epsilon-subgradients with epsilon equal to the corresponding defect divided by its polar normalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive finite normalization of polar-inequality defects into approximate subgradient contact.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Alignment Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative defects in the two polar inequalities quantify objective and residual misalignment and become exact alignment certificates when zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the defects \[\Delta_\kappa(x,y)=\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(A^*y)-\langle x,A^*y\rangle,\qquad \Delta_\rho(x,y)=\rho(r)\rho^\circ(y)-\langle r,y\rangle.\] The polar inequalities imply \(\Delta_\kappa(x,y)\geq0\) and \(\Delta_\rho(x,y)\geq0\). Therefore upper bounds on these computable quantities certify inexact objective and residual alignment. Both defects vanish precisely when the corresponding polar inequalities are attained, subject to the usual zero-vector degeneracies.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) and \(\rho\) are gauges with polar gauges \(\kappa^\circ\) and \(\rho^\circ\).
\(x\) and \(y\) are arbitrary primal and dual candidate vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounds \(\Delta_\kappa(x,y)\leq\varepsilon_\kappa\) and \(\Delta_\rho(x,y)\leq\varepsilon_\rho\) certify the two polar alignments to those tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate computable defects for objective and residual polar inequalities.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Primal-Dual Optimality Characterizations p. 154

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reliability Thresholds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is reliable only when its feasibility, multiplicative optimality, and total alignment residuals all meet their prescribed thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact gauge certificate is accepted at reliability thresholds \((\tau_f,\tau_o,\tau_a)\) if and only if \[\delta_f(x)\leq\tau_f,\qquad 0\leq G(x,y)\leq\tau_o,\qquad 0\leq\Delta_\kappa(x,y)+\Delta_\rho(x,y)\leq\tau_a.\] Here the optimality test presupposes primal and dual feasibility; otherwise it is not valid as an objective guarantee. Thresholds are absolute for feasibility and alignment, while \(\tau_o\) is a relative multiplicative tolerance under positive strong gauge duality.
assumptions_latex: A candidate pair \((x,y)\) has computable feasibility, optimality, and alignment residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair is reliable at \((\tau_f,\tau_o,\tau_a)\) exactly when all three displayed threshold tests hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise acceptance rule; thresholds must reflect the application’s scaling.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gauge sensitivity-duality correspondence associates dual solutions with supporting slopes of the value function at the origin. With the opposite perturbation sign, the multiplier set is \(-\partial V(0)\).
