knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Atoms and Minimal Atomic Hulls
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom is gauge-redundant exactly when it lies in the hull of zero and the other atoms; an irredundant dictionary lists the nonzero vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\) and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). Deleting \(a_i\) leaves \(C\), and hence its gauge, unchanged exactly when \[a_i\in\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{0\}\cup(\mathcal A\setminus\{a_i\})\bigr).\] After redundant elements and duplicates are removed, the remaining atoms are precisely the nonzero vertices of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)}=\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup(\mathcal A\setminus\{a_i\}))}\iff a_i\in\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup(\mathcal A\setminus\{a_i\}))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite one-sided dictionaries generating the same atomic convex set.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Atomic Dictionaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite dictionary generates the convex hull of its atoms and zero; its gauge measures the least dilation containing a point and is globally finite exactly when the atoms positively span the space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite atomic dictionary is a set \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset X\). Its atomic convex set is \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\), and its atomic gauge is \[\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tC\},\qquad \inf\varnothing=+\infty.\] The gauge is finite on \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)\). It is finite throughout \(X\) precisely when \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)=X\), equivalently when \(0\) is an interior point of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\), \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\), and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, one-sided atomic dictionaries; the gauge may be extended-valued.

notation.meaning: Minkowski gauge of the atomic convex set

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Gauge Unit Balls
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit sublevel set of a finite-dictionary gauge is exactly the polytope formed by the atoms and zero; positive sublevels are its dilations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(\mathcal A\) is finite, \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\) is a compact polytope. Its Minkowski gauge satisfies \[\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\leq1\}=C.\] More generally, every finite sublevel set obeys \(\{x:\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\leq t\}=tC\) for \(t\geq0\). If \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), these are full-dimensional polyhedral gauge balls and the gauge is finite and continuous on \(\mathbb R^d\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^d\) is finite and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\leq1\}=C\), and \(C\) is a polytope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed finite-dimensional atomic hulls, including possibly lower-dimensional unit balls.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Linear Program and Exact Value Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vertex coefficient program has a polar-inequality dual, and complementary slackness certifies the exact gauge value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\) and \(x\in\operatorname{cone}\{a_i\}\), \[\min_{\lambda\geq0}\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x\}=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^d}\{\langle x,y\rangle:A^\top y\leq\mathbf1\}.\] Both optima are attained. A primal-dual feasible pair \((\lambda,y)\) is optimal exactly when \[\lambda_i(1-\langle a_i,y\rangle)=0\quad(i=1,0ldots,m),\] in which case both objectives equal \(\gamma_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\lambda\geq0\}=\max\{\langle x,y\rangle:A^\top y\leq\mathbf1\}\), with complementary-slackness certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite one-sided atomic coefficient program.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Optimal Vertex Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible finite atomic gauge has an optimal coefficient representation using no more atoms than the rank of the dictionary matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever the vertex coefficient program is feasible, it has an optimal solution \(\lambda^*\) with \[|\operatorname{supp}\lambda^*|\leq\operatorname{rank}A\leq d.\] Thus every point of finite gauge has a gauge-attaining conic representation using at most \(\operatorname{rank}A\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda^*\in\arg\min\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\lambda\geq0\}\) with \(|\operatorname{supp}\lambda^*|\leq\operatorname{rank}A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-size bound for an optimal finite-dictionary coefficient vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Based Gauge Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite atomic gauge equals the infimum of the total nonnegative coefficient mass over all representations of the point by dictionary columns, with value positive infinity when no representation exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), the gauge generated by the vertices has the representation \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\left\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\right\}.\] Its value is \(+\infty\) when the constraint is infeasible. This representation is a linear program in the atomic coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\ \lambda\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-programming representation for a finite one-sided dictionary.

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns are the atoms

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Based Polar Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized facet normals are the polar polytope’s vertices, and the primal gauge is the maximum of their linear functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The normalized facet description and polar vertex description are equivalent: \[C^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{y_1,\ldots,y_r\}.\] Consequently, the gauge is the support function of the polar and has the finite maximum representation \[\gamma_C(x)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(x)=\max_{1\leq j\leq r}\langle y_j,x\rangle.\] Conversely, the vertices of \(C^\circ\) determine the nonredundant facets of \(C\), up to repeated or redundant inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:\langle y_j,x\rangle\leq1,\ j=1,\ldots,r\}\) is an irredundant facet description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{y_1,\ldots,y_r\}\) and \(\gamma_C(x)=\max_j\langle y_j,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional polytopes with the origin strictly inside.

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Polar Sets p. 136
3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional polytope with normalized facet inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I(x)=\{j:\langle y_j,x\rangle=\gamma_C(x)\}\), \[\partial\gamma_C(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{y_j:j\in I(x)\}.\] Thus an active normal certifies the maximum value, and \(\partial\gamma_C(0)=C^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active normalized facet normals generate the gauge subdifferential and certify the maximum value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\gamma_C(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{y_j:j\in I(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: indices attaining the facet maximum at x

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Facet Subgradient and Evaluation Certificate

children.title: Infinite-Dictionary Atomic Gauges
children.top_down_role: Atomic gauges indexed by continuous or infinite parameter spaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\Theta\) be an infinite index set, and let \(a:\Theta\to X\) be an atom map. Set \(\mathcal A=a(\Theta)\) and \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional decision space with a continuous or otherwise infinite dictionary; closure is included explicitly to handle limiting atoms and decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The infinite-dictionary atomic gauge is \[\gamma_{a}(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}.\] Equivalently, it is the lower-semicontinuous envelope of the finite-decomposition cost \[x\mapsto\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i:m\in\mathbb N,\ c_i\ge0,\ \theta_i\in\Theta,\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a(\theta_i)\right\}.\] Its polar admits the pointwise dictionary formula \[\gamma_a^\circ(y)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle y,a(\theta)\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite family of atoms generates a gauge through the closed convex hull of all atoms and the origin. Primal evaluation asks for the least total weight in finite atomic representations, allowing closure for limiting representations. Polar evaluation is the supremum of the dual pairing over the entire parameter space.
assumptions_latex: The closed convex hull \(C\) is used as the gauge unit set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_a=\gamma_{\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(a(\Theta)\cup\{0\})}\) and \(\gamma_a^\circ(y)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle y,a(\theta)\rangle\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Theta\) is compact and \(a\) is continuous, then \(a(\Theta)\) is compact and the polar supremum is attained.
special_cases_latex: Trigonometric, exponential, and rank-one parameterized atoms yield continuous-dictionary gauges.
immediate_consequences_latex: The polar oracle is an optimization problem over \(\Theta\), even when no finite dictionary matrix exists.
boundary_notes: The gauge need not be computationally tractable merely because the parameterization is explicit.
In infinite-dimensional decision spaces, additional topology and compactness hypotheses are required and are outside this record.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Description of a Parameterized Atomic Hull
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a continuously parameterized atomic hull is the intersection of all atom inequalities, with a supremum that need not be a finite maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup a(T))\). Then \[C^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\langle y,a(t)\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }t\in T\}.\] The associated atomic support value is \(\sup_{t\in T}\langle y,a(t)\rangle\), which need not be attained or finite without compactness or boundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\circ=\bigcap_{t\in T}\{y:\langle y,a(t)\rangle\leq1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly noncompact continuously parameterized atomic images in finite dimensions.

notation.meaning: polar of the closed parameterized atomic hull

knowledge_statements.title: Continuously Parameterized Atomic Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous atom map indexes an infinite dictionary; its atomic gauge is formed from the closed convex hull of the image and zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuously parameterized atomic set is the image \(\mathcal A=a(T)=\{a(t):t\in T\}\) of a continuous map into \(\mathbb R^d\). Its closed atomic convex set and gauge are defined by \[C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup a(T)),\qquad \gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\{s>0:x\in sC\}.\] The closure is part of the definition unless compactness or another hypothesis already guarantees that the convex hull is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a topological space and \(a:T\to\mathbb R^d\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A=a(T)\), \(C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\), and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional atomic images of a general topological parameter space.

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Finite-Support Attainment after Closure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure can give a countable atomic gauge its exact limiting value even though no finite-support decomposition attains that value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_n=1-1/n\) for \(n\geq2\). Then \[C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup\{a_n:n\geq2\})=[0,1],\qquad \gamma_C(1)=1.\] The infimum of \(\sum_n\lambda_n\) over exact finite-support nonnegative representations \(\sum_n\lambda_na_n=1\) is also \(1\), but no such representation has total mass \(1\). Thus the finite-support atomic-mass infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(1)=q(1)=1\), but the infimum defining \(q(1)\) is not attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional countable dictionary whose closed hull adds a limiting atom.

notation.meaning: countable atoms approaching the missing endpoint one

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge as the Lower-Semicontinuous Envelope of Finite Atomic Mass
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a countable dictionary, the closed atomic gauge is the lower-semicontinuous relaxation of minimum finite-support coefficient mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[q(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda_n:\lambda\in c_{00,+},\ \sum_{n\geq1}\lambda_na_n=x\right\}.\] For \(C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup\{a_n:n\geq1\})\), the closed atomic gauge is the lower-semicontinuous envelope of \(q\): \[\gamma_C(x)=\operatorname{cl}q(x)=\liminf_{z\to x}q(z).\] Equivalently, \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\left\{\liminf_{k\to\infty}\sum_n\lambda_n^{(k)}:\lambda^{(k)}\in c_{00,+},\ \sum_n\lambda_n^{(k)}a_n\to x\right\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is the extended finite-support nonnegative atomic-mass functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0,a_1,a_2,\ldots\})}=\operatorname{cl}q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Countable one-sided dictionaries with finite-support coefficient representations.

notation.meaning: infimum finite-support atomic mass before closure

knowledge_statements.title: Countably Infinite Atomic Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A countably infinite dictionary of distinct atoms generates the closure of all finite nonnegative atomic combinations having total coefficient mass at most one, and its gauge is the Minkowski functional of that closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\{a_n:n\geq1\}\), and let \(c_{00,+}\) denote the set of finitely supported sequences \(\lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\lambda_n\geq0\). The closed atomic convex set is \[C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)=\overline{\left\{\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda_na_n:\lambda\in c_{00,+},\ \sum_{n\geq1}\lambda_n\leq1\right\}},\] and its gauge is \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tC\},\qquad \inf\varnothing=+\infty.\]
assumptions_latex: \((a_n)_{n\geq1}\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a sequence of pairwise distinct atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A=\{a_n:n\geq1\}\), \(C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\), and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Countably infinite dictionaries in finite-dimensional spaces, with closure explicitly retained.

notation.meaning: set of finitely supported nonnegative real sequences

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49

knowledge_statements.title: Attained Finite Atomic Decomposition under Compact Indexing
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact indexing makes the atomic-mass infimum attainable, with a gauge-optimal decomposition using at most d atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be compact, \(a:T\to\mathbb R^d\) continuous, and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup a(T))\). For every \(x\) with \(0<\gamma_C(x)<+\infty\), there exist \(k\leq d\), parameters \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\in T\), and coefficients \(\lambda_i>0\) such that \[x=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i a(t_i),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=\gamma_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i a(t_i)\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=\gamma_C(x)\), for some \(k\leq d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact continuously indexed atoms in finite-dimensional space.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Index Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous image of a compact index set is compact, and its finite-dimensional convex hull is compact; an interior-origin assumption makes the gauge finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The image \(a(T)\) is compact, and in finite dimensions \[C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup a(T))\] is also compact and hence closed. Therefore the closed-hull convention introduces no additional points. If additionally \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), then \(C\) is an absorbing compact convex body, its gauge is finite and continuous on \(\mathbb R^d\), and every set \(\{x:\gamma_C(x)\leq r\}=rC\) is compact for \(r\geq0\).
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is compact and \(a:T\to\mathbb R^d\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(T)\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup a(T))\) are compact, so no closure is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous atomic parameterizations over compact spaces in finite dimensions.

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Atomic Families Can Collapse Definiteness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded positive atomic dictionary generates a ray whose gauge vanishes in every positive direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\subset\mathbb R\) and
\[
C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)=[0,+\infty).
\]
Its Minkowski functional is
\[
\gamma_C(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&x\geq0,\\
+\infty,&x<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every positive point has zero gauge, so an unbounded noncompact atomic family can destroy definiteness completely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=[0,+\infty)\), with \(\gamma_C(x)=0\) for \(x\geq0\) and \(\gamma_C(x)=+\infty\) for \(x<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge degeneracy caused by an unbounded noncompact atomic dictionary.

notation.meaning: Minkowski functional of the atomic hull C

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Index Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without compactness, a continuous atomic image may have a nonclosed hull; then the gauge’s closed unit sublevel can strictly exceed the proposed unclosed atomic ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\mathbb N\) with the discrete topology and define \(a(n)=1-1/n\) in \(\mathbb R\). Then \(a\) is continuous but \(a(T)\) is noncompact, and \[C_0=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup a(T))=[0,1)\] is not closed. Its Minkowski functional satisfies \(\gamma_{C_0}(1)=1\), although \(1\notin C_0\); hence \(\{x:\gamma_{C_0}(x)\leq1\}=[0,1]\neq C_0\). Taking the closed convex hull repairs this mismatch.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is noncompact; continuity of the atom map alone is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compactness and closedness of the atomic hull need not hold, and omitting closure can change the gauge unit ball.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional failure when compactness of the parameter space is removed.

children.title: Coefficient-Symmetry Atomic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Atomic constructions distinguished by symmetry and coefficient sign.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\) be nonempty. Define \(C_+=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\) and \(C_\pm=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup(-\mathcal A))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional comparison of asymmetric positive-coefficient gauges with centrally symmetric signed-coefficient atomic norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The positive-coefficient atomic gauge and symmetric atomic gauge are respectively \[\gamma_+(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_i c_i:x=\sum_i c_i a_i,\ c_i\ge0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A\right\}=\gamma_{C_+}(x),\] \[\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_i|\alpha_i|:x=\sum_i\alpha_i a_i,\ \alpha_i\in\mathbb R,\ a_i\in\mathcal A\right\}=\gamma_{C_\pm}(x),\] with closure understood and infima taken over finite decompositions. The first permits only positive atomic coefficients and can be asymmetric or infinite; the second absorbs signs into the symmetrized atom set and is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are two distinct coefficient regimes. A one-sided atomic gauge uses nonnegative coefficients and retains directional information in the atom set. A symmetric atomic gauge allows signed coefficients, charges their absolute values, and is generated by adjoining every negative atom. The latter becomes a norm when the symmetrized atom set spans the space and its convex hull is bounded with the origin in its interior.
assumptions_latex: All decomposition infima range over finite families of atoms.
Closed convex hulls define the lower-semicontinuous gauges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_+=\gamma_{C_+}\), \(\gamma_\pm=\gamma_{C_\pm}\), and \(\gamma_\pm(x)=\gamma_\pm(-x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\gamma_\pm\) is the positive-coefficient gauge generated by the enlarged dictionary \(\mathcal A\cup(-\mathcal A)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\mathcal A=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\), \(\gamma_+\) is \(\mathbf1^Tx\) on \(\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(+\infty\) outside, whereas \(\gamma_\pm=\|x\|_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Symmetrization can strictly decrease the gauge because it enlarges the atomic unit set.
boundary_notes: Central symmetry alone does not guarantee finiteness or positive definiteness unless the atoms span the ambient space appropriately.
Complex coefficients require a phase-balanced atom set and are outside this real-space definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Atomic Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced atomic set contains every real scalar contraction of each atom. A closed convex absorbing balanced set in a real topological vector space generates a symmetric seminorm, and it generates a norm when it contains no nonzero linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(\mathcal A\) is balanced if \[a\in\mathcal A,\quad |\alpha|\leq1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha a\in\mathcal A.\] In particular, every nonempty balanced set contains \(0\) and is centrally symmetric. If \(C\subset X\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and balanced, then its gauge satisfies \(\gamma_C(-x)=\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and is a seminorm. If, additionally, \(C\) contains no nonzero linear subspace, then \(\gamma_C\) is a norm.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real Hausdorff topological vector space and \(\mathcal A\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is balanced exactly when \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(|\alpha|\leq1\) imply \(\alpha a\in\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard real-topological-vector-space meaning of balanced; the complex analogue is also called circled.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Sets in Vector Spaces p. 1

knowledge_statements.title: Norm and Degeneracy Boundary for Signed Atomic Gauges
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite signed dictionary defines a norm on its span and an ambient-space norm exactly when its atoms span the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\), the gauge \(\gamma_C\) is even and is a norm on \(L=\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\). On \(\mathbb R^d\), it is an everywhere-finite norm exactly when \(L=\mathbb R^d\); otherwise \(\gamma_C(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\notin L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a norm on \(L=\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\), and it is a norm on \(\mathbb R^d\iff L=\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness and domain of a finite signed atomic gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar and Dual Formula for a Signed Dictionary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar is defined by absolute atom inequalities, and the signed atomic gauge is their dual support maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\) and \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\). Then \[C^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1\}\] and \[\gamma_C(x)=\sup\{\langle x,y\rangle:\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1\}.\] For \(x\in\operatorname{span}\{a_i\}\), the supremum is attained and equals the minimum coefficient \(\ell_1\)-mass in the seed representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\circ=\{y:\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1\}\) and \(\gamma_C(x)=\sup_{\|A^\top y\|_\infty\leq1}\langle x,y\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite signed dictionaries in a real Euclidean space.

notation.meaning: polar of the signed atomic hull

knowledge_statements.title: Signed Atomic Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding each atom’s negative converts nonnegative atomic mass into signed coefficients, and the resulting gauge is minimum coefficient ℓ1 mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The signed enlargement of \(\mathcal A_0\) is \(\mathcal A_\pm=\mathcal A_0\cup(-\mathcal A_0)\). With \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\), its convex hull satisfies \[\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_\pm)=\{Ac:c\in\mathbb R^m,\ \|c\|_1\leq1\}.\] Consequently, its gauge has the coefficient representation \[\gamma_{\mathcal A_\pm}(x)=\inf\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\},\] where the value is \(+\infty\) if \(x\notin\operatorname{span}(\mathcal A_0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_\pm=\mathcal A_0\cup(-\mathcal A_0)\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_\pm}(x)=\inf\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite real dictionaries closed under sign reversal.

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Conic Base Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive linear normalization cuts a cone into a base whose gauge equals the normalization value on the cone and is infinite outside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset X\) be a convex cone and let \(u\in X^*\) satisfy \(\langle u,k\rangle>0\) for every \(k\in K\setminus\{0\}\). Define \[B=\{k\in K:\langle u,k\rangle=1\},\qquad C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup B).\] Every \(x\in K\setminus\{0\}\) has the representation \[x=\langle u,x\rangle b,\qquad b=\frac{x}{\langle u,x\rangle}\in B,\] and \[\gamma_C(x)=\begin{cases}\langle u,x\rangle,&x\in K,\\+\infty,&x\notin K.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup B)\) equals \(\langle u,x\rangle\) on \(K\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of a cone by a strictly positive linear functional.
review_flags: Existence of a strictly positive normalizing functional is assumed, not asserted for every cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Atomic Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using an entire cone as the atomic unit set makes the gauge zero on the cone and infinite outside; a normalized conic base is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the atomic unit set is itself a cone \(K\), then \(tK=K\) for every \(t>0\). Hence its Minkowski functional collapses to \[\gamma_K(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tK\}=\begin{cases}0,&x\in K,\\+\infty,&x\notin K.\end{cases}\] Thus a nontrivial conic atomic model requires a normalized base or cross-section of the cone as its unit atoms; using the whole cone cannot produce a definite gauge.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset X\) is a nonempty cone, so \(\lambda K\subseteq K\) for every \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_K(x)=0\) for \(x\in K\) and \(\gamma_K(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy caused by using an entire cone, rather than a bounded conic base, as the gauge unit set.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Constraints in One-Sided and Sign-Symmetric Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided coefficients produce one-sided dual inequalities, whereas signed coefficients produce absolute dual inequalities and an infinity-norm polar value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\), \[C_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_m\}),\qquad C_\pm=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}.\] Then \[C_+^\circ=\{z:A^\top z\le\mathbf1\},\qquad C_\pm^\circ=\{z:\|A^\top z\|_\infty\le1\}.\] Equivalently, \[\gamma_{C_+}^{\circ}(z)=\max\{0,\max_i\langle z,a_i\rangle\},\qquad \gamma_{C_\pm}^{\circ}(z)=\max_i|\langle z,a_i\rangle|.\]
assumptions_latex: \(C_+\) and \(C_\pm\) are the one-sided and sign-symmetric atomic hulls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_+^\circ=\{z:A^\top z\le\mathbf1\}\) and \(C_\pm^\circ=\{z:\|A^\top z\|_\infty\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dictionary comparison of polar unit balls for the two coefficient regimes.

notation.meaning: One-sided and sign-symmetric atomic unit sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Symmetry Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided atoms require nonnegative coefficients and total mass, while sign-symmetric atoms permit signed coefficients and charge their ℓ1 mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the one-sided hull \(C_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_m\})\), coefficients are constrained by sign and \[\gamma_+(x)=\inf\{\mathbf1^\top\lambda:A\lambda=x,\ \lambda\geq0\}.\] For the sign-symmetric hull \(C_\pm=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a_1,\ldots,\pm a_m\}\), coefficient signs are free and \[\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\}.\] Equivalently, \(\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf_{x=u-v}\bigl(\gamma_+(u)+\gamma_+(v)\bigr)\), with extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_+(x)=\inf_{A\lambda=x,\lambda\geq0}\mathbf1^\top\lambda\) whereas \(\gamma_\pm(x)=\inf_{Ac=x}\|c\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of one-sided and sign-symmetric finite-dictionary coefficient models.

children.title: Atomic Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Decomposition interfaces between atoms and gauge values.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Certificate for an Optimal Atomic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polar-feasible vector lower-bounds atomic mass; equality with the mass of a feasible decomposition certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). If \(x=\sum_i c_i a_i\), where \(c_i\ge0\) and \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(z\) satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\le1\), then \[\langle z,x\rangle\le\gamma_C(x)\le\sum_i c_i.\] Hence the decomposition is gauge-optimal whenever \(\langle z,x\rangle=\sum_i c_i\).
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_i c_i a_i\) is a finite nonnegative atomic decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle z,x\rangle\le\gamma_C(x)\le\sum_i c_i\), with equality certifying optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality lower bounds and equality certificates for atomic coefficient mass.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment of Atomic Mass over Compact Dictionaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact finite-dimensional dictionary, every finite atomic-gauge value has an attaining decomposition using at most d+1 atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) have dimension \(d<\infty\), let \(\mathcal A\subset X\) be nonempty and compact, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). If \(\gamma_C(x)<+\infty\), then there are \(r\le d+1\), atoms \(a_j\in\mathcal A\), and coefficients \(c_j\ge0\) such that \[x=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j a_j,\qquad \gamma_C(x)=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal decomposition exists and can use at most \(d+1\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact atomic sets; extended-valued gauges are allowed.

notation.meaning: Gauge of the atomic unit set.

knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory Support Bound for Atomic Decompositions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible finite-dimensional atomic decomposition can be replaced by one using at most d+1 atoms with the same mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\dim X=d<\infty\) and suppose \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i,\qquad c_i\ge0,\quad a_i\in\mathcal A.\] There exist \(r\le d+1\), atoms \(b_j\in\mathcal A\), and \(\lambda_j\ge0\) such that \[x=\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j b_j,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i.\] Thus restricting to at most \(d+1\) atoms does not change the atomic-mass infimum.
assumptions_latex: A finite nonnegative atomic decomposition of \(x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A decomposition with at most \(d+1\) atoms and the same total mass exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sparsification of feasible decompositions; no attainment claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connects atomic gauge values with minimum-mass finite decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\), and assume \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\). Then every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) has an optimal finite atomic decomposition, and \[\gamma_C(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i:m\le d+1,\ \theta_i\ge0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A,\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i a_i\right\}.\] Hence any feasible decomposition gives the upper bound \(\gamma_C(x)\le\sum_i\theta_i\), while equality certifies that its total coefficient mass realizes the gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact absorbing atomic hull, the gauge is the minimum total nonnegative coefficient mass, attained using at most dimension plus one atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)\) equals the attained minimum atomic coefficient mass, with at most \(d+1\) active atoms.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\), and let \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}\) be the gauge of \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\). Fix \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\gamma_{\mathcal A}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic sums in a finite-dimensional space; both exact minimizing decompositions and nonattained infima are covered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An atomic decomposition of \(x\) is a finite family \((c_i,a_i)_{i=1}^m\) satisfying \(c_i\ge0\), \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\). Its cost is \(\sum_i c_i\). It is gauge-attaining when \[\sum_{i=1}^m c_i=\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x).\] For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), it is an \(\varepsilon\)-atomic decomposition when \[\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\le\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)+\varepsilon.\] In the symmetric regime, the same object may be written \(x=\sum_i\alpha_i a_i\) with cost \(\sum_i|\alpha_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atomic decomposition represents a point as a finite nonnegative combination of atoms and measures its quality by total coefficient weight. A decomposition is exact for the gauge when that weight equals the atomic gauge value. Approximate decompositions allow an additive tolerance. For a symmetric atom set, signed coefficients and their absolute-value sum give the equivalent representation.
assumptions_latex: Each decomposition uses finitely many atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition cost upper-bounds \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\), with equality precisely for a gauge-attaining decomposition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(x\ne0\), a gauge-attaining decomposition is equivalent to a convex representation \(x/\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\) with \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), after allowing the origin when necessary.
special_cases_latex: For coordinate atoms \(\{\pm e_i\}\), the canonical decomposition has cost \(\sum_i|x_i|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the infimum is not attained, then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) an \(\varepsilon\)-atomic decomposition exists whenever the unclosed finite-decomposition value equals the gauge value.
boundary_notes: Closure of the atomic hull can produce points whose gauge value is approached only by a sequence of decompositions.
Decompositions need not be unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Atomic Polar Evaluation and Maximizing-Atom Oracle
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional, let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\) be nonempty, let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\), and let \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support optimization for finite-dimensional atomic gauges; the maximizing atom may fail to exist for noncompact atom sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The atomic polar-oracle interface is the support-optimization identity \[\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)=\sigma_C(y)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A\cup\{0\}}\langle y,a\rangle,\qquad y\in X^*.\] An exact maximizing-atom oracle is a map \(\mathcal O:X^*\rightrightarrows\mathcal A\cup\{0\}\) with \[\mathcal O(y)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in\mathcal A\cup\{0\}}\langle y,a\rangle.\] An \(\varepsilon\)-oracle returns \(a_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(\langle y,a_\varepsilon\rangle\ge\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of an atomic gauge is evaluated by maximizing the dual pairing over the atoms. An exact oracle returns a maximizing atom, while an approximate oracle returns an atom whose pairing is within \(\varepsilon\) of the polar value. Convexifying the atom set does not alter this support value.
assumptions_latex: For an exact nonempty oracle value, the support supremum must be attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A\cup\{0\}}\langle y,a\rangle\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)\le1\iff \langle y,a\rangle\le1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
special_cases_latex: For a symmetric atom set, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(y)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|\langle y,a\rangle|\) when \(\mathcal A\) is listed without duplicated signs.
For a finite dictionary, the supremum is a finite maximum.
immediate_consequences_latex: A polar unit-ball membership test is equivalent to checking all atomic linear inequalities.
boundary_notes: An oracle for the polar value does not by itself provide an atomic decomposition of a primal point.
For noncompact atom sets, exact argmax sets may be empty even when the supremum is finite.

notation.meaning: Set of atoms maximizing the pairing with \(y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Halfspace Representation of the Polar Unit Ball
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar unit ball of an atomic hull is the intersection of atom-indexed halfspaces, or absolute-value slabs in the symmetric case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\) in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Then \[C^\circ=\{z:\langle z,a\rangle\le1\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A\}.\] If \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\), then \[C^\circ=\{z:|\langle z,a\rangle|\le1\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A\}.\]
assumptions_latex: The space is finite-dimensional with a fixed inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^\circ=\bigcap_{a\in\mathcal A}\{z:\langle z,a\rangle\le1\}\), with absolute inequalities when \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set representation corresponding to atomic polar-gauge evaluation.

notation.meaning: Polar of the closed convex atomic hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Polar-Gauge Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate an atomic polar gauge by maximizing the linear pairing over the atoms; use the absolute pairing when the atomic set is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z\in X\), define the polar gauge by
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sup\{\langle z,x\rangle:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}.
\]
Because the unit sublevel set of \(\gamma_C\) is \(C\),
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle z,x\rangle
=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle.
\]
If \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\), the same value is \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|\langle z,a\rangle|\). All suprema are understood in the extended real line.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-valued evaluation; the supremum need not be finite or attained.

notation.meaning: Gauge of the closed convex atomic hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Support Oracles
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support oracle returns an atom whose pairing with the query direction is within a declared additive tolerance of the atomic support value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z\in X\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), compute
\[
s_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle
\]
and return an atom \(a_\varepsilon\in\mathcal A\) satisfying
\[
\langle z,a_\varepsilon\rangle\ge s_{\mathcal A}(z)-\varepsilon.
\]
If no such atom exists, the oracle reports nonattainment at the requested tolerance. For \(\varepsilon=0\), a successful output is an exact support point. The oracle output consists of the value \(\langle z,a_\varepsilon\rangle\), the atom \(a_\varepsilon\), and the declared tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(\mathcal A\subset X\) is nonempty, and \(z\in X\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_\varepsilon\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(\langle z,a_\varepsilon\rangle\ge\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error linear maximization oracle, with exact evaluation when \(\varepsilon=0\).
review_flags: The supplied source supports support points and functions; the approximate-oracle convention is locally specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar–Support Oracle Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic polar evaluation and atomic linear optimization have the same value, and an atom satisfies the exact or approximate oracle criterion exactly when its pairing satisfies the corresponding polar-value test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(z\in X\),
\[
\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)=\sigma_C(z)=\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle.
\]
Consequently, polar-gauge evaluation and atomic linear optimization have the same value. An atom \(a\in\mathcal A\) is an exact oracle output precisely when \(\langle z,a\rangle=\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)\). For \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), it is additive-\(\varepsilon\) optimal precisely when \(\langle z,a\rangle\ge\gamma_C^{\circ}(z)-\varepsilon\). This equivalence concerns values and atomic-output tests; it does not assert that every optimizer over \(C\) is an atom.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) contains \(0\), where \(\mathcal A\subset X\) is nonempty.
\(z\in X\), and \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness Does Not Ensure Support Attainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex atomic set can have a finite but unattained support value; closedness alone cannot replace compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\mathcal A=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge e^u\},\qquad z=(0,-1).\] Then \(\mathcal A\) is closed and convex and \[\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{(u,v)\in\mathcal A}(-v)=0,\] but every \((u,v)\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(-v<0\). Thus the finite support value is not attained despite closedness and convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=0\) and \(\operatorname{argmax}_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed convex unbounded atomic set with a finite unattained support value.

notation.meaning: Support function of the atomic set.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Attainment Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, compact atomic sets have finite attained support values. Noncompact sets can have a finite unattained supremum, and unbounded sets can have infinite support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\mathcal A\) is compact, then for every \(z\in X\), the value \(\sigma_{\mathcal A}(z)=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\) is finite and is attained by some \(a^\star\in\mathcal A\). Compactness cannot simply be discarded: for \(X=\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal A=(0,1)\), and \(z=1\),
\[
\sigma_{\mathcal A}(1)=1,
\]
but no atom attains this value. Unboundedness creates a second boundary: for \(\mathcal A=[0,\infty)\) and \(z=1\), the support value is \(+\infty\). Hence an exact atomic oracle may fail through either finite nonattainment or an infinite objective.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(\mathcal A\subset X\) is nonempty, and support values are taken in the extended real line.
An exact atomic oracle must return an atom attaining the support value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal A\) is compact, every support value is finite and attained; without compactness, finite nonattainment or infinite support can occur.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distinction among compact attainment, finite nonattainment, and infinite support.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq X\) be a symmetric atom set encoding elementary sparse components. Let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\) be its atomic norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex sparse recovery; coordinate and grouped atoms are included, while continuous-measure atoms are treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse recovery gauge model is \[\inf_{x\in X}\{\|x\|_{\mathcal A}:\rho(b-Ax)\le\sigma\},\] where \(\rho\) is a residual gauge and \(\sigma\ge0\). Equivalently, using atomic coefficients, it minimizes total absolute atomic weight among decompositions \(x=\sum_i\alpha_i a_i\) whose synthesized signal satisfies the fidelity constraint. The penalized form is \[\inf_x\{L(Ax,b)+\lambda\|x\|_{\mathcal A}\},\qquad\lambda\ge0,\] for a proper convex data-fit function \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse recovery is modeled by choosing atoms that represent individual allowable components and minimizing the atomic norm subject to data fidelity, or adding it as a convex penalty. Coordinate atoms give ordinary \(\ell_1\) recovery, while block-supported atoms give group-sparse gauges.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\) and its convex hull is absorbing on the modeled subspace.
\(\rho\) is a residual gauge with \(\sigma\ge0\), or \(L\) is a proper convex loss with \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural objective equals the minimum total absolute coefficient weight over atomic representations compatible with the fidelity model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exact data, \(\rho=\delta_{\{0\}}\) gives \(\inf\{\|x\|_{\mathcal A}:Ax=b\}\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\mathcal A=\{\pm e_i\}\), the exact model is basis pursuit \(\inf\{\|x\|_1:Ax=b\}\).
With atoms supported on prescribed groups and Euclidean-normalized within each group, the gauge is a group-sparsity norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The polar structural cost is the largest correlation of a dual vector with any sparse atom.
boundary_notes: The definition specifies a convex surrogate and does not assert recovery of the sparsest feasible representation.
Nonconvex \(\ell_0\) minimization is outside this gauge family.

notation.meaning: Symmetric atomic gauge generated by \(\mathcal A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Coordinate Atomic Gauges
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling signed coordinate atoms gives the weighted one-norm and its reciprocal-weight infinity polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w_i>0\), let
\[
\mathcal A_w=\{\pm w_i^{-1}e_i:1\leq i\leq n\}.
\]
Then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^nw_i|x_i|,
\qquad
\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}^{\circ}(z)=\max_i\frac{|z_i|}{w_i}.
\]
Zero weights make the normalized atoms undefined, and signed weights do not define this positive weighted-norm convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}(x)=\sum_iw_i|x_i|\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_w}^{\circ}(z)=\max_i|z_i|/w_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coordinate sparsity with strictly positive weights.
review_flags: Strict positivity is required for the stated normalization and norm interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Envelope of Coordinate Cardinality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the infinity-norm unit cube, the one-norm is exactly the convex envelope of coordinate cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\|x\|_0=|\{i:x_i\neq0\}|\). On
\[
B_\infty=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_\infty\leq1\},
\]
the greatest convex function bounded above by \(\|x\|_0\) is
\[
\operatorname{conv}_{B_\infty}(\|\cdot\|_0)(x)=\|x\|_1.
\]
Thus the signed-coordinate atomic gauge is the convex envelope of cardinality under \(|x_i|\leq1\). Without an amplitude-bounded domain, \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is not the global convex envelope of scale-invariant cardinality.
assumptions_latex: The convex envelope is taken relative to \(B_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}_{B_\infty}(\|\cdot\|_0)=\|\cdot\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate vectors restricted to the infinity-norm unit cube.
review_flags: The amplitude-bounded domain is essential and must accompany the convex-envelope claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Sparsity Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coordinate atomic gauge and its polar norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive weights \(w_i\), define the coordinate atomic set \(\mathcal A_w=\{\pm e_i/w_i:1\leq i\leq n\}\). Its closed convex hull has gauge \[\gamma_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i|x_i|.\] Thus the gauge is the weighted \(\ell_1\) norm, whose unit ball promotes representations using few coordinate atoms. Its polar gauge is \[\gamma_w^{\circ}(z)=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\frac{|z_i|}{w_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate atoms generate the weighted l1 gauge; its polar is the correspondingly weighted maximum norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_w(x)=\sum_iw_i|x_i|\) and \(\gamma_w^{\circ}(z)=\max_i|z_i|/w_i\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite collection of nonempty subsets of \(I\) whose union is \(I\), and let \(p\in[1,+\infty)\). For each \(G\in\mathcal G\), let \(X_G=\{z\in\mathbb R^N:\operatorname{supp}z\subseteq G\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional grouped and overlapping-group sparsity; this is the latent decomposition gauge, which differs from directly summing norms of overlapping subvectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The latent group structured-sparsity gauge is \[\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}w_G\|z_G\|_p:z_G\in X_G,\ \sum_{G\in\mathcal G}z_G=x\right\},\] where \(w_G>0\) are prescribed group weights. Its unit set is the convex hull of the weighted group atoms \[\mathcal A=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\{z\in X_G:w_G\|z\|_p\le1\}.\] Thus \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}\) is an atomic gauge whose decompositions allocate the signal among allowed support groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge decomposes a vector into components supported on prescribed groups and charges the weighted sum of their within-group norms. Overlapping groups are handled by optimizing the allocation of shared coordinates. The same functional is the atomic gauge of the union of the weighted group unit balls.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is finite, each group is nonempty, and \(\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}G=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}=\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)}\), with \(\mathcal A\) equal to the union of weighted group unit balls.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(L((z_G)_G)=\sum_Gz_G\) and \(f((z_G)_G)=\sum_Gw_G\|z_G\|_p\), one has \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}=L\mathbin{\triangleright}f\), the infimal postcomposition.
special_cases_latex: If the groups form a partition and \(w_G=1\), then \(\Omega_{\mathcal G,p}(x)=\sum_G\|x_G\|_p\).
Singleton groups with \(p=1\) recover the \(\ell_1\) norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: The gauge promotes representations using few active groups because inactive components have \(z_G=0\).
boundary_notes: For overlapping groups, this latent gauge generally differs from \(\sum_Gw_G\|x_G\|_p\), which counts shared coordinates repeatedly.
The group family and weights are model inputs, not inferred by the definition.

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition of \(f\) by the synthesis map \(L\).

knowledge_statements.title: Block Soft-Thresholding Proximal Map
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map independently shrinks each block radially and deletes blocks below their weighted thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda\ge0\),
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Omega}(x)\bigr)_g=
\begin{cases}
\left(1-\dfrac{\lambda w_g}{\|x_g\|_2}\right)_+x_g,&x_g\ne0,\\
0,&x_g=0.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map is block soft-thresholding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal map for the nonoverlapping weighted group gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential of the Weighted Group Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subgradient is the weighted unit direction on active blocks and belongs to the corresponding weighted Euclidean ball on inactive blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\Omega(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2\), one has \(z\in\partial\Omega(x)\) exactly when
\[
z_g=w_g\frac{x_g}{\|x_g\|_2}\quad(x_g\ne0),
\qquad \|z_g\|_2\le w_g\quad(x_g=0)
\]
for every group \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed blockwise conditions characterize \(\partial\Omega(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonoverlapping positive-weight Euclidean groups.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonoverlapping weighted group gauge and its polar norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define the weighted group-sparsity gauge by
\[
\Omega(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.
\]
Because the groups form a partition and all weights are positive, \(\Omega\) is a norm. Its polar norm is
\[
\Omega^{\circ}(z)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|z_g\|_2}{w_g}.
\]
The gauge aggregates group magnitudes with an outer one-norm, whereas its polar tests the largest weight-normalized group magnitude. Singleton groups with unit weights recover the coordinate one-norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted sum of Euclidean block norms is a group-sparsity norm; its polar is the largest weight-normalized block norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Latent-Decomposition Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent allocation is optimal exactly when one polar-feasible vector simultaneously supports every nonzero group component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=\sum_gv^g\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(v^g)\subseteq g\). This decomposition attains \(\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)=\sum_gw_g\|v^g\|_2\) if and only if there exists \(z\) such that
\[
\|z_g\|_2\le w_g\quad\forall g,
\qquad z_g=w_g\frac{v^g}{\|v^g\|_2}\quad\text{whenever }v^g\ne0.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is finite, covers all coordinates, and \(w_g>0\).
The proposed group-supported components sum to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition is gauge-minimizing exactly when the common supporting vector exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for a proposed decomposition attaining the latent overlapping-group gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Overlapping-Group Gauge and Polar
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct overlap convention repeatedly charges shared coordinates, and its polar uses a dual decomposition rather than a maximum of group restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite covering family \(\mathcal G\), define
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{dir}}(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.
\]
Its polar norm is
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{dir}}^\circ(z)=\inf\left\{t\ge0:z=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}z^g,\ \operatorname{supp}(z^g)\subseteq g,\ \|z^g\|_2\le tw_g\ \forall g\right\}.
\]
Unlike the latent gauge, a coordinate contributes directly to every containing group.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a finite family of nonempty groups covering all coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed infimal decomposition is the polar of \(\Omega_{\mathrm{dir}}\).

\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)=
\inf\left\{\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|v^g\|_2:
 x=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}v^g,
\ \\operatorname{supp}(v^g)\subseteq g\right\}.
\]
The covering and positivity assumptions make this a norm, and its polar is
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}^{\circ}(z)=
\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|z_g\|_2}{w_g}.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Pass Proximal Map for Laminar Euclidean Groups
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For laminar Euclidean groups, processing group soft-thresholding from smaller descendant sets to larger ones computes the exact proximal map in one tree pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Order the descendant groups so that \(D(u)\subsetneq D(v)\) implies that \(u\) is processed before \(v\). Starting from \(q=x\), replace successively
\[
q_{D(v)}\leftarrow\left(1-\frac{\lambda w_v}{\|q_{D(v)}\|_2}\right)_+q_{D(v)}.
\]
After every vertex has been processed once, the resulting vector is \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Omega_T}(x)\).
assumptions_latex: The descendant groups form a finite laminar family.
The within-group norm is Euclidean and \(w_v>0\).
Groups are processed in an inclusion-compatible order from descendants toward ancestors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordered composition of group soft-thresholding maps equals \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Omega_T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation for the direct descendant-group norm on a finite tree.

notation.meaning: Current vector during the tree pass.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Representation for the Descendant-Group Norm
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar norm decomposes a dual vector among descendant groups under a common normalized radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\Omega_T(x)=\sum_{v\in V}w_v\|x_{D(v)}\|_2\),
\[
\Omega_T^\circ(z)=\inf\left\{t\ge0:z=\sum_{v\in V}z^v,\ \operatorname{supp}(z^v)\subseteq D(v),\ \|z^v\|_2\le tw_v\ \forall v\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, its polar unit ball is the Minkowski sum of the embedded descendant-group Euclidean balls of radii \(w_v\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed infimal decomposition equals \(\Omega_T^\circ(z)\).

\(D(v)\) is the set of descendant leaves of \(v\), and \(w_v>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define

\Omega_T(x)=\sum_{v\in V}w_v\|x_{D(v)}\|_2.

Since the descendant sets of leaves cover all coordinates and all weights are positive, \(\Omega_T\) is a norm. knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Support Gauges
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying Euclidean atoms supported on admissible combinatorial models yields a latent decomposition gauge whose polar selects the largest admissible restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathcal M}=
\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal M}\{a\in\mathbb R^n:
\operatorname{supp}(a)\subseteq S,\ \|a\|_2\le1\}.
\]
The gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_{\mathcal M})\) has the decomposition representation
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal M}(x)=
\inf\left\{\sum_{S\in\mathcal M}\|v^S\|_2:
 x=\sum_{S\in\mathcal M}v^S,
\ \\operatorname{supp}(v^S)\subseteq S\right\}.
\]
Its polar is
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal M}^{\circ}(z)=\max_{S\in\mathcal M}\|z_S\|_2.
\]
Thus the chosen support family determines both the allowed atomic components and the polar search domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a nonempty finite family of nonempty subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) whose union is all coordinates.

children.title: Off-Grid Sparse-Measure Gauges
children.top_down_role: Continuous-dictionary sparse recovery models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a compact Hausdorff parameter space, let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(a:\Theta\to X\) be continuous. Let \(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) be the finite signed Radon measures on \(\Theta\), with total-variation norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), and define \(\Phi\mu=\int_\Theta a(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-dictionary sparse recovery through finite signed measures on a compact parameter space; discretized grids are not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The off-grid sparse-measure gauge on \(\operatorname{range}\Phi\) is \[\gamma_{a}(x)=\inf\{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta),\ \Phi\mu=x\}.\] It is the atomic gauge generated by \(\mathcal A=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\). An off-grid recovery model therefore has the form \[\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta)}\{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:\rho(b-A\Phi\mu)\le\sigma\}.\] For an atomic measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^mc_i\delta_{\theta_i}\), its cost is \(\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\sum_i|c_i|\) after combining repeated locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous parameter space supplies atoms without choosing a finite grid. A signed measure records atom locations and amplitudes, the synthesis map integrates the atom map against that measure, and total variation measures coefficient mass. Minimizing total variation subject to data fidelity is therefore the continuous-dictionary counterpart of finite-dimensional \(\ell_1\) recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact Hausdorff and \(a:\Theta\to X\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) consists of finite signed Radon measures.
\(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(\rho\) is a residual gauge, and \(\sigma\ge0\) for the recovery model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_a(x)=\inf_{\Phi\mu=x}\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\gamma_{\operatorname{conv}\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}}(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The polar gauge is \(\gamma_a^\circ(y)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|\langle y,a(\theta)\rangle|\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Theta\) is finite, measures reduce to coefficient vectors and total variation reduces to the \(\ell_1\) norm.
A finitely supported measure represents a sparse off-grid superposition \(\sum_i c_i a(\theta_i)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Atom locations range over all of \(\Theta\), so the model does not impose quantization to a predetermined grid.
boundary_notes: Existence or uniqueness of a sparsest representing measure is not asserted.
For complex measures the symmetric atom set must include all unit-modulus phases; that variant is outside this real formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar of the Total-Variation Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar norm of total variation is the uniform norm on continuous test functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) be locally compact Hausdorff and pair \(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) with \(C_0(\Theta)\) by integration. Then
\[
\sup_{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1}\left|\int_\Theta f\,d\mu\right|=\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|f(\theta)|.
\]
The equality does not require the pointwise supremum to be attained.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) and \(C_0(\Theta)\) are paired by integration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^\circ=\|\cdot\|_\infty\) under the stated dual pairing.

standard_field_rationale: total variation is the atomic norm generated by signed Dirac measures.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real signed Radon measures; positive-measure mass gauges and complex phases require separate conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta)\), define the sparse-measure gauge by
\[
\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|\mu|(\Theta),
\]
where \(|\mu|\) is the variation measure. Its unit ball is the closed convex hull, in the natural weak-star topology, of the signed Dirac atoms \(\{\pm\delta_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\). In particular, if
\[
\mu=\sum_{j=1}^{k}c_j\delta_{\theta_j}
\]
with distinct \(\theta_j\), then \(\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\sum_{j=1}^{k}|c_j|\). Hence finite atomic measures are charged by total coefficient mass without imposing a parameter grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total-variation norm is the atomic gauge generated by signed Dirac measures and equals coefficient mass for finitely supported measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Off-Grid Conditional-Gradient Oracle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Off-grid Frank-Wolfe uses a global continuous maximum-correlation search and adds at most one atom per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{y\in\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)}f(y),\qquad
\mathcal A=\{\pm\phi(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}.
\]
At \(y_k\), choose
\[
\theta_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\theta\in\Theta}|\langle\nabla f(y_k),\phi(\theta)\rangle|
\]
and a sign minimizing the gradient pairing, obtaining \(s_k\in\tau\mathcal A\). Then
\[
y_{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)y_k+\eta_ks_k
\]
remains feasible and adds at most one continuously located signed atom.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A maximum-absolute-correlation signed atom solves the Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth convex minimization over a bounded continuous atomic ball.

notation.meaning: Selected signed atom scaled by tau

review_flags: When all correlations vanish, any feasible minimizer of the linear oracle, including zero, is valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Polar-Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous polar correlation gives a Frank-Wolfe gap certifying objective suboptimality, whereas an uncorrected grid maximum does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible \(y\in\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), define
\[
g(y)=\langle\nabla f(y),y\rangle+\tau\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(-\nabla f(y)).
\]
Then
\[
0\leq f(y)-f^*\leq g(y).
\]
Thus \(g(y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. The certificate is rigorous only when the continuous supremum is evaluated globally or bounded above rigorously; a grid maximum alone can underestimate the gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-f^*\leq\langle\nabla f(y),y\rangle+\tau\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(-\nabla f(y))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori Frank-Wolfe certificate using the global continuous-dictionary polar oracle.
review_flags: A lower estimate of the polar supremum is insufficient for a rigorous stopping certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Gradient Rate with an Exact Off-Grid Oracle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact off-grid Frank-Wolfe has the standard O(1/k) objective bound and a linear support-size bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_f<\infty\) be the Frank-Wolfe curvature of \(f\) on \(\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). If every continuous linear-minimization subproblem is solved exactly and \(\eta_k=2/(k+2)\), then
\[
f(y_k)-f^*\leq\frac{2C_f}{k+2}.
\]
After \(k\) updates, \(y_k\) is a convex combination of at most \(k+1\) selected signed atoms. Approximate atom searches require an explicit oracle-error term; the displayed bound cannot otherwise be asserted.
assumptions_latex: The continuous linear-minimization oracle is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y_k)-f^*\leq2C_f/(k+2)\), with at most \(k+1\) selected atoms after \(k\) updates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous linear minimization and finite Frank-Wolfe curvature.
review_flags: The iteration count does not include the potentially nontrivial cost of globally solving the continuous parameter oracle.

assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact and \(\phi:\Theta\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(y)=\inf_{\Phi\mu=y}\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(z)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|\langle z,\phi(\theta)\rangle|\).

standard_field_rationale: continuous symmetric dictionaries yield total-variation synthesis representations and supremum polar formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric real continuous dictionaries on compact parameter spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal M(\Theta)\) denote the finite signed Radon measures on \(\Theta\). For \(\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta)\), define the synthesis map by
\[
\Phi\mu=\int_{\Theta}\phi(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta).
\]
The gauge generated by the continuous symmetric dictionary satisfies
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(y)=\inf\{\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}:\mu\in\mathcal M(\Theta),\ \Phi\mu=y\}.
\]
For every \(z\in\mathbb R^m\), its polar gauge is
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(z)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|\langle z,\phi(\theta)\rangle|.
\]
Compactness and continuity ensure that this polar supremum is attained. The representation optimizes directly over the continuous parameter space rather than over a discretized dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An off-grid atomic gauge minimizes measure total variation under continuous-dictionary synthesis; its polar maximizes absolute correlation over the full parameter space, with attainment under compactness and continuity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For feasible \(y\in\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), define
\[
g(y)=\langle\nabla f(y),y\rangle+	au\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(-\nabla f(y)).
\]
Then
\[
0\leq f(y)-f^*\leq g(y).
\]
Hence \(g(y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. The certificate is rigorous only when the supremum defining \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(-\nabla f(y))\) is globally evaluated or enclosed by a valid upper bound; a grid maximum alone can underestimate the gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous-parameter linear minimization and finite Frank-Wolfe curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_f<\infty\) be the Frank-Wolfe curvature of \(f\) on \(\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). If each continuous maximum-correlation subproblem is solved exactly and \(\eta_k=2/(k+2)\), then the iterates satisfy
\[
f(y_k)-f^*\leq\frac{2C_f}{k+2}.
\]
After \(k\) updates, \(y_k\) is a convex combination of at most \(k+1\) continuously located signed atoms. The rate need not hold with the same constant when the atom search is only approximate unless its oracle error is explicitly controlled.

Exposed Faces of a Continuous Atomic Ball
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vector exposes the convex hull of exactly those signed dictionary atoms attaining maximum correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z\neq0\), let
\[
M(z)=\{s a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta,\ s\in\{-1,1\},\ \langle z,s a(\theta)\rangle=\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(z)\}.
\]
The face of \(B_{\mathcal A}=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) exposed by \(z\) is
\[
F_z=\operatorname{conv}M(z).
\]
If \(x/\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\in F_z\), every atom carrying positive mass in any optimal signed representation of \(x\) belongs to \(M(z)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact and \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_z=\operatorname{conv}M(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact symmetric continuous dictionaries in finite dimensions.
review_flags: The representation statement concerns optimal mass decompositions; arbitrary nonoptimal decompositions need not use only maximizing atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Attainment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every signal has an optimal continuous-dictionary representation supported on at most n parameter values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and suppose \(\mathcal A=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\) spans \(\mathbb R^n\). For every nonzero \(x\), the minimum-total-variation representation defining \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\) is attained by
\[
\mu=\sum_{j=1}^s c_j\delta_{\theta_j},\qquad s\leq n,
\]
so that
\[
x=\sum_{j=1}^s c_ja(\theta_j),\qquad
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\sum_{j=1}^s|c_j|.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal representing measure exists with support cardinality at most \(n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact continuous symmetric dictionaries spanning a finite-dimensional signal space.
review_flags: The bound n uses the supporting face containing the normalized boundary point; a direct ambient Caratheodory bound would be n+1.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Dictionary Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous, centrally symmetric atomic dictionaries in finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be a compact Hausdorff space and let \(a:T\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous. Define \(\mathcal A=\{\pm a(t):t\in T\}\) and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). For \(x,z\in\mathbb R^n\), define the continuous-dictionary gauge and its polar by
\[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{\lambda\geq0:x\in\lambda C\},\qquad \gamma_C^\circ(z)=\sup_{u\in C}\langle z,u\rangle=\sup_{t\in T}|\langle z,a(t)\rangle|.\]
The gauge is finite on \(\operatorname{span}\mathcal A\), is infinite outside that span, and its unit ball relative to \(\operatorname{span}\mathcal A\) is \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact continuous dictionary generates an atomic gauge whose polar is the largest absolute correlation with any continuously indexed atom.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is compact Hausdorff and \(a:T\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous.
The dictionary is symmetrized as \(\mathcal A=\{\pm a(t):t\in T\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C^\circ(z)=\sup_{t\in T}|\langle z,a(t)\rangle|\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the symmetric continuous dictionary.

x=\sum_{j=1}^s c_ja(\theta_j),\qquad

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Attainment for Continuous Atomic Gauges
Dense-Grid Recovery of the Continuous Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested dense grids recover an absorbing compact continuous atomic gauge monotonically from above.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and let finite grids \(G_k\subseteq G_{k+1}\subseteq\Theta\) have dense union. Define
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in G_k\},\qquad
\mathcal A=\{\pm a(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}.
\]
If \(0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_k}(x)\downarrow\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)
\]
for every \(x\), uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\). The interior assumption ensures eventual absorption by the grid hulls and finiteness in every direction.
assumptions_latex: Each \(G_k\) is finite, the grids are nested, and their union is dense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_k}\downarrow\gamma_{\mathcal A}\) pointwise and uniformly on compact sets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested finite grids for a compact continuous dictionary with an absorbing atomic hull.
review_flags: No universal convergence rate follows without quantitative regularity and grid-coverage assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicative Grid-Approximation Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grid has a uniform multiplicative gauge guarantee when its hull contains a fixed positive scaling of the continuous atomic ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_G\subseteq B\) be closed convex origin-containing sets and suppose
\[
\rho B\subseteq B_G
\]
for some \(0<\rho\leq1\). Then
\[
\gamma_B(x)\leq\gamma_{B_G}(x)\leq\rho^{-1}\gamma_B(x)
\]
for every \(x\), while
\[
\rho\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)\leq\gamma_{B_G}^{\circ}(z)\leq\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)
\]
for every \(z\). Without a positive inclusion factor, grid density alone gives no uniform relative gauge bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_B\leq\gamma_{B_G}\leq\rho^{-1}\gamma_B\), with the corresponding polar sandwich.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of an absorbing continuous atomic ball with an inner grid approximation.
review_flags: The containment condition is sufficient and, with the best possible rho, exactly encodes the uniform multiplicative comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Dual Bias under Grid Restriction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grid restriction can only increase the primal gauge and decrease the polar maximum correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\mathcal A_G\subseteq\mathcal A\), then
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_G}(x)\geq\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x),
\]
with the left side possibly \(+\infty\), and
\[
\gamma_{�mathcal A_G}^{\circ}(z)
=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A_G}\langle z,a\rangle
\leq\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle
=\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}(z).
\]
Thus grid restriction inflates the primal gauge and underestimates the polar oracle; either inequality can be strict.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_G\subseteq\mathcal A\) are symmetric atomic sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_G}\geq\gamma_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_G}^{\circ}\leq\gamma_{\mathcal A}^{\circ}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted subdictionaries of continuous symmetric atomic dictionaries.
review_flags: Strictness and nonrepresentability are instantiated by the immutable moment-curve seed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact replacement of a curved continuous dictionary by a finite grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(t_0\in\Theta\setminus G\) and set \(x=a(t_0)\). Then \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=1\). Every point \(a(t)\) on the moment curve is an extreme point of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\); hence \(a(t_0)\notin\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_G)\). Consequently
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_G}(x)>1,
\]
with the convention \(\gamma_{\mathcal A_G}(x)=+\infty\) when \(x\notin\operatorname{span}(\mathcal A_G)\). Thus a finite grid need not preserve either the continuous atomic unit ball or its gauge values.
