knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplicative Approximation Criterion for a Discretized Atomic Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative comparison of an absorbing continuous atomic ball and an inner grid approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
B=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A),\qquad B_G=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_G),
\]
with \(B_G\subseteq B\), and suppose that for some \(0<\rho\leq1\),
\[
\rho B\subseteq B_G.
\]
Then for every \(x\),
\[
\gamma_B(x)\leq\gamma_{B_G}(x)\leq\rho^{-1}\gamma_B(x),
\]
and for every \(z\),
\[
\rho\,\gamma_B^{\circ}(z)
\leq\gamma_{B_G}^{\circ}(z)
\leq\gamma_B^{\circ}(z).
\]
Without a positive inclusion factor \(\rho\), grid density alone supplies no uniform relative-error bound for the gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Signed Nullspace Criterion for Basis Pursuit
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique basis-pursuit recovery is equivalent to strict domination of the signed active-support variation by the off-support one-norm along every nonzero nullspace direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{supp}(x_0)\). The vector \(x_0\) is the unique minimizer of \(\min_x\|x\|_1\) subject to \(Ax=Ax_0\) if and only if every \(0\ne h\in\ker A\) satisfies
\[

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Recovery Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact uniqueness certificate for finite-dimensional basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(x_\star\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(Ax_\star=b\). Define \(S=\{i:(x_\star)_i\neq0\}\). If \(A_S\) has full column rank and there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying
\[A_S^{\mathsf T}y=\operatorname{sign}(x_{\star,S}),\qquad \|A_{S^c}^{\mathsf T}y\|_\infty<1,\]
then \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in\partial\|x_\star\|_1\), with strict inequality in the subgradient coordinates outside \(S\). These conditions certify that \(x_\star\) is the unique minimizer of \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{\|x\|_1:Ax=b\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Certificate for Basis-Pursuit Sparse Recovery
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(x^\star\) satisfy \(Ax^\star=b\). Write \(S=\{i:x_i^\star\ne0\}\), and let \(A^*\) denote the adjoint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real basis pursuit with the coordinate sparsity gauge \(\|\cdot\|_1\); the definition concerns exact certificates, not noisy or approximate recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is a sparse-recovery dual certificate for \(x^\star\) if \(z=A^*y\) belongs to \(\partial\|x^\star\|_1\), equivalently if \((A^*y)_S=\operatorname{sign}(x_S^\star)\) and \(\|(A^*y)_{S^c}\|_\infty\le1\). It is a strict certificate when \(\|(A^*y)_{S^c}\|_\infty<1\). Thus the certificate is simultaneously dual-feasible for the polar gauge and supporting at \(x^\star\): \(\|A^*y\|_\infty\le1\) and \(\langle A^*y,x^\star\rangle=\|x^\star\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse-recovery dual certificate is a measurement-space vector whose adjoint image is an l1-subgradient at the proposed sparse solution. On the support it equals the coordinate signs, while off the support its absolute coordinates do not exceed one. A strict certificate has all off-support absolute coordinates strictly below one. Equivalently, the adjoint image is feasible for the polar l-infinity unit ball and exposes the l1 ball at the proposed solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\text{ is a certificate}\iff A^*y\in\partial\|x^\star\|_1\iff (A^*y)_S=\operatorname{sign}(x_S^\star),\ \|(A^*y)_{S^c}\|_\infty\le1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(A^*y\in\partial\|x^\star\|_1\iff \|A^*y\|_\infty\le1\ \text{and}\ \langle A^*y,x^\star\rangle=\|x^\star\|_1.\)
special_cases_latex: If \(x^\star=0\), the certificate condition reduces to \(\|A^*y\|_\infty\le1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A strict certificate together with \(\ker(A)\cap\{h:h_{S^c}=0\}=\{0\}\) is the standard nondegenerate certificate pattern used to establish uniqueness.
boundary_notes: The non-strict certificate definition alone does not assert uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\), let \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{m\times n}\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and write \(\sigma(X)=(\sigma_1(X),\ldots,\sigma_q(X))\) for the singular values in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional matrix models whose structural regularizer is a convex unitarily invariant gauge of the singular-value vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}_+^q\to[0,+\infty]\) be convex, positively homogeneous, lower semicontinuous, and invariant under coordinate permutations; when extended to \(\mathbb{R}^q\), assume invariance under sign changes. The associated spectral gauge is \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\). A low-rank spectral gauge model is an optimization model in which \(\kappa_\phi(X)\) is used as an objective, constraint, or level-set parameter to encode singular-value structure. Its unit ball is \(C_\phi=\{X:\phi(\sigma(X))\le1\}\), and its polar gauge is \(\kappa_\phi^\circ(Y)=\phi^\circ(\sigma(Y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank spectral gauge is obtained by applying a convex, positively homogeneous, permutation-invariant scalar gauge to the singular values of a matrix. The resulting matrix function is invariant under left and right unitary transformations. A low-rank spectral gauge model uses that function as a regularizer, constraint, or level-set parameter. Its unit ball consists exactly of matrices whose singular-value vectors lie in the scalar gauge ball, and its polar is obtained by applying the polar scalar gauge to the singular values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\phi(\sigma(X)),\qquad C_\phi=\{X:\kappa_\phi(X)\le1\},\qquad \kappa_\phi^\circ(Y)=\phi^\circ(\sigma(Y)).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\kappa_\phi(UXV^*)=\kappa_\phi(X)\) for all compatible unitary matrices \(U,V\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\phi(s)=\|s\|_1\), \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\|X\|_*\), the nuclear norm.
For \(\phi(s)=\|s\|_\infty\), \(\kappa_\phi(X)=\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The nuclear-norm unit ball is the closed convex hull of unit-norm rank-one matrix atoms.
boundary_notes: Not every spectral gauge promotes low rank; the nuclear norm is the canonical convex rank-one atomic gauge.
The definition does not include nonconvex rank penalties or Schatten quasi-norms with exponent below one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Atomic Gauge Generated by Rank-One Matrices
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E=\mathbb{F}^m\) and \(F=\mathbb{F}^n\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Let \(U\subset E\) and \(V\subset F\) be compact, balanced sets that span their respective spaces and contain no requirement of convexity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional balanced matrix gauges generated by outer products; asymmetric or positive-semidefinite-only atomic families are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the rank-one atomic set \(\mathcal A=\{uv^*:u\in U,\ v\in V\}\) and its closed convex hull \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). The associated rank-one matrix gauge is \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{t\ge0:X\in tC\}\). Equivalently, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{\sum_{j=1}^r c_j:X=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j u_jv_j^*,\ c_j\ge0,\ u_j\in U,\ v_j\in V,\ r\in\mathbb N\}\). Its polar gauge is \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(Y)=\sup_{u\in U,v\in V}|\langle Y,uv^*\rangle|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose balanced spanning sets of left and right factors and form every admissible rank-one outer product. The rank-one matrix gauge is the Minkowski functional of the closed convex hull of those atoms. It is also the smallest total nonnegative coefficient weight among all finite atomic decompositions of the matrix. The polar gauge is the largest absolute pairing of a dual matrix with an admissible rank-one atom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_{\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)},\qquad \gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(Y)=\sup_{u\in U,v\in V}|u^*Yv|.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(U\) and \(V\) are unit balls of gauges \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), then \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\inf\{\sum_j\alpha(u_j)\beta(v_j):X=\sum_j u_jv_j^*\}\).
special_cases_latex: With Euclidean unit spheres for \(U\) and \(V\), \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(X)=\|X\|_*\) and \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}^\circ(Y)=\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every atom \(a\in\mathcal A\) satisfies \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(a)\le1\).
boundary_notes: If the atomic family does not span the matrix space, the gauge may take value \(+\infty\).
Removing balance generally produces an asymmetric gauge and removes the absolute value from the support formula.

Nuclear-Norm Gauge Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear norm is the atomic gauge of unit rank-one matrices, and its dual gauge is the spectral operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A_1=\{uv^{\mathsf T}:\|u\|_2=\|v\|_2=1\}\). The gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_1)\) satisfies
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_1}(X)=\|X\|_*=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_i(X).
\]
Under the pairing \(\langle Y,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(Y^{\mathsf T}X)\), its polar gauge is
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A_1}^{\circ}(Y)=\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_1(Y).
\]
Thus the nuclear unit ball and operator-norm unit ball are polar to one another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nuclear norm is the gauge of the rank-one spectral atoms, and its polar gauge is the operator norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real rectangular matrices with the Frobenius pairing.

knowledge_statements.title: Hermitian Trace-Norm Convention
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Hermitian matrices the trace norm is the sum of absolute eigenvalues and equals the ordinary trace exactly in the PSD regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(H=H^*\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(H),\ldots,\lambda_n(H)\), then
\[
\|H\|_* = \sum_{i=1}^n|\lambda_i(H)|=\operatorname{tr}|H|.
\]
Consequently, \(\|H\|_*=\operatorname{tr}(H)\) if and only if \(H\succeq0\), while \(\|H\|_*=-\operatorname{tr}(H)\) if and only if \(H\preceq0\). In general \(|\operatorname{tr}(H)|\leq\|H\|_*\), with strict inequality possible through cancellation of positive and negative eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^*\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\), or \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) in the real case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|H\|_*=\sum_i|\lambda_i(H)|\), and \(\|H\|_*=\operatorname{tr}(H)\iff H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real symmetric or complex Hermitian matrices.
review_flags: Standard spectral-theorem specialization; ordinary trace must not be substituted outside the PSD regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Norm Gauge Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard trace-norm convention for rectangular, symmetric, and positive-semidefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the trace norm means the nuclear norm
\[\|X\|_{\mathrm{tr}}:=\|X\|_*:=\sum_{i=1}^{\min\{m,n\}}\sigma_i(X).\]
If \(X\) is real symmetric, then \(\|X\|_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_i|\lambda_i(X)|\). If additionally \(X\succeq0\), then \(\|X\|_{\mathrm{tr}}=\operatorname{tr}(X)\). Thus trace norm denotes the sum of singular values, not \(|\operatorname{tr}(X)|\) for a general matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace norm means the sum of singular values; it equals the ordinary trace only on the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\succeq0\Longrightarrow\|X\|_{\mathrm{tr}}=\operatorname{tr}(X)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Factorization Formula
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear atomic gauge equals the minimum balanced squared Frobenius mass of a rank-one factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(q\geq\operatorname{rank}(X)\),
\[
\|X\|_* = \min_{LR^{\mathsf T}=X}\frac12\bigl(\|L\|_F^2+\|R\|_F^2\bigr),
\]
where \(L\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\) and \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\). Equivalently,
\[
\|X\|_* = \min_{X=\sum_{j=1}^q a_jb_j^{\mathsf T}}\frac12\sum_{j=1}^q\bigl(\|a_j\|_2^2+\|b_j\|_2^2\bigr).
\]
The minima are attained; an SVD gives \(L=U\Sigma^{1/2}\), \(R=V\Sigma^{1/2}\), with zero columns appended if needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real matrices; factor width is at least the matrix rank.
review_flags: The factor-width condition is sharp for feasibility: no factorization exists when q is smaller than the rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Atomic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational representation of the nuclear norm by unit rank-one atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A=\{uv^{\mathsf T}:u\in\mathbb R^m,\ v\in\mathbb R^n,\ \|u\|_2=\|v\|_2=1\}\). For every \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\),
\[\|X\|_*=\inf\left\{\sum_{j=1}^k\theta_j:k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0},\ X=\sum_{j=1}^k\theta_j u_jv_j^{\mathsf T},\ \theta_j\geq0,\ \|u_j\|_2=\|v_j\|_2=1\right\}.\]
The infimum is attained by a singular-value decomposition with \(k=\operatorname{rank}(X)\), \(\theta_j=\sigma_j(X)\), and corresponding left and right singular vectors; when \(X=0\), this is the empty decomposition with \(k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear norm is the minimum total nonnegative weight in a finite decomposition into unit-norm rank-one atoms, with the empty decomposition used for the zero matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X\|_*\) equals the atomic gauge generated by \(\mathcal A\).

Rectangular Semidefinite Lift
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rectangular nuclear norm has an exact attained semidefinite lift with PSD blocks of sizes m and n.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\),
\[
\|X\|_* = \frac12\min_{W\in\mathbb S^m,\,Z\in\mathbb S^n}
\left\{\operatorname{tr}(W)+\operatorname{tr}(Z):
\begin{bmatrix}W&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&Z\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.
\]
The minimum is attained. If \(X=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a compact SVD, then \(W=U\Sigma U^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Z=V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) are optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|X\|_*\) equals one half of the minimum trace sum in the block-PSD lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Trace Gauges
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge generated by zero and the PSD rank-one atoms is trace on the PSD cone and infinity elsewhere; its polar is the positive part of the largest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_+=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A_+)\). Its Minkowski functional is the extended-valued gauge
\[
\gamma_+(X)=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{tr}(X),&X\succeq0,\\
+\infty,&X\not\succeq0.
\end{cases}
\]
Because \(B_+\) is not centrally symmetric, \(\gamma_+\) is a gauge but not a norm. Under the trace pairing, its polar gauge is
\[
\gamma_+^{\circ}(Y)=\sup_{X\in B_+}\operatorname{tr}(YX)=\max\left\{0,\sup_{\|u\|_2=1}u^{\mathsf T}Yu\right\}=\max\{0,\lambda_{\max}(Y)\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\), the space of real symmetric matrices.
\(\mathcal A_+=\{uu^{\mathsf T}:u\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \|u\|_2=1\}\), and \(\gamma_+\) is the Minkowski functional of \(\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A_+)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_+\) equals the trace on the positive-semidefinite cone and is infinite outside it, while its polar gauge is \(\max\{0,\lambda_{\max}(Y)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided gauge on the positive-semidefinite cone; inclusion of zero in the generating convex set is essential.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Spectral Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD trace-minimization candidate is certified by a PSD dual slack annihilating its range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{X\succeq0}\operatorname{tr}(X)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(X)=b,
\]
and let \(X_0\succeq0\) be feasible. If some \(y\) satisfies
\[
A^*y\preceq I,\qquad \langle y,b\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(X_0),
\]
then \(X_0\) is optimal. Equivalently, for \(S=I-A^*y\),
\[
S\succeq0,\qquad SX_0=0.
\]
Thus the dual slack vanishes on the range of \(X_0\) and is nonnegative on its orthogonal complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(A^*y\preceq I\) and \(\langle y,b\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(X_0)\), then \(X_0\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace minimization over the PSD cone with affine equality measurements.
review_flags: This is the eigenspace analogue of the rectangular singular-space certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Descent-Cone Uniqueness Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuclear-norm recovery is unique exactly when the measurement nullspace contains no nonzero descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible matrix \(X_0\), define
\[
\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{H:\exists t>0\text{ with }\|X_0+tH\|_*\leq\|X_0\|_*\}.
\]
Then \(X_0\) is the unique solution of
\[
\min_X\|X\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(X)=A(X_0)
\]
if and only if
\[
\ker A\cap\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{0\}.
\]
A strict tangent-space spectral certificate together with injectivity of \(A\) on the tangent space is a standard sufficient condition for this exact test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_0\) is uniquely optimal if and only if \(\ker A\cap\mathcal D_*(X_0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained nuclear-norm minimization at a fixed feasible matrix.

notation.meaning: Nuclear-norm descent cone at the candidate

review_flags: The descent cone need not be closed; the displayed definition is the exact one relevant to uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness certificate for nuclear-norm recovery using singular-space geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^p\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and consider \(\min_X\{\|X\|_*:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\). Let a feasible matrix \(X_\star\) have rank \(r\) and compact singular-value decomposition \(X_\star=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns. Define
\[T=\{UK^{\mathsf T}+LV^{\mathsf T}:K\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},\ L\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\}.\]
If \(\ker\mathcal A\cap T=\{0\}\) and there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfying
\[\mathcal A^*y=UV^{\mathsf T}+W,\qquad U^{\mathsf T}W=0,\qquad WV=0,\qquad\|W\|_2<1,\]
then \(\mathcal A^*y\in\partial\|X_\star\|_*\), and these conditions certify that \(X_\star\) is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual matrix aligned with the recovered singular spaces, strictly contractive on their orthogonal complement, certifies unique nuclear-norm recovery when the measurement operator is injective on the tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^p\) is linear and \(\mathcal A(X_\star)=b\).
\(X_\star=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a rank-\(r\) compact singular-value decomposition.
There exist \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfying the displayed certificate conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_\star\) is the unique minimizer of \(\min_X\{\|X\|_*:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correspondence Among Constrained, Penalized, and Level-Set Gauge Models
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a closed gauge, and let \(\rho:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper closed convex fidelity function.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex gauge models; correspondence means equality or inclusion of solution sets at matched parameters, not universal identity of formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau,\sigma,\lambda\ge0\), define \(P_\tau=\operatorname*{argmin}\{\rho(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\), \(Q_\sigma=\operatorname*{argmin}\{\kappa(x):\rho(x)\le\sigma\}\), and \(R_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\rho(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}\). Two parameterized formulations correspond at their stated parameters when their solution sets have a common point; they correspond exactly when the solution sets are equal. A point \(x^\star\) gives an active parameter match between the constrained models when \(\tau=\kappa(x^\star)\), \(\sigma=\rho(x^\star)\), and \(x^\star\in P_\tau\cap Q_\sigma\). A multiplier match with the penalized model additionally requires \(0\in\partial\rho(x^\star)+\lambda\partial\kappa(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge formulation correspondence relates three families built from the same fidelity and structural gauge: fidelity minimization under a gauge bound, gauge minimization under a fidelity bound, and a weighted sum of fidelity and gauge. Correspondence at chosen parameters means that the formulations share a solution; exact correspondence means their entire solution sets coincide. Active constrained parameters are the attained fidelity and gauge values, while correspondence with a penalized model requires a compatible nonnegative multiplier stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in P_{\kappa(x^\star)}\cap Q_{\rho(x^\star)}\) defines an active constrained correspondence, and \(x^\star\in R_\lambda\) is matched when \(0\in\partial\rho(x^\star)+\lambda\partial\kappa(x^\star)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constrained pair corresponds at \((\tau,\sigma)\) precisely when \(P_\tau\cap Q_\sigma\ne\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\rho(x)=\|Ax-b\|\), the two constrained families are residual minimization with a gauge budget and minimum-gauge recovery with a residual tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Matched formulations have the same attained pair \((\kappa(x^\star),\rho(x^\star))\) at a shared solution.
boundary_notes: Nonunique solutions may yield intersection without equality of solution sets.
A weighted-sum parameter need not represent every boundary solution without convexity and suitable regularity.
The endpoint \(\lambda=0\) can ignore the gauge entirely.

notation.meaning: Solution sets of the three gauge formulations.

children.title: Gauge-Constrained Models
children.top_down_role: Fidelity minimization over gauge-bounded structural models.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Dual of a Gauge-Constrained Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of the gauge ball produces a Fenchel dual penalized by the polar gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma^\circ(y)=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:\gamma(x)\leq1\}\). For \(\tau>0\), the Fenchel dual of \[\inf_{\gamma(x)\leq\tau}f(x)\] is \[\sup_{y\in X^*}\{-f^*(-y)-\tau\gamma^\circ(y)\}.\] If \(\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{int}\{x:\gamma(x)\leq\tau\}\neq\varnothing\), the values agree and, when the primal value is finite, the dual maximum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper closed convex and \(\gamma\) is a closed convex gauge on a finite-dimensional space.
\(\tau>0\) and \(\operatorname{dom}f\) intersects the interior of the gauge ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{\gamma(x)\leq\tau}f(x)=\max_y\{-f^*(-y)-\tau\gamma^\circ(y)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation for fidelity minimization over a positive-radius gauge ball.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Constrained Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge-constrained model minimizes convex fidelity on a gauge ball; under a Slater-type condition, optimality is characterized equivalently by normal-cone or multiplier subgradient conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(C_\tau=\{x\in X:\gamma(x)\leq\tau\}\). The gauge-constrained model is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\ f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in C_\tau.
\]
A feasible point \(x_\tau\) is optimal if and only if
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\tau)+N_{C_\tau}(x_\tau).
\]
Under the stated constraint qualification, this is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) such that
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\tau)+\lambda\partial\gamma(x_\tau),\qquad \lambda\bigl(\gamma(x_\tau)-\tau\bigr)=0.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex, and \(\gamma:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed convex gauge.
\(\tau>0\), and there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) such that \(\gamma(\bar x)<\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model minimizes fidelity over the gauge sublevel set, and the displayed normal-cone and multiplier conditions characterize its minimizers under the stated constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex fidelity minimized over a closed gauge ball under a Slater-type constraint qualification.

notation.meaning: Gauge sublevel set of radius tau

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex constrained model and Fermat condition

children.title: Gauge-Penalized Models
children.top_down_role: Penalty formulations balancing fidelity and structural gauge cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Gauge Dual of Gauge Penalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge penalization is dual to a polar-gauge constraint, with optimality certified by polar-inequality saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), the Fenchel dual of \[\inf_x\{f(x)+\lambda\gamma(x)\}\] is \[\sup_{y\in X^*}\{-f^*(-y):\gamma^\circ(y)\leq\lambda\}.\] Under a Fenchel qualification ensuring equality and attainment, \(x,y\) are primal-dual optimal exactly when \[-y\in\partial f(x),\qquad y\in\lambda\partial\gamma(x).\] The second inclusion is equivalently \(\gamma^\circ(y)\leq\lambda\) and \(\langle y,x\rangle=\lambda\gamma(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper closed convex and \(\gamma\) is a closed convex gauge on a finite-dimensional space.
\(\lambda>0\), and a standard Fenchel qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_x\{f(x)+\lambda\gamma(x)\}=\sup_{\gamma^\circ(y)\leq\lambda}-f^*(-y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual and primal-dual certificate for gauge regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Penalized Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge penalization minimizes fidelity plus a positive multiple of structural gauge cost; optimality balances their subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gauge-penalized model with parameter \(\lambda>0\) is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+\lambda\gamma(x)\bigr\}.
\]
A point \(x_\lambda\) is a minimizer if and only if
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\lambda)+\lambda\partial\gamma(x_\lambda),
\]
provided the standard convex subdifferential sum rule applies. Equivalently, there exist \(g\in\partial f(x_\lambda)\) and \(z\in\partial\gamma(x_\lambda)\) satisfying \(g+\lambda z=0\). The parameter \(\lambda\) therefore fixes the supporting tradeoff between fidelity and structural gauge cost.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex, and \(\gamma\) is a closed convex gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model balances fidelity and gauge cost, and its minimizers satisfy the displayed subgradient equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex gauge regularization with a positive penalty parameter.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex composite Fermat condition

children.title: Gauge Level-Set Models
children.top_down_role: Parameterized formulations organized through gauge value functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bracketed Level-Set Bisection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact monotone-value bisection locates the least feasible gauge radius to interval accuracy ε in logarithmically many evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume an exact value oracle for \(v\), a bracket \(0\leq a<b\) with \(v(a)>\eta\geq v(b)\), and a least feasible radius \(\tau_*:=\min\{\tau\in[a,b]:v(\tau)\leq\eta\}\). Bisection using the predicate \(v(\tau)\leq\eta\) maintains \(a_k<\tau_*\leq b_k\) and satisfies \[b_k-a_k=2^{-k}(b-a).\] Thus an interval of length at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtained after \(\lceil\log_2((b-a)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) value-oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: An exact value oracle and a valid feasible-infeasible bracket are available.
The least feasible radius in the bracket exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k\geq\left\lceil\log_2\frac{b-a}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil\Longrightarrow b_k-a_k\leq\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity for locating the least radius meeting a target fidelity.

notation.meaning: Least radius attaining the target fidelity

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Sensitivity of the Level-Set Value
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal gauge-constraint multipliers are negatives of subgradients of the radius value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(\tau)=\min\{f(x):\gamma(x)\leq\tau\}\). If strong Lagrange duality holds at \(\tau\) and \(\mu_\tau\geq0\) is an optimal multiplier, then \[v(s)\geq v(\tau)-\mu_\tau(s-\tau)\quad(s\geq0),\] hence \(-\mu_\tau\in\partial v(\tau)\). If \(v\) is differentiable at \(\tau\), every optimal multiplier equals \(-v'(\tau)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper closed convex and \(\gamma\) is a closed convex gauge on a finite-dimensional space.
The problem at \(\tau\) is attained and has strong duality with an optimal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\mu_\tau\in\partial v(\tau).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity at a gauge radius admitting an optimal multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Level-Set Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The level-set value function gives optimal fidelity at gauge radius τ; it is nonincreasing and convex and supports scalar parameter searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gauge level-set value function is
\[
v(\tau)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ \gamma(x)\leq\tau\},\qquad \tau\geq0.
\]
For \(0\leq\tau_1\leq\tau_2\), nested feasible sets give \(v(\tau_2)\leq v(\tau_1)\). Joint convexity of the constraint \(\gamma(x)\leq\tau\) and convexity of \(f\) imply that \(v\) is convex on its effective domain. Thus a target fidelity \(\eta\) can be imposed through the scalar condition \(v(\tau)\leq\eta\), with any attaining \(x_\tau\) solving the corresponding gauge-constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex and \(\gamma:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed convex gauge on finite-dimensional \(X\).
For the parameter values considered, the feasible set is nonempty and the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value function records the optimal fidelity at each gauge radius and is nonincreasing and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar level-set parameterization by the gauge radius.

children.title: Parameter-Value Formulation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence and nonequivalence boundaries among the principal gauge formulations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) and \(\rho:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions on a finite-dimensional space, with \(\kappa\) a gauge.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function correspondence for convex constrained formulations, including explicit nonequivalence at slack constraints and unattained infima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v(\tau)=\inf\{\rho(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\) and \(w(\sigma)=\inf\{\kappa(x):\rho(x)\le\sigma\}\), with value \(+\infty\) for an empty feasible set. A pair \((\tau,\sigma)\) is a parameter-value correspondence point when \(\sigma=v(\tau)\), \(\tau=w(\sigma)\), and both infima are attained by at least one common point. It is an active correspondence point when every selected common minimizer \(x^\star\) satisfies \(\kappa(x^\star)=\tau\) and \(\rho(x^\star)=\sigma\). The correspondence graph records these mutually minimal attainable boundary pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first value function gives the least fidelity achievable under a gauge budget, and the second gives the least gauge achievable under a fidelity tolerance. A parameter pair corresponds when each coordinate is the optimal value generated by the other coordinate and the two infima possess a common optimizer. Active correspondence further requires that the optimizer attain both bounds as equalities. This definition separates true boundary correspondence from a merely feasible or slack parameter choice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G=\{(\tau,\sigma):\sigma=v(\tau),\ \tau=w(\sigma),\ \operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa\le\tau}\rho\cap\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\le\sigma}\kappa\ne\varnothing\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: At an active correspondence point, a common optimizer realizes the attainable pair \((\kappa(x^\star),\rho(x^\star))=(\tau,\sigma)\).
special_cases_latex: If each constrained problem has a unique optimizer and both constraints are active, correspondence of the parameters implies equality of the singleton solution sets.
immediate_consequences_latex: The function \(v\) is nonincreasing in \(\tau\), and \(w\) is nonincreasing in \(\sigma\).
boundary_notes: The identities \(\sigma=v(\tau)\) and \(\tau=w(\sigma)\) can fail at flat value-function segments or slack constraints.
Infimal values without attainment do not define a correspondence point under this definition.
This definition does not assert differentiability or a one-to-one multiplier map.

notation.meaning: Optimal fidelity as a function of gauge budget.
Optimal gauge as a function of fidelity tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-to-Value Correspondence for Gauge-Constrained Problems
Penalty Weights as Supporting Slopes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty weights are negative supporting slopes of the constrained value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[p(\tau)=\inf\{r(x):\kappa(x)\leq\tau\}.\] Suppose \(p(\tau)\) is attained by \(x_\tau\) with \(\kappa(x_\tau)=\tau\). If \(-\lambda\in\partial p(\tau)\), then \[x_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{r(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}.\] Conversely, if \(x\) minimizes \(r+\lambda\kappa\) and \(\tau=\kappa(x)\), then \(x\) attains \(p(\tau)\) and \(-\lambda\in\partial p(\tau)\). Thus differentiability gives \(\lambda=-p'(\tau)\), while a kink can admit an interval of weights.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) and \(\kappa\) are proper closed convex functions, with \(\kappa\) a gauge.
The stated constrained or penalized minimizer exists.
For the forward implication, the constrained solution is active at \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\lambda\in\partial p(\tau)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{supporting constraint–penalty correspondence at }\tau.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion between gauge budgets and penalty weights through the constrained value function.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under attainment, each feasible residual level determines the least gauge budget, and each gauge budget determines the least residual level through generalized inverse value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau,\sigma\ge0\), define \(p(\tau):=\min\{r(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\) and \(v(\sigma):=\min\{\kappa(x):r(x)\le\sigma\}\), with value \(+\infty\) for an empty feasible set. Then \(p\) and \(v\) are nonincreasing, and attainment gives \[v(\sigma)=\min\{\tau\ge0:p(\tau)\le\sigma\},\qquad p(\tau)=\min\{\sigma\ge0:v(\sigma)\le\tau\}.\] Thus a residual level and a gauge budget correspond through the lower generalized inverses of their value functions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, and \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) and \(r:X\to[0,+\infty]\) are closed gauges.
The minima defining \(p(\tau)\) and \(v(\sigma)\) are attained whenever their feasible sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(\sigma)=\min\{\tau\ge0:p(\tau)\le\sigma\}\) and \(p(\tau)=\min\{\sigma\ge0:v(\sigma)\le\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-inverse correspondence for attained gauge-constrained value functions.

notation.meaning: Residual-minimization value at gauge budget tau.
Gauge-minimization value at residual budget sigma.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 The Value Function p. 67

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Values as a Conjugate Transform of Constrained Values
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalized optimal values are the negative conjugate transform of constrained values, with recovery under closed convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extend \[p(\tau)=\inf\{r(x):\kappa(x)\leq\tau\}\] by \(p(\tau)=+\infty\) for \(\tau<0\), and define \[q(\lambda)=\inf_x\{r(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\},\qquad\lambda\geq0.\] Then \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{\tau\geq0}\{p(\tau)+\lambda\tau\}=-p^*(-\lambda).\] If \(p\) is proper, closed, convex, and nonincreasing, then \[p(\tau)=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\{q(\lambda)-\lambda\tau\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is proper convex and \(\kappa\) is a convex gauge.
For recovery, the extended function \(p\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\lambda)=-p^*(-\lambda),\qquad p(\tau)=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\{q(\lambda)-\lambda\tau\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-level correspondence between gauge constraints and gauge penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With attained minima, a residual target is achievable under a gauge budget exactly when the minimum gauge required for that target does not exceed the budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\tau,\sigma\ge0\), \[p(\tau)\le\sigma\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v(\sigma)\le\tau.\] Whenever the values are finite, \[\{\tau\ge0:p(\tau)\le\sigma\}=[v(\sigma),+\infty),\qquad \{\sigma\ge0:v(\sigma)\le\tau\}=[p(\tau),+\infty).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, and \(\kappa,r:X\to[0,+\infty]\) are closed gauges.
For \(\tau,\sigma\ge0\), the minima defining \(p(\tau):=\min\{r(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\) and \(v(\sigma):=\min\{\kappa(x):r(x)\le\sigma\}\) are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(\tau)\le\sigma\iff v(\sigma)\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-equivalence between the feasibility thresholds encoded by the two attained constrained value functions.

notation.meaning: Optimal residual under gauge budget tau.
Optimal gauge under residual budget sigma.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 The Value Function p. 67

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint–Penalty Equivalence Through Positive Multipliers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalized solution solves the constraint at its attained radius, and a constrained solution is recovered by any positive supporting KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}\) with \(\lambda>0\), then for \(\tau=\kappa(x_\lambda)\), \[x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa(x)\leq\tau}f(x).\] Conversely, if \(x_\tau\) solves \(\min\{f(x):\kappa(x)\leq\tau\}\) and its KKT system admits \(\lambda>0\), then \[x_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\lambda\kappa(x)\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper convex and \(\kappa\) is a convex gauge.
For the converse, the constrained solution admits the stated positive KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>0\text{ and KKT support imply constraint–penalty solution correspondence}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution correspondence between a gauge constraint and positive gauge penalty.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At mutually corresponding attained parameter values, the two constrained formulations have the same solution set, consisting exactly of points with gauge tau and residual sigma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_p(\tau):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa(x)\le\tau}r(x)\) and \(S_v(\sigma):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r(x)\le\sigma}\kappa(x)\). If \(p(\tau)=\sigma\) and \(v(\sigma)=\tau\), then \[S_p(\tau)=\{x\in X:\kappa(x)=\tau,\ r(x)=\sigma\}=S_v(\sigma).\]
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, and \(\kappa,r:X\to[0,+\infty]\) are closed gauges.
For \(\tau,[0m\sigma\ge0\), define \(p(\tau):=\min\{r(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\) and \(v(\sigma):=\min\{\kappa(x):r(x)\le\sigma\}\), with both minima attained and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\kappa(x)\le\tau}r(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r(x)\le\sigma}\kappa(x)=\{x\in X:\kappa(x)=\tau,\ r(x)=\sigma\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-set equivalence at mutually corresponding attained parameter values.

notation.meaning: Residual minimizers under gauge budget tau.
Gauge minimizers under residual budget sigma.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Multiplier Failure of Positive-Penalty Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained boundary solution having only a zero multiplier can be missed by every positive penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\), \(\kappa(x)=|x|\), and \(\tau=1\). The problem \[\min\{(x-1)^2:|x|\leq1\}\] has unique solution \(x=1\), and its only KKT multiplier is \(0\). For every \(\lambda>0\), the unique minimizer of \[(x-1)^2+\lambda|x|\] is \(x_\lambda=\max\{1-\lambda/2,0\}<1\). Thus no positive penalty parameter recovers the constrained solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1\notin\bigcup_{\lambda>0}\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{(x-1)^2+\lambda|x|\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attained convex example not recoverable by a strictly positive gauge penalty.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Nonequivalence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat tradeoff frontiers, unmatched parameters, infinite values, or unattained infima can destroy parameter recovery and equality of optimal solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equivalence of optimal solution sets is not guaranteed if \(\sigma\ne p(\tau)\), \(\tau\ne v(\sigma)\), or either defining infimum is unattained. A flat portion of the attainable tradeoff frontier can make several budgets share one value, so generalized inverses need not recover the original parameter. Without attainment, \(p(\tau)=\sigma\) need not provide any \(x\) with \(\kappa(x)\le\tau\) and \(r(x)=\sigma\). Thus value equality alone, without mutual correspondence and attainment, does not establish formulation equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) and \(v\) are the two gauge-formulation value functions.
At least one of attainment, mutual parameter correspondence, or finiteness fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of the two argmin sets is then not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanisms outside the mutually corresponding attained Pareto frontier.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\). Let \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional computational access model; complexity claims are relative to a specified encoding, arithmetic model, accuracy, and bounded query domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gauge tractability interface for \((C,\kappa_C,C^\circ,\kappa_C^\circ)\) is a declared collection of exact or approximate procedures chosen from: evaluation \(x\mapsto\kappa_C(x)\); membership for \(x\in tC\); separation from \(tC\); support optimization \(y\mapsto\sup_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle\); polar membership for \(y\in sC^\circ\); and proximal or projection operations. The interface is polynomially tractable when every declared procedure returns its specified output within time polynomial in the encoded instance size and, for approximate procedures, in \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) or the stated accuracy measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge tractability interface states exactly how an algorithm may access a gauge ball and its polar. Permitted primitives can include value evaluation, scaled-ball membership, separation, support optimization, polar membership, projection, or proximal evaluation. The interface must say whether each primitive is exact or approximate and must specify the input encoding and accuracy convention. It is polynomially tractable only relative to those choices, when each promised primitive has polynomial running time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak I(C)\subseteq\{\mathrm{Eval}_{\kappa_C},\mathrm{Mem}_{tC},\mathrm{Sep}_{tC},\mathrm{Supp}_C,\mathrm{Mem}_{sC^\circ},\mathrm{Proj}_C,\mathrm{Prox}_{\kappa_C}\}\) together with exactness, accuracy, and complexity specifications defines the interface.
special_cases_latex: An explicit conic representation supplies an implementation of several interface primitives when the associated conic problems are tractable.
An atomic set may instead provide only a support-optimization oracle.
immediate_consequences_latex: Tractability of one primitive must not be silently interpreted as tractability of every other primitive.
boundary_notes: Polynomial equivalences between membership, separation, and optimization require additional geometric and numerical assumptions.
The definition excludes an unspecified black box whose accuracy and cost are not declared.

children.title: Explicit Gauge Representations

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Representation of a Gauge Ball and Epigraph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex set containing \(0\), and let \(\kappa_C\) be its Minkowski gauge. Representations may use finitely many auxiliary variables but must have finite encoded data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact representations by explicit inequalities, equations, or finite-dimensional lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit representation of \(\kappa_C\) is finite data defining either its unit ball \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ F(x,z)\in D\}\) or its epigraph \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):\exists z,\ G(x,t,z)\in D,\ t\ge0\}\), where the maps, auxiliary dimension, and primitive set \(D\) are specified. The representation is exact when projection eliminates \(z\) to give precisely \(C\) or \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C\). For a unit-ball representation, the induced gauge obeys \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\exists z,\ F(x/t,z)\in D\}\), interpreted directly as \(x\in tC\) at \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit gauge representation is finite encoded data that describes either the gauge unit ball or the gauge epigraph, possibly as the projection of a finite-dimensional lifted set. Exactness means that eliminating the auxiliary variables yields exactly the intended ball or epigraph, not merely an inner or outer approximation. The gauge value is then the smallest nonnegative scaling for which the point satisfies the represented unit-ball constraints.

special_cases_latex: Taking no auxiliary variable gives a direct representation.
Choosing \(D\) polyhedral, second-order conic, or semidefinite produces the corresponding representation class.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Polyhedral Gauge Program
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing a lifted polyhedral description gives an attained linear program for the gauge and retains recession directions at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+Bz\le b\}\) be a nonempty closed convex polyhedron containing \(0\) and absorbing \(\mathbb R^n\). Then, for every \(x\), \[\gamma_C(x)=\min\{t:t\ge0,\ \exists w\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+Bw\le tb\}.\] The minimum is attained. Moreover, \(\gamma_C(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in\operatorname{rec}C\), equivalently when the displayed system is feasible at \(t=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ Ax+Bz\le b\}\) is a nonempty closed polyhedron containing \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\min\{t\ge0:\exists w,\ Ax+Bw\le tb\}\), and \(\gamma_C(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname{rec}C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact gauge evaluation from a finite lifted-polyhedral description, including zero-gauge recession directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Gauge Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized inequality description represents a polyhedral gauge as the maximum of zero and finitely many linear forms; a bounded vertex description represents it as a linear-program value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C=\{x:h_i^{\mathsf T}x\le1,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), then \[\gamma_C(x)=\max\left\{0,\max_{1\le i\le m}h_i^{\mathsf T}x\right\}.\] If additionally \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_q\}\) is bounded and \(V=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_q]\), then \[\gamma_C(x)=\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda:V\lambda=x,\ \lambda\ge0\}.\] Thus evaluation reduces to a finite maximum or a linear program, respectively.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex polyhedron containing \(0\) and absorbing \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A normalized halfspace description yields \(\gamma_C(x)=\max\{0,\max_i h_i^{\mathsf T}x\}\), and a bounded vertex description yields a linear-programming representation of \(\gamma_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite halfspace and bounded vertex representations of a polyhedral gauge.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex polyhedron containing \(0\), and assume a normalized inequality description \(C=\{x:a_i^Tx\le1,\ i=1,\ldots,N\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral gauges, allowing asymmetric gauges and zero directions when the unit ball is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedral gauge represented by \(C\) is \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:a_i^Tx\le t\ \forall i\}\). Whenever this infimum is finite, \(\kappa_C(x)=\max\{0,a_1^Tx,\ldots,a_N^Tx\}\). Its epigraph has the finite linear description \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ a_i^Tx\le t\ \forall i\}\), and its polar unit set is \(C^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_N\}\). A lifted polyhedral representation permits additional variables and obtains \(C\) by projection of finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral gauge is the Minkowski functional of a polyhedral unit set containing the origin. With normalized facet inequalities, its value is the maximum of zero and the finitely many facet linear forms. Consequently, its epigraph is described by finitely many linear inequalities, while its polar unit set is the convex hull of the origin and the facet normals. Auxiliary variables are allowed in a lifted polyhedral representation, provided projection recovers the exact unit set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_C(x)=\max\{0,\max_i a_i^Tx\},\quad \operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ a_i^Tx\le t\ \forall i\},\quad C^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_N\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A finite vertex-ray description of \(C\) and a finite inequality description are alternative exact polyhedral representations.
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is centrally symmetric and bounded with nonempty interior, \(\kappa_C\) is a polyhedral norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: Gauge evaluation in the normalized direct representation requires evaluating finitely many linear forms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic and Semidefinite Lift of a Gauge
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) be a closed convex cone, let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contain \(0\), and let \(\kappa_C\) denote its gauge.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional lifted representations; semidefinite lifts are the specialization in which the primitive cone is a product of positive-semidefinite cones and linear subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(K\)-conic lift of the gauge unit ball is affine data \((A,B,c)\) such that \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ Ax+Bz+c\in K\}\). A homogeneous epigraph lift is affine-linear data satisfying \(\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\{(x,t):t\ge0,\ \exists z,\ Ax+Bz+tc\in K\}\). The lift is semidefinite when \(K\) is a finite product of cones \(\mathbb S_+^{d_j}\) and any explicitly stated linear cones, so membership is expressed by linear matrix inequalities. Lift size comprises the auxiliary dimension and cone-block dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic gauge lift represents the unit ball or epigraph as the projection of an affine slice of a closed convex cone. An epigraph lift is homogeneous in the gauge scaling variable and includes its nonnegativity. A semidefinite gauge lift is a conic lift whose primitive cone consists of positive-semidefinite matrix cones, possibly with explicit linear components. Exactness requires the projected lifted feasible set to equal the intended ball or epigraph exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,z):Ax+Bz+c\in K\}\quad\text{or}\quad\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}\{(x,t,z):t\ge0,\ Ax+Bz+tc\in K\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A semidefinite lift can be written as finitely many linear matrix inequalities \(M_j(x,t,z)\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: A polyhedral lift is obtained when \(K\) is a nonnegative orthant.
A second-order-cone lift is obtained when \(K\) is a product of Lorentz cones.
immediate_consequences_latex: Gauge evaluation reduces formally to minimizing \(t\) over the lifted conic epigraph.
boundary_notes: Representability does not by itself provide polynomial-time guarantees without encoding, regularity, and numerical assumptions.
A spectrahedral shadow is generally a projection, not necessarily a direct spectrahedron in the original variables.

notation.meaning: Primitive closed convex cone used in the lift.

review_flags: The hinted conic-representation sources were not inspected for this exact homogeneous gauge-epigraph definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic and Semidefinite Lift of a Gauge
Attainment Boundary of the Lifted Scaling Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed cone may have a nonclosed projection, so a finite lifted gauge value need not have an attaining auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the unit-set hypotheses, \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:\exists z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}.\] Closedness of \(K\) alone does not imply closedness of the projected feasible set in \((x,t)\). If \((x,\gamma_C(x))\) lies in its closure but not in the projection, the finite infimum has no feasible lift at \(t=\gamma_C(x)\). Thus replacing \(\inf\) by \(\min\) requires projection closedness or another attainment condition.
assumptions_latex: \(K,B,D,d,C\) satisfy the unit-set assumptions of the immutable Conic Lifted Gauge Models seed.
Closedness of the homogenized projection is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:\exists z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\},\quad\text{and the infimum need not be attained}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The infimal conic value formula remains valid without projection closedness, but an optimal lifting variable may not exist.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Lifted Gauge Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed homogenized affine conic lift represents the gauge as the attained minimum of its scalar scaling variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gauge of \(C\) has the homogenized conic representation \[\gamma_C(x)=\min\{t\ge0:\exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}.\] The minimum is finite for every \(x\in X\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, \(K\) is a closed convex cone, \(B:X\to Y\) and \(D:Z\to Y\) are linear maps, and \(d\in Y\).
\(C:=\{x\in X:\exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+d\in K\}\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\).
The homogenized projection \(H:=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge0,\ \exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\min\{t\ge0:\exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of an affine conic lift of a gauge unit ball, with closedness sufficient for attainment.

notation.meaning: Closed convex cone used by the lift.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.2 Conic quadratic representations p. 132

knowledge_statements.title: PSD-Projection Attainment Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD lift can become nonclosed after projection, so an auxiliary semidefinite gauge model need not attain its value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Linear images of the closed positive-semidefinite cone need not be closed. For example, projecting \[\left\{\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}\] onto \((a,b)\) gives \[\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},\] which is not closed because \((1/n,1)\to(0,1)\). Consequently, a projected semidefinite gauge epigraph can omit boundary points, and its finite infimum need not be attained without projection closedness or another attainment condition.
assumptions_latex: A gauge model is obtained by projecting a positive-semidefinite affine system.
No projection-closedness or independent attainment condition is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{closedness of }\mathbb S_+^k\not\Rightarrow\text{closedness of its projected gauge model}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD-cone closedness does not guarantee closedness of a spectrahedral shadow or attainment of a projected gauge model.

notation.meaning: Cone of real positive-semidefinite matrices of order \(k\)

knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear-Norm Semidefinite Gauge Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear norm is the optimal half-sum of two traces in a positive-semidefinite block lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \[\|X\|_*=\min_{U\in\mathbb S^m,\,V\in\mathbb S^n}\left\{\frac12\bigl(\operatorname{tr}U+\operatorname{tr}V\bigr):\begin{bmatrix}U&X\\X^\top&V\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|X\|_*=\min\left\{\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}U+\operatorname{tr}V):\begin{bmatrix}U&X\\X^\top&V\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical lifted SDP representation of the rectangular nuclear norm.

notation.meaning: Sum of the singular values of \(X\)
Space of real symmetric matrices of order \(k\)

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Norm Semidefinite Gauge Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block positive-semidefinite inequality represents the spectral-norm ball and its gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \[\|X\|_2=\min\left\{t\geq0:\begin{bmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^\top&tI_n\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|X\|_2\leq t\iff t\geq0\ \text{and}\ \begin{bmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^\top&tI_n\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct LMI representation of the rectangular spectral norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Gauge Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrahedral-shadow unit ball yields a semidefinite gauge model by multiplying its constant matrix by the scaling variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[C=\left\{x:\exists z,\ F_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iF_i+\sum_{j=1}^q z_jG_j\succeq0\right\}.\] Then its gauge has the semidefinite representation \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\left\{t\ge0:\exists z,\ tF_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iF_i+\sum_{j=1}^q z_jG_j\succeq0\right\}.\] If the projected feasible set in \((x,t)\) is closed, this formula is exact and finite for every \(x\) because \(C\) is absorbing.
assumptions_latex: The projected spectrahedron \(C\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\exists z,\ tF_0+\sum_i x_iF_i+\sum_jz_jG_j\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite specialization of a homogenized conic gauge lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Closure Boundary for Conic Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without projection closedness, the raw homogenized conic projection can omit boundary points, while its closure is the gauge epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[H:=\{(x,t):t\geq0,\ \exists z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}.\] Under the unit-set hypotheses of the immutable seed but without assuming that \(H\) is closed, \[H\subseteq\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C\subseteq\overline H.\] Since \(\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C\) is closed, these inclusions give \(\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C=\overline H\). Thus a point of \(\overline H\setminus H\) is a gauge-epigraph boundary point lacking an attaining lift.
assumptions_latex: \(K,B,D,d,C\) satisfy the unit-set assumptions of the immutable Conic Epigraph Representations seed.
The homogenized projection \(H\) is not assumed closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C=\overline H,\qquad H=\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C\ \text{if }H\text{ is closed}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the raw homogenized projection from the closed gauge epigraph.

notation.meaning: Topological closure of the raw projection

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Epigraph Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed homogenized conic lift of the unit ball represents the entire gauge epigraph, including its zero-scale recession slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gauge epigraph has the exact conic representation \[\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge0,\ \exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}.\] Its slice at \(t=0\) consists of the zero-gauge recession directions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, \(K\) is a closed convex cone, \(B:X\to Y\) and \(D:Z\to Y\) are linear maps, and \(d\in Y\).
\(C:=\{x\in X:\exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+d\in K\}\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\).
The homogenized projection \(H:=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge0,\ \exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}\gamma_C=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge0,\ \exists z\in Z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Unit-Ball Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic projection represents a gauge unit ball exactly when the gauge is the Minkowski functional of that projected set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any closed convex absorbing set \(C\) containing \(0\), its Minkowski gauge satisfies \[C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}.\] Hence an affine conic representation \[C=\{x:\exists z,\ Bx+Dz+d\in K\}\] is exactly a conic unit-ball representation of \(\gamma_C\). Conversely, any gauge whose unit ball has this conic lift satisfies \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\exists z,\ Bx+Dz+td\in K\}\).
assumptions_latex: The projection \(C=\{x:\exists z,\ Bx+Dz+d\in K\}\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Oracle Interface for a Gauge and Its Polar
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), let \(\kappa=\gamma_C\), and let \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based finite-dimensional access used when no finite explicit representation is supplied; both exact and tolerance-qualified interfaces are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit gauge-polarity oracle interface is a finite specification of callable maps for \(C\), \(\kappa\), \(C^\circ\), or \(\kappa^\circ\), together with input domains, output contracts, tolerances, and costs. Admissible calls include \(\mathrm{Eval}_\kappa(x)\), \(\mathrm{Mem}_C(x)\), \(\mathrm{Sep}_C(x)\), \(\mathrm{Supp}_C(y)\), and their polar counterparts. Consistency requires \(\kappa(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathrm{Mem}_C(x/t)=1\}\) and \(\kappa^\circ(y)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle\), with appropriate conventions for zero scaling, infeasibility, and infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit gauge-polarity interface replaces a finite constraint description by declared oracle calls. Each call must specify its legal inputs, exact or approximate output, tolerance, and computational cost. The gauge-side and polar-side calls must be mutually consistent: gauge evaluation is scaling membership in the unit ball, and polar-gauge evaluation is support optimization over that ball. An interface may expose only a subset of these primitives, but it may not claim undeclared operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak O=(\mathrm{Eval}_\kappa,\mathrm{Mem}_C,\mathrm{Sep}_C,\mathrm{Supp}_C,\mathrm{Eval}_{\kappa^\circ},\mathrm{Mem}_{C^\circ},\ldots)\) is an interface only when every included oracle has a specified and polarity-consistent contract.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(\kappa^\circ=\sigma_C\), an exact support oracle for \(C\) is an exact evaluation oracle for the polar gauge.
special_cases_latex: For an atomic hull, support optimization may be implemented by maximizing over the atom set without explicitly constructing its convex hull.
immediate_consequences_latex: An optimization method using only declared calls remains meaningful even when \(C\) has no practical explicit representation.
boundary_notes: Approximate membership and weak separation require a specified norm and tolerance model.
Evaluation, membership, separation, and optimization are not automatically interchangeable without boundedness and conditioning assumptions.

notation.meaning: Specified collection of gauge and polar oracle calls.

review_flags: No inspected source supports the entire gauge-polarity oracle interface and its consistency conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gauge Evaluation and Scaled-Ball Membership Interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact oracle access to an extended-valued finite-dimensional gauge; approximate variants require separate tolerance promises.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact gauge evaluation-membership interface consists of an evaluation oracle returning \(\kappa_C(x)\in[0,+\infty]\) and a scaled-membership oracle returning whether \(x\in tC\) for \(t\ge0\), subject to the consistency rule \(\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\iff\kappa_C(x)\le t\). Conversely, evaluation induced by membership is \(\kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\}\). At \(t=0\), membership means \(x\in0C\), with the convention chosen consistently with the closed perspective and recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This interface exposes two views of the same gauge geometry. The evaluation oracle returns the gauge value, including infinity when appropriate. The membership oracle answers whether a point lies in a specified nonnegative scaling of the unit set. Exact consistency requires membership at scale t to be equivalent to the gauge value being at most t, and the value to equal the infimum of all accepted scales. Zero scale and recession directions must be handled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\iff x\in tC\iff\kappa_C(x)\le t,\qquad \kappa_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:\mathrm{Mem}_C(x,t)=1\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The epigraph-membership query \((x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\kappa_C\) is the scaled-ball membership query for \(t\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(C\) is the unit ball of a norm, the zero-scale query accepts only \(x=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An exact evaluation oracle immediately implements exact scaled membership by comparison with \(t\).
boundary_notes: Binary search using membership yields approximate evaluation only when finite bounds and a numerical model are specified.
For nonabsorbing \(C\), evaluation may return \(+\infty\).
Unbounded unit sets can have nontrivial zero-gauge directions.

notation.meaning: Exact membership predicate for the scaled unit set.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Evaluation and Scaled-Ball Membership Interface
Relative-Accuracy Gauge-Value Oracle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative gauge oracle gives multiplicative accuracy for positive finite values; certified interval output needs the corresponding ratio condition, while zero and infinity require special conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\eta<1\) and \(0<\gamma_C(x)<+\infty\), a relative-accuracy oracle returns \(\widehat\gamma\) satisfying \[(1-\eta)\gamma_C(x)\le\widehat\gamma\le(1+\eta)\gamma_C(x).\] A certified enclosure \(0<\ell\le\gamma_C(x)\le u\) supports such a common estimate for every enclosed value exactly when \(u/\ell\le(1+\eta)/(1-\eta)\); one may then select \(\widehat\gamma\in[(1-\eta)u,(1+\eta)\ell]\). At gauge value zero this specification requires exact zero output, while \(+\infty\) requires a separate response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (1-\eta)\gamma_C(x)\le\widehat\gamma\le(1+\eta)\gamma_C(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative evaluation variant for positive finite gauge values.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of the gauge value.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-accuracy value oracle for the Minkowski gauge of a specified convex unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, convex, absorbing, and contain \(0\). A gauge-value oracle for \(B\) accepts an input \((x,\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty)\) and terminates with a scalar \(v\in[0,\infty)\) satisfying \[|v-\gamma_B(x)|\leq\varepsilon.\] The case \(\varepsilon=0\) is an exact oracle. If \(B\) is not absorbing, the codomain is extended to \([0,+\infty]\), and the oracle must also identify the value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge-value oracle returns the Minkowski gauge at the queried point, exactly or within a requested additive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(v\) satisfies \(|v-\gamma_B(x)|\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Ball Membership Oracles
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact membership tests whether the gauge is at most one; weak membership permits either answer only within a specified gauge-distance band around the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact unit-ball membership oracle receives \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and returns \(M_C(x)=1\) if \(\gamma_C(x)\le1\), and \(M_C(x)=0\) otherwise. A weak oracle with tolerance \(\delta>0\) must return inside when \(\gamma_C(x)\le1-
\delta\) and outside when \(\gamma_C(x)\ge1+
\delta\); either response is permitted in the boundary band \(|\gamma_C(x)-1|<\delta\). Thus weak membership avoids requiring an exact decision at numerically indistinguishable boundary points.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}\) is the closed unit ball of a finite gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact oracle decides \(x\in C\); its weak version certifies inside or outside except within a prescribed boundary band.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-aware membership specifications in gauge coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrected Bisection Reduction from Membership to Gauge Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled exact membership gives gauge threshold comparisons, so bisection evaluates a bounded gauge value to absolute accuracy ε in max(0, ceiling(log₂(R/ε))) queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma_C\) be a finite gauge with unit ball \(C=\{z:\gamma_C(z)\leq1\}\), fix \(x\), and suppose a known \(R>0\) satisfies \(\gamma_C(x)\leq R\). For every \(t>0\),
\[
x/t\in C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\gamma_C(x)\leq t.
\]
If \(0<\varepsilon<R\), bisection of \([0,R]\) using these exact membership tests produces an interval containing \(\gamma_C(x)\) with width at most \(\varepsilon\) after at most \(\lceil\log_2(R/\varepsilon)\rceil\) queries. If \(\varepsilon\geq R\), no query is needed. Thus the universal bound is
\[
\max\{0,\lceil\log_2(R/\varepsilon)\rceil\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: A query point \(x\) and a known bound \(R>0\) with \(\gamma_C(x)\leq R\) are given.
Exact membership queries for \(C\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing \(\gamma_C(x)\) is obtained using at most \(\max\{0,\lceil\log_2(R/\varepsilon)\rceil\}\) membership queries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prescribed-accuracy pointwise evaluation from exact scaled unit-ball membership, including the zero-query accuracy regime.

notation.meaning: positive known upper bound on the queried gauge value

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Membership Access Cannot Give Exact Unrestricted Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely many membership comparisons cannot identify an unrestricted real gauge value exactly, although they can approximate it to any positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\ne0\). Over any admissible family for which \(\gamma_C(x)\) ranges through a nondegenerate real interval, no deterministic procedure using finitely many exact queries of the form \(x/t\in C\) can recover \(\gamma_C(x)\) exactly for every member of the family. Prescribed-accuracy evaluation remains possible through threshold search.
assumptions_latex: The admissible gauge family permits \(\gamma_C(x)\) to range through a nondegenerate real interval.
Only finitely many exact membership queries are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact finite-query evaluation is impossible without additional discreteness or algebraic structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for exact recovery of unrestricted real gauge values from membership comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation–Membership Interreducibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact threshold reduction and radial bisection reduction under known inner and outer radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex and suppose \(r\mathbb{B}_2\subseteq B\subseteq R\mathbb{B}_2\), where \(0<r\leq R\). For \(x\neq0\), an exact gauge oracle decides membership by testing whether \(\gamma_B(x)\leq1\). Conversely, given an exact membership oracle and \(\varepsilon>0\), initialize \(L_0=\|x\|_2/R\) and \(U_0=\|x\|_2/r\). Starting with \(L=L_0\) and \(U=U_0\), while \(U-L>\varepsilon\), set \(m=(L+U)/2\), query whether \(x/m\in B\), and replace \(U\) by \(m\) after a positive response or \(L\) by \(m\) otherwise. The final interval contains \(\gamma_B(x)\). The algorithm uses no queries when \(U_0-L_0\leq\varepsilon\), and otherwise uses at most \[\left\lceil\log_2\!\left(\frac{U_0-L_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\right\rceil\] membership queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact gauge evaluation gives membership by thresholding, while exact radial membership gives an additive gauge approximation by bisection with a logarithmic query bound.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex with \(r\mathbb{B}_2\subseteq B\subseteq R\mathbb{B}_2\), where \(0<r\leq R\).
The membership or gauge oracle used by the corresponding reduction is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact membership and additive gauge evaluation reduce to one another; radial bisection returns an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing \(\gamma_B(x)\), with the stated query bound.

notation.meaning: known inner and outer Euclidean radii
current lower and upper gauge bounds
