children.title: Exceptional Polyhedral Cases
children.top_down_role: Boundary conventions needed for representations, faces, and polarity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in \(\mathbb R^n\) and adopt the finite-intersection definition of a polyhedron. Recession and lineality are assigned only to nonempty sets in this record.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The record fixes conventions for the empty set, whole space, and zero-dimensional polyhedra, which otherwise create edge cases in dimension and representation statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exceptional polyhedral cases are normalized as follows. The inconsistent system \(0^Tx\leq-1\) represents \(\varnothing\), with \(\operatorname{aff}\varnothing=\varnothing\) and \(\dim\varnothing=-1\). The empty system represents \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(\operatorname{aff}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\), \(\operatorname{rec}\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{lin}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\). A nonempty zero-dimensional polyhedron is a singleton \(\{x_0\}\), with \(\operatorname{rec}\{x_0\}=\operatorname{lin}\{x_0\}=\{0\}\). Faces are taken to include \(\varnothing\) and the polyhedron itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The empty set is regarded as a polyhedron represented by an inconsistent finite system, has empty affine hull, and has dimension \(-1\). The whole space is the intersection of no constraints and has itself as affine hull, recession cone, and lineality space. Every nonempty zero-dimensional polyhedron is a singleton and has only the zero recession direction. Under the stated face convention, the empty face and the whole polyhedron are included among the faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim\varnothing=-1\), \(\operatorname{rec}\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{lin}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\), and \(\dim P=0\neq P\Rightarrow P=\{x_0\}\) with \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\mathbb R^n\) is the intersection of the empty collection of halfspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty polyhedron is the feasible set of an infeasible finite system of affine inequalities and is still admitted as a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An empty polyhedron is a polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(P=\varnothing\). In an inequality representation \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\},\] emptiness means that no \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies all rows simultaneously. Thus emptiness is a property of the represented feasible set, not of any individual inequality, and different infeasible systems may represent the same empty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\varnothing\) exactly when the finite inequality system \(Ax\le b\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty-set case under the finite-intersection definition of a polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the inequality system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inequality descriptions of the empty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). Then \(P=\varnothing\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[y\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Such a multiplier is an exact finite certificate of emptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-defined polyhedron is empty exactly when a nonnegative linear combination of its inequalities has zero left-hand side and a strictly negative right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\varnothing\iff\exists y\ge0:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedron represented by the finite inequality system.

Improper Polyhedral Objects
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: “Improper polyhedral object” is not canonical terminology; its meaning must be declared before dimension, recession, polarity, or face statements are interpreted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The phrase “improper polyhedral object” is not assigned a universal set-theoretic meaning by the basic definition of a polyhedron. Depending on context, exceptional objects may include \(\varnothing\), the whole space \(\mathbb{R}^n\), nonpointed cones, or extended-valued objects derived from improper convex functions. Consequently, any theorem using this phrase must explicitly declare the admitted class before properties such as dimension, recession, polarity, or facial structure are applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No invariant mathematical predicate for an “improper polyhedral object” can be fixed without an explicit local convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology boundary: “improper” has incompatible meanings across convex and polyhedral settings.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary appropriately records the noncanonical terminology, but the asserted range of competing meanings cannot be accepted without sources documenting those usages.

knowledge_statements.title: Exceptional-Case Conventions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common bookkeeping convention gives the empty set affine hull empty and dimension minus one; recession and similar operations require separate declarations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exceptional-case bookkeeping, one may adopt \[\operatorname{aff}(\varnothing)=\varnothing,\qquad \dim(\varnothing)=-1.\] These assignments extend the face-dimension convention to the empty face, but they are conventions rather than consequences of the nonempty definition \(\dim(C)=\dim(\operatorname{aff}(C)-x_0)\). Operations whose quantified definitions become vacuous on \(\varnothing\), including some recession-cone definitions, must be specified separately rather than inferred from these assignments.
assumptions_latex: The local theory admits \(\varnothing\) as a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignments \(\operatorname{aff}(\varnothing)=\varnothing\) and \(\dim(\varnothing)=-1\) extend affine-dimension notation but remain explicit conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit empty-set conventions; these must not be inferred from nonempty affine geometry.

children.title: Boundedness-Pointedness-Lineality Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Regimes separating vertex-dominated geometry from ray and lineality phenomena.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Define \(R:=\operatorname{rec}P\) and \(L:=R\cap(-R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The taxonomy applies to nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedra and separates compact, ray-bearing, and line-bearing geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The boundedness–pointedness–lineality class of \(P\) is determined by the inclusions \(\{0\}\subseteq L\subseteq R\). The polyhedron is bounded exactly when \(R=\{0\}\); pointed exactly when \(L=\{0\}\), equivalently when it contains no affine line; pointed unbounded exactly when \(L=\{0\}\) and \(R\neq\{0\}\); and nonpointed exactly when \(L\neq\{0\}\). If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), then \(R=\{d\mid Ad\leq0\}\) and \(L=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron, its recession cone contains all directions of infinite feasible motion and its lineality space contains the directions permitting motion in both signs. The set is bounded precisely when it has no nonzero recession direction. It is pointed precisely when it contains no line. Thus the three mutually exclusive regimes are bounded, pointed but unbounded, and nonpointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(R=\{0\}\), \(L=\{0\}\subsetneq R\), or \(\{0\}\subsetneq L\subseteq R\) holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in L\) if and only if \(P+d=P\), and then \(x+\mathbb Rd\subseteq P\) for every \(x\in P\).
A nonempty closed convex set is bounded if and only if its recession cone contains no nonzero vector.
special_cases_latex: Every bounded polyhedron is pointed.
A nonzero affine subspace is nonpointed.
A pointed polyhedral cone has the origin as its unique possible extreme point and has no nonzero subspace.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonpointed nonempty closed convex set has no extreme points.
Writing \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\) separates lineality from a line-free transverse polyhedron.
boundary_notes: Unboundedness alone does not imply nonpointedness: a ray is pointed and unbounded.
Pointedness does not imply full dimensionality or boundedness.

children.title: Bounded Polyhedral Geometry
children.top_down_role: The regime with no nonzero recession directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Polyhedral Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is bounded exactly when its recession cone contains no direction other than zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define its recession cone by \[\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:x+td\in P\text{ for every }x\in P\text{ and }t\ge0\}.\] Then \[P\text{ is bounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}.\] If \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), then \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d:Ad\le0\}\), so boundedness is equivalent to the homogeneous system \(Ad\le0\) having only the zero solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is bounded if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness characterized by absence of nonzero recession directions.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the nonempty polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointed Unbounded Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is pointed and unbounded precisely when it has no lineality but has a nonzero recession direction; it then has vertices and a finite point-ray representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. It is pointed and unbounded if and only if \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\neq\{0\}\). In this regime, \(P\) has at least one vertex and admits finite sets \(V\subseteq P\) and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\setminus\{0\}\) such that \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R).\] The nonzero vectors in \(R\) may be chosen along the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is pointed and unbounded exactly when \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional characterization of the pointed, unbounded polyhedral regime.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron with recession cone \(R:=\operatorname{rec}P\) and lineality space \(L:=R\cap(-R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime contains unbounded polyhedra with rays but no affine lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) has pointed unbounded geometry when \(R\neq\{0\}\) and \(L=\{0\}\). Equivalently, \(P\) is unbounded and contains no affine line. In this regime \(P\) admits a finite representation \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\), where \(p\geq1\), at least one \(r_j\neq0\), and the recession cone \(R=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is pointed unbounded when it has at least one nonzero recession direction but no direction whose positive and negative both permit indefinite motion. Equivalently, it is unbounded but contains no line. Its Minkowski–Weyl representation has finitely many point generators and at least one ray generator, while the cone generated by the rays has zero lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ pointed unbounded}\iff\operatorname{rec}P\neq\{0\}\text{ and }\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)=\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set, absence of affine lines is equivalent to existence of an extreme point.
If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), pointedness is equivalent to \(\ker A=\{0\}\), while unboundedness is equivalent to the existence of \(d\neq0\) with \(Ad\leq0\).
special_cases_latex: A ray \(x_0+\mathbb R_+d\) with \(d\neq0\) is pointed and unbounded.
A pointed polyhedral cone other than \(\{0\}\) is a pointed unbounded polyhedron.
immediate_consequences_latex: A pointed unbounded polyhedron has at least one vertex and finitely many vertices and extreme rays.
Its unboundedness is represented entirely by one-sided rays, never by a lineality subspace.
boundary_notes: Having a vertex does not imply boundedness.
A generating list may contain opposite rays redundantly; pointedness concerns the generated cone, not the syntax of a chosen list.

children.title: Nonpointed Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometry containing nontrivial lineality and possibly no vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpointed Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron is nonpointed exactly when it contains a nonzero lineality direction. In that case every point lies on a line contained in the polyhedron, so the polyhedron has no extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)=\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap-\operatorname{rec}(P)\). Then \(P\) is nonpointed if and only if \(L\neq\{0\}\). If \(L\neq\{0\}\), then \(x+td\in P\) for every \(x\in P\), \(d\in L\), and \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(P\) has no extreme points or vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is nonpointed exactly when \(\operatorname{lin}(P)\neq\{0\}\), in which case \(P\) has no extreme points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonpointed polyhedra and their lineality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, with \(R:=\operatorname{rec}P\) and \(L:=R\cap(-R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This regime consists precisely of line-bearing nonempty polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) has nonpointed geometry when \(L\neq\{0\}\). Equivalently, there exist \(x\in P\) and \(d\neq0\) such that \(x+td\in P\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\); indeed this then holds for every \(x\in P\). The lineality decomposition is \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\), where \(P\cap L^\perp\) is a polyhedron containing no affine line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is nonpointed exactly when its lineality space contains a nonzero vector. This means the polyhedron contains a full affine line and is invariant under translation by every lineality vector. It decomposes as the sum of its lineality subspace and a transverse polyhedron in the orthogonal complement that contains no line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ nonpointed}\iff L\neq\{0\}\iff\exists x\in P,\ d\neq0:\ x+\mathbb Rd\subseteq P\), and \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in L\) if and only if \(P+d=P\).
If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), then \(L=\ker A\), so nonpointedness is equivalent to \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\).
special_cases_latex: Every affine subspace of positive dimension is nonpointed.
A strip such as \(\{x\in\mathbb R^2\mid0\leq x_1\leq1\}\) is nonpointed with lineality parallel to the \(x_2\)-axis.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonpointed nonempty closed convex set has no extreme points.
A nonpointed polyhedron is necessarily unbounded.
boundary_notes: A polyhedron may be unbounded while pointed; nonpointedness specifically requires two-sided recession.
The transverse factor \(P\cap L^\perp\) depends on the selected inner product, although the quotient geometry modulo \(L\) does not.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal complement of the lineality space.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). All matrices and generator lists below have finitely many rows or columns.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition organizes external, generator, homogeneous, and lifted finite descriptions in finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite representation of \(P\) is any finite data system defining \(P\) in one of the equivalent polyhedral forms: an external form \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\); a generator form \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\) for nonempty \(P\); a homogeneous slice \(P=\{x\mid(x,1)\in K\}\) of a polyhedral cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\); or a lifted form \(P=\{x\mid\exists y:\ A x+B y\leq c,\ F x+G y=h\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite representation describes a polyhedron using finitely many inequalities and equations, finitely many point and ray generators, a slice of a finitely generated homogeneous cone, or the projection of a polyhedron in a higher-dimensional space. These forms encode the same class of nonempty polyhedral sets, although their sizes and auxiliary variables may differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite external, point-and-ray, homogeneous-slice, and lifted-projection descriptions all define polyhedral sets; every nonempty polyhedron has external, generator, and homogeneous-slice descriptions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Minkowski–Weyl gives \(\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\) for suitable finite \(V\neq\varnothing\) and \(R\).
A lifted form is the coordinate projection of the polyhedron \(Q:=\{(x,y)\mid Ax+By\leq c,\ Fx+Gy=h\}\).
special_cases_latex: A polytope requires no ray generators.
A polyhedral cone requires no affine normalization other than the homogeneous coordinate \(0\).
An ordinary external description is a lifted description with no auxiliary variable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different finite representations of the same polyhedron need not have the same number of inequalities, generators, or auxiliary variables.
Linear images and coordinate projections of polyhedra are polyhedral.
boundary_notes: Equivalence concerns the represented set, not equality of the representation data.
The generator form displayed for nonempty sets does not directly represent the empty polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^p\). Inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: External representations describe finite-dimensional polyhedra as intersections of halfspaces and affine hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An external representation of a set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a finite system \((A,b,F,g)\) such that \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\). Each row \(a_i^Tx\leq b_i\) specifies a closed halfspace and each row \(f_j^Tx=g_j\) specifies an affine hyperplane, so \(P\) is their finite intersection. Equality rows may be replaced by paired opposite inequalities without changing \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external representation specifies a set by finitely many weak linear inequalities and affine equations. Geometrically, the represented polyhedron is the intersection of the corresponding closed halfspaces and hyperplanes. Equations can be encoded as pairs of opposite inequalities, so a pure finite halfspace description is equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\mid a_i^Tx\leq b_i\}\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^p\{x\mid f_j^Tx=g_j\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(Fx=g\iff Fx\leq g\text{ and }-Fx\leq-g\).
The representation is an inverse image \(P=(x\mapsto(Ax,Fx))^{-1}((-\infty,b]\times\{g\}))\), with the interval interpreted componentwise.
special_cases_latex: With \(m=0\), the representation defines an affine set.
With \(p=0\), it is a pure halfspace or H-description.
An inconsistent system represents \(\varnothing\), and the empty system represents \(\mathbb R^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every externally represented set is closed and convex.
For nonempty \(P\), \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{d\mid Ad\leq0,\ Fd=0\}\).
boundary_notes: The same polyhedron generally has many external representations, including redundant ones.
Strict inequalities do not define closed polyhedra under this convention.

knowledge_statements.title: H-Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An H-representation describes a polyhedron by finitely many linear inequalities and equations, and every finite-dimensional polyhedron admits such a description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For matrices \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) and vectors \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\), the set \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\] is a polyhedron, and the displayed finite system is an H-representation of \(P\). Conversely, every polyhedron in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) has such a representation. Equations may equivalently be replaced by paired inequalities, although retaining them explicitly records the affine hull more economically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\) is an H-representation of a polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Write \(a_i^T\) for row \(i\) of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The H-representation is the pure finite-halfspace form; affine equations are encoded by paired inequalities when necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An H-representation of \(P\) is a finite pair \((A,b)\) satisfying \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b\}=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\mid a_i^Tx\leq b_i\}\). A mixed representation \(Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\) is converted to H-form by adjoining the rows \(F\) and \(-F\) with right-hand sides \(g\) and \(-g\). The representation is homogeneous precisely when \(b=0\), in which case it defines a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An H-representation is a description of a polyhedron as the intersection of finitely many closed halfspaces. Any affine equations can be included by replacing each equation with its two opposite weak inequalities. When every right-hand side is zero, all boundary hyperplanes pass through the origin and the represented set is a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), with mixed systems encoded as \(\begin{bmatrix}A\\F\\-F\end{bmatrix}x\leq\begin{bmatrix}b\\g\\-g\end{bmatrix}\).

Its lineality space is \(\operatorname{lin}P=\{d\mid Ad=0\}=\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: A single row gives a closed halfspace.
Opposite proportional rows with matching right-hand sides can encode a hyperplane.
No rows gives \(\mathbb R^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: H-represented sets are closed and convex.
Feasibility, boundedness, and lineality are properties of the represented system but are invariant under replacement by an equivalent H-representation.
boundary_notes: An H-representation need not be irredundant or unique.
A row with zero normal is either vacuous or makes the system infeasible, depending on its right-hand side.

children.title: Standard-Form Slack-Lift Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equality and nonnegativity descriptions in lifted spaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Introduce \(s\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The correspondence converts weak linear inequalities into affine equations plus nonnegativity in a lifted finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The slack lift of \(P\) is \(Q:=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\mid Ax+s=b,\ Fx=g,\ s\geq0\}\). Its coordinate projection satisfies \(P=\{x\mid\exists s:\ (x,s)\in Q\}\), and the projection \((x,s)\mapsto x\) is bijective on \(Q\) because the unique slack associated with \(x\in P\) is \(s=b-Ax\). If nonnegative variables are required throughout, write \(x=x^+-x^-\) with \(x^+,x^-\geq0\), giving an equality-and-nonnegativity lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each inequality row, a nonnegative slack variable records the unused margin. The system \(Ax\leq b\) is therefore equivalent to the existence of \(s\geq0\) satisfying \(Ax+s=b\). Feasible points and lifted feasible points correspond one-to-one because the slack is uniquely \(b-Ax\). Splitting every unrestricted coordinate into the difference of two nonnegative variables yields a standard-form description using only equalities and nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P\iff\exists!s\geq0:\ Ax+s=b,\ Fx=g\), where \(s=b-Ax\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P=\pi_x(Q)\), where \(\pi_x(x,s)=x\).
With \(x=x^+-x^-\), \(P\) is the image of \(\{(x^+,x^-,s)\geq0\mid A(x^+-x^-)+s=b,\ F(x^+-x^-)=g\}\) under \((x^+,x^-,s)\mapsto x^+-x^-\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), no slack variables are needed.
An active inequality at \(x\) has slack component \(s_i=0\); a strict inequality has \(s_i>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The slack lift is a polyhedron in \(\mathbb R^{n+m}\).
Faces determined by active inequalities correspond to coordinate faces of the slack nonnegative orthant.
boundary_notes: The split \(x=x^+-x^-\) is not unique, unlike the slack vector associated with a fixed \(x\).
Slack lifting preserves the represented feasible set under projection but increases ambient dimension.

notation.meaning: Projection from the lifted space onto the original coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Representations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard form expresses a polyhedron using linear equations and componentwise nonnegative variables; projections and affine images allow it to represent general polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard-form polyhedron is a set \[Q=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:Az=b,\ z\ge0\},\] where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the inequality is componentwise. More generally, an affine image or coordinate projection of such a set is a standard-form representation of the resulting polyhedron. Free variables can be replaced by differences of nonnegative variables, and finite inequalities can be converted into equalities by adjoining nonnegative slack variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:Az=b,\ z\ge0\}\) is a polyhedron in standard form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-plus-nonnegativity convention for standard-form polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack Coordinates Encode Constraint Activity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack coordinate is zero exactly for an active inequality and positive exactly for a strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the canonical slack lift \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\ge0\), every feasible pair satisfies \[s_i=b_i-a_i^\top x.\] Hence \[a_i^\top x=b_i\iff s_i=0,\qquad a_i^\top x<b_i\iff s_i>0.\] For any index set \(I\), points where all inequalities in \(I\) are active lift exactly to the coordinate section \(s_i=0\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^\top x=b_i\iff s_i=0,\qquad a_i^\top x<b_i\iff s_i>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise interpretation of canonical nonnegative slacks.

notation.meaning: Slack coordinate corresponding to the ith inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting of inequalities into equations with nonnegative auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m,p\) be nonnegative integers, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and set \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ Cx=d\}\). Define the slack lift \[\widehat P=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m:Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\geq0\}.\] For the projection \(\pi_x:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\pi_x(x,s)=x\), one has \(\pi_x(\widehat P)=P\). Moreover, every \(x\in P\) has the unique lifted slack \(s=b-Ax\), so \(x\mapsto(x,b-Ax)\) is a bijection from \(P\) onto \(\widehat P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing each inequality by an equality and a nonnegative slack gives an exact lift; every feasible original point has one uniquely determined slack vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(\widehat P)=P\), and \(x\mapsto(x,b-Ax)\) is a bijection from \(P\) onto \(\widehat P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Preserved by the Canonical Slack Isomorphism
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical slack bijection preserves the face structure, dimension, recession and lineality data, and boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\), let \(Q=\{(x,s):Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\ge0\}\), and define \(\phi(x)=(x,b-Ax)\). The affine isomorphism \(\phi:P\to Q\) induces a dimension-preserving bijection \[F\longmapsto\phi(F)\] between the faces of \(P\) and \(Q\). Moreover, \[\operatorname{rec}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\},\qquad \operatorname{lin}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{lin}(P)\}.\] Consequently, \(P\) and \(Q\) have the same dimension, are bounded simultaneously, and have corresponding vertices and face incidences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\mapsto\phi(F)\text{ is a dimension-preserving face-lattice isomorphism, and }\operatorname{rec}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face, dimension, recession, lineality, and boundedness consequences of the canonical slack bijection.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and optimization equivalence under the canonical slack lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m,p\) be nonnegative integers, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\). Define \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ Cx=d\}\) and \[\widehat P=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m:Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\geq0\}.\] For every objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), regarded on \(\widehat P\) through \((x,s)\mapsto f(x)\), \[\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=\inf_{(x,s)\in\widehat P}f(x).\] For every \(x^\star\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(x^\star\in P\) if and only if \((x^\star,b-Ax^\star)\in\widehat P\); moreover, \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f\) over \(P\) if and only if \((x^\star,b-Ax^\star)\) minimizes \((x,s)\mapsto f(x)\) over \(\widehat P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical slack lift preserves feasible points, objective values, infima, and minimizers, with unique slack insertion and projection translating points in both directions.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) depends only on the original variable \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=\inf_{(x,s)\in\widehat P}f(x)\), with feasible points and minimizers corresponding under \(x\mapsto(x,b-Ax)\).

notation.meaning: extended-real objective on the original variable space
candidate feasible point or minimizer in the original variable space

children.title: Irredundant External Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Minimal inequality systems and facet-defining constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Redundancy Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is redundant exactly when the remaining constraints imply it; this can be certified either by an optimization bound or by nonnegative Farkas multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) and let \[Q_{-i}=\{x:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},\ Cx=d\}\ne\varnothing.\] The row is redundant if and only if \[\sup_{x\in Q_{-i}}a_i^\top x\le b_i.\] Equivalently, it is redundant if and only if there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and a free vector \(\mu\) such that \[A_{-i}^\top\lambda+C^\top\mu=a_i,\qquad b_{-i}^\top\lambda+d^\top\mu\le b_i.\] If it is not redundant, any \(x\in Q_{-i}\) satisfying \(a_i^\top x>b_i\) is a witness of necessity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^\top x\le b_i\text{ is implied by }Q_{-i}\iff\exists\lambda\ge0,\mu:\ A_{-i}^\top\lambda+C^\top\mu=a_i,\ b_{-i}^\top\lambda+d^\top\mu\le b_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-wise primal witnesses and Farkas multiplier certificates for an external description.

notation.meaning: System obtained after deleting the ith inequality.
Nonnegative multipliers for the remaining inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Irredundant External Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-affine characterization of minimal inequality descriptions by facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty polyhedron of dimension \(d\) in its affine hull \(L\), represented as \(P=\{x\in L:a_i^\top x\leq b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), with no proportional duplicate inequalities. The description is irredundant exactly when removing any one inequality strictly enlarges the represented subset of \(L\). In an irredundant description, every set \(F_i=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\}\) is a facet, so \(\dim F_i=d-1\); conversely, one supporting inequality for each facet yields an irredundant description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to the affine hull, an inequality description is irredundant when every inequality is essential; its inequalities correspond exactly to distinct facets.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron of dimension \(d\) in \(L=\operatorname{aff}P\).
The external description has no proportional duplicate inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The description is irredundant exactly when its inequalities are essential; minimally, they correspond one-to-one with the facets of \(P\).

notation.meaning: face where the i-th inequality is active

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in M\mid a_i^Tx\leq b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\), where \(M=\operatorname{aff}P\) is explicitly represented by an independent affine-equation system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irredundancy is defined relative to the affine hull, so implicit equalities are separated from genuine facet inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The external description is irredundant when every listed inequality is indispensable: for each \(i\), \(\{x\in M\mid a_j^Tx\leq b_j\ \forall j\neq i\}\) strictly contains \(P\). Equivalently, for each \(i\) there exists \(x_i\in M\) satisfying \(a_j^Tx_i\leq b_j\) for all \(j\neq i\) but \(a_i^Tx_i>b_i\). An affine-equation subsystem is irredundant when its rows are independent and its solution set equals \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external description is irredundant when deleting any one inequality strictly enlarges the represented set within its affine hull. Equivalently, every inequality has a witness that satisfies all the other constraints but violates that inequality. The equations describing the affine hull are required to be independent. For a polyhedron that is full-dimensional relative to its affine hull, each nontrivial inequality in such a description supports a facet.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The description is irredundant iff \(\forall i\ \exists x_i\in M:\ a_j^Tx_i\leq b_j\ (j\neq i)\) and \(a_i^Tx_i>b_i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Deleting any inequality changes the feasible set.
When \(P\) is full-dimensional in \(M\), each indispensable valid inequality defines the facet \(P\cap\{x\in M\mid a_i^Tx=b_i\}\).
special_cases_latex: For a full-dimensional polytope, an irredundant H-description has one inequality for each facet, up to positive rescaling.
A zero row with a valid right-hand side is always redundant in a nonempty description.
immediate_consequences_latex: Duplicate inequalities and positive scalar multiples defining the same halfspace cannot both occur in an irredundant description.
Irredundancy is invariant under positive rescaling of individual inequalities.
boundary_notes: Without first extracting \(\operatorname{aff}P\), inequalities encoding implicit equalities may occur in opposite pairs and need not be facet-defining.
Irredundant descriptions are unique only up to ordering and positive scaling after the affine hull and facets are fixed.

notation.meaning: Affine hull relative to which redundancy is tested.

children.title: Generator Representations
children.top_down_role: Internal descriptions by points, rays, and lineality directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The representation applies to nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedra and explicitly separates bounded points, one-sided rays, and two-sided lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generator representation of a nonempty polyhedron \(P\) is a finite description \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\), meaning \(x\in P\) exactly when \(x=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_iv_i+\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_jr_j+\ell\), where \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), \(\mu_j\geq0\), and \(\ell\in L\). The lineality term may be absorbed into the conic list by including \(\ell_k\) and \(-\ell_k\) for a basis \(\{\ell_k\}\) of \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generator representation expresses every point of a nonempty polyhedron as a convex combination of finitely many point generators, plus a nonnegative combination of finitely many ray generators, plus an arbitrary lineality vector. Conversely, every such finite point–ray–lineality expression defines a polyhedron. Lineality can alternatively be represented by including both signs of each basis direction among the ray generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\left\{\sum_i\lambda_iv_i+\sum_j\mu_jr_j+\ell\mid\lambda\geq0,\ \mathbf1^T\lambda=1,\ \mu\geq0,\ \ell\in L\right\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Absorbing a basis of \(L\) with both signs gives \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}\widetilde R\).
In homogeneous coordinates, \(P=\{x\mid(x,1)\in\operatorname{cone}(\{(v_i,1)\}_i\cup\{(r_j,0)\}_j\cup\{(\pm\ell_k,0)\}_k)\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(R=\varnothing\) and \(L=\{0\}\), then \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\) is a polytope.
If \(p=1\) and the point is \(0\), the representation describes a polyhedral cone.
For pointed \(P\), one may take \(L=\{0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}P=\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
A finite generator representation determines a closed convex set and hence a polyhedron by Minkowski–Weyl.
boundary_notes: At least one point generator is required for a nonempty affine slice with coefficients summing to one.
Generator lists are generally nonunique and may contain nonextreme points, redundant rays, or lineality hidden as opposite rays.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Representations of Polytopes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty polytope is the convex hull of its finitely many vertices, and every convex hull of finitely many points is a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polytope, then its vertex set \(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) is finite and \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)=\left\{\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv:\lambda_v\ge0,\ \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1\right\}.\] Conversely, the convex hull of every nonempty finite set in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is a polytope. Any finite point representation of \(P\) must contain every vertex of \(P\), although it may also contain nonvertex points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{vert}(P))\), and \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex representation for nonempty bounded polyhedra.

notation.meaning: Set of vertices of the polytope

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, convex, and bounded. A point \(v\in P\) is a vertex, equivalently an extreme point, when \(v=(1-\lambda)x+\lambda y\), \(x,y\in P\), and \(0<\lambda<1\) imply \(x=y=v\). Write \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) for the set of vertices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, nonempty, bounded polyhedra. The definition uses all vertices, not an arbitrary finite generating set containing redundant nonvertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vertex representation of \(P\) is the equality \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i v^i:\lambda_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i=1\right\},\qquad V=\operatorname{vert}(P)=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}.\] Thus every \(x\in P\) is a convex combination of vertices, and every listed generator is a vertex of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex representation writes a nonempty polytope as the convex hull of its finite set of vertices. Every point of the polytope is a convex combination of those vertices, and no listed point is merely a redundant nonvertex generator.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
\(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) denotes the set of all extreme points of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{vert}(P))\), with \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) finite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(x\in P\), there exist \(\lambda_v\geq0\) for \(v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)\) such that \(\sum_v\lambda_v=1\) and \(x=\sum_v\lambda_vv\).
A set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) admits such a finite vertex representation exactly when it is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
special_cases_latex: If \(P=\{v\}\), then \(\operatorname{vert}(P)=\{v\}\).
If \(P\) is a line segment with distinct endpoints \(u,v\), then \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{u,v\}\) and these endpoints are its vertices.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any finite set \(W\) satisfying \(P=\operatorname{conv}(W)\) must contain every vertex of \(P\).
A linear functional attaining a unique maximum over \(P\) attains it at a vertex.
boundary_notes: The empty polytope is excluded because it has no nonempty convex-combination representation.
For unbounded polyhedra, vertices alone do not generate the set; recession directions are also required.
An arbitrary finite equality \(P=\operatorname{conv}(W)\) is a point-generator representation, but it is a vertex representation only when \(W=\operatorname{vert}(P)\).

notation.meaning: set of vertices, or extreme points, of the polytope
convex hull of the point set

knowledge_statements.title: Point–Ray Representations of Pointed Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty pointed polyhedron is the sum of the convex hull of its vertices and the cone generated by its recession cone's extreme rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron. Its vertex set \(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) is nonempty and finite, and its recession cone has finitely many extreme rays. Choosing one nonzero generator for each such ray gives a finite set \(R\) satisfying \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R).\] Equivalently, every \(x\in P\) can be written as \(x=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv+\sum_{r\in R}\mu_rr\), where \(\lambda_v\ge0\), \(\sum_v\lambda_v=1\), and \(\mu_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) for finite vertex and extreme-ray generators \(V,R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski–Weyl representation specialized to pointed polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite point–ray representation of a pointed polyhedron
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron, meaning that its lineality space \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\{d:x+td\in P\ \forall x\in P,\ \forall t\in\mathbb R\}\) equals \(\{0\}\). Let \(V=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}\subseteq P\) and let \(R=\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\setminus\{0\}\) be finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, nonempty, pointed polyhedra. Rays account for unboundedness; no lineality generators occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite point–ray representation of \(P\) is an equality \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i v^i+\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_jr^j:\lambda\geq0,\ \mathbf1^\top\lambda=1,\ \mu\geq0\right\}.\] In a canonical extreme representation, \(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) and the members of \(R\) generate the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\), one nonzero representative per ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point–ray representation writes a nonempty pointed polyhedron as the Minkowski sum of the convex hull of finitely many points and the cone generated by finitely many recession directions. A canonical extreme representation uses all vertices and one generator for each extreme recession ray.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty pointed polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every \(x\in P\) admits coefficients \(\lambda_i,\mu_j\geq0\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\) and \(x=\sum_i\lambda_iv^i+\sum_j\mu_jr^j\).
The recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\operatorname{cone}(R)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is bounded, then \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}\), so the ray term disappears and \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\).
If \(P=v+K\) for a pointed polyhedral cone \(K\), one may take \(V=\{v\}\) and any finite ray-generating set for \(K\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The bounded and unbounded components are separated as \(\operatorname{conv}(V)\) and \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\).
Because \(P\) is pointed, it has no nonzero direction whose positive and negative multiples both belong to \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\).

Ray representatives are defined only up to multiplication by a positive scalar.
The representation need not be irredundant unless extremality and nonduplication are imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession and Paired-Direction Forms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone combines one-sided rays with lineality, which may equivalently be represented by paired positive and negative generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\) and suppose \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\), with \(\operatorname{cone}(R)\) pointed modulo \(L\). Then \[\operatorname{rec}(P)=\operatorname{cone}(R)+L,\qquad \operatorname{lin}(P)=L.\] If a finite set \(D\) spans \(L\), equivalently \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R\cup D\cup(-D)).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\), and a spanning set of \(L\) yields an equivalent paired-direction representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent encodings of the lineality component in a finite generator representation.

notation.meaning: Finite spanning set of the lineality space

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Aware Generator Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator representation separating the lineality space from the pointed quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\). There exist finite sets \(X\subseteq P\) and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\) such that
\[P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L.\]
For the quotient map \(q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d/L\), the quotient \(q(P)\) is pointed and satisfies
\[q(P)=\operatorname{conv}(q(X))+\operatorname{cone}(q(R)).\]
Thus generators in \(R\) need only describe the recession cone modulo lineality; a basis of \(L\) supplies all two-sided directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polyhedron is generated by finitely many points, finitely many one-sided recession directions, and its lineality space; quotienting by lineality produces a pointed polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\).

notation.meaning: quotient map modulo the lineality space
finite point and recession-direction generator sets

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Set \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)=\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap(-\operatorname{rec}(P))\). Choose finite point generators \(V\subseteq P\), finite recession generators \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\), and vectors \(B=\{\ell^1,\ldots,\ell^s\}\) spanning \(L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite-dimensional nonempty polyhedra, including polyhedra containing lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lineality-aware generator representation is \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(B),\] or explicitly \[P=\left\{\sum_i\lambda_iv^i+\sum_j\mu_jr^j+\sum_k\nu_k\ell^k:\lambda,\mu\geq0,\ \mathbf1^\top\lambda=1,\ \nu\in\mathbb R^s\right\},\] where \(\operatorname{span}(B)=L\) and the images of \(R\) generate the pointed cone \(\operatorname{rec}(P)/L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lineality-aware representation decomposes a general nonempty polyhedron into a bounded convex-combination component, a one-sided recession-cone component modulo lineality, and a linear-space component whose coefficients may have either sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\), with \(L=\operatorname{span}(B)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: After choosing an inner product and \(P_0=P\cap L^\perp\), one has \(P=P_0+L\), where \(P_0\) contains no lines and has a point–ray representation.
Under the quotient map \(\pi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n/L\), \(\pi(P)=\operatorname{conv}(\pi(V))+\operatorname{cone}(\pi(R))\) is pointed.
special_cases_latex: If \(L=\{0\}\), the span term vanishes and the representation becomes a point–ray representation.
If \(P\) is an affine space \(v+L\), one may take \(V=\{v\}\) and \(R=\varnothing\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every \(d\in L\) may be added to or subtracted from every point of \(P\).
The recession cone decomposes as \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\).
boundary_notes: The separation between \(R\) and \(B\) is not unique until a complement of \(L\) or quotient normalization is chosen.
Including both \(\ell\) and \(-\ell\) as ray generators represents lineality but does not expose its linear-space structure.
The empty polyhedron is excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Data Are Not Literally Unique Without Normalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generator descriptions are nonunique under positive ray scaling, lineality shifts, basis changes, and duplicate representatives, so irredundancy requires explicit normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a representation \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L,\] the represented polyhedron is unchanged if a ray generator \(r\) is replaced by \(\alpha r\) with \(\alpha>0\), if a point or ray representative is shifted by an element of \(L\), or if a basis of \(L\) is replaced by another basis. Adding duplicate quotient-point or quotient-ray representatives also leaves \(P\) unchanged but destroys deletion irredundancy. Consequently, uniqueness claims for irredundant generator data are meaningful only modulo positive ray scaling, lineality, choice of lineality basis, and an explicit no-duplicate convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Literal uniqueness of }(V,R,D)\text{ fails without quotient and normalization conventions.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness caused by scaling, lineality shifts, duplicate representatives, and changes of lineality basis.

notation.meaning: Lineality space of the represented polyhedron.
A positive rescaling of a ray representative.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Characterization of Lineality-Aware Irredundancy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After quotienting out lineality, irredundant point and ray generators are exactly the quotient vertices and extreme recession rays, while the lineality generators form a basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty polyhedron with lineality space \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\), let \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n/L\) be the quotient map, and suppose \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(D),\qquad \operatorname{span}(D)=L,\] with finite sets and \(q(r)\ne0\) for every \(r\in R\). Under deletion irredundancy and the convention that duplicate quotient point images and duplicate quotient rays are forbidden: (i) \(D\) is a basis of \(L\); (ii) \(q(V)\) is exactly the vertex set of \(q(P)\), with one lift for each vertex; and (iii) the rays \(\mathbb{R}_+q(r)\), \(r\in R\), are exactly the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(q(P))\), with one representative per ray. Conversely, data satisfying (i)–(iii) give a deletion-irredundant description under these conventions.
assumptions_latex: Duplicate quotient point images and duplicate quotient rays are disallowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is a basis of }L,\quad q(V)=\operatorname{vert}(q(P)),\quad\{\mathbb{R}_+q(r):r\in R\}=\operatorname{ExtRays}(\operatorname{rec}(q(P))).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic characterization after quotienting out the lineality space.

notation.meaning: Quotient map modulo the lineality space.
Set of extreme rays of a cone K.

knowledge_statements.title: Irredundant Generator Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-minimal point, ray, and lineality generators characterized through the pointed quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\), and let \(q:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d/L\) be the quotient map. Consider a finite representation
\[P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(B),\]
where \(X\subseteq P\), \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\), and \(B\subseteq L\). This representation is irredundant in its point, ray, and lineality generators precisely when \(q(X)\) contains exactly one representative of each vertex of \(q(P)\), \(q(R)\) contains exactly one nonzero representative of each extreme ray of \(\operatorname{rec}(q(P))\), and \(B\) is a basis of \(L\). Under these conditions, deleting any member of \(X\), \(R\), or \(B\) changes the represented set or its lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An irredundant generator description uses one lift of each vertex and extreme recession ray of the pointed quotient, together with a basis of the lineality space; deleting any selected generator changes the description.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(R\), and \(B\) are finite generator sets with \(X\subseteq P\), \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\), and \(B\subseteq L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(X)\) represents exactly the vertices of \(q(P)\), \(q(R)\) represents exactly the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(q(P))\), and \(B\) is a basis of \(L\).

notation.meaning: quotient map modulo the lineality space
finite point, ray, and lineality-basis generator sets

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(B)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where all three generator sets are finite, \(B\) spans \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\), and recession rays are compared modulo \(L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite point, ray, and lineality generator systems. Irredundancy is defined relative to the appropriate geometric type of each generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The triple \((V,R,B)\) is irredundant when \[P
eq\operatorname{conv}(V\setminus\{v\})+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(B)\quad( orall v\in V),\] \[P
eq\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R\setminus\{r\})+\operatorname{span}(B)\quad( orall r\in R),\] and \[\operatorname{span}(B\setminus\{\ell\})
eq\operatorname{span}(B)\quad( orall\ell\in B).\] Thus no point, ray, or lineality generator can be deleted without changing the represented polyhedron or its lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite generator description is irredundant if deleting any point generator or ray generator changes the represented polyhedron, and deleting any lineality generator changes the spanned lineality space.
assumptions_latex: No two members of \(R\) are positive scalar multiples modulo \(\operatorname{lin}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generator in \(V\cup R\cup B\) is indispensable in its corresponding deletion test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lineality condition is equivalent to linear independence of \(B\).
In the pointed case, canonical irredundancy is obtained by taking all vertices and one nonzero representative of every extreme ray of \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\).
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, \(R=B=\varnothing\), and irredundancy means \(v\notin\operatorname{conv}(V\setminus\{v\})\) for every \(v\in V\).
For a pointed polyhedral cone, the origin need not be listed as a point generator; irredundancy concerns one representative per extreme ray.
immediate_consequences_latex: In an irredundant polytope representation, the point generators are exactly the vertices.
An irredundant basis of the lineality space has cardinality \(\dim L\).
boundary_notes: Irredundancy does not make ray scaling or the choice of a lineality basis unique.
For nonpointed polyhedra, deletion tests must prevent a nominal ray from being reproducible by other rays together with lineality.
Minimal cardinality and inclusionwise irredundancy coincide in the standard extreme-generator regimes but are conceptually distinct notions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in \(\mathbb R^n\). An H-representation is \(P=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) with finitely many inequalities. A finite generator representation is \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) with finite \(V,R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real polyhedra, including bounded, unbounded, pointed, and nonpointed cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Minkowski–Weyl representation class consists of precisely those sets \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) for which the following equivalent finite descriptions exist: \[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\] for some finite matrix–vector pair \((A,b)\), and \[P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\] for finite point and direction sets. Lineality may be encoded by opposite rays or displayed separately as a linear-space summand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minkowski–Weyl theory identifies the same finite-dimensional sets in two ways: intersections of finitely many affine halfspaces and sums of a finitely generated polytope with a finitely generated cone.
assumptions_latex: All constraint, point-generator, and ray-generator families are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron if and only if \(P=Q+C\) for some polytope \(Q\) and finitely generated cone \(C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P\) is polyhedral if and only if there exist finite \(V,R\) with \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\).
The homogeneous specialization says that \(C=\{x:Ax\leq0\}\) if and only if \(C=\operatorname{cone}(R)\) for a finite \(R\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is bounded, the cone summand is \(\{0\}\), yielding the polytope equivalence.
If \(P\) is a cone, the affine right-hand side is zero and no nonzero point component is needed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every polyhedron has a finitely generated recession cone.
Finite linear images of polyhedra are polyhedra because generator descriptions are preserved by linear maps.
boundary_notes: The result is finite-dimensional; analogous statements require additional closure or compactness qualifications in infinite-dimensional spaces.
Neither the H-representation nor the generator representation is generally unique.
The empty-set convention requires separate handling because a convex hull generated by at least one point is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of a polytope and a cone
componentwise finite system of affine inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty set is a bounded polyhedron exactly when it is the convex hull of finitely many points; its vertices provide a canonical finite generating set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty. The following are equivalent: \(P\) is a bounded polyhedron, meaning \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) for some finite system and \(P\) is bounded; and there exists a nonempty finite set \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V).\] Moreover, when these conditions hold, \(V\) may be chosen as the finite vertex set \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\). Thus finite bounded H-representations and finite vertex representations describe exactly the class of nonempty polytopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a bounded polyhedron if and only if it is the convex hull of finitely many points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded finite-dimensional case of the Minkowski–Weyl theorem.

notation.meaning: Convex hull of a finite point set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonempty bounded sets in the polyhedral regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfies the bounded representation equivalence when \[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\ \text{for finitely many inequalities and }P\text{ is bounded}\] if and only if \[P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}\ \text{for finitely many points}.\] Such a set is called a polytope; it may canonically be generated by \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty bounded polyhedron is exactly the convex hull of finitely many points. Conversely, every convex hull of finitely many points has a finite halfspace description and is bounded.
assumptions_latex: The H-system or V-generator family under consideration is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a bounded polyhedron if and only if \(P\) is a polytope.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P\) is a bounded polyhedron if and only if \(P=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{vert}(P))\) and \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) is finite.
In a Minkowski–Weyl representation \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), boundedness is equivalent to \(\operatorname{cone}(R)=\{0\}\).

A bounded polyhedron may lie in a proper affine subspace; full dimensionality is not required.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every linear functional attains both its minimum and maximum on a nonempty polytope.
A polytope has finitely many faces and finitely many vertices.
boundary_notes: Closedness is automatic from either finite representation but is not by itself sufficient for finite representability.
Unbounded polyhedra require ray generators and therefore fall outside this bounded equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality Obstructs Vertex Generation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonzero lineality eliminates vertices and prevents a vertices-only point component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a nonempty polyhedron \(P\) has nonzero lineality, then it has no vertices. Consequently, a general Minkowski–Weyl representation cannot replace its point representatives and explicit lineality component by the vertices of \(P\). The vertices-plus-extreme-rays specialization requires pointedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}P\ne\{0\}\) implies \(\operatorname{vert}P=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary requiring an explicit linear component in the general representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession and Lineality of a Point–Ray Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ray and linear terms recover the recession cone and its maximal linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(L)\) with finite \(V\ne\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{rec}P=\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(L)\) and \(\operatorname{lin}P=\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)\). The generators may be chosen with \(\operatorname{span}(L)=\operatorname{lin}P\), while the images of \(R\) generate the pointed quotient \(\operatorname{rec}P/\operatorname{lin}P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}P=\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(L)\) and \(\operatorname{lin}P=\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the intrinsic unbounded components.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Minkowski–Weyl equivalence for arbitrary nonempty polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty set \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), the following are equivalent: there exist \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\leq b\};\]
and there exist a finite nonempty set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and a finite set \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) such that
\[P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R).\]
Equivalently, the generator data may be chosen so that lineality is displayed explicitly:
\[P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R_0)+L,\]
where \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\) and the image of \(\operatorname{cone}(R_0)\) in \(\mathbb{R}^d/L\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty set is a polyhedron exactly when it is the sum of the convex hull of finitely many points and a finitely generated cone. Its lineality space may instead be displayed as a separate summand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\leq b\}\iff P=\operatorname{conv}(X)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) for suitable finite data.

notation.meaning: finite inequality count, matrix, and right-hand-side vector

The quotient recession cone modulo \(\operatorname{lin}(P)\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general nonempty polyhedron has a finite inequality description exactly when it has finitely many point generators, finitely many one-sided recession generators, and a finite basis for its lineality space.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) has a finite H-description if and only if \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(B)\) for finite \(V,R,B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Exchange of Finite Conic Descriptions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative polarity exchanges finite conic generators and finite homogeneous inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\), then \(K^\circ=\{y:r_i^{\mathsf T}y\le0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Conversely, if \(K=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}\), then \(K^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite V- and H-descriptions of cones are exchanged by negative polarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator/inequality exchange under the negative-polar convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray and Lineality Generation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral cone is its lineality space plus finitely many lifted quotient-extreme rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a polyhedral cone and \(L:=K\cap(-K)\). The quotient cone \(K/L\) is pointed and has finitely many extreme rays. Choosing one lift from each such ray gives a finite set \(R\) with \(K=L+\operatorname{cone}(R)\). If \(K\) is pointed, its extreme rays are finite and every generating family contains a vector on each extreme ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=L+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) for finitely many representatives of the extreme rays of \(K/L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical geometric form of finite conic generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Finite-Generation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous Minkowski–Weyl equivalence for finite-dimensional convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), the following are equivalent: there exist \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\) such that
\[K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\leq0\};\]
and there exist \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) and vectors \(r_1,\ldots,r_p\in\mathbb{R}^d\) such that
\[K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_p\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i r_i:\lambda_i\geq0\right\}.\]
Lineality is permitted and may be represented by including both directions of each vector in a basis of the lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone is the intersection of finitely many homogeneous halfspaces exactly when it is the conic hull of finitely many vectors; lineality is allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is polyhedral}\iff K\text{ is finitely generated}.\)

notation.meaning: finite inequality count and homogeneous inequality matrix
finite number and list of conic generators

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A polyhedral cone has a homogeneous H-description \(C=\{x:Ax\leq0\}\). A finitely generated cone has a V-description \(C=\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real convex cones; pointedness is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conic finite-generation equivalence identifies the two classes \[\left\{C:C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq0\}\text{ for a finite }A\right\}\] and \[\left\{C:C=\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\text{ for finitely many }r^j\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.\] Equivalently, a cone is polyhedral if and only if it is finitely generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex cone is the intersection of finitely many homogeneous halfspaces exactly when it is the set of all nonnegative combinations of finitely many vectors.
assumptions_latex: The inequality rows or generator vectors are finite in number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a polyhedral cone if and only if \(C\) is a finitely generated cone.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist matrices \(A\) and \(R\) such that \(C=\{x:Ax\leq0\}=\{R\mu:\mu\geq0\}\).
If \(C\) is pointed and nonzero, it is generated by one representative of each of its finitely many extreme rays.
special_cases_latex: The zero cone is \(\{0\}=\operatorname{cone}(\varnothing)\) under the empty-generation convention and also has a homogeneous finite H-description.
A linear subspace is polyhedral and can be generated conically by the positive and negative vectors of any finite basis.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every polyhedral cone is closed.
Every linear image of a polyhedral cone is again polyhedral.
boundary_notes: A finitely generated cone need not be pointed because opposite generators may create lines.
Generators are nonunique and may be rescaled positively or be redundant.
Closed convex cones that are not polyhedral generally require infinitely many inequalities or generators.

notation.meaning: all nonnegative linear combinations of the columns of R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Conversion of Finite Conic Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite generator/inequality conversion under the negative-polar convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\), its negative polar is \(K^\circ=\{y:r_i^{\mathsf T}y\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\}\). Conversely, if \(K=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\}\), then \(K^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\). Hence finite V-to-H and H-to-V conic conversion are polar operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the polar exchanges finite conic generators with finite homogeneous inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The negative polar is \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite generators of one cone are finite defining inequalities of its polar, and conversely.

children.title: Carathéodory Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Dimension-controlled reduction of point and ray representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Dependence Elimination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated coefficient moves along lifted dependencies remove generators while preserving the represented point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lift the positively weighted point generators to \((v_i,1)\) and ray generators to \((r_j,0)\). Whenever these lifted generators are linearly dependent, move their nonnegative coefficients maximally along a nonzero dependence in a sign that preserves nonnegativity until at least one positive coefficient becomes zero. Deleting zero coefficients and repeating leaves \((x,1)\) unchanged and terminates with linearly independent positive generators.
assumptions_latex: An explicit finite feasible point–ray representation with \(k\) positive coefficients is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After at most \(k-1\) eliminations, the remaining positive generators are linearly independent and number at most \(\dim\operatorname{span}(G)\le d+1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive sparsification of an explicitly supplied finite representation.

notation.meaning: Matrix or family of lifted generators

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of Carathéodory Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplexes and simplicial cones show that the dimension bounds are sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relative-interior point of a \(d\)-simplex requires all \(d+1\) vertices in every representation using those vertices. If \(r_1,\ldots,r_d\) are linearly independent, a relative-interior point of \(\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_d\}\) requires all \(d\) rays. Thus the uniform convex bound \(d+1\), the conic bound \(d\), and the joint point–ray bound \(d+1\) cannot be reduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uniform bounds \(d+1\) and \(d\) are sharp in their respective regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case sharpness of convex, conic, and joint bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Point–Ray Carathéodory Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization reduces any point-plus-ray representation to at most d+1 generators in total.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:=\{(v,1):v\in V\}\cup\{(r,0):r\in R\}\subseteq\mathbb R^{d+1}\). If \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), then \((x,1)\in\operatorname{cone}(G)\) has a representation using at most \(\dim\operatorname{span}(G)\le d+1\) linearly independent generators. Consequently, \(x\) has a point–ray representation using at most \(d+1\) generators in total, at least one of which is a point generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) has a point–ray representation using at most \(\dim\operatorname{span}(G)\le d+1\) generators in total.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized sparsification of a point-plus-ray representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension bounds for sparse convex, conic, and mixed point–ray representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V,R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\). Every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is a convex combination of at most \(d+1\) points of \(V\), and every \(y\in\operatorname{cone}(R)\) is a conic combination of at most \(d\) vectors of \(R\). More generally, if \(z\in\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), then there are finite subsets \(I\subseteq V\) and \(J\subseteq R\), with \(|I|+|J|\leq d+1\), and coefficients satisfying
\[z=\sum_{v\in I}\lambda_vv+\sum_{r\in J}\mu_rr,\qquad \lambda_v\geq0,\quad\sum_{v\in I}\lambda_v=1,\quad\mu_r\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex combinations need at most d+1 points, conic combinations need at most d vectors, and mixed point–ray representations need at most d+1 active generators in total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\) has a mixed representation using at most \(d+1\) point and ray generators in total.

notation.meaning: finite active point and ray generator subsets
