children.title: Conic Polar-Dual Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Conic polarity and exchange of inequalities with generators.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed polyhedral convex cone. Adopt the nonpositive polar convention \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\leq0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional homogeneous polarity, emphasizing the exchange between finite generator and finite inequality descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A conic polar-dual representation pair consists of the mutually polar cones
\[
K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\},\qquad K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle r_j,y\rangle\leq0,5 j\leq q\},
\]
and, equivalently, whenever
\[
K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle a_i,x\rangle\leq0,5 i\leq m\},
\]
one has
\[
K^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}.
\]
Redundant generators or inequalities are permitted. Closedness gives \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\), so the generator-to-inequality exchange is involutive at the level of the represented cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic polar-dual representation pair is a closed polyhedral cone and its polar. A finite generating list for the primal cone becomes a finite list of homogeneous inequalities for the polar. Conversely, the normal vectors in a homogeneous inequality description of the primal generate its polar. Applying polarity again returns the original closed cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_j\}_{j=1}^q\Longleftrightarrow K^\circ=\{y:\langle r_j,y\rangle\leq0\ \forall j\},\qquad K^{\circ\circ}=K.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(R=[r_1\ \cdots\ r_q]\), \[K=\{R\lambda:\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^q\},\qquad K^\circ=\{y:R^\top y\leq0\}.\]
If \(K=\{x:A x\leq0\}\) and the rows of \(A\) are \(a_i^\top\), then \[K^\circ=\{A^\top\mu:\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), \(K^\circ=\mathbb{R}_-^n\).
For a linear subspace \(L\), \(L^\circ=L^\perp\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Facets in an irredundant full-dimensional inequality representation correspond to extreme rays of the polar, and extreme rays correspond to polar facets.
The representation exchange remains valid with redundant rows or generators, although such descriptions do not encode a bijection of individual entries.
boundary_notes: With the nonnegative dual-cone convention \(K^*=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}\), one has \(K^*=-K^\circ\).
For infinitely generated cones, closure may be required when recovering a generator cone from inequalities.

notation.meaning: Set of all nonnegative linear combinations of the vectors r_j.

source_refs.locator: §14, Theorem 14.1 and the generator/inequality formulas immediately following it

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Polyhedrality Boundary for Polar Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone has a polyhedral polar exactly when its closed convex conic hull is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \[K^\circ\text{ is polyhedral}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}K\text{ is a polyhedral cone}.\] Thus polyhedrality of the polar does not imply that a nonclosed or nonconvex original cone is itself polyhedral; it characterizes its closed convex conic hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K^\circ\text{ is polyhedral}\iff\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}K\text{ is polyhedral}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-dimensional characterization for an arbitrary nonempty cone under nonpositive polarity.

notation.meaning: Polar cone under the nonpositive convention

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Polyhedral Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar cone contains vectors pairing nonpositively with every cone vector; it is closed and convex, and remains polyhedral when the original cone is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its polar cone under the nonpositive convention is \[K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}.\] The set \(K^\circ\) is always a closed convex cone. If \(K\) is polyhedral, then \(K^\circ\) is polyhedral as well. The definition depends only on \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}K\), so replacing \(K\) by its closed convex conic hull leaves its polar unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,x\rangle\le0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\), and it is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the nonpositive polar convention in Euclidean space.

notation.meaning: Polar cone under the nonpositive pairing convention

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Polyhedral Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual cone contains vectors pairing nonnegatively with every cone vector; it is the negative of the nonpositive polar and is polyhedral for polyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its dual cone is \[K^*=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}.\] It is a closed convex cone and satisfies \(K^*=-K^\circ\) when \(K^\circ\) denotes the nonpositive polar. If \(K\) is polyhedral, then \(K^*\) is polyhedral. For a closed convex cone, biduality gives \(K^{**}=K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^*=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\), and \(K^*=-K^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean dual cone, distinguished from the nonpositive polar cone.

notation.meaning: Dual cone under the nonnegative pairing convention
Polar cone under the nonpositive pairing convention

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sums and intersections of polyhedral cones; no closure is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For polyhedral cones \(K_1,\ldots,K_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[\left(\sum_{i=1}^m K_i\right)^*=\bigcap_{i=1}^m K_i^*,\qquad \left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m K_i\right)^*=\sum_{i=1}^m K_i^*.\] The second sum is polyhedral and therefore closed; for arbitrary closed convex cones a closure may be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges finite sums and intersections of polyhedral cones, with no closure required in the intersection-to-sum formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\sum_iK_i)^*=\bigcap_iK_i^*\) and \((\bigcap_iK_i)^*=\sum_iK_i^*\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative dual of the ith cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Sum–Intersection Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex cones, specialized here to polyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polyhedral cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[K\text{ is pointed}\iff\operatorname{int}K^*\ne\varnothing,\qquad \operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\iff K^*\text{ is pointed}.\] Equivalently, duality exchanges pointedness with full dimensionality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges pointedness and full dimensionality for polyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is pointed iff \(K^*\) is full-dimensional, and \(K\) is full-dimensional iff \(K^*\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointedness–Full-Dimensionality Exchange
Incremental Double-Description Conversion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The double-description method converts homogeneous inequalities to extreme rays incrementally; polar conversion supplies the reverse direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a pointed cone \(K=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le0, i=1,\ldots,m\}\), the double-description method inserts the inequalities successively while maintaining an extreme-ray representation. At each insertion it retains satisfying rays, discards violating rays, forms candidate rays on the new supporting hyperplane from appropriate adjacent rays on opposite sides, and removes nonextreme or redundant candidates. After the final insertion, the maintained rays generate \(K\). Applying the conversion to the polar provides the reverse V-to-H conversion.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a pointed polyhedral cone given by finitely many homogeneous inequalities.
A valid initial double description is available for a cone containing \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After finitely many insertions and extremality tests, the maintained rays generate exactly \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Size Boundary for Explicit H/V Conversion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit H/V conversion has an unavoidable exponential worst case because the requested output can itself be exponentially large.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are rational polyhedral-cone families with polynomially many homogeneous inequalities and exponentially many extreme rays. By polarity, there are families with polynomially many generators and exponentially many facets. Consequently, any algorithm explicitly listing the opposite representation may require exponential time and storage solely to emit its output; unrestricted explicit H/V conversion cannot have an input-polynomial worst-case bound.
assumptions_latex: Dimension is part of the input.
The rational input and output explicitly list all inequalities, facets, generators, or extreme rays requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit opposite representation can be exponentially larger than the input, forcing corresponding worst-case time and storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case explicit conversion when dimension is part of the input.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet–Extreme-Ray Exchange
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity exchanges facet-defining inequalities with extreme rays of the polar cone, and primal extreme rays with polar facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be full-dimensional and pointed. A nonzero \(y\in K^\circ\) generates an extreme ray of \(K^\circ\) if and only if \[F_y:=K\cap y^\perp\] is a facet of \(K\). Symmetrically, extreme rays of \(K\) correspond to facets of \(K^\circ\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a full-dimensional pointed polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R_+y\) is an extreme ray of \(K^\circ\) iff \(K\cap y^\perp\) is a facet of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irredundant H/V data for full-dimensional pointed polyhedral cones under nonpositive polarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality–Generator Exchange
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity turns each cone generator into a homogeneous inequality and turns the normals of a homogeneous inequality system into generators of the polar cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\), polarity converts generators into inequalities: \[K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,v_j\rangle\le0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Conversely, if \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le0\}\) and \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) are the rows of \(A\), then \[K^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_p\}.\] Thus finite conic generators and finite homogeneous inequalities exchange roles under polarity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) has row vectors \(a_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,a_p^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cone}\{v_j\}_{j=1}^m{}^\circ=\{y:\langle y,v_j\rangle\le0\ \forall j\}\) and \(\{x:Ax\le0\}^\circ=\operatorname{cone}\{a_i\}_{i=1}^p\).

Polarity Sign Conventions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative dual equals the negative of the nonpositive polar; both conventions yield the original closed convex cone after two applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the nonpositive convention, \(K^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le0\text{ for all }x\in K\}\); under the nonnegative convention, \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for all }x\in K\}\). Hence \(K^*=-K^\circ\). Applying the same convention twice removes the sign: for every closed convex cone \(K\), one has \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\) and \(K^{**}=K\). Any formula transferring between the conventions must therefore negate the polar variable or cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^*=-K^\circ\); if \(K\) is closed and convex, then \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\) and \(K^{**}=K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the two standard sign conventions and their bipolar identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness Boundary for Polar Polytopes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar is bounded exactly when the origin is interior. A boundary origin yields an unbounded polar, while an excluded origin is adjoined by double polarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional polytope and define \(P^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in P\}\). Then
\[
P^\circ\text{ is bounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\operatorname{int}P.
\]
If \(0\in P\setminus\operatorname{int}P\), then \(P^\circ\) is unbounded but \((P^\circ)^\circ=P\). If \(0\notin P\), then
\[
(P^\circ)^\circ=\operatorname{conv}(P\cup\{0\}),
\]
so double normalized polarity does not recover \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^\circ\) is bounded iff \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and \((P^\circ)^\circ=\operatorname{conv}(P\cup\{0\})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp role of origin interiority in normalized bounded polarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized polarity for full-dimensional polytopes containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a full-dimensional polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\). Its polar polytope is \[P^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\text{ for every }x\in P\}.\] Then \(P^\circ\) is again a full-dimensional polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P^\circ\), and \((P^\circ)^\circ=P\). If \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\), then \[P^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:\langle y,v_i\rangle\leq1,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional polytope containing the origin has a bounded polar defined by unit support inequalities, and taking the polar twice recovers the polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^\circ\text{ is a full-dimensional polytope},\quad0\in\operatorname{int}P^\circ,\quad(P^\circ)^\circ=P.\)

children.top_down_role: The order-reversing correspondence between primal and polar faces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and let \(P^\circ=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\leq1\ \forall x\in P\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face polarity for full-dimensional polytopes with the origin in their interiors; this avoids quotient-space qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty proper face \(F\) of \(P\), its polar face is
\[
F^\triangle:=\{y\in P^\circ:\langle x,y\rangle=1\ \text{for every }x\in F\}.
\]
The assignment \(F\mapsto F^\triangle\) is an inclusion-reversing bijection between the nonempty proper faces of \(P\) and those of \(P^\circ\). Its inverse is the same construction in the opposite direction:
\[
(F^\triangle)^\triangle=F.
\]
If \(F\) has dimension \(k\), then \(F^\triangle\) has dimension \(n-1-k\). With the conventional extensions \(\varnothing^\triangle=P^\circ\) and \(P^\triangle=\varnothing\), this is an anti-isomorphism of the complete face lattices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-dimensional polytope containing zero in its interior, the face polar to F consists of the points of the polar polytope that pair to one with every point of F. This operation reverses inclusion, is bijective, and returns F when applied twice. The dimensions of paired proper faces add to n minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F\subseteq G\Longleftrightarrow G^\triangle\subseteq F^\triangle,\qquad(F^\triangle)^\triangle=F,\qquad\dim F+\dim F^\triangle=n-1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any \(x_F\in\operatorname{ri}F\), \[F^\triangle=\{y\in P^\circ:\langle x_F,y\rangle=1\}.\]
The vertices of \(P\) correspond to facets of \(P^\circ\), while facets of \(P\) correspond to vertices of \(P^\circ\).
special_cases_latex: If \(F=\{v\}\) is a vertex, then \[F^\triangle=P^\circ\cap\{y:\langle v,y\rangle=1\}\] is a facet.
If \(F\) is a facet supported by \(\langle a,x\rangle\leq1\), then \(F^\triangle=\{a\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The face lattices of \(P\) and \(P^\circ\) are anti-isomorphic.
The numbers of \(k\)-faces of \(P\) and \((n-1-k)\)-faces of \(P^\circ\) coincide.
boundary_notes: If the origin is on the boundary or outside the polytope, the stated polar need not be a full-dimensional polytope and the dimension formula requires modification.
The inspected local sources establish polarity and faces separately but do not provide a locator for this exact face-lattice anti-isomorphism.

notation.meaning: Face of the polar polytope corresponding to F.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Face Correspondence
Primal–Polar Face Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each nonempty proper face of a normalized polytope corresponds to the polar face whose points pair to one with every point of the primal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be full-dimensional with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and let \(P^\circ\) be its normalized polar. For every nonempty proper face \(F\) of \(P\), define \[F^\triangle=\{y\in P^\circ:\langle y,x\rangle=1\ \text{for every }x\in F\}.\] Then \(F^\triangle\) is a nonempty proper face of \(P^\circ\). Applying the analogous construction in \(P^\circ\) returns \(F\), so this assignment is a bijection between the nonempty proper faces of \(P\) and those of \(P^\circ\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty proper face of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^\triangle=\{y\in P^\circ:\langle y,x\rangle=1\ \forall x\in F\}\) is a nonempty proper face of \(P^\circ\), and \((F^\triangle)^\triangle=F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between nonempty proper faces under normalized polytope polarity.

notation.meaning: Face of the polar corresponding to a primal face

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind and face-correspondence formulation fit the leaf, but the bijection and involutivity claims have no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Order Reversal
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containment reverses under face polarity: a smaller primal face corresponds to a larger polar face, giving an anti-isomorphism of proper face lattices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be full-dimensional with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\). For nonempty proper faces \(F\) and \(G\) of \(P\), their corresponding faces in \(P^\circ\) satisfy \[F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G^\triangle\subseteq F^\triangle.\] Thus normalized polarity is inclusion-reversing: enlarging a primal face imposes more unit-pairing equalities and produces a smaller polar face. Together with involutivity, this makes the proper face lattices of \(P\) and \(P^\circ\) anti-isomorphic.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(G\) are nonempty proper faces of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq G\) if and only if \(G^\triangle\subseteq F^\triangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order reversal on the proper nonempty face lattices of polar polytopes.

notation.meaning: Polar face corresponding to a primal face

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property accurately expresses order reversal for nonempty proper faces, but no inspectable source supports the face-lattice anti-isomorphism claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Face Dimensions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Corresponding proper faces of a polytope and its polar have dimensions summing to one less than the ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be full-dimensional with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and let \(F\) be a nonempty proper face. For its polar-corresponding face \(F^\triangle\subseteq P^\circ\), the dimensions satisfy \[\dim F+\dim F^\triangle=d-1.\] Equivalently, a face of dimension \(k\) corresponds to a face of dimension \(d-1-k\). In particular, vertices correspond to facets, facets correspond to vertices, and intermediate-dimensional faces occur in complementary pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty proper face of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F+\dim F^\triangle=d-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension complementarity for nonempty proper faces of full-dimensional polar polytopes.

notation.meaning: Polar face corresponding to the face

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and complementary-dimension formula fit the exact leaf, but the record lacks a source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Improper-Face Boundary Cases
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assigning the empty face to the whole polar and the whole polytope to the empty face extends polarity to the complete face lattices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-dimensional polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), extend the polar-face correspondence by \[\varnothing^\triangle=P^\circ,\qquad P^\triangle=\varnothing.\] With the reciprocal conventions \(\varnothing^\triangle=P\) and \((P^\circ)^\triangle=\varnothing\) on the polar side, polarity becomes an order-reversing bijection between the complete face lattices, including both improper faces. The dimension relation remains uniform if \(\dim\varnothing=-1\) and \(\dim P=d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varnothing^\triangle=P^\circ\) and \(P^\triangle=\varnothing\), extending polarity to the complete face lattices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of face polarity to the empty face and whole polytope.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Use the coordinate order on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\). A convex corner is a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) that is lower comprehensive: \(0\leq z\leq x\in C\Rightarrow z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative, order-compatible polarity for closed convex corners, also called antiblocker polarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonnegative polar, or antiblocker, of a convex corner \(C\) is
\[
\operatorname{abl}(C):=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\langle x,y\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }x\in C\}=C^\circ\cap\mathbb{R}_+^n.
\]
It is itself a convex corner. The transformation is order reversing on convex corners and involutive:
\[
C_1\subseteq C_2\Rightarrow\operatorname{abl}(C_2)\subseteq\operatorname{abl}(C_1),
\qquad \operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(C))=C.
\]
Thus convex corners form a polarity class within the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex corner is a closed convex lower-comprehensive subset of the nonnegative orthant. Its antiblocker consists of the nonnegative vectors whose inner product with every point of the corner is at most one. Antiblocking reverses containment, maps convex corners to convex corners, and applying it twice recovers the original corner.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{abl}(C)=C^\circ\cap\mathbb{R}_+^n,\qquad \operatorname{abl}^2(C)=C.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{abl}(C)=\{y\geq0:\sigma_C(y)\leq1\}.\]
For \(y\geq0\), membership in \(\operatorname{abl}(C)\) is equivalent to validity of the inequality \(y^\top x\leq1\) over all \(x\in C\).
special_cases_latex: For the box \(C=[0,u]\) with \(u\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), \[\operatorname{abl}(C)=\{y\geq0:u^\top y\leq1\}.\]
For \(C=\{x\geq0:a^\top x\leq1\}\) with \(a>0\), \(\operatorname{abl}(C)=[0,a]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Extreme nonnegative valid inequalities of one member correspond to generator geometry of its antiblocker.
The restriction \(y\geq0\) makes polarity compatible with coordinatewise downward closure.
boundary_notes: The involution is asserted only for closed convex lower-comprehensive sets in \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\); arbitrary nonnegative sets must first be closed and convexified appropriately.
No inspected source hint supported the exact antiblocker terminology and involution.

notation.meaning: Antiblocker or nonnegative polar of C.

knowledge_statements.title: Antiblocker Polarity of Convex Corners
Dominant Representation of Blocking Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty blocking polyhedron is the nonnegative dominant of the convex hull of finitely many vertices, and its recession cone is the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^d\) be a nonempty polyhedron satisfying \(B+\mathbb{R}_+^d=B\). Then \[\operatorname{rec}B=\mathbb{R}_+^d.\] Consequently \(B\) is pointed, has a nonempty finite vertex set \(V(B)\), and \[B=\operatorname{conv}V(B)+\mathbb{R}_+^d.\] Conversely, every set \(\operatorname{conv}V+\mathbb{R}_+^d\) with nonempty finite \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^d\) is a blocking polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}B=\mathbb{R}_+^d\) and \(B=\operatorname{conv}V(B)+\mathbb{R}_+^d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession and vertex representation of nonempty upward-comprehensive polyhedra in the nonnegative orthant.

notation.meaning: Finite vertex set of the blocking polyhedron

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is blocking exactly when \(B+\mathbb{R}_+^d=B\); its blocker is \(b(B)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^d:\langle y,x\rangle\ge1\ \forall x\in B\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative, upward-closed polyhedra and their normalized blocker operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty polyhedron \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^d\) is blocking when it is upward closed in the coordinate order, equivalently, \[B+\mathbb{R}_+^d=B.\] Its blocker is the nonnegative polyhedron \[b(B)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^d:\langle y,x\rangle\ge1\ \text{for every }x\in B\}.\] Thus points of \(b(B)\) certify a unit lower bound against every point of \(B\). Under the standard nonempty blocking hypotheses for which the blocker is proper, blocker duality is involutive: \(b(b(B))=B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking polyhedron is a nonnegative polyhedron closed upward coordinatewise; its blocker consists of nonnegative vectors pairing to at least one with every point.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Inequality Representation of Anti-Blocking Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anti-blocking polyhedra are exactly nonnegative polyhedra describable by upper inequalities with nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Then \(P\) is lower-comprehensive if and only if there exist \(m\geq0\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) such that \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax\leq b\}.\] Rows may be absent in unbounded coordinate directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is lower-comprehensive}\iff\exists A\geq0,\ b\geq0:\ P=\{x\geq0:Ax\leq b\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inequality characterization of lower-comprehensive polyhedra in the nonnegative orthant, including unbounded instances.

notation.meaning: Every entry of the inequality matrix is nonnegative

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is anti-blocking exactly when it is lower-comprehensive in the coordinatewise order.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise partial order on the nonnegative orthant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the downward-closed convention for anti-blocking polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is anti-blocking if
\[
x\in P,\quad y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n,\quad 0\leq y\leq x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y\in P.
\]
Thus membership is preserved by decreasing any coordinates without making them negative. In particular, every nonempty anti-blocking polyhedron contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anti-blocking polyhedron lies in the nonnegative orthant and contains every nonnegative vector dominated coordinatewise by one of its points.
knowledge_statements.title: Anti-Blocking Polyhedra

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The downward-closed definition and its consequence that 0 belongs to every nonempty anti-blocking polyhedron are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Bipolar Closure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Double nonnegative polarity returns the closed convex lower-comprehensive hull; without those fixed-point properties it can enlarge the set strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty \(S\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), define \(\operatorname{down}(S):=\{z\in\mathbb R_+^n:\exists x\in S,\ 0\le z\le x\}\). Then
\[
\operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(S))=\operatorname{cl}\!\bigl(\operatorname{down}(\operatorname{conv}S)\bigr).
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{abl}^2(S)=S\) exactly when \(S\) is closed, convex, and lower-comprehensive. For example, \(S=\{(1,1)\}\) has \(\operatorname{abl}^2(S)=[0,1]^2\ne S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{abl}^2(S)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{down}(\operatorname{conv}S))\), with equality to \(S\) exactly for closed convex lower-comprehensive \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp arbitrary-set extension of anti-blocker bipolarity.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise lower closure of S in the nonnegative orthant.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and lower-comprehensive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{abl}(C)\) has the same structural properties and \(\operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(C))=C\).

notation.meaning: Anti-blocker, or nonnegative-orthant polar, of a set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States anti-blocker polarity for closed convex lower-comprehensive sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the nonnegative-orthant polar of \(C\) by
\[
\operatorname{abl}(C):=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\langle x,y\rangle\leq1\text{ for every }x\in C\}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{abl}(C)\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and lower-comprehensive, and the bipolar identity is
\[
\operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(C))=C.
\]
Consequently this polarity reverses inclusion: if \(C_1\subseteq C_2\), then \(\operatorname{abl}(C_2)\subseteq\operatorname{abl}(C_1)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Function and Exposed Face of a Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex polyhedron. Extended-real values are allowed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional support geometry for bounded or unbounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function of \(P\) is
\[
\sigma_P(u):=\sup_{x\in P}\langle u,x\rangle\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\qquad u\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
For every \(u\) for which the supremum is finite and attained, the objective-selected exposed face is
\[
F_P(u):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P}\langle u,x\rangle
      =\{x\in P:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}.
\]
For a nonempty polyhedron, every finite support value is attained. Hence \(F_P(u)\neq\varnothing\) exactly when \(u\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P\). The support function is closed, convex, positively homogeneous, and polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a nonempty polyhedron assigns to each objective vector the supremum of the corresponding linear objective. Whenever this value is finite, it is attained and the maximizers form an exposed face. This couples a polyhedral convex function in objective space with the facial geometry of the original set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma_P(u)=\sup_{x\in P}\langle u,x\rangle,\qquad F_P(u)=\{x\in P:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[P=\{x:\langle u,x\rangle\leq\sigma_P(u)\ \forall u\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.\]
For \(x\in P\), \[x\in F_P(u)\Longleftrightarrow u\in N_P(x),\] where \(N_P(x)=\{u:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in P\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is bounded, then \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=\mathbb{R}^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two closed convex polyhedra with the same support function are equal.
The domains on which a fixed face is optimal are polyhedral cones in objective space.
boundary_notes: For an arbitrary closed convex set, a finite support value need not be attained; polyhedrality supplies attainment here.
The empty-set support function is convention-dependent and is excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Lipschitz Bound for Polytope Support
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope's support function is globally Lipschitz, with optimal constant equal to the greatest Euclidean norm of a point in the polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polytope and set \(R_P:=\max_{x\in P}\|x\|\). Then for all \(c,d\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
|\sigma_P(c)-\sigma_P(d)|\le R_P\|c-d\|.
\]
Moreover, \(R_P\) is the least global Lipschitz constant of \(\sigma_P\) for the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(\sigma_P)=\max_{x\in P}\|x\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness consequence distinguishing polytope support from the extended-valued unbounded regime.

notation.meaning: Maximum Euclidean norm attained on P.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Functions of Polytopes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope's support function is the finite maximum of the linear forms defined by its vertices, hence is finite-valued and polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every objective \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the support function satisfies
\[
\sigma_P(c):=\sup_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle
 =\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\langle c,v_i\rangle.
\]
Hence \(\sigma_P\) is finite-valued, convex, positively homogeneous, and polyhedral. On each region where one fixed collection of vertices maximizes the displayed expressions, \(\sigma_P\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_P(c)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\langle c,v_i\rangle\) is finite for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum representation for a nonempty polytope.

notation.meaning: Generating points, which may be chosen as the vertices of the polytope.

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Maximum Support Function of a Polytope
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded finite-dimensional polyhedral regime; the support function is real-valued on all objective vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function of the polytope \(P\) is the finite polyhedral sublinear function
\[
\sigma_P(u):=\max_{x\in P}\langle u,x\rangle
             =\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\langle u,v_i\rangle,
\qquad u\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Its selected face is
\[
F_P(u)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_i:\langle u,v_i\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}.
\]
Thus \(\sigma_P\) is finite, convex, continuous, positively homogeneous, and piecewise linear. A nonminimal generating list is permitted: all listed points attaining the maximum generate the selected face, while nonvertices among them cause only redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a polytope is the maximum of the finitely many linear functions obtained from any finite vertex-generating list. It is finite everywhere and piecewise linear. The points in the list that attain the maximum generate the exposed face selected by the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma_P(u)=\max_i\langle u,v_i\rangle<+\infty,\qquad F_P(u)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_i:\langle u,v_i\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{epi}\sigma_P=\{(u,t):t\geq\langle u,v_i\rangle,5 i\leq m\}.\]
\[P=\{x:\langle u,x\rangle\leq\sigma_P(u)\ \forall u\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For a singleton \(P=\{v\}\), \(\sigma_P(u)=\langle u,v\rangle\).
For a segment \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{a,b\}\), \(\sigma_P(u)=\max\{\langle u,a\rangle,\langle u,b\rangle\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The domains of linearity of \(\sigma_P\) are unions of normal cones of faces.
The subdifferential satisfies \(\partial\sigma_P(u)=F_P(u)\).
boundary_notes: The formula remains valid for a redundant finite generating set, but the displayed points need not all be vertices.
For unbounded polyhedra the support function may equal \(+\infty\), so a recession-domain restriction is necessary.

notation.meaning: Points in a finite convex-hull representation of P.

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski–Weyl Support Formula
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a Minkowski–Weyl representation, support is finite exactly when the objective is nonpositive on every recession generator; its finite value is the maximum over point generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}
\]
be a nonempty polyhedron. Then
\[
\sigma_P(c)=
\begin{cases}
\max_{1\le i\le m}\langle c,v_i\rangle,&\langle c,r_j\rangle\le0\quad(j=1,\ldots,q),\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The formula also covers lineality when both directions of every line are included among the recession generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_P(c)=\max_i\langle c,v_i\rangle\) when \(\langle c,r_j\rangle\le0\) for all j, and \(+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-generator evaluation of support in the unbounded polyhedral regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Functions of Unbounded Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded polyhedron has finite support precisely in directions nonpositive on its recession cone; each finite value is attained on a face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function \(\sigma_P(c)=\sup_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle\) is finite exactly for objectives nonpositive on every recession direction:
\[
\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P
 =\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,r\rangle\leq0\text{ for all }r\in R\}
 =R^\circ.
\]
For each \(c\in R^\circ\), the supremum is attained on a nonempty face of \(P\); for \(c\notin R^\circ\), one has \(\sigma_P(c)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=R^\circ\), and every finite support value is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective support domain characterized by recession geometry.

notation.meaning: Negative polar cone of the recession cone.
Effective domain of the support function.

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=Q+K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(Q=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) is a nonempty polytope and \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}=\operatorname{rec}P\) is a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded polyhedra represented by points and recession directions; extended-real support functions are used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The support function of \(P\) is
\[
\sigma_P(u)=
\begin{cases}
\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\langle u,v_i\rangle,&\langle u,r_j\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }j,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently its effective domain is the polar of the recession cone:
\[
\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ
=\{u:\langle u,r_j\rangle\leq0,5 j\leq q\}.
\]
For each \(u\) in this domain the finite maximum is attained, and the maximizing set \(F_P(u)=\{x\in P:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}\) is a nonempty face, possibly unbounded when \(u\) annihilates a recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron written as a polytope plus its recession cone, the support value is finite precisely on objectives that are nonpositive on every recession direction. On that domain it is the maximum over the bounded point generators. A selected face can still be unbounded when the objective is zero along some recession directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ,\qquad \sigma_P(u)=\max_i\langle u,v_i\rangle\ \text{on this domain}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\sigma_P=\sigma_Q+\delta_{K^\circ},\] where \(\delta_{K^\circ}\) is zero on \(K^\circ\) and \(+\infty\) outside it.
For \(u\in K^\circ\), \[\operatorname{rec}F_P(u)=K\cap u^\perp.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(K=\{0\}\), then \(P\) is a polytope and the domain is all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
If \(P=K\) is a cone, then \(\sigma_K(u)=0\) on \(K^\circ\) and \(+\infty\) outside.
immediate_consequences_latex: Objectives outside \((\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ\) define unbounded-above linear programs on \(P\).
Objectives in the relative interior of \((\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ\) are strictly negative on every nonlineality recession direction and therefore select bounded faces.
boundary_notes: If the recession cone has lineality, its polar lies in the orthogonal complement of that lineality.
The representation assumes the standard finite point-plus-direction decomposition of a nonempty polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Extended-real indicator of the cone K polar.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face Selected by a Linear Objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(u\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization convention for finite linear objectives on polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The face selected by the objective \(u\) is
\[
F_P(u):=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P}\langle u,x\rangle
       =P\cap\{x:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\}.
\]
For a nonempty face \(F\unlhd P\), its closed normal region is
\[
N_P(F):=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:F\subseteq F_P(u)\}
       =\{u:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in P,\ \forall x\in F\}.
\]
The objectives selecting exactly \(F\) form \(\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\). Thus objectives are grouped by their common optimal face, and incidence is reversed: \(F\subseteq G\) implies \(N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite objective selects the face on which its maximum is attained. The normal region of a face consists of all objectives for which that face is contained in the optimizer set. Its relative interior consists of the objectives selecting exactly that face. Larger primal faces therefore have smaller normal regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_P(u)=\{x\in P:\langle u,x\rangle=\sigma_P(u)\},\qquad F_P(u)=F\Longleftrightarrow u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\), \[N_P(F)=N_P(x)=\{u:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in P\}.\]
\[u\in N_P(F)\Longleftrightarrow F\subseteq F_P(u).\]
special_cases_latex: \(F_P(0)=P\) and \(N_P(P)=(\operatorname{lin}(P-P))^\perp\).
If \(v\) is a vertex, \(N_P(v)\) is full-dimensional relative to the objective space modulo lineality exactly when \(v\) is a zero-dimensional face.
immediate_consequences_latex: The support function is linear on every normal cone \(N_P(F)\), with value \(\langle u,x\rangle\) for any \(x\in F\).
Optimal-face changes occur when the objective crosses a boundary between normal regions.
boundary_notes: For unbounded \(P\), only objectives in \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P\) have nonempty selected faces.
Using minimization instead of maximization reverses the sign of the normal regions.

notation.meaning: F is a face of P.
Normal cone or closed objective region attached to F.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Inequality Certificate for Supporting Objectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objectives supporting a face are precisely nonnegative combinations of inequalities active throughout that face, yielding a finite multiplier certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}
\]
is nonempty, with row normals \(a_i^\top\), and let \(F\) be a nonempty face. Define
\[
I(F):=\{i:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F\}.
\]
Then
\[
N_P(F)=\operatorname{cone}\{a_i:i\in I(F)\}.
\]
Consequently, \(c\) supports \(F\) if and only if there is \(\lambda\ge0\), supported on \(I(F)\), such that \(c=A^\top\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(F)=\operatorname{cone}\{a_i:i\in I(F)\}\), equivalently \(c=A^\top\lambda\) for some \(\lambda\ge0\) supported on \(I(F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multiplier representation of the supporting-objective cone of a face.

notation.meaning: Outward row normal of the i-th inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting Objectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting objective for a face is a linear objective maximized at every point of that face. These objectives form the face normal cone, which can be computed at any relative-interior point of the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An objective \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) supports the face \(F\) when every point of \(F\) maximizes \(\langle c,\cdot\rangle\) over \(P\). The set of all such objectives is
\[
N_P(F):=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:F\subseteq M_P(c)\}
=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,y-x\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }y\in P\text{ and every }x\in F\}.
\]
Equivalently, for any fixed \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\),
\[
N_P(F)=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,y-x\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }y\in P\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objectives supporting \(F\) are exactly \(N_P(F)=\{c:F\subseteq\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting objectives use the maximization sign convention; the pointwise normal-cone formula uses a relative-interior point of the face.

notation.meaning: Set of maximizers of the objective over the polyhedron.
Normal cone associated with the face.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4 Tangent and Normal Cones p. 125

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Faces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite linear objective selects a nonempty face of a polyhedron, and every nonempty polyhedral face is selected by some linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The maximizer set of a finite supporting objective is
\[
F_c:=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle
 =\{x\in P:\langle c,x\rangle=\sigma_P(c)\}.
\]
It is a nonempty face of \(P\). Conversely, because \(P\) is polyhedral, every nonempty face \(F\) is exposed: there exists \(c\in\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P\) such that \(F=F_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_c=\{x\in P:\langle c,x\rangle=\sigma_P(c)\}\) is a nonempty face, and every nonempty face arises this way.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face exposure by finite linear objectives on polyhedra.

notation.meaning: Optimal face selected by the objective.

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Support Functions p. 135

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Fan Stratification of Objective Space
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite objective space is partitioned by relative interiors of face normal cones; their closure order reverses face inclusion and their dimensions complement face dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. The relative interiors of its face normal cones form a disjoint partition of the finite-objective domain:
\[
\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=\bigsqcup_{\varnothing\ne F\unlhd P}\operatorname{ri}N_P(F).
\]
Moreover,
\[
F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F),
\qquad \dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n.
\]
Thus objective-equivalence regions are the relatively open cones of the normal fan, with closure order opposite to face inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P\) is the disjoint union of \(\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\), ordered oppositely to the nonempty faces of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global organization of objective-equivalence regions for a fixed polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Normal cone of F under the maximization convention.
F is a face of P.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Equivalence Regions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objectives selecting exactly the same face constitute the relative interior of that face's normal cone; boundary objectives may select a larger face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the optimal-face map \(F_c=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in P}\langle c,x\rangle\), one has
\[
\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:F_c=F\}=\operatorname{ri}N_P(F).
\]
Consequently two finite objectives \(c\) and \(d\) select the same face exactly when they lie in the relative interior of the same normal cone. Passing to the boundary of \(N_P(F)\) can enlarge the selected face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objectives selecting exactly \(F\) form \(\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective-equivalence classes are relative interiors of normal cones.

notation.meaning: Normal cone to the face under the maximization convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent and Normal Cones as Polar Cones
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex set and let \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex tangent and normal cones under the nonpositive polar convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The tangent cone and normal cone of \(C\) at \(x\) are
\[
T_C(x):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}(C-x)
=\operatorname{cl}\{\alpha(y-x):\alpha\geq0,\ y\in C\},
\]
\[
N_C(x):=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle s,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }y\in C\}.
\]
They form a polar pair:
\[
N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ,
\qquad T_C(x)=N_C(x)^\circ.
\]
Both are closed convex cones. For a polyhedron they are polyhedral, and the closure in the tangent-cone formula may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point of a closed convex set, the tangent cone is the closure of all nonnegative multiples of feasible displacements, while the normal cone consists of vectors making a nonpositive inner product with every feasible displacement. Each cone is the polar of the other. In the polyhedral case both are polyhedral and the generated tangent cone is already closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ,\qquad T_C(x)=N_C(x)^\circ.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[d\in T_C(x)\Longleftrightarrow\langle s,d\rangle\leq0\ \forall s\in N_C(x).\]
\[s\in N_C(x)\Longleftrightarrow x\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in C}\langle s,y\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\), then \(T_C(x)=\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(N_C(x)=\{0\}\).
If \(C=K\) is a closed convex cone and \(x=0\), then \(T_K(0)=K\) and \(N_K(0)=K^\circ\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For a polyhedron \(C=\{z:Az\leq b\}\) with active row set \(I(x)\), \[T_C(x)=\{d:A_{I(x)}d\leq0\},\qquad N_C(x)=\{A_{I(x)}^\top\lambda:\lambda\geq0\}.\]
Normal directions encode precisely the linear objectives maximized at the base point.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex sets, several inequivalent tangent and normal constructions exist; this record uses the convex contingent tangent and its polar normal.
Sign conventions vary: a nonnegative dual cone introduces a minus sign.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Cones to Faces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any relative-interior point of a face, the normal cone is constant and equals the negative polar of the tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal cone associated with \(F\) is
\[
N_P(F)=N_P(x):=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,y-x\rangle\leq0
\text{ for every }y\in P\}.
\]
It is constant for \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\). If \(T_P(x)\) denotes the tangent cone to \(P\) at \(x\), then
\[
N_P(F)=T_P(x)^\circ.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty face of \(P\), and \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(F)=N_P(x)=T_P(x)^\circ\), independently of the chosen \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal cones follow the maximizing-objective sign convention.

notation.meaning: Tangent cone at a relative-interior point of the face.

children.title: Tangent Cones to Faces
children.top_down_role: Local feasible-direction geometry along polyhedral faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Radial and Lineality Structure Along a Face
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a polyhedral face, the tangent cone equals the radial cone without closure, and its lineality is precisely the direction space of the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\), \[T_P(F)=T_P(x)=\operatorname{cone}(P-x),\qquad \operatorname{lin}T_P(F)=\operatorname{span}(F-F).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(F)=\operatorname{cone}(P-x)\) and \(\operatorname{lin}T_P(F)=\operatorname{span}(F-F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedrality makes the radial cone closed.

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of the face.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Cones to Faces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a face's relative interior, the tangent cone is fixed and is described by the homogeneous inequalities corresponding to constraints active on that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The tangent cone is constant on \(\operatorname{ri}F\) and may be written
\[
T_P(F):=T_P(x)=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(P-x)}
 =\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i d\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I(F)\}.
\]
It consists precisely of first-order feasible directions from \(x\). Moreover, its negative polar is the face normal cone: \(T_P(F)^\circ=N_P(F)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty face, \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\), and \(I(F)=\{i:A_i x=b_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(F)=\{d:A_i d\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I(F)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-inequality representation at relative-interior points of a face.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active throughout the relative interior of the face.

children.title: Polyhedral Critical Cones
children.top_down_role: Local cones used in optimality and variational analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar of a Polyhedral Critical Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative polar of a polyhedral critical cone is the normal cone plus the line spanned by the supporting objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_P(x,c)=T_P(x)\cap c^\perp\), \[K_P(x,c)^\circ=T_P(x)^\circ+(c^\perp)^\circ=N_P(x)+\operatorname{span}\{c\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron, \(x\in P\), and \(c\in N_P(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_P(x,c)^\circ=N_P(x)+\operatorname{span}\{c\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the nonpositive polar convention; polyhedrality makes the polar sum closed.

notation.meaning: Line generated by the objective vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical Cone as the Tangent Cone to the Optimal Face
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical cone equals the tangent cone at the reference point to the face exposed by the supporting objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F_c:=\operatorname{argmax}_{z\in P}\langle c,z\rangle.\] If \(c\in N_P(x)\), then \(x\in F_c\) and \[K_P(x,c)=T_P(x)\cap c^\perp=T_{F_c}(x).\]
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximizing-objective convention with a supporting normal.

notation.meaning: Face of maximizers of the supporting objective.
Critical cone at x relative to c.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Multiplier Representation of a Critical Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive active multipliers force equality in critical directions, while zero-multiplier active constraints retain their tangent inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I(x)=\{i:A_i x=b_i\}\), write \(c=A_{I(x)}^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) with \(\lambda\ge0\), and put \(I_+(\lambda)=\{i\in I(x):\lambda_i>0\}\). Then \[K_P(x,c)=\{d:A_i d=0\ \forall i\in I_+(\lambda),\quad A_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x)\setminus I_+(\lambda)\}.\] The resulting cone is independent of the chosen nonnegative multiplier representation of \(c\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{z:Az\le b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_P(x,c)=\{d:A_i d=0\ (i\in I_+(\lambda)),\ A_i d\le0\ (i\in I(x)\setminus I_+(\lambda))\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit equality-and-inequality representation from an active normal certificate.

notation.meaning: Indices active at the reference point.
Active indices with strictly positive multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Critical Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical cone for a feasible point and a supporting objective under maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron, let \(x\in P\), and let \(c\in N_P(x)\). The critical cone associated with \((x,c)\) is
\[K_P(x,c):=T_P(x)\cap c^\perp=\{d\in T_P(x):\langle c,d\rangle=0\}.\]
Because \(c\in N_P(x)\), every \(d\in T_P(x)\) satisfies \(\langle c,d\rangle\leq0\); thus the critical cone contains precisely the tangent directions with zero first-order change in the supported linear objective. Since \(T_P(x)\) is polyhedral, \(K_P(x,c)\) is also a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical cone contains feasible tangent directions orthogonal to a supporting objective, hence directions with zero first-order objective change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_P(x,c)=T_P(x)\cap c^\perp\) is a polyhedral cone.

notation.meaning: Critical cone associated with x and c.
Subspace of vectors orthogonal to c.
Tangent cone to P at x.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, and for every nonempty face \(F\unlhd P\) let \(N_P(F)=\{u:F\subseteq F_P(u)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-space conical complex attached to a possibly unbounded polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal-fan complex of \(P\) is the finite collection
\[
\mathcal{N}(P):=\{N_P(F):\varnothing\neq F\unlhd P\}.
\]
Its cones satisfy the conical-complex compatibility conditions: every face of a cone in \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is another cone in the collection, and the intersection of two cones is a face of each. Its support is
\[
|\mathcal{N}(P)|:=\bigcup_{F\unlhd P,\,F\neq\varnothing}N_P(F)
=\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ.
\]
The relatively open cones \(\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\) partition this support according to the exact optimal face: \(u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\) exactly when \(F_P(u)=F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-fan complex of a polyhedron is the finite family of normal cones attached to all nonempty faces. These cones meet face-to-face and include all their faces. Their union is the domain of finite support objectives, and the relative interiors partition that domain according to which primal face is exactly optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal{N}(P)=\{N_P(F):\varnothing\neq F\unlhd P\},\qquad |\mathcal{N}(P)|=(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{dom}\sigma_P=\bigsqcup_{\varnothing\neq F\unlhd P}\operatorname{ri}N_P(F).\]
The cones of \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) are the closures of the objective regions on which the optimizer face of \(P\) is constant.
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is a polytope, \(|\mathcal{N}(P)|=\mathbb{R}^n\), so the fan is complete.
If \(P\) has lineality space \(L\), every normal cone lies in \(L^\perp\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Face inclusion is reversed by the normal-cone assignment.
The support function \(\sigma_P\) is linear on each cone of \(\mathcal{N}(P)\).
boundary_notes: For unbounded polyhedra the normal fan is generally not complete in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
The inspected sources define normal cones and objective-selected faces but do not explicitly state the full conical-complex compatibility claim.

notation.meaning: Union, or support, of the cones in the complex.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Lineality of a Polytope Normal Fan
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All cones in a polytope's normal fan share the orthogonal complement of the polytope's direction space as lineality; quotienting by it gives a pointed complete fan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polytope and put \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P-P)\). For every nonempty face \(F\), \[\operatorname{lin}N_P(F)=L^\perp,\qquad \bigcap_{F\ne\varnothing}N_P(F)=N_P(P)=L^\perp.\] Therefore all cones of the normal fan are pointed exactly when \(P\) is full-dimensional. In general, their images in \(\mathbb R^n/L^\perp\) form a pointed complete fan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}N_P(F)=L^\perp\) for every nonempty face \(F\), and the cones are pointed exactly when \(L=\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lineality and essential quotient of the complete normal fan, allowing lower-dimensional polytopes.

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of the polytope.
Orthogonal complement of the polytope direction space.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Fans of Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness and fan compatibility of all face-normal cones of a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope and define its normal fan by
\[\mathcal{N}(P):=\{N_P(F):F\text{ is a nonempty face of }P\}.\]
Every face of a cone in \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) also belongs to \(\mathcal{N}(P)\), and the intersection of any two cones in \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is a face of each. Moreover,
\[\bigcup_{F\preceq P}N_P(F)=\mathbb{R}^n.\]
Thus \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is a complete polyhedral fan: every linear objective has a nonempty maximizing face, and its objective-equivalence region is the relative interior of one fan cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal cones of all nonempty faces of a polytope form a complete polyhedral fan covering the entire objective space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is a complete polyhedral fan with support \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: F is a nonempty face of P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Normal Fan of a Polytope
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope. For each nonempty face \(F\), define \(N_P(F)=\{u:F\subseteq F_P(u)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded polyhedral regime; lower-dimensional polytopes are allowed with their lineality in objective space made explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal fan of \(P\) is
\[
\mathcal{N}(P)=\{N_P(F):\varnothing\neq F\unlhd P\}.
\]
Because \(P\) is bounded, every linear objective has a maximizer, and hence
\[
\bigcup_{F\unlhd P,\,F\neq\varnothing}N_P(F)=\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is a complete polyhedral fan. Its maximal cones are the normal cones of vertices; more generally, if \(P\) is full-dimensional then \(\dim N_P(F)=n-\dim F\). The relative interior of \(N_P(F)\) consists exactly of the objectives selecting \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal fan of a polytope contains the normal cone of every nonempty face. Boundedness ensures that these cones cover all objective space, so the fan is complete. Vertex normal cones are maximal, and the dimension of a normal cone complements the dimension of its primal face for a full-dimensional polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\mathcal{N}(P)|=\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\Longleftrightarrow F_P(u)=F.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The domains of linearity of \(\sigma_P(u)=\max_{v\in\operatorname{vert}P}\langle u,v\rangle\) form the normal fan.
For every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there is a unique face \(F\) such that \(u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\).
special_cases_latex: For a simplex, the maximal cones correspond to its vertices and meet along cones corresponding to higher-dimensional faces.
If \(P\) is contained in an affine space parallel to \(L\), every cone contains \(L^\perp\); completeness still holds in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Generic objectives, lying outside lower-dimensional cone boundaries, select vertices.
The fan records the full objective-space sensitivity of linear optimization over \(P\).
boundary_notes: The dimension formula as written requires full-dimensional \(P\); in general it is interpreted after quotienting by \((\operatorname{lin}(P-P))^\perp\).
No supplied source locator explicitly developed complete normal fans.
review_flags: A precise normal-fan reference is needed for completeness, maximal cones, and the dimension correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambient Lineality of an Unbounded Normal Fan
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every face normal cone has the orthogonal complement of the polyhedron's direction space as its lineality. Lower-dimensional polyhedra therefore require a fan convention allowing lineality, or passage to a quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\operatorname{span}(P-P)\). For every nonempty face \(F\) of \(P\), \[\operatorname{lin}N_P(F)=L^\perp.\] Thus all cones of the normal fan are pointed exactly when \(P\) is full-dimensional. If \(P\) is lower-dimensional, their images in \(\mathbb R^n/L^\perp\) form a pointed fan; in the ambient space the collection is a fan only under conventions allowing common lineality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty face of \(P\), and \(L=\operatorname{span}(P-P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}N_P(F)=L^\perp\); the ambient normal cones are pointed iff \(L=\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarifies when the normal cones constitute a strongly convex fan in the ambient space.

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of the polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Fans of Unbounded Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the generally incomplete normal fan and its recession-determined support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron with recession cone \(R=\operatorname{rec}P\). Its face-normal cones form a polyhedral fan \(\mathcal{N}(P)\), but its support is only
\[|\mathcal{N}(P)|=\bigcup_{F\preceq P}N_P(F)=R^\circ:=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,d\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }d\in R\}.\]
Indeed, a maximizing linear objective has finite value on \(P\) exactly when \(c\in R^\circ\), and then its maximum is attained on a nonempty face. Consequently, the normal fan is complete precisely when \(R^\circ=\mathbb{R}^n\), equivalently when \(R=\{0\}\) and \(P\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded polyhedron’s normal fan covers the polar of its recession cone, not generally the whole objective space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal{N}(P)|=R^\circ\), and \(\mathcal{N}(P)\) is complete if and only if \(P\) is bounded.

notation.meaning: Negative polar cone under the maximizing convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Normal Fan of an Unbounded Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty unbounded polyhedron with recession cone \(K=\operatorname{rec}P\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded finite-dimensional polyhedra; the fan is supported only on bounded-above objective directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal fan of \(P\) is the conical complex
\[
\mathcal{N}(P):=\{N_P(F):\varnothing\neq F\unlhd P\},
\qquad N_P(F)=\{u:F\subseteq F_P(u)\}.
\]
Its support is the polar recession cone
\[
|\mathcal{N}(P)|=K^\circ=\{u:\langle u,d\rangle\leq0\ \forall d\in K\}.
\]
It is therefore generally incomplete in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(u\in K^\circ\), the selected face is nonempty and
\[
\operatorname{rec}F_P(u)=K\cap u^\perp.
\]
Hence objectives in the relative interior of \(K^\circ\) select bounded faces when \(K\) is pointed, whereas boundary objectives may select unbounded faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal fan of an unbounded polyhedron consists of its face normal cones, but these cones cover only objectives that are nonpositive on every recession direction. This is the polar of the recession cone. Boundary objectives can be constant along recession directions and therefore select unbounded faces; interior objectives select bounded faces when the recession cone is pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\mathcal{N}(P)|=(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ,\qquad \operatorname{rec}F_P(u)=\operatorname{rec}P\cap u^\perp.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[u\notin|\mathcal{N}(P)|\Longleftrightarrow\sigma_P(u)=+\infty.\]
\[u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\Longleftrightarrow F_P(u)=F.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(P=Q+K\) with \(Q\) a polytope, then every finite support value is determined by \(Q\), while \(K^\circ\) determines the fan support.
If \(P\) contains a lineality space \(L\), then \(|\mathcal{N}(P)|\subseteq L^\perp\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Completeness occurs only after restricting objective space to \((\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ\), or globally when \(P\) is bounded.
The recession geometry determines which parametric objective regions exist.
boundary_notes: The assertion that relative-interior objectives select bounded faces needs pointedness of the recession cone.
The source inspected for unbounded support functions does not explicitly formulate the resulting collection as an incomplete fan.
review_flags: A source explicitly treating normal fans of unbounded polyhedra is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Face–Normal Dimensions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dimensions of a face and its normal cone add to the ambient dimension; vertices therefore correspond to full-dimensional normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polytope and let \(F\) be a nonempty face. Under the maximization convention, \[\dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n.\] Consequently, vertices correspond to full-dimensional normal cones, while \(N_P(P)=\operatorname{lin}(P-P)^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient-dimensional rank relation for nonempty faces of a polytope, including lower-dimensional polytopes.

notation.meaning: Normal cone of the face under the maximization convention.
Direction space parallel to the affine hull of the polytope.

knowledge_statements.title: Face–Normal Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-reversing correspondence for nonempty faces of a full-dimensional polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional polytope. The assignment \(F\mapsto N_P(F)\) is an inclusion-reversing bijection between the nonempty faces of \(P\) and the cones of its normal fan. For nonempty faces \(F,G\),
\[F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_P(G)\text{ is a face of }N_P(F).\]
In particular, \(F\subseteq G\) implies \(N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F)\), and complementary dimensions satisfy
\[\dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n.\]
Thus primal incidence is reversed in objective space: larger primal faces correspond to smaller normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Faces of a full-dimensional polytope correspond bijectively to normal-fan cones, with inclusions reversed and dimensions summing to the ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq G\iff N_P(G)\preceq N_P(F)\), and \(\dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n\).

notation.meaning: C is a face of the cone D.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. For every nonempty face \(F\unlhd P\), choose any \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face-to-cone correspondence for polyhedra under maximization-oriented normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normal cone attached to \(F\) is
\[
N_P(F):=N_P(x)=\{u:\langle u,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \text{for every }y\in P\},
\qquad x\in\operatorname{ri}F.
\]
This definition is independent of the chosen relative-interior point. It satisfies
\[
u\in N_P(F)\Longleftrightarrow F\subseteq F_P(u),
\qquad u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F)\Longleftrightarrow F=F_P(u).
\]
The correspondence reverses incidence:
\[
F\subseteq G\Longleftrightarrow N_P(G)\ \text{is a face of }N_P(F).
\]
For full-dimensional \(P\), \(\dim F+\dim N_P(F)=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal cone of a face is the point normal cone at any relative-interior point of that face. It consists of objectives for which the face is contained in the optimizer set, while its relative interior consists of objectives selecting exactly that face. Face containment is reversed as face containment among the corresponding normal cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F\subseteq G\Longleftrightarrow N_P(G)\unlhd N_P(F),\qquad F_P(u)=F\Longleftrightarrow u\in\operatorname{ri}N_P(F).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[N_P(F)=\bigcap_{x\in F}N_P(x)=N_P(x_F)\quad(x_F\in\operatorname{ri}F).\]
The map \(F\mapsto N_P(F)\) is an anti-isomorphism from the nonempty face poset of \(P\) to the cone poset of its normal fan.
special_cases_latex: Vertices correspond to maximal normal cones.
Facets of a full-dimensional polyhedron correspond to one-dimensional normal cones generated by outward facet normals.
immediate_consequences_latex: Intersections of adjacent maximal normal cones encode the smallest face containing their corresponding vertices.
The face lattice can be recovered from the normal fan together with reversed order.
boundary_notes: For non-full-dimensional \(P\), all normal cones contain the orthogonal complement of the direction space, so the dimension formula must be adjusted.
