knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
A polyhedron \(P
i\mathbb R^n\) may be represented externally as \(P=\{x:Axi b\}\) or internally as \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\), where \(V,R\) are finite and \(L\) is a linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact polyhedral representations, structure-preserving operations, and representation-sensitive computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedral operations-computation interface is the specification of a polyhedral object by a finite representation together with operations whose outputs admit finite polyhedral representations. Its primitive operations include affine images and preimages, finite intersections, Cartesian products, Minkowski sums, polarity under the required origin conventions, face extraction, and coordinate projection. An operation is representation preserving when an output \(H\)- or \(V\)-description can be obtained from the input descriptions by finitely many linear-algebraic, linear-inequality, redundancy-removal, and projection or elimination steps. Representation conversion is the task of passing between \(H\)- and \(V\)-descriptions of the same polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The operations-computation interface connects finite descriptions of polyhedra with operations that preserve polyhedral structure. A polyhedron may be given by inequalities or by finitely many points, rays, and a lineality space. Intersections, affine transformations, products, sums, polarity under suitable conventions, faces, and projections remain within the polyhedral class. Computation depends on the input and requested output representations, and conversion between inequality and generator descriptions is itself a central operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every object produced by the stated finite affine, intersection, product, Minkowski-sum, face, polarity, and projection operations is polyhedral and admits a finite \(H\)- or \(V\)-representation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An \(H\)-description specifies finitely many affine halfspaces whose intersection is \(P\).
A \(V\)-description specifies finite sets \(V,R\) and a subspace \(L\) with \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
special_cases_latex: Intersection is immediate in \(H\)-representation by concatenating inequalities.
Minkowski addition is immediate in \(V\)-representation by combining generators, while projection is immediate as a linear image of generators.
immediate_consequences_latex: The most convenient representation depends on the requested operation.
Finite representability is preserved even when the output description may be much larger than the input description.
boundary_notes: Closure under an operation does not imply polynomial output size or polynomial running time.

children.title: Polyhedral Set Calculus
children.top_down_role: Basic operations preserving polyhedrality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in finite-dimensional real spaces. A polyhedron is a set \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), with finitely many weak linear inequalities; the empty set is allowed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This entry concerns exact set operations on finite-dimensional polyhedra, not numerical approximation or infinite-dimensional generalized polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedral set calculus consists of the operations \(P_1\cap\cdots\cap P_k\), \(P_1\times\cdots\times P_k\), affine inverse image \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x: Mx+c\in Q\}\), affine image \(T(P)=\{Mx+c:x\in P\}\), and Minkowski sum \(P+Q=\{p+q:p\in P,q\in Q\}\). For every finite family of polyhedra and every affine map \(T(x)=Mx+c\), each resulting set is again a polyhedron. A direct constraint description exists for intersections, products, and inverse images; images and sums may instead be obtained as projections of higher-dimensional polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral set calculus is the collection of finite intersection, Cartesian product, affine inverse-image, affine-image, and Minkowski-sum operations on finite-dimensional polyhedra. Every listed operation returns a polyhedron. Intersections, products, and inverse images have immediate finite inequality descriptions, while images and sums can be represented as projections of polyhedra in product spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_i,Q\text{ polyhedral and }T\text{ affine}\Longrightarrow \bigcap_iP_i,\ \prod_iP_i,\ T^{-1}(Q),\ T(P_1),\ P_1+P_2\text{ are polyhedral}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P+Q=L(P\times Q)\), where \(L(p,q)=p+q\).
\(T(P)=\{y:\exists x,\ Ax\le b,\ y=Mx+c\}\) when \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\).
special_cases_latex: Affine subspaces, polyhedral cones, and polytopes are closed under the applicable listed operations.
Coordinate projection is the affine-image case in which \(M\) selects coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every set produced by this calculus admits both a finite half-space description and a finite point-ray-lineality description.
Minkowski sums of polyhedra are closed, unlike sums of arbitrary closed convex sets.
boundary_notes: Set union and ordinary set difference do not generally preserve convexity and are not included.
An affine image can have a much larger irredundant inequality description than its input.

notation.meaning: Affine image of a set under T.

children.title: Constraint-Side Set Calculus
children.top_down_role: Constraint-side constructions with direct finite descriptions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_ix\le b_i\}\), \(Q=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:Cy\le d\}\), and \(T(x)=Mx+c\). Inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The calculus is restricted to constructions whose output inequalities follow directly from input inequalities, without existential variable elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Constraint-side set calculus assigns finite inequality descriptions to intersections, Cartesian products, and affine inverse images. Explicitly, \(\bigcap_{i=1}^kP_i=\{x:[A_1^\top\ \cdots\ A_k^\top]^\top x\le[b_1^\top\ \cdots\ b_k^\top]^\top\}\); \(P_1\times P_2=\{(x,z):A_1x\le b_1,\ A_2z\le b_2\}\); and \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x:CMx\le d-Cc\}\). Equalities may be retained or replaced by two opposite inequalities. These formulas define polyhedra even when the resulting system is infeasible or contains redundant constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-side polyhedral calculus forms intersections by stacking inequalities, Cartesian products by placing systems on separate variable blocks, and affine inverse images by substituting the affine map into the target inequalities. The formulas remain valid for infeasible and redundant systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_iP_i,\ P_1\times P_2,\text{ and }T^{-1}(Q)\) have the displayed finite constraint descriptions and are polyhedra.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Q=\{y:Cy\le d,\ Ey=f\}\), then \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x:CMx\le d-Cc,\ EMx=f-Ec\}\).
special_cases_latex: For a linear map \(T(x)=Mx\), the pullback is \(\{x:CMx\le d\}\).
Intersecting with an affine subspace amounts to appending linear equations.
immediate_consequences_latex: The number of displayed constraints is additive under finite intersection and Cartesian product.
No projection or conversion procedure is needed for these operations.
boundary_notes: Affine images generally do not have a direct constraint description by substitution and belong to projection-elimination calculus.
The displayed systems need not be irredundant.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Intersections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite intersection of polyhedra is polyhedral and is represented by stacking their inequality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the vertically stacked data by \[\widehat A=\begin{pmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_r\end{pmatrix},\qquad \widehat b=\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\ \vdots\\ b_r\end{pmatrix}.\] Then \[\bigcap_{i=1}^rP_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\widehat Ax\leq\widehat b\}.\] Consequently, every finite intersection of polyhedra in the same ambient space is a polyhedron; the intersection may be empty, and redundant rows may be removed without changing the represented set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The intersection \(\bigcap_{i=1}^rP_i\) is a polyhedron represented by stacking all defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections in a common Euclidean ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Products of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cartesian product of two polyhedra is described by stacking their inequalities in block-diagonal form, and is therefore a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Cartesian product admits the block inequality representation
\[
P_1\times P_2=\left\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^{n_1+n_2}:\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0\\0&A_2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{pmatrix}\le\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\b_2\end{pmatrix}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, Cartesian products preserve polyhedrality; the representation uses the combined constraints without introducing auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\times P_2\) is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inequality representation of a Cartesian product.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of the two sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Sections of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a polyhedron with an affine set amounts to adjoining affine equality constraints, producing another, possibly empty, polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine section has the explicit representation
\[
P\cap L=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}.
\]
Equivalently, replacing the equality by two inequalities gives
\[
P\cap L=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Cx\le d,\ -Cx\le-d\}.
\]
Thus an affine section of a polyhedron is a polyhedron. No consistency assumption is required, so the resulting polyhedron may be empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap L=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\) is a polyhedron, possibly empty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-side description; empty sections are allowed.

children.title: Affine Transformation Pair
children.top_down_role: Transformation of polyhedra under affine mappings.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(T(x)=Mx+c\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine maps are allowed to be singular, injective, surjective, or constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine transformation pair consists of the image \(T(P)=\{Mx+c:x\in P\}\) and inverse image \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Mx+c\in Q\}\). If \(Q=\{y:Ay\le b\}\), then \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x:AMx\le b-Ac\}\). If \(P=\{x:Bx\le d\}\), then \(T(P)=\{y:\exists x,\ Bx\le d,\ y=Mx+c\}\). Both members of the pair are polyhedra; the inverse image has a direct constraint description, whereas the image is naturally an existential projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine map, the transformation pair is its image operation and its inverse-image operation. Substitution gives the inverse-image inequalities directly. The image is the set of target vectors admitting a feasible preimage and is therefore a projection. Both operations preserve polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P,Q\text{ polyhedral}\Longrightarrow T(P)\text{ and }T^{-1}(Q)\text{ are polyhedral}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in T(P)\iff \exists x\in P\text{ such that }y=Mx+c\).
\(x\in T^{-1}(Q)\iff T(x)\in Q\).
special_cases_latex: Translation is obtained with \(M=I\).
Coordinate projection is obtained when \(M\) selects a subset of coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine equivalences preserve the face dimensions and inclusion structure of a polyhedron.
A singular image may reduce affine dimension or collapse distinct generators.
boundary_notes: The notation \(T^{-1}(Q)\) denotes a set preimage and does not require an inverse mapping.
The displayed existential image need not be an irredundant formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Images of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-dimensional affine image of a polyhedron is a polyhedron, even when the affine map is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine image
\[
T(P)=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:\exists x\in P,\ y=Mx+q\}
\]
is a polyhedron. In particular, if \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), then \(T(P)\) is the projection onto the \(y\)-coordinates of
\[
\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}:Ax\le b,\ y=Mx+q\}.
\]
No injectivity, surjectivity, or full-rank hypothesis on \(M\) is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(P)=\{Mx+q:x\in P\}\) is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine-image closure, including rank-deficient maps.

notation.meaning: Affine mapping from the source space to the target space.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Preimages of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting an affine map into a polyhedron's inequalities gives an explicit polyhedral description of its preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine preimage is
\[
T^{-1}(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Mx+q\in Q\}=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:AMx\le b-Aq\}.
\]
Hence affine preimages preserve polyhedrality without any rank assumption on \(M\). The preimage may be empty; if \(M\) has a nontrivial kernel and the preimage is nonempty, it contains every translate of \(\ker M\) through each of its points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^{-1}(Q)=\{x:AMx\le b-Aq\}\) is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct substitution into a finite inequality description.

notation.meaning: Preimage of the target polyhedron under the affine map.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Sensitive Transformation Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The map controls image dimension and can collapse image recession directions, while its kernel supplies recession directions to every nonempty affine preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine image satisfies
\[
\dim T(P)=\dim M(L),\qquad \operatorname{rec}(T(P))=M(K).
\]
Accordingly, \(T(P)\) is bounded if and only if \(K\subseteq\ker M\). If \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(T^{-1}(Q)\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\operatorname{rec}(T^{-1}(Q))=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Md\in\operatorname{rec}(Q)\}.
\]
In particular, a nonempty bounded affine preimage requires \(\ker M=\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(T(x)=Mx+q\), where \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(q\in\mathbb R^m\).
For the preimage identity, \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(T^{-1}(Q)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim T(P)=\dim M(L)\), \(\operatorname{rec}(T(P))=M(K)\), and \(\operatorname{rec}(T^{-1}(Q))=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Md\in\operatorname{rec}(Q)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional rank effects on image dimension, image boundedness, and nonempty affine-preimage recession behavior.

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of the polyhedron.

children.title: Polyhedral Additive-Erosion Calculus
children.top_down_role: Additive and erosion-type operations that retain polyhedral structure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P,Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedra. For \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), write \(\sigma_Q(a)=\sup_{q\in Q}a^\top q\), with values in \(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty,-\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is finite-dimensional exact set calculus. The explicit erosion formula uses an H-description of the minuend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The additive-erosion pair is the Minkowski sum \(P+Q=\{p+q:p\in P,q\in Q\}\) and the geometric erosion \(P\ominus Q=\{x:x+Q\subseteq P\}=\bigcap_{q\in Q}(P-q)\). If \(P=\{x:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), then \(P\ominus Q=\{x:a_i^\top x\le b_i-\sigma_Q(a_i),\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), interpreted as empty if some required support value is \(+\infty\). Thus both \(P+Q\) and \(P\ominus Q\) are polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minkowski addition collects all sums of one point from each set. Erosion collects all translations whose copy of the second set lies in the first. For a polyhedral minuend, each erosion inequality is obtained by subtracting the support value of the eroding set in the corresponding normal direction. Both operations preserve polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P,Q\text{ polyhedral}\Longrightarrow P+Q\text{ and }P\ominus Q\text{ are polyhedral}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in P\ominus Q\iff x+q\in P\) for every \(q\in Q\).
\(P+Q=L(P\times Q)\) for \(L(p,q)=p+q\).
special_cases_latex: \(P\ominus\{q\}=P-q\).
For \(Q=\{0\}\), both operations return \(P\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(Q\) is a polytope, each \(\sigma_Q(a_i)\) is attained at a vertex.
Erosion may be empty even when both input polyhedra are nonempty.
boundary_notes: Erosion is not ordinary Minkowski subtraction and need not invert Minkowski addition.
If \(Q\) is empty, conventions for \(P\ominus Q\) must be fixed separately.

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski Sums of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Minkowski sum of two nonempty polyhedra is a polyhedron and is the addition-map image of their Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Minkowski sum
\[
P+Q=\{p+q:p\in P,\ q\in Q\}
\]
is a polyhedron. It is also the linear image
\[
P+Q=S(P\times Q),\qquad S(p,q)=p+q.
\]
Its recession cone satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rec}(P+Q)=\operatorname{rec}(P)+\operatorname{rec}(Q).
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P+Q=\{p+q:p\in P,\ q\in Q\}\) is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure under finite-dimensional Minkowski addition.

knowledge_statements.title: Pontryagin Differences of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Pontryagin difference is obtained by tightening each inequality of the minuend by the support value of the subtrahend in that inequality's normal direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
P\ominus Q=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:z+Q\subseteq P\},\qquad \sigma_Q(u)=\sup_{q\in Q}u^{\mathsf T}q.
\]
Then
\[
P\ominus Q=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}z\le b_i-\sigma_Q(a_i),\ i=1,\ldots,r\}.
\]
If some \(\sigma_Q(a_i)=+\infty\), the difference is empty; otherwise the displayed finite inequalities show that it is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\ominus Q\) is a possibly empty polyhedron described by support-function bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint representation using extended-real support values.

notation.meaning: Pontryagin difference, or erosion, of the two sets.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The support-function formula is mathematically plausible and representation is the correct kind, but the cited conjugacy chapter is not a sufficiently direct locator for the Pontryagin-difference formula and its extended-value case.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness-Sensitive Additive Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum is bounded exactly when both polyhedra are bounded; a nonempty Pontryagin difference inherits precisely the recession directions of its minuend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The recession identities are
\[
\operatorname{rec}(P+Q)=\operatorname{rec}(P)+\operatorname{rec}(Q),\qquad
\operatorname{rec}(P\ominus Q)=\operatorname{rec}(P).
\]
Therefore \(P+Q\) is bounded if and only if both \(P\) and \(Q\) are bounded. If \(P\ominus Q\ne\varnothing\), it is bounded if and only if \(P\) is bounded. Moreover, nonemptiness of \(P\ominus Q\) requires \(\operatorname{rec}(Q)\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\).
assumptions_latex: When discussing \(P\ominus Q\), assume it is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P+Q\) is bounded exactly when both summands are bounded, while \(P\ominus Q\) is bounded exactly when \(P\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonempty polyhedra; boundedness is characterized through recession cones.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of a nonempty closed convex set.

children.title: Projection-Elimination Calculus

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p:Ax+Bz\le b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The entry concerns exact elimination of finitely many real variables from weak linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projection-elimination calculus identifies the coordinate projection \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p,\ Ax+Bz\le b\}\) with elimination of the quantified variables \(z\). An elimination description is any finite system \(Cx\le d\) satisfying \(\{x:Cx\le d\}=\operatorname{proj}_x(P)\). Such a system always exists because coordinate projections, and therefore arbitrary linear images, of polyhedra are polyhedra. Successive one-variable elimination is one valid realization of this calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection-elimination calculus treats projecting a polyhedron onto selected coordinates as eliminating existentially quantified variables from a finite linear-inequality system. An elimination description is any finite inequality system defining exactly the projected set. It always exists in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P)=\{x:\exists z,\ Ax+Bz\le b\}=\{x:Cx\le d\}\) for some finite \(C,d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every linear image can be written as a coordinate projection of \(\{(x,y):x\in P,\ y=Mx\}\).
special_cases_latex: Eliminating one scalar variable gives Fourier–Motzkin elimination.
If \(p=0\), no elimination occurs.
immediate_consequences_latex: The projection is closed and polyhedral.
The output description may contain redundant inequalities.
boundary_notes: Projection here is a linear image, not nearest-point metric projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Existentially eliminating variables from a finite linear-inequality system produces its coordinate projection, which remains a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The coordinate projection of \(R\) is the polyhedron
\[
\pi_x(R)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^m,\ Ax+By\le b\}.
\]
Thus existential elimination of finitely many real variables preserves polyhedrality. An explicit inequality representation may require elimination and may be substantially larger than the original system.
assumptions_latex: \(R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}:Ax+By\le b\}\) is a polyhedron, where \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(R)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^m,\ Ax+By\le b\}\) is a polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedral projection of \(P\) onto the \(x\)-space is \(\pi(P)=\operatorname{proj}_x(P)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p,\ (x,z)\in P\}\). If \(P=\{(x,z):Ax+Bz\le b\}\), membership in the projection is exactly feasibility of \(Bz\le b-Ax\). The projected set is a polyhedron, including when it is empty, all of \(\mathbb R^n\), or lower-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral projection is the set of retained-coordinate vectors having at least one feasible completion in the eliminated coordinates. For an inequality description, membership is equivalent to feasibility of the remaining inequalities in the eliminated variables. The result is again a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ polyhedral}\Longrightarrow \pi(P)=\{x:\exists z,\ (x,z)\in P\}\text{ polyhedral}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\pi(P)\) is the linear image of \(P\) under the coordinate-selection matrix.
\(x\notin\pi(P)\) exactly when the completion system in \(z\) is infeasible.

A general linear image \(MP\) is a projection of the graph formulation \(y=Mx\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fourier–Motzkin Elimination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fourier–Motzkin elimination pairs every upper bound with every lower bound on an eliminated variable, retaining constraints independent of that variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the inequalities by \(I_+=\{i:\alpha_i>0\}\), \(I_-=\{i:\alpha_i<0\}\), and \(I_0=\{i:\alpha_i=0\}\). Retain \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) for \(i\in I_0\). For every \((i,j)\in I_+\times I_-\), generate
\[
(\alpha_i a_j-\alpha_j a_i)^{\mathsf T}x\le \alpha_i b_j-\alpha_j b_i.
\]
Remove the variable \(t\), optionally discard redundant inequalities, and repeat for further variables. The final system represents the required coordinate projection.
assumptions_latex: A finite system is written as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha_i t\le b_i\), with one scalar variable \(t\) to eliminate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated inequalities describe exactly the projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-variable elimination; iteration eliminates several variables.

notation.meaning: Indices with positive, negative, and zero coefficients of the eliminated variable.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The single-variable Fourier–Motzkin update and its signs are correct, and algorithm is the exact content kind for this leaf. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{(x,t):a_i^\top x+\alpha_i t\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(t\in\mathbb R\) is to be eliminated.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is exact elimination for weak real linear inequalities; redundancy removal is not part of the defining rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the rows into \(I_+=\{i:\alpha_i>0\}\), \(I_-=\{i:\alpha_i<0\}\), and \(I_0=\{i:\alpha_i=0\}\). Fourier–Motzkin elimination of \(t\) retains \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) for \(i\in I_0\) and, for every \((i,k)\in I_-\times I_+\), adds the comparison of the lower bound from row \(i\) with the upper bound from row \(k\): \((b_i-a_i^\top x)/\alpha_i\le(b_k-a_k^\top x)/\alpha_k\). The resulting finite system defines exactly \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fourier–Motzkin elimination partitions inequalities according to the sign of the eliminated variable's coefficient. It retains zero-coefficient rows and combines every lower-bound row with every upper-bound row. The resulting inequalities define exactly the projection after eliminating that variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P)\) equals the solution set of the retained \(I_0\) inequalities and all pairwise \(I_-\)-to-\(I_+\) bound comparisons.
equivalent_formulations_latex: After positive rescaling, every generated inequality is the sum of one row with positive \(t\)-coefficient and one row with negative \(t\)-coefficient, cancelling \(t\).
special_cases_latex: If \(I_+=\varnothing\) or \(I_-=\varnothing\), no paired inequalities are generated.
Repeated application eliminates a block of variables.
immediate_consequences_latex: One step produces at most \(|I_0|+|I_-||I_+|\) inequalities before redundancy removal.
The projection remains polyhedral.
boundary_notes: Generated inequalities may be duplicate or redundant.
Strict inequalities and integer quantifiers require different elimination rules.

notation.meaning: Sign partition for the eliminated variable's coefficients.

children.title: Projection through Generators
children.top_down_role: Image computation from point, ray, and lineality descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection through Generators
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To project a generator representation, project every point, ray, and lineality generator, then remove zero or redundant images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite generator sets \(V,R,L\), the affine image is
\[
T(P)=\operatorname{conv}\{Mv+q:v\in V\}+\operatorname{cone}\{Mr:r\in R\}+\operatorname{span}\{M\ell:\ell\in L\}.
\]
Zero images may be deleted, and duplicate or redundant generators may be removed without changing the set. For a coordinate projection, \(M\) is the corresponding coordinate-selection matrix, so projection requires only mapping the point, ray, and lineality generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(P)=\operatorname{conv}(MV+q)+\operatorname{cone}(MR)+\operatorname{span}(ML)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine projection or image computed directly from generators.

notation.meaning: Finite sets of point, ray, and lineality generators.
Elementwise images of finite generator sets.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The affine mapping of point, ray, and lineality generators is correct, and representation fits the terminal container. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}+\operatorname{cone}\{d_1,\ldots,d_s\}+L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(L\) is a linear subspace, and let \(T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This formula describes the image directly from point, ray, and lineality generators; redundant or zero images may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projection through generators is the operation \(T(P)=\operatorname{conv}\{Tv_1,\ldots,Tv_r\}+\operatorname{cone}\{Td_1,\ldots,Td_s\}+T(L)\). Equivalently, the same nonnegative coefficients and convex-combination constraint used to represent a point of \(P\) represent its image after applying \(T\) to every generator. Hence a generator description passes through a linear projection without variable elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To project a generator-described polyhedron, apply the linear map to every point generator, ray generator, and lineality direction. Their convex, conic, and linear hulls give the image. The resulting list is valid but may contain zero, duplicate, or nonextreme generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(P)=\operatorname{conv}(TV)+\operatorname{cone}(TD)+T(L)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(P=\{\sum_i\lambda_iv_i+\sum_j\mu_jd_j+\ell:\lambda,\mu\ge0,\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ell\in L\}\), apply \(T\) termwise.
special_cases_latex: For coordinate projection, delete the eliminated coordinates from every generator.
For a polytope, only the convex-hull term remains.
immediate_consequences_latex: Linear images of finitely generated polyhedra are finitely generated.
Extreme generators of the image form a subset of the nonzero mapped generators after redundancy removal.
boundary_notes: An extreme generator of the input can become nonextreme or zero after projection.
The formula does not itself produce an irredundant generator set.

children.title: Elimination Pathology Family
children.top_down_role: Representation explosion, redundancy, and intrinsic-dimension changes during elimination.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a polyhedral formulation \(P_k\) and projection \(Q_k=\pi_k(P_k)\), let \(m(P_k)\) denote the number of input inequalities, \(f(Q_k)\) the number of inequalities in an irredundant H-description, and \(g_j\) the number of inequalities present after elimination step \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition classifies representation behavior of exact real-variable elimination, independently of a particular implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elimination pathology family is a sequence \((P_k,\pi_k)\) for which at least one of the following quantities is unbounded with \(k\): the output expansion ratio \(f(Q_k)/m(P_k)\); the intermediate expansion ratio \(\max_j g_j/f(Q_k)\); the redundancy ratio \(g_{\mathrm{final}}/f(Q_k)\); or the affine-dimension drop \(\dim P_k-\dim Q_k\). The first records intrinsically large projected descriptions, the next two distinguish transient or final redundancy, and the last records collapse under projection. These properties can coexist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elimination pathology family is a sequence of polyhedral projections exhibiting unbounded output growth, excessive intermediate growth, excessive redundancy, or increasing affine-dimension loss. The measures separate intrinsically large projections from blow-up caused by the chosen elimination process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P_k,\pi_k)\) is pathological when at least one of \(f(Q_k)/m(P_k)\), \(\max_jg_j/f(Q_k)\), \(g_{\mathrm{final}}/f(Q_k)\), or \(\dim P_k-\dim Q_k\) is unbounded.
special_cases_latex: The cross-polytope extended formulation gives a family with linearly many extension facets and exponentially many projected facets.
Fourier–Motzkin pairing can cause large intermediate systems even when the final irredundant system is small.
immediate_consequences_latex: Redundancy removal can control transient size but cannot remove intrinsic output-size growth.
Elimination order can change the intermediate expansion ratio.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert that every projection has pathological growth.
Counts depend on the chosen formulation and, for intermediate ratios, the elimination order.

notation.meaning: Constraint count after elimination step j.

source_refs.locator: §3.15, projection-size discussion and Example 3.45, pp. 113–115
Chapter I, §9, Problem 1 and following remark on inequality growth, p. 38

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Representation Blow-Up
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One elimination step can replace m variable-dependent inequalities by about m²/4 pairwise inequalities, and repeated steps can compound this growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fourier–Motzkin elimination forms one new inequality for each positive-negative pair, so the raw number generated is
\[
pq.
\]
If \(p+q=m\), then
\[
pq\le\left\lfloor\frac{m^2}{4}\right\rfloor,
\]
and equality occurs when the positive and negative classes are as balanced as possible. Hence a single elimination step can cause quadratic representation growth, while repeated steps can compound the growth unless redundancy detection substantially reduces intermediate systems.
assumptions_latex: One Fourier–Motzkin step eliminates a variable appearing positively in \(p\) inequalities and negatively in \(q\) inequalities.
No generated inequality is removed as duplicate or redundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step generates \(pq\) inequalities, which can be \(\lfloor m^2/4\rfloor\) when \(p+q=m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case raw output size for one elimination step.

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive and negative occurrences of the eliminated variable.
Number of inequalities involving the eliminated variable.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The raw pair count and the bound floor(m squared over 4) are correct for one elimination step under the stated assumptions. Complexity bound is the correct kind for this blow-up leaf, but no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Affine Equalities
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection can force affine equations among retained variables even when the lifted formulation contains no explicit equation involving only those variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{(x,y):Ax+By\le b\}\) be nonempty and let \(Q=\operatorname{proj}_xP\). It may happen that \(Q\) is contained in a proper affine subspace although no equality involving only \(x\) occurs explicitly in the lifted description. Equivalently, there can exist \(c\ne0\) and \(\delta\in\mathbb R\) such that \(c^Tx=\delta\) for every \(x\in Q\). Such equalities are generated by compatible linear combinations of eliminated inequalities and must be identified to obtain the intrinsic affine description of \(Q\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}:Ax+By\le b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Elimination can convert inequalities into affine equalities defining \(\operatorname{aff}Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-hull constraints revealed by projection rather than explicit in the retained variables.

notation.meaning: Projection of the lifted polyhedron onto the x-coordinates.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification fits the elimination-pathology leaf, and the statement is mathematically plausible and internally consistent. No cited source with an inspectable locator supports the projection-induced equality claim or its linear-combination characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Induced Redundancy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination may create duplicate or dominated inequalities, so an irredundant lifted system need not yield an irredundant projected system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let elimination of \(y\) from \(Ax+By\le b\) produce \(Q=\{x:Cx\le d\}\). An output row \(C_i x\le d_i\) is elimination-induced redundant when removing it leaves \(Q\) unchanged, equivalently when \(C_i x\le d_i\) is implied by the other output rows together with the affine equalities of \(Q\). Such redundancy can occur even when the lifted description is irredundant, because distinct combinations of lifted inequalities may project to identical or dominated supporting inequalities.
assumptions_latex: A valid inequality description \(Q=\{x:Cx\le d\}\) is produced by eliminating \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting system can contain inequalities implied by its remaining rows and affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy introduced by projection-elimination, independently of redundancy in the input system.

notation.meaning: The ith row of the eliminated inequality system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The statement accurately identifies elimination-induced redundancy and fits a failure-boundary container. An authoritative source with a specific section, theorem, or page locator is required for the implication characterization and the claim that irredundant lifted systems can yield redundant projected systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic-Dimension Changes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection cannot increase affine dimension; over a relative-interior projected point, the lost dimension equals the dimension of the fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) and \(Q=\operatorname{proj}_xP\), one has \(0\le\dim Q\le\min\{n,\dim P\}\). If \(x_0\in\operatorname{ri}Q\), the fiber \(F_{x_0}=P\cap(\{x_0\}\times\mathbb R^m)\) has the generic fiber dimension and satisfies \(\dim P=\dim Q+\dim F_{x_0}\). Hence elimination can lower intrinsic dimension; the lost dimension is the dimension carried by a relative-interior fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection may strictly reduce intrinsic dimension, with \(\dim Q=\dim P-\dim(P\cap(\{x_0\}\times\mathbb R^m))\) on relative-interior fibers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine dimension under coordinate projection of a nonempty polyhedron.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property is locally appropriate and states a precise relative-interior fiber dimension formula. Because that exact formula is the substantive claim and no citation is supplied, its hypotheses and generic-fiber conclusion require an authoritative source.

children.title: Representation-Conversion Problems
children.top_down_role: Transformations between external, generator, and incidence descriptions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: A polyhedron may be represented externally as \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\), internally as \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(L)\), or combinatorially by its finite face-incidence structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion means exact equality of represented sets or exact recovery of incidence data; it does not prescribe one algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representation-conversion problem takes one finite representation \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{in}}\) of a polyhedron \(P\) and asks for a finite representation \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}})=\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{in}})=P\), or for the face-incidence relation determined by \(P\). The principal geometric conversions are H-to-V, V-to-H, and H/V-to-incidence. Minkowski–Weyl equivalence guarantees existence of finite H- and V-representations, while finiteness of the face lattice guarantees finite incidence output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral representation-conversion problem asks for a new finite description of exactly the same polyhedron, or for its finite face-incidence structure. The main directions are constraints to generators, generators to constraints, and geometric descriptions to incidence data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{in}})=P\Longrightarrow\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}})=P\), with \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}}\) finite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: H-to-V seeks \(V,R,L\) with \(\{x:Ax\le b,Ex=f\}=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(L)\).
V-to-H seeks \(A,b,E,f\) satisfying the reverse equality.
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, the V-description contains only points.
For a pointed cone, conversion reduces to inequalities versus extreme rays.
immediate_consequences_latex: Vertex enumeration and facet enumeration are dual conversion problems under polarity in suitable full-dimensional settings.
Conversion output can be exponentially larger than input.
boundary_notes: A valid output need not be irredundant unless minimality is explicitly required.
Bit complexity and enumeration order are separate algorithmic specifications.

notation.meaning: Polyhedron represented by finite data R.

children.title: Extreme-Generator Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Conversion from external constraints to generators.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron, with lineality space \(L=\{d:Ad=0,\ Ed=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The output is geometric and irredundant up to positive rescaling of rays and choice of a basis for lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extreme-generator enumeration is the H-to-V problem of producing all vertices \(V(P)\), one nonzero representative of every extreme ray of the pointed quotient recession cone \(\operatorname{rec}(P)/L\), and a basis of \(L\), so that \(P=\operatorname{conv}V(P)+\operatorname{cone}R(P)+L\). If \(P\) contains no lines, \(L=\{0\}\) and \(R(P)\) consists precisely of representatives of the extreme directions of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given linear constraints, extreme-generator enumeration outputs every vertex, one representative of each extreme recession ray after removing lineality, and a basis for the lineality space. These data reconstruct the polyhedron as a convex hull plus a conic hull plus lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V(P)+\operatorname{cone}R(P)+L\), with \(V(P)\) and \(R(P)\) complete and nonredundant in the stated senses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a pointed polyhedron, enumerate all zero- and one-dimensional proper faces representing vertices and extreme rays.
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, enumerate only vertices.
For a pointed polyhedral cone, enumerate only extreme rays; the origin is its unique vertex.
immediate_consequences_latex: The output is finite.
For full-dimensional polytopes, this is the vertex-enumeration problem.
boundary_notes: A polyhedron with lineality has no ordinary extreme points or extreme rays before quotienting by lineality.
Duplicate positive multiples do not represent distinct rays.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate feasible full-rank active systems, remove duplicate solutions, and return precisely the vertices whose convex hull is the input polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an inequality description \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) of a polytope. Enumerate feasible candidates obtained from subsystems of active inequalities, or traverse adjacent bases. Retain a candidate \(v\) exactly when \(Av\le b\) and the active normals satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}A_{I(v)}=d\); merge duplicate candidates. Stop after every feasible basis or every vertex-adjacency state has been processed, and output the resulting set \(V\). Then \(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) and \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is exactly \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\), without duplicates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex enumeration from an inequality description of a bounded polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Set of vertices of a polytope.
Rows active at a feasible point.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm classification fits the enumeration leaf, and the active-normal rank test is a standard vertex characterization for a polytope represented in the ambient space. No source with a specific locator supports the enumeration procedure or its completeness conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate normalized feasible directions whose active normals have rank one below full rank, obtaining one representative per extreme ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pointed cone \(K=\{x:Ax\le0\}\). Generate nonzero feasible directions \(r\) from rank-defining active subsystems, normalize each candidate by a fixed convention, and retain it exactly when \(Ar\le0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}A_{I(r)}=d-1\). Remove positive scalar duplicates. Stop after all candidate active subsystems, or all adjacent extreme rays, have been processed. The output contains exactly one representative of each extreme ray \(\mathbb R_+r\) of \(K\).
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le0\}\) is a pointed polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output contains one nonzero representative of every extreme ray of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of extreme rays of a pointed polyhedral cone from inequalities.

notation.meaning: Ray generated by a nonzero vector.
Rows active at the ray generator.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is appropriately scoped to a pointed polyhedral cone and states the expected rank test and duplicate normalization. Its completeness and exact-one-representative conclusion require a cited authoritative enumeration source.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointed Polyhedron Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pointed polyhedron, enumerate vertices and recession-cone extreme rays; together they form an exact finite generator description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonempty pointed polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\). Enumerate its vertices by feasible active systems of rank \(d\), and enumerate normalized extreme-ray generators of \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{r:Ar\le0\}\) by active systems of rank \(d-1\). Remove duplicates and stop when both finite enumerations are exhausted. With the resulting sets \(V\) and \(R\), output \((V,R)\). The representation is exact: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty and pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumerated vertices and extreme rays give \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined generator enumeration for nonempty pointed, possibly unbounded polyhedra.

notation.meaning: Normalized representatives of recession-cone extreme rays.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm classification and pointed-polyhedron scope fit the leaf, and the generator conclusion has the correct form. No inspectable citation supports the combined vertex and recession-ray enumeration procedure or the exact representation claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Sensitive Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate lineality, enumerate point and ray generators in the pointed quotient, then lift them and add the lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonempty polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\). Compute its lineality space \(L=\{r:Ar=0\}\), choose a complement \(W\) with \(\mathbb R^d=W\oplus L\), and enumerate the vertices and extreme recession rays of the pointed polyhedron represented in the quotient \(\mathbb R^d/L\), equivalently in \(W\). Lift representatives to finite sets \(V\) and \(R\), and output bases for \(L\) together with \((V,R)\). Then \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Enumeration modulo \(L\) yields \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator enumeration after separating the lineality space.

notation.meaning: A linear complement of the lineality space.
Finite point and ray representative sets.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly separates lineality conceptually and fits the terminal container. A source is needed for the quotient-to-complement realization, lifting procedure, and exact generator representation, especially because these steps are only described at a high level.

children.title: Facet Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Conversion from generators to irredundant external descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find supporting inequalities valid on every generator, retain those exposing codimension-one faces, and output them with the affine-hull equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\). Compute \(\operatorname{aff}P\), then generate supporting pairs \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^Tv\le\beta\) for all \(v\in V\), \(a^Tr\le0\) for all \(r\in R\), and \(a^T\ell=0\) for all \(\ell\in L\). Retain one normalized pair exactly when its equality set has dimension \(\dim P-1\), and remove duplicates. Output affine-hull equations and the retained inequalities; their intersection is \(P\), and each retained inequality defines a facet.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a nonempty polyhedron with finite generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an irredundant equality-and-facet description of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a finite generator description into affine-hull equations and facet inequalities.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and generator-to-facet conversion match the node role. The validity conditions and codimension-one contact criterion are plausible, but no source with a section, theorem, or page locator supports completeness or irredundancy of the output.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, and let \(d=\dim P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet inequalities are taken relative to \(\operatorname{aff}P\); affine-hull equations are reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Facet enumeration is the V-to-H problem of producing equations defining \(\operatorname{aff}P\) and one supporting inequality \(a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\) for every facet \(F\) of \(P\), where \(F=P\cap\{x:a_F^\top x=\beta_F\}\) and \(\dim F=d-1\). The output must satisfy \(P=\operatorname{aff}P\cap\bigcap_F\{x:a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\}\), and distinct output inequalities must define distinct facets, modulo positive scaling and addition of affine-hull equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facet enumeration converts point, ray, and lineality generators into an irredundant external description. It outputs the affine-hull equations and exactly one supporting inequality for each codimension-one face. Their intersection with the affine hull must equal the input polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{aff}P\cap\bigcap_{F\text{ facet}}\{x:a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\}\), with \(F=P\cap\{a_F^\top x=\beta_F\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For full-dimensional \(P\), enumerate the inequalities in an irredundant H-description.
Under polarity for suitable polytopes containing the origin, facet enumeration becomes vertex enumeration of the polar.
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, the input contains only point generators.
A zero-dimensional polytope has no facets under the codimension-one convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: The output is finite because a polyhedron has finitely many faces.
Every nonredundant inequality of a full-dimensional irredundant H-description defines a facet.
boundary_notes: Lower-dimensional affine-hull equations are not facet inequalities.
Positive scalar multiples define the same oriented half-space.

notation.meaning: A facet, namely a face of dimension d minus one.

children.title: Convex Hull Computation
children.top_down_role: Facet construction from finite point sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Hull Computation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the affine hull and all supporting hyperplanes whose contact points span codimension-one faces, yielding exactly the hull's facet description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite nonempty \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Compute \(H=\operatorname{aff}V\) and \(k=\dim H\). Generate normalized supporting pairs \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^Tv_i\le\beta\) for every \(i\), and retain a pair exactly when \(\operatorname{aff}\{v_i:a^Tv_i=\beta\}\) has dimension \(k-1\). Remove duplicate supports and stop when all candidate supports have been processed. Output equations for \(H\) and the retained inequalities; their feasible set equals \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output describes exactly \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\) by affine-hull equations and facet inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the external facet description of a finite point hull.

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the input points.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Hull Computation as V-to-H Conversion
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S=\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be finite and let \(P=\operatorname{conv}S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The target is an exact external description of a bounded polyhedron; lower-dimensional hulls are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convex hull computation takes \(S\) and returns equations \(Ex=f\) for \(\operatorname{aff}S\) together with facet inequalities \(Ax\le b\) such that \(\operatorname{conv}S=\{x:Ex=f,\ Ax\le b\}\). When an irredundant output is required, each row of \(Ax\le b\) defines a distinct facet of \(P\), and points of \(S\) that are not vertices may be omitted from the minimal V-description. Membership in the hull is equivalently \(x=\sum_i\lambda_iv_i\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex hull computation converts a finite point set into affine-hull equations and facet inequalities defining exactly its convex hull. In an irredundant output, each inequality represents one facet. The same set is characterized by convex-combination coefficients on the input points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}S=\{x:Ex=f,\ Ax\le b\}=\{\sum_i\lambda_iv_i:\lambda\ge0,\sum_i\lambda_i=1\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a full-dimensional hull, the task is facet enumeration for a V-polytope.
The coefficient formulation is an extended formulation whose projection onto \(x\) is \(P\).
special_cases_latex: If all points coincide, the hull is a singleton.
If the points are affinely independent, the hull is a simplex.
immediate_consequences_latex: The hull is a polytope and therefore compact.
Only extreme input points are needed in a minimal generator description.
boundary_notes: Repeated or nonextreme input points do not change the hull.
Numerical orientation and degeneracy handling are outside this exact definition.

notation.meaning: Set of all convex combinations of points in S.

children.title: Face-Incidence Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Construction of face-lattice and adjacency information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron. A face is a set \(F=P\cap\{x:c^\top x=\delta\}\), where \(c^\top x\le\delta\) is valid for \(P\); include \(\varnothing\) and \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The output is the finite combinatorial structure of an exact polyhedron, not merely its vertex-edge graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Face-incidence enumeration produces the finite poset \(\mathcal F(P)\) of all faces ordered by inclusion. An incidence output may be represented by all pairs \((F,G)\) with \(F\subseteq G\), or minimally by cover relations \(F\lessdot G\), meaning \(F\subsetneq G\) and no face lies strictly between them. When facets and vertices are indexed, the vertex-facet incidence matrix has entry \(I_{vF}=1\) exactly when \(v\in F\). The complete cover relation determines the face lattice and its adjacency relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Face-incidence enumeration lists every face of a polyhedron and records inclusion, usually through cover relations. Vertex-facet incidence is the corresponding binary membership matrix. The full cover relation determines the finite face lattice, including vertex-edge and facet-ridge adjacency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(P)=(\{F:F\text{ is a face of }P\},\subseteq)\) is finite, and its cover relation determines all face incidences.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Two vertices are adjacent when their least containing face is one-dimensional.
Two facets are ridge-adjacent when their intersection is a face of codimension two.
special_cases_latex: For a simplex, the face lattice is the Boolean lattice on its vertices, with the empty face included.
For a polytope, every nonempty face is the convex hull of the vertices it contains.
immediate_consequences_latex: The vertex-edge graph and facet-ridge graph are induced substructures of the face lattice.
Incidence data are invariant under affine equivalence.
boundary_notes: Vertex-facet incidence alone may require closure operations to reconstruct all faces.
Improper faces must be handled consistently when reporting ranks.

notation.meaning: G covers F in the face poset.

knowledge_statements.title: Face Enumeration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate inequalities, discard empty intersections, canonicalize each nonempty face by its full active set, and output every nonempty face exactly once; add the empty face separately when required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) with irredundant inequalities and affine-hull equations \(Ex=f\). Starting with \(P\), generate candidate faces by imposing equalities \(A_i x=b_i\). Discard empty candidates, replace each nonempty candidate \(F\) by its closure index set \(I(F)=\{i:A_i x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F\}\), and merge candidates having equal closure sets. Continue until no new closure set occurs. Output the associated sets \(F_I\); these are exactly the nonempty faces of \(P\), including \(P\). Add the empty face separately if it is required by convention.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a polyhedron given by a finite irredundant inequality description, with affine-hull equations separated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs every nonempty face of \(P\) exactly once; the empty face may be added separately if required by convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of all nonempty faces from an irredundant external description.

notation.meaning: Face determined by making the indexed inequalities active.
Set of inequalities active throughout a nonempty face.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Incidence Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is determined by the facets containing it, and face containment corresponds to reverse containment of facet-incidence sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty face \(F\) of a polyhedron \(P\) with facets \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\), define \(I(F)=\{i:F\subseteq G_i\}\). Then \(F=P\cap\bigcap_{i\in I(F)}G_i\), with the intersection interpreted through the corresponding supporting equalities. For faces \(F\) and \(H\), one has \(F\subseteq H\) if and only if \(I(F)\supseteq I(H)\). Thus the facet-incidence sets, ordered by reverse inclusion, represent the nonempty face poset.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron with facets \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) and nonempty faces \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Containment among faces is encoded by reverse containment of their facet-incidence sets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding the face poset by incidences between faces and facets.

notation.meaning: Indices of facets containing a face.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the structure leaf, and the reverse-inclusion encoding is stated consistently. No authoritative face-lattice source with a specific locator is cited for face determination by containing facets or for the order equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Adjacency Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal-dimensional faces have two distinct adjacency relations: upper adjacency means their smallest common containing face has dimension one greater, while lower adjacency means their nonempty intersection has dimension one less. Vertex adjacency is the upper relation, and facet adjacency through a ridge is the lower relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) and \(H\) be distinct nonempty \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyhedron \(P\). They are upper adjacent when their join \(F\vee H\), the smallest face containing \(F\cup H\), satisfies \(\dim(F\vee H)=k+1\). They are lower adjacent when \(F\cap H\ne\varnothing\) and \(\dim(F\cap H)=k-1\). Thus two vertices are upper adjacent exactly when their join is an edge, whereas two facets are lower adjacent exactly when their intersection is a ridge.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(H\) are distinct nonempty faces of \(P\) having the same dimension \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upper adjacency is characterized by \(\dim(F\vee H)=k+1\), while lower adjacency is characterized by \(F\cap H\ne\varnothing\) and \(\dim(F\cap H)=k-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper and lower adjacency relations between equal-dimensional faces in the graded face poset.

notation.meaning: Smallest face of the polyhedron containing both faces.
Affine dimension of a nonempty face.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Lattice Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order all enumerated faces by vertex-set inclusion, add the empty face and polytope, and retain only cover relations to obtain the face-lattice Hasse diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(\mathcal F(P)\) by adjoining \(\varnothing\) and \(P\) to the enumerated proper faces. For \(F,G\in\mathcal F(P)\), set \(F\leq G\) exactly when the vertex set of \(F\) is contained in that of \(G\). Record a cover \(F\prec G\) when \(F<G\) and no enumerated face \(H\) satisfies \(F<H<G\). Output the Hasse diagram \((\mathcal F(P),\prec)\), with ranks \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=\dim F+1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\varnothing)=0\).
assumptions_latex: All faces of \(P\), together with their dimensions and vertex sets, have been enumerated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting ordered set is the face lattice of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction from complete face and vertex-incidence data.

notation.meaning: cover relation in the face poset

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports face-lattice reconstruction.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its content kind fit Face-Lattice Reconstruction, and vertex-set inclusion correctly orders faces of a polytope when complete face data are available. No cited source supports the reconstruction procedure or rank convention, so the record requires a specific inspectable source.

children.top_down_role: Canonical conversion paradigms without procedural payload.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Classification of Conversion Method Families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathsf H(P)\), \(\mathsf V(P)\), and \(\mathsf F(P)\) denote external, generator, and face-incidence representations of the same polyhedron \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition classifies methods by maintained invariant and input-output relation; it intentionally omits procedural pseudocode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representation-conversion method family is a class of finite procedures sharing a conversion relation and a mathematical invariant. The canonical families are paired-description methods maintaining \(\operatorname{set}(H_i)=\operatorname{set}(V_i)\); traversal methods enumerating adjacent faces while preserving validity and nonrepetition; incremental hull methods maintaining \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}\); and elimination or polarity reductions translating one conversion problem into projection or a dual conversion problem. A member is correct only when its terminal representation defines exactly the input polyhedron or its complete requested face set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation-conversion methods are grouped by the invariant they maintain: paired constraints and generators, adjacency traversal, incremental hulls, or reductions through elimination and polarity. Correctness means that the terminal output represents exactly the input polyhedron or the complete requested incidence structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every method in the family maintains its stated invariant and terminates, when defined, with \(\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}})=\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{in}})\) or the complete requested face set.
special_cases_latex: Double-description methods are paired-description methods.
Reverse-search methods are traversal methods; incremental convex-hull algorithms are incremental methods.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different families may solve the same conversion relation while having different intermediate representations.
Polarity exchanges suitable vertex- and facet-enumeration tasks.
boundary_notes: This classification does not impose a uniform complexity bound.
A heuristic that can omit output objects is not a conversion method under this exact definition.

children.title: Double-Description Methods
children.top_down_role: Incremental maintenance of paired constraint and generator descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Double-Description Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert inequalities one at a time, retain feasible generators, create boundary generators from eligible crossing pairs, and remove redundancies while maintaining both representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the current generators by the sign of \(a^Tv-\beta\). Retain generators in \(V^+\cup V^0\), using the convention \(V^+=\{v:a^Tv<\beta\}\). For each eligible adjacent pair \((u,v)\in V^+\times V^-\), insert the intersection point \(w=u+\lambda(v-u)\), where \(\lambda=(\beta-a^Tu)/(a^T(v-u))\). Apply the homogeneous analogue to rays, then delete redundant generators and append \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) to the constraint description. Stop after all inequalities have been inserted.
assumptions_latex: A new inequality \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) is to be inserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces paired constraint and generator descriptions of \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:a^Tx\leq\beta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic incremental double-description update; implementation-specific filtering is abstracted.

notation.meaning: generators satisfying, lying on, or violating the inserted inequality

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports double-description methods.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Double-Description Methods, but the stated point partition does not define the distinct homogeneous sign rule for rays, and the phrase "homogeneous analogue" is insufficient to determine the update for an unbounded polyhedron. Adjacency eligibility, lineality, and redundancy rules also require authoritative support before a mathematically reliable replacement can be made.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), call \((A,R)\) an MW-pair when \(\{x:Ax\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R)\). Let \(A_i\) contain the first \(i\) rows of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The canonical homogeneous cone form is stated; general polyhedra may be homogenized before applying it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A double-description method incrementally maintains an MW-pair \((A_i,R_i)\). On adding the inequality \(a^\top x\le0\), partition columns \(r^j\) of \(R_i\) into \(J^+=\{j:a^\top r^j>0\}\), \(J^0=\{j:a^\top r^j=0\}\), and \(J^-=\{j:a^\top r^j<0\}\). Retain columns indexed by \(J^0\cup J^-\), and for each \((j,k)\in J^-\times J^+\) form \(r^{jk}=(a^\top r^k)r^j-(a^\top r^j)r^k\). After optional removal of nonextreme or duplicate columns, the new matrix \(R_{i+1}\) must satisfy \(\{x:A_{i+1}x\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R_{i+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A double-description method maintains both inequalities and generators of the same cone while adding constraints one at a time. Generators satisfying the new inequality are retained; pairs lying on opposite sides create boundary generators by a linear combination cancelling the new inequality. The updated generator cone must equal the updated constraint cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every stage, \((A_i,R_i)\) is an MW-pair, and finally \(\{x:Ax\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R_m)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(r^{jk}\) spans the ray in \(\operatorname{cone}(r^j,r^k)\cap\{x:a^\top x=0\}\).
special_cases_latex: For one initial half-space, generators may be chosen from \(-a\) and a basis of \(\{x:a^\top x=0\}\).
Homogenization converts vertex-and-ray enumeration for a polyhedron into cone-generator enumeration.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method gives a finite constructive H-to-V conversion.
Without adjacency and extremality filtering, one update may create \(|J^-||J^+|\) candidates.
boundary_notes: Candidate generators need not all be extreme and may require redundancy removal.
Intermediate and final generator counts can be exponential.

notation.meaning: Minkowski–Weyl pair of inequalities and cone generators.
Boundary generator formed from an opposite-sign pair.

children.title: Reverse-Search Methods
children.top_down_role: Enumeration through compact traversal of adjacency structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse-Search Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orient a connected adjacency graph toward a root with a parent rule, then depth-first traverse the induced tree to enumerate every object once.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Output \(r\). At a current vertex \(v\), scan its neighbors in a fixed order and descend to a neighbor \(w\) precisely when \(p(w)=v\); output \(w\) upon descent. When no unvisited child remains, return to \(p(v)\), terminating after the root has no remaining child. Because the arcs \((w,p(w))\) form a rooted spanning tree, the traversal visits every \(v\in V\) exactly once without storing a global visited set.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected adjacency graph.
A root \(r\in V\) and a parent map \(p:V\setminus\{r\}\to V\) are available.
Repeated application of \(p\) reaches \(r\) from every vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every vertex of \(G\) is output exactly once using storage proportional to traversal depth plus local adjacency data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract reverse search on a finite polyhedral adjacency graph.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports reverse search.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The abstract rooted-tree traversal is consistent with reverse search, and algorithm is the correct content kind. The storage conclusion and its polyhedral-enumeration interpretation are nontrivial claims with no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse Search on a Finite Adjacency Graph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph whose vertices are the objects to be enumerated. Assume that an adjacency oracle lists \(N(v)=\{w\in V:\{v,w\}\in E\}\), and fix a root \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact enumeration from local adjacency and a deterministic parent rule; randomized traversal and approximate adjacency are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reverse-search structure on \(G\) is a map \(p:V\setminus\{r\}\to V\) such that \(p(v)\in N(v)\) for every \(v\ne r\), and for every \(v\in V\) there exists \(k\ge 0\) with \(p^{k}(v)=r\), where \(p(r)=r\) by convention. The directed arcs \((v,p(v))\) form an arborescence toward \(r\). Reverse search enumerates \(V\) by traversing the reverse arcs \(v\to w\) satisfying \(p(w)=v\), generating such children by scanning \(N(v)\). Each vertex is reported exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse-search method equips a finite connected adjacency graph with a root and a deterministic parent for every nonroot object. The parent must be adjacent and repeated parent steps must reach the root. The resulting parent arcs form a rooted spanning tree. Traversing these arcs in reverse, while testing adjacent objects to identify children, enumerates every object exactly once without storing the entire visited set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p(v)\in N(v)\quad(v\ne r),\qquad \forall v\in V\ \exists k\ge0:\ p^k(v)=r,\qquad V=\bigsqcup_{v\in V}\{v\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The functional digraph of \(p\), after adjoining \(p(r)=r\), has the unique directed cycle \((r)\); deleting that loop gives a spanning tree of \(G\) oriented toward \(r\).
A vertex \(w\) is a child of \(v\) precisely when \(w\in N(v)\) and \(p(w)=v\).
special_cases_latex: For polyhedral vertex enumeration, \(V\) may be the set of feasible bases or vertices and \(E\) the pivot-adjacency relation.
If \(G\) itself is a tree rooted at \(r\), the unique neighbor closer to \(r\) is the parent map.
immediate_consequences_latex: A depth-first implementation needs only the current root-to-vertex path plus local oracle state, rather than a global visited set.
Termination follows from finiteness of \(V\) and the requirement that every parent chain reaches \(r\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself bound the time needed to compute \(p(v)\), scan \(N(v)\), or test equality of represented objects.
If distinct encodings represent the same object, the graph must first specify whether vertices are objects or encodings; otherwise exact-once enumeration is not defined.

notation.meaning: Neighbors of vertex v in the enumeration graph.
Deterministic parent map directed toward the root.
The k-fold iterate of the parent map.

review_flags: No supplied local source was found that states the reverse-search parent-map definition and exact-once traversal with this scope.
