children.title: Linear Optimization Geometry
children.top_down_role: Optimal faces, recession tests, and normal-cone regions underlying linear programming.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Certificate for Polyhedral Linear Optimality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementary slackness exactly certify linear optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\ne\varnothing\). A feasible point \(x^*\) minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\) if and only if there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and free \(\mu\) such that \(c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+E^{\mathsf T}\mu=0\) and \(\lambda_i(A_i x^*-b_i)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if the displayed multiplier certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: H-representation certificate under the minimization convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Optima Need Not Contain Vertices
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointed polyhedra admit vertex optima, whereas lineality can leave a finite optimal face with no vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a nonempty polyhedron \(P\) is pointed and \(\inf_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\) is finite, its optimal face contains a vertex of \(P\). Pointedness cannot be omitted: for \(P=\{(t,0):t\in\mathbb R\}\) and \(c=(0,1)\), every feasible point is optimal although \(P\) has no vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vertex attainment holds under pointedness and fails without it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the vertex-optimum formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Optimization Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal faces, recession directions, and objective-space normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and consider maximizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\). Its optimal value is finite if and only if \(c^{\mathsf T}d\le0\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{rec}P\). Under this condition the optimizer set \[F(c)=\{x\in P:c^{\mathsf T}x=\max_{z\in P}c^{\mathsf T}z\}\] is a nonempty exposed face. For a nonempty face \(F\) of \(P\), define \[N_P(F)=\{c\in\mathbb R^n:c^{\mathsf T}(z-x)\le0\text{ for every }z\in P\text{ and every }x\in F\}.\] Thus \(c\in N_P(F)\) exactly when every point of \(F\) is a maximizer of \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\). The face normal cones form the normal fan of \(P\), whose support is \((\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective has a finite maximum exactly when it is nonpositive on every recession direction. Its optimizers form an exposed face, and the face normal cones stratify the bounded-objective region, which is the polar of the recession cone.
assumptions_latex: The problem is posed as maximization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x<+\infty\iff c\in(\operatorname{rec}P)^\circ\), and then \(F(c)\) is a nonempty exposed face.

notation.meaning: vectors having nonpositive inner product with every recession direction
normal cone associated with face F

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Faces, Recession Directions, and Normal Cones
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider \(v(c)=\inf_{x\in P}c^Tx\). Define \(N_P(x)=\{y:y^T(z-x)\le0\ \forall z\in P\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact geometry of linear minimization over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear-optimization geometry of \((P,c)\) consists of the recession test, optimal face, and normal-cone region. The objective is bounded below precisely when \(c^Td\ge0\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{rec}P\). When the minimum is finite, the optimal set \(F_c=\{x\in P:c^Tx=v(c)\}\) is a nonempty exposed face of \(P\). For every \(x\in P\), \(x\in F_c\) exactly when \(-c\in N_P(x)\). Consequently, the cost vectors producing a fixed face \(F\) as part of the optimum are described by the negatives of normal cones along \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear optimization over a nonempty polyhedron is governed by three linked objects. Recession directions determine whether the objective can decrease without bound. If the value is finite, all minimizers form a nonempty exposed face. A feasible point is optimal exactly when the negative cost vector belongs to its normal cone, so normal cones partition cost space into regions sharing optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v(c)>-\infty\iff c^Td\ge0\ \forall d\in\operatorname{rec}P,\qquad F_c=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}c^Tx,\qquad x\in F_c\iff-c\in N_P(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F_c=P\cap\{x:c^Tx=v(c)\}\) is the face exposed by the supporting hyperplane with normal \(-c\).
A direction \(d\in\operatorname{rec}P\) with \(c^Td<0\) is an unboundedness direction for the minimization problem.
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is a polytope, \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}\), so every linear objective has a finite attained minimum.
If \(-c\) lies in the relative interior of the normal cone of a face \(F\), then \(F8) is the exact optimal face.
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(F_c\) is a singleton, its point is an optimal vertex.
Costs on boundaries between normal-cone regions can expose a higher-dimensional optimal face.
boundary_notes: For the empty polyhedron, feasibility must be diagnosed before recession and optimal-face assertions are applied.
The statement concerns exact linear objectives and does not include numerical conditioning or a linear-programming algorithm.

notation.meaning: Optimal exposed face for cost c.
Convex-analytic normal cone to P at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Composite Polyhedral Epigraph Formulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting an affine map into a max-affine term's domain and epigraph inequalities yields an exact linear formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(z)=\max_{1\le i\le m}(a_i^{\mathsf T}z+\beta_i)+\delta_D(z)\), where \(D=\{z:Fz\le g\}\), and set \(z=Mx+q\). Then \[\operatorname{epi}(h\circ(M\cdot+q))=\{(x,t):F(Mx+q)\le g,\ t\ge a_i^{\mathsf T}(Mx+q)+\beta_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\}.\] Thus an affine objective plus this composite polyhedral term has a finite linear epigraph formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) has the displayed domain-restricted max-affine representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(h\circ(M\cdot+q))\text{ has the displayed finite linear description}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear epigraph formulation of a domain-restricted max-affine function composed with an affine map.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Value and Weighted L1 Linearization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted absolute-value objectives admit an exact linear formulation with one epigraph variable per residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i\ge0\), affine residuals \(r_i(x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\), and a nonempty feasible set \(X\), \[\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m w_i|r_i(x)|=\inf_{x,t}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m w_it_i:x\in X,\ -t_i\le r_i(x)\le t_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\right\}.\] If \(X\) is polyhedral, the formulation is a linear program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_iw_i|r_i(x)|\text{ is represented exactly by }t_i\ge r_i(x),\ t_i\ge-r_i(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral formulation of weighted absolute-value losses and penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Positive-Part Penalty Threshold
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-part penalty is exact at an optimal-multiplier bound, and strict excess forces every penalized minimizer to be feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[v=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\},\] where \(X\) is convex and \(f,h_i\) are convex. Suppose the constrained problem attains \(v\) and admits an optimal multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\) with zero duality gap. Define \[P_\rho(x):=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\max\{0,h_i(x)\}.\] Every constrained optimizer minimizes \(P_\rho\) over \(X\) when \(\rho\ge\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\). If \(\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\), every minimizer of \(P_\rho\) is feasible and solves the constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda^*\ge0\) is dual optimal and the duality gap is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\ge\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathrm{feas}}f\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}_XP_\rho,\quad \rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{argmin}_XP_\rho\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathrm{feas}}f.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex penalty result locally relevant to positive-part polyhedral modeling.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Nonsmooth Modeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real max-affine representation and its epigraph formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper lower-semicontinuous polyhedral convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) admits a representation \[f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le r}\{a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_i\}+\delta_D(x),\] where \(D\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(\delta_D\) is its indicator. Conversely, every function of this form is proper lower-semicontinuous polyhedral convex. Minimizing \(f\) is equivalent to the linear epigraph model \[\min_{x,t}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in D,
\ t\ge a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_i\ \text{for all }i.\] Thus finite max-affine, minimax, and polyhedral exact-penalty terms have linear extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closed proper polyhedral convex function is max-affine on a polyhedral domain, and its minimization has a linear epigraph formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\max_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}\cdot+\beta_i)+\delta_D\), with a linear epigraph formulation.

notation.meaning: zero on D and positive infinity outside D

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Cx\le d\}\) be a polyhedron and let \((a_i,b_i)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,8,\ldots,m\). Let \(\delta_P\) denote the indicator of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex nonsmooth models whose objective epigraph is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A canonical polyhedral nonsmooth model is the extended-real function \(f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}(a_i^Tx+b_i)+\delta_P(x)\). Its epigraph is \(\{(x,t):Cx\le d,8 a_i^Tx+b_i\le t\ (i=1,8\ldots,m)\}\), hence a polyhedron. Minimizing \(f\) is equivalently the linear epigraph problem \(\min\{t:Cx\le d,8 a_i^Tx+b_i\le t\ \forall i\}\). At \(x\in P\), the active affine-piece set is \(I(x)=\{i:a_i^Tx+b_i=8\max_j(a_j^Tx+b_j)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical polyhedral nonsmooth model is a finite maximum of affine functions restricted to a polyhedron by an extended-value indicator. Its epigraph has one linear inequality for each affine piece plus the constraints describing the domain. Therefore its minimization can be written as a linear epigraph problem. Nonsmoothness occurs where two or more affine pieces are simultaneously active or where the polyhedral domain contributes a normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}(a_i^Tx+b_i)+\delta_P(x),\qquad \operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):Cx\le d,8 a_i^Tx+b_i\le t\ \forall i\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The finite-valued part \(x\mapsto\max_i(a_i^Tx+b_i)\) is a convex piecewise-affine function.
The minimax problem \(\min_{x\in P}\max_i(a_i^Tx+b_i)\) is the stated epigraph linear program.
special_cases_latex: The absolute value \(|a^Tx+b|\) is the maximum of the two affine functions \(a^Tx+b\) and \(-a^Tx-b\).
A weighted \(\ell_1\) penalty is polyhedral because it is a finite sum, equivalently a finite maximum after expansion, of affine pieces.
immediate_consequences_latex: All sublevel sets \(\{x:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) are polyhedra.
The active-piece set supplies the local combinatorial data used by bundle, cutting-plane, and active-set interfaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parametric Polyhedral Value and Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(u\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) and define \(P(u)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b+Bu\}\). Let \(c(u)=c_0+Cu\), \(v(u)=\inf_{x\in P(u)}c(u)^Tx\), and \(S(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P(u)}c(u)^Tx\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional parametric linear optimization with affine data dependence; global regularity is not asserted without additional feasibility and nondegeneracy hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The parametric sensitivity interface is the pair \((v,S)\) together with its feasibility domain \(\mathcal D=\{u:P(u)\ne\varnothing\}\), optimal active-set correspondence, and critical-region decomposition. For \(x\in S(u)\), define \(I(x,u)=\{i:A_ix=b_i+B_i u\}\). A critical region associated with an optimal active pattern \(J\) is a maximal connected polyhedral subset \(R_J\subseteq\mathcal D\) on which there exists an optimal selection having the same declared active or basis pattern \(J\). A transition occurs at a parameter belonging to the boundaries of two or more such regions or where feasibility, boundedness, or attainment status changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric sensitivity interface records the optimal value, minimizer set, feasible parameter domain, and optimal active patterns of a polyhedral optimization family. A critical region is a maximal connected polyhedral parameter set on which a selected optimal basis or active pattern remains unchanged. Region boundaries mark active-set transitions or changes in feasibility, boundedness, or attainment. This definition does not assume that every parameter has a unique optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal D=\{u:P(u)\ne\varnothing\},\qquad v(u)=\inf_{x\in P(u)}c(u)^Tx,8\qquad S(u)=\{x\in P(u):c(u)^Tx=v(u)\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The value function is the marginal function obtained by partially minimizing the jointly parameterized objective plus the indicator of the polyhedral graph \(\{(u,x):Ax-Bu\le b\}\).
When an optimal basis is fixed and nonsingular, the associated primal and dual candidates are affine functions of the parameter, and its validity inequalities describe a polyhedral region.
special_cases_latex: Right-hand-side sensitivity has \(C=0\) and varies only \(b+Bu\).
Objective sensitivity has \(B=0\) and varies only \(c_0+Cu\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Set-valued \(S\) is required at degenerate parameters where several optimal faces or bases coexist.
Critical-region boundaries identify candidate locations for changes in directional derivatives of the value function.
boundary_notes: Piecewise-affineness and finiteness of a global critical-region partition require hypotheses not included in the bare interface definition.
Nonlinear parameter dependence or integer variables can destroy the stated polyhedral critical-region structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Polyhedral Value and Solution Maps
All-or-None Lower Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The common recession cone makes all feasible instances unbounded below or none of them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(D\ne\varnothing\). If some \(d\) satisfies \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then \(v(p)=-\infty\) for every \(p\in D\). If no such direction exists, every nonempty fiber has a finite attained minimum. Thus lower unboundedness cannot occur for only some feasible parameters in this fixed-\(A,c\) model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direction \(d\) with \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) exists if and only if every feasible parameter has value \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower-unboundedness alternative for fixed \(A\) and \(c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Parameter Domain and Common Recession Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible parameters form a polyhedron, and all nonempty fibers share one recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(p)=\{x:Ax\le b+Bp\}\), the feasible parameter domain \(D:=\{p:F(p)\ne\varnothing\}\) is the projection of \(\{(p,x):Ax-Bp\le b\}\), hence is a polyhedron. For every \(p\in D\), \(\operatorname{rec}F(p)=\{d:Ad\le0\}\), independently of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is polyhedral and \(\operatorname{rec}F(p)=\{d:Ad\le0\}\) for every \(p\in D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural facts for the fixed-matrix right-hand-side model.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Polyhedral Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric polyhedral model is a linear program whose polyhedral feasible set depends affinely on a parameter, together with its value and minimizer mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
F(p):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b+Bp\},\qquad v(p):=\inf_{x\in F(p)}c^{\mathsf T}x,
\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). The associated solution map is
\[
S(p):=\{x\in F(p):c^{\mathsf T}x=v(p)\}
\]
when \(v(p)\in\mathbb R\), and \(S(p):=\varnothing\) otherwise. This quadruple \((F,v,S,p)\) is a parametric polyhedral model because the joint feasible set \(\{(p,x):Ax-Bp\le b\}\) is a polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: The parameter and decision spaces are finite-dimensional: \(p\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The matrices and vectors \(A,B,b,c\) are fixed and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functions \(v\) and \(S\) define the value and solution maps of a parametric polyhedral optimization model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional right-hand-side-parametric linear programs with extended-real value convention.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Polyhedral Functions p. 76

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower-unboundedness boundary for the fixed objective and constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\ne\varnothing\). If there exists \(d\) with \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then \(v(p)=-\infty\) for every \(p\in D\). If no such direction exists, every feasible fiber has a finite attained minimum. Thus, in this fixed-\(A,c\) right-hand-side model, lower unboundedness cannot occur for only some feasible parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every fiber has the same recession cone, either all feasible parameter instances are unbounded below or none are.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(d\) with \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) is equivalent to \(v(p)=-\infty\) for all \(p\in D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Independent Unboundedness Alternative
Dual Max-Affine Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The value is an attained supremum of affine parameter functions indexed by a parameter-independent dual polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y:=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:y\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=-c\}\). If the value function is proper, then \(Y\ne\varnothing\) and, in the extended-real sense, \[v(p)=\sup_{y\in Y}-(b+Bp)^{\mathsf T}y.\] For every \(p\in\operatorname{dom}v\), the supremum is finite and attained.
assumptions_latex: The primal value function is proper.
\(F(p)=\{x:Ax\le b+Bp\}\) and the objective is \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(p)=\sup_{y\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=-c}-(b+Bp)^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation for the fixed right-hand-side-parametric linear program.

knowledge_statements.title: Properness Boundary for the Value Function
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Properness requires a feasible parameter and excludes a common negative-cost recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the fixed-\(A,c\) model, \(v(p)=+\infty\) exactly when \(F(p)=\varnothing\). If some \(d\) satisfies \(Ad\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then \(v(p)=-\infty\) for every feasible \(p\). Hence \(v\) is proper exactly when the feasible parameter domain is nonempty and no such direction exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is proper if and only if \(\{p:F(p)\ne\varnothing\}\ne\varnothing\) and no \(d\) satisfies \(Ad\le0\), \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of infeasibility and lower unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradients as Shadow-Price Images
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value subgradients are images of optimal dual multipliers; at interior parameters, a unique image characterizes differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\operatorname{dom}v\), define \(Y^*(p):=\arg\max_{y\in Y}-(b+Bp)^{\mathsf T}y\). Then \[\partial v(p)=\{-B^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y^*(p)\}.\] In particular, when \(p\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}v)\), \(v\) is differentiable at \(p\) exactly when this image is a singleton, and its sole element is \(\nabla v(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial v(p)=-B^{\mathsf T}Y^*(p)\), with the stated interior differentiability criterion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order value sensitivity, including domain-boundary normals through the dual optimal set.

notation.meaning: Optimal dual multiplier set at parameter \(p\)

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Value Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper value function obtained by partially minimizing a linear objective over affine polyhedral constraints is closed, convex, polyhedral, and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
v(p):=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+Bp\}.
\]
If \(v(p)>-\infty\) for every \(p\) and \(\operatorname{dom}v:=\{p:v(p)<+\infty\}\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\operatorname{epi}v=\{(p,t):\exists x,\ Ax\le b+Bp,\ c^{\mathsf T}x\le t\}
\]
is a polyhedron. Consequently, \(v\) is a proper closed convex polyhedral function. In particular, \(\operatorname{dom}v\) admits a finite polyhedral subdivision such that the restriction of \(v\) to every cell is affine.
assumptions_latex: The parametric model is the finite-dimensional model of the preceding record.
The value never equals \(-\infty\), and its effective domain is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value function \(v\) is proper, closed, convex, and polyhedral, hence piecewise affine on its polyhedral domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real value function for a right-hand-side-parametric linear program.

notation.meaning: Optimal value as a function of the parameter
Effective domain of the value function

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Sensitivity Under a Stable Nondegenerate Basis
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular active basis with strictly positive multipliers makes the optimizer unique and affine throughout its critical region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+Bp\}\). Let \(I\) contain \(n\) indices, let \(A_I\) be nonsingular, and suppose \(\lambda_I:=-(A_I^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c>0\). On \[R_I:=\{p:A A_I^{-1}(b_I+B_Ip)\le b+Bp\},\] one has \[S(p)=\{x_I(p)\},\qquad x_I(p):=A_I^{-1}(b_I+B_Ip).\] Hence \(S\) is affine and Lipschitz on \(R_I\), with derivative \(A_I^{-1}B_I\) along directions remaining in that region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(p)=\{A_I^{-1}(b_I+B_Ip)\}\quad(p\in R_I).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local single-valued sensitivity for a right-hand-side-parametric linear program under a fixed nonsingular active basis with strictly positive multipliers.

notation.meaning: Parameter region on which the basis solution is feasible

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Continuous Selection at an Optimal-Face Transition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an optimal-face transition, a polyhedral solution multifunction may become multivalued and admit no continuous local selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[S(p):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le x\le1}px,\] one has \[S(p)=\begin{cases}\{1\},&p<0,\\ [0,1],&p=0,\\ \{0\},&p>0.\end{cases}\] Its graph is a finite union of polyhedra, but \(S(0)\) is multivalued and no continuous single-valued selection exists on a neighborhood of \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is a finite union of polyhedra, but no continuous selection exists near }0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that a finite-union polyhedral graph does not imply local single-valuedness or a continuous selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Map Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimizer map of a parametric linear program has a graph assembled from finitely many polyhedra, one for each affine regime of the value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a finite polyhedral subdivision \(\{C_j\}_{j=1}^N\) satisfies \(v(p)=\alpha_j^{\mathsf T}p+\beta_j\) on \(C_j\). Then
\[
\operatorname{gph}S\cap(C_j\times\mathbb R^n)
=\{(p,x):p\in C_j,\ Ax\le b+Bp,\ c^{\mathsf T}x=\alpha_j^{\mathsf T}p+\beta_j\}
\]
is a polyhedron for every \(j\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{gph}S=\bigcup_{j=1}^N\bigl(\operatorname{gph}S\cap(C_j\times\mathbb R^n)\bigr)
\]
is a finite union of polyhedra. Thus solution sensitivity is governed by finitely many polyhedral regimes, although \(S(p)\) may be empty, multivalued, or unbounded.
assumptions_latex: The value function \(v\) is finite on the parameter region under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution map \(S\) has a graph that is a finite union of polyhedra and is polyhedral on every value-function cell.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-polyhedral sensitivity representation, without asserting single-valuedness or differentiability.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral cells on which the value is affine

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Single-Valued Continuity at an Optimal-Face Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing that a piecewise-polyhedral graph does not imply a continuous optimizer selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[S(p):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le x\le1}px,\] one has \[S(p)=\begin{cases}\{1\},&p<0,\\[0,1],&p=0,\\\{0\},&p>0.\end{cases}\] Thus \(\operatorname{gph}S\) is a finite union of polyhedra, but \(S\) is multivalued at \(0\), has no continuous single-valued selection on any neighborhood of \(0\), and is not differentiable there as a single-valued map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a change of optimal face, a polyhedral solution multifunction can become multivalued and admit no continuous local selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is piecewise polyhedral, but no continuous selection exists near }p=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Single-Valued Continuity at an Optimal-Face Transition
Locally Stable Active Basis
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular, strictly feasible and strictly complementary optimal basis persists locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the unique optimizer \(x_0\) at \(p_0\) has exactly \(n\) active inequalities indexed by \(I\), the square matrix \(A_I\) is nonsingular, every inactive slack is strictly positive, and the unique multipliers associated with \(I\) are strictly positive. Then a neighborhood of \(p_0\) exists on which the same basis is primal and dual feasible, the optimizer is unique and affine in \(p\), and its exact active set is \(I\). The boundary is reached when basis nonsingularity, an inactive strict slack, or a positive basic multiplier is lost.
assumptions_latex: Exactly \(n\) constraints are active, \(A_I\) is nonsingular, inactive slacks are positive, and basic multipliers are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimizer is locally unique and affine, with exact active set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient hypotheses for a genuine constant-active-set critical region.

notation.meaning: Stable optimal basis and exact active set

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Permits Full-Dimensional Active-Set Overlap
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonunique optimizers can realize multiple exact active sets on the same open parameter region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(p\in\mathbb R\), consider \(\min 0\) subject to \(0\le x\le1\), with parameter-independent constraints. Every feasible point is optimal. The optimizers \(x=0\), \(x=1\), and \(x=1/2\) realize three different exact active sets throughout the same full-dimensional parameter region \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact realizable active-set regions need not be disjoint or meet only on lower-dimensional boundaries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact-active-set partitioning without uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Included-Active-Set Regions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameters admitting an optimizer with a prescribed included active set form polyhedral regions that may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and a polyhedral cell \(C\) on which the finite value function is affine, \(v(p)=a^{\mathsf T}p+\gamma\). The pairs \((p,x)\) satisfying \(p\in C\), \(Ax\le b+Bp\), \(c^{\mathsf T}x=a^{\mathsf T}p+\gamma\), and \(A_i x=b_i+B_i p\) for every \(i\in I\) form a polyhedron. Its parameter projection is therefore polyhedral and consists of parameters admitting an optimizer at which every constraint in \(I\) is active. Regions for different \(I\) may overlap and need not form a partition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a polyhedral cell on which \(v\) is finite and affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The included-active-set realizability region is polyhedral, without any disjointness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General set-valued active-set geometry without uniqueness assumptions.

assumptions_latex: The parameter region lies in \(\operatorname{dom}v\), and the optimum is attained there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each active-set regime has polyhedral closure, and active sets can change only on the boundaries of finitely many such regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in S(p)\), define
\[
I(p,x):=\{i:A_i x=b_i+B_i p\}.
\]
For each \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let
\[
R_I:=\{p:\exists x\in S(p),\ A_i x=b_i+B_i p\ (i\in I),\ A_i x<b_i+B_i p\ (i\notin I)\}.
\]
After intersecting with each affine cell of \(v\), the set \(R_I\) is the projection of a relatively open polyhedron; its closure is polyhedral. There are finitely many such closures, and an exact active set is locally constant away from their relative boundaries. Consequently, every active-set transition occurs on a finite union of lower-dimensional polyhedral faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameters split into finitely many polyhedral regimes with fixed realizable active sets; changes occur only on regime boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supplied source locator does not reliably support the exact-active-set projection claim, and the mathematical statement is overstated. Because R_I records active sets realizable by some optimizer, several distinct R_I may overlap on full-dimensional parameter regions when optimal solutions are nonunique or degenerate. Thus an exact active set need not be locally constant away from regime boundaries, and transitions need not be confined to lower-dimensional faces without additional uniqueness or nondegeneracy hypotheses. A source and corrected hypotheses are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient hypotheses for genuine locally constant active-set regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that at \(p_0\) the parametric linear program has a unique optimal solution \(x_0\), and there is an optimal basis \(I\) whose active constraint matrix has full rank, whose inactive slacks are strictly positive, and whose associated dual multipliers on the basis are strictly positive. Then there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(p_0\) on which the same basis remains primal and dual feasible, the optimizer is unique and affine in \(p\), and its active set is exactly \(I\). Loss of one of the strict inequalities or basis nonsingularity marks the boundary of this stability region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate strictly complementary optimal basis persists locally, giving a unique affine optimizer with constant active set.
assumptions_latex: An optimal basis is nonsingular, has positive inactive slacks, and has positive basic dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis and exact active set are locally constant and the optimizer depends affinely on the parameter.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General set-valued active-set geometry without uniqueness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the parametric model \(F(p)=\{x:Ax\le b+Bp\}\), fix \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and a polyhedral cell \(C\) on which the finite value function is affine, \(v(p)=a^{\mathsf T}p+\gamma\). The set of pairs \((p,x)\) satisfying \(p\in C\), \(Ax\le b+Bp\), \(c^{\mathsf T}x=a^{\mathsf T}p+\gamma\), and \(A_i x=b_i+B_i p\) for \(i\in I\) is a polyhedron. Its projection is therefore a polyhedral parameter region on which some optimizer has every constraint in \(I\) active. These finitely many regions may overlap and need not form a partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parameters admitting an optimizer with a prescribed included active set form polyhedral regions, but different regions can overlap.
assumptions_latex: The value is finite and affine on the polyhedral cell \(C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Robust Feasibility and Discrete Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be a nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set of data realizations \(\xi\), with constraint system \(A(8\xi)x\le b(8\xi)\). Let \(D=\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}\) encode designated integer variables, and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a deterministic polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust linear decisions and polyhedral relaxations of mixed-integer feasible sets; adjustable decisions and nonpolyhedral uncertainty are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The robust feasible set is \(R=\{x\in X:A(8\xi)x\le b(8\xi)\ \forall\xi\in\mathcal U\}\). The robust-discrete feasible set is \(S=R\cap D\). A polyhedral relaxation is any polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(S\subseteq P\); it is ideal when \(P=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S\). The modeling boundary consists of the two operations that change semantics: universal quantification over \(\mathcal U\) creates robust feasibility, whereas replacing \(S\) by a containing polyhedron \(P\) removes or relaxes integrality. Neither operation may be omitted when interpreting the resulting optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the robust-discrete boundary, uncertainty and integrality are separate mathematical operations. Static robust feasibility requires one fixed decision to satisfy every constraint realization in the uncertainty set. Discrete feasibility then intersects that robust set with the required integer lattice. A polyhedral relaxation contains the discrete feasible set, and it is ideal when it equals the closed convex hull. Solving the relaxation does not by itself solve the discrete problem unless an integral optimum is recovered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R=X\cap\bigcap_{\xi\in\mathcal U}\{x:A(8\xi)x\le b(8\xi)\},\qquad S=R\cap(8\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}),\qquad S\subseteq P.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For rowwise uncertainty, robust feasibility is equivalent to \(\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U}(a_i(8\xi)^Tx-b_i(8\xi))\le0\) for every constraint row \(i\).
The natural continuous relaxation is obtained by replacing \(\mathbb Z^p\) by \(\mathbb R^p\) while retaining the robust constraints.
special_cases_latex: With \(p=0\), the model is a continuous static robust linear problem.
With singleton \(\mathcal U\), the robust quantifier reduces to an ordinary mixed-integer linear feasible set.
For binary variables, \(D=\{0,1\}^p\times\mathbb R^{n-p}\) after adding the corresponding bounds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every feasible point of \(S\) is feasible for any relaxation \(P\), but the converse need not hold.
For minimization, optimizing over a containing relaxation gives a lower bound on the discrete robust optimum whenever both values are well-defined.
boundary_notes: Adjustable robust optimization permits decisions depending on revealed uncertainty and is not represented by the static intersection defining \(R\).
An ideal formulation concerns convex-hull equality; it does not guarantee that its explicit inequality description is small.

notation.meaning: Robust feasible set with integrality restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Criterion for Finite Worst-Case Values
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case linear value is finite exactly when its direction is nonpositive on every recession direction of the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\ne\varnothing\), with recession cone \(U^\infty=\{d:Fd\le0\}\). Then \[\sigma_U(y)<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \text{for every }d\in U^\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y\in(U^\infty)^\circ.\] If some \(d\in U^\infty\) satisfies \(y^{\mathsf T}d>0\), then \(\sigma_U(y)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}\sigma_U=(U^\infty)^\circ.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finiteness domain of the support function of a nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the uncertainty set
Polar cone of the recession cone

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Representation of Bounded Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded polyhedral uncertainty set is the convex hull of finitely many vertices, and every linear worst case occurs at one of them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set \(U\) is bounded, then it has finitely many vertices \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\) and \[U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\},\qquad \sigma_U(y)=\max_{1\le k\le N}y^{\mathsf T}v^k.\] Thus every worst-case linear perturbation over \(U\) is attained at a vertex.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is nonempty, polyhedral, and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\},\qquad\sigma_U(y)=\max_ky^{\mathsf T}v^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario representation of a polytope and its support function.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral uncertainty set is a nonempty solution set of finitely many linear inequalities; worst-case linear perturbations are its support-function values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polyhedral uncertainty set is a nonempty set
\[
U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^r:Fu\le g\},
\]
where \(F\in\mathbb R^{s\times r}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^s\). Its support function is
\[
\sigma_U(y):=\sup_{u\in U}y^{\mathsf T}u\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}.
\]
Thus evaluating worst-case affine dependence on \(u\) is a linear program. The set is a polytope precisely when it is bounded; boundedness guarantees that \(\sigma_U(y)\) is finite for every \(y\in\mathbb R^r\).
assumptions_latex: The uncertain vector belongs to a finite-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(U\) is polyhedral, and its support function is the optimal value of a linear program.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inequality representation, allowing bounded or unbounded uncertainty sets.

notation.meaning: Support function of the uncertainty set
Direction in which support is evaluated

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Support Functions and Polar Sets p. 133

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary of the Linear Robust-Counterpart Template
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-dependent uncertainty or nonlinear dependence on the uncertain vector can destroy the standard finite linear counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard linear counterpart obtained by dualizing \(\sup_{u\in U}(P^{\mathsf T}x)^{\mathsf T}u\) uses a fixed nonempty polyhedral set \(U\) and affine dependence on \(u\). If the inequalities defining \(U\) depend on \(x\), dualization can introduce products of decision variables and dual multipliers. If the uncertain expression is nonlinear in \(u\), its worst-case evaluation is not generally a linear program. Thus polyhedrality of each fixed uncertainty fiber alone does not guarantee a linear robust counterpart.
assumptions_latex: The comparison is with the fixed-set, affine-uncertainty LP-dualization template.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Polyhedral uncertainty fibers alone do not guarantee a linear robust counterpart.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which fixed-set affine LP dualization no longer guarantees a finite linear counterpart.

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier that may couple bilinearly with x

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Enumerated Robust Counterpart
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For polytopal uncertainty given by its vertices, robust affine feasibility is exactly feasibility at every vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\). Then \[(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\quad\text{for every }u\in U\] is equivalent to \[(a_0+Pv^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\qquad(k=1,\ldots,N).\] This formulation requires no multiplier variables, although its number of inequalities equals the number of listed vertices.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain inequality depends affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall u\in U,\ (a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\iff\forall k,\ (a_0+Pv^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario formulation for a robust affine inequality over a polytope.

notation.meaning: Vertex scenario of the uncertainty polytope

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\) is nonempty.
For the fixed decision \(x\), the support value \(\sigma_U(P^{\mathsf T}x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semi-infinite robust constraint is equivalent to the existence of a finite-dimensional nonnegative dual certificate \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraintwise robust counterpart obtained from finite-dimensional linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R\). The robust inequality
\[
(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\qquad\text{for every }u\in U
\]
is equivalent to
\[
a_0^{\mathsf T}x+\sigma_U(P^{\mathsf T}x)\le b.
\]
If \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\) is nonempty and the support value is finite, linear-programming strong duality gives the finite counterpart
\[
\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^s:\qquad F^{\mathsf T}\lambda=P^{\mathsf T}x,
\qquad g^{\mathsf T}\lambda+a_0^{\mathsf T}x\le b.
\]
Thus a robust affine inequality over polyhedral uncertainty is represented by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the worst-case linear perturbation converts a robust affine constraint over a nonempty polyhedron into finitely many linear constraints with nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Polyhedral Counterparts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust-counterpart formula is mathematically plausible and the duality content kind fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied. Authoritative, inspectable locators are required for both the linear-programming strong-duality step and the robust polyhedral counterpart before the exact assumptions and equivalence can be accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonic Tightening of Polyhedral Relaxations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening a relaxation with valid inequalities improves every minimization bound, but equality for one objective does not establish ideality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq Q_2\subseteq Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(Q_1,Q_2\) are polyhedra. For every linear minimization objective, \[\inf_{x\in Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in X}c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Thus adding inequalities valid for \(X\) cannot weaken the relaxation bound. Equality with the discrete optimum for one objective does not imply \(Q_2=\operatorname{conv}X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_Xc^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of linear-objective bounds under addition of valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Polyhedral Relaxations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted polyhedron containing a lift of every discrete feasible point projects to a valid polyhedral relaxation with the same linear-objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[R:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+q}:Gx+Hy\le h\}\] be a polyhedron such that every \(x\in X\) has a lift \(y\) with \((x,y)\in R\). Then \[Q:=\operatorname{proj}_xR=\{x:\exists y,\ Gx+Hy\le h\}\] is a polyhedral relaxation of \(X\), and \[\inf_{(x,y)\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x.\]
assumptions_latex: For every \(x\in X\), some \(y\) satisfies \((x,y)\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q=\operatorname{proj}_xR,\qquad \inf_Rc^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_Qc^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted polyhedral formulations whose projection supplies a relaxation in the original variables.

assumptions_latex: The mixed-discrete feasible set \(X\) is nonempty.
The relaxation \(Q\) is a polyhedron satisfying \(\operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization over \(Q\) gives a valid linear-programming bound, and the relaxation is ideal exactly when \(Q=\operatorname{conv}X\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the discrete feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer relaxations of finite-dimensional mixed-integer feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
X:=\{x\in\mathbb Z^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}:Ax\le b\}.
\]
A polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedral relaxation of \(X\) when
\[
\operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q.
\]
For every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), this inclusion yields the minimization bound
\[
\inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x\le \inf_{x\in X}c^{\mathsf T}x,
\]
with the usual extended-real conventions. The relaxation is called ideal when \(Q=\operatorname{conv}X\); then every linear objective has the same infimum over \(Q\) and \(X\), whenever either value is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral relaxation contains the convex hull of a mixed-discrete feasible set and supplies valid linear-programming bounds; it is ideal when it equals that hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Polyhedral Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and minimization bound are standard and internally consistent, and definition is an appropriate content kind for this leaf. However, the record has no source reference; an inspectable integer-programming or polyhedral-relaxation definition locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive and Multiplicative Integrality Gaps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additive gap is the relaxation-value difference; the usual maximization ratio requires positive finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem with discrete optimum \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\) and relaxation optimum \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)\ge z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\), define \[\Delta(c):=z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)-z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c).\] When \(0<z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\le z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)<+\infty\), define \[\Gamma(c):=\frac{z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)}{z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)}.\] This ratio convention is not meaningful when the integer optimum is zero, negative, or infinite.
assumptions_latex: The multiplicative definition additionally requires \(0<z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\le z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta(c)\ge0,\qquad \Gamma(c)\ge1\text{ whenever defined}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-dependent gap conventions for a maximization relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Boundary for Additive Gaps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero additive gap can be made arbitrarily large by rescaling the objective, so additive bounds require normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an objective \(c\) has \(0<\Delta(c)<+\infty\), then for every \(\alpha>0\), \[\Delta(\alpha c)=\alpha\Delta(c).\] Hence a scale-free uniform additive-gap bound cannot hold over an objective class closed under arbitrary positive scaling unless every objective in the class has zero gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta(\alpha c)=\alpha\Delta(c).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive gaps are not invariant under positive rescaling of the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Characterization of an Ideal Relaxation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the discrete convex hull is closed, a closed convex relaxation is ideal exactly when every linear objective has zero gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:=\operatorname{conv}X\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(Q\) be a nonempty closed convex set with \(C\subseteq Q\). Then \[Q=C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in C}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n.\] Thus every strict closed convex outer enlargement is exposed by at least one linear objective with a strict extended-real value gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=C\iff\forall c\in\mathbb R^n,\ \inf_Qc^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_Cc^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-objectives characterization when the discrete convex hull is closed.

notation.meaning: Closed convex hull of the discrete feasible set

assumptions_latex: The comparison uses maximization with nonnegative finite optimal values.
For each \(n\ge2\), the relaxation is the edge relaxation of the stable-set problem on \(K_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplicative integrality gap equals \(n/2\), so polyhedral relaxation alone gives no dimension-independent gap bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded multiplicative gap for the elementary edge relaxation of maximum stable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge2\), consider
\[
z_{\mathrm{IP}}:=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i:x_i\in\{0,1\},\ x_i+x_j\le1\ \text{for }i\ne j\right\}
\]
and its polyhedral relaxation
\[
z_{\mathrm{LP}}:=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i:0\le x_i\le1,\ x_i+x_j\le1\ \text{for }i\ne j\right\}.
\]
Because every stable set of \(K_n\) has at most one vertex, \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=1\). The point \(x_i=1/2\) is relaxation-feasible, and summing the pairwise inequalities shows \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}=n/2\). Hence
\[
\frac{z_{\mathrm{LP}}}{z_{\mathrm{IP}}}=\frac n2\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
No uniform multiplicative integrality-gap bound follows merely from polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The edge relaxation for maximum stable set on a complete graph has ratio n/2, proving that polyhedral relaxations can have unbounded integrality gaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind correctly matches the terminal container, and the stated K_n gap is mathematically standard. Nevertheless, no source is supplied, and the statement includes derivational proof text beginning with the justification of the two optimum values. An authoritative stable-set relaxation locator is required, after which the record should be restated without proof text.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative inequality multiplier and equality multiplier produces a dual lower bound on the primal value. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual construction architecture for a convex minimization problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\) be the primal space and let the primal value be \(p^\star=\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x)\), where \(\Phi:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex. A construction may additionally use a finite-dimensional perturbation space \(U\), a multiplier space \(U^*\), a cone \(K\), or an explicit constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex minimization. The definition organizes the standard Lagrangian, perturbation-conjugate, geometric, and conic routes; it does not assert strong duality or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual construction architecture is a rule that augments the primal data by a family of lower bounds \(d:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfying \(d(y)\le p^\star\) for every dual-feasible \(y\in Y_{\mathrm f}\), and defines the associated dual problem as \(\sup_{y\in Y_{\mathrm f}}d(y)\). Canonical realizations are: (i) the multiplier construction \(d(\lambda,\nu)=\inf_x L(x,\lambda,\nu)\); (ii) the perturbation-conjugate construction, for \(p(u)=\inf_xF(u,x)\), given by \(d(u^*)=\inf_u\{p(u)+\langle u^*,u\rangle\}=-p^*(-u^*)\); (iii) separation of a convex epigraph or attainable set by supporting affine functionals; and (iv) conic polarity, in which multipliers belong to the dual cone \(K^*\). The output of the architecture is the pair \((Y_{\mathrm f},d)\), and its dual value is \(d^\star=\sup_{y\in Y_{\mathrm f}}d(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual construction architecture assigns to a convex primal problem a dual-feasible parameter set and a parameterized family of lower bounds on the primal value. Maximizing those bounds defines the dual problem. Standard architectures obtain the bounds from a Lagrangian, from the conjugate of a perturbation value function, from separating affine functionals, or from polar/dual cones. The definition itself guarantees only that every dual-feasible parameter gives a lower bound; equality with the primal value and attainment require separate hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\Phi)=(Y_{\mathrm f},d),\qquad d(y)\le p^\star\ \forall y\in Y_{\mathrm f},\qquad d^\star:=\sup_{y\in Y_{\mathrm f}}d(y)\le p^\star.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a perturbation function \(p\), the multiplier and conjugate descriptions agree whenever \(d(u^*)=\inf_u\{p(u)+\langle u^*,u\rangle\}=-p^*(-u^*)\).
A geometric construction records the same lower bound as an affine minorant \(u\mapsto d(y)-\langle y,u\rangle\) of the perturbation value function.
special_cases_latex: For \(f_i(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\), take \(Y_{\mathrm f}=\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\) and \(d=g\), the Lagrange dual function.
For a cone constraint \(G(x)\in-K\), take its multiplier in \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every architecture satisfying the lower-bound condition obeys weak duality \(d^\star\le p^\star\).
Different parameterizations can describe the same architecture when they induce the same feasible lower-bound family.
boundary_notes: The listed routes are construction templates, not mutually exclusive classes; a conic dual is also a Lagrangian and perturbational dual.
No constraint qualification, zero duality gap, or existence of an optimal multiplier is included in this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian duality for inequality and equality constrained problems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and consider \(p^\star=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in D,\ f_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,p)\}\), where the displayed functions are real-valued on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional minimization, with no convexity required for the construction. Convexity and constraint qualifications enter only in later strong-duality results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Lagrangian is \(L:D	imes\mathbb R^m	imes\mathbb R^p	o\mathbb R\), \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p
u_jh_j(x)\). Its dual function is \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,\lambda,
u)\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\). Lagrangian duality associates with the primal problem the maximization \(d^\star=\sup\{g(\lambda,
u):\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ 
u\in\mathbb R^p\}\). The inequality multipliers are nonnegative and the equality multipliers are unrestricted. For every primal-feasible \(x\) and every \(\lambda\ge0\), \(L(x,\lambda,
u)\le f_0(x)\), so each dual-feasible multiplier gives the lower bound \(g(\lambda,
u)\le p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian duality adds each inequality constraint to the objective with a nonnegative multiplier and each equality constraint with an unrestricted multiplier. Minimizing this Lagrangian over the primal domain gives the dual function. Maximizing the dual function over admissible multipliers gives the Lagrange dual problem. This construction applies even to a nonconvex primal problem and always yields lower bounds for a minimization problem, although equality of primal and dual values is not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)+
u^Th(x),\quad g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,\lambda,
u),\quad d^\star=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}g(\lambda,
u)\le p^\star.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The dual objective is the best lower bound obtained from the affine penalty family \(x\mapsto f_0(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)+\nu^Th(x)\).
Using the extended-value convention, the multiplier sign restriction can be incorporated through \(g(\lambda,\nu)=-\infty\) for \(\lambda\notin\mathbb R_+^m\).
special_cases_latex: With no equality constraints, \(g(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in D}\{f_0(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)\}\) for \(\lambda\ge0\).
With equality constraints only, every multiplier \(\nu\in\mathbb R^p\) is admissible.
immediate_consequences_latex: The function \(g\) is concave because it is a pointwise infimum of affine functions of \((\lambda,\nu)\).
Weak duality \(d^\star\le p^\star\) holds independently of primal convexity.
boundary_notes: The infimum defining \(g\) need not be attained and may equal \(-\infty\).
Strong duality and existence of optimal multipliers require additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-indicator and multiplier representations of a primal objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):D\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(h:D\to\mathbb R^p\). Write \(\delta_C(z)=0\) for \(z\in C\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary finite-dimensional inequality and equality constraints. The representation is pointwise in the primal variable and uses extended-real indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The constrained primal objective has the hard-constraint representation \(\Phi(x)=f_0(x)+\delta_{\mathbb R_-^m}(f(x))+\delta_{\{0\}}(h(x))\) for \(x\in D\). Its Lagrangian representation is the affine multiplier family \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)+
u^Th(x)\), indexed by \((\lambda,
u)\in\mathbb R_+^m	imes\mathbb R^p\). These representations satisfy the pointwise identity \(\Phi(x)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u\in\mathbb R^p}L(x,\lambda,
u)\): at a feasible \(x\), the supremum equals \(f_0(x)\), while violation of any displayed constraint makes it \(+\infty\). The associated lower-envelope representation in multiplier space is \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,\lambda,
u)\). Thus the same constrained model is represented by a supremum of affine multiplier penalties in primal space and by an infimum of affine functions in dual space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained objective can be represented either by adding extended-valued indicator functions of its constraint sets or by a family of ordinary Lagrangians indexed by admissible multipliers. Pointwise maximization of the Lagrangian over all admissible multipliers recovers the hard constrained objective exactly. Pointwise minimization over the primal variable instead produces the dual function. These are two different envelopes of the same Lagrangian family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\Phi(x)=f_0(x)+\delta_{\mathbb R_-^m}(f(x))+\delta_{\{0\}}(h(x))=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}L(x,\lambda,
u),\qquad g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,\lambda,
u).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Each scalar indicator obeys \(\delta_{(-\infty,0]}(t)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\lambda t\), and \(\delta_{\{0\}}(s)=\sup_{\nu\in\mathbb R}\nu s\).

The primal value is \(\inf_{x\in D}\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}L(x,\lambda,
u)\), whereas the dual value is \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}\inf_{x\in D}L(x,\lambda,
u)\).
special_cases_latex: A set constraint \(x\in C\) is represented by adding \(\delta_C(x)\) to the objective.
For affine equalities \(Ax=b\), the equality term is \(\nu^T(Ax-b)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal and dual constructions differ only in the order of \(\inf_x\) and \(\sup_{\lambda,\nu}\).
The minimax inequality immediately gives the value relation \(d^\star\le p^\star\).
boundary_notes: The pointwise supremum identity does not imply that a finite maximizing multiplier exists at an infeasible point.
Interchanging the infimum and supremum requires a separate minimax or strong-duality condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Concavity of the Ordinary Dual Function
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary dual function is concave in the multipliers because it is a pointwise infimum of affine functions; primal convexity is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x)+\langle
u,h(x)angle\), the function \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,
u)\) is concave in \((\lambda,
u)\) on \(\mathbb R^m	imes\mathbb R^p\), even when the primal functions are not convex.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\), and \(L(x,\lambda,\nu)\) is defined for the displayed multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is concave on \(\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^p\), hence also on \(\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural property of the dual function generated by finitely many ordinary constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Multiplier-Supremum Feasibility Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing over sign-compatible ordinary multipliers leaves the objective unchanged at feasible points and gives positive infinity at infeasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in X\),
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\,\nu\in\mathbb R^p}L(x,\lambda,\nu)=
\begin{cases}
f_0(x),&f_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h(x)=0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently, the constrained primal value equals \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}L(x,\lambda,\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{f_0(x):f_i(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}L(x,\lambda,\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise feasibility representation specific to ordinary scalar inequalities and equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Constraint Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar inequality and affine equality constraints enter the Lagrangian through nonnegative and unrestricted multipliers, respectively. Minimization over the primal variable produces a lower bound on every feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\inf\{f_0(x):x\in X,\ f_i(x)\leq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h(x)=0\}\), the ordinary constraint Lagrangian is
\[
L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x)+\langle
u,h(x)angle,
\]
where \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb R^p\). Its dual function is \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,
u)\). Every primal-feasible \(x\) satisfies \(g(\lambda,
u)\leq L(x,\lambda,
u)\leq f_0(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(m,p\in\mathbb N\), \(X\neq\varnothing\) is a subset of a real vector space, \(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_m:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(h:X\to\mathbb R^p\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda,\nu)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\nu)\) is the associated dual function and is a lower bound on every primal-feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite families of scalar inequalities and affine equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concavity and Upper Semicontinuity of the Ordinary Dual Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space structure of the dual function generated by an ordinary finite scalar-constraint Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extend \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,
u)\) to \(\mathbb R^m	imes\mathbb R^p\). Then \(g\) is concave and upper semicontinuous, possibly taking the value \(-\infty\). Consequently every superlevel set \(\{(\lambda,
u):g(\lambda,
u)\geq\alpha\}\) is closed and convex. These conclusions do not require convexity of the primal functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary dual function is concave and upper semicontinuous in the multipliers because it is the pointwise infimum of continuous affine functions, even for a nonconvex primal problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is concave and upper semicontinuous, and its superlevel sets are closed and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Multiplier Supremum Representation of Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise representation supplied specifically by ordinary scalar and equality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in X\),
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\,\nu\in\mathbb R^p}L(x,\lambda,\nu)=
\begin{cases}
f_0(x),&f_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h(x)=0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently the constrained primal value equals \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}L(x,\lambda,\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the ordinary Lagrangian over sign-compatible multipliers leaves the objective unchanged at feasible points and diverges at infeasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf\{f_0(x):f_i(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}L(x,\lambda,\nu).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Multiplier Supremum Representation of Feasibility
Convexity of Cone-Inequality Lagrangian Slices
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-dual-cone scalarization converts a cone-convex constraint map into a convex scalar function, making each admissible-multiplier Lagrangian slice convex in the primal variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be convex, let \(f_0:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex, and let \(G:X\to Y\) be \(K\)-convex in the sense that
\[
G(tx+(1-t)z)\preceq_K tG(x)+(1-t)G(z)
\]
for \(t\in[0,1]\). Then for every \(y\in K^*\), the scalarization \(x\mapsto\langle y,G(x)\rangle\) is convex, and consequently
\[
L(x,y)=f_0(x)+\langle y,G(x)\rangle
\]
is convex in \(x\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(X\) is convex, \(f_0\) is convex, \(G\) is \(K\)-convex, and \(y\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functions \(x\mapsto\langle y,G(x)\rangle\) and \(x\mapsto L(x,y)\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-variable convexity induced by cone convexity and positive-dual-cone scalarization.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthant Specialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary nonnegative-multiplier Lagrangian is precisely the generalized cone Lagrangian for the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Y=\mathbb R^m\) and \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), one has \(K^*=K\). Writing \(G(x)=(f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x))\), the cone constraint \(G(x)\preceq_K0\) is exactly \(f_i(x)\leq0\) for every \(i\), and
\[
L(x,\lambda)=f_0(x)+\langle\lambda,G(x)\rangle=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x),\qquad \lambda\geq0.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(Y=\mathbb R^m\) with its standard inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized inequality and Lagrangian reduce exactly to componentwise inequalities and nonnegative scalar multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of the cone Lagrangian to finitely many scalar inequality multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Inequality Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone inequality is paired with a multiplier from the dual cone; the resulting Lagrangian infimum gives a lower bound on every feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(G(x)\preceq_K0\) when \(-G(x)\in K\), and define \(K^*=\{y\in Y:\langle y,k\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }k\in K\}\). For
\[
\inf\{f_0(x):x\in X,\ G(x)\preceq_K0\},
\]
the generalized-inequality Lagrangian is \(L(x,y)=f_0(x)+\langle y,G(x)\rangle\), with \(y\in K^*\), and \(g(y)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,y)\). If \(x\) is feasible, then \(\langle y,G(x)\rangle\leq0\), hence \(g(y)\leq f_0(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(y\in K^*\), \(g(y)=\inf_{x\in X}[f_0(x)+\langle y,G(x)\rangle]\) is a primal lower bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-ordered inequalities in finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Admissible Cone of Generalized-Inequality Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp characterization of multipliers preserving the weak-duality sign for every cone-feasible residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a closed convex cone and use \(G(x)\preceq_K0\iff G(x)\in-K\). Then
\[
y\in K^*\iff \langle y,v\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }v\in-K.
\]
Thus \(K^*\) is exactly the multiplier set for which \(f_0(x)+\langle y,G(x)\rangle\leq f_0(x)\) holds for every cone-feasible residual. If \(y\notin K^*\), some \(k\in K\) satisfies \(\langle y,k\rangle<0\), and the feasible residual \(-k\) has \(\langle y,-k\rangle>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive dual cone is exactly the set of multipliers whose pairing has the required sign on every feasible cone residual.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in K^*\iff \langle y,v\rangle\leq0\ \forall v\in-K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Admissible Cone of Generalized-Inequality Multipliers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordinary Inequalities as an Orthant Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of the cone Lagrangian to finitely many scalar inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Y=\mathbb R^m\) and \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), one has \(K^*=K\). Writing \(G(x)=(f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x))\), the cone constraint \(G(x)\preceq_K0\) is exactly \(f_i(x)\le0\) for all \(i\), and
\[
L(x,\lambda)=f_0(x)+\langle\lambda,G(x)\rangle=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f_i(x),\qquad \lambda\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary nonnegative-multiplier Lagrangian is precisely the generalized cone Lagrangian for the nonnegative orthant.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=\mathbb R^m\) with its standard inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized inequality and Lagrangian reduce exactly to componentwise inequalities and nonnegative scalar multipliers.

Closure Produced by Double Partial Conjugation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonclosed convex perturbation slice, double partial conjugation recovers its lower-semicontinuous closure rather than necessarily the original slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(F(x,\cdot)\) is proper convex but not lower semicontinuous, then reconstruction from \(L(x,y^*)=-F(x,\cdot)^*(y^*)\) yields
\[
\sup_{y^*}\bigl(\langle y^*,u\rangle+L(x,y^*)\bigr)=F(x,\cdot)^{**}(u)=\operatorname{cl}F(x,\cdot)(u),
\]
which may be strictly smaller than \(F(x,u)\).
assumptions_latex: For the fixed \(x\), \(F(x,\cdot)\) is proper and convex but need not be lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{y^*}[\langle y^*,u\rangle+L(x,y^*)]=F(x,\cdot)^{**}(u)\leq F(x,u)\), with possible strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for exact reconstruction of a nonclosed perturbation slice.

notation.meaning: biconjugate or lower-semicontinuous convex closure of the slice

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction from the Extended-Valued Lagrangian
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex perturbation slice is reconstructed exactly as the supremum of its affine Lagrangian representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that for a fixed \(x\), the slice \(F(x,\cdot)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and define
\[
L(x,y^*)=-F(x,\cdot)^*(y^*).
\]
Then Fenchel-Moreau biconjugacy gives
\[
F(x,u)=\sup_{y^*\in U^*}\bigl(\langle y^*,u\rangle+L(x,y^*)\bigr).
\]
Thus partial conjugation is lossless on proper closed convex slices.
assumptions_latex: For the fixed \(x\), \(F(x,\cdot)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x,u)=\sup_{y^*}[\langle y^*,u\rangle+L(x,y^*)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biconjugate recovery of each closed convex perturbation slice from its Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Valued Lagrangian Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-valued perturbation function yields a Lagrangian by partial conjugation; indicator values can encode hard constraints, and the dual function is a slice of the negative full conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in X\) and \(y^*\in U^*\), define the extended-valued Lagrangian by
\[
L(x,y^*)=\inf_{u\in U}\bigl(F(x,u)-\langle y^*,u\rangle\bigr)=-F(x,\cdot)^*(y^*).
\]
The associated dual function satisfies
\[
g(y^*)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,y^*)=-\sup_{(x,u)\in X\times U}\bigl(\langle y^*,u\rangle-F(x,u)\bigr)=-F^*(0,y^*).
\]
Indicator functions embedded in \(F\) can encode hard constraints without a separate restriction of the infimum domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, with dual space \(U^*\).
\(F:X\times U\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex, and the unperturbed primal value is \(\inf_{x\in X}F(x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation representation incorporating constraints through infinite values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The extended-valued Lagrangian is \( ar L:\mathbb R^n	imes\mathbb R^m	imes\mathbb R^p	o\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) defined by \( ar L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\sum_i\lambda_if_i(x)+\sum_j
u_jh_j(x)\) when \(x\in C\), and \( ar L(x,\lambda,
u)=+\infty\) when \(x
otin C\). Equivalently, \( ar L(x,\lambda,
u)=f_0(x)+\delta_C(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)+
u^Th(x)\), with the finite-valued terms interpreted on \(C\). Its dual function is \(g(\lambda,

Minimizing it over the whole ambient space is exactly the same as minimizing the ordinary Lagrangian over the retained domain. For convex data and nonnegative inequality multipliers, the extended-valued Lagrangian remains convex in the primal variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of Lagrange dual lower bounds
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a primal minimization problem with nonempty domain \(D\), let \(L(x,y)\) be a Lagrangian, where \(y\) denotes all inequality and equality multipliers and \(Y_{\mathrm f}\) is the multiplier sign cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The family is defined for arbitrary primal data; convexity of the primal functions is unnecessary for concavity of the dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual-function family is the collection of primal infima \(\{g(y):y\in Y_{\mathrm f}\}\) generated by \(g(y)=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,y)\). Equivalently, each \(y\) selects the lower-bounding function \(x\mapsto L(x,y)\), and \(g(y)\) is its greatest constant lower bound. For ordinary constraints, \(y=(\lambda,
u)\), \(Y_{\mathrm f}=\mathbb R_+^m	imes\mathbb R^p\), and \(g(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in D}\{f_0(x)+\lambda^Tf(x)+
u^Th(x)\}\). The effective members are those with \(g(y)>-\infty\). The pointwise infimum construction makes \(g\) concave on its multiplier space, and every effective feasible member satisfies \(g(y)\le p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual-function family consists of all lower bounds obtained by fixing admissible multipliers and minimizing the corresponding Lagrangian over the primal domain. Some members may be the vacuous value minus infinity. The effective members are finite lower bounds. As a function of the multipliers, the family forms a concave dual function even if the primal problem is not convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(y):=\inf_{x\in D}L(x,y),\qquad \mathcal G:=\{g(y):y\in Y_{\mathrm f}\},\qquad g(y)\le p^\star\ \forall y\in Y_{\mathrm f}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(g(y)=\sup\{\alpha\in\mathbb R:L(x,y)\ge\alpha\ \forall x\in D\}\), with value \(-\infty\) when no finite constant lower bound exists.
The hypograph of g is \(\{(y,\alpha):\alpha\le L(x,y)\ \forall x\in D\}\).
special_cases_latex: When D is finite, \(g\) is the pointwise minimum of finitely many affine functions of y.
When L is strictly convex and coercive in x for fixed y, the family member is attained at a unique primal minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: Maximizing over the family selects the best Lagrangian lower bound.
The effective dual domain is convex because it is the effective domain of the convex function \(-g\).
boundary_notes: The family may contain only vacuous lower bounds in degenerate problems.
Attainment of the inner infimum is not part of the definition.
