knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Gap–Recovery Consistency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Fenchel primal-dual gap bounds both Fenchel–Young recovery residuals and yields the corresponding epsilon-subgradient inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)=f(x)+g(Ax)\), \(D(y)=-f^*(-A^*y)-g^*(y)\), and define \[R_f(x,y)=f(x)+f^*(-A^*y)+\langle x,A^*y\rangle,\qquad R_g(x,y)=g(Ax)+g^*(y)-\langle Ax,y\rangle.\] If all terms are finite, then \(G(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=R_f(x,y)+R_g(x,y)\), where \(R_f,R_g\ge0\). Consequently, \[G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow R_f(x,y)\le\varepsilon,\quad R_g(x,y)\le\varepsilon,\] equivalently \(-A^*y\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax)\).
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow -A^*y\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\ \text{and}\ y\in\partial_\varepsilon g(Ax)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate consistency between the Fenchel gap and its two component Fenchel–Young recovery residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Stopping–Recovery Consistency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero primal–dual gap is equivalent to both Fenchel recovery conditions, so exact termination and mutually consistent primal and dual recovery identify the same solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gap decomposes into two Fenchel–Young residuals:
\[
G(x,y)=f(x)+f^*(-A^*y)+\langle x,A^*y\rangle+g(Ax)+g^*(y)-\langle Ax,y\rangle.
\]
Both summands are nonnegative. Consequently, \(G(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(-A^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial g(Ax)\). Equivalently, exact gap-based stopping holds precisely when \(x\) is recoverable from \(y\), \(y\) is recoverable from \(x\), and their coupling and stationarity residuals can both be chosen zero. Thus the stopping certificate and the two recovery interfaces select the same exact primal–dual solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,A,f,g\) satisfy the finite-dimensional proper closed convex setting of the Fenchel composite problem.
The candidate pair \((x,y)\) has finite primal and dual objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,y)=0\iff -A^*y\in\partial f(x)\ \text{and}\ y\in\partial g(Ax)\); hence exact stopping and exact mutual recovery coincide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consistency of gap termination with the two Fenchel recovery correspondences.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Concordance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional self-concordance with normalization constant 2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(Q\subset E\) be nonempty, open, and convex. A convex function \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) of class \(C^3\) is self-concordant if, for every \(x\in Q\) and \(h\in E\),
\[
\left|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\right|\le 2\left(D^2f(x)[h,h]\right)^{3/2}.
\]
Thus the third directional derivative is controlled intrinsically by the local quadratic form induced by the Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A thrice differentiable convex function is self-concordant when every third directional derivative is bounded by twice the corresponding Hessian quadratic form raised to the three-halves power.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space and \(Q\subset E\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\right|\le 2\left(D^2f(x)[h,h]\right)^{3/2}\) for all \(x\in Q\) and \(h\in E\).

notation.meaning: Second derivative of f at x applied twice to direction h.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(Q\subseteq E\) be nonempty, open, and convex, and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be three times continuously differentiable and convex. For \(x\in Q\), write \(D^k f(x)\) for the symmetric \(k\)-linear derivative and \(\|h\|_x=(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{1/2}\), which may be a seminorm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional classical smooth convex theory, allowing a singular Hessian. The constant-explicit convention is used so that normalization changes can be stated unambiguously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\ge 0\), the function \(f\) is \(M\)-self-concordant on \(Q\) if
\[
 |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}=M\|h\|_x^3
\]
for every \(x\in Q\) and every \(h\in E\). Convexity ensures \(D^2f(x)[h,h]\ge0\). The standard or normalized convention is the case \(M=2\). The definition concerns control of the third derivative by the intrinsic quadratic form generated by the Hessian; positive definiteness of that form is an additional regime, not part of this general definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-times continuously differentiable convex function on a nonempty open convex domain is \(M\)-self-concordant when, at every point and in every direction, the absolute third directional derivative is at most \(M\) times the three-halves power of the second directional derivative. The usual normalized class takes \(M=2\); the Hessian is permitted to be singular.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and real, and \(Q\subseteq E\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\iff \forall x\in Q\;\forall h\in E:\ |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(x\in Q\) and \(h\in E\), the univariate restriction \(\phi(t)=f(x+th)\), on \(I_{x,h}=\{t:x+th\in Q\}\), satisfies \(|\phi'''(t)|\le M(\phi''(t))^{3/2}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(M=2\), \(f\) is standard self-concordant.
If \(D^3f\equiv0\), every convex quadratic function is \(M\)-self-concordant for every \(M\ge0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(D^2f(x)[h,h]=0\), the defining inequality forces \(D^3f(x)[h,h,h]=0\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not impose lower semicontinuity of the extended-real extension, boundary blow-up, a barrier-gradient inequality, or positive-definite Hessians.
Generalized self-concordance using a different power or an external norm is outside this slot.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, \(Q\subseteq E\) nonempty, open, and convex, and \(f\in C^3(Q)\) convex. Define \(H_x=D^2f(x)\) and extend \(f\) to \(\bar f:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(\bar f=f\) on \(Q\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This entry fixes the principal classical subclasses by three independent attributes: derivative normalization, closed extended-real behavior, and Hessian rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The classical \(M\)-self-concordant class consists of the triples \((Q,f,M)\) satisfying
\[
 |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}
 \quad(x\in Q,\ h\in E).
\]
Within this class, \(f\) is normalized when \(M=2\); it is in the closed-extension regime when \(\bar f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; and it is metrically nondegenerate when \(H_x\succ0\) for every \(x\in Q\). If \(H_x\succeq0\) is singular, the intrinsic object is instead a local seminorm, with null space \(\ker H_x\). These labels are logically separate and may be combined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical class contains smooth convex functions whose third directional derivatives are controlled by the three-halves power of their second directional derivatives. Normalization means that the control constant is two. Closed extension means that extension by positive infinity outside the open domain is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function. Metric nondegeneracy means that every Hessian is positive definite; otherwise the Hessian supplies only a seminorm.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq E\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q,f,M)\) belongs to the classical class exactly when the displayed derivative inequality holds; normalization, closed extension, and Hessian nondegeneracy are the additional predicates \(M=2\), \(\bar f\in\Gamma_0(E)\), and \(D^2f(x)\succ0\), respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The normalized predicate is equivalently \(|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le2\|h\|_x^3\) for all \(x,h\).
The closed-extension predicate is equivalently that every sublevel set of \(\bar f\) is closed and \(\bar f\) is proper convex in finite dimensions.
special_cases_latex: A positive-definite normalized member has a genuine local norm at every point.
A convex quadratic has vanishing third derivative and may be Hessian-degenerate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The taxonomy distinguishes analytic self-concordance from topological closure and from the rank of the intrinsic quadratic form.
boundary_notes: A self-concordant barrier additionally requires boundary behavior and a gradient bound; it is not defined here.
No claim is made that one subclass automatically implies another.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Self-Concordance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex C³ function is normalized self-concordant when every third directional derivative is bounded by twice the corresponding Hessian quadratic form to the three-halves power.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, open, and convex, and let \(f\in C^3(U)\) be convex. The function \(f\) is normalized self-concordant if
\[
\lvert D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\rvert\le 2\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}
\]
for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Since convexity gives \(D^2f(x)[h,h]\ge0\), the right-hand side is well-defined, including in degenerate Hessian directions.
assumptions_latex: \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and three times continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is normalized self-concordant exactly when \(\lvert D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\rvert\le 2\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}\) for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the classical normalization constant \(2\), allowing a positive-semidefinite Hessian.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional, let \(Q\subseteq E\) be nonempty, open, and convex, and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be convex and \(C^3\). Define the canonical extension \(\bar f:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(\bar f(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in Q\) and \(\bar f(x)=+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This entry uses “strong closed-extension regime” for the classical self-concordant inequality together with closed proper extended-real behavior. It does not silently add the barrier-gradient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\ge0\), \(f\) belongs to the strong closed-extension \(M\)-self-concordant regime when
\[
 |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}
 \quad\text{for all }x\in Q,a0h\in E,
\]
and its canonical extension satisfies \(\bar f\in\Gamma_0(E)\). Thus \(\bar f\) is not identically \(+\infty\), never takes \(-\infty\), is convex, and has a closed epigraph. Equivalently, whenever \(x_k\in Q\) and \(x_k\to x\in E\), one has \(\bar f(x)\le\liminf_k f(x_k)\), including boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is in the strong closed-extension self-concordant regime when it satisfies the parameterized classical self-concordance inequality on its open convex domain and its extension by positive infinity is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous. The latter condition records the boundary values through epigraph closure and prevents an unrecorded downward jump at the boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq E\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
\(f\in C^3(Q)\) is convex and satisfies the \(M\)-self-concordance inequality.
\(\bar f=f+\delta_Q\) uses the value \(+\infty\) on \(E\setminus Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is in the closed-extension regime iff \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\) and \(\bar f\in\Gamma_0(E)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In finite dimensions, \(\bar f\in\Gamma_0(E)\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{epi}\bar f\) being a nonempty closed convex set containing no vertical point with value \(-\infty\).
Lower semicontinuity is equivalently \(\bar f(x)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}\bar f(x_k)\) for every convergent sequence \(x_k\to x\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x\in Q\) approaches any finite boundary point, then the canonical extension is lower semicontinuous at the boundary.
When \(Q=E\), the condition reduces to ordinary closedness of the finite-valued convex function.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every sublevel set \(\{x:\bar f(x)\le c\}\) is closed and convex.
boundary_notes: Closed extension does not imply coercivity, attainment of a minimum, positive-definite Hessians, or barrier parameter bounds.
Terminology for “strongly self-concordant” varies; the source locator must verify this chosen closed-extension convention.

notation.meaning: Convex indicator, zero on Q and positive infinity outside Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-extension self-concordance regime
Strong Self-Concordance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the closed-extension convention, strong self-concordance means normalized interior self-concordance together with a proper lower-semicontinuous convex extended-real closure having that interior domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be normalized self-concordant on a nonempty open convex set \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\). In the closed-extension convention, \(f\) is strongly self-concordant when its lower-semicontinuous extension \(\bar f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, satisfies \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\bar f)=U\), and agrees with \(f\) on \(U\). Thus strong self-concordance combines the normalized differential inequality on the interior with a compatible closed convex extended-real representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extended-real closure \(\bar f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\bar f)=U\) and \(\bar f\vert_U=f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adopts the closed extended-real convention; some texts use “strong” differently.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Extensions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed extension assigns each closure point the interior liminf of the function and assigns positive infinity outside the domain closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex function \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\), define its closed extension by
\[
\bar f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\liminf_{U\ni y\to x} f(y),&x\in\overline U,\\
+\infty,&x\notin\overline U.
\end{cases}
\]
Whenever this extension is proper, it is the lower-semicontinuous convex function whose epigraph is \(\overline{\operatorname{epi}f}\). On every interior point where \(f\) is continuous, one has \(\bar f(x)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar f(x)=\liminf_{U\ni y\to x}f(y)\) on \(\overline U\), and \(\bar f(x)=+\infty\) outside \(\overline U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the canonical lower-semicontinuous extended-real closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Compatibility of Closed Extensions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary compatibility requires every extension value to equal the interior liminf; infinity occurs exactly when the function diverges along every interior approach.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A closed extension \(\bar f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is boundary-compatible with \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) when, for every \(z\in\partial U\),
\[
\bar f(z)=\liminf_{U\ni x\to z}f(x).
\]
Consequently, a finite boundary value is permitted only when it is the lower-semicontinuous interior trace. Moreover, \(\bar f(z)=+\infty\) holds exactly when every sequence \((x_k)\subset U\) converging to \(z\) satisfies \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, and \(\bar f\) denotes its closed extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z\in\partial U\), \(\bar f(z)=\liminf_{U\ni x\to z}f(x)\), with value \(+\infty\) precisely when all interior approaches diverge to \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records compatibility as equality with the interior lower limit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian rank regimes for self-concordant functions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^3(Q)\) be convex and self-concordant on a nonempty open convex set \(Q\subseteq E\). For \(x\in Q\), let \(H_x=D^2f(x)\), \(K_x=\ker H_x\), and \(r(x)=\operatorname{rank}H_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional taxonomy separating genuine local metrics, constant-rank seminorm geometry, and variable-rank degeneracy. Quotient statements are made only under a common-kernel hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Hessian-rank regime of \(f\) is classified as follows. It is nondegenerate when \(H_x\succ0\) for every \(x\in Q\). It is constant-rank degenerate when \(r(x)=r<\dim E\) for every \(x\in Q\). It is common-kernel degenerate when there exists a fixed subspace \(K\subset E\) such that \(K_x=K\) for every \(x\in Q\). It is variable-rank when \(r(\cdot)\) is not constant. In the nondegenerate regime, \(\|h\|_x=(H_x[h,h])^{1/2}\) is a norm. In the common-kernel regime it induces a norm on \(E/K\) by \(\|[h]\|_x=\|h\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-concordant function is Hessian-nondegenerate when every Hessian is positive definite. It is constant-rank degenerate when all Hessians have the same deficient rank, common-kernel degenerate when their kernels are one fixed subspace, and variable-rank when the rank changes. Positive definiteness gives a local norm; a fixed kernel gives a well-defined norm only after passing to the quotient by that kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicates \(H_x\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}H_x\equiv r<\dim E\), \(\ker H_x\equiv K\), and nonconstant \(r(x)\) define the nondegenerate, constant-rank, common-kernel, and variable-rank regimes, respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H_x\succ0\) is equivalent to \(D^2f(x)[h,h]>0\) for every nonzero \(h\in E\).
For positive-semidefinite \(H_x\), \(h\in K_x\) is equivalent to \(D^2f(x)[h,h]=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(K=\{0\}\), the common-kernel regime is the nondegenerate regime.
A convex affine function has rank zero and common kernel \(E\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Newton systems are uniquely solvable in the ambient space only in the nondegenerate regime; common-kernel systems naturally live on \(E/K\).
boundary_notes: Constant rank alone does not assert that the kernel subspace is constant.
No theorem asserting rank constancy from self-concordance alone is included.

notation.meaning: Kernel of the Hessian at x.

Degenerate Hessian Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degenerate regime consists of points where the positive-semidefinite Hessian has a nonzero kernel, so the intrinsic local metric is only a seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a normalized self-concordant function \(f\in C^3(U)\), a point \(x\in U\) lies in the degenerate Hessian regime when
\[

knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Hessian Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nondegenerate regime consists of points with positive-definite Hessian, where the intrinsic Hessian seminorm becomes a genuine norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a normalized self-concordant function \(f\in C^3(U)\), a point \(x\in U\) lies in the nondegenerate Hessian regime when
\[
\nabla^2f(x)\succ0.
\]
Equivalently, \(D^2f(x)[h,h]>0\) for every nonzero \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Hence \(\lVert h\rVert_x=\sqrt{D^2f(x)[h,h]}\) is a norm, and its dual norm is defined using the inverse Hessian \(\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) is normalized self-concordant on an open convex set \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nondegenerate regime is characterized by \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), equivalently by \(D^2f(x)[h,h]>0\) for every \(h\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies points carrying a genuine intrinsic Hessian metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Space Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-concordant function with constant Hessian kernel factors, up to an affine term, through the quotient by that kernel and becomes nondegenerate there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a linear subspace, let \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n/N\) be the quotient map, and suppose \(U=\pi^{-1}(V)\) for an open convex set \(V\). If \(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex and \(\ker\nabla^2f(x)=N\) throughout \(U\), then there exist \(a\in N\) and a convex function \(g:V\to\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
f(x)=g(\pi x)+\langle a,x\rangle.
\]
Normalized self-concordance passes from \(f\) to \(g\), whose quotient Hessian is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Rank Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian rank is constant throughout one open convex self-concordant region; transitions can occur only at boundaries, between strata, or after regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\in C^3(U)\) is normalized self-concordant on a nonempty open convex set \(U\), then
\[
\ker\nabla^2f(x)=\ker\nabla^2f(y)

for all \(x,y\in U\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{rank}\nabla^2f(x)\) cannot change inside \(U\). A rank transition can therefore occur only upon leaving the common smooth self-concordant region, for example at a boundary point, across distinct strata, or where the required differentiability or self-concordance inequality ceases to hold.

children.title: Analytic Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent or complementary ways to organize the classical derivative-growth structure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^3(Q)\) be convex on a nonempty open convex subset \(Q\) of a finite-dimensional real vector space \(E\), and let \(M\ge0\). Set \(\|h\|_x=(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition organizes three local analytic representations of the same classical derivative-growth structure; finite-distance Hessian comparison is excluded and treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The \(M\)-self-concordant analytic representation package consists of the following predicates: the diagonal predicate
\[
|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\|h\|_x^3;
\]
the line predicate, under which every \(\phi(t)=f(x+th)\) satisfies \(|\phi'''(t)|\le M(\phi''(t))^{3/2}\); and the multilinear predicate
\[
|D^3f(x)[u,v,w]|\le M\|u\|_x\|v\|_x\|w\|_x.
\]
All quantifiers range over points and directions for which the displayed objects are defined. The package records these coordinate-free, univariate, and multilinear views as representations of classical self-concordance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The analytic representation package records self-concordance in three forms: a diagonal third-derivative inequality, the same inequality for every univariate line restriction, and a bound for the complete symmetric third-derivative tensor by the product of three Hessian seminorms. The representations are local and use the same constant \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The package is the collection of the diagonal, line-restriction, and multilinear derivative-growth predicates displayed in the statement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The diagonal and line predicates are equivalent by \(\phi''(t)=D^2f(x+th)[h,h]\) and \(\phi'''(t)=D^3f(x+th)[h,h,h]\).
For the classical self-concordant cubic form, the diagonal representation admits the corresponding symmetric multilinear representation with the same normalization.
special_cases_latex: Taking \(u=v=w=h\) in the multilinear predicate recovers the diagonal predicate.
For \(E=\mathbb R\), all three representations reduce to \(|f'''(x)|\le M(f''(x))^{3/2}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Each representation is invariant under a change of linear coordinates when derivatives and directions are transformed together.
boundary_notes: The equivalence with the full multilinear bound requires an authoritative source because polarization constants for arbitrary symmetric tensors do not generally remain unchanged without the convex self-concordant structure.
Finite displacement bounds on Hessians are not part of this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Restriction Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multivariate normalized self-concordance is equivalent to the normalized univariate inequality on every affine-line restriction of the function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(I_{x,h}=\{t\in\mathbb{R}:x+th\in U\}\) and define \(\phi_{x,h}(t)=f(x+th)\). Then \(f\) is normalized self-concordant if and only if every such restriction satisfies
\[
\lvert\phi_{x,h}'''(t)\rvert\le2\bigl(\phi_{x,h}''(t)\bigr)^{3/2}
\]
for every \(t\in I_{x,h}\). The identities \(\phi_{x,h}''(t)=D^2f(x+th)[h,h]\) and \(\phi_{x,h}'''(t)=D^3f(x+th)[h,h,h]\) identify the two formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is normalized self-concordant if and only if every line restriction \(\phi(t)=f(x+th)\) satisfies \(\lvert\phi'''(t)\rvert\le2\phi''(t)^{3/2}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The line-restriction representation of \(M\)-self-concordance is the requirement that, for every \(x\in Q\), every \(h\in E\), and every \(t\in I_{x,h}\),
\[
 |\phi_{x,h}'''(t)|\le M\bigl(\phi_{x,h}''(t)\bigr)^{3/2}.
\]
Here \(I_{x,h}\) is an open interval containing zero, possibly unbounded, and convexity gives \(\phi_{x,h}''(t)\ge0\). Since \(\phi_{x,h}''(t)=D^2f(x+th)[h,h]\) and \(\phi_{x,h}'''(t)=D^3f(x+th)[h,h,h]\), the condition quantifies the diagonal derivative bound along every affine line.

equivalent_formulations_latex: It is enough to state the inequality at \(t=0\) for every choice of base point \(x\in Q\), because every \(x+th\in Q\) can serve as a new base point.

knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear-Derivative Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-concordance bounds the cubic derivative tensor on repeated directions by twice the cube of the intrinsic Hessian seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At each \(x\in U\), the derivatives \(D^2f(x)\) and \(D^3f(x)\) are symmetric multilinear forms. Define the intrinsic seminorm by \(\lVert h\rVert_x=\sqrt{D^2f(x)[h,h]}\). Normalized self-concordance has the coordinate-free representation
\[
\lvert D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\rvert\le2\lVert h\rVert_x^3
\]
for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\). This formulation is independent of a basis and remains meaningful when \(D^2f(x)\) is positive semidefinite but singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition is \(\lvert D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\rvert\le2\lVert h\rVert_x^3\) for all \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The multilinear \(M\)-self-concordance representation is
\[
 |T_x[u,v,w]|\le M\|u\|_x\|v\|_x\|w\|_x
\]
for every \(x\in Q\) and all \(u,v,w\in E\). Equivalently, \(T_x\) is a bounded symmetric trilinear form on the Hessian seminormed space with operator seminorm
\[
 \|T_x\|_{H_x}:=\sup\{|T_x[u,v,w]|:\|u\|_x,\|v\|_x,\|w\|_x\le1\}

at most \(M\), after quotienting null directions when necessary.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Variation Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two points whose displacement has local norm less than one, the Hessian-comparison theorem bounds the metric at the second point by the standard multiplicative factors based at the first point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, open, and convex, let \(f\in C^3(U)\) be normalized self-concordant, and let \(x,y\in U\). Suppose \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\) and \(r=\lVert y-x\rVert_x<1\). Then
\[
(1-r)^2\nabla^2f(x)\preceq\nabla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}\nabla^2f(x).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
(1-r)\lVert h\rVert_x\le\lVert h\rVert_y\le(1-r)^{-1}\lVert h\rVert_x.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\((1-r)^2
abla^2f(x)\preceq
abla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}
abla^2f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the local Hessian-comparison theorem inside the unit Dikin ball; it is a consequence of self-concordance rather than an equivalent representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Hessian-variation representation with constant \(M\) is
\[
 |D^3f(x)[u,h,h]|\le M\|u\|_x\,H_x[h,h]
 \quad(x\in Q,a0u,h\in E).
\]
Whenever \(H_x[h,h]>0\), this is equivalently
\[
 |D_u\log(H_x[h,h])|\le M\|u\|_x.
\]
Thus the relative directional rate of change of every positive Hessian quadratic value is controlled by the length of the displacement direction in the same intrinsic geometry. If \(H_x[h,h]=0\), the nonlogarithmic formulation requires \(D^3f(x)[u,h,h]=0\).

Where the quadratic value is positive, this is a bound on its logarithmic directional derivative. Null curvature directions are handled by the nonlogarithmic formula.

The displayed inequality is the repeated-argument case \(v=w=h\) of a multilinear third-derivative bound.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\), where \(Q\subseteq E\) is open and convex. Let \(A:F\to E\) be linear, \(b\in E\), \(\alpha>0\), and let \(\ell:F\to\mathbb R\) be affine. Define \(P=A^{-1}(Q-b)=\{y:Ay+b\in Q\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine pullbacks, domain restrictions represented by affine parametrizations, positive rescaling, and affine-value perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The elementary transformation operator is
\[
 \mathcal T_{A,b,\alpha,\ell}f(y)=\alpha f(Ay+b)+\ell(y),\qquad y\in P.
\]
Its second and third derivatives are
\[
D^2(\mathcal Tf)(y)[u,u]=\alpha D^2f(Ay+b)[Au,Au],
\]
\[
D^3(\mathcal Tf)(y)[u,u,u]=\alpha D^3f(Ay+b)[Au,Au,Au].
\]
The transformed function is \(M/\sqrt\alpha\)-self-concordant on every nonempty open convex component of \(P\). The affine term does not affect derivatives of order at least two. Singular \(A\) is allowed and may create Hessian degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-preserving transformation consists of affine precomposition, positive multiplication, and addition of an affine function. Pullback replaces each direction by its image under the linear map; scaling multiplies both the Hessian and third derivative. The resulting self-concordance constant is \(M/\sqrt\alpha\), while affine output terms have no effect.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\) and \(Q\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
\(A:F\to E\) is linear, \(b\in E\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(\ell\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_{A,b,\alpha,\ell}f\in\mathrm{SC}_{M/\sqrt\alpha}(P).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Affine precomposition alone preserves \(M\); positive scaling by \(\alpha\) changes \(M\) to \(M/\sqrt\alpha\); affine addition preserves \(M\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is invertible and \(\alpha=1\), this is an affine coordinate change with unchanged constant.
If \(A\) parametrizes an affine subspace, the operator gives an affine-slice restriction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Choosing \(\alpha=M^2/4\) for \(M>0\) converts the parameterized inequality to the standard constant \(2\).
boundary_notes: Negative or zero scaling is excluded because it does not preserve the required convex smooth structure in general.
A noninjective pullback may destroy positive definiteness even though self-concordance remains valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Invariance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precomposition with any affine map preserves normalized self-concordance on the nonempty affine preimage of the original domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

D^2g(y)[h,h]=D^2f(Ay+b)[Ah,Ah]
\]
and
\[
D^3g(y)[h,h,h]=D^3f(Ay+b)[Ah,Ah,Ah].
\]
Substitution into the normalized self-concordance inequality shows that \(g\) is normalized self-concordant on \(V\), without requiring \(A\) to be invertible.

g(y)=f(Ay+b),\qquad y\in P,

D^2g(y)[u,v]=D^2f(Ay+b)[Au,Av],

Consequently,
\[
|D^3g(y)[u,u,u]|\le M(D^2g(y)[u,u])^{3/2}
\]
for every \(y\in P\) and \(u\in F\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\), with \(Q\subseteq E\) nonempty, open, and convex. Let \(L=x_0+V\) be an affine subspace meeting \(Q\), and let \(U:F\to E\) be an injective linear parametrization with \(\operatorname{range}U=V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained affine subspaces, represented intrinsically by coordinates on their direction spaces. Openness is relative to the slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(y_0\in F\) so that \(x_0+Uy_0\in Q\), define
\[
P=\{y\in F:x_0+Uy\in Q\},
\qquad g(y)=f(x_0+Uy),
\]
and regard \(P\) as an open convex subset of \(F\). The affine-slice restriction is \(g\), and it satisfies
\[
|D^3g(y)[u,u,u]|
=|D^3f(x_0+Uy)[Uu,Uu,Uu]|
\le M(D^2g(y)[u,u])^{3/2}.
\]
Thus the restriction inherits the same self-concordance constant. Different injective parametrizations yield affinely equivalent restricted functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To restrict a self-concordant function to an affine equality-constrained slice, parametrically identify the slice with its direction space and compose the function with that affine parametrization. The relative domain is open and convex, and the restricted function has the same self-concordance constant. Changing slice coordinates only produces an affine reparametrization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(y)=f(x_0+Uy)\) belongs to \(\mathrm{SC}_M(P)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a constraint \(Bx=d\), choose any feasible \(x_0\) and let the columns of \(U\) span \(\ker B\); then \(x=x_0+Uy\) parametrizes the slice.
Intrinsically, the restriction has derivatives \(D^kf|_L(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_k]=D^kf(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_k]\) for \(v_i\in V\).
special_cases_latex: A one-dimensional slice gives the line-restriction representation.
A zero-dimensional slice gives a constant function on a singleton relative domain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Equality constraints preserve self-concordance after elimination of constrained coordinates.
boundary_notes: The slice domain need not be open in \(E\); it is open relative to \(L\).
Restriction to a nonaffine manifold is not covered.

notation.meaning: Affine slice with direction subspace V.
Injective parametrization of the direction subspace.

children.title: Normalization Transformation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Changes of normalization and associated class parameters.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^3(Q)\) be convex on a nonempty open convex set and satisfy \(|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le M(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}\). Let \(\alpha>0\), \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\ell\) be affine.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical constant-explicit self-concordance under positive rescaling and affine-value shifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g=\alpha f+\ell+\beta\). Since
\[
D^2g=\alpha D^2f,
\qquad D^3g=\alpha D^3f,
\]
the normalization parameter transforms by
\[
M_g=\frac{M}{\sqrt\alpha}.
\]
Thus \(g\in\mathrm{SC}_{M/\sqrt\alpha}(Q)\). For \(M>0\), the canonical scaling to the standard constant \(2\) is \(\alpha=M^2/4\). Conversely, if \(g=\alpha f\) is known to have constant \(M_g\), then the corresponding constant for \(f\) is \(M_g\sqrt\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying a self-concordant function by a positive scalar \(\alpha\) divides its self-concordance constant by \(\sqrt\alpha\). Adding affine or constant terms changes neither the Hessian nor the third derivative. A function with constant \(M>0\) is converted to the standard constant two by multiplying it by \(M^2/4\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha f+\ell+\beta\in\mathrm{SC}_{M/\sqrt\alpha}(Q).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The squared parameter transforms as \(M_g^2=M^2/\alpha\).
Standard normalization \(M_g=2\) is equivalent to \(\alpha=M^2/4\) when \(M>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\alpha=1\), affine perturbations preserve the parameter.
If \(M=0\), positive scaling retains parameter zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any positive finite self-concordance parameter can be converted to the standard convention by rescaling function values.
boundary_notes: Scaling the argument is an affine-coordinate transformation, not the value-normalization operation defined here.
Nonpositive value scaling is excluded.

notation.meaning: Self-concordance parameter assigned to the transformed function.

review_flags: The normalization formula lacks an inspected authoritative self-concordance locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization and positive-scaling calculus
Positive Function Rescaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplication by a positive scalar preserves self-concordance and divides the generalized self-concordance parameter by the scalar's square root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g:=cf\), the transformed self-concordance inequality is \[ |D^3g(x)[h,h,h]|\le \frac{M}{\sqrt c}\bigl(D^2g(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex and \(M\)-self-concordant on an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(cf\) is \(M/\sqrt c\)-self-concordant on \(U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Renormalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling an M-self-concordant function by M squared over four converts it to the standard convention with constant two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical renormalization \[ \widehat f:=\frac{M^2}{4}f \] satisfies \[ |D^3\widehat f(x)[h,h,h]|\le 2\bigl(D^2\widehat f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex and \(M\)-self-concordant on an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The renormalized function \(\widehat f:=(M^2/4)f\) is standard self-concordant on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical conversion to the convention having third-derivative constant \(2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Class-Parameter Transformation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive barrier scaling divides the third-derivative parameter by the square root of the scale and multiplies the barrier parameter by the scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G:=cF\), the parameter transformation is \[ (M,\nu)\longmapsto\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt c},c\nu\right). \] Thus \(G\) satisfies the corresponding third-derivative and barrier-gradient inequalities on \(U\).
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(F\in C^3(U)\) is an \((M,\nu)\)-self-concordant barrier satisfying the \(M\)-third-derivative inequality and \(|DF(x)[h]|\le\sqrt{\nu D^2F(x)[h,h]}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier \(G:=cF\) has parameters \((M/\sqrt c,c\nu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint scaling law for generalized self-concordance and barrier-gradient parameters.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.3 Definition of self-concordant function p. 175

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Convention Equivalence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any two positive constants in the classical self-concordance inequality define equivalent normalizations after scaling the function by the squared ratio of the constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \[ |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le a\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] holds for all \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\) if and only if \(g:=(a/b)^2f\) satisfies \[ |D^3g(x)[h,h,h]|\le b\bigl(D^2g(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] for all \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex on an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(a\)- and \(b\)-normalizations are equivalent under \(f\mapsto(a/b)^2f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between positive constants used in the classical self-concordance inequality.

children.title: Aggregation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Closure mechanisms for assembling structured self-concordant objectives.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq E\) be nonempty, open, and convex. For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(f_i\in\mathrm{SC}_{M_i}(Q)\), and let \(\alpha_i>0\). Define \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive sums on a common domain. The terms may couple the same variables and may have different self-concordance parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The weighted aggregation calculus assigns to
\[
F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(x)
\]
the valid self-concordance parameter
\[
M_F=\max_{1\le i\le m}\frac{M_i}{\sqrt{\alpha_i}}.
\]
Indeed, the defining aggregate tensors are
\[
D^2F=\sum_i\alpha_iD^2f_i,
\qquad D^3F=\sum_i\alpha_iD^3f_i,
\]
and the class rule is \(F\in\mathrm{SC}_{M_F}(Q)\). The assigned constant is a generally nonminimal upper bound; cancellations or stronger curvature may permit a smaller parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite positive weighted sum of self-concordant functions on the same open convex domain remains self-concordant. A valid aggregate constant is the largest individual constant divided by the square root of its weight. The calculus records a safe class parameter and does not claim that it is always the smallest possible one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\sum_i\alpha_i f_i\in\mathrm{SC}_{\max_i(M_i/\sqrt{\alpha_i})}(Q).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If all \(M_i=2\) and all \(\alpha_i\ge1\), then \(F\) is standard self-concordant.
After defining \(g_i=\alpha_i f_i\), each \(g_i\) has parameter \(M_i/\sqrt{\alpha_i}\), and their sum uses the maximum of these parameters.
special_cases_latex: For one summand, the rule reduces to positive-scaling calculus.
For equal unit weights and common parameter \(M\), the sum has valid parameter \(M\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Structured objectives can be assembled from finitely many compatible self-concordant terms without multiplying the parameter by the number of terms.
boundary_notes: Negative weights are excluded.
The formula requires all terms to be finite and smooth on the common domain under consideration.

notation.meaning: Valid self-concordance parameter assigned to the aggregate.
Positive weight of the ith term.

review_flags: No inspected source supports the exact weighted-sum parameter formula.

children.title: Separable Aggregation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Aggregation of compatible terms and separable blocks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(i=1,a0\ldots,a0m\), let \(E_i\) be finite-dimensional, \(Q_i\subseteq E_i\) nonempty, open, and convex, and \(f_i\in\mathrm{SC}_{M_i}(Q_i)\). Put \(E=\prod_iE_i\), \(Q=\prod_iQ_i\), and choose \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-product domains and block-separable sums, with directions decomposed blockwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The separable aggregate is
\[
F(x_1,a0\ldots,a0x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i f_i(x_i),
\qquad x\in Q.
\]
For \(h=(h_1,a0\ldots,a0h_m)\),
\[
D^2F(x)[h,h]=\sum_i\alpha_iD^2f_i(x_i)[h_i,h_i],
\]
\[
D^3F(x)[h,h,h]=\sum_i\alpha_iD^3f_i(x_i)[h_i,h_i,h_i].
\]
The block-separable calculus assigns \(M_F=\max_iM_i/\sqrt{\alpha_i}\), so \(F\in\mathrm{SC}_{M_F}(Q)\). Its Hessian is block diagonal with the scaled component Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a Cartesian-product domain, sum positively weighted self-concordant functions that depend on separate variable blocks. The Hessian is block diagonal, the derivative forms split blockwise, and a valid self-concordance constant is the maximum component constant divided by the square root of its weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathrm{SC}_{\max_i(M_i/\sqrt{\alpha_i})}(\prod_iQ_i).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The aggregate local seminorm satisfies \(\|h\|_{F,x}^2=\sum_i\alpha_i\|h_i\|_{f_i,x_i}^2\).
The Hessian operator is \(D^2F(x)=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_1D^2f_1(x_1),\ldots,\alpha_mD^2f_m(x_m))\).
special_cases_latex: With unit weights and normalized component functions, the separable sum is normalized self-concordant.
If each component Hessian is positive definite, the aggregate Hessian is positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: Independent self-concordant blocks combine without cross-Hessian or cross-third-derivative terms.
boundary_notes: Functions sharing variables belong to the general aggregation rule, not this strictly separable definition.
An infinite product or infinite series requires additional convergence conditions.
review_flags: No inspected authoritative source establishes this block-separable parameter rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-separable self-concordant aggregation
Compatible Function Sums
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive weighted sum of self-concordant functions on one domain is self-concordant with parameter bounded by the largest weight-adjusted component parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i f_i\) and \(M:=\max_{1\le i\le m}M_i/\sqrt{c_i}\), \[ |D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(f_i\in C^3(U)\) is convex and \(M_i\)-self-concordant for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i f_i\) is \(M\)-self-concordant for \(M:=\max_{1\le i\le m}M_i/\sqrt{c_i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted sums on a common domain under the generalized third-derivative convention.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.3 Definition of self-concordant function p. 175

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Constructions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing block functions on a Cartesian-product domain produces a self-concordant separable function with the largest weight-adjusted block parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in U\), define \(F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i f_i(x_i)\). Then \[ |D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2},\qquad M:=\max_{1\le i\le m}\frac{M_i}{\sqrt{c_i}}, \] for every \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\in\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\).
assumptions_latex: \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is open and convex, and \(f_i\in C^3(U_i)\) is convex and \(M_i\)-self-concordant for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(U:=\prod_{i=1}^mU_i\), the function \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i f_i(x_i)\) is \(M\)-self-concordant for \(M:=\max_{1\le i\le m}M_i/\sqrt{c_i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable construction on a finite Cartesian product of Euclidean spaces.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.3 Definition of self-concordant function p. 175

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Parameter Aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent barrier blocks, adjusted third-derivative parameters aggregate by maximum, while barrier-gradient parameters aggregate by weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The separable barrier \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iF_i(x_i)\) admits the parameters \[ M_F:=\max_{1\le i\le m}\frac{M_i}{\sqrt{c_i}},\qquad \nu_F:=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\nu_i. \]
assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(F_i\) is an \((M_i,\nu_i)\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(U:=\prod_{i=1}^mU_i\), the product barrier \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iF_i(x_i)\) has admissible parameters \(M:=\max_{1\le i\le m}(M_i/\sqrt{c_i})\) and \(\nu:=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\nu_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint aggregation of generalized self-concordance and barrier-gradient parameters across independent blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing negative aggregation weights destroys closure: negating the logarithmic barrier makes it concave and therefore not self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f(x):=-\log x\) is standard self-concordant on \((0,\infty)\), whereas its negatively weighted aggregate \(F:=-f=\log x\) satisfies \(F''(x)=-1/x^2<0\). Thus negative aggregation weights do not preserve convex self-concordance.
assumptions_latex: The aggregation coefficient is permitted to equal \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The negatively weighted aggregate \(F:=-f\) is not convex and therefore is not self-concordant under the convex self-concordance convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure when the positive-weight hypothesis in sum closure is removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Augmentations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a convex quadratic preserves self-concordance and its parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:=f+q\), \[ |D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\le M\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2} \] for every \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex and \(M\)-self-concordant on an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(q(x):=\tfrac12\langle x,Qx\rangle+\langle b,x\rangle+c\), where \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(Q\succeq0\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented function \(F:=f+q\) is \(M\)-self-concordant on \(U\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\) on a nonempty open convex set \(Q\subseteq E\). Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,Hx\rangle+\langle c,x\rangle+\gamma\), where \(H\succeq0\), and define \(F=f+q\) on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addition of a finite convex quadratic, including affine and constant terms, in finite-dimensional classical self-concordance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex quadratic augmentation is the operation
\[
F(x)=f(x)+\tfrac12\langle x,Hx\rangle+\langle c,x\rangle+\gamma,
\qquad H\succeq0.
\]
It has
\[
D^2F(x)=D^2f(x)+H\succeq D^2f(x),
\qquad D^3F(x)=D^3f(x).
\]
The augmentation preserves the parameter: \(F\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\). The new quadratic curvature can remove Hessian degeneracy in directions on which \(H\) is positive, while the affine and constant pieces do not affect derivatives of order two or three.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding any finite convex quadratic to an \(M\)-self-concordant function preserves the same parameter. The quadratic adds positive-semidefinite curvature to the Hessian and contributes no third derivative. Linear and constant terms are included as the zero-Hessian special case. The augmentation may make a previously singular local metric nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=f+q\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The rule applies to every convex polynomial of degree at most two because its third derivative vanishes.
For every direction \(h\), \(D^2F(x)[h,h]=D^2f(x)[h,h]+\langle h,Hh\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H=0\), the augmentation is affine and leaves both Hessian and third derivative unchanged.
If \(D^2f(x)+H\succ0\) for every \(x\), the augmented function has a genuine local norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic regularization can strengthen local curvature without worsening the self-concordance constant.
boundary_notes: An indefinite quadratic need not preserve convexity or the defining inequality.
A general smooth convex augmentation with nonzero third derivative requires a separate compatibility condition.
review_flags: The exact quadratic-augmentation closure claim lacks an inspected self-concordance source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Compatible Objective Augmentations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian-relative third-derivative bound between an objective and a self-concordant reference function guarantees self-concordance of every nonnegative parameterized augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Call \(f\) \(\beta\)-compatible with \(F\) when, for all \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le\beta D^2f(x)[h,h]\sqrt{D^2F(x)[h,h]}.
\]
Then \(F_t:=F+tf\) is convex and obeys
\[
|D^3F_t(x)[h,h,h]|\le\max\{2,\beta\sqrt t\}\bigl(D^2F_t(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}.
\]
Thus this compatibility predicate is sufficient for every nonnegative member of the augmented family to be self-concordant.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^3(U)\) is convex and standard self-concordant on an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(f\in C^3(U)\) is convex and satisfies \(|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le\beta D^2f(x)[h,h]\sqrt{D^2F(x)[h,h]}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family \(F_t=F+tf\) is \(M_t\)-self-concordant with \(M_t\le\max\{2,\beta\sqrt t\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit Hessian-relative compatibility convention for forming parameterized self-concordant families.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited definition section does not specifically support this compatibility predicate or its parameter bound. Moreover, the displayed hypothesis yields a mixed term proportional to \(\beta D^2(tf)\sqrt{D^2F}\); the asserted bound \(\max\{2,\beta\sqrt t\}\) does not follow uniformly from the stated assumptions and can fail for small positive \(t\) with large \(\beta\). A source confirming the intended compatibility convention and the correct bound is required.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in\mathrm{SC}_M(Q)\) on a nonempty open convex set \(Q\subseteq E\), and let \(\psi\in C^3(Q)\) be convex. Write \(\|h\|_{f,x}=(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized convex objective additions controlled relative to a fixed self-concordant reference function. The stated parameter is a valid upper bound, not necessarily optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The objective \(\psi\) is \(\kappa\)-third-derivative-compatible with the reference \(f\) when \(\kappa\ge0\) and
\[
|D^3\psi(x)[h,h,h]|\le\kappa\|h\|_{f,x}^3
\quad\text{for every }x\in Q,a0h\in E.
\]
For \(t\ge0\), define the parameterized augmentation \(F_t=f+t\psi\). The compatible-family calculus assigns
\[
F_t\in\mathrm{SC}_{M+t\kappa}(Q),

a valid bound based on \(D^2F_t\succeq D^2f\) and \(D^3F_t=D^3f+tD^3\psi\). Compatibility is relative to the chosen reference metric and need not be symmetric in \(f\) and \(\psi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth convex objective is third-derivative-compatible with a self-concordant reference when its third directional derivative is bounded by \(\kappa\) times the cube of the reference Hessian seminorm. Adding a nonnegative multiple \(t\psi\) to the reference then forms a self-concordant family with valid parameter \(M+t\kappa\). The definition is directional: changing the reference function changes compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_t=f+t\psi\in\mathrm{SC}_{M+t\kappa}(Q).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Compatibility is \(\sup_{x,h:\|h\|_{f,x}>0}|D^3\psi(x)[h,h,h]|/\|h\|_{f,x}^3\le\kappa\), together with vanishing on reference-null directions.
For affine or convex quadratic \(\psi\), one may take \(\kappa=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\psi(x)=\langle c,x\rangle\), then every \(F_t=f+t\langle c,x\rangle\) retains parameter \(M\).
Convex quadratic augmentation is the case \(D^3\psi=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A single reference function can generate a nonnegative parameterized family of self-concordant objectives whenever the augmentation has controlled third derivative in the reference metric.
boundary_notes: This compatibility notion is stronger than merely requiring \(\psi\) to be convex.
The terminology and parameter rule must be checked against the intended source; other literature uses different compatibility inequalities involving first or second derivatives.

Parameterized augmented objective f plus t times psi.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(\mathbb E^*\). Let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be closed and convex, with nonempty open domain \(U\), three continuous derivatives on \(U\), and positive-definite Hessian \(H_x=\nabla^2 f(x)\) for every \(x\in U\). Assume that \(f\) is self-concordant with constant \(M_f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, strictly convex self-concordant conjugacy on the effective domains; the statement does not cover nonsmooth or degenerate conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Fenchel–Legendre conjugate is \[f^*(s)=\sup_{x\in U}\{\langle s,xangle-f(x)\},\qquad \operatorname{dom}f^*=\{s\in\mathbb E^*:f^*(s)<+\infty\}.\] For every \(s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\), the maximizer \(x(s)\) is unique and satisfies \(s=
abla f(x(s))\). The correspondence is \[s=
abla f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=
abla f^*(s),\qquad f(x)+f^*(s)=\langle s,xangle.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{dom}f^*=
abla f(U)\) is open, \(f^*\) is self-concordant with \(M_{f^*}=M_f\), and its Hessian is the inverse of the primal Hessian at corresponding points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed, smooth, strictly convex self-concordant function, Fenchel conjugacy pairs each primal point \(x\) with the dual point \(s=\nabla f(x)\). The conjugate is \(f^*(s)=\sup_x\{\langle s,x\rangle-f(x)\}\); on its finite domain the maximizer is unique, equals \(\nabla f^*(s)\), and satisfies the Fenchel equality. The gradient maps are inverse coordinate maps, and conjugation preserves the self-concordance constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
abla f^*=(
abla f)^{-1},\qquad 
abla^2f^*(
abla f(x))=[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1},\qquad M_{f^*}=M_f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: At corresponding points, \[s\in\partial f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\partial f^*(s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)+f^*(s)=\langle s,x\rangle,\] and the subgradients are singletons under the stated smoothness and positive-definiteness assumptions.
special_cases_latex: For a standard self-concordant function, \(M_f=1\), its conjugate is also standard self-concordant.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal and conjugate coordinates describe the same local geometry through mutually inverse gradient maps.
The conjugate effective domain is exactly the gradient image \(\nabla f(U)\).
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is material: with a singular Hessian, the gradient map need not be one-to-one and the smooth inverse correspondence can fail.
The conjugate may take value \(+\infty\) outside \(\nabla f(U)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel–Legendre correspondence for self-concordant functions

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Map Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex Legendre function, the primal and conjugate gradient maps are inverse bijections, and paired coordinates attain equality in the Fenchel–Young relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in U\) and \(y\in U^*\), \[ y=
abla f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=
abla f^*(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)+f^*(y)=\langle x,yangle. \] In particular, \(
abla f^*=(
abla f)^{-1}\), and \(
abla f\) maps \(U\) bijectively onto \(U^*\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a proper closed convex Legendre function, and \(U:=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gradient maps \(\nabla f:U\to U^*\) and \(\nabla f^*:U^*\to U\) are mutual inverses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Legendre correspondence on interiors of the primal and conjugate domains.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) satisfy the smooth, positive-definite self-concordant hypotheses of the Fenchel–Legendre correspondence on an open domain \(U\subset\mathbb E\), and let \(f^*\) be its conjugate with open domain \(U^*=\operatorname{dom}f^*\subset\mathbb E^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional Legendre correspondence restricted to the effective domains of \(f\) and \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gradient-map correspondence is the bijection \[
abla f:U\longrightarrow U^*,\qquad x\longmapsto s=
abla f(x),\] whose inverse is \[
abla f^*:U^*\longrightarrow U,\qquad s\longmapsto x=
abla f^*(s).\] Thus, for all \(x\in U\) and \(s\in U^*\), \[s=
abla f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=
abla f^*(s).\] The paired points are precisely the unique stationary pairs for \(x\mapsto f(x)-\langle s,xangle\), and they satisfy \(f(x)+f^*(s)=\langle s,xangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and conjugate coordinates are connected by the gradient of \(f\): a primal point \(x\) has dual coordinate \(s=\nabla f(x)\), while the inverse coordinate map is \(x=\nabla f^*(s)\). These maps are bijections between the open effective domains. A pair corresponds exactly when it attains Fenchel equality and when \(x\) uniquely minimizes \(f(\cdot)-\langle s,\cdot\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
abla f(U)=U^*,\qquad 
abla f^*\circ
abla f=\operatorname{id}_U,
\qquad 
abla f\circ
abla f^*=\operatorname{id}_{U^*}.\]

\[s=\nabla f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)+f^*(s)=\langle s,x\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)=\tfrac12\langle Hx,x\rangle\) with \(H\succ0\), then \(s=Hx\), \(f^*(s)=\tfrac12\langle s,H^{-1}s\rangle\), and \(x=H^{-1}s\).

Differentiating the inverse gradient maps gives the inverse-Hessian correspondence.

No claim is made for dual points where \(f^*(s)=+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Metric Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At conjugate points linked by the gradient map, the conjugate Hessian is the inverse primal Hessian, and the induced squared lengths agree under differential transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y=
abla f(x)\). Legendre conjugacy gives \(x=
abla f^*(y)\). Differentiating these mutually inverse gradient maps yields \[
abla^2 f^*(y)=[
abla^2 f(x)]^{-1}.\] Consequently, if a primal tangent vector \(h\) is transported to \(k=
abla^2 f(x)h\), then \[h^{\mathsf T}
abla^2 f(x)h=k^{\mathsf T}
abla^2 f^*(y)k.\] Thus the primal Hessian metric and conjugate Hessian metric are inverse local metrics under the gradient map.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb R\) is Legendre type, twice continuously differentiable, and strictly convex on an open convex set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\).
\(\nabla^2 f(x)\succ0\) for every \(x\in\Omega\), and \(y=\nabla f(x)\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f^*)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse primal and conjugate Hessian metrics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(x\in U\) and \(s=
abla f(x)\in U^*\) be corresponding points for a smooth convex function \(f\) with positive-definite Hessian. Put \(H_x=
abla^2f(x):\mathbb E	o\mathbb E^*\) and \(H_s^*=
abla^2f^*(s):\mathbb E^*	o\mathbb E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise finite-dimensional Hessian geometry at corresponding Legendre coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inverse-metric correspondence is the identity \[H_s^*=H_x^{-1}\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad s=\nabla f(x).\] Consequently, the primal quadratic form on \(\mathbb E\), \(h\mapsto\langle H_xh,h\rangle\), and the conjugate quadratic form on \(\mathbb E^*\), \(g\mapsto\langle g,H_s^*g\rangle\), are dual metrics. The musical maps \(h\mapsto H_xh\) and \(g\mapsto H_s^*g\) are inverse isometries: \[\|h\|_x^2=\langle H_xh,h\rangle=\|H_xh\|_{s,f^*}^2,\qquad \|g\|_{x,*}^2=\langle g,H_x^{-1}g\rangle=\|g\|_{s,f^*}^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At paired coordinates \(s=\nabla f(x)\), the Hessian of the conjugate is exactly the inverse of the Hessian of the primal function. Hence the tangent metric at \(x\) and the cotangent metric at \(s\) are the same geometry in inverse coordinates. Applying the primal Hessian to a tangent vector preserves its local length when that image is measured by the conjugate Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
abla^2f^*(
abla f(x))=[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(h\in\mathbb E\), \[\|h\|_x=\|\nabla^2f(x)h\|_{\nabla f(x),f^*}.\]
For every \(g\in\mathbb E^*\), \[\|g\|_{x,*}=\|g\|_{\nabla f(x),f^*}.\]
special_cases_latex: For a positive-definite quadratic \(f(x)=\tfrac12\langle Hx,x\rangle\), both metrics are constant and equal to \(H\) and \(H^{-1}\), respectively.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal local balls are mapped to conjugate local balls by the Hessian at the base point.
The condition numbers of the paired Hessians are reciprocal under a fixed Euclidean identification.
boundary_notes: The inverse formula requires nonsingular Hessians.
The equality is pointwise at conjugate points; it does not identify Hessians at unrelated \(x\) and \(s\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse primal and conjugate Hessian metrics

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Newton Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton correction transported through the gradient map becomes the negative residual, while its primal length, residual decrement, and conjugate-coordinate length coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_x=
abla^2 f(x)\), \(y=
abla f(x)\), and let \(r\) be a covector residual. The primal Newton correction is \(p=-H_x^{-1}r\). Its image under the differential of the gradient map is \(k=H_xp=-r\). Since \(
abla^2 f^*(y)=H_x^{-1}\), \[\|p\|_x^2=p^{\mathsf T}H_xp=r^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}r=k^{\mathsf T}
abla^2 f^*(y)k.\] Hence the Newton correction, its residual-based decrement, and its conjugate-coordinate image encode the same local length.
assumptions_latex: A covector residual \(r\in\mathbb R^n\) is given at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric correspondence for Newton corrections represented in primal and conjugate coordinates.

notation.meaning: Newton correction generated by residual r

A source and explicit Newton problem are needed to validate the intended mathematical version.

abla f(x)\), let \(H_x=
abla^2f(x)\succ0\), and let \(\delta\in\mathbb E^*\) be a perturbation of the dual coordinate. The linearized primal displacement solving \(
abla f(x+p)=s+\delta\) is \(p_N=H_x^{-1}\delta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Conjugate Newton geometry is the identification of the dual coordinate step \(\delta\) with the primal Newton displacement \(p_N=H_x^{-1}\delta\). At \(s=
abla f(x)\), \[p_N=
abla^2f^*(s)\delta,\qquad H_xp_N=
\delta.\] The associated decrement is coordinate invariant: \[\lambda^2(\delta;x)=\langle\delta,H_x^{-1}\deltaangle=\langle H_xp_N,p_Nangle=\langle\delta,
abla^2f^*(s)\deltaangle.\] Thus the Newton direction in primal coordinates and the ordinary tangent direction in conjugate coordinates represent the same locally measured displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbation \(\delta\) of the conjugate coordinate corresponds, under Newton linearization, to the primal displacement \(p_N=[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\delta\). Because the conjugate Hessian equals the inverse primal Hessian, this displacement can also be written \(p_N=\nabla^2f^*(s)\delta\). Its squared primal local norm equals the squared conjugate local norm of \(\delta\), so the Newton decrement is unchanged by switching between paired coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|p_N\|_x=\|\delta\|_{s,f^*}=\|\delta\|_{x,*},\qquad p_N=[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\delta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The maps \(p_N\mapsto\delta=H_xp_N\) and \(\delta\mapsto p_N=H_x^{-1}\delta\) are mutually inverse local isometries.
special_cases_latex: For the residual \(r=\nabla f(x)-a\), the Newton correction for solving \(\nabla f(x)=a\) is \(-H_x^{-1}r\), with decrement \(\sqrt{\langle r,H_x^{-1}r\rangle}\).

Hessian solves in the primal representation are metric multiplications in the conjugate representation.

Signs depend on whether \(\delta\) denotes a target displacement or a residual to be cancelled.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary of the classical self-concordant function class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subset\mathbb E\) be a nonempty open convex set and let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) have effective domain \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional Euclidean self-concordance; generalized self-concordance and nonsmooth analogues are adjacent theories, not members of this class by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical self-concordant class consists of closed convex functions \(f\in C^3(U)\) for which there exists a finite constant \(M_f\ge0\) satisfying \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\le 2M_f\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}\qquad\forall x\in U,\ \forall h\in\mathbb E.\] Its function-class boundary comprises the failures of the defining analytic requirements: nonconvexity, a nonopen effective domain for the smooth restriction, absence of three continuous derivatives, or absence of any finite uniform \(M_f\) in the displayed inequality. A function outside the class may satisfy some but not all of these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical self-concordance is the class of closed convex functions that are three-times continuously differentiable on an open domain and whose third directional derivative is uniformly bounded by a finite constant times the three-halves power of the Hessian quadratic form. The boundary of the class is reached whenever convexity or the required smooth domain is lost, or whenever no finite constant controls this derivative ratio uniformly over all points and directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f\in\mathrm{SC}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f\text{ has the stated closedness, convexity, open-domain, }C^3\text{, and finite-}M_f\text{ properties}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The derivative-growth condition is equivalently \[|D^3f(x)[h_1,h_2,h_3]|\le2M_f\prod_{i=1}^3\sqrt{D^2f(x)[h_i,h_i]}\] for every triple of directions.
special_cases_latex: The functions \(e^x\), \(x^{-p}\) on \((0,\infty)\) for \(p>0\), and \(|x|^p\) for \(p>2\) are smooth convex examples identified as lying outside the classical class.
Convex quadratic functions belong to the class with \(M_f=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of one defining condition prevents use of the classical Dikin-radius and Hessian-distortion conclusions without an additional theory.
boundary_notes: Being outside the classical class does not imply that a function is unsuitable for optimization.
Alternative derivative-growth exponents define generalized classes but are not included here.

notation.meaning: Class of classical self-concordant functions under this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Convexity or Regular Smoothness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loss of convexity, third differentiability, or Hessian definiteness makes the classical derivative inequality undefined, nonreal, or geometrically degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical inequality \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\leq 2\bigl(D^2f(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}\] requires \(D^3f(x)\) to exist and \(D^2f(x)[h,h]\geq0\). If convexity is lost, the right-hand side need not be real; if third-order regularity is lost, the left-hand side is undefined. If \(\nabla^2 f(x)\) is singular, \(\|\cdot\|_x\) is only a seminorm and inverse-Hessian constructions fail. Thus classical Dikin and Newton geometry requires the stated analytic hypotheses, even when a weaker notion of self-concordance remains meaningful.
assumptions_latex: Classical local-metric self-concordance is interpreted on an open convex domain with a three-times differentiable convex function.
A genuine local norm requires \(\nabla^2 f(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without these hypotheses, the classical third-derivative inequality or its Hessian-induced geometry is undefined or degenerate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the positive-definite, three-times differentiable classical local-metric theory.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied. The record also blends requirements for the classical derivative inequality with stronger requirements for nondegenerate Dikin and inverse-Hessian geometry: positive-definite Hessians are not required merely to state classical self-concordance, and some conventions permit singular Hessians. An authoritative source is needed to fix the convention and boundary claim.

knowledge_statements.source_title: Loss of Convexity or Regular Smoothness

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) have effective domain \(U\), and consider the classical self-concordance definition on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition identifies exclusion from the classical smooth convex class; it makes no assertion about generalized, weak, or distributional variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A loss-of-convexity or regular-smoothness regime occurs if at least one of the following holds: \[f\text{ is not closed convex};\qquad U\text{ is not open for the smooth restriction};\qquad f|_U\notin C^3(U);\] or there exist \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb E\) with \(D^2f(x)[h,h]<0\). In any such case, \(f\) is not a classical self-concordant function as defined by the Hessian-controlled third-derivative inequality, even if a formal third derivative exists at some points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical analytic setting breaks down when the function is not closed and convex, when its effective domain does not provide an open smooth region, when it lacks three continuous derivatives there, or when its Hessian has a negative direction. Any one of these failures excludes the function from classical self-concordance. This is an exclusion criterion, not a claim that no alternative local theory can apply.

eg\operatorname{ClosedConvex}(f)\ \lor\ U	ext{ not open}\ \lor\ f|_U
otin C^3(U)\ \lor\ \exists(x,h):D^2f(x)[h,h]<0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f

A convex but merely twice differentiable function is outside the classical \(C^3\) definition.

Classical third-derivative and Dikin-ellipsoid formulas cannot be invoked at points where the required derivatives do not exist.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Derivative-Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth convex function lies outside a chosen controlled regime when its normalized third-derivative growth is unbounded, so no finite global class constant exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Classical derivative growth is uncontrolled when \[\sup_{x\in\Omega,\,h
eq0} rac{|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|}{(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}}=+\infty.\] More generally, for a specified exponent \(
u\), the model \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\leq M igl(D^2f(x)[h,h] igr)^{
u/2}\|h\|_2^{3-
u}\] is uncontrolled if its normalized left-hand side is unbounded over \(x\) and nonzero \(h\). In either case no finite global \(M\) certifies membership in that chosen classical or generalized class, despite smoothness and convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(\Omega)\) is convex on an open convex set \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the normalized derivative-growth ratios are unbounded, no finite global constant places \(f\) in the corresponding controlled self-concordant class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic boundary for global classical and parameterized generalized derivative-growth inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of uniform self-concordant derivative control
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subset\mathbb E\) be open and convex, and let \(f\in C^3(U)\) be convex. For directions with positive curvature define the dimensionless ratio \[R_f(x,h)=\frac{|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|}{2(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth convex functions whose third derivative is not uniformly controlled by the classical Hessian scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The uncontrolled derivative-growth regime is defined by the nonexistence of a finite classical self-concordance constant: \[\sup_{\substack{x\in U,\ h\in\mathbb E\\D^2f(x)[h,h]>0}}R_f(x,h)=+\infty,\] or by the existence of \(x,h\) such that \(D^2f(x)[h,h]=0\) but \(D^3f(x)[h,h,h]\ne0\). Equivalently, for every finite \(M\ge0\), there exist \(x\in U\) and \(h\in\mathbb E\) for which \[|D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|>2M(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth convex function is in an uncontrolled derivative-growth regime when no finite constant uniformly bounds its third directional derivative by the three-halves power of its local curvature. This occurs either because the normalized ratio becomes arbitrarily large or because the Hessian vanishes in a direction while the third derivative does not. Such a function lies outside the classical self-concordant class despite retaining convexity and three derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall M<+\infty\ \exists(x,h):\ |D^3f(x)[h,h,h]|>2M(D^2f(x)[h,h])^{3/2}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f\notin\mathrm{SC}\] within the stated smooth convex ambient class.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(D^2f(x)[h,h]>0\) for all nonzero \(h\), uncontrolled growth is equivalent to \(\sup_{x,h\ne0}R_f(x,h)=+\infty\).
special_cases_latex: The univariate functions \(f(x)=e^x\), \(f(x)=x^{-p}\) on \((0,\infty)\) for \(p>0\), and \(f(x)=|x|^p\) for \(p>2\) are cited examples outside classical self-concordance.
immediate_consequences_latex: No uniform positive Dikin radius \(1/M\) follows from classical self-concordance for such a function.
Classical neighboring-Hessian bounds with a global constant \(M\) are unavailable.
boundary_notes: Unbounded classical ratio does not exclude a generalized inequality with another curvature exponent or an additional norm factor.
A large but finite optimal constant still defines a classical self-concordant function.
