knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be self-concordant with constant \(M_f>0\) on an open convex domain \(U\subset\mathbb E\), and assume \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\) at the base point \(x\in U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Local-metric Dikin geometry is the point-dependent primal–dual norm system \[\|h\|_x=\sqrt{\langle H_xh,h\rangle},\qquad \|g\|_{x,*}=\sqrt{\langle g,H_x^{-1}g\rangle},\] together with the intrinsic ellipsoids \[W^0_f(x;r)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x<r\},\qquad W_f(x;r)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x\le r\}.\] The distinguished self-concordant neighborhood has radius \(1/M_f\); its open ellipsoid lies in \(U\). Within any smaller radius \(r<1/M_f\), the Hessian and both local norms at neighboring points are quantitatively comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dikin geometry equips each interior point with the norm generated by the local Hessian and the dual norm generated by its inverse. Balls in this norm are ellipsoids rather than Euclidean spheres. For a self-concordant function with constant \(M_f\), the open ellipsoid of radius \(1/M_f\) is certified to remain in the domain, while smaller ellipsoids are regions in which Hessians and local measurements have controlled distortion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[W_f^0(x;1/M_f)\subseteq U,\qquad (1-M_fr)^2H_x\preccurlyeq H_y\preccurlyeq(1-M_fr)^{-2}H_x\quad\text{if }\|y-x\|_x=r<1/M_f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The primal unit ball is the polar, under the dual pairing, of the dual unit ball: \[\|g\|_{x,*}=\sup_{\|h\|_x\le1}|\langle g,h\rangle|.\]
special_cases_latex: For standard self-concordance, \(M_f=1\), the distinguished Dikin radius is one.
For a quadratic function with constant positive-definite Hessian, the geometry is globally constant and has zero distortion.
immediate_consequences_latex: The construction is invariant under invertible affine changes of coordinates.
Newton directions and decrements are naturally measured in this local norm pair.
boundary_notes: If the Hessian is singular, the primal expression is only a seminorm and the inverse dual norm is undefined without restriction or quotienting.
The certified ellipsoid is open at the limiting radius.

children.title: Primal–Dual Local-Norm Pair
children.top_down_role: Tangent and cotangent measurements induced by local curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal and dual Hessian local norms
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x\) lie in the open domain of a twice differentiable convex function \(f\), and suppose \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x):\mathbb E\to\mathbb E^*\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate finite-dimensional tangent and cotangent measurements at one base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal–dual local-norm pair induced by \(f\) at \(x\) is \[\|h\|_x=\sqrt{\langle H_xh,h\rangle}\quad(h\in\mathbb E),\qquad \|g\|_{x,*}=\sqrt{\langle g,H_x^{-1}g\rangle}\quad(g\in\mathbb E^*).\] These are dual norms under the canonical pairing: \[\|g\|_{x,*}=\sup_{h\ne0}\frac{|\langle g,h\rangle|}{\|h\|_x},\qquad |\langle g,h\rangle|\le\|g\|_{x,*}\|h\|_x.\] The Hessian and inverse Hessian exchange the two measurements isometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an interior point with positive-definite Hessian, tangent directions are measured by the square root of the Hessian quadratic form, and covectors are measured by the inverse-Hessian quadratic form. These are genuine dual norms: their pairing obeys Hölder's inequality with constant one, and each norm is the support-function dual of the other. The Hessian maps a tangent vector to a covector of the same local length.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\|h\|_x=\sup_{\|g\|_{x,*}\le1}|\langle g,h\rangle|,\qquad \|g\|_{x,*}=\sup_{\|h\|_x\le1}|\langle g,h\rangle|.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(H_x=I\) under a Euclidean identification, both local norms are the Euclidean norm.
The Newton decrement is \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_{x,*}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The steepest local linear response to a covector \(g\) is attained in the direction proportional to \(H_x^{-1}g\).
Dikin ellipsoids are precisely balls of the primal local norm.
boundary_notes: Positive semidefiniteness alone gives only a seminorm; the displayed dual norm requires invertibility.
The norms depend on the base point unless the Hessian is constant.

children.title: Primal Local Norm
children.top_down_role: Hessian-induced measurement of directions and displacements.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Local Norm
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal local norm measures a direction using the positive-definite Hessian at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in\Omega\), set \(H_x=\nabla^2 f(x)\). The primal local norm of a tangent direction or displacement \(h\in\mathbb R^n\) is \[\|h\|_x:=\sqrt{h^{\mathsf T}H_xh}.\] Positive definiteness of \(H_x\) makes this a norm; if \(H_x\) is merely positive semidefinite, the same formula defines only a seminorm.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on an open set \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal local norm is \(\|h\|_x=(h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2 f(x)h)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Hessian norm at a point of positive-definite curvature.

children.title: Dual Local Norm
children.top_down_role: Inverse-Hessian measurement of gradients, residuals, and covectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Local Norm
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual local norm measures covectors using the inverse Hessian and is dual to the primal local norm under the standard pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H_x=\nabla^2 f(x)\succ0\), the dual local norm of a covector \(s\) is \[\|s\|_{x,*}:=\sqrt{s^{\mathsf T}H_x^{-1}s}.\] It is the norm dual to \(\|\cdot\|_x\): \[\|s\|_{x,*}=\sup_{h\neq0}\frac{\langle s,h\rangle}{\|h\|_x},\qquad |\langle s,h\rangle|\leq\|s\|_{x,*}\|h\|_x.\]
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses defining the primal local norm hold at \(x\).
A covector \(s\in(\mathbb R^n)^*\) is identified with its coordinate vector under the Euclidean pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual local norm is \(\|s\|_{x,*}=(s^{\mathsf T}[\nabla^2 f(x)]^{-1}s)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-Hessian norm dual to the primal Hessian norm.

children.title: Dikin Ellipsoid Geometry
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic ellipsoidal localization and its relation to the domain boundary.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be twice differentiable on an open convex domain \(U\subset\mathbb E\). At \(x\in U\), assume \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), and let \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoidal localization induced by a nondegenerate Hessian at a fixed interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The open and closed Dikin ellipsoids of \(f\) at \(x\) with radius \(r\) are \[W_f^0(x;r)=\{y\in\mathbb E:\langle H_x(y-x),y-x\rangle<r^2\},\] \[W_f(x;r)=\{y\in\mathbb E:\langle H_x(y-x),y-x\rangle\le r^2\}=\operatorname{cl}W_f^0(x;r).\] Equivalently, they are the open and closed balls \(\|y-x\|_x<r\) and \(\|y-x\|_x\le r\) of the Hessian local norm. For an \(M_f\)-self-concordant function, \(W_f^0(x;1/M_f)\subseteq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Dikin ellipsoid is the ball centered at an interior point in the norm generated by the Hessian at that point. Its axes and radii are determined by the local curvature: high-curvature directions have shorter Euclidean semiaxes and low-curvature directions have longer ones. Classical self-concordance makes the open ellipsoid of radius \(1/M_f\) an intrinsic neighborhood certified to stay inside the function's domain.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under any linear coordinates in which \(H_x=Q^\mathsf{T}Q\), \[W_f(x;r)=\{x+h:\|Qh\|_2\le r\}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(H_x=I\), the Dikin ellipsoid is the Euclidean ball of radius \(r\).
For standard self-concordance, the certified interior radius is one.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dikin ellipsoids transform covariantly under invertible affine coordinate changes.
Their polar centered bodies are the unit balls of the dual local norm, with reciprocal radius.
boundary_notes: The closed limiting ellipsoid \(W_f(x;1/M_f)\) is not generally asserted to lie in the open domain.
With a singular Hessian, the displayed set can be unbounded and is not an ellipsoid in the nondegenerate sense.

children.title: Interior-Containment Principle
children.top_down_role: Certified interior neighborhoods supplied by the local metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Containment Principle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard self-concordant barrier, every point at local distance less than one from an interior base point remains inside the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the open unit Dikin ellipsoid at \(x\) by \[E_x:=\{x+h:h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)h<1\}.\] Then \[E_x\subseteq\Omega.\] Thus every displacement whose local norm at \(x\) is strictly below one is certified to remain in the barrier domain. The barrier and maximal-domain hypotheses exclude artificial restrictions of an otherwise self-concordant function.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a standard self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\subseteq\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit Dikin containment for a standard self-concordant barrier.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be self-concordant with constant \(M_f>0\) on its open domain \(U\), and let \(x\in U\). The Hessian may be positive semidefinite; \(\|h\|_x=\sqrt{D^2f(x)[h,h]}\) is then a seminorm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical self-concordant domain containment at the sharp open local radius supplied by the standard theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The interior-containment property is \[W_f^0(x;1/M_f)=\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1/M_f\}\subseteq U\qquad\forall x\in U.\] Equivalently, every direction \(h\) satisfying \(M_f\|h\|_x<1\) generates a feasible endpoint \(x+h\in U\); indeed, the whole segment \(x+th\) for \(0\le t\le1\) lies in the same certified interior neighborhood. This property makes the local Hessian a domain-feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every point of a classical self-concordant domain, any displacement whose local Hessian length is strictly less than \(1/M_f\) remains in the domain. Thus the open Dikin ellipsoid at that radius is an automatically feasible neighborhood. The assertion uses a strict inequality: a point at exactly the limiting local radius can lie on the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M_f\|h\|_x<1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x+h\in U.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every nonzero direction \(h\), the maximal feasible forward distance satisfies \[\sup\{t\ge0:x+\tau h\in U\text{ for }0\le\tau<t\}\ge\frac{1}{M_f\|h\|_x}.\]
special_cases_latex: For standard self-concordance, \(\|h\|_x<1\) guarantees \(x+h\in U\).
If \(M_f=0\), the convention suggested by the theorem is an infinite certified radius, consistent with globally defined quadratic-affine examples.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full Newton step is domain-feasible whenever its local norm is strictly below \(1/M_f\).
The local metric gives a lower bound on directional distance to the domain boundary.
boundary_notes: Containment is guaranteed for the open, not necessarily the closed, limiting ellipsoid.
The property alone does not state that every point outside the ellipsoid is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Dikin-certified interior containment

children.title: Intrinsic Boundary-Distance Geometry
children.top_down_role: Relationship between local radius and approach to the domain boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Boundary-Distance Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the Hessian metric frozen at an interior point, the domain boundary is at least one local unit away.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\Omega\), define the boundary distance in the frozen Hessian metric by \[\delta_x:=\inf_{z\in\partial\Omega}\sqrt{(z-x)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)(z-x)}.\] Unit Dikin containment implies \[\delta_x\geq1.\] Equivalently, no boundary point can be reached from \(x\) by a displacement of local norm strictly smaller than one.
assumptions_latex: The boundary-distance infimum is taken over the Euclidean boundary \(\partial\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{z\in\partial\Omega}\|z-x\|_x\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separation measured in the frozen local metric at an interior point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional boundary distance in the local metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\) be the open domain of an \(M_f\)-self-concordant function, let \(x\in U\), and let \(h\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided intrinsic distance to the boundary measured along rays and normalized by the Hessian at the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the forward directional boundary distance by \[\rho_U(x;h)=\sup\{t\ge0:x+\tau h\in U\text{ for every }0\le\tau<t\}\in(0,+\infty].\] Its dimensionless local-metric form is \[d_f(x;h)=\rho_U(x;h)\|h\|_x.\] Classical self-concordance implies \[d_f(x;h)\ge\frac1{M_f},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \rho_U(x;h)\ge\frac1{M_f\|h\|_x},\] whenever \(\|h\|_x>0\). Thus the local Dikin radius is a direction-uniform lower bound on the normalized distance from \(x\) to the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional boundary distance is the largest distance one may travel from \(x\) along a ray while remaining in the domain. Multiplying it by the local Hessian length of the direction removes the arbitrary scaling of that direction. For an \(M_f\)-self-concordant function, this normalized distance is at least \(1/M_f\) in every curved direction, because the corresponding open Dikin ellipsoid is contained in the domain.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The largest centered local-norm ball certified solely by self-concordance has radius at least \(1/M_f\).
special_cases_latex: If the forward ray never meets the boundary, then \(\rho_U(x;h)=+\infty\).
For standard self-concordance, every curved direction has normalized boundary distance at least one.
immediate_consequences_latex: A boundary point reachable along \(h\) cannot occur at parameter \(t<1/(M_f\|h\|_x)\).
The quantity \(d_f(x;h)\) is unchanged when \(h\) is replaced by a positive scalar multiple.
boundary_notes: The lower bound need not be an equality; the domain may extend much farther than the Dikin radius.
If \(\|h\|_x=0\), the normalized formula with division is not used; nondegeneracy follows under the additional assumption that the domain contains no complete line.

notation.meaning: Forward ray distance to the boundary.
Boundary distance normalized by the local norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Dikin Geometry on Affine Slices
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an affine equality slice, the Hessian restricted to feasible directions defines a Dikin ellipsoid that remains inside the sliced domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The restriction \(F|_{L\cap\Omega}\) is self-concordant on its relative-open domain. Its Hessian quadratic form on the tangent space \(T=\ker A\) is \(h\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)h\). Consequently, its unit Dikin ellipsoid is \[E_x^L:=\{x+h:h\in T,\ h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)h<1\},\] and it satisfies \[E_x^L\subseteq L\cap\Omega.\]
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a standard self-concordant barrier on \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(L=x_0+\ker A\) is an affine subspace meeting \(\Omega\), and \(x\in L\cap\Omega\).
The Hessian is positive definite on the tangent space \(T=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x+h:h\in T,\ h^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)h<1\}\subseteq L\cap\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of Dikin containment to equality-constrained tangent directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Dikin geometry on an affine feasible set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be \(M_f\)-self-concordant on \(U\subset\mathbb E\). Let \(L=x_0+V\) be an affine subspace with direction space \(V\), assume \(U_L=U\cap L\ne\varnothing\), and define the restriction \(f_L=f|_{U_L}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained restriction to the relative interior of an affine slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Dikin geometry on the affine slice \(L\) is generated by the restricted quadratic form \[\|h\|_{x,L}=\sqrt{\langle\nabla^2f(x)h,h\rangle},\qquad h\in V,\ x\in U_L.\] Its open ellipsoid is \[W^0_{f,L}(x;r)=\{x+h:h\in V,\ \|h\|_{x,L}<r\}=W_f^0(x;r)\cap L.\] The affine restriction \(f_L\) is self-concordant with the same admissible constant \(M_f\), and therefore \[W^0_{f,L}(x;1/M_f)\subseteq U_L.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality-constrained problem, the local metric is obtained by restricting the ambient Hessian quadratic form to feasible directions. The resulting Dikin ellipsoid is exactly the intersection of the ambient ellipsoid with the affine feasible set. Affine invariance of self-concordance preserves the constant, so the sliced open ellipsoid of radius \(1/M_f\) is contained in the relative interior of the sliced domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[W^0_{f_L}(x;r)=W_f^0(x;r)\cap L,
\qquad W^0_{f_L}(x;1/M_f)\subseteq U\cap L.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(P:\mathbb F\to\mathbb E\) parametrizes \(L\) injectively by \(z\mapsto x_0+Pz\), then the sliced Hessian is \[\nabla^2(f\circ(x_0+P\cdot))(z)=P^*\nabla^2f(x_0+Pz)P.\]
special_cases_latex: For linear equalities \(Ax=b\), the feasible direction space is \(V=\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Equality constraints preserve the intrinsic containment certificate along feasible directions.
If the ambient Hessian is positive definite, its restriction is positive definite on every nonzero feasible direction.
boundary_notes: The domain on \(L\) is interpreted in the relative topology of \(L\).
A noninjective parametrization produces a degenerate coordinate Hessian and should be quotiented by its kernel.

notation.meaning: Direction space of the affine slice.

children.title: Local Distortion Theorem Families
children.top_down_role: Comparison principles for curvature and local norms at neighboring interior points.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be \(M_f\)-self-concordant on \(U\), let \(x,y\in U\), and put \(r=\|y-x\|_x<1/M_f\). Assume the relevant Hessians are positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighboring-point comparison inequalities inside a strict Dikin neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local distortion family consists of the mutually compatible comparisons \[(1-M_fr)^2H_x\preccurlyeq H_y\preccurlyeq(1-M_fr)^{-2}H_x,\] \[(1-M_fr)\|h\|_x\le\|h\|_y\le(1-M_fr)^{-1}\|h\|_x\quad\forall h\in\mathbb E,\] and \[(1-M_fr)\|g\|_{x,*}\le\|g\|_{y,*}\le(1-M_fr)^{-1}\|g\|_{x,*}\quad\forall g\in\mathbb E^*.\] These inequalities define controlled transport of curvature, tangent lengths, and cotangent lengths between neighboring Dikin points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within local distance \(r<1/M_f\), self-concordance bounds how much the Hessian metric can change. The Hessian at \(y\) lies spectrally between factors \((1-M_fr)^2\) and \((1-M_fr)^{-2}\) of the Hessian at \(x\). Taking quadratic-form square roots gives the corresponding tangent-norm bounds, while inversion gives the same two-sided factors for dual norms in reversed operator order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\max\left\{\frac{\|h\|_y}{\|h\|_x},\frac{\|h\|_x}{\|h\|_y},\frac{\|g\|_{y,*}}{\|g\|_{x,*}},\frac{\|g\|_{x,*}}{\|g\|_{y,*}}\right\}\le(1-M_fr)^{-1}\] whenever the displayed denominators are nonzero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The eigenvalues of \(H_x^{-1/2}H_yH_x^{-1/2}\) lie in \([(1-M_fr)^2,(1-M_fr)^{-2}]\).
special_cases_latex: For \(M_f=1\), the distortion factors are \(1-r\) and \((1-r)^{-1}\).
For a quadratic function, \(M_f=0\) is admissible and the distortion factor is one.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local metric topology agrees at all neighboring interior points.
Linear systems formed with nearby Hessians are spectrally preconditioned by the base Hessian.
boundary_notes: The upper factor diverges as \(M_fr\uparrow1\).
The theorem supplies a local comparison and does not imply a uniform global Hessian bound over an unbounded domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Norm Transport Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent vector's local norm at a nearby point differs from its original norm by at most factors of one minus the local displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=\|y-x\|_x<1\). For every tangent vector \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), the primal local norms satisfy \[(1-r)\|h\|_x\leq\|h\|_y\leq\frac{1}{1-r}\|h\|_x.\] These inequalities follow by evaluating the local Hessian comparison on \(h\) and taking nonnegative square roots.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent vector can be measured at either of two neighboring interior points. If their base-point local distance is \(r<1/M_f\), its two lengths differ by at most the factor \((1-M_fr)^{-1}\). For constant Hessian geometry, \(\|h\|_x=\|h\|_y\) for all \(x,y,h\).

The norms induce the same local topology and have uniformly equivalent unit balls.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Norm Transport Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covector's inverse-Hessian norm at a nearby point obeys the same local distortion factors as the primal norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r=\|y-x\|_x<1\). Inverting the positive-definite Hessian comparison reverses the Loewner inequalities and gives \[(1-r)^2[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}\preceq[
abla^2f(y)]^{-1}\preceq(1-r)^{-2}[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}.\] Therefore every covector \(s\) satisfies \[(1-r)\|s\|_{x,*}\leq\|s\|_{y,*}\leq rac{1}{1-r}\|s\|_{x,*}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual local-norm transport inside a Dikin neighborhood
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a standard self-concordant convex function on an open convex set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). Define \(\|u\|_x=(u^TH_xu)^{1/2}\) and \(\|g\|_x^*=(g^TH_x^{-1}g)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, standard self-concordant geometry with positive-definite Hessian; transport is local and uses the base-point distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y\in D\), put \(r=\|y-x\|_x\). The dual-norm transport family is the collection of inequalities
\[
(1-r)\|g\|_x^*\leq \|g\|_y^*\leq \frac{1}{1-r}\|g\|_x^*,\qquad g\in(\mathbb R^n)^*,\quad 0\leq r<1.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
(1-r)^2H_x\preceq H_y\preceq(1-r)^{-2}H_x
\]
induces the stated comparison after inversion and evaluation on covectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any two points \(x,y\) whose base-point distance \(r=\|y-x\|_x\) is less than one, every covector has comparable dual local norms at the two points: \((1-r)\|g\|_x^*\leq\|g\|_y^*\leq(1-r)^{-1}\|g\|_x^*\). Thus cotangent measurements distort by at most the reciprocal factor \((1-r)^{-1}\) within the open unit Dikin neighborhood.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[(1-r)^2H_x\preceq H_y\preceq(1-r)^{-2}H_x.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(g=\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(x)\), the relation compares the same gradient displacement in the two endpoint metrics.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(r\leq\rho<1\), then the identity map between the two cotangent normed spaces is uniformly bounded in both directions by \((1-\rho)^{-1}\).
boundary_notes: The factors diverge as \(r\uparrow1\); this statement supplies no finite comparison at or beyond the unit boundary.
If \(H_x\) is singular, the inverse-Hessian dual norm is not defined on all covectors without quotient-space or pseudoinverse conventions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a standard self-concordant convex function with \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). For \(x,y\in D\), write \(h=y-x\) and \(r=\|h\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition packages the canonical zeroth-, first-, and second-order local residuals; their quantitative envelopes apply in the standard finite-dimensional regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The local-model theorem family at \((x,y)\) is the ordered residual package
\[
\mathfrak M_f(x,y)=\bigl(R_0(x;h),R_1(x;h),R_2(x;h)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
R_0=f(x+h)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle,
\]
\[
R_1=\nabla f(x+h)-\nabla f(x)-H_xh,
\]
and
\[
R_2=H_x^{-1/2}H_{x+h}H_x^{-1/2}-I.
\]
Its canonical intrinsic controls are expressed solely through \(r\): \(R_0\) lies between \(\omega(r)\) and \(\omega_*(r)\), \(R_1\) is measured in \(\|\cdot\|_x^*\), and \(R_2\) is measured in operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local-model family is the ordered collection of the error in the affine function model, the error in the linear gradient model, and the normalized change of Hessian. Each residual is defined at a base point \(x\) and displacement \(h=y-x\), and each is controlled intrinsically by the single scalar \(r=\|h\|_x\), rather than by a fixed Euclidean Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\mathfrak M_f(x,y)=\left(f(y)-f(x)-\langle
abla f(x),y-xangle,\ 
abla f(y)-
abla f(x)-H_x(y-x),\ H_x^{-1/2}H_yH_x^{-1/2}-Iight).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The package may equivalently be indexed by \((x,h)\) with \(x+h\in D\), since \(y=x+h\).
special_cases_latex: For a positive-definite quadratic function, \(R_1=0\), \(R_2=0\), and \(R_0=\tfrac12\|h\|_x^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine changes of coordinates preserve the scalar \(r\) and the intrinsic meaning of all three residual measurements.
boundary_notes: The upper growth envelope, gradient-remainder bound, and two-sided Hessian comparison require \(r<1\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be standard self-concordant, let \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\), and choose \(h\) with \(x+h\in D\) and \(r=\|h\|_x<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order gradient-model error measured in the dual norm at the expansion point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the gradient remainder
\[
\mathcal R_{\nabla f}(x;h)=\nabla f(x+h)-\nabla f(x)-H_xh.
\]
The canonical gradient-remainder family consists of the intrinsic bounds
\[
\|\mathcal R_{\nabla f}(x;h)\|_x^*\leq \frac{r^2}{1-r},\qquad r=\|h\|_x<1.
\]
Equivalently, the complete gradient displacement satisfies
\[
\|\nabla f(x+h)-\nabla f(x)\|_x^*\leq\frac{r}{1-r}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient remainder is the difference between the true gradient at \(x+h\) and its linear prediction \(\nabla f(x)+H_xh\). For a displacement of local length \(r<1\), its dual local norm is at most \(r^2/(1-r)\). Consequently the gradient model has second-order error for small \(r\), with deterioration as the unit Dikin boundary is approached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|\nabla f(x+h)-\nabla f(x)-H_xh\|_x^*\leq\frac{\|h\|_x^2}{1-\|h\|_x}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal R_{\nabla f}(x;h)=\left(\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x+th)\,dt-H_x\right)h.\]
special_cases_latex: For quadratic \(f\), the Hessian is constant and \(\mathcal R_{\nabla f}(x;h)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: On every fixed neighborhood \(r\leq\rho<1\), the normalized remainder obeys \(\|\mathcal R_{\nabla f}(x;h)\|_x^*\leq r^2/(1-\rho)\).
boundary_notes: No finite bound of this form is asserted for \(r\geq1\).
The remainder is measured at \(x\); transporting it to the metric at \(x+h\) introduces additional distortion factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Remainder Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed standard self-concordant function, a displacement of local norm less than one remains in the domain, and the new Hessian is bounded above and below by explicit multiples of the base Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y=x+h\), one has \(y\in D\) and
\[
(1-r)^2H_x\preceq\nabla^2f(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}H_x.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\bigl\|H_x^{-1/2}\bigl(\nabla^2f(y)-H_x\bigr)H_x^{-1/2}\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le (1-r)^{-2}-1.
\]
Hence the local quadratic metrics remain uniformly comparable throughout each strict unit Dikin neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, convex, and standard self-concordant on \(D=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+h\in D\) and \((1-r)^2H_x\preceq\nabla^2f(x+h)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}H_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided Hessian comparison and normalized Hessian-remainder control; closedness prevents artificial domain restriction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be standard self-concordant with \(H_x\succ0\). For \(y=x+h\in D\), set \(r=\|h\|_x<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order metric distortion within the open unit Dikin neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the normalized Hessian remainder by
\[
\mathcal R_H(x,y)=H_x^{-1/2}H_yH_x^{-1/2}-I.
\]
The Hessian-remainder family is characterized by
\[
(1-r)^2I\preceq I+\mathcal R_H(x,y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}I.
\]
In particular,
\[
\|\mathcal R_H(x,y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq(1-r)^{-2}-1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian remainder is the change from \(H_x\) to \(H_y\), normalized by the base Hessian so that it is coordinate-free. If \(y\) has local distance \(r<1\) from \(x\), every eigenvalue of the relative Hessian lies between \((1-r)^2\) and \((1-r)^{-2}\). Its operator-norm deviation from the identity is therefore at most \((1-r)^{-2}-1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[(1-r)^2H_x\preceq H_y\preceq(1-r)^{-2}H_x.\]
special_cases_latex: When \(H_y=H_x\), the normalized remainder vanishes.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(r\leq\rho<1\), the condition number of the relative Hessian is at most \((1-\rho)^{-4}\).
boundary_notes: The estimate is relative, not an absolute Euclidean Hessian-Lipschitz bound.
The upper factor becomes singular as \(r\uparrow1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed standard self-concordant function, a displacement of local norm less than one remains in the domain, and the affine-model error lies between the canonical omega and omega-star growth envelopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure boundary for local self-concordant geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be self-concordant, and let the local metric at \(x\in D\) be induced by \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\) whenever \(H_x\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This record identifies where the standard inverse-Hessian metric or unit-radius comparison formulas cease to be defined or controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The geometry-failure boundary is the set of metric-point pairs
\[
\mathcal B_f=\{(x,y)\in D\times D:H_x\not\succ0\}\cup\{(x,y)\in D\times D:H_x\succ0,\ \|y-x\|_x\geq1\}.
\]
The first component is the degeneracy boundary of the primal–dual metric. The second is the localization boundary at which estimates containing \((1-\|y-x\|_x)^{-1}\) no longer provide finite control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pair belongs to the geometry-failure boundary when either the Hessian at the base point is not positive definite, so the full dual local norm is unavailable, or the target lies at local distance at least one, so the canonical unit-neighborhood comparison factors are no longer finite. This definition marks failure of the standard local theorem package, not necessarily failure of domain membership or smoothness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal B_f=\{H_x\not\succ0\}\cup\{H_x\succ0,\ \|y-x\|_x\geq1\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Outside \(\mathcal B_f\), the base Hessian is invertible and \(0\leq\|y-x\|_x<1\), so the standard local comparison package is well posed.
special_cases_latex: If \(D\) contains no affine line, self-concordance implies \(H_x\succ0\), leaving only the unit-radius component.
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal B_f\) prevents direct use of the usual upper Hessian, norm-transport, and upper growth bounds based at \(x\).
boundary_notes: A point with local distance at least one may still lie in \(D\); the definition concerns loss of the canonical estimates, not automatic infeasibility.
Degenerate Hessians can be treated on quotient spaces, but that variant is excluded here.

notation.meaning: Geometry-failure boundary in the pair space \(D\times D\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Neighborhood Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed standard self-concordant function, the open unit Dikin ellipsoid is contained in the domain, but its radius-one boundary may meet the domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Self-concordance and closedness guarantee
\[
\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\subset D.
\]
The strict inequality is sharp. For \(f(t)=-\log t\) on \(D=(0,\infty)\), one has \(\|h\|_x=|h|/x\). Taking \(h=-x\) gives \(\|h\|_x=1\), while \(x+h=0\notin D\). Thus closed unit Dikin containment and comparison at radius one cannot be asserted in general.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, convex, and standard self-concordant on \(D=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\subset D\), but replacing \(<1\) by \(\le1\) is invalid in general.

The open unit neighborhood and its boundary are
\[
W^0(x;1)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x<1\},\qquad \partial W(x;1)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x=1\}.
\]
Self-concordance guarantees
\[
W^0(x;1)\subseteq D.
\]
The sphere \(\partial W(x;1)\) is the canonical threshold at which denominators \(1-\|y-x\|_x\) in local upper-comparison formulas vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit neighborhood at \(x\) is the open ellipsoid of points whose displacement has local norm less than one. Its unit-neighborhood boundary is the corresponding local-norm sphere. The entire open ellipsoid lies in the domain of a standard self-concordant function, while the boundary is the limiting radius for the canonical upper metric and growth estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[W^0(x;1)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x<1\}\subseteq D,\qquad \partial W(x;1)=\{y:\|y-x\|_x=1\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\partial W(x;1)=\{x+h:h^TH_xh=1\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=-\sum_i\ln x_i\) on the positive orthant, the unit neighborhood is the Hessian ellipsoid centered at the positive point \(x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every step \(h\) with \(\|h\|_x<1\) remains in the domain.
The closed unit ellipsoid need not be contained in the open domain.
boundary_notes: Containment is guaranteed for the open ellipsoid; equality-radius points require separate domain verification.
For self-concordance constant \(M_f\), the canonical guaranteed radius is \(1/M_f\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession rays and centered local geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty open convex domain, set \(C=\operatorname{cl}D\), and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex recession geometry coupled to a self-concordant local metric; it distinguishes unbounded rays from bounded centered ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The recession geometry of \(D\) is the cone
\[
\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:x+td\in C\ \text{for every }x\in C,\ t\geq0\}.
\]
For a base point \(x\in D\) with \(H_x\succ0\), its centered Dikin ellipsoids are
\[
W(x;r)=\{x+h:\|h\|_x\leq r\}.
\]
Thus \(d\neq0\) in \(\operatorname{rec}(C)\) generates an unbounded feasible ray, whereas each finite-radius \(W(x;r)\) is bounded. For a self-concordant barrier and a recession direction \(d\), the raywise local geometry obeys
\[
\|d\|_x\leq-\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession geometry is the cone of directions that can be followed indefinitely without leaving the closure of the domain. A nonzero recession direction produces an unbounded ray, while any Dikin ellipsoid of finite radius around a point with positive-definite Hessian is bounded. For a self-concordant barrier, the local length of a recession direction is controlled by the negative directional derivative, showing why centered ellipsoids do not describe the whole unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d:x+td\in C\ \forall x\in C,\ \forall t\geq0\},\qquad d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\Rightarrow\|d\|_x\leq-\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For closed convex \(C\), it suffices that \(x_0+td\in C\) for one \(x_0\in C\) and every \(t\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: A nonempty closed convex set is unbounded exactly when its recession cone contains a nonzero direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: No bounded, centered ellipsoid can cover a domain having a nonzero recession direction.
boundary_notes: The barrier inequality requires the barrier form of self-concordance; a general self-concordant function needs the additional hypotheses in the recession-direction theorem.
Recession directions describe asymptotic domain geometry, not membership in a fixed unit Dikin neighborhood.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the closed convex set \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Domain Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex set is unbounded exactly when it has a nonzero recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The recession cone \(\operatorname{rec}C\) is a closed convex cone. In finite dimension,
\[
C\text{ is unbounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rec}C\ne\{0\}.
\]
Consequently, an unbounded closed convex domain possesses a nonzero direction along which every ray starting in the domain remains in the domain. Applied to an open convex domain, this statement concerns its closed convex closure.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is unbounded if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}C\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional characterization of unbounded closed convex geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Directions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recession direction is a vector whose nonnegative ray remains feasible from every point of the convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is a recession direction of \(C\) when
\[
x+td\in C\qquad\text{for every }x\in C\text{ and every }t\ge0.
\]
The set of all such vectors is the recession cone \(\operatorname{rec}C\). If \(C\) is closed, it suffices to verify the ray condition from one point \(x_0\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in\operatorname{rec}C\) exactly when \(x+td\in C\) for every \(x\in C\) and \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain recession directions in finite-dimensional convex geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Dikin Ellipsoid Escape Behavior
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the positive ray, fixed Dikin radius corresponds to Euclidean radius proportional to the center, so ellipsoids escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard self-concordant logarithmic barrier, \(f''(x)=x^{-2}\), hence \(\|h\|_x=|h|/x\) and
\[
E_x(r)=\bigl((1-r)x,(1+r)x\bigr).
\]
Although every \(E_x(r)\) with \(r<1\) lies in \(D\), its Euclidean radius is \(rx\), which tends to infinity along the recession direction \(d=1\). Therefore intrinsic containment gives no center-independent Euclidean localization on unbounded domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_x(r)=((1-r)x,(1+r)x)\), whose Euclidean radius \(rx\) diverges as \(x\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escape of fixed-radius Dikin neighborhoods along an unbounded domain.

notation.meaning: Local norm for the logarithmic barrier

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Free Geometric Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional convex domain is recession-free exactly when it is bounded, which prevents Dikin neighborhoods from escaping along rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The recession-free condition is
\[
\operatorname{rec}(\overline D)=\{0\}.
\]
Because \(\overline D\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in finite dimension, this condition holds exactly when \(\overline D\), equivalently \(D\), is bounded. Hence every Dikin ellipsoid contained in \(D\) is also confined to one bounded Euclidean set; escape along a nonzero recession ray is excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{0\}\) if and only if \(D\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional criterion excluding geometric escape along recession rays.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and convex, and let \(x\in D\) satisfy \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior unconstrained local quadratic geometry; constrained variants replace the full space by a feasible tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton decrement datum at \(x\) is the quadratic local model
\[
q_x(h)=f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\tfrac12\langle H_xh,h\rangle,
\]
together with its minimizer
\[
n_x=\arg\min_h q_x(h)=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)
\]
and scalar decrement
\[
\lambda_f(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*=\sqrt{-\langle\nabla f(x),n_x\rangle}.
\]
The predicted model decrease is \(f(x)-\min_hq_x(h)=\lambda_f(x)^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton decrement theory begins with the Hessian quadratic model at an interior point. The Newton direction is the unique minimizer of that model, and the decrement is simultaneously the local norm of this direction, the dual local norm of the gradient, and the square root of the negative directional derivative. One half of its square is the decrease predicted by the quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[n_x=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x),\qquad \lambda_f(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*,\qquad f(x)-\min_hq_x(h)=\tfrac12\lambda_f(x)^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex:
\[\lambda_f(x)^2=
abla f(x)^TH_x^{-1}
abla f(x)=-
abla f(x)^Tn_x=n_x^TH_xn_x.\]
special_cases_latex: For an exactly quadratic objective, \(x+n_x\) is the unconstrained minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: The decrement is invariant under nonsingular affine changes of coordinates.
The condition \(\lambda_f(x)=0\) is equivalent to first-order stationarity.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness of \(H_x\) is required for the unique full-space direction and inverse-Hessian formula.
The model decrease is a local quadratic prediction; objective-gap certification requires additional self-concordance hypotheses.

children.title: Newton Direction-Decrement Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-free Newton geometry expressed through the local metric.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_x\succ0\) induce primal and dual local norms, and put \(g_x=\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-free unconstrained correspondence between a cotangent residual and its metric-dual Newton displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton direction–decrement correspondence is the metric-duality relation
\[
H_xn_x=-g_x,
\]
with
\[
\lambda_f(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|g_x\|_x^*=\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{-\langle g_x,v\rangle}{\|v\|_x}.
\]
The supremum is attained by every positive multiple of \(n_x\), and
\[
\langle g_x,n_x\rangle=-\lambda_f(x)^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local Hessian identifies the gradient covector with the negative Newton displacement. Under this identification, the decrement is both the primal size of the displacement and the dual size of the gradient. It is also the largest normalized descent slope, attained in the Newton direction, and its square is the magnitude of the directional derivative along that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H_xn_x=-g_x,\qquad \|n_x\|_x=\|g_x\|_x^*=\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{-\langle g_x,v\rangle}{\|v\|_x},\qquad \langle g_x,n_x\rangle=-\lambda_f(x)^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[n_x=\arg\min_v\{\langle g_x,v\rangle+\tfrac12\|v\|_x^2\}.\]
\[\lambda_f(x)^2=\langle g_x,H_x^{-1}g_x\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(g_x=0\), then \(n_x=0\) and \(\lambda_f(x)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The Newton direction is a strict descent direction whenever \(\lambda_f(x)>0\).
boundary_notes: The full-space correspondence requires \(H_x\) to be invertible.
On an affine feasible set, the supremum and minimization are restricted to feasible tangent directions.

notation.meaning: Metric-dual negative gradient, i.e. Newton direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Newton Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton direction minimizes the local quadratic model, and its local Hessian norm equals the dual local norm of the gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconstrained Newton direction is the unique minimizer
\[
n_x=\mathop{\arg\min}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle+\tfrac12d^\top H_xd\right\}=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x).
\]
Its intrinsic length is the Newton decrement:
\[
\lambda(x)=\sqrt{n_x^\top H_xn_x}=\sqrt{\nabla f(x)^\top H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)}.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is twice differentiable on open \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n_x=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) and \(\lambda(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite unconstrained Newton direction and its intrinsic length.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(x\in D\) have \(H_x\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space Newton geometry without equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconstrained Newton geometry at \(x\) is the triple
\[
\left(n_x,\lambda_f(x),x^+\right)
=\left(-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x),\ \sqrt{\nabla f(x)^TH_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)},\ x-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)\right).
\]
The direction solves \(H_xn_x=-\nabla f(x)\), and the full Newton point is \(x^+=x+n_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an unconstrained interior point, the Newton direction is obtained by applying the inverse Hessian to the negative gradient. The decrement is the inverse-Hessian norm of the gradient, and the full Newton point is the current point plus that direction. All directions in \(\mathbb R^n\) are admissible in the local quadratic model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[n_x=\arg\min_{h\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\tfrac12h^TH_xh\right\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex quadratic function, one full Newton update reaches the unique minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\nabla f(x)^Tn_x=-\lambda_f(x)^2\), so every nonzero Newton direction is a descent direction.
boundary_notes: The full step \(x^+\) need not lie in \(D\); self-concordant step-size rules or line search address feasibility.
If the Hessian is singular, this definition must be replaced by a restricted or generalized-inverse construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Constrained Newton Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine-constrained Newton direction minimizes the quadratic model over feasible tangent directions; its Hessian norm defines the restricted decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine-feasible Newton direction is
\[
n_x=\mathop{\arg\min}_{Ad=0}\left\{\nabla f(x)^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top H_xd\right\}.
\]
It is uniquely characterized with a multiplier \(\nu\) by
\[
H_xn_x+\nabla f(x)+A^\top\nu=0,\qquad An_x=0.
\]
The restricted decrement satisfies
\[
\lambda_A(x)^2=n_x^\top H_xn_x=-\nabla f(x)^\top n_x.
\]
assumptions_latex: The feasible affine set is \(\{z:Az=b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(Ax=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(H_xn_x+
abla f(x)+A^	op
u=0\), \(An_x=0\), and \(\lambda_A(x)^2=n_x^	op H_xn_x=-
abla f(x)^	op n_x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton geometry on an affine feasible set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable, let \(Ax=b\), and fix a feasible \(x\in D\). Assume the equality-constrained quadratic model has a unique solution, equivalently that the relevant KKT matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-start equality-constrained Newton geometry with tangent space \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine-constrained Newton direction \(n_x^A\) and multiplier \(w_x\) are defined by
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H_x&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}n_x^A\\w_x\end{bmatrix}
=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla f(x)\\0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
n_x^A=\arg\min_{h:Ah=0}\left\{\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\tfrac12h^TH_xh\right\}.
\]
The constrained decrement is
\[
\lambda_A(x)=\|n_x^A\|_x,
\]
and \(x+n_x^A\) remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible point under affine equalities, the Newton direction minimizes the quadratic model only over tangent directions satisfying \(Ah=0\). It is equivalently the primal component of the KKT linear system. Its local norm is the constrained Newton decrement, and adding it to the current point preserves feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H_xn_x^A+A^Tw_x=-\nabla f(x),\qquad An_x^A=0,\qquad \lambda_A(x)=\sqrt{(n_x^A)^TH_xn_x^A}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[f(x)-\inf_{h:Ah=0}q_x(h)=\tfrac12\lambda_A(x)^2.\]
special_cases_latex: When \(A\) has no rows, the construction reduces to unconstrained Newton geometry.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\nabla f(x)^Tn_x^A=-\lambda_A(x)^2\); hence a nonzero constrained Newton direction is feasible and descending.
boundary_notes: The definition assumes the current point is feasible.
Redundant constraints are allowed only when the KKT system or an equivalent reduced-space system remains well posed.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Direction Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After normalization, the Newton direction is the direction of steepest decrease in the Hessian-induced unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normalized Newton direction solves the local steepest-descent problem
\[
\frac{n}{\lambda}=\mathop{\arg\min}_{\|d\|_x\le1}g^\top d.
\]
Its minimum value is \(-\lambda\). Thus the Newton direction is the negative Riesz representative of the gradient under the Hessian inner product, scaled in magnitude so that \(\|n\|_x=\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n/\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|d\|_x\le1}g^\top d\), where \(n=-H^{-1}g\) and \(\lambda=\sqrt{g^\top H^{-1}g}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton direction as steepest descent in the local Hessian metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Decrement Measure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton decrement is the gradient’s dual Hessian norm, equal to the Newton step’s local norm and twice the predicted decrease’s square root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton decrement is the local dual norm of the gradient:
\[
\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*=\sqrt{\nabla f(x)^\top H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)}.
\]
If \(n_x=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)\), then \(\lambda(x)=\|n_x\|_x\) and
\[
q_x(0)-q_x(n_x)=\tfrac12\lambda(x)^2.
\]
Thus it measures both local first-order nonstationarity and the quadratic model’s predicted improvement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic gradient magnitude and quadratic-model decrease at an unconstrained point.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction–Decrement Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton decrement is simultaneously the local norm of the Newton direction and the dual local norm of the gradient; its square is the predicted linear decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_x=\nabla f(x)\) and \(H_x=\nabla^2f(x)\). The Newton direction \(n_x=-H_x^{-1}g_x\) satisfies \[\|n_x\|_x^2=n_x^\top H_xn_x=g_x^\top H_x^{-1}g_x=\|g_x\|_{x,*}^2.\] Consequently the Newton decrement has equivalent direction and gradient representations, \(\lambda(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|g_x\|_{x,*}\), and the directional derivative obeys \(g_x^\top n_x=-\lambda(x)^2\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is convex and twice differentiable on an open convex set \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(x)=\|n_x\|_x=\|\nabla f(x)\|_{x,*}\) and \(\nabla f(x)^\top n_x=-\lambda(x)^2\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate family induced by the Newton decrement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be strictly convex and standard self-concordant with \(H_x\succ0\), and define \(\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic local certificates in the controlled regime \(\lambda(x)<1\), assuming the minimizer exists or under hypotheses that guarantee its existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton-decrement certificate family at \(x\) is the collection
\[
\mathcal C(x)=\left(\lambda(x),\ \frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)},\ \omega_*(\lambda(x))\right),\qquad \lambda(x)<1.
\]
Its components certify, respectively, local stationarity and Newton-step size, the solution-distance bound
\[
\|x-x^*\|_x\leq\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)},
\]
and the objective-gap bound
\[
f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\omega_*(\lambda(x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the decrement is below one, it generates a family of intrinsic certificates. The decrement itself measures the gradient residual and Newton displacement; the transformed value \(\lambda/(1-\lambda)\) bounds the local distance to the minimizer; and \(\omega_*(\lambda)\) bounds objective suboptimality. These quantities are affine invariant and require no external Euclidean conditioning constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda(x)<1\Longrightarrow \|x-x^*\|_x\leq\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)},\qquad f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\omega_*(\lambda(x)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For self-concordance constant \(M_f\), replace \(\lambda\) by \(M_f\lambda\) and scale distances and gaps by \(M_f^{-1}\) and \(M_f^{-2}\), respectively.
special_cases_latex: At \(\lambda(x)=0\), all three certificate values vanish and \(x=x^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any threshold on \(\lambda(x)\) below one simultaneously yields explicit distance and objective-quality tolerances.

Without strict convexity or an appropriate quotient-space convention, the minimizer and local distance may fail to be unique.

children.title: Stationarity-Step-Size Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Residual and Newton-displacement interpretations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x\) with \(H_x\succ0\), and let \(n_x=-H_x^{-1}\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained intrinsic residual and step-size certification at a point with invertible Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the stationarity–step-size certificate is the predicate
\[
\operatorname{SSC}_\varepsilon(x)\iff\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*=\|n_x\|_x\leq\varepsilon.
\]
It simultaneously certifies
\[
|\langle\nabla f(x),v\rangle|\leq\varepsilon\|v\|_x\quad\text{for every }v,
\]
and
\[
\|n_x\|_x\leq\varepsilon.
\]
Moreover, \(\operatorname{SSC}_0(x)\) is equivalent to \(\nabla f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point satisfies the tolerance-\(\varepsilon\) stationarity–step-size certificate when its Newton decrement is at most \(\varepsilon\). The same scalar bounds every directional derivative after normalization by the local norm and bounds the local length of the Newton displacement. At tolerance zero, the certificate is exactly first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{SSC}_\varepsilon(x)\iff\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*=\|n_x\|_x\leq\varepsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\lambda(x)=\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{|\langle\nabla f(x),v\rangle|}{\|v\|_x}.\]
\[\lambda(x)^2=-\langle\nabla f(x),n_x\rangle.\]
special_cases_latex: For convex differentiable \(f\), \(\operatorname{SSC}_0(x)\) implies that \(x\) is a global minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate is invariant under nonsingular affine coordinate changes.
boundary_notes: Small local residual need not imply a small Euclidean gradient when the Hessian is poorly conditioned.
Objective-gap and solution-distance conclusions require self-concordance and the additional hypotheses of their respective certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Size Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative Newton step whose local length is below one is certified to remain in the domain; analytic damping always meets this test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\alpha\ge0\), the condition \(\alpha\lambda(x)<1\) certifies \(x+\alpha n_x\in D\). The analytic choice \(\alpha=(1+\lambda(x))^{-1}\) satisfies this condition and therefore certifies feasibility of the analytically damped Newton point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant on an open convex domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le\alpha\lambda(x)<1\) implies \(x+\alpha n_x\in D\); in particular, \(\alpha=(1+\lambda(x))^{-1}\) is certified feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Displacement Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual local norm of an approximate solve's residual equals the primal local norm of its error relative to the exact Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual and direction displacement obey \[d-n_x=H_x^{-1}r,\qquad \|d-n_x\|_x=\|r\|_{x,*}.\] Thus a residual bound in the dual Hessian norm is exactly the corresponding displacement-error bound in the primal Hessian norm.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is an approximate Newton direction with residual \(r=H_xd+g_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic correspondence for approximate local Newton solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificates break when the Hessian is noninvertible; at decrement one, a self-concordant function may have neither a minimizer nor a finite optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\nabla^2f(x)\) is singular, the inverse-Hessian norm, Newton direction, and decrement need not be defined, so their certificates are unavailable. Even with a positive Hessian, the strict threshold \(\lambda(x)<1\) is essential for solution localization and finite gap bounds: for \(f(t)=-\log t\) on \((0,\infty)\), one has \(f''(t)>0\) and \(\lambda(t)=1\) for every \(t\), yet \(f\) has no minimizer and its infimum is \(-\infty\).
assumptions_latex: Newton certificates are formed from \(\nabla f(x)\), \(\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\), and local self-concordant inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificates fail when the local Hessian norm is undefined, and localization or gap conclusions requiring \(\lambda(x)<1\) cannot be extended to \(\lambda(x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp structural and unit-decrement boundaries of the certificate system.

children.title: Solution-Distance Certificate
children.top_down_role: Localization of a minimizer from an interior point.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Distance Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the decrement is below one, any minimizer lies in an explicitly computable Hessian ellipsoid centered at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an interior point \(x\), suppose the computable Newton decrement satisfies \(\lambda(x)<1\). Then every minimizer \(x^*\in D\) is localized in the Hessian geometry at \(x\) by \[\|x^*-x\|_x\le\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)}.\] Thus the decrement and local Hessian alone provide an ellipsoidal solution-distance certificate, with certified region \(x+\{h:\|h\|_x\le\lambda(x)/(1-\lambda(x))\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant and convex with \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^*-x\|_x\le \lambda(x)/(1-\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localization in the norm based at the observed interior point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-distance certificate at the observation point \(x\); it is valid when the decrement is strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda(x)<1\), define the solution-distance certificate radius
\[
R_{\mathrm{sol}}(x)=\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)}.
\]
The certificate is the ellipsoidal localization statement
\[
x^*\in\{y:\|y-x\|_x\leq R_{\mathrm{sol}}(x)\},
\]
or equivalently
\[
\|x-x^*\|_x\leq\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the Newton decrement at \(x\) is below one, the unique minimizer lies in the base-point Dikin ellipsoid of radius \(\lambda(x)/(1-lambda(x))\). This converts a computable local residual into an intrinsic solution-distance bound. For small decrement the certified radius is asymptotic to \(\lambda(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda(x)<1\Longrightarrow\|x-x^*\|_x\leq\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x^*\in W\!\left(x;\frac{\lambda(x)}{1-\lambda(x)}\right).\]
The sharper two-sided relation is \(\lambda(x)/(1+\lambda(x))\leq\|x-x^*\|_x\leq\lambda(x)/(1-\lambda(x))\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda(x)\leq1/2\), then \(\|x-x^*\|_x\leq2\lambda(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence with \(\lambda(x_k)\to0\) has certified local distance \(\|x_k-x^*\|_{x_k}\to0\).
boundary_notes: The radius diverges at \(\lambda=1\); the certificate is not defined there.
The bound is in the metric at \(x\), not necessarily in a fixed Euclidean norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Suboptimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decrement below one gives a computable upper bound on objective suboptimality, asymptotically equal to one half the squared decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\lambda(x)<1\), the objective error is bounded solely by the Newton decrement: \[0\le f(x)-f(x^*)\le\omega_*(\lambda(x))=-\lambda(x)-\log(1-\lambda(x)).\] Hence evaluating the gradient and Hessian at \(x\) supplies a computable upper certificate on suboptimality. In particular, since \(\omega_*(t)=t^2/2+O(t^3)\) as \(t\downarrow0\), the certified objective error is locally quadratic in the decrement.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant and convex with \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x)-f(x^*)\le\omega_*(\lambda(x))=-\lambda(x)-\log(1-\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap certification in the subunit-decrement regime.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be strictly convex and standard self-concordant, let \(x^*\) be its minimizer, and let \(\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided objective-quality certification in the controlled decrement regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the suboptimality certificate interval
\[
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{gap}}(x)=\bigl[\omega(\lambda(x)),\ \omega_*(\lambda(x))\bigr],
\]
where \(\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\) and \(\omega_*(t)=-t-\ln(1-t)\). The certified objective gap satisfies
\[
\omega(\lambda(x))\leq f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\omega_*(\lambda(x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the decrement is less than one, the objective gap belongs to an explicit interval determined only by the decrement. Its lower endpoint is \(\omega(\lambda)\), and its upper endpoint is \(\omega_*(\lambda)\). Both are asymptotic to \(\lambda^2/2\), so the usual quadratic-model estimate becomes quantitatively reliable in the controlled regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\omega(\lambda(x))\leq f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\omega_*(\lambda(x)),\qquad \lambda(x)<1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[f(x)-\omega_*(\lambda(x))\leq f(x^*)\leq f(x)-\omega(\lambda(x)).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(0\leq\lambda\leq0.68\), the simpler bound \(f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\lambda(x)^2\) is valid.
As \(\lambda\downarrow0\), \(f(x)-f(x^*)=\tfrac12\lambda^2+O(\lambda^3)\) within the two envelopes.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stopping rule \(\omega_*(\lambda(x))\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x)-f(x^*)\leq\varepsilon\).
boundary_notes: The upper certificate requires \(\lambda<1\) and diverges as \(\lambda\uparrow1\).
For self-concordance constant \(M_f\), the interval is \(M_f^{-2}[\omega(M_f\lambda),\omega_*(M_f\lambda)]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fast-Region Membership Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decrement at most one quarter certifies feasibility of the full Newton step, invariance of the local region, and quadratic decrement contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the observable decrement satisfies \(\lambda(x)\le1/4\), then the full Newton step has local length below one and is therefore feasible. At \(x^+=x+n_x\), self-concordance gives \[\lambda(x^+)\le\frac{\lambda(x)^2}{(1-\lambda(x))^2}.\] In particular, \(\lambda(x^+)\le1/9<1/4\), so the iterate remains in the same controlled region and repeated full steps exhibit quadratic decrement contraction. Thus \(\lambda(x)\le1/4\) certifies fast-region membership.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+n_x\in D\) and \(\lambda(x+n_x)\le\lambda(x)^2/(1-\lambda(x))^2\le1/9\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conservative, explicit full-step quadratic-convergence neighborhood.

children.title: Newton Step Regimes
children.top_down_role: Globalized and local Newton regimes determined by intrinsic curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\), \(M_f\), and \(\lambda_f\) satisfy the self-concordant setting above. Fix a switching value \(\beta\in(0,1/(2M_f)]\), and let \(n(x)=-[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) denote the exact Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A global-to-local two-regime organization for exact Newton directions in finite-dimensional self-concordant minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Newton step regime at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is defined by \[\mathsf R_\beta(x)=\begin{cases}\mathsf{damped},&\lambda_f(x)\ge\beta,\\ \mathsf{local},&\lambda_f(x)<\beta.\end{cases}\] In the damped regime the analytic step is \(x_+=x+n(x)/(1+M_f\lambda_f(x))\). In the local regime one uses a locally fast Newton-family step, such as the intermediate update \(x_+=x+n(x)/(1+\xi(x))\), where \(\xi(x)=M_f^2\lambda_f(x)^2/(1+M_f\lambda_f(x))\). The particular choice \(\beta=1/(2M_f)\) matches the certified region \(\mathcal Q_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regimes are a partition of the domain by the Newton decrement. Points whose decrement is at least the chosen switching threshold are assigned to the globalized damped regime and use the analytic damping factor. Points below the threshold are assigned to the local regime and use a Newton-family step that approaches a full step as the decrement tends to zero. Choosing the threshold equal to one over twice the self-concordance parameter reproduces the source's global-to-local strategy.
assumptions_latex: The decrement and Newton direction are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is partitioned into \(\{\lambda_f\ge\beta\}\) and \(\{\lambda_f<\beta\}\), with the stated damped and local step rules.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\mathsf R_\beta(x)=\mathsf{local}\Longleftrightarrow M_f\lambda_f(x)<M_f\beta\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\beta=1/(2M_f)\), the local regime is exactly \(\mathcal Q_f\).
As \(\lambda_f(x)\to0\), the intermediate step multiplier \(1/(1+\xi(x))\to1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The regime indicator is computable from local gradient and Hessian data.
The damped regime provides uniform objective decrease while the decrement stays above \(\beta\).
boundary_notes: The partition defines a strategy, not a claim that every undamped rule is safe below every positive threshold.
Line-search, trust-region, and inexact regimes require separate acceptance or accuracy conditions.

children.title: Analytically Damped Newton Method
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic damping before entry into the fast local region.

knowledge_statements.title: Analytically Damped Newton Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the Newton direction and scale it by one over one plus the decrement; stop when the decrement meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k=0\) and \(x_0\in D\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(n_k=-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(\lambda_k=\|n_k\|_{x_k}\). If \(\lambda_k\le\varepsilon\), stop and output \(x_k\). Otherwise set \[\alpha_k=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_k},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kn_k,\] increment \(k\), and repeat. Since \(\|\alpha_kn_k\|_{x_k}=\lambda_k/(1+\lambda_k)<1\), every generated trial point is certified to remain in \(D\).
assumptions_latex: A stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and initial point \(x_0\in D\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each nonterminal update is feasible and uses \(x_{k+1}=x_k+n_k/(1+\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic globalizing damping determined by the current decrement.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\to\mathbb R\) be convex and self-concordant with parameter \(M_f>0\), open domain, and positive-definite Hessian. Set \(n(x)=-[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) and \(\lambda_f(x)=\|n(x)\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic Newton iteration with damping chosen analytically from the intrinsic decrement, without a line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The analytically damped Newton map is \[T_{\mathrm{dN}}(x):=x+\alpha(x)n(x),\qquad \alpha(x):=\frac{1}{1+M_f\lambda_f(x)}.\] Starting from any \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), the method generates \(x_{k+1}=T_{\mathrm{dN}}(x_k)\). Its intrinsic step length is \[\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|_{x_k}=\frac{\lambda_f(x_k)}{1+M_f\lambda_f(x_k)}<\frac1{M_f},\] and hence the update lies in the self-concordant Dikin neighborhood of \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iterate, solve the exact Newton system, then multiply the Newton direction by one divided by one plus the self-concordance parameter times the Newton decrement. This step size is determined entirely by local differential information. Its local norm is always strictly less than the guaranteed Dikin radius, so the next point remains in the domain. No backtracking parameter or trial evaluation is part of this definition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\alpha(x)=\omega'(M_f\lambda_f(x))/(M_f\lambda_f(x))\) for \(\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\), with the continuous value \(\alpha(x)=1\) when \(\lambda_f(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda_f(x)=0\), then \(n(x)=0\) and the iterate is stationary.
For \(M_f=1\), \(\alpha(x)=1/(1+\lambda_f(x))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every analytically damped step is domain-feasible under the stated assumptions.
The multiplier approaches one as the decrement approaches zero.
boundary_notes: This is not a backtracking line search.
The formula requires an invertible Hessian and an exact decrement.
The definition alone does not cover approximate linear solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Step Newton Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inside the certified fast region, repeatedly take the entire Newton direction and stop when the decrement reaches tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k=0\) at \(x_0\in D\) with \(\lambda_0\le1/4\). Compute \(n_k=-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(\lambda_k=\|n_k\|_{x_k}\). If \(\lambda_k\le\varepsilon\), output \(x_k\); otherwise take the undamped update \[x_{k+1}=x_k+n_k.\] Increment \(k\) and repeat. The fast-region certificate ensures feasibility and gives \(\lambda_{k+1}\le\lambda_k^2/(1-\lambda_k)^2\), so subsequent iterates remain controlled.
assumptions_latex: The initial point satisfies \(\lambda(x_0)\le1/4\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration uses \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) until \(\lambda(x_k)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undamped iteration initialized in a conservative fast region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Step Newton Iteration in the Local Metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\subseteq\mathbb E	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable with \(
abla^2f(x)\succ0\), and define \(n(x)=-[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}
abla f(x)\) and \(\lambda_f(x)=\|n(x)\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, undamped Newton iteration for smooth convex self-concordant minimization; feasibility is certified locally by the decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The full-step Newton map is \[T_{\mathrm N}(x):=x+n(x)=x-[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x).\] The full-step method is the sequence \(x_{k+1}=T_{\mathrm N}(x_k)\) whenever the map is defined and the new point belongs to \(\operatorname{dom}f\). For an \(M_f\)-self-concordant function, the sufficient intrinsic feasibility condition \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\) places \(T_{\mathrm N}(x)\) in the open Dikin neighborhood because \(\|T_{\mathrm N}(x)-x\|_x=\lambda_f(x)<1/M_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-step method adds the entire exact Newton direction, with step multiplier one. Its definition differs from damped Newton solely by the absence of a damping factor. In the self-concordant setting, a decrement below one over the self-concordance parameter certifies that this full step stays in the domain. Local contraction requires a stronger small-decrement condition than mere feasibility.
assumptions_latex: For the stated feasibility certificate, \(f\) is \(M_f\)-self-concordant and \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm N}(x)=x-[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\) under the stated decrement certificate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The full step is variant A of \(x_+=x-[1+\xi]^{-1}[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) with \(\xi=0\).
special_cases_latex: At a stationary point, \(T_{\mathrm N}(x)=x\).
For a strictly convex quadratic function, one exact full step reaches its minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\), the next decrement satisfies \(\lambda_f(T_{\mathrm N}(x))\le M_f\lambda_f(x)^2/(1-M_f\lambda_f(x))^2\).
boundary_notes: Outside the certified Dikin neighborhood, the full step need not remain in the domain.
Positive semidefiniteness without invertibility does not define the displayed Newton direction.
This entry does not include line-search acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Newton Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard self-concordant objective, a relative dual-norm residual bound controls the approximate direction's error and length; a local length below one certifies feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An approximate local solve is in the relative inexact Newton regime when \[\|H_xd+g_x\|_{x,*}\le\eta\lambda(x),\qquad 0\le\eta<1.\] This condition certifies \[\|d-n_x\|_x\le\eta\lambda(x),\qquad \|d\|_x\le(1+\eta)\lambda(x).\] The additional inequality \((1+\eta)\lambda(x)<1\) certifies that the full approximate displacement satisfies \(x+d\in D\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is standard self-concordant on an open convex domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
An approximate direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) has residual \(r=H_xd+g_x\), and \(\eta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r\|_{x,*}\le\eta\lambda(x)\) implies \(\|d-n_x\|_x\le\eta\lambda(x)\) and \(\|d\|_x\le(1+\eta)\lambda(x)\); if additionally \((1+\eta)\lambda(x)<1\), then \(x+d\in D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative residual control measured in intrinsic Hessian norms for a standard self-concordant objective.
