knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a point \(x\), with Hessian \(H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)\) and gradient \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)\). Fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and a forcing parameter \(\eta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local inexact Newton theory. The residual criterion is general and is not by itself a self-concordant global-feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(p\) is an \(\eta\)-inexact Newton direction at \(x\) if its Newton-equation residual \[r(x,p):=H(x)p+g(x)\] satisfies \[\|r(x,p)\|\le\eta\|g(x)\|.\] An iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) is in the residual-controlled inexact Newton regime when each \(p_k\) obeys this condition with a forcing sequence \(0\le\eta_k<1\). The exact Newton regime is recovered when \(r(x,p)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact Newton direction approximately solves the Newton linear system. Its approximation quality is measured by the norm of the linear-system residual relative to the gradient norm. A sequence of such steps is governed by forcing parameters strictly below one. Bounded forcing parameters support local linear contraction under the standard nonsingularity assumptions; forcing parameters tending to zero support superlinear behavior, and forcing parameters of gradient order support quadratic behavior under a locally Lipschitz Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable in the neighborhood under consideration.
For local convergence claims, the limiting Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(p_k\) belongs to the inexact Newton regime exactly when \(\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\le\eta_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For invertible \(H(x)\), \(p=-H(x)^{-1}g(x)+H(x)^{-1}r(x,p)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\eta_k=0\) gives the exact Newton direction.
If \(\eta_k\to0\), the standard local theory permits superlinear convergence.
If \(\eta_k=O(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|)\) and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz, the standard local theory permits quadratic convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual criterion can terminate an iterative linear solver without forming an exact factorization.
boundary_notes: A Euclidean residual test is not automatically affine invariant.
Self-concordant domain feasibility and decrement contraction require additional intrinsic error and step-size controls.
The criterion does not handle indefinite curvature without a globalization mechanism.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian, decrement \(\lambda_f\), and \(\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\). Let \(T_{\mathrm{dN}}\), \(T_{\mathrm N}\), and \(T_{\mathrm I}\) denote the analytic damped, full-step, and intermediate Newton maps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An indexed family of exact progress and contraction relations, rather than a single theorem assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The self-concordant Newton decrease family \(\mathfrak T_f\) is the collection of the following map-bound pairs: \[\bigl(T_{\mathrm{dN}},\ f(T_{\mathrm{dN}}x)\le f(x)-M_f^{-2}\omega(M_f\lambda_f(x))\bigr),\] \[\bigl(T_{\mathrm N},\ \lambda_f(T_{\mathrm N}x)\le M_f\lambda_f(x)^2/(1-M_f\lambda_f(x))^2\bigr),\] valid for \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\), and \[\bigl(T_{\mathrm I},\ \lambda_f(T_{\mathrm I}x)\le M_f\lambda_f(x)^2(1+2M_f\lambda_f(x))\bigr),\] valid under the intermediate-step condition of Theorem 5.2.2(3).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This theorem family is the indexed collection of the canonical exact inequalities used in global-to-local self-concordant Newton analysis. Its damped member controls objective decrease globally. Its full-step and intermediate members control the next Newton decrement locally. The family records each result together with its own update map and applicability condition, preventing a local contraction inequality from being applied as if it were global.
assumptions_latex: Each family member is invoked only under its displayed step-specific hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak T_f\) consists of the stated objective-decrease and decrement-contraction map-bound pairs.
special_cases_latex: When \(M_f=1\), all parameter-scaled expressions reduce to the standard normalization.
immediate_consequences_latex: The damped member supplies global progress away from stationarity.
The local members supply quadratic decrement bounds near stationarity.
boundary_notes: Membership in the family does not make every inequality valid for every Newton variant.
The family excludes inexact directions unless separate perturbation bounds are supplied.

notation.meaning: Indexed family of Newton progress relations.

children.title: Damped-Newton Decrease Family
children.top_down_role: Guaranteed progress in the globalized regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Damped-Newton Decrease Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analytic damping guarantees a positive objective decrease equal to at least the canonical self-concordant function of the current decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in D\), let \(\lambda=\|n_x\|_x\) and take the analytic damping factor \(\alpha=(1+\lambda)^{-1}\). Then \(x^+=x+\alpha n_x\in D\) and \[f(x^+)\le f(x)-\omega(\lambda),\qquad \omega(\lambda)=\lambda-\log(1+\lambda).\] Since \(\omega(\lambda)>0\) for \(\lambda>0\), every nonstationary damped Newton step produces a guaranteed objective decrease determined only by the current decrement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\!\left(x+n_x/(1+\lambda)\right)\le f(x)-\omega(\lambda)\), where \(\omega(t)=t-\log(1+t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical decrease bound for the analytically damped Newton step.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant, let \(\lambda_f(x)\) be its Newton decrement, and define \(\omega(t)=t-\ln(1+t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact analytically damped Newton steps in the globalized regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each decrement lower threshold \(\beta>0\), define the damped-Newton decrease relation \[\mathcal D_f(\beta):=\left\{(x,x_+):x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \lambda_f(x)\ge\beta,\ x_+=T_{\mathrm{dN}}(x),\ f(x)-f(x_+)\ge\frac{\omega(M_f\beta)}{M_f^2}\right\}.\] The full decrease family is \(\mathfrak D_f:=\{\mathcal D_f(\beta):\beta>0\}\). Pointwise, its sharp analytic member is \[f(x)-f(T_{\mathrm{dN}}x)\ge M_f^{-2}\omega(M_f\lambda_f(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The damped-decrease family groups the global objective-progress inequalities by a positive lower bound on the current Newton decrement. Whenever the decrement remains at least the selected threshold, every analytically damped step decreases the objective by at least the corresponding positive constant. The pointwise member uses the actual decrement and is stronger than the thresholded form.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(x_+)\ge M_f^{-2}\omega(M_f\lambda_f(x))\ge M_f^{-2}\omega(M_f\beta)>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(M_f=1\), the guaranteed decrease is \(\omega(\lambda_f(x))\).
special_cases_latex: At the phase threshold \(\beta=1/(2M_f)\), each damped step decreases \(f\) by at least \(M_f^{-2}\omega(1/2)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A bounded initial objective gap yields a finite bound on the number of iterations with \(\lambda_f(x_k)\ge\beta\).
boundary_notes: The positive uniform bound disappears as \(\beta\downarrow0\).
The relation is specific to the analytic damping rule.

children.title: Full-Step Acceptance Family

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Step Acceptance Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full Newton step stays feasible when the decrement is below one and passes an Armijo test once the decrement satisfies the displayed scalar threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n(x)=-\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) and \(\lambda(x)=\|n(x)\|_x\). If \(\lambda(x)<1\), self-concordance gives \(x+n(x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and
\[
f(x+n(x))\le f(x)-\lambda(x)^2+\omega_*(\lambda(x)),\qquad \omega_*(t)=-t-\log(1-t).
\]
Consequently, for an Armijo parameter \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), the full step is accepted whenever
\[
\omega_*(\lambda(x))\le(1-\alpha)\lambda(x)^2,
\]
because then \(f(x+n(x))\le f(x)+\alpha\nabla f(x)^\top n(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\subset\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is standard self-concordant, convex, and has positive-definite Hessian.
The line search uses the Armijo parameter \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+n(x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and the unit Newton step satisfies the Armijo test whenever \(\omega_*(\lambda(x))\le(1-\alpha)\lambda(x)^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo acceptance criterion for the exact full Newton step.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian. Let \(T_{\mathrm N}(x)=x-[\nabla^2f(x)]^{-1}\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact full Newton steps, with acceptance defined by sufficient intrinsic feasibility and contraction thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho\in(0,1)\), define the full-step acceptance set \[\mathcal A_f(\rho):=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}f:M_f\lambda_f(x)\le\rho\}.\] Membership certifies feasibility of the full step because \(\|T_{\mathrm N}(x)-x\|_x=\lambda_f(x)<1/M_f\) when \(\rho<1\). The contraction-certified subfamily is obtained by choosing \(\rho\) so that \[\frac{\rho}{(1-\rho)^2}<1,\] equivalently \(0<\rho<(3-\sqrt5)/2\); then \(\lambda_f(T_{\mathrm N}x)<\lambda_f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-step acceptance family is indexed by a dimensionless decrement radius. Any radius below one certifies that the undamped Newton point remains in the domain. Radii below the positive root of the stated scalar equation additionally certify strict decrement contraction. This separates mere feasibility of a full step from entry into a fast local regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal A_f(\rho)\) certifies \(T_{\mathrm N}(x)\in\operatorname{dom}f\); if \(\rho<(3-\sqrt5)/2\), it also certifies \(\lambda_f(T_{\mathrm N}x)<\lambda_f(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The contraction threshold is the positive solution range of \(\rho/(1-\rho)^2<1\).
special_cases_latex: Under \(M_f=1\), the acceptance condition becomes \(\lambda_f(x)\le\rho\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A switching policy may accept full steps once the scaled decrement crosses a chosen contraction-certified radius.
boundary_notes: Feasibility for \(\rho<1\) does not by itself imply contraction.
The threshold is sufficient and need not be necessary for a particular function.

children.title: Newton-Decrement Contraction Family
children.top_down_role: Fast reduction of the intrinsic residual after full-step entry.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Decrement Contraction Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After an admissible exact full Newton step, the next decrement is at most the square of the current decrement divided by its feasibility margin squared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), define \(n(x)=-\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x)\), \(x^+=x+n(x)\), and \(\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*\). If \(\lambda(x)<1\), then \(x^+\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and
\[
\lambda(x^+)\le \frac{\lambda(x)^2}{(1-\lambda(x))^2}.
\]
Thus, on every fixed neighborhood \(\lambda(x)\le\beta<1\), the next decrement is bounded by \((1-\beta)^{-2}\lambda(x)^2\); in particular, the intrinsic first-order residual contracts quadratically once full steps are admissible.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(x+n(x))\le \lambda(x)^2/(1-\lambda(x))^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decrement recurrence after a feasible full Newton step.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant with decrement \(\lambda_f\). Let \(T_{\mathrm N}\), \(T_{\mathrm{dN}}\), and \(T_{\mathrm I}\) be the exact full, damped, and intermediate Newton maps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step local contraction bounds measured in the intrinsic Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Newton-decrement contraction family \(\mathfrak C_f\) consists of triples \((T,D,B)\) for which \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\lambda_f(Tx)\le B(\lambda_f(x))\) for every \(x\in D\). Its canonical members are \[B_{\mathrm N}(t)=\frac{M_ft^2}{(1-M_ft)^2},\quad D_{\mathrm N}=\{M_f\lambda_f<1\},\] \[B_{\mathrm{dN}}(t)=M_ft^2\left(1+\frac1{1+M_ft}\right),\quad D_{\mathrm{dN}}=\operatorname{dom}f,\] and \[B_{\mathrm I}(t)=M_ft^2(1+2M_ft)\] on the intermediate-step domain specified by \(M_ft+M_f^2t^2+M_f^3t^3\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family records one-step bounds on the next Newton decrement, indexed by the update rule. Each member includes a map, an applicability domain, and a scalar majorant. All three majorants are quadratic at zero, but their global domains differ. The full-step bound has a denominator that becomes singular at the Dikin boundary, while the damped member is globally defined.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
Each bound is used only on its displayed applicability domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \((T,D,B)\in\mathfrak C_f\) and \(x\in D\), \(\lambda_f(Tx)\le B(\lambda_f(x))\).
special_cases_latex: As \(t\downarrow0\), \(B_{\mathrm N}(t)=M_ft^2+o(t^2)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{dN}}(t)=2M_ft^2+o(t^2)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every canonical member exhibits local quadratic decrement reduction.
A scalar threshold ensuring \(B(t)<t\) yields an invariant contraction region.
boundary_notes: The three bounds are not interchangeable among step rules.
These exact bounds do not include linear-solve residual errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Decrement Contraction Relations

children.title: Quadratic-Convergence Family
children.top_down_role: Local fast convergence of iterates and decrements.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Convergence Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with decrement at most one quarter, exact full Newton steps remain feasible, the decrement contracts quadratically, and the intrinsic distance to the minimizer is bounded by the decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(\lambda_k=\lambda(x_k)\). If \(\lambda_0\le 1/4\), every full step is feasible and
\[
\lambda_{k+1}\le\frac{\lambda_k^2}{(1-\lambda_k)^2}\le\frac{16}{9}\lambda_k^2.
\]
The sequence converges to \(x^*\), and its local error obeys
\[
\|x_k-x^*\|_{x_k}\le\frac{\lambda_k}{1-\lambda_k}.
\]
Thus the decrement contracts quadratically, while the intrinsic iterate error is controlled by the decrement.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\subset\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is standard self-concordant and convex, has positive-definite Hessian on its domain, and attains its minimum at \(x^*\).
Exact full Newton steps are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(x_{k+1})\le(16/9)\lambda(x_k)^2\) and \(\|x_k-x^*\|_{x_k}\le\lambda(x_k)/(1-\lambda(x_k))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic decrement contraction and decrement-based control of iterate error for exact full-step Newton iteration.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(T\) be a Newton-family map on a subset \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). Use the Newton decrement \(\lambda_f\) as the intrinsic residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-quadratic convergence expressed through decrements, with iterate and objective measures included only where their local equivalence is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((T,D)\) belongs to the quadratic-convergence family \(\mathfrak Q_f\) if there exist \(C>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that \[x\in D,\quad \lambda_f(x)\le\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T(x)\in D,\qquad \lambda_f(Tx)\le C\lambda_f(x)^2.\] For exact self-concordant Newton variants, the canonical decrement bounds supply such constants on sufficiently small invariant neighborhoods. If \(x_f^*\) exists, the standard local equivalences among decrement, objective gap, and local distance transfer this quadratic behavior to those measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic-convergence family contains Newton update maps that preserve a sufficiently small neighborhood and square the intrinsic residual up to a fixed constant. This is a local property with explicit quantifiers: a radius and constant must work uniformly throughout the selected neighborhood. The exact full, damped, and intermediate Newton maps are members after their respective decrement bounds are restricted to sufficiently small invariant regions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
The selected neighborhood is invariant under \(T\).
For distance or objective-gap interpretations, a minimizer exists and the cited local equivalences apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((T,D)\in\mathfrak Q_f\Longleftrightarrow\exists C,\delta>0\ \forall x\in D:\lambda_f(x)\le\delta\Rightarrow T(x)\in D\text{ and }\lambda_f(Tx)\le C\lambda_f(x)^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Along a convergent nonstationary sequence, Q-quadratic decrement convergence means \(\sup_k\lambda_f(x_{k+1})/\lambda_f(x_k)^2<\infty\) eventually.
special_cases_latex: For the full step, one may take \(C=M_f/(1-M_f\delta)^2\) on \(M_f\delta<1\).
For the damped step, one may take \(C=M_f(1+1/(1+M_f\delta))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Once inside an invariant quadratic region, the number of correct digits grows rapidly.
A fixed linear contraction is weaker than membership in \(\mathfrak Q_f\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be convex, \(M_f\)-self-concordant, bounded below, and have positive-definite Hessian. Let \(x_f^*\) be its minimizer and let \(\mathcal A\) be a specified Newton strategy producing \(x_k\) from \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration complexity counts outer Newton updates, not arithmetic operations or linear-solver work; barrier path-following is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define the Newton-iteration complexity of \(\mathcal A\) by \[N_{f,\mathcal A}(x_0,\varepsilon):=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N:\lambda_f(x_k)\le\varepsilon\},\] with value \(+\infty\) if the set is empty. Define the normalized initial level \[\Delta_f(x_0):=M_f^2\bigl(f(x_0)-f(x_f^*)\bigr).\] For the cited two-stage exact strategy, the entry-phase count is controlled by \(\Delta_f(x_0)/\omega(1/2)\), while the subsequent decrement sequence is quadratically convergent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-concordant minimization complexity is the number of Newton-family outer iterations needed to reduce the intrinsic Newton decrement to a prescribed tolerance. The normalized initial objective gap is the natural scale-free quantity controlling the global damped phase. This definition separates the count of outer updates from the cost of evaluating derivatives or solving each Newton system.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{f,\mathcal A}(x_0,\varepsilon)=\inf\{k:\lambda_f(x_k)\le\varepsilon\}\), with global-phase scale \(\Delta_f(x_0)=M_f^2(f(x_0)-f(x_f^*))\).
special_cases_latex: For the two-stage threshold \(1/(2M_f)\), at most \(\Delta_f(x_0)/\omega(1/2)\) damped steps occur before local entry.
immediate_consequences_latex: Iteration complexity is affine invariant when formulated through the decrement and normalized gap.
The local quadratic phase contributes a doubly logarithmic dependence on a sufficiently small decrement tolerance.

children.title: Global-to-Local Phase Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of reaching and then exploiting the fast Newton region.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-to-Local Phase Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Damped Newton spends at most the initial gap divided by a fixed decrease reaching the local region; full Newton then needs doubly logarithmic iterations in the target decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\beta\in(0,1/4]\). While \(\lambda(x_k)>\beta\), take \(x_{k+1}=x_k+n(x_k)/(1+\lambda(x_k))\); afterward take full Newton steps. Each damped iteration decreases the objective by at least \(\omega(\beta)\), where \(\omega(t)=t-\log(1+t)\). Therefore the global phase has at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{f(x_0)-f^*}{\omega(\beta)}\right\rceil
\]
iterations. The full-step recurrence \(\lambda_{k+1}\le\lambda_k^2/(1-\lambda_k)^2\) then reaches \(\lambda_k\le\varepsilon\) in \(O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\) additional iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is standard self-concordant, has positive-definite Hessian, and attains \(f^*\).
Damped steps \(x^+=x+n(x)/(1+\lambda(x))\) are used above a fixed \(\beta\in(0,1/4]\), followed by full steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration count is \(O((f(x_0)-f^*)/\omega(\beta)+\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-phase bound for exact damped-then-full Newton minimization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be produced by the exact two-stage strategy: analytic damping while \(M_f\lambda_f(x_k)\ge1/2\), followed by the intermediate Newton update while \(M_f\lambda_f(x_k)<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-iteration phase accounting for unconstrained self-concordant minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the fast-region entry time and local finishing time by \[N_{\mathrm{ent}}:=\inf\{k\ge0:M_f\lambda_f(x_k)<\tfrac12\},\] \[N_{\mathrm{loc}}(\varepsilon):=\inf\{j\ge0:\lambda_f(x_{N_{\mathrm{ent}}+j})\le\varepsilon\}.\] The global-to-local phase complexity is the ordered pair \[\mathcal K_f(x_0,\varepsilon):=(N_{\mathrm{ent}},N_{\mathrm{loc}}(\varepsilon)),\] and its total outer count is their sum. The cited decrease estimate gives \[N_{\mathrm{ent}}\le\frac{M_f^2(f(x_0)-f(x_f^*))}{\omega(1/2)},\] while the local phase obeys the quadratic decrement recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global-to-local complexity records two separate iteration counts: the number of damped updates required to enter the certified fast region and the number of local updates required to reach the final decrement tolerance. The first count is controlled by the normalized initial objective gap. The second is governed by repeated quadratic contraction. Keeping the pair rather than only its sum identifies which phase dominates.
assumptions_latex: The exact two-stage strategy is used.
The Hessian is positive definite throughout the generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_f(x_0,\varepsilon)=(N_{\mathrm{ent}},N_{\mathrm{loc}}(\varepsilon))\), with \(N_{\mathrm{ent}}\le\Delta_f(x_0)/\omega(1/2)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The total iteration count is \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}=N_{\mathrm{ent}}+N_{\mathrm{loc}}(\varepsilon)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(M_f\lambda_f(x_0)<1/2\), then \(N_{\mathrm{ent}}=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The global phase is linear in the normalized initial objective gap.
Once local entry occurs, decrement accuracy improves quadratically.
boundary_notes: The formula counts exact outer steps only.
Changing the switching threshold changes both phase counts and constants.

children.title: Initial-Level Centering Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Dependence on the starting point and initial objective level.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\) be bounded below, convex, and \(M_f\)-self-concordant, with minimizer \(x_f^*\). Fix an initial point \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and a decrement threshold \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact damped-Newton entry effort measured by the initial objective level; this is not barrier central-path centering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the normalized initial-level burden and its threshold-dependent centering budget by \[\Delta_f(x_0):=M_f^2\bigl(f(x_0)-f(x_f^*)\bigr),\qquad B_\beta(x_0):=\frac{\Delta_f(x_0)}{\omega(M_f\beta)}.\] The initial-level centering tradeoff is the relation \[N_{\mathrm{damp}}(\beta;x_0)\le B_\beta(x_0),\] where \(N_{\mathrm{damp}}(\beta;x_0)\) counts analytic damped-Newton iterations for which \(\lambda_f(x_k)\ge\beta\). A smaller target threshold raises the budget because \(\omega(M_f\beta)\downarrow0\), whereas a better-centered starting level lowers it linearly through \(\Delta_f(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tradeoff quantifies how the starting objective level and the desired decrement threshold determine the maximum damped-Newton centering effort. The numerator is the initial objective gap in the natural self-concordant scale. The denominator is the guaranteed decrease per damped step while the decrement remains above the selected threshold.
assumptions_latex: Exact analytically damped Newton steps are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{damp}}(\beta;x_0)\le M_f^2(f(x_0)-f(x_f^*))/\omega(M_f\beta)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: At \(\beta=1/(2M_f)\), \(B_\beta(x_0)=\Delta_f(x_0)/\omega(1/2)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x_0)=f(x_f^*)\), then \(\Delta_f(x_0)=0\) and no positive-decrement damped phase is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reducing the initial normalized gap by a factor reduces the worst-case damped-step budget by the same factor.
boundary_notes: The bound depends on the unknown optimal value unless an upper estimate of the gap is available.
It counts iterations, not the cost of producing a better initial point.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial Objective-Level versus Newton-Centering Effort
Initial-Level Dependence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every iteration outside a fixed centered neighborhood consumes a fixed amount of objective gap, so the global-phase length is linear in the initial gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta_0=f(x_0)-f^*<\infty\), and fix \(\beta\in(0,1)\). For every iterate with \(\lambda(x_k)>\beta\), the damped Newton update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+n(x_k)/(1+\lambda(x_k))\) satisfies
\[
f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\omega(\lambda(x_k))\ge\omega(\beta),
\]
where \(\omega(t)=t-\log(1+t)\). Consequently, the number of damped iterations before \(\lambda(x_k)\le\beta\) is at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{\Delta_0}{\omega(\beta)}\right\rceil.
\]
Thus the global-phase bound depends linearly on the available initial objective-gap bound.
assumptions_latex: Damped Newton steps are used whenever \(\lambda(x_k)>\beta\), for fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of iterations with \(\lambda(x_k)>\beta\) is at most \(\lceil\Delta_0/\omega(\beta)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear dependence of the damped phase on initial objective suboptimality.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Centering Dependence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the initial decrement is sufficiently small, full Newton begins immediately and the iteration count depends doubly logarithmically on accuracy, with constants determined by the initial centering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\lambda_0=\lambda(x_0)\le\beta<1/2\) and \(C_\beta\beta<1\), where \(C_\beta=(1-\beta)^{-2}\). Exact full Newton steps satisfy
\[
\lambda_{k+1}\le\frac{\lambda_k^2}{(1-\lambda_k)^2}\le C_\beta\lambda_k^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
C_\beta\lambda_k\le(C_\beta\lambda_0)^{2^k}.
\]
The smallest \(k\) for which the right-hand side is at most \(C_\beta\varepsilon\) is \(O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\), with constants depending on \(C_\beta\lambda_0\). No preceding objective-gap phase is required.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
Exact full Newton steps are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterations required for \(\lambda(x_k)\le\varepsilon\) are \(O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))\), with constants depending on \(\beta\) and \(\lambda(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration dependence when the initial point is already sufficiently centered.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.title: Level-to-Centering Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The self-concordant comparison functions translate between objective suboptimality and Newton decrement, with a two-sided equivalence once the decrement is below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), let \(\lambda(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_x^*\). The objective gap always satisfies
\[
f(x)-f^*\ge\omega(\lambda(x)),
\qquad \omega(t)=t-\log(1+t).
\]
If additionally \(\lambda(x)<1\), then
\[
f(x)-f^*\le\omega_*(\lambda(x)),
\qquad \omega_*(t)=-t-\log(1-t).
\]
Thus a decrement bound yields a two-sided level certificate in the local region, while a known level bound \(f(x)-f^*\le\Delta\) implies \(\lambda(x)\le\omega^{-1}(\Delta)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is standard self-concordant, has positive-definite Hessian, and attains its minimum at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\omega(\lambda(x))\le f(x)-f^*\le\omega_*(\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap and intrinsic-centering comparison below unit decrement.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Initialization Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the self-concordant function x minus log x, both initial gap and decrement become arbitrarily large, ruling out initialization-independent global iteration bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(f(x)=x-\log x\) on \((0,\infty)\). It is standard self-concordant, has minimizer \(x^*=1\), and satisfies
\[
\lambda(x)=\frac{|f'(x)|}{\sqrt{f''(x)}}=|x-1|,
\qquad f(x)-f(1)=x-1-\log x.
\]
Both quantities diverge as \(x\to\infty\). Hence no constant depending only on self-concordance can uniformly bound the initial decrement, initial level, or number of fixed-decrease damped iterations. Global complexity must retain initialization data or impose a bounded starting level set or centering condition.
assumptions_latex: The initialization may be any point in the domain.
No initial objective-gap or Newton-decrement bound is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Standard self-concordance alone provides no initialization-independent bound on the number of global Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded level and decrement under unrestricted initialization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer and Inner Complexity of Residual-Controlled Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), where \(p_k\) satisfies \(\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\le\eta_k\|

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define the inexact-Newton outer complexity and cumulative inner work by \[N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon):=\inf\{k:\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\},\qquad W_{\mathrm{in}}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{k=0}^{N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)-1}m_k.\] The complexity specification is completed by the forcing sequence \((\eta_k)\): a uniform bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) encodes a local linear regime, \(\eta_k\to0\) a superlinear regime, and \(\eta_k=O(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|)\), with a locally Lipschitz Hessian, a quadratic regime.

Inner work counts all iterative linear-solver steps used to construct those updates. The forcing sequence links solve accuracy to the attainable local convergence order. children.title: Newton-Theory Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Analytic and computational situations not covered by the classical decrement theory.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Applicability Boundary of Classical Decrement Theory
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a differentiable convex function \(f\), classical self-concordant decrement theory uses the inverse Hessian, the Dikin local norm, self-concordant distortion inequalities, and exact or controlled Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal boundary-of-applicability object; it identifies missing hypotheses and does not claim that every boundary point causes numerical divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the classical-theory applicability set \[\mathcal G_f:=\{x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f): f\text{ is self-concordant near }x,\ \nabla^2f(x)\succ0,\ \lambda_f(x)<\infty\}.\] The Newton-theory failure boundary is \[\mathcal B_f:=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\setminus\mathcal G_f,\] augmented, for a proposed step \(p\), by the uncontrolled-step conditions \(x+p\notin\operatorname{dom}f\) or absence of a cited local-norm/error certificate. Thus \(\mathcal B_f\) contains points where the decrement is undefined, self-concordant distortion control is unavailable, or the proposed computation falls outside the hypotheses of the classical bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The failure boundary is the complement of the points at which all ingredients of classical decrement theory are defined and justified. It includes singular or indefinite Newton systems, lack of self-concordance, boundary points outside the open domain, and steps whose size or approximation error lacks a valid certificate. Membership means that the classical theorem cannot be invoked; it does not alone prove that a particular implementation fails.
assumptions_latex: The intended theory is the classical smooth convex self-concordant Newton theory.
Applicability requires an interior point and a positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal B_f\) exactly when at least one defining condition of \(\mathcal G_f\) fails, with uncontrolled proposed steps treated as additional out-of-scope cases.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\notin\mathcal B_f\Longleftrightarrow x\in\mathcal G_f\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f_0(x)=-\ln x\) on \(x>0\), the decrement equals its critical threshold everywhere while the function is unbounded below, showing that strict decrement hypotheses cannot generally be weakened to non-strict ones.
immediate_consequences_latex: No Newton-decrement certificate should be reported when the Hessian inverse does not exist.
Failure of a sufficient hypothesis must be distinguished from a counterexample to convergence.
boundary_notes: The set is an applicability boundary, not necessarily a topological boundary.
Nonsmooth generalized Newton theories are outside this definition.
Indefinite nonconvex Newton methods require different globalization results.

children.title: Uncontrolled Full Steps

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Full Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x minus log x, a full Newton step from any x greater than two becomes negative and exits the domain, despite standard self-concordance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x-\log x\) on \((0,\infty)\), one has \(f'(x)=1-1/x\), \(f''(x)=1/x^2\), and the exact Newton direction is
\[
n(x)=-\frac{f'(x)}{f''(x)}=x(1-x).
\]
The uncontrolled full step is therefore
\[
x^+=x+n(x)=2x-x^2.
\]
For every \(x>2\), \(x^+<0\), so the iterate leaves \(\operatorname{dom}f\) and the objective is undefined there. Self-concordance consequently does not justify unit steps outside a decrement-certified neighborhood; damping or a feasibility-aware line search is required.
assumptions_latex: A unit Newton step is taken without checking decrement, feasibility, or sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A full Newton step can leave the domain even for a standard self-concordant objective with a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain loss from an uncertified unit Newton step.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and \(M_f\)-self-concordant at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), with \(
abla^2f(x)\succ0\), full Newton point \(x^{\mathrm N}=x-[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}
abla f(x)\), and decrement \(\lambda_f(x)=\|x^{\mathrm N}-x\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact undamped steps taken outside a stated feasibility or contraction certificate; uncontrolled means uncertified, not necessarily unsuccessful.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The full Newton step at \(x\) is called uncontrolled relative to the classical self-concordant certificate when \[M_f\lambda_f(x)\ge1\] or when the quantities needed to verify \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\) are unavailable or unreliable. Equivalently, the step lacks the Dikin-neighborhood implication \[\|x^{\mathrm N}-x\|_x<1/M_f\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^{\mathrm N}\in\operatorname{dom}f.\] It is contraction-uncontrolled when no stronger threshold is established that makes the full-step majorant \[\frac{M_f\lambda_f(x)^2}{(1-M_f\lambda_f(x))^2}\] both defined and strictly smaller than \(\lambda_f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full step is uncontrolled when it is taken without the intrinsic small-step certificate supplied by self-concordance. The designation includes steps whose scaled decrement is at least one and computations for which the decrement or Hessian metric cannot be trusted. Such a step may leave the domain or fail to contract, but the definition asserts absence of a guarantee rather than inevitable failure.
assumptions_latex: The proposed update uses multiplier one.
The classical certificate is evaluated in the local Hessian norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step is uncontrolled whenever \(M_f\lambda_f(x)\ge1\) or the decrement certificate cannot be validly evaluated; contraction control additionally requires a stricter verified threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(\|x^{\mathrm N}-x\|_x=\lambda_f(x)\), feasibility control is exactly the strict local-radius test \(\|x^{\mathrm N}-x\|_x<1/M_f\).
special_cases_latex: A point with \(M_f\lambda_f(x)<1\) has a domain-feasible full step, though decrement contraction may still require a smaller threshold.
immediate_consequences_latex: An uncontrolled full step should be replaced by damping, line search, trust-region control, or another justified safeguard if a guarantee is required.
boundary_notes: Uncontrolled does not mean that the step must fail on the particular instance.
The strict inequality cannot be replaced by equality in the general Dikin-domain certificate.
Approximate Newton directions require their own error-aware radius test.

children.title: Singular or Ill-Conditioned Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Failure of reliable direction computation despite valid function theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular or Ill-Conditioned Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-concordance permits flat directions unless positive definiteness is imposed; then the Newton inverse is undefined, while near-flat directions make computed steps highly error-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The convex function \(f(x_1,x_2)=-\log x_1\) on \((0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\) is standard self-concordant, but
\[
\nabla^2f(x_1,x_2)=
\begin{pmatrix}x_1^{-2}&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
is singular. Hence \(\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\), the usual Newton direction, and the inverse-Hessian decrement are not defined on the ambient space. More generally, when a positive-definite Hessian is numerically ill-conditioned, small gradient or solve perturbations can produce large direction errors in the ambient norm. Exact self-concordant inequalities do not replace nonsingularity and adequate numerical solution of the Newton system.
assumptions_latex: Convex self-concordance is allowed without strict convexity or a uniformly nonsingular Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton direction and decrement may be undefined, and near-singularity makes their numerical computation arbitrarily sensitive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic failure when intrinsic Hessian geometry is degenerate or poorly resolved.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Global Complexity Bounds p. 268

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular and Ill-Conditioned Local Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F\in C^2(D)\) be convex on an open convex set \(D\subset E\), and fix \(x\in D\). Write \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x):E\to E^*\) and \(g_x=\nabla F(x)\). A Newton direction is a solution of \(H_xd=-g_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact arithmetic definition. Singularity is intrinsic, whereas ill-conditioning is relative to specified primal and dual norms or to a chosen coordinate representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Newton system at \(x\) is singular if \(\ker H_x\neq\{0\}\). It is consistent singular when \(-g_x\in\operatorname{range}H_x\), in which case its solution set is \(d_0+\ker H_x\); it is inconsistent singular when \(-g_x\notin\operatorname{range}H_x\). Given norms on \(E\) and \(E^*\), an invertible Newton system is \(\kappa\)-ill-conditioned when \(\operatorname{cond}(H_x)=\|H_x\|\,\|H_x^{-1}\|\geq\kappa\). For a positive-semidefinite self-adjoint matrix representation, \(\operatorname{cond}_2(H_x)=\lambda_{\max}(H_x)/\lambda_{\min}(H_x)\), with value \(+\infty\) when \(\lambda_{\min}(H_x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an interior point \(x\), the Newton equation is \(H_xd=-g_x\). It is singular exactly when the Hessian has a nonzero null direction. A singular system is consistent if the negative gradient lies in the Hessian range and inconsistent otherwise. An invertible system is ill-conditioned relative to chosen norms when \(\|H_x\|\|H_x^{-1}\|\) is large. For a positive-semidefinite symmetric matrix in Euclidean coordinates, this condition number is the ratio of its largest to smallest eigenvalue and is infinite in the singular case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker H_x\neq\{0\}\) characterizes singularity, while \(\|H_x\|\|H_x^{-1}\|\geq\kappa\) characterizes the selected ill-conditioning threshold for invertible \(H_x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For self-adjoint \(H_x\succeq0\), singularity is equivalent to \(\inf_{\|h\|_2=1}\langle H_xh,h\rangle=0\).

If \(H_x\) is nonsingular, the squared Newton decrement is \(\lambda_F(x)^2=\langle g_x,H_x^{-1}g_x\rangle\); this inverse formula is unavailable for a singular Hessian unless a generalized inverse and compatibility convention are introduced.
special_cases_latex: When \(g_x\in\operatorname{range}H_x\), the minimum-norm Newton direction is \(-H_x^{\dagger}g_x\), where \(H_x^{\dagger}\) is the Moore--Penrose inverse relative to an inner product.
immediate_consequences_latex: A consistent singular system does not determine a unique direction.
A large condition number permits small perturbations of \(H_x\) or \(g_x\) to produce large relative changes in the computed direction.
boundary_notes: Ill-conditioning has no coordinate-free numerical threshold until norms or a scaling are fixed.
A singular Hessian does not contradict the generalized definition of a self-concordant barrier; the inverse-Hessian form of gradient control requires nondegeneracy.

children.title: Incompatible Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Derivative or solve errors exceeding intrinsic tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Inexactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error larger than the squared decrement can dominate the local Newton remainder; a nonzero admissible residual can move even an exact minimizer to a point with nonzero decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an approximate direction satisfying \(\nabla^2f(x)d=-\nabla f(x)+r\), the term \(\|r\|_x^*\) enters the next intrinsic residual in addition to the quadratic self-concordant remainder. Thus preservation of quadratic decrement contraction requires local residual control on the scale \(\|r\|_x^*=O(\lambda(x)^2)\). For a concrete failure, take \(f(x)=x-\log x\) at its minimizer \(x^*=1\). Here \(f'(1)=0\) and \(f''(1)=1\). For any \(c\in(-1,\infty)\setminus\{0\}\), choosing \(r=c\) gives \(d=c\), so the next point is \(1+c\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and its decrement is \(|c|\). Therefore an uncontrolled additive residual can move an exact minimizer to a point with nonzero decrement, and exact local contraction cannot be guaranteed unless the residual decreases at the required intrinsic scale.
assumptions_latex: No bound ties the residual \(r\) to the current Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quadratic contraction and exact-convergence guarantees can fail; even at an exact minimizer, a nonzero admissible residual can produce a nonzero next decrement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of local contraction when approximation errors exceed intrinsic residual scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexactness Incompatible with the Local Newton Metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\in C^2(D)\) be convex on an open convex set \(D\subset E\), with \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\). Define \(\|h\|_x=\langle H_xh,h\rangle^{1/2}\) and \(\|s\|_x^*=\langle s,H_x^{-1}s\rangle^{1/2}\). Suppose an approximate direction \(\widetilde d\) is computed from approximate derivative data \(\widetilde g\) and \(\widetilde H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local, deterministic definition relative to a stated admissible forcing tolerance. It does not select a universal tolerance or assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta(x)\in[0,1)\) be the residual tolerance required by a specified inexact Newton theorem, and define the true-system residual \(r_x=H_x\widetilde d+g_x\). The direction computation is compatible at \(x\) when \(\|r_x\|_x^*\leq\eta(x)\|g_x\|_x^*\), together with every derivative-approximation condition required to ensure that \(\widetilde H\) induces an equivalent positive-definite local metric. It is incompatible when at least one required condition fails; in particular, when \(\|r_x\|_x^*>\eta(x)\|g_x\|_x^*\), when \(\widetilde H\not\succ0\), or when the stipulated spectral comparison \((1-\delta)H_x\preceq\widetilde H\preceq(1+\delta)H_x\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix the exact local Hessian metric and the residual or derivative-error tolerances required by the inexact Newton result being used. An approximate solve is compatible if its residual in the dual local norm is at most the permitted fraction of the exact gradient norm and its approximate Hessian satisfies the required positive-definiteness and metric-comparison bounds. It is incompatible if any such intrinsic tolerance is exceeded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde d\) has incompatible inexactness at \(x\) exactly when the declared admissibility predicate for the chosen inexact Newton regime is false.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(d_N=-H_x^{-1}g_x\), then \(r_x=H_x(\widetilde d-d_N)\) and hence \(\|r_x\|_x^*=\|\widetilde d-d_N\|_x\). Thus the residual test is equivalent to \(\|\widetilde d-d_N\|_x\leq\eta(x)\|d_N\|_x\).
special_cases_latex: For an exact Hessian and an iterative linear solver, only the residual condition remains.
At a stationary point with \(g_x=0\), a relative residual rule forces \(r_x=0\); an absolute tolerance must be specified if nonzero residual is intended.
immediate_consequences_latex: Compatibility is theorem-relative: changing the admissible forcing sequence changes the classification.
Euclidean residual control alone need not imply local-dual-norm control when \(H_x\) is ill-conditioned.
boundary_notes: No supplied source was found that canonically names this predicate “incompatible inexactness” with these exact quantifiers.
This definition does not claim that every incompatible step diverges; it states only that the hypotheses of the selected inexact Newton guarantee are not met.

notation.meaning: residual in the exact Newton equation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain Geometry Induced by a Self-Concordant Barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subset E\) be nonempty, open, and convex, and let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Set \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x)\), \(\|h\|_x=\langle H_xh,h\rangle^{1/2}\), and \(W_F(x;r)=\{x+h:\|h\|_x<r\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic finite-dimensional geometry on directions where the Hessian is positive definite; quotient conventions are required if the Hessian is degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The barrier domain geometry of \((D,F)\) consists of the local Hessian seminorms \(\|\cdot\|_x\), their dual seminorms, and the associated Dikin sets. Under the standard normalization, the unit Dikin ellipsoid satisfies \(W_F(x;1)\subset D\) whenever \(H_x\succ0\). The barrier property further requires finite-boundary isolation: if \(x_k\in D\) and \(x_k\to\bar x\in\partial D\), then \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\). The barrier-specific gradient geometry is \(|\langle\nabla F(x),h\rangle|\leq\sqrt\nu\|h\|_x\) for all \(x\in D\) and \(h\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-concordant barrier equips its open convex domain with the Hessian local metric. The open unit Dikin ellipsoid at an interior point remains in the domain, finite boundary points are separated by blow-up of the barrier value, and the barrier gradient is uniformly bounded in the dual local metric by the square root of the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_F(x;1)\subset D\), boundary blow-up holds at every finite boundary point, and \(\|\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\leq\sqrt\nu\) whenever the inverse-Hessian norm is defined.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
When \(H_x\succ0\), \(\|
abla F(x)\|_x^*=\langle
abla F(x),H_x^{-1}
abla F(x)angle^{1/2}\).
The Dikin inclusion is equivalently \(\{h:\langle H_xh,h\rangle<1\}\subset D-x\).
special_cases_latex: For \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln x_i\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^m\), \(\|h\|_x^2=\sum_i(h_i/x_i)^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Local distances and admissible full steps are affine invariant under injective affine coordinate changes.
The local metric becomes increasingly restrictive in directions approaching a regular finite boundary.
boundary_notes: The boundary blow-up condition concerns finite boundary points; recession to infinity is a distinct regime.
If \(D\) contains lineality and \(H_x\) is degenerate along it, the geometry is naturally interpreted on a quotient space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Boundary and Recession Regimes of a Barrier Domain
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subset E\) be a nonempty open convex set, let \(Q=\operatorname{cl}D\), and let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a barrier. Define \(\operatorname{rec}Q=\{d\in E:x+td\in Q\ \forall x\in Q,\ t\geq0\}\) and \(\operatorname{lin}Q=\operatorname{rec}Q\cap(-\operatorname{rec}Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates convergence to finite boundary points from escape along recession directions in a finite-dimensional closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((x_k)\subset D\) is in the finite-boundary regime when \(x_k\to\bar x\in\partial Q\); a barrier isolates this regime when \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\) for every such sequence. It is in a recession regime when \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\) and, after normalization or parametrization, it follows a direction \(d\in\operatorname{rec}Q\). A two-sided recession direction belongs to \(\operatorname{lin}Q\) and generates a line \(x+\mathbb Rd\subset Q\). Thus finite-boundary blow-up does not by itself prescribe the behavior of \(F\) along recession or lineality directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of an open convex barrier domain has three geometrically distinct behaviors. Approaching a finite boundary point must make a barrier diverge to infinity. Escaping to infinity may occur along a recession direction and is not a finite-boundary approach. A direction that is feasible in both signs is lineality and produces an entire affine line in the closed domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial Q\), \(\operatorname{rec}Q\), and \(\operatorname{lin}Q\) define distinct finite-boundary, one-sided recession, and two-sided lineality regimes for \((D,F)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in\operatorname{lin}Q\) if and only if \(x+td\in Q\) for every \(x\in Q\) and every \(t\in\mathbb R\).
For closed convex \(Q\), membership of \(d\) in \(\operatorname{rec}Q\) can be checked from any fixed \(x\in Q\) by requiring \(x+td\in Q\) for all \(t\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Q\) is bounded, \(\operatorname{rec}Q=\{0\}\), so only the finite-boundary regime is nontrivial.
If \(Q\) is a pointed cone, \(\operatorname{lin}Q=\{0\}\) but nonzero recession directions remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Universal-barrier constructions that exclude straight lines are naturally applied after removing lineality.
Boundary blow-up cannot be inferred merely from growth along rays to infinity.
boundary_notes: The phrase “boundary at infinity” is descriptive and is not identified with the Euclidean boundary \(\partial Q\).
Relative-boundary conventions are needed when the represented set is not full-dimensional in its ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Open Convex Barrier Domains
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier domain is a nonempty convex set open in its affine hull; the extended barrier is finite precisely there and diverges toward its relative boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An open convex barrier domain is a nonempty convex set \(D\subseteq E\) that is open relative to \(\operatorname{aff}D\). Equivalently, \(D=\operatorname{ri}(\overline D)\), where closure and relative interior are taken in \(\operatorname{aff}D\). A barrier on \(D\) is represented as an extended-real convex function \(F:E\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) with \(\operatorname{dom}F=D\), whose restriction to \(D\) is finite and smooth and whose values diverge when a sequence in \(D\) approaches the relative boundary.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is a finite-dimensional real vector space \(E\).
The effective domain \(D\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is the relative interior of its closure in \(\operatorname{aff}D\), and a barrier is finite exactly on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Openness is relative to the affine hull, allowing lower-dimensional convex domains.

notation.meaning: barrier function extended by positive infinity

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Boundary Isolation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite boundary regime is convergence of domain points to an ordinary relative-boundary point, rather than unbounded escape; it does not require that the boundary point be isolated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional affine space \(A\). A sequence \((x_k)\subset D\) approaches a finite boundary point when there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\) such that \(x_k\to\bar x\) in \(A\). Such convergence implies that \((x_k)\) is bounded and therefore excludes escape to infinity. The word “finite” does not assert that \(\bar x\) is an isolated point of \(\operatorname{rbd}D\).
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional affine space \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sequence \((x_k)\subset D\) approaches the finite boundary point \(\bar x\) when \(x_k\to\bar x\) in \(A\); every such sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here “finite” means convergence to an ordinary point of the affine space, in contrast with unbounded escape; it does not mean that the boundary point is topologically isolated.

notation.meaning: relative boundary in the affine space

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1 Lower Semicontinuous Convex Functions p. 157

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Blow-Up Behavior
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier blows up along every domain sequence converging to a finite relative-boundary point; equivalently, its extension by positive infinity is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The boundary blow-up property requires that, for every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\) and every sequence \((x_k)\subset D\) with \(x_k\to\bar x\), one has \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\). If \(F\) is continuous on \(D\), this is equivalent to lower semicontinuity on \(A\) of the extension \(\overline F:A\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) defined by \(\overline F(x)=F(x)\) for \(x\in D\) and \(\overline F(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\notin D\).
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an open convex barrier domain in a finite-dimensional affine space \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary blow-up means that \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x_k\in D\) and \(x_k\to\bar x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\); equivalently, the extension of \(F\) by \(+\infty\) outside \(D\) is lower semicontinuous on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This property concerns finite relative-boundary points and does not assert coercivity along unbounded sequences.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.2 Definition of self-concordant barriers p. 193

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Boundary Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary point is nonisolated when distinct boundary points converge to it; this is stronger than approximation by interior points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A boundary point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\) lies in a nonisolated boundary regime when every relative neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) contains a distinct boundary point, equivalently \((U\setminus\{\bar x\})\cap\operatorname{rbd}D\neq\varnothing\). Thus there exists a sequence \((y_k)\subset\operatorname{rbd}D\setminus\{\bar x\}\) with \(y_k\to\bar x\). This condition is separate from the always-valid existence of interior sequences \((x_k)\subset D\) converging to \(\bar x\).
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a nonempty relatively open convex set in a finite-dimensional affine space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary is nonisolated at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(\bar x\in\overline{\operatorname{rbd}D\setminus\{\bar x\}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The condition concerns accumulation within the boundary, not merely approximation of a boundary point from the interior.

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Barrier Gradient Control
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The barrier parameter bounds the gradient's dual norm in the local Hessian metric by the square root of that parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in D\) and direction \(h\) in the translation space of \(\operatorname{aff}D\), a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier satisfies \[|\langle
abla F(x),hangle|\le\sqrt{
u}\,\sqrt{\langle
abla^2F(x)h,hangle}.\] Equivalently, \(\|
abla F(x)\|_{x,*}\le\sqrt{
u}\). The inequality is intrinsic: under an invertible affine reparameterization of the domain, both sides transform together and the same parameter \(
u\) remains valid.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\).
The local norm is induced by the positive-definite Hessian of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla F(x)\|_{x,*}\le\sqrt{\nu}\) for every \(x\in D\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intrinsic Gradient Bound and Barrier Parameter
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a standard self-concordant function on an open convex set \(D\subset E\). At \(x\in D\), let \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x)\) and \(\|h\|_x^2=\langle H_xh,h\rangle\).

The intrinsic barrier gradient bound with parameter \(
u\geq0\) is the quantified inequality \[\langle

children.title: Dimensional-Lineality Reduction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reductions required for empty-interior, nonpointed, or non-full-dimensional domains.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-Hull and Lineality Reduction of Barrier Domains
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\) be a nonempty closed convex set, \(A=\operatorname{aff}Q\), \(V=A-A\), and \(L=\operatorname{lin}Q\subset V\). Let \(\pi:V\to V/L\) be the quotient map and choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{ri}Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional reduction used before applying full-dimensional pointed-domain barrier theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dimensional-lineality reduction of \(Q\) is the two-stage replacement \[Q\subset E\longmapsto Q_A=Q-x_0\subset V\longmapsto\widehat Q=\pi(Q_A)\subset V/L.\] The first stage replaces ambient interior by relative interior: \(\operatorname{int}_V(Q_A)=\operatorname{ri}_E(Q)-x_0\neq\varnothing\). The second removes all two-sided recession directions: \(\operatorname{lin}\widehat Q=\{0\}\). A reduced barrier is a function \(\widehat F:\operatorname{int}\widehat Q\to\mathbb R\); its pullback \(F(x)=\widehat F(\pi(x-x_0))\) is constant on cosets parallel to \(L\) and has Hessian kernel containing \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First restrict a non-full-dimensional convex set to its affine hull, where its relative interior becomes an ordinary interior. Then quotient the direction space by the lineality subspace. The resulting closed convex set is full-dimensional in its own space and pointed. A barrier on the quotient pulls back to a barrier that is constant along lineality directions and consequently has a degenerate Hessian there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q=\pi(Q-x_0)\) has nonempty interior in \(V/L\) and no nonzero lineality, while \(F=\widehat F\circ\pi(\cdot-x_0)\) satisfies \(D^2F(x)[\ell,\ell]=0\) for every \(\ell\in L\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Choosing a linear complement \(V=L\oplus W\) identifies \(V/L\) with \(W\) and identifies \(\widehat Q\) with a pointed cross-section of \(Q-x_0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Q\) is full-dimensional and pointed, then \(V=E\), \(L=\{0\}\), and no reduction occurs.
For an affine subspace \(Q=A\), the quotient set is a singleton and contains no nontrivial barrier geometry.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inverse-Hessian formulas should be applied on the reduced space, not along removed lineality directions.
Affine pullbacks can reconstruct the original representation after analysis on the quotient.
boundary_notes: A precise supplied source for the complete affine-hull-plus-quotient calculus was not located.
Quotienting lineality is distinct from projecting away arbitrary recession directions.

notation.meaning: direction space of the affine hull
quotient map onto the lineality-free space

review_flags: Needs an authoritative source explicitly supporting barrier transfer through affine-hull restriction and lineality quotient.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Hull and Lineality Reduction of Barrier Domains
Lower-Dimensional Domain Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine coordinates on the domain's affine hull convert a lower-dimensional barrier problem into a full-dimensional one without changing its parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(u)=x_0+Au\) be an affine isomorphism from \(\mathbb{R}^k\) onto \(\operatorname{aff}D\), and set \(\widehat D=T^{-1}(D)\) and \(\widehat F=F\circ T\). Then \(\widehat D\) is open and convex in \(\mathbb{R}^k\), while \(D=T(\widehat D)\). Its derivatives satisfy \(D^j\widehat F(u)[v_1,\ldots,v_j]=D^jF(Tu)[Av_1,\ldots,Av_j]\) for \(j=1,2,3\). Consequently, the self-concordance inequalities, boundary blow-up, and barrier parameter are identical in the two representations.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is relatively open and convex with affine dimension \(k\).
\(T:\mathbb{R}^k\to\operatorname{aff}D\) is an affine isomorphism and \(F\) is a barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pullback \(\widehat F=F\circ T\) preserves self-concordance, barrier blow-up, and the parameter \(\nu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-domain barrier theory is represented in full-dimensional affine coordinates.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.3 Definition of self-concordant function p. 175

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Space Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function constant along the fibers of a lineality quotient descends uniquely to the quotient, and its Hessian descends there; nondegeneracy requires that lineality account for the entire original Hessian kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq E\) satisfy \(D+L=D\), and let \(\pi:E\to E/L\) be the quotient map. If \(F(x+\ell)=F(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(\ell\in L\), then there is a unique function \(\widetilde F:\pi(D)\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \(F=\widetilde F\circ\pi\) on \(D\). Every derivative of \(F\) vanishes when one of its arguments lies in \(L\), and its Hessian is the pullback of the Hessian of \(\widetilde F\). The quotient Hessian is positive definite precisely when the kernel of \(\nabla^2F(x)\) is exactly \(L\) at every \(x\in D\).
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(L\subseteq E\) is a linear subspace, and \(D\subseteq E\) satisfies \(D+L=D\).
\(F:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is smooth and satisfies \(F(x+\ell)=F(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(\ell\in L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique function \(\widetilde F:\pi(D)\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(F=\widetilde F\circ\pi\), and the Hessian of \(F\) factors through the quotient with \(L\) contained in its kernel.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fiber invariance is required for descent. The quotient Hessian is nondegenerate only under the additional condition that the original Hessian has no kernel beyond the lineality space.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1 General convex functions p. 111

knowledge_statements.title: Pointed Quotient Domains
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quotienting a closed convex cone by its entire lineality space yields a pointed cone and carries relative interiors onto relative interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=K\cap(-K)\) and \(\overline K=\pi(K)\subseteq E/L\). Then \(\overline K\) is a convex cone and is pointed, namely \(\overline K\cap(-\overline K)=\{0\}\). Moreover, \(\pi(\operatorname{ri}K)=\operatorname{ri}\overline K\). Hence any function on \(\operatorname{ri}K\) that is constant on the cosets of \(L\) descends uniquely to \(\operatorname{ri}\overline K\); when the descended function is a self-concordant barrier, its parameter and derivative inequalities are computed on the quotient space.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional vector space.
\(L=K\cap(-K)\) is its lineality space and \(\pi:E\to E/L\) is the quotient map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient cone \(\pi(K)\) is pointed: \(\pi(K)\cap(-\pi(K))=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotienting by all lineality produces the canonical pointed cone supporting nondegenerate conic barrier geometry.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1 General convex functions p. 111

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slice lying inside a quotient fiber can turn a nondegenerate quotient barrier into a constant function, so faithful affine coordinates and exact quotient compatibility are essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Valid affine reduction must supply coordinates for the relevant affine hull, and valid quotient reduction must respect quotient fibers. Let \(D=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\), let \(q:D\to(0,[?25l∞)\) be defined by \(q(x,y)=x\), and let \(F(x,y)=-\log x\), the pullback under \(q\) of the logarithmic barrier on \((0,[?25l∞)\). For the affine embedding \(T:\mathbb{R}\to D\) defined by \(T(t)=(1,t)\), one has \((F\circ T)(t)=0\), so the pullback Hessian vanishes. Thus a slice contained in one quotient fiber loses the nondegenerate quotient barrier geometry and cannot replace affine-hull or lineality reduction.
assumptions_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}\to D\) be the affine embedding \(T(t)=(1,t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(F\) is the pullback under \(q\) of the logarithmic barrier on \((0,\infty)\), the incompatible slice satisfies \((F\circ T)(t)=0\) and loses all Hessian barrier geometry.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The example concerns loss of quotient barrier geometry under a slice lying inside one quotient fiber; it does not claim that the degenerate ambient pullback is itself a nondegenerate barrier on the full affine hull.

notation.meaning: pullback of the logarithmic quotient barrier
affine embedding along a quotient fiber

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hierarchy of General, Logarithmically Homogeneous, and Self-Scaled Barriers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a closed pointed convex cone with nonempty interior. Let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and let \(K^*=\{s\in E^*:\langle s,x\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class hierarchy on proper cones. The final self-scaled level is recorded only schematically because an exact supplied source for its defining scaling axiom was not located.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\) as all self-concordant barriers on \(K\). Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\subset\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\) by the additional identity \(F(tx)=F(x)-\nu\ln t\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(t>0\). Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(K)\subset\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\) by requiring the standard primal--dual self-scaling axiom: the Hessian-induced scaling maps generated by interior points act as cone isomorphisms between \(K\) and \(K^*\), with the corresponding dual-barrier compatibility. Hence \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General self-concordant barriers satisfy the barrier differential inequalities. Logarithmically homogeneous barriers additionally transform by subtracting \(\nu\ln t\) under positive radial scaling. Self-scaled barriers form a still narrower conic class whose Hessian scalings are compatible with the primal and dual cones. These requirements give nested classes, not three synonymous names.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\).

For \(F\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\), logarithmic homogeneity implies \(\langle
abla F(x),xangle=-
u\) and \(
abla^2F(x)x=-
abla F(x)\).
special_cases_latex: The logarithmic barriers on the nonnegative orthant, Lorentz cone, and positive-semidefinite cone belong to the logarithmically homogeneous level.
Canonical barriers on direct products of Lorentz and positive-semidefinite cones inherit logarithmic homogeneity with additive parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every assertion valid for all self-concordant barriers applies to the two narrower classes.
Primal--dual scaling conclusions require the self-scaled level and cannot be inferred from logarithmic homogeneity alone.
boundary_notes: The exact self-scaled axiom varies in presentation and requires a dedicated authoritative locator.
Logarithmic homogeneity is defined only for conic domains closed under positive scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: General Self-Concordant Barriers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general self-concordant barrier has a positive Hessian, satisfies the cubic derivative and parameter-controlled gradient inequalities, and diverges along every domain sequence converging to a finite relative-boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(F\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\) if, for every \(x\in D\) and every direction \(h\) in the translation space of \(A\), \[|D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\le 2 igl(D^2F(x)[h,h] igr)^{3/2}\] and \[|DF(x)[h]|\le\sqrt{
u} igl(D^2F(x)[h,h] igr)^{1/2}.\] In addition, for every \( ar x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\) and every sequence \((x_k)\subset D\) with \(x_k	o ar x\), one has \(F(x_k)	o+\infty\). The Hessian \(
abla^2F(x)\) is positive definite on the translation space of \(A\) for every \(x\in D\).
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a nonempty open convex subset of a finite-dimensional affine space \(A\).
\(F:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and three times continuously differentiable, \(\nu\ge 0\), and \(\nabla^2F(x)\) is positive definite on the translation space of \(A\) for every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier when it satisfies the cubic derivative inequality, the \(\nu\)-gradient inequality, and blow-up at every finite relative-boundary point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the finite-dimensional general-domain definition with standard self-concordance normalization and boundary blow-up quantified pointwise over the relative boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier is logarithmically homogeneous and its Hessians identify the primal and dual cones while satisfying a precise dual-barrier identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier \(F\) is self-scaled if, for every \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\), the Hessian operator maps the cone onto its dual, \[
abla^2F(w)K=K^*,\] and, for every \(x,w\in\operatorname{int}K\), satisfies \[F_*(
abla^2F(w)x)=F(x)-2F(w)-
u.\] Here \(F_*(s)=\sup_{z\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,zangle-F(z)\}\). These identities strengthen logarithmic homogeneity by making each Hessian a primal-to-dual cone isomorphism compatible with the barrier's duality transform.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a regular cone and \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
The dual barrier uses the convention \(F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,x\rangle-F(x)\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Scaled Barrier on a Proper Cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, let \(K^*\subset E^*\) be its dual, and let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) be a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier. Denote \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal--dual cone setting. This candidate states the characteristic scaling structure but requires an exact source for the conventional normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A self-scaled barrier is a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for which the Hessian scaling is compatible with the cone and its dual: for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(H_x\) is a linear isomorphism satisfying \(H_x(\operatorname{int}K)=\operatorname{int}K^*\), and the barrier obeys the standard self-scaling identity relating \(F\), its dual barrier \(F_*\), and the transformation induced by \(H_x\). Equivalently in the symmetric-cone model, every pair of interior primal points admits a cone automorphism under which the canonical barrier changes only by an additive constant, and the associated inverse action scales dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier is not merely logarithmically homogeneous. Its Hessian provides primal-to-dual cone isomorphisms, and these isomorphisms are compatible with the barrier and its Fenchel-dual barrier. On symmetric cones this yields automorphisms that can move any interior point to any other while changing the canonical barrier only by a constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining extra structure is the cone-isomorphism and dual-compatibility property of \(H_x\), beyond self-concordance and logarithmic homogeneity.
special_cases_latex: On \(\mathbb R_+^n\), \(F(x)=-\sum_i\ln x_i\) is the canonical self-scaled barrier.
On \(\mathbb S_+^n\), \(F(X)=-\ln\det X\) supplies the canonical primal--dual matrix scaling.
On a Lorentz cone, \(F(z,t)=-\ln(t^2-\|z\|_2^2)\) supplies the canonical Lorentz scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: The cone must admit the corresponding homogeneous primal--dual scaling structure.
Direct products of canonical symmetric-cone barriers retain blockwise scaling structure.
boundary_notes: No inspected supplied source states the full conventional self-scaled-barrier definition with its normalization.
The transitivity of a cone automorphism group alone is insufficient; barrier compatibility is also required.
