abla F(x(t))=0.\] The path-complexity interpretation of \(
u\) is the pair of controls \[\langle c,x(t)angle-c^*\le rac{
u}{t}\] and \[N(\epsilon)=O\!\left(\sqrt
u\log rac{
u\|c\|_{x_F^*,*}}{\epsilon}ight),\] where \(x_F^*\) is the analytic center and \(N(\epsilon)\) is the number of standard short-step updates needed to obtain objective error at most \(\epsilon\) from a suitably centered start. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each open convex domain \(D_i\) in a finite-dimensional space, let \(F_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier. Parameters below are admissible upper bounds, not necessarily minimal values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional standard self-concordant barriers under finite sums, affine pullbacks, epigraph lifting, and partial minimization with attained unique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Barrier-parameter calculus is the collection of closure rules assigning an admissible parameter to a barrier constructed from known barriers. Its basic rules are: (i) on a nonempty intersection, \[F=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(F)\le\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i;\] (ii) for an affine map \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\), \[F\circ\mathcal A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(F\circ\mathcal A)\le
u(F);\] (iii) for the epigraph construction, \[\widehat F(x,s)=F(x)-\log(s-F(x))\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(\widehat F)\le
u(F)+1;\] and (iv) if \(\Phi(x,y)\) has parameter \(
u\) and \(y(x)\) is the unique attained minimizer, then \[G(x)=\min_y\Phi(x,y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(G)\le
u.\] These assignments permit parameters to be propagated through explicit formulations without recomputing the defining gradient inequality from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-parameter calculus consists of closure rules for barriers built from other barriers. Parameters add when barriers are summed over intersected constraints or independent blocks. An affine pullback does not increase the inherited parameter. The standard epigraph lift adds one. Partial minimization over uniquely attained auxiliary variables preserves the parameter upper bound. Every resulting number is an admissible upper bound and can exceed the smallest possible parameter of the resulting domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The calculus maps sums, affine pullbacks, epigraph lifts, and admissible partial minimizations to the parameter bounds \(\sum_i
u_i\), \(
u\), \(
u+1\), and \(
u\), respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The sum rule covers intersections in one space and Cartesian products after coordinate pullback.
An affine slice is the pullback by the inclusion map of the affine subspace.
special_cases_latex: The logarithmic barrier \(-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) for a polyhedron has the calculus bound \(\nu=m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Repeated epigraph lifting adds one parameter unit per standard lift.
Eliminating auxiliary variables by admissible partial minimization cannot worsen the inherited parameter bound.
boundary_notes: The calculus gives representation-dependent upper bounds and does not establish parameter optimality.
The partial-minimization rule requires the regularity and attainment conditions stated in the implicit-barrier construction.

u_i.\] More generally, if constraints are represented by affine maps \(\mathcal A_i:E	o E_i\), then \[D=\{x:\mathcal A_i(x)\in D_i\  orall i\},\qquad F(x)=\sum_iF_i(\mathcal A_i(x))\] inherits the same bound \(\sum_i
u_i\). The block-product rule is the special case in which each \(\mathcal A_i\) is a coordinate projection; the ordinary intersection rule uses identity maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The separable sum of barriers on independent blocks is a barrier for the Cartesian product, and the sum of barriers defined on one space is a barrier for the intersection of their domains. In either case the inherited parameter is the sum of the component parameters. The same formula applies to combined affine constraint representations. This is parameter accounting for a chosen construction, so the resulting sum may be larger than the smallest parameter available for the product or intersection itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
u(F_{	imes})\le\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i,\qquad 
u(F_{\cap})\le\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A product is an intersection of coordinate-pullback domains \(\{x:\pi_i(x)\in D_i\}\).
Combined constraints represented by \(F_i\circ\mathcal A_i\) have aggregate parameter at most \(\sum_i\nu_i\).
special_cases_latex: For \(D=\mathbb R_{++}^m\), summing the one-dimensional barriers \(-\log x_i\) gives parameter \(m\).
For inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\), the sum of the one-dimensional logarithmic barriers has parameter at most the number of inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adding one represented constraint block increases the calculus parameter by at most that block's parameter.
Block separability makes the Hessian block diagonal, although parameter additivity alone does not quantify the cost of exploiting that structure.
boundary_notes: Nonempty interior is required for the resulting barrier domain.
Parameter additivity is an upper-bound rule; equality requires a separate optimality result.

notation.meaning: Separable barrier on a Cartesian product.
Parameter supplied by the construction calculus.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Domain Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of finitely many component barriers is a barrier on the Cartesian product with certified parameter equal to the sum of the component parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\prod_{i=1}^mK_i\) and \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i)\). Then \(F\) is a \(\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\right)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K\). The displayed sum is a certified parameter and need not be minimal.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(K_i\subset\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F_i:K_i\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i)\) is a \(\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\right)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K:=\prod_{i=1}^mK_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Cartesian products equipped with the unweighted sum of their component barriers.

notation.meaning: Sum barrier on the product domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-Domain Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing finitely many component barriers on their nonempty intersection yields a barrier whose certified parameter is the sum of the component parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\bigcap_{i=1}^mK_i\) be nonempty and define \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i|_K\). Then \(F\) is a \(\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\right)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K\). The parameter sum is a certificate rather than a minimality assertion.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(K_i\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(F_i:K_i\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i|_K\) is a \(\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\right)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections represented by summing barriers defined in one ambient space.

notation.meaning: Sum of the restricted component barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Parameter Accounting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameters add when finitely many barriers are summed, but the total is a decomposition-dependent upper bound and need not be minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite barrier sum \(F:=F_1+\cdots+F_m\), the standard sum calculus gives \(
u(F)\leq
u_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i\). This accounting is associative and independent of the order of finite summation. The value \(
u_{\mathrm{sum}}\) is attached to the displayed decomposition and need not be the smallest admissible parameter.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(F_i\) is a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier, and all restrictions needed to form \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\) are defined on a common nonempty open convex domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The finite-sum calculus certifies \(F\) with parameter \(
u(F)\leq
u_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter bookkeeping for finite barrier sums; the aggregate certificate need not be minimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Representation Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating the logarithmic term for one positivity constraint raises the certified parameter from one to the number of duplicates without changing the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=(0,\infty)\) and \(r\geq1\), summing \(r\) identical logarithmic terms gives \(F_r(x):=-r\log x\). This is a standard self-concordant barrier satisfying \(\|\nabla F_r(x)\|_{x,*}^2=r\), so its certified parameter is \(r\). Thus duplicate constraint terms can raise the certificate from \(1\) to \(r\) without changing \(K\).
assumptions_latex: The domain \(K:=(0,\infty)\) is represented by \(r\) duplicate positivity constraints, and their logarithmic barrier terms are summed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_r(x):=-r\log x\) has certified self-concordant barrier parameter \(r\), although the represented domain remains \(K=(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional duplicate-constraint example demonstrating representation-dependent parameter inflation.

notation.meaning: Barrier produced by the duplicated representation.
Squared intrinsic dual gradient norm of the barrier.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter preservation under affine pullback and restriction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E,E_1\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(D\subset E_1\) be open and convex, and let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Let \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\) be affine.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine preimages and affine slices having nonempty relative interior. The result supplies an inherited parameter; degeneracy can prevent the pullback Hessian from being positive definite on an unreduced ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine pullback domain and barrier are \[D_{\mathcal A}:=\{x\in E:\mathcal A(x)\in D\},\qquad F_{\mathcal A}(x):=F(\mathcal A(x)).\] Affine pullback-slice calculus assigns \(F_{\mathcal A}\) the same admissible parameter \(
u\), because for every \(x\in D_{\mathcal A}\) and \(h\in E\), \[\langle
abla F_{\mathcal A}(x),hangle=\langle
abla F(\mathcal A x),Ahangle,\quad \langle
abla^2F_{\mathcal A}(x)h,hangle=\langle
abla^2F(\mathcal A x)Ah,Ahangle.\] If \(L=x_0+V\) is an affine subspace meeting \(D\), choose an affine parametrization \(\iota:V	o L\). The restriction \(F|_{D\cap L}\), represented as \(F\circ\iota\) on \(\iota^{-1}(D)\), therefore inherits parameter at most \(
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a ν-self-concordant barrier with an affine map produces a barrier on the affine preimage and does not increase the inherited parameter. Restricting a barrier to an affine slice is the same construction applied to an affine parametrization of that slice. The local metric is pulled back through the linear part of the map, so both the directional derivative and Hessian quadratic form are tested on the image direction Ah.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
u(F\circ\mathcal A)\le
u(F),\qquad 
u(F|_{D\cap L})\le
u(F).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an inclusion \(\iota:L\hookrightarrow E_1\), affine restriction is the pullback \(F\circ\iota\).
An equality-constrained feasible set \(D\cap\{x:Bx=d\}\) uses the restriction of \(F\) to the affine solution space.
special_cases_latex: Restricting \(-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) to \(\{x:Bx=d\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\) retains the admissible parameter \(n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Invertible affine changes of coordinates preserve the minimal parameter exactly, by applying the rule in both directions.
An affine formulation can inherit a parameter determined by its lifted or cone domain even when the slice itself admits a smaller barrier.
boundary_notes: When \(A\) has a nontrivial nullspace, the pullback Hessian is singular along that nullspace; a reduced affine parametrization removes redundant directions.
The rule does not state that the inherited value is optimal for the preimage or slice.

notation.meaning: Affine preimage of the barrier domain.

source_refs.locator: Theorem 5.3.3, affine transformation of a self-concordant barrier, p. 375; affine restriction example in Section 5.4.3, p. 391 in the extracted text

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Pullback Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pulling a barrier back through an injective affine map preserves its certified parameter as an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) be nonempty, where \(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective. Then the affine pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\). Thus an injective affine pullback does not increase the certified parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
\(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G:D\to\mathbb{R}\), \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\), is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical positive-definite formulation, with injectivity excluding null directions in the pullback Hessian.

notation.meaning: Affine preimage of the original barrier domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Slice Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expressing a nonempty affine slice in injective coordinates preserves the original barrier parameter as an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:=x_0+\operatorname{range}(U)\) and \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:x_0+Uz\in K\}\), where \(U\) is injective and \(D\neq\varnothing\). Then \(G(z):=F(x_0+Uz)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\). Accordingly, restriction to an affine slice does not increase the certified parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
\(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(U:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective, and \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:x_0+Uz\in K\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G:D\to\mathbb{R}\), \(G(z):=F(x_0+Uz)\), is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction to a nonempty affine slice expressed in injective reduced coordinates.

notation.meaning: Affine slice in the original space.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Pullback Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient affine pullback has a singular Hessian and becomes a classical barrier only after its null directions are removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\ker A
eq\{0\}\), then the pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) has Hessian \(
abla^2G(y)=A^{\mathsf T}
abla^2F(Ay+b)A\), which is singular on \(D\). Hence \(G\) is not a classical self-concordant barrier on the full parameter space. A quotient construction or complementary reduced coordinates are required.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a self-concordant barrier with positive-definite Hessian.
\(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has a nontrivial kernel, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) has singular Hessian on \(D\) and is not a classical self-concordant barrier on the full space \(\mathbb{R}^p\); null directions must first be removed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the classical positive-definite barrier definition under a rank-deficient parameterization.

notation.meaning: Null directions of the linear map.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Parameter Preservation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing coordinates complementary to the affine map's kernel restores a nondegenerate pullback with the original parameter bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:=\operatorname{rank}A\geq1\) and choose \(U:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(\mathbb{R}^p=\ker A\oplus\operatorname{range}(U)\). On \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^q:A(y_0+Uz)+b\in K\}\), the reduced pullback \(H(z):=F(A(y_0+Uz)+b)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Removing the null coordinates therefore does not increase the certified parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H:D\to\mathbb{R}\), \(H(z):=F(A(y_0+Uz)+b)\), is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of precisely the affine-map null directions before applying injective affine invariance.

notation.meaning: Direct-sum reduction removing exactly the null directions of A.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Representation Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular lifted barrier can be minimized over auxiliary variables to obtain a barrier for the projection without increasing the lift's aggregate parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=
\operatorname{proj}_xL\) and define the marginal \(F(x)=
\inf\{G(x,z):(x,z)\in L\}\). Under unique interior attainment and the stated nondegeneracy, differentiation through the minimizer gives the Schur-complement Hessian of \(G\). The self-concordance and barrier-gradient inequalities then pass to the marginal without increasing \(\nu\), so \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(K\). If the lifted barrier is assembled from independent factors, their parameters are first added; that aggregate parameter is therefore inherited as an upper bound after projection.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is open and convex, and \(G:L\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
For every \(x\) in \(K=\operatorname{proj}_xL\), the minimizer \(z(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z:(x,z)\in L}G(x,z)\) exists uniquely.
The marginal Hessian is positive definite on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(F(x)=\inf_{z:(x,z)\in L}G(x,z)
\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for the projected domain \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth partial minimization of a lifted barrier; epigraph and perspective formulations require verifying the stated attainment conditions.

notation.meaning: Lifted feasible set and its projection.
Barrier obtained by eliminating lifted variables.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The partial-minimization claim requires an authoritative projection theorem and careful hypotheses ensuring finiteness, smooth attainment, self-concordance, gradient-parameter preservation, and barrier behavior at the projected boundary. Its mathematical role is also closer to a property/theorem than a representation record.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter accounting for epigraph and auxiliary-variable lifts
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\subset E\). Separately, let \(\Phi\) be a \(\mu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex lifted domain \(\widehat D\subset E\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard epigraph lifting and implicit barriers obtained by uniquely attained partial minimization. General perspectives or arbitrary projections require separate hypotheses and are not included automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the epigraph lift \[\operatorname{epi}^{\circ}f:=\{(x,s)\in D\times\mathbb R:s>f(x)\},\] the standard lifted barrier is \[F_{\mathrm{epi}}(x,s):=f(x)-\log(s-f(x)),\] and its calculus parameter is \(\nu+1\). For an auxiliary-variable representation whose projected domain is \[D_{\mathrm{proj}}:=\{x:\exists y\text{ with }(x,y)\in\widehat D\},\] suppose that for every \(x\in D_{\mathrm{proj}}\), the minimizer \(y(x)=\arg\min_y\Phi(x,y)\) exists and is unique. The implicit barrier \[F_{\mathrm{proj}}(x):=\min_y\Phi(x,y)\] inherits parameter \(\mu\). A lifted-representation parameter is the admissible parameter assigned to the barrier on the lifted space before elimination, together with the parameter inherited by the projected implicit barrier after admissible elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard epigraph of a ν-self-concordant barrier has a barrier obtained by adding a logarithmic slack term, and this construction increases the parameter by one. For a more general lifted domain with auxiliary variables, partial minimization of its barrier preserves the parameter when the minimizing auxiliary variable exists uniquely at every projected point. These rules distinguish parameter accounting in the lifted representation from the parameter of the resulting projected barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
u(F_{\mathrm{epi}})\le
u+1,\qquad 
u(F_{\mathrm{proj}})\le\mu.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The epigraph slack \(r=s-f(x)>0\) contributes the one-dimensional logarithmic-barrier parameter \(1\).
The implicit barrier is the value function of the lifted barrier over each projection fiber.
special_cases_latex: Repeated standard epigraph lifts give the calculus bound \(\nu+k\) after \(k\) lifts.
If no auxiliary variables are present, partial minimization is vacuous and the parameter remains \(\mu\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Projection through an implicit-barrier construction need not add to the lifted parameter.
A compact extended formulation can improve structural evaluation costs while carrying a parameter inherited from the lifted domain.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary projection does not by itself define a computable implicit barrier; attainment, uniqueness, and regularity are material.
Perspective constructions are not covered unless realized by a supported affine, epigraph, or implicit-barrier operation.

notation.meaning: Standard barrier for the open epigraph.
Implicit barrier obtained by minimizing over auxiliary variables.

children.title: Barrier-Parameter Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Lower, universal upper, and structure-sensitive bounds on barrier quality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower, universal, and structure-sensitive parameter bounds
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a closed convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior and no lines, let \(\mathcal B(Q)\) denote its standard self-concordant barriers, and define the intrinsic optimal parameter \(\nu_*(Q)=\inf_{F\in\mathcal B(Q)}\nu(F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional full-dimensional convex domains. The classification concerns mathematical parameter bounds and separates them from computability of the corresponding barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A barrier-parameter bound family is an inequality for \(
u_*(Q)\) or for the parameter of an explicit barrier, classified by the information used. A lower-bound family has the form \[L(Q)\le
u_*(Q),\] where \(L(Q)\) follows from intrinsic geometry such as recession directions or a canonical cone. A universal upper-bound family has the form \[
u_*(Q)\le U(n)\] for every admissible \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\), independent of an explicit representation. A structure-sensitive family provides a computable barrier \(F_{\mathcal R}\) from representation data \(\mathcal R\) and an estimate \[
u_*(Q)\le
u(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R).\] The three inequalities answer different questions: impossibility of too small a parameter, existence based only on dimension, and attainable quality from specified algebraic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-parameter bounds fall into three distinct families. Intrinsic lower bounds limit the smallest parameter any barrier on the domain can have. Universal upper bounds guarantee the existence of a parameter controlled only by ambient dimension. Structure-sensitive bounds attach an explicit, preferably computable barrier and parameter to representation data such as inequalities, cone blocks, or spectral structure. These bounds need not coincide, and only the third automatically supplies an explicit barrier oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical comparison is \[L(Q)\le\nu_*(Q)\le\min\{U(n),\ S(\mathcal R)\},\] whenever the representation-specific construction \(\mathcal R\) is available.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The gap \(S(\mathcal R)-\nu_*(Q)\) measures parameter loss attributable to the selected construction.
Taking a supremum over all \(n\)-dimensional domains converts universal existence bounds into bounds on a worst-case optimal parameter.
special_cases_latex: For \(Q=\mathbb R_+^n\), the logarithmic barrier and the lower bound both give \(\nu_*(Q)=n\).
The universal barrier yields an upper bound \(U(n)=c n\) for an absolute constant \(c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A universal existence result can be optimal in dimension order while being unsuitable computationally.
An explicit structural barrier can beat a coarse universal constant without attaining \(\nu_*(Q)\).
boundary_notes: Bounds for a particular represented barrier must not be confused with lower bounds applying to every barrier on the domain.
Dimension may refer to the effective affine hull rather than a redundant ambient representation.

notation.meaning: Infimum of admissible parameters over barriers on Q.
Structure-sensitive parameter bound for representation R.

children.title: Dimension-Dependent Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic obstructions to arbitrarily small barrier parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some n-dimensional convex domains require barrier parameter proportional to n, ruling out a dimension-independent universal parameter bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There is a universal constant \(c>0\) and a family of full-dimensional open convex domains \(K_n\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) such that every standard \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K_n\) satisfies \[
u\geq c n.\] Equivalently, \(
u_{\mathrm{sc}}(K_n)
\geq c n\). Thus no universal construction can assign barriers of dimension-independent parameter to all convex domains. The assertion is worst-case over domains and does not preclude smaller parameters for particular structured families.
assumptions_latex: Barrier parameters use the standard self-concordant gradient inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(n\)-dimensional convex domains \(K_n\) with \(\nu_{\mathrm{sc}}(K_n)\geq c n\) for a universal constant \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case existential lower bound, not a claim that every full-dimensional domain requires a parameter linear in dimension.

notation.meaning: Infimum of admissible self-concordant barrier parameters for a domain.
A universal positive constant independent of dimension.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the lower-bound leaf, but no cited source identifies a domain family or proves the asserted universal linear lower bound for general standard self-concordant barriers. The lower-complexity sections in the inventory do not by their titles support this barrier-parameter theorem.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension-dependent obstructions to small barrier parameters
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\) be a closed convex set with nonempty interior and let \(\nu_*(Q)\) be the infimum of parameters of standard self-concordant barriers on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The strongest displayed dimension lower bound is for the canonical orthant and positive-semidefinite cones. A linear-in-dimension bound is not asserted for every convex body.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dimension-dependent lower bound is an inequality \(
u_*(Q_n)\ge L(n)\) for a dimension-indexed domain family \(Q_n\), applying to every self-concordant barrier on each member. Canonical examples are \[
u_*(\mathbb R_+^n)\ge n\] and \[
u_*(\mathbb S_+^n)\ge n,\] where the second \(n\) is matrix order rather than the vector-space dimension \(n(n+1)/2\). These lower bounds are attained by \(-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) and \(-\log\det X\), respectively. More generally every nontrivial barrier domain satisfies \(
u_*(Q)\ge1\), and recession-direction configurations can give additive lower bounds \[
u_*(Q)\ge\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i/ eta_i\] under the corresponding geometric hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dimension-dependent lower bound states that every self-concordant barrier on a specified n-indexed family must have parameter at least a function of n. For the nonnegative orthant, every barrier has parameter at least n, and the standard logarithmic barrier attains n. The same statement holds for the positive-semidefinite cone with n denoting matrix order. Such linear bounds are properties of these domain families, not universal lower bounds for all n-dimensional convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
u_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n,\qquad 
u_*(\mathbb S_+^n)=n,\qquad 
u_*(Q)\ge1\ 	ext{for every nontrivial barrier domain }Q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: No self-concordant barrier for \(\mathbb R_+^n\) or \(\mathbb S_+^n\) can have admissible parameter strictly below \(n\).
special_cases_latex: For an interval, the one-dimensional lower bound is \(1\).
An affine slice of \(\mathbb R_+^n\) may have a smaller intrinsic lower bound than the full orthant.
immediate_consequences_latex: The standard logarithmic barriers on the orthant and semidefinite cone are parameter-optimal.
Worst-case universal parameter bounds cannot have order smaller than linear in \(n\), because the orthant is an \(n\)-dimensional example.
boundary_notes: The semidefinite lower bound scales with cone rank or matrix order, not ambient vector-space dimension.
Restriction to an affine subspace can reduce the intrinsic optimum even though the inherited barrier retains its original parameter.

notation.meaning: Intrinsic optimal barrier parameter of Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper n-dimensional convex domain admits a self-concordant barrier whose parameter is at most a universal constant times n.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that every nonempty open convex set \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) containing no affine line admits a \(Cn\)-self-concordant barrier. Equivalently, if \(
u_*(K)\) denotes the infimum of \(
u\) over all \(
u\)-self-concordant barriers on \(K\), then \[
u_*(K)\le Cn.\] The constant is independent of \(K\), its boundary regularity, and any particular inequality or conic representation.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty open convex set containing no affine line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_*(K)\le Cn\) for a universal constant \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional universal existence bound, stated up to an absolute constant.

notation.meaning: Infimum of barrier parameters over all self-concordant barriers on K.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with nonempty interior and containing no affine line. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\), define the polar body based at \(x\) by \[P_Q(x)=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\langle s,y-x\rangle\le1\ \forall y\in Q\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence theory for full-dimensional line-free convex sets. The construction is universal but is not claimed to provide an efficiently evaluable oracle for an arbitrary input set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(U:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_+\) is a universal barrier-parameter upper bound if every admissible \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) possesses a self-concordant barrier with parameter at most \(U(n)\). The universal-barrier construction sets \[V_Q(x)=\operatorname{vol}_nP_Q(x),\qquad F_Q(x)=c_1\log V_Q(x),\] for an absolute normalization constant \(c_1>0\). There are absolute constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) such that \(F_Q\) is a \(c_2n\)-self-concordant barrier. Consequently \[\nu_*(Q)\le c_2n\] for every such \(Q\), so \(U(n)=c_2n\) is a dimension-controlled universal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal upper bound depends only on dimension and guarantees a barrier for every full-dimensional convex set containing no line. The universal barrier is defined from the volume of the polar body centered at the evaluation point. With absolute normalization constants, it has parameter at most a constant times n. This is an existence statement; evaluating the polar volume and its derivatives may be computationally difficult.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall Q\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ closed, convex, full-dimensional, and line-free},\qquad \nu_*(Q)\le c_2n.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The worst-case optimal parameter \(\sup_Q\nu_*(Q)\) over admissible \(n\)-dimensional domains is \(O(n)\).
special_cases_latex: For a bounded convex body, the line-free condition is automatic.
For the orthant, an explicit logarithmic barrier achieves \(n\), avoiding the generally noncomputable polar-volume construction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every admissible finite-dimensional convex domain has a self-concordant barrier with parameter linear in dimension.
The associated idealized path-following iteration scale is \(O(\sqrt n\log(n/\epsilon))\), apart from initialization factors.
boundary_notes: The theorem does not make the universal barrier efficiently computable from a generic membership oracle.
Sets containing lines should first be reduced to an effective line-free quotient or affine representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Sensitive Parameter Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polyhedral logarithmic barrier has the number of displayed inequalities as a valid parameter, while barriers on Cartesian-product factors combine with additive valid parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and contain no affine line. Then \[F_P(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^{m}\log\bigl(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)\] is a self-concordant barrier on \(P\) with valid parameter \(m\). More generally, if \(F_j\) is a \(\nu_j\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,q\), then \[F(x_1,\ldots,x_q)=\sum_{j=1}^{q}F_j(x_j)\] is a self-concordant barrier on \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\) with valid parameter \(\sum_{j=1}^{q}\nu_j\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty and contains no affine line.
For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), \(K_j\) is an open convex domain and \(F_j\) is a \(\nu_j\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logarithmic barrier on \(P\) has valid parameter \(m\), and the product barrier has valid parameter \(\sum_{j=1}^q\nu_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical additive valid-parameter bounds for polyhedral and Cartesian-product structure; the displayed parameters need not be minimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation-sensitive bounds from explicit cone and block structure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a convex domain \(Q\) be given through representation data \(\mathcal R\), such as scalar inequalities, Cartesian cone blocks, affine slices, or a positive-semidefinite matrix variable. Let \(F_{\mathcal R}\) be the barrier produced by the applicable calculus rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional polyhedral, conic, spectral, and separable representations supported by standard logarithmic barriers and parameter calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structure-sensitive parameter bound is an estimate \[
u(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R)\] whose right-hand side depends on algebraic representation data rather than only on ambient dimension. Canonical instances include \[F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x),\qquad 
u(F)\le m,\] for \(m\) strict affine inequalities; \[F(X)=-\log\det X,\qquad 
u(F)=r,\] on \(\mathbb S_{++}^r\); and additive aggregation \[S(\mathcal R)=\sum_{j=1}^k
u_j\] for products or intersections of blocks with parameters \(
u_j\). Affine restriction preserves the inherited bound. Such a bound may be much smaller than one based on the vector-space dimension of a lifted matrix representation, but it remains tied to the selected formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-sensitive bound uses explicit features of the formulation. A polyhedron represented by m inequalities has the standard logarithmic barrier bound m. A positive-semidefinite cone of matrix order r has the log-determinant parameter r, despite having vector-space dimension r(r+1)/2. Product and combined-constraint parameters add across blocks, while affine slicing does not increase the inherited value. The result is a bound for the represented barrier and may differ across equivalent formulations of the same projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For supported representation blocks, \[\nu(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R)=\sum_j\nu_j,\] with scalar logarithmic inequalities contributing \(1\) each and an \(r\times r\) semidefinite block contributing \(r\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a block-diagonal semidefinite cone with block orders \(r_j\), the separable log-determinant barrier has parameter \(\sum_jr_j\).
A polyhedral logarithmic barrier is the sum of pullbacks of one-dimensional ray barriers.
special_cases_latex: The orthant \(\mathbb R_+^n\) has the structure-sensitive and optimal value \(n\).
The Lorentz-cone logarithmic barrier has parameter \(2\), independent of the cone's vector-space dimension.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exploiting block structure can improve both parameter accounting and Newton-system structure.
Redundant represented inequalities can enlarge the calculus parameter without changing the feasible set.
boundary_notes: The number of represented constraints is not an intrinsic invariant of the domain.
A smaller structure-sensitive parameter does not alone imply lower arithmetic cost if derivative evaluation or factorization becomes more expensive.

notation.meaning: Parameter bound extracted from that representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Universal-Parameter Results
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst intrinsic barrier parameter among n-dimensional convex domains grows linearly with n, matching universal upper and lower bounds up to constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[U_n=\sup\left\{\nu_*(K):K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a proper open convex domain}\right\}.\] Under the standard self-concordant-barrier convention, there exist absolute constants \(c,C>0\) such that \[cn\le U_n\le Cn.\] Hence the optimal universal barrier parameter has linear order in the dimension: universal constructions achieve \(O(n)\), and no construction can give \(o(n)\) uniformly over all \(n\)-dimensional domains.
assumptions_latex: The supremum ranges over proper open convex domains \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(cn\le\sup_K\nu_*(K)\le Cn\) for absolute constants \(c,C>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case optimal order over all proper convex domains in fixed dimension.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_n\) be the class of closed, full-dimensional, line-free convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\). For \(Q\in\mathcal Q_n\), define \(\nu_*(Q)=\inf_F\nu(F)\), where the infimum ranges over standard self-concordant barriers on \(\operatorname{int}Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal order of the worst-case universal parameter in finite dimension. The record does not claim a sharp leading constant or efficient evaluation of an optimal barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the worst-case intrinsic universal parameter by \[\mathfrak U(n):=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_n}\nu_*(Q).\] An optimal-order universal-parameter result consists of matching dimension-order bounds on \(\mathfrak U(n)\). The orthant gives \[\mathfrak U(n)\ge\nu_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n,\] while the universal-barrier construction gives an absolute constant \(c_2\) such that \[\mathfrak U(n)\le c_2n.\] Therefore \[\mathfrak U(n)=\Theta(n).\] This means that linear dependence on dimension is simultaneously sufficient for every admissible domain and necessary in the worst case. It does not imply that each individual domain has optimal parameter proportional to its ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst-case intrinsic universal parameter is the supremum, over all full-dimensional line-free convex domains in dimension n, of the smallest barrier parameter available on that domain. The nonnegative orthant forces this quantity to be at least n. The universal barrier bounds it above by an absolute constant times n. Hence the optimal worst-case order is linear in dimension, although particular domains or affine slices can have smaller intrinsic parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[n\le\mathfrak U(n)\le c_2n,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \mathfrak U(n)=\Theta(n).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist absolute constants \(a,b>0\) such that \(an\le\mathfrak U(n)\le bn\) for every \(n\ge1\).
No universal guarantee \(o(n)\) can hold over all \(n\)-dimensional domains, while an \(O(n)\) guarantee does hold.
special_cases_latex: The orthant attains the lower comparison \(\nu_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The worst-case short-step iteration factor derived solely from universal barrier existence has optimal dimension order \(\sqrt n\), up to constants and logarithmic terms.
Improving the universal-barrier constant does not change the linear parameter order.
boundary_notes: This is an order-optimal result, not a sharp-constant characterization.
The supplied evidence establishes the classical \(\Theta(n)\) conclusion; it does not support a stronger modern asymptotic constant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint parameter and oracle quality of a barrier representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\) be a convex feasible set and let \(\mathfrak R(Q)\) be a class of barrier representations. Each \(R\in\mathfrak R(Q)\) supplies a barrier \(F_R\), an admissible parameter \(\nu_R\), and a per-iteration oracle or Newton-system cost \(C_R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic comparison model for exact short-step methods. The cost component must be fixed for the computational model being compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every barrier representation has at least two relevant quality coordinates: its admissible parameter and the cost of using its derivative oracle and Newton system. One representation dominates another only if it is no worse in both coordinates. For short-step methods, a natural total-work proxy multiplies per-iteration cost by the square root of the parameter and a logarithmic accuracy factor. The best parameter alone need not select the least expensive formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation choice is evaluated through \[\min_{R\in\mathfrak R(Q)}C_R\sqrt{\nu_R}\log(S_R/\epsilon),\] or through the Pareto frontier of \((\nu_R,C_R)\) when no single cost model is fixed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Iteration complexity and arithmetic complexity are separate coordinates of barrier quality.
A representation with larger \(\nu_R\) can have smaller total work if it sufficiently reduces \(C_R\).
special_cases_latex: A universal barrier has \(\nu_R=O(n)\) but may have prohibitive polar-volume oracle cost.
An explicit logarithmic barrier can have a larger representation parameter yet inexpensive structured derivatives.
immediate_consequences_latex: Parameter-optimal and runtime-optimal representations need not coincide.
Redundant lifting can worsen \(\nu_R\) while improving sparsity or factorization structure, producing an actual tradeoff.
boundary_notes: The cost proxy omits constants, numerical conditioning, and inexact-solve effects unless included in \(C_R\).
Comparisons require a common accuracy criterion and computational model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tradeoff between barrier parameter and Newton-oracle cost
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of computable self-concordant barriers for a fixed optimization model. For \(F\in\mathcal F\), let \(
u(F)\) be an admissible parameter and let \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(F)\) denote the chosen cost of evaluating \(F,
abla F,
abla^2F\) and computing one Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic short-step complexity under a declared arithmetic or oracle cost model. Storage, conditioning, and inexactness must be incorporated into the cost coordinate if relevant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The parameter–oracle profile of \(F\) is \[p(F):=(
u(F),C_{\mathrm{or}}(F)).\] Its short-step work proxy at accuracy \(\epsilon\) is \[W(F,\epsilon):=C_{\mathrm{or}}(F)\,O\!\left(\sqrt{
u(F)}\log rac{S(F)}{\epsilon}ight),\] where \(S(F)\) is the initialization and objective scale appearing in the iteration bound. A parameter–oracle tradeoff occurs when two barriers \(F_1,F_2\) satisfy \(
u(F_1)<
u(F_2)\) but \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(F_1)>C_{\mathrm{or}}(F_2)\), so neither profile dominates the other. Selection by total work minimizes \(W(F,\epsilon)\), while selection without a fixed scalar cost uses the Pareto-minimal profiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier is characterized computationally by both its parameter and the cost of its oracle and Newton step. The parameter governs the leading square-root iteration factor, while derivative evaluation and linear algebra govern work per iteration. A genuine tradeoff occurs when improving one worsens the other. The preferred barrier minimizes their combined accuracy-dependent work estimate or lies on the nondominated frontier if no common scalar cost model is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relevant comparison is not \(\min_F\nu(F)\) alone but \[\min_{F\in\mathcal F}C_{\mathrm{or}}(F)\sqrt{\nu(F)}\log(S(F)/\epsilon).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Profiles \((\nu,C)\) are ordered componentwise; nondominated profiles form a Pareto frontier.
Ignoring slowly varying logarithmic factors gives the proxy \(C_{\mathrm{or}}(F)\sqrt{\nu(F)}\).
special_cases_latex: A universal barrier offers \(O(n)\) parameter quality but can have an impractical oracle.
A separable barrier can have a larger aggregate parameter while permitting cheaper blockwise derivatives and Newton algebra.
immediate_consequences_latex: The barrier with minimum parameter need not minimize runtime.
Changes in target accuracy can alter the preferred barrier when initialization scales or oracle strategies differ.
boundary_notes: The proxy is model-dependent and does not by itself capture finite-precision stability.
The cost of forming and solving the Newton system should not be omitted when it dominates derivative evaluation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\) be bounded, closed, and convex with nonempty interior, let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a closed \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier with positive-definite Hessian, and let \(c^*=\min_{x\in Q}\langle c,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal deterministic short-step theory for a linear objective and a standard self-concordant barrier, from a suitably centered feasible start. It excludes infeasible-start and primal-dual neighborhood variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier central path is the trajectory \[x(t)=\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}\{t\langle c,xangle+F(x)\},\qquad t\ge0,\] equivalently characterized by \(tc+
abla F(x(t))=0\). For a fixed \(0< eta<1\), the central neighborhood is \[\mathcal N_ eta(t):=\{x\in\operatorname{int}Q:\|tc+
abla F(x)\|_{x,*}\le eta\}.\] Exact path points satisfy \[\langle c,x(t)angle-c^*\le
u/t,\] while a neighborhood point satisfies \[\langle c,xangle-c^*\le rac1t\left(
u+ rac{( eta+\sqrt
u) eta}{1- eta}ight).\] Central-path complexity theory consists of neighborhood-preserving Newton updates that raise \(t\) geometrically by a factor \(1+\Theta(1/\sqrt
u)\), yielding an \(\epsilon\)-accurate point after \[O\!\left(\sqrt
u\log rac{
u\|c\|_{x_F^*,*}}{\epsilon}ight)\] iterations from an appropriate approximation to the analytic center \(x_F^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The central path minimizes the linear objective multiplied by a penalty parameter plus the barrier. Its points satisfy a first-order centrality equation. A central neighborhood contains points whose residual in the dual local norm is at most a fixed radius. Both exact and approximate central points carry explicit objective-gap certificates. Short-step Newton updates preserve this neighborhood while increasing the penalty parameter geometrically, producing the characteristic square-root dependence on the barrier parameter and logarithmic dependence on accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The central-path objects \(x(t)\) and \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)\) provide explicit objective certificates, and standard neighborhood-preserving tracking reaches error \(\epsilon\) in \[O\!\left(\sqrt\nu\log\frac{\nu\|c\|_{x_F^*,*}}{\epsilon}\right)\] iterations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact centrality is the zero-residual condition \(\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_{x,*}=0\).
The approximate-centering residual is the Newton decrement of \(x\mapsto t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(t=0\), the central-path point is the analytic center \(x_F^*=\arg\min F(x)\), when it exists.
For an orthant logarithmic barrier with \(\nu=n\), the iteration factor becomes \(O(\sqrt n)\) times a logarithmic term.
immediate_consequences_latex: To certify exact-path objective error at most \(\epsilon\), it suffices that \(t\ge\nu/\epsilon\).
The iteration bound counts Newton updates and must be multiplied by their arithmetic cost for a runtime estimate.
boundary_notes: Boundedness is used here to ensure the stated primal optimum and analytic-center path model; other central-path theories cover unbounded or conic formulations.
Constants depend on the selected neighborhood radius and update rule.
The definition does not cover predictor-corrector or infeasible-start variants.

The path-generating model determined by \((f_0,F,A,b)\) is the parameterized family \(\Phi_t:D	o\mathbb R\), \(\Phi_t(x)=t f_0(x)+F(x)\), for \(t>0\). At parameter t, its central points minimize this objective over the relative-interior feasible set. If that minimizer is unique for every positive t, the graph of these minimizers is the central path. The equality-constrained first-order condition gives an equivalent characterization.

abla f_0(x)+

u=0\) for some \(

With reciprocal parameter \(\mu=1/t\), the same minimizers solve \(\min_{x\in D} f_0(x)+\mu F(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier–Objective Central Paths
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The barrier–objective central path maps each positive parameter to the unique minimizer of the scaled objective plus the barrier; each point satisfies the combined-gradient stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(t>0\) for which the minimizer exists uniquely, define the barrier–objective central point by \[x(t)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\bigl\{t f(x)+F(x)\bigr\}.\] The central path is the map \(t\mapsto x(t)\). Because \(f\) and \(F\) are differentiable, every central point satisfies \[t\nabla f(x(t))+\nabla F(x(t))=0.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a differentiable self-concordant barrier.
For every considered \(t>0\), the function \(x\mapsto t f(x)+F(x)\) has a unique minimizer in \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The central path is \(t\mapsto x(t)\), where \(x(t)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\{t f(x)+F(x)\}\), and its points satisfy \(t\nabla f(x(t))+\nabla F(x(t))=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained interior formulation; affine equalities may be absorbed into the ambient affine space.

knowledge_statements.title: Compatible Self-Concordant Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is compatible with a reference barrier when all members have uniformly bounded curvature and curvature variation in the barrier's local norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parameterized convex family \(\{\phi_t:t\in T\}\) is uniformly \((M_2,M_3)\)-compatible with the reference barrier \(F\) if finite constants \(M_2,M_3\ge0\), independent of \(t\), satisfy for every \(x\in K\) and \(h\inb{R}^n\), \[0le D^2ight.\phi_t(x)[h,h]\le M_2D^2F(x)[h,h]\] and \[\left|D^3ight.\phi_t(x)[h,h,h]\right|\le M_3\bigl(D^2F(x)[h,h]\bigr)^{3/2}.\] These inequalities make the curvature and curvature variation of every family member uniformly measurable in the local geometry generated by \(F\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^3(K)\) is a self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is compatible when its second and third directional derivatives obey the displayed uniform bounds relative to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local uniform derivative-control formulation of compatibility.

notation.meaning: Local norm generated by the barrier Hessian.

review_flags: A standard authoritative definition of compatibility and its normalization is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family Uniformly Compatible with a Reference Barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E_1,E_2\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(Q\subset E_1\) be closed and convex with nonempty interior, let \(K\subset E_2\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. For the order induced by \(K\), write \(u\preccurlyeq_K v\) when \(v-u\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-valued, three-times differentiable concave maps controlled uniformly by one reference self-concordant metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta\ge1\) and \(T\) be an index set. A family \(\{\xi_\tau:Q\to E_2\}_{\tau\in T}\) is uniformly \(\beta\)-compatible with \(F\) relative to \(K\) if every \(\xi_\tau\) is three-times continuously differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}Q\), is \(K\)-concave, and, for every \(\tau\in T\), \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\), and \(h\in E_1\), satisfies \[\pm D^3\xi_\tau(x)[h,h,h]\preccurlyeq_K-3\beta D^2\xi_\tau(x)[h,h]\,\langle\nabla^2F(x)h,h\rangle^{1/2}.\] The two signs mean that both the displayed inequality and the same inequality with \(D^3\xi_\tau\) replaced by \(-D^3\xi_\tau\) hold. Uniformity means that the same \(F\) and \(\beta\) work for all \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameterized family is uniformly compatible with a reference self-concordant barrier when every member is cone-concave and its third derivative, in either sign, is bounded in cone order by its negative second derivative times the local norm induced by the barrier. The compatibility constant and reference barrier must be independent of the family parameter.
assumptions_latex: For every \(\tau\in T\), \(D^2\xi_\tau(x)[h,h]\preccurlyeq_K0\) for all admissible \(x,h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed derivative inequalities define uniform \(\beta\)-compatibility of \(\{\xi_\tau\}_{\tau\in T}\) with the single barrier geometry generated by \(F\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The pair of signed inequalities is equivalent to requiring the source definition for both directions \(h\) and \(-h\).
For scalar-valued \(\xi_\), compatibility reads \(\lvert D^3\xi_\tau(x)[h,h,h]\rvert\le -3\beta D^2\xi_\tau(x)[h,h]\|h\|_x\), where \(\|h\|_x=\langle\nabla^2F(x)h,h\rangle^{1/2}\).
special_cases_latex: A singleton family recovers ordinary \(\beta\)-compatibility of one map with \(F\).
Positive conic combinations of uniformly \(\beta\)-compatible maps remain \(\beta\)-compatible with \(F\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reference Hessian \(\nabla^2F(x)\) supplies a common local metric for every family member.
Uniformity prevents compatibility constants from deteriorating with \(\tau\).
boundary_notes: This is compatibility of derivative geometry, not the assertion that every \(\xi_\tau\) is itself a self-concordant barrier.
If constants depend on \(\tau\) without a finite uniform bound, the family is not uniformly compatible in this sense.

children.top_down_role: Barrier-theoretic interface to coupled central paths for conic primal–dual pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Primal–Dual Path Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a logarithmically homogeneous conic barrier, the negative scaled barrier gradient is the dual slack along the central path, and complementarity equals ν divided by the path parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and its conic dual. For \(t>0\), a central primal–dual triple \((x(t),y(t),s(t))\) satisfies \[Ax(t)=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y(t)+s(t)=c,\qquad s(t)=-\frac{1}{t}\nabla F(x(t)),\] where \(x(t)\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s(t)\in\operatorname{int}K^*\). Logarithmic homogeneity gives \[\langle x(t),s(t)\rangle=\frac{\nu}{t}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a proper cone, and \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a logarithmically homogeneous \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
The primal and dual affine systems have strictly feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every central triple satisfies \(Ax(t)=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y(t)+s(t)=c\), \(s(t)=-t^{-1}\nabla F(x(t))\), and \(\langle x(t),s(t)\rangle=\nu/t\).

Consider \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:X\in(L-B)\cap K\}\) and \(\max\{\langle B,S\rangle:S\in(L^\perp+C)\cap K\}\), assumed strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly feasible conic primal–dual pairs equipped with the same canonical barrier on a self-dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), the conic primal–dual path interface is the unique pair \(Z_*(t)=(X_*(t),S_*(t))\in\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \[X_*(t)\in L-B,\qquad S_*(t)\in L^\perp+C,\qquad S_*(t)=-t^{-1}\nabla F(X_*(t)).\] Equivalently, \(X_*(t)=-t^{-1}\nabla F(S_*(t))\). Its primal component minimizes \(t\langle C,X\rangle+F(X)\) over \((L-B)\cap\operatorname{int}K\), and its dual component minimizes \(-t\langle B,S\rangle+F(S)\) over \((L^\perp+C)\cap\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic primal–dual path interface couples the primal and dual central points at the same positive parameter. Both points are strictly feasible, and the barrier gradient maps either component to the other after scaling by the reciprocal parameter. The same pair is equivalently obtained from the primal and dual barrier minimization problems.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a proper self-dual cone carrying the canonical barrier \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_*(t)=(X_*(t),S_*(t))\) is defined by strict primal–dual feasibility and the augmented complementarity relation \(tS_*(t)+\nabla F(X_*(t))=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The gap on the path is \(\langle X_*(t),S_*(t)\rangle=\theta/t\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb S_+^k\) and \(F(X)=-\log\det X\), augmented complementarity becomes \(X_*(t)S_*(t)=t^{-1}I\).
For \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), it becomes componentwise complementarity \(X_{*,i}(t)S_{*,i}(t)=t^{-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Either component and \(t\) determine the other component through the barrier gradient.
The primal–dual gap decreases exactly as \(1/t\) along this canonical path.

children.title: Central-Path Well-Posedness
children.top_down_role: Well-posedness of central points across the path parameter.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\) be a nonempty relatively open convex feasible set and let \(\Phi_t:D\to\mathbb R\) be a barrier subproblem objective for every \(t\in I\subset(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and local stability of finite-dimensional central points over a prescribed parameter interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The central path is well posed on \(I\) if: (i) for every \(t\in I\), \(\Phi_t\) attains its infimum at a unique point \(x(t)\in D\); and (ii) the solution map is locally stable, meaning that for every \(t_0\in I\) and every sequence \(t_k\to t_0\), one has \(x(t_k)\to x(t_0)\). It is strongly well posed on \(I\) if, additionally, \(\nabla^2_{xx}\Phi_t(x(t))\) is positive definite on the feasible tangent space for every \(t\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central path is well posed when every parameter value has exactly one attained central point and those points vary continuously with the parameter. Strong well-posedness also requires a nonsingular positive-definite reduced Hessian at every central point.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\Phi_t\) is proper and convex on \(D\).
Strong well-posedness is stated only when \(\Phi_t\) is twice differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Well-posedness makes \(t\mapsto x(t)\) a single-valued continuous central-point map; strong well-posedness adds reduced-Hessian nondegeneracy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In metric spaces, the sequential stability condition is equivalent to continuity of \(x:I\to D\).
For affine constraints \(Ax=b\), strong well-posedness means \(h^T\nabla^2_{xx}\Phi_t(x(t))h>0\) for every nonzero \(h\in\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: Strict convexity and attainment of every \(\Phi_t\) provide the existence-and-uniqueness portion of well-posedness.
On compact parameter subintervals, a continuous central-point map has compact image.
immediate_consequences_latex: A well-posed path cannot branch at a fixed parameter.
Strong well-posedness supplies the nonsingular linear system used to define local sensitivity.
boundary_notes: Uniqueness without attainment is insufficient.
The definition does not claim uniform conditioning as \(t\) approaches an endpoint of \(I\).

notation.meaning: Unique central point at parameter t.
