knowledge_statements.title: Central-Point Existence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central point exists when the lower-semicontinuous barrier objective has a nonempty compact sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(t>0\) and define \(\Phi_t:K\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(\Phi_t(x)=t f(x)+F(x)\). If there exists \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) such that the sublevel set \[\{x\in K:\Phi_t(x)\le\alpha\}\] is nonempty and compact, then \(\Phi_t\) attains its infimum on \(K\). Equivalently, there exists \[x(t)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\Phi_t(x).\]
assumptions_latex: \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous and satisfies \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\) whenever a sequence \((x_k)\subset K\) approaches \(\partial K\).
\(f:K\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
For the chosen \(t>0\), there exists \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(\{x\in K:t f(x)+F(x)\le\alpha\}\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x(t)\in K\) such that \(x(t)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\{t f(x)+F(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence from lower semicontinuity and a nonempty compact sublevel; self-concordance is not required for this attainment statement.

notation.meaning: A central minimizer at parameter t.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Minimizing the self-concordant function p. 187

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Point Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the central objective attains its minimum and the barrier is strictly convex, then the central point is unique; an everywhere positive-definite barrier Hessian is sufficient for strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t>0\) and define \(\Phi_t=t f+F\) on the convex set \(K\). If \(f\) is convex, \(F\) is strictly convex, and \(\Phi_t\) attains its minimum on \(K\), then there exists a unique \(x(t)\in K\) such that \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\Phi_t(x)=\{x(t)\}.\] Positive definiteness of \(\nabla^2F(x)\) for every \(x\in K\) is a sufficient condition for the required strict convexity when \(F\) is twice differentiable.
assumptions_latex: \(f:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is strictly convex.
The function \(\Phi_t=t f+F\) attains its minimum on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a unique \(x(t)\in K\) such that \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\Phi_t(x)=\{x(t)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness follows under strict convexity of the barrier contribution; existence is assumed separately.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.5 Minimizing the self-concordant function p. 187

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Parameter Coverage
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The central path covers exactly the positive parameters for which the barrier-penalized objective attains its minimum. Inf-compactness of every path objective is a sufficient condition for full coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(t>0\), let \(\phi_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\) for \(x\in Q\). The central point \(x(t)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\phi_t(x)\) exists exactly for \(t\in T:=\{s>0:\phi_s\text{ attains its infimum on }Q\}\), and it is unique whenever it exists. If \(\phi_t\) is inf-compact on \(Q\) for every \(t>0\), then \(T=(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\{t>0:\phi_t\text{ attains its infimum on }Q\}\); in particular, \(T=(0,\infty)\) if \(\phi_t\) is inf-compact on \(Q\) for every \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal central path with positive penalty parameter. Inf-compact means that every sublevel set is compact in the relative topology of Q.

notation.meaning: Set of parameters having a central point

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posedness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded recession direction can eliminate central points, while a flat direction can produce infinitely many central points when strict convexity is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Existence can fail on \(Q=(0,\infty)\) with \(F(x)=-\log x\) and \(c=-1\): for every \(t>0\), \(\phi_t(x)=-tx-\log x\to-\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\). Uniqueness can fail when strict convexity is removed: on \(Q=(-1,1)\times\mathbb{R}\), let \(F(x)=-\log(1-x_1^2)\) and \(c=0\). Then every \((0,s)\), with \(s\in\mathbb{R}\), minimizes \(\phi_t=F\).
assumptions_latex: The examples use open convex domains in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
In the first example, coercivity is absent; in the second, strict convexity is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Barrier growth at the finite boundary need not prevent escape along an unbounded recession direction, and loss of strict convexity can destroy uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure boundaries for existence and uniqueness of central points.

children.title: Central-Path Regularity-Sensitivity Theory
children.top_down_role: Smooth dependence of central points on parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x(t)\) be a strongly well-posed central path for \(\Phi_t(x)=t f_0(x)+F(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with multiplier \(\nu(t)\). Assume \(f_0,F\) are sufficiently smooth and \(A\) has constant rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order parameter sensitivity for smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained barrier subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The central path is regular on an interval \(I\) if \(t\mapsto(x(t),
u(t))\) is continuously differentiable and satisfies the stationarity system \[t
abla f_0(x(t))+
abla F(x(t))+A^T
u(t)=0,\qquad Ax(t)=b.\] Its sensitivity \((\dot x(t),\dot
u(t))\) is defined by the differentiated KKT system \[ egin{bmatrix}H_t&A^T\A&0\end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix}\dot x(t)\\dot
u(t)\end{bmatrix}=- egin{bmatrix}
abla f_0(x(t))\0\end{bmatrix},\qquad H_t=t
abla^2f_0(x(t))+
abla^2F(x(t)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular central path is a continuously differentiable solution of the barrier stationarity and feasibility equations. Its parameter sensitivity is the unique solution of the bordered Hessian system obtained by differentiating those equations with respect to the path parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0\) and \(F\) are twice continuously differentiable near the path.
The bordered matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}H_t&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nonsingular for every \(t\in I\).
\(x(t)\) remains in the interior barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularity identifies \(\dot x(t)\) and \(\dot\nu(t)\) through the displayed nonsingular sensitivity system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: After eliminating equality constraints with a basis \(U\) of \(\ker A\), \(\dot x(t)=-U(U^TH_tU)^{-1}U^T\nabla f_0(x(t))\).
For logarithmic parameter \(s=\log t\), \(dx/ds=t\dot x(t)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\), then \(\dot x(t)=-H_t^{-1}\nabla f_0(x(t))\).
For linear \(f_0(x)=c^Tx\), \(H_t=\nabla^2F(x(t))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The sensitivity is tangent to the feasible affine space because \(A\dot x(t)=0\).
The same bordered matrix governs equality-constrained Newton corrections and path sensitivity.
boundary_notes: At a singular reduced Hessian, the path may branch or fail to be differentiable.
This definition concerns sensitivity to the scalar path parameter, not perturbations of all problem data.

notation.meaning: Hessian of the barrier subproblem at its central point.
Derivative of the central point with respect to t.

source_refs.locator: §11.2.2, central-path optimality condition (11.7); Exercise 11.7, tangent to the central path

knowledge_statements.title: Differentiable Central-Path Sensitivity System

source_witnesses.locator: §11.2.2, central-path optimality condition (11.7); Exercise 11.7, tangent to the central path

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth barrier with an everywhere positive-definite Hessian yields a central path having one fewer continuous derivative than the barrier, and an analytic barrier yields an analytic path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x(t)\) be the unique solution of \(
abla F(x(t))+tc=0\) for \(t\in I\). Since \(D_x(
abla F(x)+tc)=
abla^2F(x)\) is nonsingular throughout \(Q\), the mapping \(t\mapsto x(t)\) is \(C^{k-1}\) on \(I\). In particular, when \(F\) is analytic, the central path is analytic wherever it exists and its Hessian remains positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^k(Q)\), with \(k\geq2\), and \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\) for every \(x\in Q\).
For every \(t\) in an open interval \(I\subset(0,\infty)\), the central point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The central path \(x:I\to Q\) is of class \(C^{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-function regularity for a smooth strictly convex barrier.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The regularity claim and theorem content kind fit the leaf, and the C^{k-1} conclusion is consistent with the implicit-function formulation. However, no citation or inspectable locator is supplied, and the statement includes derivational proof-style text. A source must establish both the smooth and analytic variants before promotion.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The derivative of a central point with respect to its penalty parameter is the negative inverse barrier Hessian applied to the objective vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Differentiating the centrality equation \(\nabla F(x(t))+tc=0\) gives \(H(t)x'(t)+c=0\). Consequently,
\[
x'(t)=-H(t)^{-1}c,
\qquad
\|x'(t)\|_{x(t)}=\|c\|_{x(t)}^*.
\]
For a relative perturbation \(t\mapsto t(1+\varepsilon)\), the first-order displacement is \(x(t(1+\varepsilon))-x(t)=-\varepsilon tH(t)^{-1}c+o(|\varepsilon|)\).
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses of central-path regularity hold on \(I\subset(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential sensitivity to the scalar path parameter.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The derivative and local-norm identities are internally consistent and the property kind fits parameter sensitivity. No source reference is provided, however, and the statement contains a derivation rather than only the knowledge statement. A specific implicit-differentiation or central-path sensitivity locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Data Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small objective perturbation moves the central point by the inverse barrier Hessian times the perturbation, scaled by the path parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The central point satisfies \(\nabla F(x(t,c))+tc=0\). For any direction \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), implicit differentiation with respect to \(c\) yields
\[
D_cx(t,c)[h]=-t\nabla^2F(x(t,c))^{-1}h.
\]
Thus \(\|D_cx(t,c)[h]\|_{x(t,c)}=t\|h\|_{x(t,c)}^*\). This is a local statement: the formula applies while the perturbed central point remains in \(Q\) and the barrier Hessian remains nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^2(Q)\) and \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\) on the open convex set \(Q\).
At fixed \(t>0\), the central point exists for objective vectors near \(c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local sensitivity to perturbations of linear objective data.

notation.meaning: Central point for parameter and objective data

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The local objective-data derivative and norm identity are mathematically coherent under the stated nonsingularity and local-existence conditions. The property kind fits the terminal container, but there is no citation with a specific locator and the statement contains proof-style differentiation text.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central-path regularity may break when a central point disappears, reaches the domain boundary or infinity, or encounters a singular barrier Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The implicit-function description of the central path breaks down at a parameter \(t_0\) if the central point ceases to exist, if \(x(t)\) approaches \(\partial Q\) or escapes to infinity as \(t	o t_0\), or if \(
abla^2F(x(t))\) becomes singular. In the singular regime, the formulas \(x'(t)=-
abla^2F(x(t))^{-1}c\) and \(D_cx(t,c)[h]=-t
abla^2F(x(t,c))^{-1}h\) are undefined, and uniqueness or differentiability need not persist.
assumptions_latex: Central points are characterized by \(\nabla F(x)+tc=0\).
No uniform positive-definiteness or compact containment assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularity can fail only after loss of existence, escape from the domain, or singularity of the linearized centrality equation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes for implicit-function central-path regularity.

notation.meaning: Linearization with respect to the central point

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The listed regimes correctly describe standard obstructions to the local implicit-function formulas, and failure_boundary is the appropriate kind. The word 'only' makes the conclusion exhaustive, so an authoritative source or a more carefully scoped local continuation statement is needed. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Intrinsic Path-Speed Control
children.top_down_role: Local-metric control of central-point motion.

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Path-Speed Control
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measured in the barrier Hessian metric, central-point speed is at most the square root of the barrier parameter divided by the path parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Along the central path, differentiation gives \(x'(t)=-
abla^2F(x(t))^{-1}c\). Since \(tc=-
abla F(x(t))\) and a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier satisfies \(\|
abla F(x)\|_x^*\leq\sqrt{
u}\),
\[
\|x'(t)\|_{x(t)}=\|c\|_{x(t)}^*= rac{1}{t}\|
abla F(x(t))\|_{x(t)}^*\leq rac{\sqrt{
u}}{t}.
\]
Thus logarithmic changes in the path parameter control central-point motion intrinsically.
assumptions_latex: The central point \(x(t)\) exists and satisfies \(\nabla F(x(t))+tc=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x'(t)\|_{x(t)}\leq\sqrt{\nu}/t\), equivalently \(\|d x/d\log t\|_{x(t)}\leq\sqrt{\nu}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-Hessian speed bound under logarithmic reparameterization.

notation.meaning: Local norm generated by the barrier Hessian

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The speed bound fits the intrinsic path-speed leaf and is standard for the convention in which a nu-self-concordant barrier satisfies the stated gradient bound. Because conventions for barrier parameters vary, a source with the exact definition and locator is required. The statement also includes a derivation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Metric Speed and Uniform Speed Control
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x:(0,\infty)\to\operatorname{int}Q\) be a differentiable central path generated by a twice differentiable barrier \(F\), and let \(\|h\|_x=\langle\nabla^2F(x)h,h\rangle^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic rather than Euclidean speed, with logarithmic path parameter used for scale-free control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The intrinsic path speed at \(t>0\) is \[v_F(t)=\|\dot x(t)\|_{x(t)}.\] The logarithmic intrinsic speed is \[\widehat v_F(t)=\left\|\frac{dx}{d\log t}(t)\right\|_{x(t)}=t\,v_F(t).\] The path has \(\kappa\)-controlled intrinsic speed on \(I\subset(0,\infty)\) if \(\widehat v_F(t)\le\kappa\) for every \(t\in I\), equivalently \(v_F(t)\le\kappa/t\). Its intrinsic displacement over \([t_0,t_1]\subset I\) is bounded by the path length \(\int_{t_0}^{t_1}v_F(t)dt\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intrinsic speed is the norm of the path derivative in the barrier Hessian metric at the current central point. Multiplying by t gives speed per unit change of log t. A path is kappa-controlled when this scale-free speed is uniformly bounded, which is the same as a one-over-t bound on ordinary parameter speed.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla^2F(x(t))\) is positive definite on feasible tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat v_F(t)=t\|\dot x(t)\|_{x(t)}\) is the scale-free intrinsic speed, and \(\widehat v_F\le\kappa\) defines uniform path-speed control.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\widehat v_F(t)\le\kappa\iff\|\dot x(t)\|_{x(t)}\le\kappa/t\).
Writing \(s=\log t\), the control condition is \(\|dx/ds\|_{x(e^s)}\le\kappa\).
special_cases_latex: For \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\), \(v_F(t)^2=\sum_i(\dot x_i(t)/x_i(t))^2\).
If \(x(t)\) is constant, both intrinsic speeds vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under \(\kappa\)-control, the intrinsic length between parameters is at most \(\kappa|\log(t_1/t_0)|\).
Multiplicative parameter changes are the natural scale for a logarithmically controlled path.
boundary_notes: The definition supplies a control criterion; whether a particular barrier path satisfies it depends on the barrier and model.
A small Euclidean derivative need not imply small intrinsic speed near the boundary.

notation.meaning: Intrinsic speed per unit log t.

source_refs.locator: §6.2.2–§6.2.4, smooth central path, local barrier geometry, and multiplicative penalty updates, pp. 377–383

review_flags: The source supports intrinsic local geometry and multiplicative path motion; the explicit term κ-controlled intrinsic speed is a formal packaging of those quantities.

children.title: Optimal-Face Endpoint Geometry
children.top_down_role: Limiting behavior as the trajectory approaches optimal boundary faces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f_0\) have finite optimum \(p^*=\min_{x\in Q}f_0(x)\), define \(Q^*=\{x\in Q:f_0(x)=p^*\}\), and let \(x(t)\in\operatorname{ri}Q\) be a central path for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal endpoint behavior as the penalty parameter tends to infinity; no uniqueness of the limiting optimum is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The endpoint cluster set of the central path is \[\Omega_\infty(x)=\{\bar x\in Q:\exists\,t_k\to\infty\text{ with }x(t_k)\to\bar x\}.\] The path has optimal-face endpoint geometry if \(\Omega_\infty(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\Omega_\infty(x)\subseteq Q^*\). It converges to an optimal-face endpoint if \(\Omega_\infty(x)=\{x_\infty\}\) for some \(x_\infty\in Q^*\). For a linear objective on a convex feasible set, \(Q^*\) is an exposed face, so the endpoint lies on that optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The endpoint geometry is described by all limits of central points along parameter sequences tending to infinity. It is optimal-face geometry when at least one such limit exists and every such limit is optimal. A genuine endpoint exists when the cluster set is a singleton. For linear optimization, the optimal set is an exposed face.
assumptions_latex: Cluster points are taken in the ambient finite-dimensional topology.
Nonemptiness of \(\Omega_\infty(x)\) requires boundedness or another compactness condition on the path tail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega_\infty(x)\subseteq Q^*\) defines approach to the optimal face, while \(\Omega_\infty(x)=\{x_\infty\}\) defines a unique endpoint.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If the path tail is relatively compact, \(\Omega_\infty(x)\ne\varnothing\).
A singleton cluster set for a relatively compact continuous path is equivalent to \(x(t)\to x_\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Q^*=\{x^*\}\) and the path tail is relatively compact with optimal cluster points, then \(x(t)\to x^*\).
For \(f_0(x)=c^Tx\), \(Q^*=Q\cap\{x:c^Tx=p^*\}\) is exposed by \(c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every convergent subsequence of a path with optimal-face endpoint geometry terminates at an optimal solution.
A non-singleton optimal face does not by itself determine which point, if any, is selected by the barrier.
boundary_notes: The analytic center of the optimal face is a stronger selection statement and is not included without additional barrier-specific hypotheses.
Unbounded paths can have an empty endpoint cluster set even when objective values converge.

notation.meaning: Optimal solution set or optimal face.
Cluster set of the central path at infinite parameter.

source_refs.locator: §6.2.2, statement that all limiting points of the central path as t tends to infinity belong to the optimal set, pp. 377–379

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Endpoint Limits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible set, central-path objective values approach the optimum, and every endpoint cluster point lies in the optimal solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The barrier duality-gap estimate gives \(0\leq\langle c,x(t)\rangle-p^*\leq\nu/t\). Therefore \(\langle c,x(t)\rangle\to p^*\) as \(t\to\infty\). Compactness of \(K\) ensures that every sequence \(t_j\to\infty\) has a subsequence for which \(x(t_j)\to\bar x\in K\). Continuity of the linear objective then yields \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle=p^*\), so \(\bar x\in X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point of \(x(t)\) as \(t\to\infty\) belongs to \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\langle c,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal endpoint optimality for a compact feasible region.

notation.meaning: Optimal solution set of the linear objective

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role and cluster-point conclusion fit endpoint limits, but the asserted nu/t gap estimate must be tied to the precise self-concordant-barrier convention. No source or locator is supplied, and the statement contains proof text.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizers of an attained linear objective over a closed convex set form the exposed face cut out by the optimal supporting hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The optimal set is
\[
X^*=K\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle c,x\rangle=p^*\}.
\]
It is convex and closed. Moreover, if \(z=\theta x+(1-\theta)y\in X^*\) for \(x,y\in K\) and \(0<\theta<1\), then \(\langle c,x\rangle\geq p^*\) and \(\langle c,y\rangle\geq p^*\) force \(x,y\in X^*\). Hence \(X^*\) is the exposed face supported by the hyperplane \(\{x:\langle c,x\rangle=p^*\}\).
assumptions_latex: The linear objective \(x\mapsto\langle c,x\rangle\) attains its minimum on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*=K\cap\{x:\langle c,x\rangle=p^*\}\) is a nonempty exposed face of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed-face structure induced by a linear objective.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exposed-face claim is standard, precise, and correctly classified as a property of optimal-face geometry. Nevertheless, no authoritative convex-analysis citation with a section, proposition, or page locator is supplied, and the statement contains a proof argument.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit-Point Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded full-dimensional polytope, the logarithmic central path converges to the analytic center of the optimal face, even when the linear optimum is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), let \(x(t)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\}\). Define \(I^*=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in X^*\}\) and \(F_{X^*}(x)=-\sum_{i\notin I^*}\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) for \(x\in\operatorname{ri}X^*\). Then \(x(t)\) converges as \(t\to\infty\) to the unique point \(x^*_{\mathrm{ac}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{ri}X^*}F_{X^*}(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\) is a bounded full-dimensional polytope and \(Q=\operatorname{int}P=\{x:Ax<b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logarithmic central path converges to the analytic center of \(X^*\) determined by the inequalities that are not identically active on \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral logarithmic-barrier selection of the analytic center of the optimal face.

notation.meaning: Optimal face of the closed polytope
Indices of inequalities active everywhere on the optimal face
Relative logarithmic barrier on the optimal face

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Endpoint Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing objective gap can approach different points of a positive-dimensional optimal face; a unique endpoint requires an additional barrier-based selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K=[0,1]^2\) and \(c=(1,0)\), the optimal value is \(0\) and
\[
X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\langle c,x\rangle=\{0\}\times[0,1].
\]
The sequences \(x_k=(1/k,0)\) and \(y_k=(1/k,1)\) both have objective values converging to the optimum, but their limits are distinct. Hence vanishing objective gap guarantees only approach to the optimal face; uniqueness of the endpoint requires an additional selection mechanism, such as a specified barrier.
assumptions_latex: No barrier-based selection rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal endpoint set is \(X^*=\{0\}\times[0,1]\), so objective convergence alone does not determine a unique endpoint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of optimal endpoints without a selecting barrier geometry.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly shows that objective-gap convergence alone does not select a unique point of a positive-dimensional optimal face, and failure_boundary is the correct role. No source with a specific endpoint-selection or convex-analysis locator is supplied.

children.title: Central-Path Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Equivalent and specialized centrality regions used to couple parameter motion with Newton correction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\) be a relatively open feasible domain, let \(\Phi_t:D\to\mathbb R\) be a strictly convex twice differentiable barrier objective, and let \(H_t(x)=\nabla^2\Phi_t(x)\) be positive definite on the feasible tangent space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal, feasible, local-norm neighborhoods of barrier subproblem minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in D\), let \(\Delta_t(x)\) be the equality-constrained Newton direction, characterized by \[H_t(x)\Delta_t(x)+\nabla\Phi_t(x)+A^Tw=0,\qquad A\Delta_t(x)=0.\] Its Newton decrement is \(\lambda_t(x)=\langle H_t(x)\Delta_t(x),\Delta_t(x)\rangle^{1/2}\). For radius \(\beta\ge0\), the central-path neighborhood at parameter \(t\) is \[\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in D:\lambda_t(x)\le\beta\},\] and the path neighborhood is \(\mathcal N_\beta=\{(t,x):t>0,\ x\in\mathcal N_\beta(t)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton-decrement neighborhood contains the strictly feasible points whose equality-constrained Newton decrement for the current barrier objective is at most the chosen radius. The union over positive parameters forms a tube around the central path.
assumptions_latex: The reduced Hessian of \(\Phi_t\) is positive definite, so the Newton direction is uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x:\lambda_t(x)\le\beta\}\) defines a centrality region in the intrinsic Newton metric.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without equality constraints, \(\lambda_t(x)=\|\nabla\Phi_t(x)\|_{x,t}^*\), where \(\|g\|_{x,t}^{*2}=g^TH_t(x)^{-1}g\).
The exact central point satisfies \(\lambda_t(x(t))=0\), hence belongs to every \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\mathcal N_0(t)\) is the singleton central point when \(\Phi_t\) is strictly convex and attained.
For a linear objective, \(H_t(x)=\nabla^2F(x)\), independent of \(t\) except through the evaluation point.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(0\le\beta_1\le\beta_2\), then \(\mathcal N_{\beta_1}(t)\subseteq\mathcal N_{\beta_2}(t)\).
The decrement simultaneously measures centrality and the local size of a Newton correction.
boundary_notes: Residual-based primal–dual neighborhoods can include infeasible points and are distinct from this feasible primal definition.
Useful admissible radii depend on the self-concordance normalization and the intended correction guarantee.

notation.meaning: Equality-constrained Newton direction for the barrier subproblem.

children.title: Newton-Decrement Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Centrality regions expressed through path-subproblem decrements.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Decrement Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton-decrement neighborhood contains points whose barrier-subproblem gradient is small in the inverse-Hessian norm; the exact central point has decrement zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in Q\), define
\[
\lambda_t(x)=\bigl(\nabla f_t(x)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(x)^{-1}\nabla f_t(x)\bigr)^{1/2}
=\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*.
\]
For a prescribed \(\beta\geq0\), the Newton-decrement neighborhood is \(\mathcal N_t(\beta)=\{x\in Q:\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\}\). The exact central point satisfies \(\lambda_t(x(t))=0\); positive \(\beta\) permits controlled inexact centrality in the local dual norm.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_t(\beta)=\{x\in Q:\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\}\) is the Newton-decrement neighborhood of the central point at parameter \(t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal centrality neighborhood for a barrier subproblem.

notation.meaning: Newton decrement for the path subproblem

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent because the linear term has zero Hessian, and definition is the correct content kind for this neighborhood leaf. A self-concordance source with a specific definition, section, or page locator is required to establish the Newton-decrement convention and neighborhood terminology.

children.title: Local-Norm Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Centrality regions expressed directly in barrier geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Norm Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Points within barrier-local distance rho of the exact central point form a central neighborhood, and their Hessian norms remain uniformly comparable to the center norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\leq\rho<1\), the local-norm central-path neighborhood is \[\mathcal N_t(\rho)=\{x\in Q:\|x-x(t)\|_{x(t)}\leq\rho\}.\] For every \(x\in\mathcal N_t(\rho)\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), self-concordance gives \[(1-\rho)\|h\|_{x(t)}\leq\|h\|_x\leq(1-\rho)^{-1}\|h\|_{x(t)}.\] Thus local norms throughout the neighborhood are uniformly equivalent to the norm at its center.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_t(\rho)\) is a Hessian-controlled neighborhood of \(x(t)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal central-path neighborhood defined using the barrier Hessian at the exact center.

notation.meaning: Local primal norm induced by the barrier Hessian

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.4 Path-following scheme p. 199

children.title: Primal–Dual Neighborhood Interface
children.top_down_role: Connection to complementarity-based neighborhoods used in primal–dual algorithms.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Neighborhood Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For logarithmic-barrier linear programming, the scaled complementarity residual bounds the barrier subproblem's restricted Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the barrier subproblem restricted to \(Ax=b\), primal-dual feasibility gives \[t c+\nabla F(x)-tA^{\mathsf T}y=X^{-1}(Xs/\mu-e).\] Consequently, the local dual norm of the gradient restricted to \(T\) satisfies \[\left\|\left.\nabla\bigl(t\langle c,\cdot\rangle+F\bigr)(x)\right|_T\right\|_{x,T,*}\leq\|Xs/\mu-e\|_2.\] Hence \(\|Xs/\mu-e\|_2\leq\theta\) supplies a barrier-geometric centrality certificate whose restricted Newton decrement is at most \(\theta\).
assumptions_latex: The vectors \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfy \(Ax=b\), \(x>0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(s>0\).
The primal logarithmic barrier is \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\), \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\), and \(t=1/\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled complementarity residual bounds the restricted barrier gradient in its local dual norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-programming interface between scaled complementarity residuals and barrier-gradient centrality.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix formed from the primal vector
All-ones vector in the primal variable space

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Use the strictly feasible conic pair and canonical barrier \(F\) from the conic primal–dual path interface. For \(X\in\operatorname{int}K\), define \(\|H\|_X^*=\langle[\nabla^2F(X)]^{-1}H,H\rangle^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly feasible conic primal–dual neighborhoods measured by the augmented-complementarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\) and a strictly primal–dual feasible pair \(Z=(X,S)\), define its centrality residual and distance by \[r_t(X,S)=tS+\nabla F(X),\qquad d_t(X,S)=\|r_t(X,S)\|_X^*.\] For \(\kappa\ge0\), the primal–dual neighborhood is \[\mathcal N^{\mathrm{pd}}_\kappa(t)=\{(X,S):X\in(L-B)\cap\operatorname{int}K,\ S\in(L^\perp+C)\cap\operatorname{int}K,\ d_t(X,S)\le\kappa\}.\] In the canonical self-dual setting, \(d_t(X,S)=\|tX+\nabla F(S)\|_S^*\), so the definition is symmetric between primal and dual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual central neighborhood consists of strictly feasible primal and dual points whose scaled barrier-gradient complementarity residual is small in the dual local norm at the primal point. For the canonical self-dual barrier, the same distance can be computed with primal and dual roles exchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(S\) are strictly feasible for their respective conic problems.
\(F\) is the canonical barrier on the self-dual cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_t(X,S)\le\kappa\) defines the primal–dual neighborhood linking complementarity centrality to barrier local norms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d_t(X,S)=\|tS+\nabla F(X)\|_X^*=\|tX+\nabla F(S)\|_S^*\).
\(d_t(X,S)=0\) if and only if the strictly feasible pair equals the central pair at parameter \(t\).
special_cases_latex: For semidefinite optimization, \(F(X)=-\log\det X\) and the residual is \(tS-X^{-1}\).
For linear optimization over \(\mathbb R_+^m\), the residual coordinates are \(t s_i-1/x_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The neighborhood directly interfaces barrier centrality with complementarity-based primal–dual algorithms.
The zero-radius neighborhood is exactly the coupled central path.
boundary_notes: If primal or dual feasibility is relaxed, feasibility residuals must be added; the displayed neighborhood alone does not control them.
The symmetry identity is specific to the canonical barrier framework cited here.

children.title: Path Accuracy Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates translating centrality and path parameters into optimization accuracy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a convex problem with optimum \(p^*\), a barrier path parameter \(t>0\), barrier parameter \(\vartheta>0\), and a nonnegative centrality measure \(\delta_t(x)\) that vanishes at the exact central point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates that combine path position with a quantified centrality error to upper-bound original optimization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A path accuracy certificate for a feasible point \(x\) is a tuple \((t,\delta,\varepsilon)\) together with a valid bound \[0\le f_0(x)-p^*\le B(t,\delta)\le\varepsilon,\] where \(\delta_t(x)\le\delta\), \(B(t,\delta)\) is nondecreasing in \(\delta\), and \(B(t,0)=\vartheta/t\) for the exact central path in the barrier model under consideration. The certificate is exact-central when \(\delta=0\), and approximate-central otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path accuracy certificate records a path parameter, a centrality tolerance, and an error tolerance. It is valid when feasibility and the centrality test imply an explicit upper bound on the original objective error, with the exact central-point bound equal to the barrier parameter divided by t.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible for the original primal problem.
The chosen function \(B\) is supported by the barrier model and the selected centrality measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\delta_t(x)\le\delta\) and \(B(t,\delta)\le\varepsilon\) certify \(f_0(x)-p^*\le\varepsilon\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an exact logarithmic-barrier central point with \(m\) scalar inequalities, \(B(t,0)=m/t\).
For a canonical conic barrier of parameter \(\theta\), \(B(t,0)=\theta/t\).
special_cases_latex: If a dual feasible point \(y\) accompanies \(x\), one may take \(B\) to be a certified primal–dual gap.
An exact central point is \(\varepsilon\)-accurate whenever \(t\ge\vartheta/\varepsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate separates centrality error from progress along the path.
A termination rule follows by checking feasibility, centrality, and the displayed bound.
boundary_notes: A path parameter alone does not certify an off-path point unless its centrality error is also controlled.
The form of \(B(t,\delta)\) is model-dependent; no universal off-path formula is asserted here.

notation.meaning: Selected centrality measure at parameter t.
Certified upper bound on original objective error.
Barrier complexity parameter in the exact-path gap bound.

children.title: Barrier-Subproblem Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy certification for approximate central points.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Subproblem Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton decrement below beta certifies barrier-subproblem objective error at most minus beta minus log of one minus beta.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The computable decrement certifies the subproblem error through \[0\leq f(x)-f(x_*)\leq\omega_*(\lambda_f(x))=-\lambda_f(x)-\log(1-\lambda_f(x)).\] In particular, requiring \(\lambda_f(x)\leq\beta<1\) guarantees \(f(x)-f(x_*)\leq\omega_*(\beta)\), so no knowledge of \(x_*\) is needed to verify the stated accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is standard self-concordant and has a minimizer \(x_*\).
At \(x\in Q\), the Newton decrement \(\lambda_f(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_{x,*}\) satisfies \(\lambda_f(x)<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq f(x)-f(x_*)\leq-\lambda_f(x)-\log(1-\lambda_f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-decrement certificate for the current barrier subproblem.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.4 Path-following scheme p. 199

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-Decrement Accuracy for a Barrier Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_t\) be a convex twice differentiable barrier objective on a feasible affine set and let \(x(t)\) be its unique minimizer. Let \(\lambda_t(x)\) denote the equality-constrained Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local accuracy for the current barrier subproblem, distinct from accuracy for the original constrained objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\eta\ge0\), a feasible interior point \(x\) is \(\eta\)-accurate for the barrier subproblem at parameter \(t\) if \[\Phi_t(x)-\Phi_t(x(t))\le\eta.\] A Newton-decrement certificate of barrier-subproblem accuracy is a threshold \(\rho\ge0\) and a supported function \(q\) such that \[\lambda_t(x)\le\rho\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Phi_t(x)-\Phi_t(x(t))\le q(\rho).\] For the local quadratic model, \(\lambda_t(x)^2/2\) is the predicted subproblem reduction and is the standard decrement-based stopping quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-subproblem accuracy is the objective gap between an approximate interior point and the exact minimizer of the current barrier objective. A Newton-decrement certificate converts a bound on the decrement into a bound on that gap. The common local stopping quantity is one half the squared decrement.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \(x(t)\) satisfy the affine constraints and lie in the barrier domain.
A rigorous function \(q\) requires the self-concordance regime and radius specified by its source.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_t(x)-\Phi_t(x(t))\le\eta\) defines subproblem accuracy, while \(\lambda_t(x)\le\rho\) is a local certificate when \(q(\rho)\le\eta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The decrement satisfies \(\lambda_t(x)^2=\langle H_t(x)\Delta_t(x),\Delta_t(x)\rangle\).
The quadratic model gap at its Newton minimizer equals \(\lambda_t(x)^2/2\).
special_cases_latex: At the exact central point, \(\lambda_t(x(t))=0\) and the subproblem gap is zero.
A stopping rule \(\lambda_t(x)^2/2\le\eta\) uses the quadratic-model estimate of the subproblem gap.
immediate_consequences_latex: Subproblem accuracy controls how completely a recentering phase has solved its current target.
It does not by itself quantify the original objective error, which also depends on \(t\).
boundary_notes: The quadratic-model identity is exact for the model, not automatically for the nonlinear objective.
Global objective-gap bounds from a decrement require the applicable self-concordant inequalities and their radius restrictions.

notation.meaning: Supported conversion from decrement radius to objective gap.

children.title: Original-Objective Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Transfer from path position to quality for the original constrained problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Objective Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point locally close to the central path has original linear-objective error at most the barrier-dependent quantity (nu plus rho times square root of nu) divided by t.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and \(x(t)\) minimizes \(t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\) for \(t>0\).
The value \(p_*=\inf_{z\in Q}\langle c,z\rangle\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\langle c,x\rangle-p_*\leq(\nu+\rho\sqrt{\nu})/t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective accuracy transferred from proximity to an exact barrier center.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the original linear objective over the barrier domain

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Accuracy for the Original Constrained Objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in Q,\ Ax=b\}\) be finite, and let \(x\) be feasible for the original constrained problem. Suppose a barrier path has exact central point \(x(t)\) and exact-path error bound \(f_0(x(t))-p^*\le\vartheta/t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal absolute objective accuracy and its certification from position on an exact barrier path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a feasible point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-accurate for the original objective if \[0\le f_0(x)-p^*\le\varepsilon.\] An exact central point \(x(t)\) has a path-position certificate of \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy whenever \[\frac{\vartheta}{t}\le\varepsilon.\] For the logarithmic barrier of \(m\) scalar inequalities, \(\vartheta=m\); for a canonical conic barrier, \(\vartheta\) is its barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original-objective accuracy means that a feasible point's objective value exceeds the optimum by at most epsilon. On an exact central path, the barrier parameter divided by the path parameter bounds this error, so choosing t at least the barrier parameter divided by epsilon certifies the desired accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible for the original constraints.
The exact-path bound \(f_0(x(t))-p^*\le\vartheta/t\) applies to the selected barrier model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\vartheta/\varepsilon\) implies \(f_0(x(t))-p^*\le\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an exact logarithmic-barrier central point, \(f_0(x(t))-p^*\le m/t\).
If a dual feasible certificate has value \(d\), the stronger computable condition \(f_0(x)-d\le\varepsilon\) also implies primal \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy.
special_cases_latex: For linear programming with \(m\) inequality slacks, \(t\ge m/\varepsilon\) suffices on the exact path.
When \(\varepsilon=0\), the definition requires exact primal optimality.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing \(t\) reduces the exact-path objective-error bound inversely.
Barrier-subproblem accuracy and original-objective accuracy are separate quantities and should not be conflated.
boundary_notes: An infeasible point is not primal \(\varepsilon\)-accurate under this definition, regardless of objective value.
For an approximate central point, an additional centrality-error term or primal–dual gap certificate is required.

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Barrier-theoretic connection to conic primal–dual termination certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificate Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible conic primal-dual pair, complementarity equals the duality gap and upper-bounds primal suboptimality; on the exact logarithmically homogeneous central path it equals nu divided by t.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak duality and feasibility give \[0\leq p(x)-p_*\leq p(x)-d(y)=\langle x,s\rangle.\] Hence \(\langle x,s\rangle\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(p(x)-p_*\leq\varepsilon\). On an exact logarithmically homogeneous central path satisfying the standard primal-dual centrality relation at parameter \(t>0\), \[\langle x(t),s(t)\rangle=\frac{\nu}{t}.\] Thus a neighborhood bound on complementarity converts directly into a primal-dual termination certificate.
assumptions_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone, and let \((x,y,s)\) be feasible for a conic primal-dual pair with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), primal objective \(p(x)=\langle c,x\rangle\), dual objective \(d(y)=\langle b,y\rangle\), and gap identity \(p(x)-d(y)=\langle x,s\rangle\).
The primal optimal value \(p_*\) is finite, and weak duality holds.
The cone interior is equipped with a logarithmically homogeneous barrier of parameter \(\nu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable complementarity \(\langle x,s\rangle\) equals the primal-dual gap and certifies primal suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic feasible-point certificate connecting barrier complementarity with termination by duality gap.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a conic primal–dual pair with primal objective \(p(X)\), dual objective \(d(S)\), common optimum under strong duality, and primal–dual feasible pair \((X,S)\). In the symmetric conic representation, let the complementarity pairing be \(\langle X,S\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible conic primal–dual termination certificates, including their exact value on a canonical central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal–dual gap certificate of a feasible pair \((X,S)\) is \[G(X,S)=p(X)-d(S)\ge0.\] In the symmetric conic representation, \(G(X,S)=\langle X,S\rangle\). The pair is \(\varepsilon\)-certified if \(G(X,S)\le\varepsilon\); then \(0\le p(X)-p^*\le G(X,S)\) and \(0\le d^*-d(S)\le G(X,S)\). On the canonical central path, \[G(X_*(t),S_*(t))=\frac{\theta}{t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any feasible primal and dual points, the difference between their objective values is a nonnegative certificate. It bounds both the primal error and the dual error. In symmetric conic form it equals the complementarity pairing, and on the canonical central path it equals the barrier parameter divided by t.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is primal feasible and \(S\) is dual feasible.
Weak duality holds; the two-sided error interpretation uses a common optimal value.
For the exact path formula, the cone has the cited canonical logarithmically homogeneous barrier of parameter \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(X,S)\le\varepsilon\) is a valid primal–dual termination certificate, and exact central pairs have \(G=\theta/t\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the symmetric conic form, \(G(X,S)=\langle X,S\rangle\).
For scalar inequalities on the logarithmic central path, \(G=m/t\).
special_cases_latex: In semidefinite optimization, \(G(X,S)=\operatorname{Tr}(XS)\).
A zero gap for a feasible pair certifies primal and dual optimality.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate is computable without knowing the optimal value.
The path parameter converts directly to a target gap on the exact central path.
boundary_notes: For infeasible iterates, the complementarity quantity is only a surrogate gap unless feasibility residuals are also controlled.
A small primal objective alone is not a certificate without a feasible dual lower bound.

notation.meaning: Primal objective minus dual objective at a feasible pair.

children.title: Path-Following Principle
children.top_down_role: High-level coupling of parameter advancement and Newton recentering without importing operational algorithm steps.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_t\) be a self-concordant path-generating family, let \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)\) be a specified centrality neighborhood, and let \(N_t(x)\) denote one full Newton correction for \(\Phi_t\) whenever it is defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract coupling of multiplicative parameter advancement and Newton recentering, stated as an invariant rather than an implementation procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A path-following scheme with neighborhood radius \(\beta\) is a sequence \(\{(t_k,x_k)\}_{k\ge0}\) for which \[t_{k+1}>t_k>0,\qquad x_k\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=N_{t_{k+1}}(x_k)\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_{k+1}).\] It is multiplicative with factor \(\sigma_k>1\) when \(t_{k+1}=\sigma_k t_k\). The defining principle is preservation of a controlled centrality invariant after advancing the target parameter and applying a Newton correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-following scheme is a sequence of parameter-point pairs that stays in a prescribed central neighborhood. Each parameter is increased, and a Newton correction for the new barrier objective returns the point to the same neighborhood. A multiplicative scheme advances the parameter by a factor greater than one.
assumptions_latex: \((t_0,x_0)\) belongs to the chosen path neighborhood.
Each Newton map \(N_{t_{k+1}}(x_k)\) is defined and remains in the barrier domain.
The parameter changes are small enough for the stated neighborhood invariant to hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relations \(x_k\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_k)\) and \(N_{t_{k+1}}(x_k)\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_{k+1})\) define the path-following principle.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s_k=\log t_k\), multiplicative advancement is additive: \(s_{k+1}-s_k=\log\sigma_k\).
The invariant may be expressed with a primal Newton-decrement neighborhood or a supported primal–dual residual neighborhood.
special_cases_latex: A short-step scheme uses \(\sigma_k=1+O(1/\sqrt\theta)\) for barrier parameter \(\theta\).
Exact centering corresponds to the limiting idealization \(x_k=x(t_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Maintaining centrality allows path progress and local Newton correction to be analyzed separately.
If exact-path error is \(\theta/t_k\), increasing \(t_k\) improves the associated accuracy scale.
boundary_notes: This definition does not prescribe line searches, linear solvers, or stopping implementations.
Large parameter changes may destroy the neighborhood invariant even though the next central point exists.

children.title: Parameter-Change Stability
children.top_down_role: Preservation of controlled centrality under admissible path-parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Change Stability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed iterate, changing t by a controlled relative amount preserves a controlled Newton-decrement neighborhood, with sensitivity governed by beta plus the square root of nu.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and \(\Phi_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t'>0\), \(\lambda_{t'}(x)\leq\beta+|t'/t-1|(\beta+\sqrt{\nu})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centrality bound at an unchanged iterate after modifying the path parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability of Centrality Under Parameter Advancement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_t\) be a self-concordant path family, let \(\lambda_t(x)\) be its Newton decrement, and let \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x:\lambda_t(x)\le\beta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform preservation of controlled centrality when only the target path parameter changes; Newton recentering is recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family is \((\beta,\widehat\beta,\alpha)\)-stable under multiplicative parameter increase if, for every \(t>0\), every \(x\in\mathcal N_\beta(t)\), and every \(t^+\) satisfying \[1\le\frac{t^+}{t}\le1+\alpha,\] one has \(x\in\mathcal N_{\widehat\beta}(t^+)\). It is uniformly parameter-change stable if the same constants work for all \(t>0\). It is one-step recoverable to radius \(\beta\) if additionally \[N_{t^+}(x)\in\mathcal N_\beta(t^+)\] for every such \((t,x,t^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter-change stability means that a point central for the old parameter remains within a controlled, possibly larger neighborhood for every admissible multiplicative increase. Uniformity requires constants independent of the current parameter. One-step recoverability adds that one Newton correction restores the original neighborhood radius.
assumptions_latex: For recoverability, the Newton map at \(t^+\) is well defined at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)\subseteq\mathcal N_{\widehat\beta}(t^+)\), followed optionally by \(N_{t^+}(x)\in\mathcal N_\beta(t^+)\), defines parameter-change stability and one-step recovery.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s=\log t\), the admissible change is \(0\le s^+-s\le\log(1+\alpha)\).
Uniform stability is the same inclusion with constants independent of \(t\).
special_cases_latex: For self-concordant short-step path following, admissible relative changes are typically proportional to \(1/\sqrt\theta\).
If \(t^+=t\), stability holds trivially with \(\widehat\beta=\beta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Parameter advancement and Newton recentering can be coupled through nested centrality radii.
Uniform constants permit repeated path updates without deterioration as \(t\) grows.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert numerical values of \(\alpha,\beta,\widehat\beta\); these depend on normalization and the chosen centrality measure.
Stability before correction is distinct from the stronger one-step recovery property.

notation.meaning: Permitted centrality radius immediately after parameter change.

children.title: Newton Recentering
children.top_down_role: Recovery of centrality through the self-concordant Newton mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Recentering
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full Newton step from the self-concordant local region remains in the domain and reduces the decrement quadratically, thereby restoring centrality after a parameter change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\), compute \(d=-\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x)\) and set \(x^+=x+d\). If \(\lambda_f(x)<1\), then \(x^+\in D\) and \[\lambda_f(x^+)\leq\left(\frac{\lambda_f(x)}{1-\lambda_f(x)}\right)^2.\] Repeating the update until \(\lambda_f(x)\leq\beta\), for a prescribed \(\beta\in(0,1)\), returns a point in the corresponding decrement neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian at \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(x^+=x-\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x)\), one has \(x^+\in D\) and \(\lambda_f(x^+)\leq(\lambda_f(x)/(1-\lambda_f(x)))^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full Newton correction in the local quadratic-convergence region.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton recentering for a self-concordant path objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\mathbb R\) be a self-concordant barrier with positive-definite Hessian on the open convex set \(\operatorname{dom}F\), and let \(c\in E^*\). For \(t\geq0\), set \(f_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\), \(\|u\|_x=\langle\nabla^2F(x)u,u\rangle^{1/2}\), and \(\|v\|_x^*=\langle v,[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}v\rangle^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, exact-arithmetic recentering for the primal barrier path; the definition does not cover primal-dual scaling directions or inexact linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a target parameter \(t_+\geq0\) and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), define the target Newton residual and decrement by \(r_{t_+}(x)=t_+c+
abla F(x)\) and \(\lambda_{t_+}(x)=\|r_{t_+}(x)\|_x^*\). The Newton recentering map is \(R_{t_+}(x)=x-[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\); a damped recentering with damping \(a\in(0,1]\) is \(R_{t_+,a}(x)=x-a[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\). Relative to a prescribed centrality radius \( eta\in(0,1)\), the update is a successful Newton recentering when \(R_{t_+,a}(x)\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(\lambda_{t_+}(R_{t_+,a}(x))\leq eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the barrier objective at a new path parameter, Newton recentering evaluates its gradient residual in the local Hessian metric and subtracts the inverse-Hessian residual, possibly with damping. Relative to a fixed centrality radius, the recentering is successful exactly when the updated point remains in the barrier domain and its Newton decrement for the new objective is at most that radius.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is twice differentiable on \(\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\) at the point being updated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_{t_+,a}(x)=x-a[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}(t_+c+\nabla F(x)),\qquad \text{successful}\iff R_{t_+,a}(x)\in\operatorname{dom}F\ \text{and}\ \lambda_{t_+}(R_{t_+,a}(x))\leq\beta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The undamped correction \(\Delta x=-[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\) is the unique solution of \(\nabla^2F(x)\Delta x=-r_{t_+}(x)\).
Exact centrality at the target parameter is \(r_{t_+}(x)=0\), equivalently \(\lambda_{t_+}(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(a=1\), \(R_{t_+,1}\) is the full Newton recentering map.
If \(t_+=t\), the update improves centering for the current path objective rather than compensating for a parameter change.
immediate_consequences_latex: A successful recentering returns the iterate to the certified neighborhood \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_+)=\{y\in\operatorname{dom}F:\lambda_{t_+}(y)\leq\beta\}\).
The recentering map is defined only where the local Hessian is invertible.
boundary_notes: The definition itself does not assert that a proposed parameter change or damping factor makes recentering successful.
Approximate Newton systems require a separate residual-error condition.

notation.meaning: Damped Newton recentering map for the target parameter.
Newton decrement of the barrier objective \(f_t\) at \(x\).

children.title: Initial-Center Interface
children.top_down_role: Dependence of path tracking on a certified initial neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Center Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path tracking starts in its certified local regime when the initial point is interior and its barrier-subproblem Newton decrement is below the chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)=\|t_0c+\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0,*}\). The pair \((x_0,t_0)\) is a certified initial center at radius \(\beta\) when \[x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta<1.\] This condition permits the cited local parameter-change and Newton-recentering estimates to be applied from the first path-following iteration; without such a certificate, those local estimates provide no initialization guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and \(\Phi_{t_0}(x)=t_0\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\) for \(t_0>0\).
A proposed starting point \(x_0\) lies in \(Q=\operatorname{dom}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta<1\) is a sufficient initial-center certificate for the stated local path-tracking recurrence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable entry condition for the local short-step path-following regime.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{dom}F\subset E\), let \(f_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\), and define \(\lambda_t(x)=\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\). Fix a centrality radius \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal short-step path following. This interface separates initialization from the subsequent certified tracking phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certified initial-center interface is a tuple \(I_0=(t_0,x_0,\beta,C_0)\) such that \(t_0\geq0\), \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\), and \(C_0\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}\) is a certified upper bound on the computational work used to produce \(x_0\) from the supplied problem data. A path-following complexity statement accepts this interface only when its tracking hypotheses begin at every pair \((t_0,x_0)\) satisfying the displayed membership and centrality conditions; initialization work is accounted for separately as \(C_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The initial-center interface consists of a starting path parameter, an interior point whose Newton decrement is within the prescribed central neighborhood, and a certified bound on the work needed to construct that point. The tracking phase may use the point only after these conditions are verified, and its iteration bound does not silently absorb an unspecified initialization procedure.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and its local dual norm is computable at \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_0\ \text{is certified}\iff t_0\geq0,\quad x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F,\quad \|t_0c+\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta,\quad C_0\ \text{bounds initialization work}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(t_0=0\), certification is \(\|\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta\), so \(x_0\) is an approximate analytic center.
Writing \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}F:\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\}\), the centrality condition is \(x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\).
special_cases_latex: An exact analytic center gives \(t_0=0\) and \(\lambda_0(x_0)=0\).
If the problem input directly supplies a verified center, one may take \(C_0=0\) in an iteration-only accounting convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: A tracking bound starting from \(I_0\) is conditional unless \(C_0\) is itself bounded in the chosen computational model.
Failure of either domain membership or the decrement test prevents invocation of the short-step tracking guarantee.
boundary_notes: A merely feasible point need not be a certified center.
The interface does not prescribe a unique phase-I construction; auxiliary-path and embedding methods are separate implementations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider finite-dimensional convex programs represented by a linear objective over a convex domain possessing a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Let \(\epsilon>0\) denote a requested objective-gap or primal-dual-gap accuracy, and let \(\beta\in(0,1)\) denote a certified central-neighborhood radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a definition of the common theorem template, not an assertion that every convex program or implementation satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The self-concordant path-following complexity theorem family is the collection of results indexed by a problem representation \(P\), barrier parameter \(
u\), neighborhood radius \( eta\), initialization certificate \(I_0\), correction model \(\mathfrak C\), and accuracy certificate \(\mathfrak A\), whose hypotheses guarantee: every generated iterate remains in the declared interior neighborhood; the path parameter changes by a relative amount of order \(
u^{-1/2}\) per bounded number of corrections; and an \(\epsilon\)-certificate is obtained after \(K\leq C\sqrt
u\log(M/\epsilon)+K_0\) corrections. Here \(C\) is independent of \(
u\) and \(\epsilon\), \(M>0\) is the theorem's stated initial scale, and \(K_0\) is its separately stated initialization contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This theorem family consists of path-following results whose data explicitly identify the barrier quality, central neighborhood, starting certificate, correction accuracy, and stopping certificate. A member guarantees neighborhood invariance and reaches the requested accuracy in a number of Newton-type corrections proportional to the square root of the barrier parameter times a logarithmic accuracy factor, plus any separately quantified initialization cost.
assumptions_latex: The problem representation supplies a computable \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on a nonempty interior domain.
The initial-center certificate \(I_0\), correction model \(\mathfrak C\), and accuracy certificate \(\mathfrak A\) satisfy the particular member theorem's explicit hypotheses.
The scale \(M\) and initialization contribution \(K_0\) are finite and specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K(P,\epsilon)\leq C\sqrt\nu\log(M/\epsilon)+K_0,\quad x_k\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_k)\ \text{for all generated iterates},\quad \mathfrak A(x_K)\leq\epsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A constant-factor increase in the path parameter costs \(O(\sqrt\nu)\) corrections, while a reduction of the accuracy scale from \(M\) to \(\epsilon\) requires \(O(\log(M/\epsilon))\) such factors.
special_cases_latex: For linear programming with the standard logarithmic barrier, \(\nu\) is proportional to the number of inequality or cone coordinates.
For an exact short-step method with a certified initial center, \(K_0=0\) under tracking-only iteration accounting.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family organizes distinct theorems by their initialization, neighborhood, and correction hypotheses rather than treating all interior-point variants as interchangeable.
The displayed correction count alone does not determine arithmetic or bit complexity.
boundary_notes: The constant \(C\), scale \(M\), certificate, and admissible correction errors depend on the selected member theorem.
Long-step, infeasible-start, and predictor-corrector results belong only when separately instantiated with their own hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Exact or inexact correction model specified by a member theorem.

children.title: Short-Step Path-Following Complexity
children.top_down_role: Canonical narrow-neighborhood complexity governed by the barrier parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Short-Step Path-Following Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact short-step path following reaches additive objective error epsilon in order square root of nu times the positive logarithm of the required parameter-growth factor, with constants determined by the maintained narrow neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and the original objective is linear.
A certified pair \((x_0,t_0)\), with \(t_0>0\), lies in a fixed narrow Newton-decrement neighborhood \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\), where \(\beta\in(0,1)\).

For fixed admissible constants \(\sigma>0\) and \(C_\beta>0\), each iteration replaces \(t\) by \((1+\sigma/\sqrt{\nu})t\), performs one full Newton step, preserves \(\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\), and satisfies the objective certificate \(\langle c,x\rangle-p_*\leq C_\beta\nu/t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is reached in \(O\!\left(\sqrt{\nu}\log_+\!\left(C_\beta\nu/(t_0\varepsilon)\right)\right)\) exact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact-Newton short-step bound for a linear objective and fixed narrow neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the primal-dual linear program, let \(\mathcal F^o\) be the strictly feasible set, \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(e=(1,\ldots,1)\), and \(\mu=x^Ts/n\). Define \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{(x,\lambda,s)\in\mathcal F^o:\|XSe-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic feasible-start primal-dual short-step method for linear programming, using the specific constants in Wright's Algorithm SPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Short-step path-following complexity is the correction bound attached to Algorithm SPF: start from \((x^0,\lambda^0,s^0)\in\mathcal N_2(0.4)\), choose \(\sigma=1-0.4/\sqrt n\), solve the primal-dual Newton equations exactly, and take the full step at every iteration. The iterates remain in \(\mathcal N_2(0.4)\), and \(\mu_{k+1}=\sigma\mu_k\). Consequently, if \(\mu_0\leq\epsilon^{-\kappa}\) for a constant \(\kappa>0\), the short-step correction complexity is \(K(\epsilon)=O(\sqrt n\log(1/\epsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical linear-programming short-step complexity applies to a strictly feasible point in the narrow two-norm neighborhood. Each iteration solves the exact primal-dual Newton equations, takes a unit step, and uses a centering factor equal to one minus 0.4 divided by the square root of the dimension. The neighborhood is invariant, the duality measure contracts by that factor, and the requested duality tolerance is reached in order square-root-of-dimension times logarithmic-in-accuracy iterations.
assumptions_latex: The Newton system is solved exactly and the full step is taken.
\(\epsilon>0\) and the linear program admits the stated strictly feasible primal-dual start.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_{k+1}=\left(1-\frac{0.4}{\sqrt n}\right)\mu_k,\qquad (x^k,\lambda^k,s^k)\in\mathcal N_2(0.4),\qquad K(\epsilon)=O\!\left(\sqrt n\log\frac1\epsilon\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A constant-factor reduction of \(\mu\) requires \(O(\sqrt n)\) full Newton corrections.
special_cases_latex: For a general logarithmic-barrier representation, the dimension factor is replaced by the square root of the corresponding barrier parameter when supported by the appropriate self-concordant theorem.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every iterate remains strictly primal-dual feasible.
The bound is an iteration count and does not include the cost of producing the initial point or solving each Newton system.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover the wider one-sided neighborhood used by long-step methods.
Changing the neighborhood, centering constant, or solve accuracy requires a different invariant-neighborhood result.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce epigraph variables \(\xi\) and \(\varkappa\) and form the lifted barrier \(\widehat F(x,\xi,\varkappa)=F_Q(x)+F_0(x,\xi)+\sum_{j=1}^mF_j(x,\varkappa)-\ln( ar\xi-\xi)-\ln(-\varkappa)\). If the component barrier parameters are \(

u_j+2\). Functional-constraint path complexity is the short-step correction bound obtained by applying the self-concordant path scheme to this lifted domain: its principal dependence is \(O(\sqrt{\widehat
u})\) times logarithmic factors in the requested accuracy and the explicitly stated size and Slater-depth characteristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear convex functional-constraint problem inherits self-concordant path complexity when its basic set and all relevant epigraphs have computable self-concordant barriers. After lifting the objective and constraints, the barriers add, and their parameters add together with two scalar logarithmic barriers. The leading iteration dependence is the square root of this total parameter, multiplied by logarithmic accuracy and conditioning terms.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is bounded, closed, convex, and has nonempty interior.

children.title: Starting-Neighborhood Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost attributable to reaching a certified starting neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity of reaching the starting neighborhood
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, let \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and let \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}F:\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\leq\beta\}\). Let \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\) be an available interior point that need not be centered.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-path initialization for a primal self-concordant barrier scheme; it measures the preliminary corrections before ordinary path tracking begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The starting-neighborhood complexity \(K_{\mathrm{start}}(y_0,\beta)\) is the least certified number of Newton-type corrections required by the specified initialization procedure to output some \((t_0,x_0)\) with \(x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\). For the auxiliary path joining \(y_0\) to the analytic center, this cost is bounded by a quantity of order \(\sqrt\nu\) times logarithms of \(\nu\) and the declared initial gradient scale. The total correction count is defined additively by \(K_{\mathrm{total}}(\epsilon)=K_{\mathrm{start}}+K_{\mathrm{track}}(\epsilon;t_0,x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting-neighborhood complexity counts the certified preliminary Newton corrections needed to turn an available interior point into a point satisfying the path method's centrality test. For auxiliary path initialization, its leading dependence is square root of the barrier parameter times logarithms of the barrier and initial gradient scale. This cost is added to, rather than hidden inside, the subsequent tracking cost.
assumptions_latex: An interior point \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and the local barrier oracle are available.
The initialization procedure declares a stopping test that guarantees membership in \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\).
All logarithmic scale quantities appearing in its bound are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_{\mathrm{start}}=\min\{k:\text{the initialization certificate yields }(t_0,x_0),\ x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\},\qquad K_{\mathrm{total}}=K_{\mathrm{start}}+K_{\mathrm{track}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For analytic-center initialization, the target condition is \(\|\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta\).
Initialization complexity is a phase-I correction count with a centrality certificate as its output contract.
special_cases_latex: If the supplied point already lies in \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\), then \(K_{\mathrm{start}}=0\).
If only an arbitrary interior point is known, the auxiliary central path may be traced toward an approximate analytic center.
immediate_consequences_latex: A tracking-only bound is not a complete end-to-end iteration bound unless \(K_{\mathrm{start}}\) is zero or separately controlled.
The starting procedure may have the same \(O(\sqrt\nu)\) leading barrier dependence as the main path-following phase.
boundary_notes: This definition presupposes that at least one usable interior point is available; constructing such a point can require another phase-I procedure.
The minimum is relative to the declared initialization model and oracle, not over all conceivable algorithms.

notation.meaning: Certified correction count for entering the starting neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Initialization Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-concordant Phase-I path can initialize the main path in square-root-barrier times logarithmic accuracy iterations, excluding problem-dependent construction costs.
assumptions_latex: An auxiliary Phase-I problem has a \(\nu_I\)-self-concordant barrier and linear auxiliary objective.
A certified initial center for its parameter \(t_I^0>0\) is known.
Auxiliary objective error at most \(\varepsilon_I\) suffices to produce the required main-path starting certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialization requires \(O(\sqrt{\nu_I}log(\nu_I/(t_I^0\varepsilon_I)))\) Phase-I Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional cost of obtaining a main-path start through an auxiliary self-concordant Phase-I problem.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The generic path-following citation does not specify a Phase-I construction or prove that the stated auxiliary accuracy yields the required main-path starting certificate. Those problem-dependent facts determine whether the initialization bound applies. The displayed formulas also contain malformed commands, but source support is needed before a reliable replacement can be formulated.
